Part 5:

 Isn’t “libertarian child-rearing” just another name for spoiling the child?




No. This objection confuses the distinction between freedom and license. To raise a child in freedom does not mean letting him or her walk all over you or others; it does not mean never saying “no.” It is true that free children are not subjected to punishment, irrational authority, or moralistic admonitions, but they are not “free” to violate the rights of others. As Neill put it: 

“in the disciplined home, the children have 

no

 rights. In the spoiled home, they have 

all

 the rights. The proper home is one in which children and adults have equal rights.”

 Or again: 

“To let a child have his own way, or do what he wants to 

at another’s expense,

 is bad for the child. It creates a spoiled child, and the spoiled child is a bad citizen.”

 [

Summerhill

, p. 107 and 167]




There will inevitably be conflicts of will between parents and children, and the healthy way to resolve them is discussion and coming to an agreement. The unhealthy ways are either to resort to authoritarian discipline or to spoil the child by allowing them to have all the social rights. Libertarian psychologists argue that no harm is done to children by insisting on one’s individual rights, but that the harm comes from moralism, i.e. when one introduces the concepts of right and wrong or words like “naughty,” “bad,” or “dirty,” which produce guilt.




Therefore, it should not be thought that free children are free to “do as they please.” Freedom means doing what one likes so long as it does not infringe on the freedom of others. Thus there is a big difference between compelling a child to stop throwing stones at others and compelling him or her to learn geometry. Throwing stones infringes on others’ rights, but learning geometry involves only the child. The same goes for forcing children to eat with a fork instead of their fingers; to say “please” and “thank you”; to tidy up their rooms, and so on. Bad manners and untidiness may be annoying to adults, but they are not a violation of adults’ rights. One could, of course, define an adult “right” to be free of annoyance from 

anything

 one’s child does, but this would simply be a license for authoritarianism, emptying the concept of children’s rights of all content.




As mentioned, giving children freedom does not mean allowing them to endanger themselves physically. For example, a sick child should not be asked to decide whether he wants to go outdoors or take his prescribed medicine, nor a run-down and overtired child whether she wants to go to bed. But the imposition of such forms of necessary authority is compatible with the idea that children should be given as much responsibility as they can handle at their particular age. Only in this way can they develop self-assurance. And, again, it is important for parents to examine their own motives when deciding how much responsibility to give their child. Parents who insist on choosing their children’s clothes for them, for example, are generally worried that the child might select clothes that would reflect badly on their parents’ social standing.




As for those who equate “discipline” in the home with “obedience,” the latter is usually required of a child to satisfy the adults’ desire for power. Self-regulation means that there are no power games being played with children, no loud voice saying “You’ll do it because I say so, or else!” But, although this irrational, power-seeking kind of authority is absent in the libertarian home, there still remains what can be called a kind of “authority,” namely adult protection, care, and responsibility, as well as the insistence on one’s own rights. As Neill observed: 

“Such authority sometimes demands obedience but at other times gives obedience. Thus I can say to my daughter, ‘You can’t bring that mud and water into our parlour.’ That’s no more than her saying to me, ‘Get out of my room, Daddy. I don’t want you here now,’ a wish that I, of course, obey without a word.”

 [

Op. Cit.

, p. 156]. So there will still be “discipline” in the libertarian home, but it will be of the kind that protects the individual rights of each family member.




Raising children in freedom also does not imply giving them a lot of toys, money, and so on. Reich’s followers have argued that children should not be given everything they ask for and that it is better to give them too little than too much. Under constant bombardment by commercial advertising campaigns, parents today generally tend to give their children far too much, with the result that the children stop appreciating gifts and rarely value any of their possessions. This same applies to money, which, if given in excess, can be detrimental to children’s’ creativity and play life. If children are not given too many toys, they will derive creative joy out of making their own toys out of whatever free materials are at hand — a joy of which they are robbed by overindulgence. Psychologists point out that parents who give too many presents are often trying to compensate for giving too little love.




There is less danger in rewarding children than there is in punishing them, but rewards can still undermine a child’s morale. This is because, firstly, rewards are superfluous and in fact often 

decrease

 motivation and creativity, as several psychological studies have shown (see section I.4.11 of the Anarchist FAQ). Creative people work for the pleasure of creating; monetary interests are not central (or necessary) to the creative process. Secondly, rewards send the wrong message, namely, that doing the deed for which the reward is offered is not worth doing for its own sake and the pleasure associated with productive, creative activity. Thirdly, rewards tend to reinforce the worst aspects of the competitive system, leading to the attitude that money is the only thing which can motivate people to do the work that needs doing in society.




These are just a few of the considerations that enter into the distinction between spoiling children and raising them in freedom. In reality, it is the punishment and fear of a disciplinarian home that 

spoils

 children in the most literal sense, by destroying their childhood happiness and creating warped personalities. As adults, the victims of disciplinarianism will generally be burdened with one or more anti-social secondary drives such as sadism, destructive urges, greed, sexual perversions, etc., as well as repressed rage and fear. The presence of such impulses just below the surface of consciousness causes anxiety, which is automatically defended against by psychological walls which leave the person stiff, frustrated, bitter and burdened with feelings of inner emptiness. In such a condition people easily fall victim to the capitalist gospel of super-consumption, which promises that money will enable them to fill the inner void by purchasing commodities — a promise that, of course, is hollow.




The neurotically enclosed person also tends to look for scapegoats on whom to blame his or her frustration and anxiety and against whom repressed rage can be vented. Reactionary politicians know very well how to direct such impulses against minorities or “hostile nations” with propaganda designed to serve the interests of the ruling elite. Most importantly, however, the respect for authority combined with sadistic impulses which is acquired from a disciplinarian upbringing typically produces a submissive/authoritarian personality — a man or woman who blindly follows the orders of “superiors” while at the same time desiring to exercise authority on “subordinates,” whether in the family, the state bureaucracy, or the company. Ervin Staub’s 

Roots of Evil

 includes interviews of imprisoned SS men, who, in the course of extensive interviews (meant to determine how ostensibly “normal” people could perform acts of untold ruthlessness and violence) revealed that they overwhelmingly came from authoritarian, disciplinarian homes.




In this way, the “traditional” (e.g., authoritarian, disciplinarian, patriarchal) family is the necessary foundation for authoritarian civilisation, reproducing it and its attendant social evils from generation to generation.

No doubt most members of the ruling elite are not fully conscious that their own power and privileges depend on the mass perpetuation of sex-negative attitudes. Nevertheless, they unconsciously sense it. Sexual freedom is the most basic and powerful kind, and every conservative or reactionary instinctively shudders at the thought of the “social chaos” it would unleash — that is, the rebellious, authority-defying type of character it would nourish. This is why “family values,” and “religion” (i.e. discipline and compulsive sexual morality) are the mainstays of the conservative/reactionary agenda. Thus, it is crucially important for anarchists to address every aspect of sexual suppression in society. This means affirming the right of adolescents to an unrestricted sex life.




There are numerous arguments for teenage sexual liberation. For example, many teen suicides could be prevented by removing the restrictions on adolescent sexuality. This becomes clear from ethnological studies of sexually unrepressive tribal peoples:




“All reports, whether by missionaries or scholars, with or without the proper indignation about the ‘moral depravity’ of ‘savages,’ state that the puberty rites of adolescents lead them immediately into a sexual life; that some of these primitive societies lay great emphasis on sexual pleasure; that the puberty rite is an important social event; that some primitive peoples not only do not hinder the sexual life of adolescents but encourage it is every way, as, for instance, by arranging for community houses in which the adolescents settle at the start of puberty in order to be able to enjoy sexual intercourse. Even in those primitive societies in which the institution of strict monogamous marriage exists, adolescents are given complete freedom to enjoy sexual intercourse from the beginning of puberty to marriage. None of these reports contains any indication of sexual misery or suicide by adolescents suffering from unrequited love (although the latter does of course occur). The contradiction between sexual maturity and the absence of genital sexual gratification is non-existent.”




Reich, 

Op. Cit.

,

p. 85




Teenage sexual repression is also closely connected with crime. If there are teenagers in a neighbourhood who have no place to pursue intimate sexual relationships, they will do it in dark corners, in cars or vans, etc., always on the alert and anxious lest someone discover them. Under such conditions, full gratification is impossible, leading to a build-up of tension and frustration. Thus they feel unsatisfied, disturb each other, become jealous and angry, get into fights, turn to drugs as a substitute for a satisfying sex life, vandalise property to let off “steam” (repressed rage), or even murder someone. As Reich noted, 

“juvenile delinquency is the visible expression of the subterranean sexual crisis in the lives of children and adolescents. And it may be predicted that no society will ever succeed in solving this problem, the problem of juvenile psychopathology, unless that society can muster the courage and acquire the knowledge to regulate the sexual life of its children and adolescents in a sex-affirmative manner.”

 [

Op. Cit.

, p. 271]




For these reasons, it is clear that a solution to the “gang problem” also depends on adolescent sexual liberation. We are not suggesting, of course, that gangs themselves suppress sexual activity. Indeed, one of their main attractions to teens is undoubtedly the hope of more opportunities for sex as a gang member. However, gangs’ typical obsessiveness with the promiscuous, pornographic, sadistic, and other “dark” aspects of sex shows that by the time children reach gang age they have already developed unhealthy secondary drives due to the generally sex-negative and repressive environment in which they have grown up. The expression of such drives is 

not

 what anarchists mean by “sexual freedom.” Rather, anarchist proposals for teenage liberation are based on the premise that a libertarian childhood is the necessary condition for a 

healthy

 sexual freedom in adolescence.




Applying these insights to our own society, it is clear that teenagers should have ample access to a private room where they can be undisturbed with their sexual partners. Parents should also encourage the knowledge and use of contraceptives and safe sex in general as well as respect for the other person involved in the relationship. This does not mean encouraging promiscuity or sex for the sake of it. Rather, it means encouraging teenagers to know their own minds and desires, refusing to be pressured by anyone into anything. As can be seen from experience of this anarchist activist during the 1930s:




“One time, a companero from the Juventudes [libertarian youth organisation] came over to me and said, ‘You, who say you’re so liberated. You’re not so liberated.’ (I’m telling you this so you’ll see the mentality of these men.) ‘Because if I ask you to give me a kiss, you wouldn’t.




“I just stood there staring at him, and thinking to myself, ‘How do I get out of this one?” And then I said to him, ‘Listen, when I want to go to bed with a guy, I’m the one that has to choose him. I don’t go to bed with just anyone. You don’t interest me as a man. I don’t feel anything for you… Why should you want me to ‘liberate myself,’ as you put it, by going to bed with you? That’s no liberation for me. That’s just making love simply for the sake of making love.’ ‘No,’ I said to him, ‘love is something that has to be like eating: if you’re hungry, you eat, and if you want to go to bed with a guy, then… Besides, I’m going to tell you something else… Your mouth doesn’t appeal to me… And I don’t like to make love with a guy without kissing him.’




“He was left speechless! But I did it with a dual purpose in mind… because I wanted to show him that that’s not the way to educate companeros… That’s what the struggle of women was like in Spain — even with men from our own group — and I’m not even talking about what it was like with other guys.”




quoted by Martha A. Ackelsberg,

Free Women of Spain

,

pp. 116-7




So respecting yourself and others, it must be stressed, is essential. As Maurice Brinton pointed out, attempts at sexual liberation will encounter two kinds of responses from established society — direct opposition and attempts at recuperation. The second response takes the form of 

“first alienating and reifying sexuality, and then of frenetically exploiting this empty shell for commercial ends. As modern youth breaks out of the dual stranglehold of repressive traditional morality and of the authoritarian patriarchal family it encounters a projected image of free sexuality which is in fact a manipulatory distortion of it.”

 This can be seen from the use of sex in advertising to the successful development of sex into a major consumer industry. However, such a development is the opposite of the healthy sexuality desired by anarchists. This is because 

“sex is presented as something to be consumed. But the sexual instinct differs from certain other instincts”

 as it can be satisfied only by 

“another human being, capable of thinking, acting, suffering. The alienation of sexuality under the conditions of modern capitalism is very much part of the general alienating process, in which people are converted into objects (in this case, objects of sexual consumption) and relationships are drained of human content. Undiscriminating, compulsive sexual activity, is not sexual freedom — although it may sometimes be a preparation for it (which repressive morality can never be). The illusion that alienated sex is sexual freedom constitutes yet another obstacle on the road to total emancipation. Sexual freedom implies a realisation and understanding of the autonomy of others.”

 [

“The Irrational in Politics”

, pp. 257-92, 

For Workers’ Power

, p. 277]




Therefore, anarchists see teenage sexual liberation as a means of developing free individuals 

as well as

 reducing the evil effects of sexual repression (which, we must note, also helps dehumanise individuals by encouraging the objectification of others, and in a patriarchal society particularly of women).




Part 7:

 But isn’t this concern with sexual liberation just a distraction from revolution?




It would be insulting to teenagers to suggest that sexual freedom is, or should be, their 

only

 concern. Many teens have a well-developed social conscience and are keenly interested in problems of economic exploitation, poverty, social breakdown, environmental degradation, and the like. The same can be said of people of any age!




It is essential for anarchists to guard against the attitude typically found in Marxist-Leninist parties that spontaneous discussions about sexual problems are a “diversion from the class struggle.” Such an attitude is economistic (not to mention covertly ascetic), because it is based on the premise that economic class must be the focus of all revolutionary efforts toward social change. No doubt transforming the economy is important, but without mass sexual liberation no working class revolution can be complete as there will not be enough people around with the character structures necessary to create a 

lasting

 self-managed society and economy (i.e., people who are capable of accepting freedom with responsibility). Instead, the attempt to force the creation of such a system without preparing the necessary psychological soil for its growth will lead to a reversion to some new form of hierarchy and exploitation. Equally, society would be “free” in name only if repressive social morals existed and people were not able to express themselves as they so desire.




Moreover, for many people breaking free from the sexual suppression that threatens to cripple them psychologically is a major issue in their lives. For this reason, few of them are likely to be attracted to the anarchist “freedom” movement if its exponents limit themselves to dry discussions of surplus value, alienated labour, and so forth. Instead, addressing sexual questions and problems must be integrated into a multi-faceted attack on the total system of domination. People should feel confident that anarchists are on the side of sexual pleasure and are not revolutionary ascetics demanding self-denial for the “sake of the revolution.” Rather, it should be stressed that the capacity for full sexual enjoyment is an essential part of the revolution. Indeed, 

“incessant questioning and challenge to authority on the subject of sex and of the compulsive family can only complement the questioning and challenge to authority in other areas (for instance on the subject of who is to dominate the work process — or the purpose of work itself). Both challenges stress the autonomy of individuals and their domination over important aspects of their lives. Both expose the alienated concepts which pass for rationality and which govern so much of our thinking and behaviour. The task of the conscious revolutionary is to make both challenges explicit, to point out their deeply subversive content, and to explain their inter-relation.”

 [Maurice Brinton, 

“The Irrational in Politics”

, pp. 257-92, 

For Workers’ Power

, p. 278]




We noted previously that in pre-patriarchal society, which rests on a communistic/communal social order, children have complete sexual freedom and that the idea of childhood asceticism develops as such societies turn toward patriarchy in the economic and social structure (see section B.1.5 of An Anarchist FAQ). This sea-change in social attitudes toward sexuality allows the authority-oriented character structure to develop instead of the formerly non-authoritarian ones. Ethnological research has shown that in pre-patriarchal societies the general nature of work life in the community corresponds with the free development of children and adolescents — that is, there are no rules coercing children and adolescents into specific forms of sexual life, and this creates the psychological basis for voluntary integration into the community and voluntary discipline in all forms of collective activity. This supports the premise that widespread sex-positive attitudes are a necessary condition of a viable libertarian socialism.




Psychology also clearly shows that every impediment to free expression of children by parents, teachers, or administrative authorities must be stopped. As anarchists, our preferred way of doing so is by direct action. Thus we should encourage all to feel that they have every chance of building their own personal lives. This will certainly not be an obstacle to or a distraction from their involvement in the anarchist movement. On the contrary, if they can gradually solve the problems facing their private lives, they will work on other social projects with greatly increased pleasure and concentration.




Besides engaging in direct action, anarchists can also support legal protection for free expression and sexuality (repeal of the insane statutory rape laws and equal rights for gays, for example), just as they support legislation that protects workers’ right to strike, family leave, and so forth. However, as Reich observed, 

“under no circumstances will the new order of sexual life be established by the decree of a central authority.”

 [

The Sexual Revolution

, p. 279] That was a Leninist illusion. Rather, it will be established from the bottom up, by the gradual process of ever more widespread dissemination of knowledge about the adverse personal and social effects of sexual repression, and the benefits of libertarian child-rearing and educational methods.




A society in which people are capable of sexual happiness will be one where they prefer to 

“make love, not war,”

 and so will provide the best guarantee for the general security. Then the anarchist project of restructuring the economic and political systems will proceed spontaneously, based on a spirit of joy rather than hatred and revenge. Only then can it be defended against reactionary threats, because the majority will be on the side of freedom and capable of using it responsibly, rather than unconsciously longing for an authoritarian father-figure to tell them what to do.




Therefore, concern and action upon sexual liberation, libertarian child rearing and libertarian education are 

key

 parts of social struggle and change. In no way can they be considered as “distractions” from “important” political and economic issues as some “serious” revolutionaries like to claim. As Martha A. Ackelsberg notes in relation to the practical work done by the 

Mujeres Libres

 group during the Spanish Revolution:




“Respecting children and educating them well was vitally important to the process of revolutionary change. Ignorance made people particularly vulnerable to oppression and suffering. More importantly, education prepared people for social life. Authoritarian schools (or families), based upon fear, prepared people to be submissive to an authoritarian government [or within a capitalist workplace]. Different schools and families would be necessary to prepare people to live in a society without domination.”




Free Women of Spain

,

p. 133




The personal 

is

 political and there is little point in producing a free economy if the people in it are not free to lead a full and pleasurable life! As such, the issue of sexual freedom is as important as economic and social freedom for anarchists. This can be seen when Emma Goldman recounted meeting Kropotkin who praised a paper she was involved with but proclaimed 

“it would do more if it would not waste so much space discussing sex.”

 She disagreed and a heated argument ensued about 

“the place of the sex problem in anarchist propaganda.”

 Finally, she remarked 

“All right, dear comrade, when I have reached your age, the sex question may no longer be of importance to me. But it is now, and it is a tremendous factor for thousands, millions even, of young people.”

 This, Goldman recalled, made Kropotkin stop short with 

“an amused smile lighting up his kindly face. ‘Fancy, I didn’t think of that,’ he replied. ‘Perhaps you are right, after all.’ He beamed affectionately upon me, with a humorous twinkle in his eye.”

 [

Living My Life

, vol. 1, p. 253]

author: CNT Bilbao
title: La clase trabajadora para en el 11N: huelga, calle y organización
content:
Bilbao y Euskal Herria han vivido hoy una jornada de huelga general con las ciudades paradas y manifestaciones masivas. El bloque propio de CNT en la manifestación ha contado con una gran participación. Han sido horas de movilización en las que también hemos tenido que denunciar las actuaciones de la Ertzaintza contra huelguistas y manifestantes.







Según la información de nuestras secciones sindicales, el seguimiento en la CAPV ha sido desigual según los sectores. En la enseñanza, los centros han funcionado con servicios mínimos y el seguimiento ha sido muy alto, casi absoluto. En la industria, los centros han superado el 50 % de seguimiento de forma generalizada, con alguna excepción de poco seguimiento en centros pequeños, de menos de 50 personas trabajadoras. En el transporte público han pesado los servicios mínimos. En la sanidad el seguimiento ha sido irregular, aunque muy notable en el ámbito administrativo, y conviene recordar que el sector mantiene sus propias huelgas. En el comercio, donde ha habido manifestaciones el cierre ha sido absoluto y en muchos barrios las persianas han estado bajadas por la mañana. En la hostelería, algunos bares se habían comprometido a cerrar y otros no.







Esa irregularidad no es casual. Hoy hemos hecho huelga y hemos salido a la calle porque los derechos no se piden: se conquistan y se defienden. La jornada de ocho horas, las vacaciones pagadas o la protección frente al despido no fueron regalos, sino fruto de huelgas, cajas de resistencia y décadas de organización colectiva. La huelga es mucho más que una movilización: es la protesta que interrumpe la producción, la que duele a la patronal cuando se refleja en sus cuentas, la que sale de las grandes manifestaciones y entra en los centros de trabajo. Demuestra que somos quienes hacemos funcionar la economía y que tenemos la capacidad de pararla.







Sabemos también que no todo el mundo puede hacer huelga. Las mujeres migrantes sin papeles, atrapadas por la Ley de Extranjería, se juegan mucho más que el salario de un día. Lo mismo ocurre con quienes tienen contratos tan precarios que ejercer su derecho puede costarles el empleo, con los falsos autónomos sin protección, con las trabajadoras de los cuidados y del hogar, sin convenio ni interlocutor, con quienes quedan atrapadas en cadenas de contratas y subcontratas, o con quienes temen las represalias de empresas que han hecho de la amenaza una forma de gestionar las relaciones laborales. Que no puedan hacer huelga demuestra que la precariedad está diseñada para que defender los derechos salga caro. Quienes hoy hemos podido parar hacemos nuestra también su lucha, porque el apoyo mutuo es la base de nuestro sindicalismo.







Desde CNT exigimos lo que en justicia nos corresponde: salarios y pensiones dignos, reducción de jornada sin bajar el sueldo, y trabajo y vivienda para todas las personas. Entendemos además que el Estado no es una institución neutral, y no aceptamos que la patronal y el Estado hagan con nuestros derechos lo que quieran, devolviéndonos nuestras demandas recortadas y irreconocibles. Tampoco aceptamos que se nos divida dejando a las trabajadoras migrantes sin derechos. Queremos todo para todas, y solo lo conseguiremos juntas, mediante la acción directa y en organizaciones propias de clase, independientes de gobiernos, instituciones y partidos.




Para CNT, la huelga de hoy es un punto de partida. Veinticuatro horas de paro no bastan, pero son un comienzo. Mañana tenemos que seguir juntas, quienes hemos podido parar y quienes no, reforzando la organización en nuestros centros de trabajo a través de las secciones sindicales y las asambleas, y en barrios y pueblos a través de redes de solidaridad vecinal. Que esta huelga se haya organizado de abajo arriba demuestra que la horizontalidad, las asambleas y el apoyo mutuo son la clave. La huelga es nuestra herramienta, la solidaridad nuestra fuerza y la organización nuestro camino. ¡Fuerza, compañeras!







La entrada 

La clase trabajadora para en el 11N: huelga, calle y organización

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: CNT Santander
title: Seguimos en lucha
content:
A las 4:30h de la mañana de este 11 de noviembre, comenzamos de madrugada con los piquetes informativos en los que hicimos fuerza conjunta con CGT, CJS, Sindicato de Vivienda, Acampada de Vivienda de Cantabria, Las Calles contra el Fascismo, La Asamblea Antifascista y el PCTE. Conseguimos paralizar la salida de los autobuses del Polígono Industrial Candina, paramos el tráfico en diferentes puntos de la ciudad de Santander, en Valdecilla Sur, en Marqués de la Hermida; y al llegar a la estación frenamos la circulación. Fuimos recorriendo distintas calles a medida que avanzaba la mañana.




La convocatoria que organizamos a las 12:00h en Peña Herbosa ha sido un éxito. Más de 3.000 personas han caminado junto a nosotrxs.













Secundada por el Sindicato de Estudiantes de Cantabria y acompañadas por diferentes sindicatos y colectivos, (CGT, CJS, Sindicato de Vivienda, Acampada de Vivienda de Cantabria, STEC, Libres y Combativas, etc.), junto a personas que de manera individual han querido sumarse, la concentración resultó una marea de reivindicación y lucha obrera.













Tras la parada para comer colectivamente en nuestra sede y descansar para reponer energías, ya estamos preparadas para seguir luchando en la concentración de las 19:00h en Cuatro Caminos.




Acompañaremos al Sindicato de la Vivienda de Cantabria y la Acampada en su recorrido, con el resto de los colectivos con los que llevamos semanas trabajando, porque entendemos que la lucha colectiva llena más el corazón.




Hoy ha sido un paso firme en la reivindicación de una vivienda digna y accesible para todas, que incluya la defensa de las familias y las personas más vulnerables. Porque el acceso a la vivienda no es un privilegio como quieren que creamos, es un derecho al que no vamos a renunciar.













Cuando caminamos todas a una, con un mismo objetivo, somos visibles e imparables. Hoy, lo hemos demostrado. Ha quedado evidenciado durante toda la jornada de la mañana.




Gracias a todas las que nos han acompañado y luchado a nuestro lado.




Seguimos, con más fuerzas que nunca, para luchar por nuestros derechos y conquistar al sistema capitalista y patriarcal lo que nos pertenece.




¡Que viva la lucha de la clase obrera y del colectivo estudiantil!




¡Salud!

Seguimos en lucha

 se publicó primero en 

CNT Santander

.

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: CNT Aragón-Rioja
title: CNT celebra una jornada histórica para la clase obrera
content:
Desde el Sindicato CNT Zaragoza valoramos muy positivamente la jornada de Huelga General que hemos vivido, o mejor dicho convivido, este 11 de Noviembre en nuestra ciudad. 

El apoyo mostrado entre distintas organizaciones, el buen intercambio de experiencia y funciones

 – aún con cuestiones a pulir – , 

nos ha permitido llevar la lucha por toda Zaragoza durante toda la noche y el día, dejándonos un poso muy esperanzador en el porvenir de nuestra Clase Obrera

.




Empezando por 

parar los camiones de FCC

 y ocupar la carretera de Castellón, nuestra ruta en Cogullada con empresas donde consigue victorias CNT – como 

Cerma&Arriaxa

 -, informando a autobuseros de 

Cerler

 y Trox, apoyando el piquete de los trabajadores de CAF, encontrándonos con el Bicipiquete por las calles, comprobando que al menos un 60% de la plantilla en 

CityLogin

 (Amazon) no acudía a trabajar tras las labores de nuestra Sección Sindical… y acabando por esa enorme Manifestación, a pesar del cansancio y la lluvia, con 

un Mitin final de las compañeras del Sindicato de Inquilinas del que CNT Zaragoza no cambiaríamos una coma

.




Basta de confiar en promesas de quienes usan nuestras luchas, victorias o derrotas, para apoyar en ellas su discurso político buscando ganar y gobernar en nuestro nombre. Sólo la Clase Obrera salvará a la Clase Obrera. Nuestro sindicato lo tiene claro. 

Hoy hemos gritado hasta dejarnos la voz: viva la CNT, viva la lucha obrera, viva la lucha por la vivienda, y viva la Huelga General

.




Gracias a toda las compañeras y compañeros que lo han hecho posible, de CNT o del resto de Sindicatos y organizaciones de Zaragoza. 

Nos veremos en el sindicato, nos veremos en las empresas, nos veremos en las calles. Porque la lucha es el único camino

.

author: Sofia Amaral
title: Os ventos que vêm dos EUA e o clima quente na COP31
content:
Nesta semana, acontece o evento mais importante para as negociações climáticas: a COP31, realizada na Turquia. No 

Bom dia, fim do mundo

 desta semana, Isabel Seta, Marina Amaral e Ricardo Terto explicam o que está em jogo na Conferência deste ano e — spoiler: não é nada muito diferente dos anos anteriores, afinal, as negociações climáticas andam a passos de tartaruga, enquanto o aquecimento do planeta parece seguir de vento em popa. As 

COPs

 ainda são, no entanto, a melhor aposta dos países para conter a emergência climática. Ruim com ela, pior sem ela? Com uma crise energética no horizonte e um El Niño que já faz estragos mundo afora, a melhor saída é apostar no multilateralismo — o que fica mais fácil após as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA. Ouça agora.







E MAIS:




Na Trombeta, corações partidos. E no quadro “Se é pra falar de economia…”, Eliane Barbosa fala de uma economia que continua degradando o planeta.

author: Administrador
title: Eine Entschuldigung.
content:
An die Kollektive und Familien Sucherinnen der Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos.

Eine Entschuldigung. Oder viele Entschuldigungen – derart, dass sie alle und jede einzelne Familie Sucherinnen, welche sich auf der Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos versammeln, erreichen.

Wir fühlten uns angegriffen und verletzt. Wir haben durch mich Antwort gegeben (die Compas sind gewöhnlich heftiger), und Ihr habt Euch ebenso oder noch mehr gekränkt gefühlt.

Bezüglich der Worte liegt die Verantwortung vollkommen bei mir, dem Capitán Insurgente Primero de Infantería Marcos. Meine Worte wurden als Aggressionen gegen Euch verstanden. Wirklich, ich bedauere es.

Von Herzen bitte ich Euch um Entschuldigung, Euch gekränkt, verletzt und angegriffen zu haben. Es nutzt nichts zu sagen, es war keine Absicht oder als Ausrede »den Stress« wegen der Angriffe der drei Regierungsebenen zu verwenden. Ich sollte im Gebrauch von Worten und Tonfall vorsichtiger und klüger sein. Ich hoffe, es wird mir nutzen zu lernen, mich mit Takt und Sorgfalt an diejenigen zu richten, die Wahrheit und Gerechtigkeit suchen.

Es ist klar, wir denken: Art und Weisen, Geographien und Kalender müssen respektiert werden. Wir sagen Euch mit Aufrichtigkeit: Wir hoffen, Ihr habt mit Eurer Beharrlichkeit Erfolg und findet alle möglichen Abwesenheiten/Vermissten. Und findet immerzu auch die Form, diejenigen zu umarmen, welche alleine suchen, mit nicht mehr Unterstützung als ihrer eigenen Wut.

Denn manchmal kann vergessen werden, dass sich darum alles handelt: den*diejenige*n zu finden, der*die fehlt.

Nochmals meine Entschuldigungen an Euch. Ich hoffe wirklich, Ihr findet in Euren Herzen die nötige Güte, sie anzunehmen.

Ansonsten: Jede*r nach seinem*ihrem Modus und Kalender, seiner*ihrer Geographie … und Agenda.

Aus den Bergen des Südosten Mexikos.

Bezüglich der Initiative: Wir haben keine anderen Kontakte nach außen als das Frayba, niemanden sonst. Nur wenn sich im Zeitplan, der Agenda ein Punkt konkretisiert, machen wir einen direkten Kontakt mit den Gruppen und Kollektiven der Familien Sucherinnen oder den Familien Sucherinnen im besonderen – aber immer dem Frayba Bescheid gebend, welches die Registrierung, das Register macht.

author: Administrador
title: Fragen.
content:
An die Familien Sucherinnen mit oder ohne Kollektiv.

Seit dem 3. Oktober in den Nachmittagsstunden haben Personen, die der Glorieta de Los Desaparecidos nahestehen, in ihren sozialen Netzwerken bekanntgegeben, ein Treffen zwischen Familien-Kollektiven und der EZLN für den 6. Dezember an der Glorieta de Los y Las Desapericidos sei bestätigt – zu der Zeit hatte die Comisión Sexta [Zapatista] eine Versammlung mit Beauftragten der Sexta Nacional; daran haben, ohne [vorherige] Einladung, einige Sucherinnen teilgenommen.

Tage später hat jemand und im Namen der Familien Sucherinnen der »La Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos« in seinen sozialen Netzwerken eine »Einladung« zirkulieren lassen. Durch verschiedene Medien wurde ihnen vermittelt, so sei nicht das Vorgehen. Sie sollten die Einladung via des [Menschenrechtszentrums] Frayba schicken, welches uns unterstützt hat und weiterhin unterstützt, bezüglich der Registrierung und der Vorschläge der Familien, Gruppen, Kollektive* der Sucherinnen.

Danach, ebenfalls einige Tage später, haben wir ihnen Nachrichten via verschiedene Kanäle gesandt: Sie sollten ihre Einladung zurückziehen, denn derart würde sie zurückgewiesen werden. Sie beinhalte Erwähnungen, die als Zeichen dafür betrachtet werden könnten, dass sie diejenigen, die sie eingeladen haben, nicht kennen; Dinge, die für die zapatistischen Comunidades als kränkend angesehen werden könnten.

Auch sei es nicht die Art von »Versammlungen«, an die die Comisión Sexta denke, und dass es der zapatistischen Delegation zukommt, ihre Agenda zu bestimmen, mit Daten und Uhrzeiten.

Nicht nur haben sie uns nicht beachtet, sie weiteten ihre Verbreitung [des Treffens] aus und fügten an, es sei gesichert, dass es das Treffen mit der zapatistischen Delegation auf dem Glorieta-Platz geben würde, mit gesetztem Datum, sogar in einigen Fällen mit Uhrzeit.

Wir bestanden darauf, ihnen weiter Nachrichten zu schicken, sie sollten deswegen [siehe obige Gründe] die Einladung umarbeiten. Unterdessen wuchs die Konfusion weiter an; Gruppen und Kollektive fingen an, ihre Daten zu ändern, um bei »DER« Versammlung anwesend zu sein. Wir warnten sie, dass sie uns an den Rand eines öffentlichen Widerspruchs bringen. Dies bedeutet, eine genaue Antwort, um klarzustellen.

Soweit wir verstehen, ist La Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos keine Organisation sondern ein Raum des Zusammentreffens. Das bedeutet, sie haben keine etablierten Sprecher*innen oder Leitung. Es ist ein Ort, wo Gruppen und Kollektive der Familien Sucherinnen gewöhnlich zusammenkommen. Wir haben angenommen, sie hatten oder haben eine Einrichtung, um Übereinkünfte und Entscheidungen zu treffen. Und dass sie diesem Mechanismus [der Entscheidungsfindung] deshalb die Zulässigkeit oder Nicht-Zulässigkeit des abgefassten Schreibens [der »Einladung«] unterwerfen würden, welches – und das wussten sie zuvor – bei den Zapatistas solchen Ärger erzeugt hat.

Die »Einladung« beinhaltet drei grundlegende Punkte:

1.- Den Zapatistas wird Unterstützung angeboten. Darum haben sie die zapatistischen Comunidades »eingeladen«, Fotos ihrer Verschwundengemachten mitzubringen, und dass sie uns zeigen würden: wie ein Plakat mit der Suchanzeige für gewaltsam Verschwundengemachte hergestellt wird und wie es auf der Glorieta angeklebt wird, zusammen mit hunderten Fotos von Verschwundengemachten; welche Formalitäten gemacht werden müssen, damit eine NGO Finanzierung gewährt; an wen sich innerhalb der Regierungspyramide zu richten ist etc.

Schwestern Familien Sucherinnen: Innerhalb des zapatistischen Gebietes und den Gemeinden, die zuvor zapatistisch waren und jetzt Partei-Anhänge*rinnen sind, gibt es seit 30 Jahren KEIN GEWALTSAMES VERSCHWUNDENMACHEN.

Schaut, es gibt feministische Gruppen, die all das kennen, was mit Feminiziden in Verbindung steht. Andere Gruppen mit der Ermordung von Kindern, wieder andere mit Menschenhandel, andere mit ungestraften Verbrechen, andere mit Homophobie, andere mit Rassismus und Segregation; und so weiter mit jedem dieser Schrecken, die in dieser Mexiko genannten Geographie erlitten werden.

Bevor uns Workshops für diese Probleme angeboten werden, wäre da nicht zu erwarten, dass sie zumindest die Prozentzahl der allgemeinen Gender-Gewalt – sie sagen dazu bereits nicht mehr Feminizide – untersuchen würden? Denn ja, innerhalb zapatistischen Gebietes gibt es keine Feminizide. Kein Mord an Kindern oder ungestrafte Verbrechen. Kein Menschenhandel (nun, ein Geschäft: Kauf-Verkauf von Frauen, Männern und Kindern). Und somit, ob Ihr blond, groß oder eine unverständliche Sprache sprecht, Ihr betretet und verlasst zapatistisches Gebiet, ohne verschwundengemacht, gedemütigt, verspottet, versklavt, ermordet zu werden.

Keine Homophobie. Somit wenn Ihr Otroas-AnderE seid (lesbisch, schwul, transsexuell und all die Bezeichnungen, mit der sich die sexuelle Differenz identifiziert), könnt Ihr heterosexuellen Kindern Unterricht geben (claro, wenn Ihr ausgebildet wurdet), Milizionär*in sein, verantwortliche Arbeiten in der Gemeinde und innerhalb der Organisation übernehmen, und Euch nennen, wie es Euch gefällt, und die Gender-Identität haben, die Euch Freude macht.

Es gibt sogar welche, die zu kommen versucht haben, um Unterricht in Erotik und erotischer Selbststimulation zu geben.

Schwestern, wir haben die höchste Geburtenrate, verglichen mit der großer Städte, und glaubt mir, es sind nicht Erotik-Klassen, die uns fehlen. Die Lieblingsmusik der Mehrheit der zapatistischen Jugend ist Rock, Ska, Rap, Hip-Hop … und Cumbia. Sie hören und tanzen Cumbia, und sagt mir, ob es nicht dort eine »erotische Selbststimulation« gibt.

Ok, sie sagen uns, das ist, weil sie auf dem Glorieta-Platz nicht wissen, was der Zapatismus ist. Die Gruppen, Kollektive und Netzwerke der Familien Sucherinnen haben keinen Grund, wer oder was die EZLN ist, zu wissen oder zu kennen. Ja, es ist Unwissenheit und nicht Unredlichkeit.

Einverstanden. Warum lädst du dann aber einen Unbekannten in dein Haus ein? Ist es nicht unverantwortlich, jemanden in dein Haus und zu deinen Leuten zu bringen, von dem du nichts weißt und der außerdem noch sein Gesicht verbirgt? Habt Ihr bedacht, was ein verdecktes Gesicht für viele Familien Sucherinnen bedeutet?

Wäre es nicht einfacher gewesen, der Glorieta nahestehende Leute zu fragen, sie um eine, wenn auch kurze, Vorstellung des Zapatismus »von Chiapas«, wie sie sagen, zu bitten – und so zu merken, dass dies – Unterstützung, Hilfe, Beratung anzubieten – »freundlich« gesagt, unweise war?

2.- »Warum erst jetzt?« und: »Was gewinnt die EZLN dabei?« Diese Fragen treiben Personen um, die sagen, sie sind von der Bewegung für den Frieden mit Gerechtigkeit und Würde (MPJD) – mit tristem Erinnerungsvermögen im Kampf für Wahrheit und Gerechtigkeit – sowie von der Glorieta. Und sie wiederholen die »Einladung« in anderer Handschrift:

»Ich bin sicher, dass die Zapatistas mit dieser Initiative der Umarmung etwas gewinnen. Denn keine*r macht etwas, ohne dafür etwas zu erhalten«, meinte ohne Befangenheit eine Sucherin von der MPJD und der Glorieta in einer Versammlung mit städtischen Kollektiven, die sich organisiert haben, um die zapatistische Delegation zu empfangen.

Die Frage ist nicht nur eine Beleidigung von jedem, sie spiegelt auch das Unwissen über die eigene Geschichte und die Beziehung wider, die es zwischen MPJD und EZLN vor 15 Jahren gab. Sie sagen auch, sie wollen keine Umarmungen; das ist eine bittere Ironie innerhalb einer Bewegung, die darin gipfelte, dem Psychopathen Felipe Calderón Hinojosa [mexikanischer Präsident 2006-2012; mit ihm begann der sogenannte »Krieg gegen die Drogen«] Küsse zu geben. Auch dass sie in Frage stellen, was die EZLN mit dieser Initiative wohl gewinnen mag – nachdem die MPJD dabei geendet ist, einer mittelmäßigen und miserablen Persönlichkeit wie Emilio Álvarez Icaza zum Aufstieg zu verhelfen (der verschiedene Parteien durchlief und »unabhängig« war, immer den Ultrarechten zutragend, und heute Teil der paradoxen Partei »Somos México – Wir sind Mexiko« ist). Sowie noch weiterer Lügen, die in der angeblich progressistischen Presse Widerhall fanden – welche sich nicht damit aufhält, wenigstens minimal zu untersuchen, was sie da eigentlich veröffentlicht, und damit die scheinbare Glaubwürdigkeit von Autorenbüchern und die bereits schwache Legitimität der Zeitschrift in den Müll wirft.

Schwestern Sucherinnen, hier bleibt wenig zu sagen. Es ist eine Entscheidung, die Ihr treffen müsst. Ich erzähle Euch jedoch etwas [anderes]:

Die Comunidades Originarios in Mexiko waren mehr als 500 Jahre verschwundengemacht, einige noch immer. Ich werde nicht von allen sprechen (dazu könnt Ihr auf den Congreso Nacional Indígena zurückgreifen, der gerade den 30. Jahrestag seines Kampfs als Netzwerk der indigenen Barrios, Pueblos, Sprachen, Bewegungen und Organisationen beging), sondern nur von den Comunidades der Zapatistas.

Vor 1994 haben die Comunidades Originarios von Chiapas nicht existiert. Sie wurden nicht geboren und sie starben nicht, denn ihre Geburt wurde noch nicht einmal registriert. Immer noch sind heutzutage tausende von Indígenas nicht als »Mexikaner« anerkannt, denn sie werden als Migranten in ihrem eigenen Land angesehen, wo ihre Eltern, Großeltern Urgroßeltern, Ururgroßeltern seit Jahrhunderten lebten.

Als wir uns in Waffen erhoben, vor fast 33 Jahren, hat das Land uns »gefunden, getroffen«. Natürlich hat ihnen unser In-Erscheinung-treten nicht gefallen. Vielleicht hätten sie bevorzugt, es wäre innerhalb des Kunsthandwerks geschehen, bei »lustigen« Tänzen oder an der Ecke Obst verkaufend. Aber gut, so sind wir eben: entgegengesetzt. Und so haben wir den schlechten Regierungen den Krieg erklärt und besetzten am 1. Januar 1994 sieben Landkreisstädte des Bundesstaates Chiapas im Südosten MEXIKOS.

Nach den ersten Kämpfen, mit Verlusten auf beiden Seiten, sowohl bei der Bundes-Armee wie bei den Zapatistas, »erhob sich« eine Gruppe von Leuten und sagte so etwas wie: »Moment einmal, wer sind sie eigentlich?« – und begaben sich mittenhinein. Ernsthaft, nicht im übertragenen Sinne, sondern mitten in die Schüsse. Und bei diesen Leuten waren Intellektuelle, NGOs, Leute ohne Partei … sowie Künstler*innen dabei. Nein, es tauchten nicht die revolutionären Avantgarden auf. Diese warteten darauf zu sehen, ob uns die Soldaten vernichten. Als sie sahen, dass das nicht passierte, tauchten sie auf, nun, es sind Avantgarden. Aber gut, diese Leute baten uns zuerst um ein Einstellen des Feuers, danach um einen Waffenstillstand. Und sie baten uns, eine Dialog zu führen, uns zu präsentieren, uns zu zeigen, nun, nicht schießend sondern mit Worten. Danach haben sie verschiedene Initiativen umgesetzt, um uns zu unterstützen oder diejenigen zu unterstützen, um die wir sie baten.

Und sie gaben uns eine Möglichkeit, eine Lebensmöglichkeit. Die unsere – nicht die, welche die von oben diktierten, die ja nicht Leben bedeutete. Und jede Sache, die wir bis heute tun, ist dazu da, diese Menschen zu ehren.

Schwestern Sucherinnen, glaubt Ihr, wir beschweren uns bei Euch/ bei ihnen? Dass wir fragen: »Warum erst jetzt?« »Warum, wo wir doch Jahrhunderte verschwundengemacht wurden, seht Ihr uns erst jetzt?« Nein, Schwestern Sucherinnen, stattdessen haben wir ihnen/ Euch gedankt, uns die Möglichkeit gegeben zu haben, zu leben (nicht, zu überleben oder im Stillschweigen und im Vergessenwerden zu sterben). Und wir haben damals gewusst und wissen es heute, dass sie nichts zu gewinnen hatten, jedoch viel zu verlieren.

Denn es hätte ja sein können, dass alles ein Betrug wäre (genau wie die MPJD es behauptet), wir in Wirklichkeit Zeit zu gewinnen suchten, Waffen und Munition zu erwerben, Zwangsrekrutierungen durchzuführen, Terrorismus zu praktizieren, Entführungen und Überfälle zu machen, Frauen mit heller Haut zu vergewaltigen und zu ermorden, aus Rache, aus Groll, aus Wut, einfach so, usw. Sie [die uns unterstützt haben/ uns unterstützen] gingen also ein Risiko ein. Nicht nur in Mexiko, sondern auch in anderen Teilen der Welt. Sogar in Spanien, dem Lieblingsfeind der 4T.

Und somit gab es Konzerte, Tanzvergnügen, Plakate, Theater, Tanzaufführungen, Flugblätter, Ausstellungen, Kunstwerke, Veranstaltungen, Gesprächsrunden, Runde Tische, Seminare, Trödel-Verkauf, Bücher, um ökonomische Unterstützung zusammenzubringen.

Genau wie jetzt gibt es all das und mehr, um Euch Schwestern darin zu unterstützen, nach Mexiko-Stadt zu kommen, uns die Geschichte Eures Vermissten zu erzählen, Eures Schmerzes, Eurer Hoffnung, Eurer Verpflichtung. Dass Ihr kommt, nicht zu großen Massenaktionen und Medienspektakeln, zu großen, mittleren oder kleinen Vollversammlungen, Treffen/ Kundgebungen, wo nur wenige reden und der Rest lediglich applaudiert, Parolen ruft und zuhört.

Und alles, um … eine Umarmung zu erhalten. Wie eine*r schrieb: Das erste Werk der Liebe ist eine Umarmung. Die Umarmung, die die MPJD verschmäht. Die Umarmung zwischen Schmerzen, Widerständen und Rebellionen.

Und, Schwestern, eine Umarmung hat nichts mit öffentlichen Massen-Medien-Aufführungen zu tun.

Wir bitten Euch nicht, dass Ihr von der Glorieta weggeht und Ihr [dann dort] weniger seid. Im Gegenteil, wachst an und seid viele. Jedoch wir gehen nicht dorthin, wo sie uns, wie sie sagen »eingeladen haben«, denn unser Ziel ist, persönliche Treffen zu haben, um Euch zuzuhören.

Der andere Punkt in der »Einladung« ist der Vorschlag in sich_ ein Akt auf dem Glorieta-Platz.

Sagen wir mal, es sind 400 Gruppen, die sich auf dem Platz der Glorieta treffen. Sagen wir mal, dass dort ein*e Repräsentant*in eines jedes Kollektivs spricht. Sagen wir mal, sie können ihren Schmerz, ihre Geschichte und die ihres Vermissten … in 10 Minuten … zusammenfassen? Das wären 4.000 Minuten, heißt, 66 Stunden. Fast drei Tage lang fortlaufende Beiträge, ohne Pause, ohne Essen und Schlaf. Dazu die Begrüßungsworte, das Erklären der Geschichte der Glorieta, von allen Netzwerken, Bewegungen, Zusammenschlüssen der dazu aufgerufenen Familien Sucherinnen. Nicht zur reden von den »spontanen« Beiträgen und Grüßen der politischen Partei »Somos MX«, oder wie immer sie heißen mag. Und dann noch als Letztes die zapatistischen Worte, die niemals darin brillierten, kurz zu sein. All das an einem Ort, an einem Tag, bei einer Kundgebung, die sich als ein Treffen ausgibt.

Ich glaube, wir waren darin klar: Was wir möchten, ist Euer Wort zu hören, Schwestern der Familien und Gruppen Sucherinnen. Dies an einem Tag würde nicht ausreichen.

Warum sonst sollten wir 1.530 Delegierte* haben? Warum sind sie so organisiert, dass sie sich »zerstreuen«, also in 25 Gruppen zu je 50 aufteilen? Warum ist jede Gruppe zu 50 so organisiert, dass sie sich in mehrere Untergruppen mit jeweils bis zu 5 Delegierten aufteilt?

Warum gibt es eine Haupt-Koordinierungsgruppe, die für das Ganze und seine Teile das Monotoring macht? Warum haben wir bei der Comunidad Originaria Otomí der Casa Samir insistiert, dass bei unserer Unterkunft die Räume für die gleichzeitigen Treffen Vorrang haben vor Schlafräumen und Küche? Warum haben wir ihnen gesagt, uns reicht zur Schlafenszeit eine Kartonpappe zwischen Boden und Körper? Warum haben wir ihnen gesagt, sie brauchen sich nicht um unser Essen zu sorgen, denn gemäß wissenschaftlicher Studien gibt dir eine »Guajolota« (Tamales-Sandwich) Energie für eine ganze Woche?

Wir verstehen, unsere Fahrt kann Eifersüchteleien hervorrufen: dass wir den Hauptaugenmerk auf bestimmte zwielichtige Gestalten, auf große, mittlere oder kleine Gruppen von Familien, die suchen oder von Kollektiven wegnehmen wollten; dass wir etwas dabei herausschlagen wollten (so wie es in aller Töpelhaftigkeit die MPJD behauptet, welche ja nur die Plattform der Partei »Somos México« stärken möchte. Deren gesamte Strategie basiert auf dem, wie sie es nennen, »Phänomen« des Verschwundenmachens in Mexiko; sie möchten aus dem massenhaften Schmerz ihre Wählerstimmen herausschlagen. Ohne Skrupel macht sie den Vorschlag, bei der Partido Acción Nacional (PAN) um finanzielle Unterstützung zu bitten. Obwohl unter deren Regierung (Felipe Calderón Hinojosa) ein Albtraum begann, der über vier Präsidentschaftsperioden … und denen, die noch kommen werden … andauert und sich verschärft hat. So sieht es aus: Die Verbrecher fordern Wahrheit und Gerechtigkeit.)

Compañeras und Schwestern, wir, die Comunidades, haben lediglich Schulden gewonnen, um unsere Reise zu bezahlen; wir haben für nichts Kandidaten und Kandidatinnen, wir sind nicht in einer Kampagne der Zwangsrekrutierung oder Zwanglos-Rekrutierung, wir sammeln keine Spenden für Treffen, die, wie wir uns vorstellen, für Euch und für uns sehr schmerzhaft sein werden. Die gesamte Finanzierungskampagne ist für Eure Reisen, für Euren Aufenthalt und Eure Unterkunft, für Eure Gesundheitsversorgung und für Euren Transport innerhalb Mexiko-Stadt.

Wir werden sogar Freiwillige dazu aufrufen, um eine Begleit-Equipe zu schaffen; Begleiter und Begleiterinnen, die Euch während der Strecken innerhalb der Stadt umsorgen, Euch daran erinnern, Eure Medizin zu nehmen, aufpassen, dass Ihr Euch nicht verirrt, Euch empfehlen, nichts zu essen, was Euch Schaden bereiten könnte. Derartige Dinge.

Es sind Freiwillige (und sicherlich wird es nicht an Freiwilligen* fehlen); sie werden keinen Lohn, Gehalt oder Preis erhalten, außer dem Stolz, einen humanitären Akt umzusetzen, sie erhalten nicht nur nichts, sondern setzen vor allem ihre eigene freie Zeit, ihr Einkommen sowie körperliche und emotionale Kräfte ein. Und ich sage emotional, weil Schwestern, Euch zuzuhören, wird schwer und heftig sein, und es wird jeden ehrlichen und anständigen Menschen dazu führen, sich zu fragen: »Wie schaffen sie es, all das zu erleiden und dennoch mit ihrer Suche weiterzumachen?«

Wir verstehen jedoch Euer Misstrauen. Obzwar wir nicht fahren, um Eure Anerkennung, Vertrauen und Zuneigung zu gewinnen. Wir werden Euch zuhören. Nicht denjenigen, die öffentlich gut sprechen, sich mit Worten auszudrücken wissen, die von Gesetzen und Geschichte Ahnung haben (wie zu sehen ist, sehr wenige) oder in der Redekunst geschickt sind.

Mit den Worten, die Eure Angst ausdrücken, mit den Tränen, in denen Euer Schmerz spricht, mit dem Schweigen, das sich einfindet, ist es gut für uns.

Ich habe einen Beitrag des Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés, Koordinator dieses Kapitels für das Leben, gehört, wo er den abwesenden, fehlenden Menschen als das Hauptsächliche aufzeigt. Wer ist oder war sie*er? Wie war er*sie körperlich? Wie in der Familie, in der Schule, bei der Arbeit, im Stadtteil, auf dem Feld, als Partner*in? Was ist passiert?

Und natürlich auch Euer Kampf, um sie*ihn zu finden, und was diese Abwesenheit in Euren Leben erzeugt hat, sowie die Geschwisterlicheit oder nicht mit anderen Familien, die suchen.

Zusammengefasst: Der Zeitplan der zapatistischen Delegation ist sehr einfach: Wir werden in Mexiko-Stadt, in der »Casa Samir Flores Soberanes« sein. Wir werden dort den ganzen Dezember sowie die erste Januar-Woche sein.

Einige Teile des Ganzen der Delegation gehen zu künstlerischen Aktivitäten, als jugendliche Theatermacher*innen, manchmal um ihre Stücke zu präsentieren, manchmal um Aufführungen professioneller Künstlerinnen beizuwohnen. Andere Teile werden zu Treffen mit Studierenden und Universitätslehrenden gehen. Diese Uni-Bande ist gut, sie hat Lust zu lernen und sie balgen sich mit der Arbeit herum, zu der sie sich selbst verpflichtet haben; vielleicht kann ich Euch überzeugen, dabei zu sein. All das, falls es Zeit und Raum gibt, denn das Hauptsächliche ist, Euch zuzuhören … Euch zu umarmen, jedoch freiwillig und nicht aufgezwungen.

Auch gehen Teile der Delegation in die Städte Xalapa, Guadalajara, Puebla und Querétaro. Nach Oaxaca werden wir nicht gehen können, aus Zeit- und Kostengründen. Diese Tage noch werden wir Euch die Daten zu jedem Ort sagen und wo sich zu registrieren ist. Ihr könnt wählen, zu dem Euch nahegelegenen Ort zu fahren oder nach Mexiko-Stadt, oder zu beiden.

An diesen [vereinbarten] Tagen wird eine Delegation aus Zapatistas zur Verfügung stehen, alle Originarios Maya, die bereit ist, Euch zu empfangen und Euch zuzuhören.

Bald wird auch eine Reihe von Konzerten, Tanz-, Theater- und Kino-Vorstellungen, sowie Kinder-Unterhaltung und Flohmärkte beginnen, mit dem einzigen Ziel, Geldmittel zusammenzubringen, damit Ihr reisen könnt, einen Ort zum Verweilen, eine Unterkunft, einen Ort zum Essen und einen Ort für Treffen habt.

Aus den Bergen des Südosten Mexikos.

title: Sultangazi'de 6'ncı kattaki evinin balkonundan düşen kadın ağır yaralandı
content:
İstanbul - Sultangazi'de binanın 6'ncı katındaki evinin balkonundan düşen N.T, ağır yaralanarak hastaneye kaldırıldı.

DHA'da yer alan habere göre olay, saat 22.00 sularında Sultançiftliği Mahallesi'nde meydana geldi. Binanın 6'ncı katında yaşayan N.T. adlı kadın, evinin balkonundan şüpheli bir biçimde aşağı düştü. Sağlık ekiplerinin yaptığı kontrolde ağır yaralandığı belirlenen N.T, olay yerindeki ilk müdahalesinin ardından hastaneye kaldırıldı. Soruşturma sürüyor.

Olayın gerçekleştiği sokakta çiğ köfte dükkanı işleten Ramazan Kaya, "Burada esnafım, dükkanda da müşterim vardı. O anda bir ses geldi, araba kazası sandım. Sonrasında dışarı çıktığımda milletin toplandığını gördüm. Kadının dengesini kaybederek aşağı düştüğünü tahmin ediyorum. Kendisi yıllardır komşumdur, iyi insandır. Ailecek de herhangi bir sıkıntıları yoktu. Evde eşiyle beraber kalıyordu. Çocukları da var ama başka yerde oturuyorlar. N.T'yi en son iki gün önce gördüm. Buradan geçtiğinde hal hatır sorardı. Olayın sonrasında polis ve ambulans ekipleri geldi, olay yeri inceleme ekipleri gelip çalışma yaptı" ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: UCM'den Trump ve Rubio'nun Gazze'deki soykırıma desteğinin soruşturulması istendi
content:
Fotoğraf: Official White House Photo by Molly Riley/Wikimedia Commons Public domain

Soykırıma Karşı Vergi Mükellefleri İttifakından (TAAG) yapılan yazılı açıklamada, grubun, Trump, Rubio ve bazı üst düzey ABD’li yetkililerin İsrail’in Gazze’de "işlediği soykırım", "savaş suçları" ve "insanlığa karşı suçlara yardım ettiği" iddiasının soruşturulması için dün Hollanda'nın Lahey kentindeki UCM Savcılık Ofisine resmi başvuruda bulunduğu belirtildi.

Üst düzey ABD’li yetkililerin "İsrail’in Gazze’de işlediği suçlara yardım ettiği" vurgulanan açıklamada, Gazze’de görev yapan doktorların yeminli beyanlarının, görgü tanıklarının ifadelerinin, video kayıtlarının ve ABD’nin İsrail’e verdiği askeri, mali, diplomatik ve siyasi desteğe ilişkin belgelerin savcılığa sunulduğu ifade edildi.

Açıklamada, başvuruda Gazze’de iki kez görev yapan ABD’li travma cerrahı Dr. Feroze Sidhwa ile Gazze İnsani Vakfının eski yöneticilerinden David McIntosh’un tanıklıklarının da yer aldığı vurgulanarak, "soykırımı finanse edenler, silahlandırarak suça yardım ve yataklık edenler için artık cezasızlık olmaması" ve hiçbir yetkilinin uluslararası hukukun üzerinde olmaması gerektiği çağrısı yapıldı.

Birleşmiş Milletler Filistin Özel Raportörü Francesca Albanese, başvurunun ardından Lahey’de düzenlenen basın toplantısında, uluslararası hukukun, adaletsizlikle yüzleşmek ve ileriye giden yolu açmak için elde kalan son barışçıl araç olduğunu söyledi.

author: Unknown
title: Çiğdem Doğu: Young people no longer accept the life imposed by capitalism
content:
Kurdistan Women's Communities (KJK) Executive Council member Çiğdem Doğu appeared on a special program broadcast by Medya Haber television, where she discussed the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Leader Apo (Abdullah Öcalan) and violence against women.




The first part of this in-depth interview can be read 

here

.




Looking beyond the Middle East region to world politics, Trump has not fallen, but he has become increasingly surrounded. Democrats and Republicans have clashed, and electoral balances have shifted. Meanwhile, youth-led resistance and uprisings are taking place in Spain, France and Italy. How should we interpret these developments? What direction are these changing balances giving to the broader process?




There was also an election in Brazil, where Lula won. He represents a more democratic and somewhat more left-leaning position. There was also an election in Serbia. This was a very important experience. A candidate list was formed under the leadership of the student youth movement. The students themselves were not on the list, but they supported democratic and honest politicians whom they believed in. That list won. This provides a very important indication for evaluating certain developments.




There was also a recent election in the United States. We cannot simply conclude that the peoples won or that the Democrats won in a broader democratic sense. But certain signals emerged, and it is important to evaluate them. We all know Trump. The peoples of the world know him. He emerged as a model of imperial leadership. He was perhaps the clearest example of the type described by the Kurdish People's Leader in the manifesto as a "murderous, hierarchical" personality. He disregarded everyone and paid no attention whatsoever to the peoples.




This tendency already exists within the capitalist system. At least when nation-states first emerged, there was a legal system, even if it was never fully implemented. Trump and leaders like him, however, adopted an approach that recognized no legal, moral or ethical boundaries. They put this approach into practice. People speak of a Third World War as though it has yet to begin, but it has already begun. Trump was one of those leading it. He waged war against Iran. There are other wars taking place around the world. He claims to have resolved numerous conflicts, but in reality, he played a role in provoking and escalating wars. Naturally, this has produced social, economic and humanitarian consequences. The American people have also paid a price for these policies. In this sense, the American public delivered a response, saying that such leadership could not continue and that one person could not govern in this manner.




I want my words to be understood correctly. We are people who hold a socialist ideology. Our standards and expectations are therefore much higher. Nevertheless, peoples send messages through elections. It is very important to understand the sociological dynamics behind these developments and interpret what elections reveal. This does not mean that powerful socialist movements have emerged or that the Democrats are necessarily better simply because they won. Such a comparison would not be accurate or objective. What matters is understanding what the people are saying. From this perspective, the American public has delivered a response. The message was that the escalation of wars, the refusal to recognize the will of peoples and the unilateral decisions affecting the Palestinian people and the peoples of the Middle East were not accepted. It is important to recognize this as a positive message.




'

Young people no longer accept the life imposed by capitalism'




Why is this important? Because perceptions are also being manufactured. We frequently hear claims that "the right is advancing" or "the far right is on the rise." This is also a form of psychological warfare. We must evaluate everything sociologically. We need to carefully analyze what social tendencies are telling us and what realities they express. We are leading figures within a socialist movement, and we must therefore approach these developments through sociological analysis.




The example of Brazil is important in this respect. The student movement in Serbia generated significant mobilization, struggle and rebellion. Youth movements have also become increasingly active in Paris and other French cities, as well as in Italy, Germany and various other countries. These developments tell us a great deal. They show that young people reject the imperialist-capitalist world, the capitalist system, the nation-state, industrialism and the male-dominated system. Young people have demonstrated that they no longer accept this way of life, that they refuse to be condemned to such a fate and that they are prepared to struggle against it. This is extremely important. Youth struggles also have the capacity to inspire and reinforce one another.




Serbia provides a particularly significant example. I have read some articles in which socialist and left-wing circles argue that the movement lacks a plan or program. There may be some truth to this, and I do not reject that possibility. However, this also reveals a weakness among leftist and socialist forces: our ability to understand the tendencies emerging among peoples, young people and women. The tendency toward democratic society is already expressing itself everywhere. Even in the most fascist country, society continues to preserve certain democratic values through its everyday life. These values may not be fully developed or expressed at an ideal level, but they exist. A youth movement emerged in Serbia. If I remember correctly, a wall collapsed in a Serbian city about two years ago, killing approximately 16 people. For two years, young people struggled against the government over this incident and demanded accountability. They did not limit their struggle to students. They reached out to every section of society, visiting villages, towns and cities. Young people entered society, organized within it and demanded accountability from those in power. The government fell. Through their struggle, young people brought down the government, and the list they supported won.




'Youth movements are showing the way forward'




This tells us something important. It gives us hope. But it does more than offer hope. It shows us a path forward. If young people genuinely become part of society and develop and strengthen their struggle from within it, they can unleash a force capable of bringing down even a government. That is how we must understand these developments.




Ideally, of course, it would have been better if the movement had a clear program and strategy. Nevertheless, the struggle has produced results. We must examine those results, better understand the struggle of young people and the revolutionary potential of the peoples, and listen carefully to what they are saying. We should strengthen our strategies, programs and plans on that basis rather than simply declaring that the right is rising. Leftist and socialist forces, ecological, feminist and cultural movements, and even democratic religious movements are engaged in struggles throughout the world.




We must recognize and understand these developments. Through collective action, we can bring about the rise of the left. We therefore need to look at the situation from another perspective. The issue is not simply that the right is becoming stronger.




Rather, the balance is shifting because leftist, socialist, feminist, ecological, anarchist and other movements have not yet developed sufficiently strong forms of organization. We must strengthen the weaker side of this balance. We need to organize more effectively, overcome fragmented approaches and build stronger democratic alliances. I therefore believe we should examine global developments with hope, understanding them more deeply through sociological, strategic and political analysis, and take action accordingly.




The 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) is being held in Antalya. Climate summits are organized repeatedly, and many issues concerning climate change and ecological balance are discussed. Those responsible for disrupting the climate gather to seek solutions. Some regard these summits as a kind of conspiracy or trap set by nation-states. Climate disruption also has serious consequences for violence against women and unemployment. How do you assess this?




First, I would like to say that COP31 and many other initiatives around the world address ecological problems. However, there is considerable hypocrisy and an effort to conceal reality. Perhaps the capitalist system's greatest skill is doing the worst things while marketing them as the best. This seems to be a particular characteristic of capitalism. It disguises its actions and conceals its responsibility for their consequences, presenting itself as though it bears no responsibility. International organizations and gatherings of this kind can also serve this purpose. I do not want to suggest that we oppose such initiatives altogether. But how realistic are they? To what extent do they genuinely discuss the systemic causes of ecological problems and develop a framework for struggling against them? That is the essential question.




Organizing such gatherings and discussing climate problems is positive. But how will these issues be discussed? The summit is being held in Antalya, Turkey. Some of the greatest ecological problems are caused by construction and pollution. These problems exist in Antalya, throughout Kurdistan and across Turkey. People are already engaged in ecological struggles everywhere. There are mining companies, hydroelectric power plants, dams and numerous other projects. Air pollution has reached alarming levels, and living beings are being destroyed. All these developments now pose serious threats not only to human life but to the lives of all living beings. If this continues, the planet itself will not have much time left. Why? Because the issue is not simply whether I throw rubbish somewhere. Of course, this is a moral and ethical matter. I should not litter. I should think and live ecologically in every aspect of my life. But the global climate crisis is not caused merely by an individual throwing rubbish on the ground. There is a much deeper systemic problem. We call this industrialism. These are the consequences of capitalist capital using technology in a manner completely detached from morality and conscience.




Will COP31 take a position against industrialism? Will it take a position against mining companies? Will restrictions be imposed on them? Will the views of local communities be taken into account? I consider this extremely important. This is a fundamental aspect of our strategy for democratic society, the democratic republic and democratic integration. A democratic society is one in which people organize locally and make decisions concerning their own lives. For example, a community should be able to say, "We do not permit this mining company to operate here." The people and women living in that area should be able to say, "We do not permit this because it leaves us without a living environment." Is there a system that allows them to make such decisions? Is there a legal framework recognizing this right? There is not.




Summits and conferences of this kind should therefore provide opportunities for local communities and local democracy to express themselves, present their views and make decisions that are respected. Instead, a certain number of people gather, meet and discuss these matters. But what benefit does this bring to the people living in the affected areas? For example, climate change has caused severe drought and famine in parts of Africa. Epidemics are also a serious problem. Women bear the heaviest burden of these consequences.




It also lowers the age of marriage.




Yes. In Africa, poverty drives families to sell young girls, including children, or forces them into early marriages. Rape and sexual harassment are connected to these circumstances. Women are responsible for household care and looking after children. Many women have to travel long distances to collect water, and dozens, even hundreds, are subjected to rape during these journeys. Poverty is also increasing dramatically. There are deaths caused by diseases and complications related to childbirth and women's reproductive health. These conditions have severe consequences for women, children and society as a whole. If we consider the situation globally, we are exposed to numerous chemicals simply by breathing.




These substances cause cancer and other serious illnesses, threatening physical and mental health. We are facing a very serious assault. It is an assault produced by industrialism. We frequently speak of the Third World War. When people hear the wes fighting one another, with thousands of soldiers on battlefields. But another important dimension of the Third World War is industrial warfare. It has not been named as such. You cannot see it, and there are no soldiers standing before you. Yet air pollution, climate disruption and broader ecological problems cause millions of deaths. Some are documented, while others remain unrecorded. If this is not war, what is it?




Climate and ecological discussions must therefore also be approached as a struggle against a form of warfare. They must be taken extremely seriously. Societies themselves must be at the center of these discussions. Rather than speaking only of Indigenous peoples, I would emphasize that people living in their own communities must discuss these problems and develop their own solutions. The people living there, including women and children, must have the power to make decisions. They must be able to take a position, organize protests and develop practical measures to protect their lives. Establishing this decision-making power is extremely important. If this summit genuinely discusses the fundamental problems, develops solutions and establishes plans to implement them, then it can have meaning. Otherwise, it will amount to little more than an exercise in disguising reality, concealing responsibility and delaying action.

title: YJK-E and KON-MED: Justice for Vesile Akın
content:
The Union of Kurdish Women in Germany (YJK-E) and the Confederation of Democratic Kurdish Communities in Germany (KON-MED) said in a written statement: “We learned with profound anger and sorrow that Vesile Akın, a 35-year-old mother of five, was stabbed to death on 9 November in the German city of Düren by her estranged husband.”




The statement continued: “Only recently, we raised our voices against the murder of Enda in Coesfeld. Today, once again, we are witnessing a woman being deprived of her right to life. The names and cities change, but male violence and the suffering endured by women remain the same.”




The statement, which emphasised that “violence against women is not only a women’s issue but a problem affecting society as a whole”, continued: “The murder of a woman is also an attack on the future of society and on our shared life together. According to information reported in the media, Vesile Akın had previously contacted the police, citing threats against her, and had requested protection. It has been reported that the threats continued despite restraining measures being imposed. Yet Vesile could not be protected. Today, five children have been left without their mother.




When a woman reports that she is being threatened, asks for help and turns to the state for protection, what more needs to happen to prevent her from being murdered?




Femicide is political! Laws introduced by the state to protect women must not be rendered ineffective by other legal regulations or shortcomings in their implementation. Protection orders must not remain mere words on paper; women's right to life must be guaranteed. Vesile Akın’s reports to the authorities and the protective measures taken must be investigated independently and transparently, and those responsible for any possible negligence must be held accountable.”




The statement underlined that “the male-dominated mentality that threatens women's right to life manifests itself not only through individual acts of violence but also through oppression within families and society. Women who wish to separate or divorce are sometimes pressured to abandon their decisions, even by members of their own families. Women cannot be expected to endure violence and oppression in the name of family unity. No woman should have to pay with her life for a decision she makes about her own future.




Preventing the murder of women cannot be left solely to the struggle of women themselves. Men must also take responsibility for challenging patriarchal attitudes, violence and society's silence. Because genuine social freedom cannot exist in a society where women are unable to live freely and safely. Through our campaign, launched on 1 November and continuing until 8 March, International Working Women's Day, entitled ‘We Are Strengthening Our Collective Struggle Against Femicide and the Male-Dominated Mentality!’, we are drawing attention precisely to this collective social responsibility. As part of this struggle, we aim to promote a democratic understanding of the family, strengthen equality between women and men, challenge patriarchal attitudes and raise social awareness against violence towards women. The murder of Vesile Akın has once again demonstrated just how vital the struggle we have launched truly is. We stand for life against femicide and for women's freedom against the male-dominated mentality. We are strengthening our collective struggle!”
