author: Kodao Productions
title: Witness tries to disprove Sara’s Gencorp stake
content:
Criminal charges may be awaiting Gencorp Industries Inc. counsel Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay as she insisted that Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio does not own a single share of stock in the company but admitted that Sara received P2,142,369.14  as “return of capital” from the company from 2022 to 2025, broken down as follows: P337,500 in 2022; P555,750 in 2023; P612,419.14 in 2024, and; P636,700 in 2025. Under the law, Sara cannot engage in business or earn additional compensation from the government while occupying the vice presidency.




Twisting herself in knots, Punay said the payments were for the return of capital to Sara, who invested in one company which failed to secure a Jollibee franchise. Her investment later jumped to Gencorp, whose owner is closely linked with the Dutertes. Punay claimed that through all those years, Sara was not a stockholder, officer or director of Gencorp, a company controlled by a businessman who was named by detained ex-president Rodrigo Duterte as his envoy to China to attract investments.




Punay’s statement contradicts Sara’s admission in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs) that she was a stockholder and director of the company. She executed her SALNs under oath. Yet, Punay insisted that Sara’s name did not appear in the company’s General Information Sheets (GIS) from 2022 to 2025. She also said Gencorp did not declare dividends during the same period, raising another question why Gencorp paid Sara P2.1-million during the same period for “return of capital.” However, Sara’s SALNs showed her annual “return of capital” might even be higher than the dividends for Gencorp stockholders who belong to one Chinese-Filipino family. The ties that bind them and Sara are worth investigating.




Punay’s pained defense of Sara as not being a beneficial owner of the company will not stand on the basis of her SALN disclosure. Her absence during stockholders’ meetings, board meetings, management or decision-making is of no consequence to the impeachment trial. Her unilateral declaration that she was a Gencorp stockholder in her SALN “doesn’t make her one?” Or is this the same as saying standing in a garage doesn’t make a woman a car?




Kapunan asked why Punay did not bring Duterte’s declaration of GenCorp ownership in her SALNs to the company’s attention. She said it was not her duty to examine other people’s SALNs and adjust GenCorp’s corporate records based on their declarations. “I believe that my function as counsel of GenCorp, Your Honor, does not involve looking at other people’s SALNs and adjusting our records just because somebody declared that he is a stockholder of our corporation,” she said. Kapunan then asked why Sara had declared herself a GenCorp stockholder if she had no shares in the company. Again, Punay said she is not Sara’s keeper.




From 2022 to 2025, Punay disclosed, Gencorp did not declare dividends but gladly paid huge amounts to Sara. Moreover, Sara did not participate in the management of the corporation, she added, which is irrelevant to the issue of her failure to divest herself of any business interest when she became vice president in 2022. Supposed to be an eagle-eyed counsel, Punay could not say with certainty how a corporation with a paid-up capital of only P1.25-million managed to wangle five Jollibee franchises since each franchise is estimated to cost a minimum of P35-million. She claimed she could not find any record of Sara’s investments in Gencorp. The impeachment court might as well summon such records to check on the veracity of her assertion. GenCorp operates five Jollibee branches in Davao City: Bolton, Matina Crossing, G-Mall, Times Square, and Abreeza.




Asked if Duterte had shareholdings or other interests in previous Jollibee franchisees or in the specific branches, Punay answered “no.” She wasn’t aware that another Jollibee branch in Quezon City was also operated by Gencorp. Prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan pounced on Duterte’s investment, noting that Sara’s president’s original capital contribution to Davao Bounty was only P46,875 but Gencorp.’s return on her “loose investment” ran into millions in just four years. An evaluation of the original Gencorp records might reveal the falsity of Punay’s claims or challenge the reliability of the defense’s argument that the investment was above board and did not violate the constitutional ban on vice presidents engaging in business while in office.




Punay also admitted she could not verify the amount of Duterte’s original investment in the Jollibee Times Square branch. Worse, she admitted that she doesn’t know why her own company was issuing the payments even though the investment was supposedly made through Davao Bounty, a separate company. As counsel, she could have raised questions about the remittances to Sara, but she did not. Earlier, she was asked by the defense if she were aware of any influence that Sara had in making GenCorp win 19 contracts with the Davao City government under Mayor Sebastian Duterte. She said Sara did not influence anyone at City Hall, which she headed previously. The defense, in a bid to add more brownie points for Sara, asked if the vice president got anything from the 19 contracts. The usual answer: “Nothing.”




Analyzing the tack of the defense, it appears that they believe blanket denial will save the day for them. Two of the previous defense witness availed themselves of the “I don’t know” excuse but they got bombed right at the dock. This case is not only about hidden wealth and crassness of Sara. It is also about the culture of impunity that has crept into the innards of the Duterte political dynasty; it is also about the banality of evil and Sara’s solipsism and belief that her demonstrated inability to express herself is what voters like. She has little respect for voters who may have realized that one sting is enough. It happened in 2016. It won’t happen again in 2028. #

title: Detained journalist Cumpio receives international award
content:
The International Women’s Media Foundation (IWMF) bestowed on journalist Frenchie Mae Cumpio the 2026 Wallis Annenberg Justice for Women Journalists Award in a ceremony in New York City on Tuesday.




IWMF said it honors Cumpio for reporting on social inequality in the Eastern Visayas region, including land rights abuses, the killings of farmers, disaster response, and the impacts of militarized conflict under government policies.




The prize was named after the prominent American philanthropist and heiress who championed various environmental and social advocacies such as the Liberty Canyon Wildlife Crossings LGBTQ+ and HIV/AIDS charities.




IWMF cited that as a student journalist at the University of the Philippines-Tacloban, Cumpio rose quickly within alternative media networks, becoming a leading voice in regional and grassroots reporting.




Charged with crimes widely regarded as fabricated, IWMF said Cumpio’s work – and her continued imprisonment – highlights the use of legal mechanisms, including anti-terror laws and red-tagging, to silence independent media in the Philippines.




The announcement of the 2026 Wallis Annenberg Justice for Women Journalists Award in New York City. (Photo by Vince Reasonda/Altermidya)




In a message upon learning of her victory last May, Cumpio said she is “deeply honored” to receive the award given to reporters unjustly detained, jailed, or imprisoned.




Cumpio added she gives “greater salute to everyone who continues to believe in truth and justice.”




Persecuted journalist




Cumpio had been in jail since her arrest in February 2020 in Tacloban City, along with four other fellow rights defenders.




Cumpio and church worker Marielle Domequil were acquitted from four charges of illegal possession of firearms and explosives but were convicted on the added charges of terrorism financing in 2025. Their conviction is being appealed with the Court of Appeals in the Visayas.




Both are currently detained at the Correctional Institute for Women in Mandaluyong City.







Cumpio was executive director of independent news outlet Eastern Vista and a radio broadcaster with Aksyon Radyo Tacloban at the time of their arrest.




In 2026, Cumpio was nominated for the UNESCO Guillermo Cano World Press Freedom Prize and was shortlisted for the Reporters Without Borders Courage Prize in 2025.




“Growing up in one of the poorest regions in my country, taking part in unveiling the truth and exposing abuse has rather been a necessity than a choice. Journalism in a country ruled by only one percent of its population means providing the masses and marginalized sectors with a voice. This [award] is recognition of the truth and the strength of the united people,” Cumpio said.




Cumpio’s fellow alternative journalist Vince Reasonda was present in Tuesday’s awarding ceremony. # 

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Groups defy gov’t plea to postpone mass actions
content:
Progressive groups led by Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) protest outside the House of Representatives while lawmakers’ briefing on Pax Silica is ongoing on Wednesday, November 11. (Charles Edmon Perez/Pinoy Weekly)

Where is the respect for farmers and Aytas who will be evicted from their communities because of Pax Silica?

This is the response of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) in Malacañang’s recent public statement to “show courtesy” as the Philippines hosts the 49th ASEAN Summit from November 15 to 18.

“We will hold protests before, during, and after the ASEAN Summit and Trump’s visit,” the group said in a statement. US President Donald Trump is expected to arrive in the Philippines next week.

In a press briefing on November 10, Malacañang’s Press Officer Claire Castro appealed to the protesters not to schedule rallies during the arrival of the international delegations and “show the genuine hospitality and good character of the Filipino people.”

“Respect for visitors? How about respect for vendors and urban poor displaced by ‘clearing operations’? Where is the respect for farmers and Aytas who will be evicted from their communities because of Pax Silica?” Bayan asked.

Bayan, together with multi-sectoral groups, launched the 12 days of protest which kicked off on November 4. The group stressed that the Philippine government should not welcome “war criminals and foreign plunderers” like Trump at the expense of the Filipino people’s welfare and their right to protest.

The Philippine National Police increased the number of personnel to more than 23,000, coming from the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO), Armed Forces of the Philippines, Bureau of Fire Protection, and other concerned agencies.

Human rights group Karapatan described the ASEAN preparations as “over-the-top” and are reminiscent of the huge police deployment during the State of the Nation Address (SONA) last July.

“And we all know how that played out. Fifty-one protesters were arrested even before the protest program began, with many of those arrested taken merely because they wore black,” said Cristina Palabay, secretary-general of Karapatan. “This is our country, and we have every right to protest, especially when the policies and actions of these very visitors threaten our people’s rights and interests. US President Donald Trump is not merely a guest whose presence demands deference. The US is actively intervening in our country’s affairs, advancing its economic and military interests at the expense of Filipino sovereignty and people’s rights.”

The United States leads the Pax Silica Initiative, which plans to establish a 4,000-acre industrial hub within the Philippines’ Luzon Economic Corridor. Described as the first “AI-native industrial acceleration hub,” the proposed site is being positioned as an economic security zone intended to strengthen shared supply chains for critical minerals, semiconductors, electronics, and other goods.

Read: ‘Pax Silica’ initiative seen as war production, environment destruction

Progressive groups also assailed the worsening economic situation amid grand preparations for the 49th ASEAN Summit.

Independent think tank group IBON Foundation said that the current low wages failed to keep up with the country’s inflation — climbing up to 7.8 percent in October from 7.2 percent in September. The group stressed that rising prices of these commodities, along with rice, are affecting poor and low income families.

The unemployment in the country also increased by almost 909,000, according to the data of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), though the IBON Foundation argued that the number could be higher.

The number of unemployed Filipinos has raised the Philippine unemployment rate to 5.4 percent, making it the highest among its Southeast Asian neighbors based on the latest data in Indonesia (4.8%), Malaysia (2.9%), Vietnam (2.2%), Singapore (2%), and Thailand (0.9%).

The Philippines is also performing the poorest in terms of economic performance, compared to its counterparts in Southeast Asia. It has among the lowest GDP growth in the region at 2.1 percent compared to Brunei (0.02%), Thailand (1.9%), Malaysia (5.3%), Singapore (5.4%), Indonesia (5.5%) and Vietnam (10%).

“The government’s business-as-usual approach is worsening joblessness, eroding incomes and making the cost of living soar for millions of Filipinos,” said IBON Foundation, warning the administration of Ferdinand Marcos Jr. that the country is rapidly heading towards stagflation. They called on the government to increase spending on agricultural production, support small enterprises, and boost household purchasing power.

Urban poor group Kalipunan ng Damayang Mahihirap (Kadamay) said in a statement that the rising prices of fuel and basic commodities and the temporary displacement of the informal workers affected by the ASEAN Summit are pushing the Filipino families at greater risk.

“Where will the driver get money to buy food for their family? What budget will vendors make if they have no income? What about their children’s school allowance? No matter how much Marcos Jr. tries to cover it up, he cannot hide the glaring poverty in the country,” said Kadamay secretary-general Mimi Doringo.

The transport group Piston will hold a nationwide strike. Farmers and indigenous groups will also organize camp-outs bringing their issues from the countryside to the city for the ASEAN delegates and Trump to hear.

Karapatan said that they stand in solidarity with the Filipino people “as they courageously assert their legitimate demands in the face of heightened repression.”

“The people will not be silenced or intimidated into surrendering their rights and sovereignty for the sake of the Marcos regime’s hosting of the ASEAN Summit,” Palabay concluded. (RTS, AMU, DAA)

title: Gabriela sweeps away Trump’s Pax Silica
content:
Those who violate the rights and well-being of women and children are not welcome in the Philippines.

MANILA – “Stop the rape of our motherland! Kick Trump out!”

This is the call of progressive women’s group Gabriela during a protest near the US Embassy, November 9. The women’s group asserted that there should be no red carpet welcome to warmongerers like Trump.

Jacq Ruiz, spokesperson of Kilusan ng Manggagawang Kababaihan (KMK) said, “There is no special treatment for us women workers, who remain mired in extreme poverty, while billions of pesos are being allocated solely for preparations for the signing of the Pax Silica agreement.”

Read: Economic insecurity of women workers worsen

While Filipino culture is known for warmly welcoming visitors with a feast, they said Trump is an exception as many Filipino households are struggling to put even a decent meal on their own tables.

For a mother like Lanie Buena, 54, it is a struggle to get through the day. She is working as a manicurist and pedicurist in their house in Quezon City for eight years while her husband is working as a barber.

She earns P400 or about $6 for three clients in a day. But this is not enough, she said, as there are no guaranteed clients every day.

What she earns, she said, is not adequate for a family of seven with two students still going to school. There are still household expenses such as electricity and water bills.

Meanwhile, Gabriela Women’s Partylist Rep. Sarah Elago said, “Those who violate the rights and well-being of women and children are not welcome in the Philippines.”

Elago condemned Trump, calling him a macho-fascist and a war criminal, citing his role in waging and escalating wars that have claimed countless civilian lives, including children in Palestine. She added that Trump’s links to the Epstein files makes him less welcome in the country.

The Trump administration’s war against Iran and its support to Israel has contributed to a global oil price shock, with its effects now being felt by Filipino families from rising fuel costs to increasing cost of goods in the market.

The women’s group said they are determined to ensure that Trump will not receive a warm welcome but instead will be faced by massive protests rejecting his visit and the proposed Pax Silica Initiatives.

“What we will present is a flaming protest, because individuals like Donald—a rapist, molester, and war criminal—are utterly shameless and devoid of any moral compass,” said Elle Buntag, spokesperson of Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns. (AMU, RVO)

title: Peasant organizer persists despite surveillance
content:
Jesus Monasterial. (Photo from Photo from Tanggol Magsasaka-TK)

Repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety.

When he was a university student, he questioned the purpose of agricultural education. Now he is organizing landless farmers and fisherfolk.

Jesus Monasterial has spent more than two years working with rural communities in Southern Tagalog. However, his work resulted in repeated surveillance by state forces, peasant groups said.

On October 31, Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan reported that a police intelligence operative identified as “Bruno” had been asking about Monasterial’s whereabouts in Lian, Batangas. The operative was reportedly previously assigned in Nasugbu.

At the time, Monasterial was assisting a protest camp in Barangay San Diego, where farmers, fisherfolk, and residents opposed the possible demolition of several houses.

“I was on my way back to the people’s protest camp in San Diego when news reached us that someone had been asking about my personal information,” he said.

The camp was established by Samahang Mangangawil 1979 and the San Diego Homeowners’ Association, with support from the Katipunan ng mga Samahang Magbubukid sa Timog Katagalugan (KASAMA-TK) and Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas–Timog Katagalugan (PAMALAKAYA-TK).

The incident prompted fellow organizers to discuss security measures. They also plan to file a complaint before the Commission on Human Rights (CHR).

Monasterial’s involvement in peasant organizing began at the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) where he was enrolled in BS Agricultural Biotechnology.

Coming from a family of farmers in Bicol, where his grandparents worked as agricultural tenants, he became increasingly critical of an agricultural education system that he said served the interests of transnational corporations rather than addressing farmers’ lack of land and government support.

Through the League of Filipino Students–UPLB, he became involved in social issues action and joined community immersions with farmers in Tartaria, Silang, Cavite, as well as Mangyan communities in Mindoro and Dumagat communities in Rizal.

These experiences led him to leave his studies and become a full-time organizer. He now serves as deputy secretary-general of KASAMA-TK.

His work involves staying in communities, conducting consultations and political education, and helping establish local farmers and fisherfolk associations.

“Being a full-time organizer means devoting my entire time to the communities and being far from my loved ones,” he said, adding that he had to set aside his plan to finish college.

The October 31 incident was not the first reported surveillance involving Monasterial.

On July 19, 2026, soldiers from the 16th Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army reportedly sought to identify the organizers of KASAMA-TK’s Regional Peasant Consultation in Barangay Malinis, Lemery, Batangas.

On September 21, a man introducing himself as “Del” Dela Cruz reportedly approached a member of Sugarfolks’ Unity for Genuine Agricultural Reform (SUGAR-Batangas), attempting to persuade the member to leave the organization and provide information about its activities.

According to Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan, the man showed footage of a protest outside the Department of Agriculture regional office led by the Alyansa ng Magsasaka para sa Kumpensasyon (AMK), SUGAR-Batangas, KAISAHAN, and KASAMA-TK. He allegedly warned the member against working with Monasterial, claiming that the organizer was “already drawing attention.”

The protest resulted in a dialogue with government representatives to demand agricultural inputs and implements for farmers and farmworkers affected by successive calamities.

The groups also cited previous incidents in Barangay Casile, Laguna; Lupang Ramos and Tartaria, Cavite; and Coron, Palawan.

Monasterial said that the repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety. “Repeated surveillance limits my movements as an organizer and makes me fear returning home to my family because they might also be targeted by the state due to my advocacy.”

Despite the threats, Monasterial said that his work remains rooted in the struggles of farmers and farmworkers.

In Batangas, he witnessed sugarcane cutters and loaders receiving only P350 to P400 for every ton of cane harvested and loaded onto trucks. Their wages are paid at the end of harvesting seasons that can last six months, forcing many to rely on loans and advances.

Through community discussions, he helps workers understand their rights to organize unions and demand decent wages, humane working conditions, and genuine land reform.

“I continue organizing despite the threats and dangers because I know that what I am doing is not wrong and is necessary,” he said.

Addressing allegations that he was recruiting farmers, Monasterial acknowledged encouraging them to establish their own organizations. “I am indeed encouraging them to establish their own farmers and fisherfolk associations.”

“People naturally resist a society where farmers have no land, yet land is reserved for foreigners, and those who produce the country’s food have nothing to eat,” he said.

Citing figures from their organization, Monasterial said that 56 of the 72 political prisoners in Southern Tagalog come from farming and indigenous communities or are their advocates.

Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan called on allied organizations to condemn the surveillance and urged the CHR and the local government of Lian to investigate the incident and protect the rights of Monasterial and the affected residents.

Monasterial also called for accountability for human rights violations, the repeal of the Anti-Terrorism Act, and the abolition of the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC).

For Monasterial, organizing is essential for farmers and fisherfolk confronting landlessness, displacement, and the loss of their livelihoods. Despite the surveillance, he stressed that their right to organize and defend their communities must be protected. (RTS, DAA)

title: Imeldific, Potemkin welcome for sore loser Trump
content:
The Philippine government should not put its best foot forward in welcoming the worst loser Donald Trump, who was rejected by the American electorate for joining Israel’s war against Iran and causing US gasoline and gas prices to skyrocket as well as punishing the Philippines with higher inflation. In fact, Trump should be kept out of the country to save the country from the plague that he brings along with soiled adult diapers that he would dump in Metro Manila.




American voters rejected Trump and his minions by voting for Democrats, who would control the House of Representatives and the Senate on January 2027. The Republicans were massacred for being dumb and following Trump, whose IQ, as the records of the New York Military Academy (NYMA) showed, was a moronic 73. The political upheaval was a revenge by a people that have been conned twice by the grifting Trump, whose idea of governance was borrowed from the Nazi enforcer Carl Schmitt, who promoted authoritarianism and justified the slaughter of Nazi opponents during the Kristallnacht massacre, or the Night of the Long Knives when as many as 1,000 Germans were killed by Nazi zealots. Schmitt worked in tandem with philosopher Martin Heidegger, the lover of Hannah Arendt. The only books that Trump reads are “Mein Kampf” and the blueprint of national socialism. No wonder Trump continues to fantasize that he can rule and rob by decree.




The Filipino people have no business pampering this lame-duck US president. More so, the Marcos Jr. regime should not go out of its way to create Potemkin villages along the route of Trump’s motorcade on Nov. 16, 2026. Yet, they are clearing the path and decorating the roads to appeal to the tacky taste of Trump, who is attending the 49

th

 2026 ASEAN Summit here from Nov. 16 to 18 and purportedly signing the mysterious Pax Silica accord between the Philippines and the US, which covers 1,620 hectares in Clark Freeport, including land inhabited by Aeta communities for a long time.




Pax Silica is as opaque as any deal cut by the US and it purportedly covers the manufacture of chips for military and civilian uses, assembly of microprocessors, establishment of data centers and possibly refining of rare earth elements (REEs) needed for batteries (the separation of REEs from each other requires more than a dozen operations) that is practically the monopoly of Chinese corporations since the US sold the technology more than three decades ago. The US is controlling Pax Silica and even demanded that its citizens who would eventually work at Clark be granted diplomatic status. This condition alone betrays the stupidity of the scheme and harks back to US exceptionalism.




The US has not acceded to UNCLOS, refused to ratify the Rome Statute creating the International Criminal Court (ICC) and wants out of various UN agencies. This alone exposes the character of the US as a rogue nation that is as lawless as Israel and as violent as Russia under the autocratic rule of Vladimir Putin. For Pax Silica, which was crafted only in December 2025, the US wants to make it appear that the scheme is an international one, with benefits accruing to those who sign up. Yet, an American firm has already disclosed the discovery of a lithium deposit in Arkansas and Texas while Indian startups have announced that they are developing technology that makes REEs for magnets and chip unnecessary.




There is also another sideshow, the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) that is supposed to overdevelop Regions 3 and 4 and bring in trillions of US dollars in investments. We have heard similar plans for a very long time, and the number of such plans is roughly equal to the number of economic planning secretaries the republic had. Not one of those various plans that promised tax holidays, rebates, reduced import tariffs and industrial peace through strike bans ever came to fruition. Pax Silica and LEC may also find their way to the steel cabinets and the museum of failures. The US operates on its self-interest, with one pundit reminding the rest of the world that the US is not a missionary. As the arch-enemy of world peace, Henry Kissinger, quipped: To be an enemy of the US is dangerous. To be a friend of the US is fatal. The French learned it, the Vietnamese came to know it, and the Afghans who welcomed the Americans realized their folly later on.




The Makabayan bloc at the Lower House has already filed House Resolution No. 1593 opposing Trump’s visit and blasted the reported plan for him to sign the Pax Silica Initiative, which is the latest among the many lopsided agreements between the US and the Philippines. House Assistant Minority Leader and Kabataan Partylist Rep. Atty. Renee Co said: “A convicted warmongering racist, rapist, pedophile loser should not at all be welcome to step foot on our lands.” She noted that “the American people have themselves rejected Trump. Why should we be forced to accept him here? This administration has no reason to welcome the primary imperialist oppressor of our nation.” Makabayan condemned Philippine government’s “all-out on spending and preparations” for Trump’s visit.




For its part, the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) condemned the Marcos Jr. government’s “Imeldific” cleanup drive to hide poverty from foreigners during the ASEAN summit. This requires sweeping out street vendors and urban poor residents from areas where ASEAN Summit dignitaries will pass through. It is nothing but a repeat of the Potemkin villages that Imelda Marcos and her minions created to whitewash the Filipino people’s deepening poverty. “No amount of fresh paint, swept sidewalks, or hidden human beings can erase the hunger, joblessness, and misery that this government has failed to address,” Bayan said. “We condemn the Marcos Jr. administration’s shameless attempt to prettify Manila for the cameras of foreign leaders while the poor are treated as eyesores to be swept away. The poverty of the people cannot be hidden by a cleanup drive,” it concluded. #




 




The post 

Imeldific, Potemkin welcome for sore loser Trump

 appeared first on 

Kodao Productions

.

author: Unknown
title: ziq - Unterstützen Anarchist*innen die Demokratie?
content:
Katalog Liste aller Texte AutorInnen Themen Letzte Einträge Zur Bibliothek hinzufügen

Mehr Kontakt Material Sticker, Plakate, etc.

Anarchie braucht keine Demokratie

Das Wort "Demokratie" kommt von zwei griechischen Wörtern: Demo- was "Volk" bedeutet.

-kratie: was "Herrschaft", "Regierung", "Leitungsorgan" bedeutet.

Wörtlich bedeutet Demokratie also: "Herrschaft durch das Volk". Oder genauer gesagt, von der Mehrheit des Volkes.

Meiner Meinung nach ist jede Person, die darauf abzielt, dass wir vom "Volk" regiert werden (so abstrakt und bedeutungslos dieses Konzept auch sein mag), nicht für Anarchie. Aber leider wird diese Ansicht nicht immer von den Menschen geteilt, die sich heute Anarchist*innen nennen. Es fällt mir schwer, mir vorzustellen, dass Anarchist*innen, die vermutlich gegen jede Form von Autorität sind und hoffentlich die Vorstellung von Herrschenden ablehnen, damit einverstanden sind, von "dem Volk" regiert zu werden... Ich weiß, dass ich auf keinen Fall von irgendjemandem regiert werden will. Aber viele Anarchist*innen romantisieren weiterhin die Demokratie, vielleicht weil sie nicht in der Lage sind, die jahrelange Propaganda zu durchbrechen, mit der sie vom Staat und seinen Schul- und Medienapparaten gefüttert werden.

Von klein auf wird uns eingehämmert, dass Demokratie gleich Freiheit ist. Jede*r Anarchist*in wird dir sagen, dass die meisten von uns zwar in Gesellschaften leben, die von demokratischen Formen regiert werden, aber niemand von uns so etwas wie Freiheit hat. Trotzdem machen viele uns Ausflüchte, sodass wir die Demokratie weiterhin romantisieren können... Wenn du in einem Raum voller Anarchist*innen sagst, dass du gegen die Demokratie bist, wirst du zweifelsohne die leidenschaftliche Behauptung hören, dass das, was wir jetzt haben, keine "echte" Demokratie ist, aber "wenn wir Anarchismus hätten, hätten wir eine "echte" Demokratie und die Dinge wären anders, weil Anarchismus die einzige echte Demokratie ist!"

Viele Anarchist*innen geben sich viel Mühe, an unterdrückerischen Phantomen wie der Demokratie festzuhalten, und bemühen sich sehr, diese liberalen Konzepte mit der Anarchie zu verschmelzen, obwohl es dafür eigentlich keinen Grund gibt. Anarchist*innen, die darauf bestehen, dass Anarchie und Demokratie ein und dasselbe sind, obwohl die Demokratie für eine endlose Liste von schrecklichen Gräueltaten verantwortlich ist, erweisen der Anarchie keinen Dienst.

Unsere Machthabenden nutzen die Demokratie, um uns in In- und Outgroups zu unterteilen, die Mehrheitsgruppe gegen die Minderheitsgruppen auszuspielen und allen ein falsches Gefühl der Kontrolle zu geben. Uns wird vorgegaukelt, dass wir mitbestimmen können, wie unser Leben verläuft, weil wir an der glorreichen Demokratie teilnehmen dürfen. Natürlich werden wir alle, die nicht zur herrschenden Klasse gehören, weiterhin ausgebeutet und leben in ständiger Knechtschaft. Die einzigen, die wirklich von der Demokratie profitieren, sind die Herrschenden, die sie benutzen, um uns zu entfremden und abzulenken, damit wir uns nicht erheben und sie alle für das lähmende Elend, das sie verursachen, töten. Anarchie lehnt Autorität und die Herrschaft von Mehrheitsgruppen über Minderheitsgruppen ab. In der Anarchie geht es darum, die Autonomie jeder einzelnen Person zu wahren und die Autorität, die uns von Unterdrückenden aufgezwungen wird, abzubauen. Die Demokratie gibt bevorzugten Gruppen das Recht, Minderheitsgruppen zu unterdrücken. Die Demokratie ignoriert die Autonomie des Individuums zugunsten des kollektiven Willens der herrschenden Gruppe. Die Demokratie ermöglicht es den Machthabenden, brutale Machthierarchien aufrechtzuerhalten. Sie ist der Inbegriff von Autorität und dient dazu, den tyrannischen kapitalistisch-staatlichen Status quo überall auf der Welt aufrechtzuerhalten.

Demokratie ist die Tyrannei der Mehrheit, egal wie man sie zu verschleiern versucht. In der Praxis wurden alle Formen der Demokratie von einer Mehrheitsgruppe dazu benutzt, eine Minderheitsgruppe zu kontrollieren oder ihr etwas vorzuschreiben. Alle Formen der Demokratie wurden dazu benutzt, die Autonomie zu unterdrücken, die Selbstbestimmung zu unterdrücken und die Herrschenden von der Verantwortung für ihr Handeln zu entbinden. Wie können Herrschende für ihre Gräueltaten verantwortlich sein, wenn "das Volk" sie gewählt und ermächtigt hat, diese Gräueltaten zu begehen?

Auch wenn Demokratie-Fetischist*innen das nie erwähnen werden, wurde Hitler im Einklang mit dem deutschen politischen System demokratisch gewählt. Seine Handlungen nach der Wahl wurden größtenteils von der Mehrheitsgruppe in Deutschland unterstützt. Alle Gräueltaten, die er beging, geschahen im Namen dieser Mehrheitsgruppe, um die Position der "arischen" Christ*innen in der Gesellschaft auf Kosten aller anderen zu stärken. Das deutsche Volk hat Hitler ermächtigt, seine Privilegien um jeden Preis zu erhalten. Es gibt keinen Grund, warum eine sogenannte "echte" Demokratie anders sein sollte als die Demokratie, die Nazideutschland hervorgebracht hat. Eine partizipatorische Demokratie würde es nur mehr Mitgliedern der herrschenden Gruppe ermöglichen, direkter an der Durchsetzung brutaler Politik mitzuwirken.

Eine "echte" Demokratie hält die Menschen nicht davon ab, andere zu unterdrücken, um ihre eigene Gruppe zu begünstigen. Wenn die Mehrheit der Deutschen im Zweiten Weltkrieg zugesehen und gejubelt hat, als Menschen in Konzentrationslager verschleppt wurden, warum sollte jemand glauben, dass eine "echte" Demokratie daran etwas ändern würde? Im Laufe der Geschichte hat die Mehrheitsgruppe immer dann, wenn ein geschickter Propagandist mit dem Finger auf eine Minderheitengruppe zeigt, diese in Stücke gerissen. Das ist gelebte Demokratie. Weiße Vorherrschaft und sogar Genozid wurden schon unzählige Male mit der Macht der Demokratie gestützt.

Unterstützen Anarchist*innen also die Demokratie? Nicht, wenn diese Anarchist*innen ein umfassendes Verständnis davon haben, was Anarchie bedeutet. Nicht, wenn es ihnen ernst damit ist, sich von Autoritäten zu befreien und Hierarchien zu zerschlagen, sobald sie entstehen.

Die Demokratie ist mit der Anarchie in keiner Weise vereinbar. Sie könnte ein nützliches Verfahren sein, um die Ansichten der einzelnen Mitglieder einer kleinen Gruppe abzuschätzen, aber das sollte nicht ausreichen, um zu behaupten, dass "Anarchie demokratisch ist". Anarchie ist der Widerstand gegen Autorität. Es ist der Kampf gegen Unterdrückung. Das Bestreben, das Leiden zu begrenzen. Wir sollten nicht behaupten, dass Anarchie durch die Demokratie definiert wird, die ein bestimmtes Regierungssystem ist, das verlangt, dass Menschen von anderen Menschen regiert werden. Wenn du 10 zufällige Anarchist*innen fragst, ob sie die Demokratie unterstützen, wirst du sicher eine gemischte Antwort erhalten. Jede Person, die du fragst, befindet sich an einem anderen Punkt ihres politischen Weges, und einige Anarchist*innen werden viel mehr Zeit damit verbringen, über Arbeitsrechte, Wohnungsbau, Migrant*innenhilfe und andere dringende Anliegen nachzudenken, während sie sich nur wenige philosophische Gedanken über das Wesen der Hierarchie und all die Wege machen, auf denen sie sich manifestiert und in unser Leben eindringt.

Kollektivistisch gesinnte Anarchist*innen bestehen in der Regel auf direkter Demokratie und Konsensdemokratie als Entscheidungsmechanismen, aber das führt häufig zu Problemen, wenn bestimmte Mitglieder der Gruppe nicht mit der Agenda der Mehrheit übereinstimmen. Je größer die Gruppe ist, desto wahrscheinlicher ist dies der Fall. Die Mitglieder der Minderheit werden unweigerlich frustriert über diese Unterdrückung und verlassen entweder die Gruppe oder werden gezwungen, sich anzupassen, um zu bleiben. In der Praxis könnte das zum Beispiel bedeuten, dass alle Schwarzen in einer Gemeinschaft entfremdet und an den Rand gedrängt werden oder sogar gezwungen sind, ihr Zuhause ganz zu verlassen, weil die weiße Mehrheit dafür gestimmt hat, ihre Anliegen zu ignorieren, um das weiße Privileg zu wahren. Demokratie und Marginalisierung sind in der Regel ein Gruppendeal. "Alle Macht dem Volke" bedeutet in Wirklichkeit "Macht für die mächtigste Gruppe von Menschen", und je mehr Macht die mächtige Gruppe hat, desto weniger Macht haben die marginalisierten Gruppen.

Die westliche Demokratie hat ihren Ursprung im antiken Griechenland. Dieses politische System gewährte freien Männern das demokratische Bürgerrecht, während Sklav*innen, Fremde und Frauen von der politischen Teilhabe ausgeschlossen waren. In praktisch allen demokratischen Regierungen der antiken und modernen Geschichte bedeutete Demokratie genau das. Eine elitäre Klasse freier Männer traf alle Entscheidungen für alle. Bevor Athen die Demokratie einführte, beherrschten Aristokraten die Gesellschaft. Die "Herrschaft des Volkes" oder die Idee einer Regierung, die (theoretisch) von allen (freien) männlichen Bürgern kontrolliert wird, anstatt von einigen wenigen wohlhabenden Familien, schien also eine gute Sache zu sein. Aber in Wirklichkeit war es nur eine neue Version der aristokratischen Herrschaft und nicht die Revolution, als die sie dargestellt wird. Die Reichen beherrschen die Gesellschaft immer noch, indem sie die Wählenden mit sorgfältig konstruierter Propaganda füttern und dafür sorgen, dass alle arm und überarbeitet sind und verzweifelt darauf warten, dass der Staat ihnen ihre Grundbedürfnisse gewährt.

In den heutigen Demokratien wird nur den legalen Bürger*innen eines Landes Demokratie gewährt. In vielen Ländern wird Menschen, die wegen eines "Verbrechens" verurteilt wurden, das Wahlrecht verweigert, unabhängig davon, wie lange es her ist, dass sie ihre Strafe abgesessen haben. In den USA wird dies genutzt, um Minderheiten das Wahlrecht zu verweigern, die einen großen Teil der Gefängnisinsass*innen ausmachen. In manchen Gesellschaften darf nur eine kleine Minderheit an der Demokratie teilnehmen. Im Apartheids- Südafrika gewährte sich die Minderheit (europäische Siedler*innen) selbst die Demokratie und schloss die einheimische Mehrheit aus, indem sie die Demokratie dazu nutzte, der einheimischen Bevölkerung die Rechte vorzuenthalten, die den europäischen Siedler*innen gewährt wurden. Anarchie bedeutet natürlich, dass es keine Regierung, keine Herrschenden gibt. Die Demokratie zielt darauf ab, dass die einzelne Person von anderen regiert, beherrscht und kontrolliert wird. Es liegt also auf der Hand, dass Anarchie mit Demokratie grundsätzlich unvereinbar ist.

Es ist viel darüber geschrieben worden, warum das Konzept der Demokratie einfach nicht mit Anarchie vereinbar ist. Dennoch weigern sich viele Menschen, die sich heute als Anarchist*innen bezeichnen, die Idee der Demokratie als revolutionäre Methode loszulassen, und bestehen darauf, dass sie irgendwie ihren inhärent hierarchischen Charakter und ihre lange Geschichte der Unterdrückung überwinden kann. Ehrlich gesagt sind viele dieser Leute einfach nur verwirrte Minarchist*innen, die die Hierarchie nicht wirklich abschaffen, sondern nur minimieren wollen.

Die Konsensdemokratie zielt darauf ab, dass sich alle Mitglieder einer Gruppe auf ein gemeinsames Vorgehen einigen. In der Theorie hört sich das gut an, aber die einzige Möglichkeit, alle Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen und Erfahrungen dazu zu bringen, demselben Ziel zuzustimmen, besteht darin, den Plan so weit zu verwässern, dass die Aktion wahrscheinlich sinnlos wird. Die Konsensdemokratie geht davon aus, dass die Mehrheitsgruppe die Minderheitsgruppe nicht schikanieren oder unter Druck setzen wird, damit sie sich ihrem Willen beugt. Sie ignoriert die Tatsache, dass manche Menschen anderen ihren Willen aggressiv aufzwingen oder zumindest ihre Gegner*innen beschämen oder manipulieren, damit sie sich unterwerfen.

Das ganze Konzept der Konsensdemokratie erinnert mich an das Meme mit dem selbstgefälligen Kerl, der am Stand mit dem Schild "Change my mind" sitzt und seine politischen Gegner*innen zu einer Debatte einlädt. Ich kann mit Sicherheit sagen, dass ich, wenn ich diesen Typen an diesem Stand sitzen sähe, in die andere Richtung gehen würde. Warum sollte man jemanden in eine Situation bringen, in der man gezwungen ist, seine ganze Energie darauf zu verwenden, jemandes Meinung zu ändern? Mach einfach dein eigenes Ding und kümmere dich nicht um Leute, die sich nicht an dem beteiligen wollen, was du tust. Wenn Menschen grundlegende Meinungsverschiedenheiten haben, müssen sie nicht mitmachen. Das ist nicht das Ende der Welt.

Der vergebliche Versuch, alle zu einer Einigung zu bringen, ist nur die neueste Form des bürokratischen Windens, das politisches Handeln schon lange sabotiert. Nach zahllosen Stunden hitziger Debatten und einer langen Reihe von Kompromissen wird der erzielte Konsens (wenn er denn überhaupt jemals zustande kommt) wahrscheinlich sehr verwässert und für niemanden in der Gruppe von Nutzen sein. Ein Plan für konkrete Maßnahmen wird sich in eine frustrierende Übung aus Zugeständnissen, lauen Halbmaßnahmen und schließlich Untätigkeit verwandelt haben. Und das alles nur, weil die Leute, die den Plan gemacht haben, das Bedürfnis hatten, die Zustimmung eines Ausschusses von Neinsagenden einzuholen, bevor sie ihn weiterverfolgen.

>Anstatt dass eine große Gruppe die Demokratie bemüht, um sich auf eine Vorgehensweise zu einigen, wäre es viel produktiver, wenn kleinere Gruppen, die aus Menschen mit gemeinsamen Interessen bestehen, sich abspalten und zusammenarbeiten, um ihre eigenen Pläne zu verfolgen, die keine Kompromisse erfordern, weil ihre Interessen bereits übereinstimmen. Im Laufe der Geschichte hat die Demokratie dazu gedient, Autorität zu legitimieren und hierarchische Machtstrukturen zu rechtfertigen, indem sie jede unterdrückerische Maßnahme des Staates gegen uns als "Wille des Volkes" darstellte. Sie hat es den Mächtigen lange Zeit ermöglicht, die Machtlosen zu unterdrücken. Menschen, die darauf bestehen, den Anarchismus mit der Demokratie in Verbindung zu bringen, versuchen, den Anarchismus zu legitimieren und ihn mit bequemen Institutionen in Verbindung zu bringen, die von durch und durch indoktrinierten Liberalen übernommen werden. Aber die Anarchie braucht keine Legitimation. Die Anarchie muss nicht verwässert werden, um ihre Anziehungskraft auf ein hierarchieverliebtes Publikum zu erhöhen.

Anarchist*innen sind immer gegen die Monarchie, die Herrschaft des Einzelnen. Wir sind immer gegen die Oligarchie, die Herrschaft einiger weniger. Warum sollten wir dann nicht auch gegen die Demokratie sein, also die Herrschaft der Vielen? Warum sollten die Vielen entscheiden, wie du oder ich unser Leben leben? Ein Herrscher ist ein Herrscher ist ein Herrscher. Die Demokratie wurde von den Eliten der Gesellschaft geschickt als Waffe eingesetzt. Indem sie die Demokratie mit sorgfältig ausgearbeiteter Propaganda kombinieren, können die Mächtigen die Wählenden kontrollieren und sie so manipulieren, dass sie gegen ihre eigenen Interessen stimmen.

Die Demokratie ist seit jeher ein Synonym für klassenbasierte Gesellschaften. Sie hat ganze Länder in zwei kaum unterscheidbare politische Parteien (konservativ und "progressiv") gespalten, die sich dennoch ständig an die Gurgel gehen. Selbst in ihren libertärfreundlichsten Formen hat es immer wieder versagt, Hierarchie, Zwang und die autoritären Machenschaften von Mehrheitsgruppen zu verhindern. Du kannst nicht versuchen, ein künstliches System, das so brutal hierarchisch ist wie die Demokratie, durch eine vermeintlich egalitärere Version desselben Systems zu ersetzen und es Anarchie nennen. Du musst das ganze verrottete System über Bord werfen.

Lehne die Demokratie ab. Lehne die Vorstellung ab, dass du von irgendjemandem regiert werden solltest. Umarme die Selbstbestimmung. Umarme die Anarchie.

title: Na semana da COP31, Tarcísio nomeia Ricardo Salles para o governo de São Paulo
content:
O governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcisio de Freitas (Republicanos), tem um novo nome no seu quadro: o advogado Ricardo Salles, ex-ministro do Meio Ambiente do governo Bolsonaro, que assumirá o cargo de secretário de Justiça e Cidadania no estado. Ele substituirá Arthur Lima, militar que coordenou o Gabinete de Segurança Institucional (GSI) entre 2008 e 2011 nas gestões Lula e Dilma Rousseff (PT).




A nomeação de Salles para o governo Tarcísio a partir de janeiro de 2027 acontece num momento no mínimo contraditório: nesta quarta-feira, dia 11 de novembro, o presidente Lula (PT) 

discursou

 na abertura da Cúpula de Líderes da 31ª edição da Conferência do Clima, pedindo que os países ricos cumpram seus compromissos assumidos no enfrentamento às mudanças climáticas. Na sua gestão como ministro do Meio Ambiente entre 2019 e 2021, Salles foi responsável por reduzir o trabalho de fiscalização do Ibama contra crimes ambientais.




Salles foi também o autor da célebre frase de que o governo deveria “passar a boiada” em relação à regulamentação ambiental no Brasil. A declaração aconteceu durante a também infame reunião ministerial do governo Bolsonaro, realizada em abril de 2020, em meio à pandemia de covid-19. Na data, o ministro do Meio Ambiente defendeu que: “precisa ter um esforço nosso aqui, enquanto estamos nesse momento de tranquilidade no aspecto de cobertura de imprensa, porque só se fala de covid, e ir passando a boiada, e mudando todo o regramento [ambiental), e simplificando normas”.




As falas de Salles e dos demais ministros vieram a público apenas em maio daquele ano, quando o vídeo da reunião foi tornado público por decisão do ministro Celso de Mello, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).




O ministro relatava um inquérito que apurava se Bolsonaro havia tentado interferir na Polícia Federal (PF), como foi denunciado pelo ex-ministro Sérgio Moro e agora governador eleito do Paraná. Moro rompeu com Bolsonaro na época acusando o então presidente de interferência após demitir o então diretor-geral da PF, Maurício Valeixo, e insistir em trocas de comando da corporação no Rio de Janeiro, onde vivem seus filhos. Seis anos depois, Moro apoiou Flávio Bolsonaro na eleição para presidente e foi eleito pelo PL, partido da família Bolsonaro.




Um ex-ministro do Meio Ambiente acusado de envolvimento com extração ilegal de madeira




Ricardo Salles é réu, desde 2023, em uma ação penal sobre contrabando de madeira da Amazônia. Ele é acusado de suposto envolvimento com uma organização criminosa que contrabandeava madeira para os Estados Unidos e a União Europeia. O processo segue no STF, sob relatoria de Alexandre de Moraes.




Em 2021, a 

Agência Pública

 

mostrou

 como o então ministro recebeu em seu gabinete um grupo de madeireiros envolvidos na exploração irregular no Pará. A reportagem revelou como esse primeiro encontro rendeu frutos, com Salles indo ao estado e gravando um vídeo defendendo a legalidade da extração e da ação dos madeireiros. A imagem foi usada na época para embasar uma notícia-crime da PF do Amazonas contra o ex-ministro.



















Foram as investigações contra Salles que levaram à sua saída do governo. Ele pediu exoneração do Ministério do Meio Ambiente em 23 de junho de 2021.




A 

Pública

 mostrou como a gestão de Salles no Ministério do Meio Ambiente foi marcada por uma redução na fiscalização ambiental e nas multas. Reportagem 

revelou

 como essa diminuição aconteceu justamente em locais onde o desmatamento mais crescia. No Pará, houve descontinuação das ações de fiscalização, além de exonerações e trocas no corpo técnico do Ibama. Salles também foi responsável por nomear militares, muitos deles paulistas, nas ações de combate a crimes ambientais.




A 

Pública

 também teve acesso a atas de reuniões do Conselho Nacional da Amazônia Legal (CNAL), nas quais Salles atacou, sem provas, a teoria do ponto de não retorno da Amazônia, considerada referência no mundo todo. A teoria alerta que o desmatamento do bioma pode levar a uma perda irreversível da floresta, que entraria em um processo de se tornar uma savana.




Além disso, a 

Pública

 

mostrou

 em 2023 como uma representação contra Salles, que chegou na Comissão de Ética da Presidência, foi arquivada. A denúncia partiu justamente da fala do político contra a regulamentação ambiental feita na reunião ministerial de abril de 2020. O ex-ministro teve ainda outras cinco representações analisadas pela Comissão entre 2021 e 2022, que envolviam uso de redes sociais para “divulgação de informações falsas e ofensas a terceiros” e participação indevida em evento político, entre outras possíveis infrações éticas.




Foi também na gestão de Salles que o Fundo Amazônia foi suspenso. O fundo é um mecanismo de financiamento internacional criado em 2008 para ações de combate ao desmatamento da floresta cujos recursos eram empregados também na manutenção dos órgãos ambientais, como o Ibama.




O retorno de Salles ao governo de São Paulo




A decisão de nomear Salles como secretário de Justiça e Cidadania seria um acordo de Tarcísio pela desistência de Salles em concorrer ao Senado. 

Segundo a CBN

, o cargo foi uma moeda de troca oferecida pelo governador.




Salles desistiu de concorrer a uma vaga para o Senado uma semana antes das eleições deste ano e anunciou apoio aos aliados de Tarcísio Guilherme Derrite, ex-secretário de Segurança Pública, e André do Prado, presidente da Assembleia Legislativa. O 

anúncio

 aconteceu ao lado do próprio Tarcísio, que foi ministro da infraestrutura no governo Bolsonaro na mesma época de Salles.




Esta não é a primeira vez que Salles integra o quadro de ministros do governo paulista. Ele foi secretário estadual do Meio Ambiente entre 2016 e 2017, na gestão do atual vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin, então governador pelo PSDB.




Em 2021, o então ministro do Meio Ambiente foi 

absolvido

 pelo TJSP de uma condenação por improbidade administrativa referente ao período em que foi secretário de Alckmin. O processo envolvia fraude no plano de manejo da área de proteção ambiental (APA) da várzea do rio Tietê, em 2016, para favorecer empresas. A Federação das Indústrias do Estado de São Paulo (Fiesp) também foi absolvida na mesma data.




Em 2022, Salles foi eleito deputado federal por São Paulo e, na Câmara, integrou as comissões de Meio Ambiente e de Agricultura.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Repudio europeo al INTA por la exoneración de Virginia Aparicio: "Los hallazgos de la investigación no fueron convenientes para muchas personas y sectores"
content:
Por Natalia Concina




Violette Geissen, profesora de la Universidad de Wageningen (Países Bajos) y coordinadora general del proyecto internacional Sprint (Transición Sostenible de Protección Vegetal, por sus siglas en inglés), calificó de “injusta” la 

exoneración del INTA Virginia Aparicio

, la investigadora que coordinó en Argentina el estudio sobre exposición a plaguicidas. Geissen defendió el desempeño científico de Aparicio, aseguró que cumplió rigurosamente con los protocolos establecidos por el consorcio internacional y cuestionó la decisión del organismo de apartarla. “Virginia Aparicio es una investigadora excelente”, afirmó Geissen desde Holanda, en diálogo con Tierra Viva.




“Hicimos protocolos para armonizar los métodos y que se realizaran en todos los países de la misma manera. Virginia siguió esos protocolos al pie de la letra”, sostuvo la investigadora, que también cuestionó la decisión institucional de abandonar el proyecto.




“El INTA firmó su ingreso al consorcio conociendo qué se iba a hacer y cuáles eran los objetivos. Ese contrato no lo firmó Virginia, lo firmó el responsable del organismo. Por lo tanto, no se entiende cómo luego quieren irse”, planteó.




La coordinadora de Sprint también reveló que el caso argentino no es el único que generó consecuencias para los investigadores involucrados. “Otro investigador perdió su trabajo y otras personas sufrieron hostigamiento”, contó. Y vinculó esas situaciones con los resultados de la investigación: “Es claro que los hallazgos de Sprint no fueron convenientes para muchas personas y sectores”.




El proyecto Sprint fue financiado por la Unión Europea y reunió a instituciones científicas de diez países europeos, además de Argentina. Su objetivo era desarrollar una herramienta para evaluar los riesgos de los agroquímicos a partir del análisis de residuos y mezclas de plaguicidas en el ambiente, los animales y las personas.




La Argentina fue elegida por el consorcio por su relevancia en el mercado internacional de soja. La incorporación del INTA fue aprobada en 2020 mediante la Resolución 477, firmada por la entonces presidenta del organismo, Susana Mirassou. Aparicio quedó a cargo de la coordinación local y durante 2021 se realizaron muestreos en el sudeste bonaerense a 73 voluntarios, entre productores convencionales y agroecológicos, trabajadores rurales y consumidores. También se analizaron muestras de agua, suelo y aire.




Los inconvenientes comenzaron a partir de los primeros resultados

, en junio de 2023. Aparicio había convocado a los participantes para presentarles los hallazgos, pero el INTA ordenó suspender la reunión. Seis meses después, el organismo decidió retirar a la Argentina del consorcio y abrió una investigación administrativa contra la científica. El argumento institucional fue que el proyecto involucraba investigaciones con seres humanos que excedían sus incumbencias, pese a que la participación había sido aprobada previamente.




El sumario concluyó con ocho imputaciones contra Aparicio, entre ellas presuntas irregularidades en el manejo de información confidencial, el envío de muestras al exterior y los procedimientos de evaluación. 

La investigadora rechazó las acusaciones

 y sostuvo que había actuado de acuerdo con los requerimientos del proyecto. Finalmente, el 26 de octubre de 2026, 

el Consejo Directivo del INTA dispuso su exoneración

, la sanción disciplinaria más grave del régimen de empleo público.







Para Geissen, 

los resultados científicos de S

print

 permiten dimensionar la importancia del trabajo realizado y las preguntas que todavía deben responderse. “Es el primer estudio mundial que demostró que existen múltiples plaguicidas en todas las matrices y que se acumulan en las casas”, señaló. La investigadora explicó que uno de los aportes centrales fue estudiar la exposición combinada a distintas sustancias, en lugar de analizar cada producto por separado.







“Lo que hemos visto es que la inhalación puede causar más residuos de plaguicidas que lo que se ingiere”, afirmó. También sostuvo que las personas están expuestas a mezclas de sustancias por distintas vías y que en los hogares pueden encontrarse hasta 120 combinaciones diferentes de plaguicidas.




La coordinadora mencionó, además, los experimentos realizados en modelos animales con concentraciones que habían sido consideradas seguras para los seres humanos. Según relató, en las pruebas con ratas preñadas se observaron casos de leucemia entre las crías.




Para la investigadora europea, estos resultados obligan a revisar los criterios utilizados para establecer los niveles de seguridad de los productos químicos. “Quizás hasta ahora no se habían hecho las pruebas correctas. 

Vivimos en una seguridad falsa y tenemos plaguicidas alrededor y adentro de todos nosotros

”, concluyó la investigadora.




Sprint lleva publicados 64 trabajos científicos y sus resultados abrieron nuevas líneas de investigación sobre la exposición simultánea a agroquímicos y sus posibles efectos en la salud y el ambiente. Geissen participará en modo virtual de la Audiencia Pública que se realizará el viernes 13 de noviembre a las 16 en el Anexo de la Cámara de Diputados de la Nación en apoyo Aparicio.

Repudio europeo al INTA por la exoneración de Virginia Aparicio: "Los hallazgos de la investigación no fueron convenientes para muchas personas y sectores"

 se publicó primero en 

Agencia de Noticias Tierra Viva

.

title: 11 χρόνια δίκη της Χρυσής Αυγής. Οι άνθρωποί της. Προβολή του ντοκιμαντέρ με παρουσία Μ. Φύσσα και Γ. Μάγγο. – ΦΩΤΟ/ΒΙΝΤΕΟ
content:
Σε δύο προβολές και κατάμεστη την αίθουσα του κινηματογράφου Βακούρα στη Θεσσαλονίκη, προβλήθηκε η ταινία της Χρύσας Λύκου και Στέλιου Ζαχαρία: “11 χρόνια δίκη της Χρυσής Αυγής. Οι άνθρωποί της”. Παρόντες ήταν οι συντελεστές της ταινίας, καθώς και η Μάγδα Φύσσα και ο Γιάννης Μάγγος, οι οποίοι απευθύνθηκαν στο κοινό και στις δύο προβολές, αποσπώντας παρατεταμένα χειροκροτήματα. Μετά τη δεύτερη προβολή και έως τα μεσάνυχτα πραγματοποιήθηκε συζήτηση, όπου τονίστηκε ο αγώνας ενάντια στο φασισμό και την αστυνομική βαρβαρότητα.
