title: ziq - Anarchie ist
content:
Katalog Liste aller Texte AutorInnen Themen Letzte Einträge Zur Bibliothek hinzufügen

Mehr Kontakt Material Sticker, Plakate, etc.

Anarchie ist ein fortlaufender Prozess zur Demontage von Autorität.

Anarchie ist die unerbittliche Verneinung von Herrschaftsstrukturen, das Bestreben, sich kleine Bereiche des Lebens frei von Ausbeutung und Leid zu schaffen.

Anarchie ist der kompromisslose Vorstoß gegen Unterdrückung und die lautstarke Forderung nach Autonomie und Selbstbestimmung, die Ablehnung aller Klassen, Institutionen und Dogmen, die geschaffen wurden, um Menschen zu beherrschen.

Anarchie ist vor allem eine Praxis, nicht eine Theorie. Es geht darum, aktiv daran zu arbeiten, autoritäre Verhältnisse zu beenden, wo immer sie existieren, und nicht-autoritäre Alternativen aufzubauen. Es geht nicht darum, eine Lebensweise für einen imaginären Ort, eine imaginäre Zeit und imaginäre Menschen vorzuschreiben. Es geht um reale Menschen und die Bewältigung realer Probleme.

Anarchie ist eine lebendige und atmende Praxis, die wir in unser tägliches Leben einbauen. Eine persönliche Haltung gegen die Herrschaft, die alle unsere Entscheidungen beeinflusst und so den Verlauf unserer Existenz prägt.

Es gibt kein Endziel für Anarchie. Sie ist ein fortwährender, nicht enden wollender Kampf gegen hierarchische Strukturen und die Autoritätspersonen, die im Luxus an der Spitze dieser Strukturen sitzen.

Anarchie ist der Wunsch nach Freiheit von Tyrannei. Anarchie sind unzählige Generationen verschiedener Menschen mit dem Drang, freier zu sein als sie es unter den Systemen sind, die sie gewaltsam regieren.

Anarchie ist die Ablehnung der Regierung, der Staaten, der Grenzen, des Kapitals, des Patriarchats, des Gender-Essenzialismus, der Sklaverei, der Ideologie, der Rechten, der Linken, des Klerus, der Demokratie, des Privateigentums, der Technokratie, der Kernfamilie, des Humanismus, des Imperialismus, der Gefängnisse, der Fabriken, der Gründerväter, der Bürokratie, der Ethnokratie, der Heteronormativität, der Idole, der Tradition, der Polizeiarbeit, der Neuronormativität, des Ökozids, der Zivilisation und jeder anderen Form von Autorität.

Anarchie ist Gemeinschaftsgärten, Umsonstläden, Graffiti, 3D-gedruckte Waffen, FKK, vegane Potlucks [1], Hausbesetzungen, Lebensmittelwälder, Sabotage von Pipelines, freie Software, die Befreiung von Kühen, Ladendiebstahl, das Sichern von Saatgut alter Kulturpflanzen, die Bildung autonomer Zonen, Attentate auf Tyrannen, Guerilla-Gärtnern, Zines schreiben, Regenwasser auffangen, Wahlurnen verbrennen, Biodiversität, Abschaffung der Whiteness, Hacken, Aquaponik, Musik machen, Upcycling, Polizeistationen abfackeln und Wildblumen in der ganzen Landschaft säen.

Anarchist*innen sind jene Personen, die sich weigern, von irgendjemandem oder irgendetwas regiert, beherrscht oder dominiert zu werden. Anarchist*innen sind wütende, verbitterte, verlorene, ängstliche, desillusionierte, gewalttätige, friedliche, mutige, idealistische, mitreißende, furchtlose Träumende.

Ein*e Anarchist*in steht allein gegen die riesige Flut der Autorität, die in alle Richtungen ansteigt. Anarchist*innen verbinden sich mit jeder geschundenen, geknechteten Seele im gemeinsamen Angriff gegen die rücksichtslosen Systeme, die uns entmachten und entfremden sollen.

Anarchie ist geprägt von endlosen Widersprüchen, existenzieller Angst und unerträglichen inneren Konflikten, und doch ergibt Anarchie für jede Person, die entsetzt oder wütend ist über die groben Ungerechtigkeiten, die diesen kleinen blauen Planeten verschlingen, einen perfekten Sinn. Anarchie ist für jede Person, die ein Leben in Würde anstrebt.

Anarchie ist ein unmögliches, absonderliches, aber für unser Überleben notwendiges Streben.

author: Dennis Ward
title: Australia’s inaugural Ambassador for First Nations People visits Canada
content:
Four years ago, the Australian government took a step that no other country has taken when it created the position of Ambassador for First Nations People.

The ambassador, Justin Mohamed, is a Gooreng Gooreng man from Bundaberg in Queensland.

Mohamed recently visited Canada for a series of high-level meetings with Canadian ministers, including Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty.

The ambassador also met with national Indigenous organizations and economic groups. Among the similarities between the two countries, says Mohamed, is the effort to involve Indigenous peoples in economic opportunities.

“For the first time, in my 36 years of working in Indigenous affairs, where both of our leaders are talking very positively about the uplift of economic engagement with our First peoples in our country and seeing the benefits of that,” says Mohamed on the latest episode of Face to Face.

“Obviously, here there is things that we can learn and things that Canada can learn from Australia. Our vast country, we’ve got a lot of land mass, we’ve got so many people spread across that, how to get those connections across our land and hopefully across our waters so we have more connections from country to country.”

The ambassador says Australia has strong laws and policies around consultation when it comes to mining and development on Indigenous Peoples’ lands.

However, he acknowledges that can be improved.

“With the new uptake of critical minerals, the renewable energies, that’s definitely a big conversation piece that is taking place and structures and Traditional Owner Groups as we call them in Australia are positioning themselves to be economically part of these new developments and hopefully learn from the past,” says Mohamed.

We have a long relationship with mining companies, with communities, hopefully learning from those experiences and that we can have a better relationship with the critical minerals, renewable energy space. We know this is a conversation and there’s a whole range of things that wrap around that that are taking place as we sit here,” adds Mohamed.

One of the previous roles Justin Mohamed had was chief executive officer of Reconciliation Australia.

The non-government, not-for-profit was established in January 2001 to promote a continuing national focus for reconciliation between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians.

While he believes reconciliation has come a long way since he was a child, Mohamed says there are still challenges.

“I think the appetite sways back and forth when you have different governments and political leaders and also things that kind of hit us and impact us and the focus and the direction and the energy may be diverted like pandemics or global crashes in our economy these things happen,” says Mohamed.

“I think one of the things that is staying on course is ensuring there’s a path that we still got to walk and that’s part of our history. So, I think in Australia to be fair and as honest as I can be around where we are, we’ve taken steps, but the journey is still a long way in front of us to keep going on that and there’s still healing our nation needs to have collectively together,” he adds.

Dennis is Métis from southern Manitoba. After spending a decade working in TV in Alberta and Ontario, Dennis returned to Manitoba to join APTN. In 2016, he won a Canadian Association of Journalists award for his story A Soldier Scorned for APTN Investigates. In 2017, he became a host/producer for APTN National News and Face to Face.

author: Administrador
title: PREGUNTAS
content:
A las familias buscadoras sin y con colectivo:

Desde el día 3 de octubre, en horas de la tarde, personas cercanas a la glorieta de los desaparecidos, anunciaron en sus redes sociales que estaba confirmado un encuentro, el 6 de diciembre, de colectivos de familiares y el EZLN en la Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos, mientras la Comisión Sexta mantenía una reunión con enviados de la Sexta Nacional, y a la que asistieron, sin invitación, varias buscadoras.

Días después, alguien y a nombre de las familias buscadoras de “La Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos”, circuló en sus redes una “invitación”. Por varios medios se les hizo saber que no era el conducto. Que mandaran la invitación vía el Frayba, quien nos apoyaba y apoya en todo lo referente a registro y propuestas de familias, grupos y colectivas de buscadoras.

Entonces, después de varios días también, les mandamos mensajes por varios lados. Que retiraran la invitación porque en esos términos iba a ser rechazada. Que contenía menciones que podrían considerarse síntoma de que no conocían a quien invitaban, y cosas que podrían considerarse ofensivas para las comunidades zapatistas.

Además de que no era ese tipo de “reuniones” las que pensaba la Comisión Sexta Zapatista, y que correspondía a la delegación zapatista el definir su agenda con fechas y horas.

No sólo no nos hicieron caso, sino que aumentaron su difusión agregando que era seguro que se daría la reunión con la delegación zapatista en la glorieta, poniendo fecha, y hasta hora en algunos casos.

Insistimos mandándoles mensajes de que rehicieran la invitación por lo mismo. Mientras, seguía creciendo la confusión, y colectivas y grupos empezaban a cambiar sus fechas para estar presentes en “LA” reunión. Les advertimos que nos estaban orillando a un desmentido público. Esto es, a una respuesta severa para aclarar.

Hasta donde entendemos, el espacio de La Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos no es una organización, sino un espacio de encuentro. Esto es, no tienen una vocería ni dirección establecida. Es un lugar donde suelen converger grupos y colectivas de familias buscadoras. Supusimos que tienen o tenían un mecanismo para hacer acuerdos y tomar decisiones. Y que, por lo tanto, someterían a ese mecanismo la pertinencia o no de esa redacción que, lo sabían con antelación, provocaba molestia en los zapatistas.

La “invitación” contiene 3 elementos fundamentales:

1.- Se ofrece a los zapatistas apoyo. Por eso “invitaron” a las comunidades zapatistas a que llevaran fotos de sus desaparecidos, y que nos iban a enseñar cómo se hace una ficha de desaparición forzada, cómo se pega en la glorieta – junto con cientos de fotos de desaparecidos-, qué trámites hay que hacer para que una ONG otorgue financiamiento, a quién dirigirse en la pirámide gubernamental, etc.

Hermanas familias buscadoras: en territorio zapatista y en las comunidades que fueron zapatistas y ahora son partidistas, NO HAY DESAPARICIONES FORZADAS desde hace 30 años.

Miren, hay grupos feministas que conocen todo lo relacionado con feminicidios. Otros con infanticidios. Otros con trata de personas. Otros con crímenes impunes. Otros en homofobia. Otros en racismo y segregación. Y así con cada uno de los horrores que se padecen en esta geografía llamada México.

Antes de ofrecernos cursos de qué hacer por estos problemas, ¿no es de esperar que al menos investiguen la tasa, ya no digan de feminicidios, sino de violencia de género en general? Porque sí, en territorios zapatistas no hay feminicidios. Ni infanticidios, ni crímenes impunes. Ni trata de personas (comercio, pues, compra venta de hombres, mujeres e infantes). Y así sea usted güero, alto y habla una lengua incomprensible, entra y sale de territorio zapatista sin ser desaparecido, humillado, burlado, esclavizado, asesinado.

Ni homofobia. Así sea usted otroa (lesbiana, homosexual, transexual y todos los nombres con los que identifica la diferencia sexual), no sólo puede dar clases a infantes heterosexuales (si se capacita antes, claro), ser milicianoa, ocupar cargos en las comunidades y en la organización, y llamarse como le dé la gana y tener la identidad de género que le plazca.

Hay hasta quien ha tratado de venir a dar clases de erotismo y autoestimulación erótica. Hermanas, tenemos la más alta tasa de natalidad comparada con la de las grandes urbes y, créanme, no son clases de erotismo lo que nos hace falta. Las músicas favoritas en la mayoría de la juventud zapatista son el rock, el ska, el rap, el hip hop… y la cumbia. Escuchen y bailen una cumbia y díganme si no hay ahí una “autoestimulación erótica”.

Ok, nos dicen, es que en la Glorieta no saben qué es el zapatismo. Los grupos, colectivos y redes de familias buscadoras no tienen por qué conocer o saber qué o quién es el EZLN. Sí, es ignorancia, pero no mala fe.

De acuerdo. ¿Entonces por qué invitas a un desconocido a tu casa? ¿No es irresponsable llevar a tu casa y a tu gente, a alguien del que no sabes nada y, además, oculta su rostro? ¿Se detuvieron a pensar en lo que un rostro embozado significa para muchas de las familias buscadoras?

¿No era más sencillo preguntar a la gente cercana a la Glorieta y que le pidieran una semblanza así sea breve del zapatismo “de Chiapas” -así dicen-, y darse cuenta de que eso de ofrecerles apoyo, ayuda o asesoría era, por decirlo amablemente, imprudente?

2.- “¿Por qué hasta ahora?” y “¿Qué gana el EZLN? Estas preguntas las han estado moviendo personas que dicen ser del Movimiento por la Paz con Justicia y Dignidad (MPJD), de triste memoria en la lucha por verdad y justicia, y de la Glorieta. Y que se reiteran, con otra redacción, en la “invitación”.

“Estoy segura de que los zapatistas ganan algo con la iniciativa del abrazo. Porque nadie hace nada sin obtener algo a cambio”, dijo sin empacho una buscadora del MPJD y de la Glorieta, en una reunión con colectivos ciudadanos que se organizaban para recibir a la delegación zapatista.

La pregunta no es sólo un insulto a cualquiera, también refleja el desconocimiento de su propia historia y de la relación que existió entre el EZLN y el MPJD hace 15 años. Dicen también que no quieren abrazos, lo que es una amarga ironía en un movimiento que culminó dándole besos al psicópata Felipe Calderón Hinojosa. Y que cuestionan qué gana el EZLN con esta iniciativa, después de que el MPJD terminó encumbrando a un personaje mediocre y miserable, Emilio Álvarez Icaza (que pasó por varios partidos y fue “independiente” -siempre cargado a la ultraderecha-, y que hoy es parte del paradójico partido “Somos México”). Además de otras mentiras que han encontrado eco en la supuesta prensa progresista, que ya ni se molesta en investigar mínimamente lo que publica, arrojando así a la basura la supuesta credibilidad de libros de autor y la ya muy débil legitimidad de esa revista.

Hermanas buscadoras. Aquí hay poco qué decir. Es una decisión que deben tomar ustedes. Pero les cuento algo:

Las comunidades originarias en México llevaban, y algunas todavía llevan, más de 500 años desaparecidas. No hablaré de todas (para eso pueden recurrir al Congreso Nacional Indígena, que acaba de cumplir 30 años en su lucha como red de barrios, pueblos, lenguas, movimientos y organizaciones originarias), sino sólo de las zapatistas.

Antes de 1994, las comunidades originarias de Chiapas no existían. No nacían y no morían, porque ni siquiera se registraba su nacimiento. Todavía hoy, son miles de indígenas los que no son reconocidos como “mexicanos” porque son considerados como migrantes en su propia tierra, en la que vivieron sus padres, sus abuelos, sus bisabuelos, sus tatarabuelos, y así por siglos.

Cuando nos alzamos en armas hace ya casi 33 años, el país nos “encontró”. Por supuesto que no le gustó la presentación. Tal vez hubieran preferido que fuera en artesanías, bailables “chistosos” y en una esquina vendiendo frutas. Pero bueno, así somos de contreras. Así que le declaramos la guerra a los malos gobiernos y tomamos limpiamente 7 cabeceras del suroriental estado MEXICANO de Chiapas el uno de enero de 1994.

Después de los primeros combates, con bajas de ambos lados -federales y zapatistas-, un grupo de gente “se levantó” y dijo algo como “un momento, ¿quiénes son?” y se metieron en medio. En serio, no en sentido figurado, en medio de los tiros. Y en esa gente iban intelectuales, ong´s, gente sin partido… y artistas. No, no aparecieron las vanguardias revolucionarias. Ésas esperaron a ver si nos aniquilaban los federales. Cuando vieron que no, entonces sí aparecieron, son vanguardias pues. Pero bueno, esas personas nos pidieron un alto al fuego primero, una tregua después. Y nos pidieron que dialogáramos, que nos presentáramos pues, pero no a tiros, sino con palabras. Después han realizado varias iniciativas para apoyarnos o para apoyar a quienes les pedimos que apoyen.

Y nos dieron una oportunidad, una oportunidad de vida. La nuestra, no la que dictaban los de arriba, que no era vida. Y cada cosa que hacemos hasta ahora es para honrar a esas personas.

Hermanas buscadoras, ¿ustedes creen que les reclamamos? ¿Que les preguntamos “¿por qué hasta ahora?”, “¿por qué, si llevamos siglos desaparecidos, hasta ahora nos miran? Pues no, hermanas, en su lugar lo que hicimos fue agradecerles el habernos dado la oportunidad de vivir (no de sobrevivir o de morir en silencio, en el olvido). Y sabíamos entonces y lo sabemos ahora que no tenían nada que ganar y sí mucho que perder.

Porque podría ser que todo fuera un engaño (justo como sostiene el MPJD), que en realidad buscáramos ganar tiempo y adquirir armas y municiones, hacer reclutamiento forzado, practicar el terrorismo, realizar secuestros y asaltos, violar y asesinar a mujeres de piel clara por venganza, por rencor, por rabia, porque sí, etcétera. Se arriesgaron pues. No sólo en México, también en otras partes del mundo. Incluso en las Españas, la villana favorita de la 4T.

Y entonces hubo conciertos, bailables, carteles, teatro, danza, volantes, exposiciones, arte, pláticas, conferencias, mesas redondas, semilleros, ventas de chunches, libros, para juntar apoyo económico.

Justo como ahora hay todo eso, y más, para apoyarlas a ustedes, hermanas, para que vayan a la ciudad de México, nos cuenten la historia de su faltante, de su dolor, de su esperanza, de su deber. Que vayan, no a grandes actos de masas y mediáticos, a asambleas grandes, medianas, o pequeñas, a mítines donde pocos hablan y el resto sólo aplaude, grita consignas y escucha.

Y todo para recibir… un abrazo. Como escribió alguien, el acto primario del amor: un abrazo. El abrazo que desprecia el MPJD. El abrazo entre dolores, resistencias y rebeldías.

Y un abrazo, hermanas, no tiene nada que ver con actos públicos, masivos, mediáticos.

Nosotros no les estamos pidiendo que se salgan de la glorieta. Ni que sean menos. Al contrario, crezcan y sean muchas. Pero no vamos a ir a donde, dicen, nos “invitaron” porque nuestro objetivo es tener encuentros privados para escucharlas.

El otro punto de la “invitación” es la propuesta en sí. Un acto en la Glorieta.

Digamos que son 400 grupos quienes se encuentran en el espacio de la Glorieta. Digamos que habla una representante de cada colectivo. Digamos que pueden sintetizar su dolor y su historia y la de su ausencia en… ¿10 minutos? Serían 4000 minutos, unas 66 horas. Casi 3 días de participaciones continuas, sin descanso alguno, sin comer ni dormir. Además, las palabras de bienvenida, la explicación de la historia de la glorieta, de cada una de las redes, movimientos, asociaciones y frentes de familias buscadoras convocadas. Y ni hablar de las participaciones “espontáneas” y saludos del partido político “SomosMx” o como se llame. Y, por último, las palabras zapatistas, que nunca han brillado por ser breves. Todo en un lugar, en un día, en un mitin disfrazado de encuentro.

Creo que hemos sido claros que lo que queremos es escuchar la palabra de ustedes, hermanas, de las familias y grupos de buscadoras. En un día no bastaría.

¿Por qué si no es que vamos 1530 delegadas, delegados y delegadoas? ¿Por qué están organizados para “dislocarse”, o sea partirse en 25 grupos de 50 cada uno? ¿Por qué cada grupo de 50 está organizado para partirse en varios subgrupos de hasta 5 delegados cada uno?

¿Por qué hay un grupo coordinador general que monitorea el todo y las partes? ¿Por qué le insistimos a la comunidad originaria Otomí de la Casa Samir que, en nuestro hospedaje, privilegiaran espacios para reuniones simultáneas, por encima de dormitorios y cocina? ¿Por qué les dijimos que a nosotros nos bastaba un cartón para poner entre el suelo y el cuerpo a la hora de descansar? ¿Por qué les dijimos que no se preocuparan por nuestra alimentación, porque, según estudios científicos, una “guajolota” (una torta de tamal) te da batería para una semana?

Entendemos que nuestra salida provoque celos: que sí es que queremos quitarles el protagonismo a ciertos personajes siniestros, o a grandes, medianas o pequeñas agrupaciones de familias que buscan o de colectivos y colectivas; que si queremos sacar algo (como con torpeza sostiene el MPJD que no quiere sino reforzar la plataforma del partido “Somos México” -que basa toda su estrategia en el “fenómeno” (así dicen) de la desaparición forzada en México, y que de ese dolor masivo quieren sacar sus votos-). Y que, sin recato alguno, propone pedir financiamiento al Partido Acción Nacional. Siendo que bajo su mandato (Felipe Calderón Hinojosa), inició una pesadilla que se alarga y refuerza a lo largo de 4 sexenios… y los que faltan. Así las cosas: los criminales pidiendo verdad y justicia.

Compañeras y hermanas, nosotras las comunidades sólo hemos ganado deudas para pagar nuestro viaje; no tenemos candidatos o candidatas a nada, no estamos en campaña de reclutamiento forzado o no forzado, no cobramos por reuniones que, imaginamos, serán dolorosas para ustedes y para nosotros. Toda la campaña de financiamiento es para sus viajes de ustedes, para su estancia y hospedaje, para su salud, para su transporte dentro de la Ciudad de México.

Hasta vamos a convocar a voluntarios y voluntarias para crear un equipo de acompañamiento, de guardianes y guardianas, para que las cuiden en los trayectos dentro la Ciudad de México, recordarles que tomen sus medicinas, cuidar que no se pierdan, recomendarles que no coman alimentos que les pueden hacer daño. Cosas así.

Son voluntarias y voluntarios (y seguro no faltarán voluntarioas), no percibirán salario, paga o premio alguno. A no ser el orgullo de realizar un acto humanitario, no sólo no reciben nada, también y sobre todo ponen de su propio tiempo libre, su salario y su desgaste físico y emocional. Y digo emocional porque, escucharlas, hermanas, es duro, difícil y, a cualquier persona honesta y noble, le lleva a preguntarse “¿Cómo hacen para sufrir todo eso y como quiera seguir en su búsqueda?”

Pero entendemos sus desconfianzas. Aunque tampoco vamos para ganarnos su aprecio, confianza y cariño. Vamos a escucharlas a ustedes. No a quienes hablan bien en público, se saben expresar con palabras, conocen de leyes e historia (muy poco, a lo que se ve), o son hábiles en su oratoria.

Con las palabras que expresen su angustia, con las lágrimas que hablen su dolor, con los silencios que acudan a sus gargantas, con eso nos damos por bien servidos.

He escuchado una participación del Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés, coordinador en jefe de este capítulo de la gira por la vida, donde señala lo principal: a la persona ausente. ¿Quién es o era? ¿Cómo era físicamente? ¿Cómo en la familia, en la escuela, en el trabajo, en el barrio, en el campo, en la pareja? ¿Qué pasó?

Y, claro, también su lucha de ustedes por encontrarlo, lo que esa ausencia ha provocado en sus vidas, la hermandad o no con otras familias que buscan.

En resumen: la agenda de la delegación zapatista es muy simple: vamos a estar en la Ciudad de México, en la “Casa Samir Flores Soberanes”. Estaremos todo el mes de diciembre ahí y la primera semana de enero.

Algunas partes del todo de la delegación irán a actividades artísticas, como los jóvenes y jóvenas teatristas, a veces a presentar sus obras, a veces a presenciar las de artistas profesionales. Otras partes irán a encuentros con estudiantes y maestros universitarios. Esa banda universitaria es buena, tiene ganas de aprender y se fajan en la chamba a la que se comprometen, tal vez les convenga asistir. Todo esto si da tiempo y hay espacio, porque lo principal es escucharlas… y abrazarlas, pero no obligadas, sino que voluntariamente.

También partes de la delegación irán a las ciudades de Xalapa, de Guadalajara, de Puebla y de Querétaro. A Oaxaca no podremos ir por causa del tiempo y de la paga. En estos días les diremos las fechas en cada lugar y dónde registrarse. Ustedes pueden escoger ir a la que les quede cerca, o a la Ciudad de México, o a las dos partes.

Pero, en esas fechas, habrá a la mano una delegación de zapatistas, todos de sangre originaria maya, dispuesta a recibirlas y escucharlas.

En estos días empieza una serie de conciertos, de presentaciones de danza y teatro, de funciones de cine, de espectáculos para niños, de tianguis, con el único fin de conseguir fondos para que ustedes tengan cómo viajar, a dónde llegar, dónde hospedarse, dónde alimentarse, dónde reunirse.

Desde las montañas del sureste mexicano.

Capitán Insurgente Marcos. México, noviembre del 2026.

author: Daron Letts
title: Offshore Western Arctic oil and gas exploration could be back on the table
content:
The days might be numbered for the federal government’s decade-long 

moratorium

 on oil and gas exploration in the Western Arctic — at least in its present form.




“There is a review happening,” said Northern and Arctic Affairs Minister Rebecca Chartrand during a news conference at Nunavut Arctic College in Iqaluit on Tuesday.




The moratorium, established in December 2016 by then-prime minister Justin Trudeau, remains in place as the Liberal government charts “the best path forward,” Chartrand said.




The moratorium agreement calls for a review every five years. 

This includes ongoing meetings with Inuit organizations and territorial governments, Chartrand said.




At a news conference in Montreal at the same time, Prime Minister Mark Carney highlighted $11 million in funding to support “the governance and oversight of offshore oil and gas activities in the Arctic Ocean.”




“This is capacity funding for Inuit leadership. It is absolutely not in any way, shape, or form a decision about lifting the moratorium,” Carney said.




Chartrand’s comments came in response to questions after a media event about the federal government’s $4 billion in cultural spending outlined in Thursday’s 

budget

.
















In her opening address at the event, she highlighted the new Canada Creative Credit, an annual tax cut on up to $45,000 of arts-related net business income for artists.




Qikiqtani Inuit Association President Olayuk Akesuk says he and other Inuit leaders met with Northern and Arctic Affairs Minister Rebecca Chartrand virtually two weeks ago. They discussed lifting the decade-long moratorium on oil and gas exploration in the Western Arctic. (Photo by Daron Letts)




“We are also proposing stronger support for film, television, and digital production and a new productivity mega deduction to help eligible businesses invest in equipment and technology,” she added.




Chartrand met with staff at the Inuit Broadcasting Corp. on Monday.




The budget would provide an additional $300 million in funding to the CBC and Radio-Canada. The public broadcaster got $1.46 billion in the 2025-26 fiscal year. The budget also proposes $134 million over four years for the Local Journalism Initiative, a program that supports independent local news in rural, remote, and under-served regions, including the Arctic.




She also highlighted $393 million in spending in support of francophone cultural institutions.
















As for the moratorium on oil and gas exploration, Qikiqtani Inuit Association President Olayuk Akesuk and fellow Inuit leaders expressed their perspective with Chartrand during a virtual meeting two weeks ago, he said in an interview Tuesday.




“It is important to go through the regulatory process in order for us to support anything that might impact the environment,” he said. “Let’s work together to ensure that we are doing it properly.”




Nunavut Liberal MP Lori Idlout said she is confident that discussions about any return to exploration will be made in collaboration with Inuit.




— With files from Nehaa Bimal

author: Sharon Zhang
title: “The Time Is Now for Change”: Sanders Says He Won’t Back Schumer for Leader
content:
Emerging leader Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he is refusing to fund the government next month until the war is defunded.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vermont) announced on Tuesday that he will not be supporting Sen. Chuck Schumer’s (D-New York) run for Senate majority leader in the new Congress and suggested that someone else will be running to replace him.

“I personally have known Chuck Schumer for 30 years, and I like Chuck — nobody works harder than Chuck Schumer,” said Sanders in a press conference. “But, in my view, the time is now for change. And I will not be supporting Chuck to be reelected as the Democratic leader.”

This marks the first major public defection in the caucus against Schumer. There hasn’t yet been a senator to formally nominate themselves to challenge Schumer. But Sanders suggested in his remarks that Schumer won’t be running unopposed and floated the name of progressive favorite Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) for the role.

“I think one of the names out there is Chris Van Hollen. I think Chris has indicated some interest, but you’ll have to talk to him,” Sanders said. Sanders added in an interview that he would back Van Hollen if he ran.

Van Hollen is reportedly actively considering a run. On Tuesday, Van Hollen said at the Popular Mandate conference that he is “actively listening to people who are looking for” change, and called for a “bold agenda.”

“I am in the process right now of calling my colleagues,” he said. “Because at the end of the day, this is a vote in the Democratic caucus. So let’s just keep in touch.”

Further in his press conference, Sanders said that voters must be shown that the party is ready to respond to their demands after Americans entrusted them with a massive congressional majority, adding: “We need a process, we need a vigorous debate about the direction of the Democratic Party.”

Sanders was joined by Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Michigan), who agreed that lawmakers must come together to decide on their goals. Slotkin said that Democrats should withhold quorum if Schumer is the only candidate and doesn’t present a vision for the future of the party.

The two lawmakers had just come out of a meeting with Senate Democrats in which they said Schumer had not provided a clear goal for their upcoming majority.

Flanked by Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-New York), Ruben Gallego (D-Arizona), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-Rhode Island) in a press conference after that same meeting on Tuesday, Schumer said that he’s “confident” he will be reelected as leader.

Polling by YouGov for Indivisible released on Tuesday found that only 10 percent of voters say that Democrats should choose Schumer to be majority leader, while 57 percent said they should choose someone else.

Van Hollen has long criticized Schumer’s leadership as ineffective, especially in times when Schumer has ceded Democrats’ power during the first two years of President Donald Trump’s second term. Progressives have favored the Maryland senator’s actions on foreign policy, including on Israel and Palestinian rights. They have also pointed to Van Hollen’s visit with constituent Kilmar Abrego García after he was deported to El Salvador as a sign of his willingness to fight against the Trump administration.

Michigan Senator-Elect Abdul El-Sayed (D) has said for months that he would support Van Hollen for leader, and repeated that assertion last week after winning his election.

“We have two members in that room, duly elected senators, that would not be there if Schumer and the [Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC)] had had their way,” Van Hollen said at Popular Mandate on Tuesday, likely referring to El-Sayed and Troy Jackson. “Schumer and the DSCC sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC against these candidates.”

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $50,000 in the next 9 days. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.

author: Unknown
title: Women’s vigil in Amed commemorates 14 victims of femicide and unexplained deaths
content:
Women gathered outside the courthouse in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) on Tuesday for the sixth time to protest against femicide, gender-based violence and the failure to adequately investigate suspicious deaths. The vigil, organized by the Network Against Violence, focused this week on the names and life stories of 14 women who were murdered between November 2 and 10. Numerous women joined the demonstration alongside representatives of political parties and civil society organizations.




Under a banner reading “Women Stand Vigil for Justice and Memory,” participants carried photographs of women who had been killed. Chants such as “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom), “Femicide is political” and “Bijî tekoşîna jinan” (Long live women’s struggle) echoed throughout the gathering. With the slogan “Do not protect, do not whitewash, prosecute,” they denounced impunity for violence against women.




Remembering 14 women and their life stories




Speaking on behalf of the network, Irem Ilhan of the Association for Solidarity from a Women’s Perspective (DAKAHDER) stated that women refused to allow the victims’ fates to be forgotten. She emphasized the need to insist on thorough investigations in a society where women’s deaths are frequently classified as suicides, accidents or unexplained incidents. She described the systematic threat to women’s lives as femicide.




The participants then read aloud the stories of 14 women, explicitly distinguishing between confirmed homicides and deaths whose causes have yet to be determined.




Among the victims was 33-year-old Şefika Yeşildağ, who was stabbed to death by her former husband, Osman Oruç, in Aksaray on November 2. The couple had been divorced for six years. According to her mother, the man had continued to harass Şefika. Nazmiye Özer, 56, was also killed by her former husband on November 7, six years after their divorce. Women’s organizations called for an investigation into possible previous threats and failures by state authorities responsible for providing protection.




Latife Mengüç, 50, was shot dead on November 5 by a man from whom she wanted to separate. The perpetrator subsequently took his own life.




Domestic violence




Particularly distressing was the case of Huriye Çiçek and her daughter Zeynep Demircan. The 50-year-old mother and her 25-year-old daughter were killed in an armed attack in early November, carried out by Huriye’s son, who was also Zeynep’s brother. An eleven-year-old girl was seriously injured in the attack.




Hülya Aktaş, 73, was stabbed to death by her son on November 6. Another of her sons was also killed in the same attack.




Citing these cases, women’s organizations emphasized that family ties offered no guarantee of protection against patriarchal violence and that violence within the family must not be treated as a private matter.




Other victims included 31-year-old Hilal Mete and 46-year-old Ayşe Sena Demir. Both were shot dead inside a vehicle on November 5. A suspect was arrested. Satı Aydoğmuş, 68, was also killed in an armed attack that claimed the life of another person.




Unexplained deaths must be investigated




In several of the cases presented, it has yet to be established whether the women were victims of violent crimes. Participants therefore demanded comprehensive forensic examinations and transparent investigations.




These cases include the death of 18-year-old Havva Büşra Kural, who was found dead alongside her father in an apartment on November 2. The circumstances surrounding the deaths of 44-year-old Melek Altun, Olessya Shudrina, also 44, and Melek Kaval, who were found dead in their apartments in early November, also remain unclear.




The vigil also commemorated an unidentified woman whose body was discovered on November 4 off the coast of Izmir, in the Bayraklı district. Women’s organizations called for her identity to be established and the cause of her death to be determined.




The vigil thus also drew attention to women whose deaths have not yet been confirmed as homicides but whose fates could remain unresolved without effective investigations.




“Justice is needed for all women”




After the names were read aloud, Irem Ilhan emphasized the responsibility of state institutions to protect women, saying: “When a woman is killed despite having reported violence, applied for protection or already been granted protective measures, not only the perpetrators but also any public officials who may bear responsibility must be held accountable.”




She continued: “Justice is needed not only after a woman has been murdered, but for all women who are alive,” Ilhan declared. “Women’s lives are not bargaining chips. Violence is not destiny. Impunity is unacceptable. Forgetting is not an option.”




Irem Ilhan noted that the women gathered not merely to document the number of deaths, but to change the social conditions that enabled such acts. She said their struggle was about defending women’s lives, rights and voices.




Attack on the Kabaiş family condemned




Another focus of the vigil was the still-unresolved death of Kurdish student Rojin Kabaiş. Irem Ilhan criticized shortcomings in the investigation and stated that the family’s search for the truth was now being accompanied by threats and attempts at intimidation.




Speaking on behalf of the “Justice for Rojin” initiative, Dilan Ergül addressed the recent attack on Rojin’s uncle, Ahmet Kabaiş. She said the family had repeatedly received threats because they continued to demand answers. “Although the threats were known to the authorities, adequate protection was not provided. The threats have now escalated into physical attacks,” she added.




Ergül described the attack on Ahmet Kabaiş as an attack on the entire struggle for justice in the Rojin Kabaiş case. She emphasized that the initiative would not abandon its demands for a thorough investigation.




“We are not afraid. We are fighting for Rojin and for all women whose deaths remain unexplained, and we are fighting for one another. In the face of all these attacks, we will continue our collective struggle. We will achieve real justice for Rojin Kabaiş,” Ergül declared.




The vigil concluded with a minute of silence, after which participants applauded and once again chanted their slogans.

The uncle of Rojin Kabaiş, a university student who died under unexplained circumstances in Van in 2024, was attacked and injured by four masked men in Istanbul. According to information available ...

title: Students in Rojava protest for education in Kurdish
content:
Students in several cities across the Cizîrê region of Rojava demonstrated against restrictions on Kurdish-language education imposed by the Syrian transitional government. In Qamişlo, Girkê Legê and Rimêlan, they took to the streets to demand recognition of Kurdish as a language of instruction and guarantees for the right to education in their mother tongue. The protests were sparked by a decision made by the Syrian Ministry of Education in late August to limit Kurdish-language instruction in schools to three hours per week.




In Qamişlo, students from the Hetîn and Şehîd Jîr schools participated in a demonstration that began at the Şehîd Osman Sabrî intersection in the Hilêliyê neighborhood. From there, the protesters marched to the regional administrative headquarters in the city center. During the march, they chanted slogans demanding recognition of their mother tongue and opposing restrictions on education.




Students: Our language is our identity




Outside the regional administrative headquarters, Diyana Sonchan and Viyan Mehmûd read out a joint statement in Kurdish and Arabic on behalf of the students. In the statement, they condemned the Ministry of Education’s decision to reduce the number of hours allocated to Kurdish-language instruction.




“Kurdish is not merely another school subject, but an expression of the identity, culture, history and existence of the Kurdish people. Restricting Kurdish-language instruction therefore goes far beyond a change to the school timetable. It directly infringes upon the linguistic and cultural rights of the Kurdish population,” the statement read.




The students called on the Ministry of Education and the Syrian transitional government to recognize the linguistic and educational rights of the Kurdish people. They also demanded guarantees of equal rights for all communities in Syria.




Protests in Girkê Legê and Rimêlan




Students in Girkê Legê and Rimêlan also organized joint protests. The demonstrators marched to the school administration building in Rimêlan, chanting slogans demanding the right to education in Kurdish. Participants declared that education in one’s mother tongue was a fundamental, non-negotiable right. They announced that they would continue their protests as long as restrictions on Kurdish-language education remained in place.




The latest demonstrations mark a continuation of protests against the education policies of the Syrian transitional government. Since early September, students and families in various cities across Rojava and Northeast Syria have been protesting against the reduction of Kurdish-language instruction to three hours per week.

author: Άγγελος Χατζηνικολάου
title: 15 Νοεμβρίου: Πορεία υπεράσπισης του Πολυτεχνείου, της ιστορικής μνήμης και των κοινωνικών – ταξικών αγώνων
content:
15 Νοεμβρίου: Πορεία υπεράσπισης του Πολυτεχνείου, της ιστορικής μνήμης και των κοινωνικών – ταξικών αγώνων




53 χρόνια

 μετά, η εξέγερση του Νοέμβρη του 1973, καθώς και οι αγώνες και οι κατακτήσεις που αυτή ενέπνευσε για δεκαετίες, βρίσκονται στο στόχαστρο ενός ανελέητου ρεβανσισμού από την πλευρά του κράτους και της άρχουσας τάξης της χώρας.




 




53 χρόνια

 μετά, η υφιστάμενη κυβέρνηση, το κράτος και οι ακροδεξιές εφεδρείες του πολιτικού συστήματος, επιχειρούν να αντικαταστήσουν την ιστορική μνήμη του Πολυτεχνείου με έναν επικίνδυνο αναθεωρητισμό της κοινωνικής και ταξικής ιστορίας αυτού του τόπου. Μια επιχείρηση που δεν περιορίζεται μόνο στην αμφισβήτηση των ιστορικών γεγονότων, όπως την ύπαρξη των νεκρών του Πολυτεχνείου, αλλά επεκτείνεται στη συνολική επανανοηματοδότηση της εξέγερσης, στην αποκοπή της από τις κοινωνικές και πολιτικές συγκρούσεις που ακολούθησαν την αντικατάσταση του δικτατορικού καθεστώτος από την αστική κοινοβουλευτική δημοκρατία και, τελικά, στην απονεύρωση του ίδιου του πολιτικού της περιεχομένου. Στόχος είναι να αποσυνδεθεί το Πολυτεχνείο από τα αντικρατικά – αντικαπιταλιστικά του συνθήματα, αλλά και από τους κοινωνικούς αγώνες και τις διεκδικήσεις που ακολούθησαν, ώστε να απομείνει ένα ακίνδυνο ιστορικό σύμβολο, με τις παρακαταθήκες και τις επιδράσεις του στο παρόν και το μέλλον να αποψιλώνονται.




53 χρόνια

 το πολιτικό σύστημα επιχειρεί την ενσωμάτωση της εξέγερσης στην κυρίαρχη αφήγηση περί αποκατάστασης της δημοκρατίας, με την μετατροπή της σε μια θεσμική επέτειο συμφιλίωσης και εθνικής ομοψυχίας. Σύμμαχος και εγγυητής αυτής της προσπάθειας υπήρξε επί δεκαετίες η σοσιαλδημοκρατική και ένα μεγάλο μέρος της κομμουνιστικής αριστεράς, η ιστορική συνέχεια δηλαδή αυτών που τις μέρες του Νοέμβρη μιλούσαν για «εξέγερση προβοκατόρων» και προσδοκούσαν στην φιλελευθεροποίηση της χούντας και την παλινόρθωση της αστικής δημοκρατίας χωρίς την καθοριστική συμβολή του ταξικού-λαϊκού παράγοντα.




53 χρόνια

 μετά επιχειρείται ένα ακόμη πιο επιθετικό βήμα: η πολιτική και ιστορική απονομιμοποίηση της εξέγερσης του 1973. Η εξέγερση προβάλλεται ως ένα παρωχημένο γεγονός, λίγο ή πολύ ασήμαντο στην πορεία της πτώσης της χούντας των συνταγματαρχών, οι πολιτικές της προεκτάσεις αντιμετωπίζονται ως αναχρονιστικές, ενώ οι αγώνες που εμπνεύστηκαν από αυτήν επιχειρείται να αποσυσχετιστούν από την αιματοβαμμένη ιστορική τους προέλευση. Ακόμη περισσότερο, σκοπός της αστικής προπαγάνδας και των κρατικών σχεδιασμών, είναι να στιγματιστούν τα υλικά κεκτημένα που πέτυχαν οι αγώνες που ενέπνευσε η εξέγερση του Πολυτεχνείου, όπως το πανεπιστημιακό άσυλο, οι καταλήψεις στις σχολές και οι νικηφόρες διεκδικήσεις του φοιτητικού κινήματος που σήμερα διασύρονται ως μια «ελληνική εκτροπή» από το ευρωπαϊκό καπιταλιστικό υπόδειγμα. Πρόκειται για μια συστηματική απόπειρα ανατροπής της ιστορικής μνήμης, με σκοπό να πληγεί όχι μόνο η υλική και συμβολική κληρονομιά του Νοέμβρη, αλλά και η δυνατότητα των σύγχρονων κοινωνικών και ταξικών αγώνων να αντλούν από αυτόν παραδείγματα αντίστασης και συλλογικής δράσης.




53 χρόνια

 μετά το κατεχόμενο κτήριο του Πολυτεχνείου με τα σφραγισμένα αμφιθέατρα, την αστυνομοκρατία, τις κλειδαμπαρωμένες πύλες, τις κάμερες και τις απειλές για ανατροπή, ακόμη και του θεσμικού πλαισίου του τριήμερου εορτασμού «χωρίς έκτροπα» που επί χρόνια φρουρούν οι δυνάμεις της αριστεράς και του οπορτουνισμού, αποτελούν τα απότοκα της αφρενάριστης εδώ και χρόνια κινηματικής υποχώρησης που έχουμε καθήκον να ανακόψουμε. Η στρατηγική των «εγγυητών» και των «χωροφυλάκων» ενός μουσειοποιημένου πολυτεχνείου βρίσκει σήμερα το απόγειο της αποτυχίας της σε ένα αστυνομοκρατούμενο πολυτεχνείο, που σύντομα η καταστολή σκοπεύει να παραδώσει ολοσχερώς στο νέο του, που σκοπεύει να είναι και μόνιμο, αφεντικό: το μεγάλο κεφάλαιο.




53 χρόνια

 μετά, το αίμα που έχυσε η απρόκλητη επίθεση της σοσιαλδημοκρατικής γκρούπας της ΑΡΑΣ έναν χρόνο πριν, ούτε ξεχάστηκε, ούτε η εν λόγω παράταξη σταμάτησε τις δολοφονικές επιθέσεις ή τις απειλές, ενόψει και του φετινού πολυτεχνείου. Είτε με τις σφραγίδες των «φοιτητικών συλλόγων» είτε στο όνομα ενός θολού «ανταγωνιστικού κινήματος», σοσιαλδημοκράτες και οπορτουνιστές συνεχίζουν να αξιώνουν ότι θα ασκούν πολιτική με σπασμένα κεφάλια και γνάθους, αποδεικνύοντας ότι τελικά, οι ίδιοι, είναι οι πραγματικοί προβοκάτορες! Είναι αυτοί που λειτουργούν ως «εσωτερική καταστολή» μέσα στα κινήματα και των οποίων η δράση, πρώτα ενήργησε επικουρικά στην συστημική προσπάθεια απονέκρωσης του Πολυτεχνείου και εν συνεχεία, αποτελεί αρωγός, στην πλήρη παράδοση του. Είναι αυτοί, που προσπαθούν να αντλήσουν ηθική νομιμοποίηση από τα πρόσφατα γεγονότα στην πανεπιστημιούπολη για να δικαιολογήσουν ένα νέο αιματοκύλισμα, το οποίο πρώτα και κύρια, θα είναι ένα αιματοκύλισμα της ιστορικής επετείου που το κράτος έχει βάλει στο στόχαστρο.




53 χρόνια

 βρίθουν τα μορφώματα που από χρόνο σε χρόνο που διεκδικούν τα σκήπτρα που άλλοτε κρατούσαν οι προβοκατορολόγοι του ΚΚΕ και της Πανσπουδαστικής, μιλώντας περί «κατάληψης των 350 πρακτόρων της ΚΥΠ». Η εξέγερση του 1973 ως «γιορτή της δημοκρατίας» από την μία και ως πεδίο εφόρμησης των περιφρουρητών του μουσειοποιημένου Πολυτεχνείου από την άλλη, μας φέρνει πλέον ενώπιον της απειλής ενός ιστορικού αφανισμού. Γι’ αυτό και ο λόγος περνάει πλέον σε όσους διαχρονικά αντιστέκονται σε αυτή την συνθήκη, καθώς και στις νέες γενιές των αγωνιστών και των αγωνιστριών που καλούνται να υπερασπιστούν την ιστορική μνήμη και τους αγώνες που είναι αναγκαιότητα να δοθούν στο παρόν. Γι’ αυτό και όσοι αξιώνουν να υψώσουν τις σημαίες του οπορτουνισμού και της περιφρούρησης των εχθρών της εξέγερσης, θα πρέπει άμεσα να τις κατεβάσουν και να καταλάβουν ότι οποιαδήποτε από μεριάς τους εχθροπραξία εντός του πολυτεχνείου, θα τους καταχωρίσει μια για πάντα στην ιστορία των αγώνων και της ταξικής πάλης ως μακρύ χέρι των αστικών σχεδιασμών και της πολιτικής του ιστορικού αναθεωρητισμού και ρεβανσισμού προς όφελος της μεριάς των τανκς και των ΕΑΤ-ΕΣΑ.




53 χρόνια

αντιστασιακό κάστρο της οδού Πατησίων

author: mark
title: [EN, FR, DE] Call to Action: Resist Frontex’s expanding powers on December 18, 2026!
content:
[

FR

, 

DE

 below]




On 27 October 2026, the European Commission presented its proposal for a new Frontex Regulation. The proposal would massively expand Frontex’s powers, staff, budget and activities, both inside and outside the EU. At the same time, some of the already very weak Fundamental Rights safeguards would be further weakened. The proposal would expand Frontex’s surveillance of people on the move, even before they ever reach the EU’s borders, and give the agency a stronger role in surveilling social media content about people’s movement.







The new regulation would further extend the reach of the EU’s border regime, strengthening Frontex’s role in the externalisation of EU borders and consolidating its position as a key actor in organising and coordinating deportations. The agency would now be able to conduct deportations between non-EU countries and transfers to so-called “return hubs” outside the EU, where people can be detained in places they have never set foot in. Rather than addressing the violence of deportations, these plans seek to make them easier to organise and enforce. This will further expose people on the move to violence within and beyond Europe.




We refuse to accept this expansion as inevitable.




You can read more details about the new regulation proposal on this blog post: 

https://abolishfrontex.org/blog/2026/11/05/bigger-stronger-more-violent-the-eus-plans-for-frontex/




More resources and wider powers for Frontex should not be the response to the violence of the EU border regime. They will reinforce it. Action is urgently needed.




We oppose this proposal of the new regulation and call for an International Action Day on or around 18 December 2026, International Migrants Day, asking groups in all countries to participate in any way you can, organising big or small actions or integrating our demands into your existing plans. We call on the European Commission to withdraw its proposal and on the European Parliament and the Council to reject it, as a first step to abolishing the agency altogether.




There are many ways to take action: banners, posters, flyer distributions, public gatherings, speeches, art installations and demonstrations. Be creative, organise collectively, and make our resistance visible.


We will not stand idly while deportations are expanded, borders are pushed further beyond Europe, and violence against people on the move is normalised.




Please reach out to info[at]abolishfrontex.org or via Instagram (@abolishfrontex) if you would like to collaborate or are planning an action in your city, so that we can connect efforts and share your activities through our communications.




No more powers for Frontex. Freedom of movement for all. Abolish Frontex.







[FR]




Appel à action : le 18 décembre 2026 opposons-nous à une nouvelle augmentation des pouvoirs de Frontex 




Le 27 octobre 2026, la Commission européenne a présenté sa proposition concernant un nouveau règlement pour Frontex. Cette proposition prévoit une extension massive des pouvoirs de cette agence de l’Union européenne. Elle concerne notamment ses effectifs, son budget tout comme ses activités tant au sein de l’UE comme en dehors de l’UE.




Dans le même temps, certaines des garanties en matière de droits fondamentaux, déjà très réduites, seraient encore affaiblies.




La proposition étendrait la surveillance exercée par Frontex sur les personnes en migration, avant même qu’elles n’atteignent les frontières de l’UE, et conférerait à l’agence un rôle accru dans la surveillance des contenus publiés sur les réseaux sociaux concernant les mouvements de population.




Le nouveau règlement élargirait aussi la portée du régime frontalier de l’UE en renforçant le rôle de Frontex dans l’externalisation de ses frontières et en consolidant sa position d’acteur clé dans l’organisation et la coordination des expulsions. L’agence serait désormais en mesure de procéder à des expulsions entre pays non membres de l’UE et à des transferts vers des « centres de retour » “return hubs” situés en dehors de l’UE. Dans ces centres les personnes retenues pourraient être placées en détention dans des pays où elles n’ont jamais mis les pieds ! Plutôt que de s’attaquer à la violence inhérente aux expulsions, ces projets visent à faciliter leur organisation et leur mise en œuvre. Cela exposera encore davantage les personnes en migration à la violence, tant en Europe qu’au-delà.




Nous refusons fermement de considérer cette accélération comme étant quelque chose d’inévitable.




Vous trouverez plus de détails sur cette proposition de nouveau règlement dans cet article sur notre blog : https://abolishfrontex.org/blog/2026/11/05/bigger-stronger-more-violent-the-eus-plans-for-frontex/




Accorder davantage de ressources et de pouvoirs à Frontex ne peut en aucun cas représenter une réponse à la violence exercée actuellement par le régime frontalier de l’UE. Cela ne ferait que la renforcer. Il est urgent d’agir.




Nous nous opposons à cette proposition d’un nouveau règlement et appelons à une 

Journée d’action internationale le 18 décembre 2026, 

journée internationale des migrants 

https://www.un.org/fr/observances/migrants-day

,




ou aux alentours de cette date, en appelant les collectifs de tous les pays d’y participer de toutes les manières possibles. Cela peut se faire en organisant des actions à grande ou petite échelle localement ou encore en intégrant nos revendications dans leurs projets existants.




Nous revendiquons que la Commission européenne retire sa proposition et que le Parlement européen ainsi que le Conseil de l’Union européenne la rejettent, ce serait une première étape vers la suppression pure et simple de l’agence.




Il existe toute une série de manières d’agir : que ce soient des banderoles, des affiches, la distribution de tracts, l’organisation d’un rassemblement public, des discours ou prises de paroles dans des événement existants, des installations artistiques ou des manifestations. Faites preuve de créativité, organisez-vous collectivement et rendez notre résistance visible.




Nous ne pouvons rester passifs.ves face à l’intensification des expulsions, à l’extension toujours plus lointaine des politiques frontalières européennes et à la banalisation des violences infligées aux personnes en migration.




N’hésitez pas à nous informer et à nous contacter à l’adresse info@abolishfrontex.org ou via Instagram (@abolishfrontex) si vous souhaitez collaborer ou si vous prévoyez une action dans votre ville, afin que nous puissions coordonner nos efforts et relayer toutes nos actions dans nos communications.




Stop à l’augmentation des pouvoirs de Frontex. Liberté de circulation pour tous.




Abolish Frontex !







[DE]




Am 27. Oktober 2026 stellte die Europäische Kommission ihren Vorschlag für eine neue Frontex-Verordnung vor. Der Vorschlag sieht eine massive Ausweitung der Befugnisse, des Personals, des Budgets und der Tätigkeiten von Frontex vor, sowohl innerhalb als auch außerhalb der EU. Gleichzeitig würden einige der ohnehin schon sehr schwachen Schutzvorkehrungen für Grundrechte weiter geschwächt. Frontex soll Migrant*innen künftig noch umfassender überwachen können, und zwar bereits bevor sie überhaupt die EU-Außengrenzen erreichen. Außerdem soll die Agentur eine größere Rolle bei der Überwachung der sozialen Medien spielen, insbesondere Posts, die sich mit Migrationsbewegungen befassen.




Die neue Verordnung würde den Einflussbereich des EU-Grenzregimes weiter ausdehnen, die Rolle von Frontex bei der Externalisierung der EU-Grenzen stärken und die Stellung der Agentur als zentralen Akteur bei der Organisation und Koordinierung von Abschiebungen festigen. Frontex könnte künftig auch Abschiebungen zwischen Staaten außerhalb der EU sowie Deportationen in sogenannte „Rückführungszentren“ (return hubs) außerhalb der EU durchführen. Dort könnten Menschen in Ländern inhaftiert werden, in denen sie noch nie zuvor gewesen sind. Anstatt die Gewalt von Abschiebungen zu bekämpfen, zielen diese Pläne darauf ab, Abschiebungen leichter organisieren und durchsetzen zu können. Dadurch werden Migrant*innen innerhalb und außerhalb Europas noch stärker Gewalt ausgesetzt.




Wir weigern uns, diese Ausweitung als unausweichlich hinzunehmen.




Mehr über den neuen Verordnungsvorschlag erfahrt ihr in unserem Blogbeitrag: 

https://abolishfrontex.org/blog/2026/11/05/bigger-stronger-more-violent-the-eus-plans-for-frontex/




Mehr Geld und weitreichendere Befugnisse für Frontex dürfen nicht die Antwort auf die Gewalt des EU-Grenzregimes sein. Sie werden diese Gewalt nur weiter verstärken. Es besteht dringender Handlungsbedarf.




Wir lehnen den Vorschlag für die neue Verordnung ab und rufen zu einem 

internationalen Aktionstag am oder um den 18. Dezember 2026, den Internationalen Tag der Migrant*innen,

 auf. Wir rufen Gruppen in allen Ländern dazu auf, sich auf jede erdenkliche Weise zu beteiligen: Organisiert größere oder kleinere Aktionen oder greift unsere Forderungen bei euren bereits geplanten Aktivitäten auf. Wir fordern die Europäische Kommission auf, ihren Vorschlag zurückzuziehen, und das Europäische Parlament und den Rat, ihn abzulehnen – als ersten Schritt hin zur vollständigen Abschaffung der Agentur.




Es gibt viele Möglichkeiten, aktiv zu werden: Transparente, Plakate, Flugblattaktionen, öffentliche Kundgebungen, Redebeiträge, Kunstaktionen und Demonstrationen. Seid kreativ, schließt euch zusammen und macht unseren Widerstand sichtbar.




Wir werden nicht tatenlos zusehen, wie Abschiebungen ausgeweitet, Grenzen immer weiter über Europa hinaus verlagert und Gewalt gegen Menschen auf der Flucht und in Bewegung zur Normalität wird.




Wenn ihr mit uns zusammenarbeiten möchtet oder eine Aktion in eurer Stadt plant, meldet euch bitte unter info[at]abolishfrontex.org oder über Instagram (@abolishfrontex). So können wir uns vernetzen, unsere Aktionen aufeinander abstimmen und über eure Aktivitäten berichten.




Keine weiteren Befugnisse für Frontex. Bewegungsfreiheit für alle. Frontex abschaffen.

author: Chris Walker
title: Outgoing GOP Texas Lt. Gov. Wants to Limit His Democratic Successor’s Powers
content:
Texas Republicans could convene a special session, voting to limit Democrats’ executive powers before they are sworn in.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Texas Republican Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick has called for GOP lawmakers in the state legislature to pass new limits on his Democratic successor, Lt. Gov.-elect Vikki Goodwin, who won in the state’s “blue wave” last week.

Patrick issued the call to alter the powers of his own office during an appearance on a conservative radio show on Monday.

The office of lieutenant governor has far more powers in Texas than it does in other states. Amending such powers would impose significant limitations on the incoming Democratic-controlled executive branch.

“I support the Republicans standing up for their voters,” Patrick said in his call to limit Goodwin’s future powers, adding that Republicans should make the changes to “protect the conservative majority.”

Patrick’s remarks disregard that Texas voters overwhelmingly rejected the GOP’s agenda in the midterm elections. Democratic candidate for governor Gina Hinojosa, for example, ousted incumbent Republican Gov. Greg Abbott by more than seven points in last week’s elections. Meanwhile, Goodwin won her race by over six points, and Democrats also won control of the state House of Representatives.

Yet, because Republicans retained control of the state Senate, any changes state lawmakers make to the powers of the office of lieutenant governor during the interim period would be difficult to undo once Democrats assume office. Indeed, Democratic lawmakers would likely have to pursue a lawsuit to challenge any such changes, which would put the matter into the hands of the state’s still conservative judicial system.

Texas Republican lawmakers indicated they were considering changes to the governor’s and lieutenant governor’s powers shortly after Hinojosa’s and Goodwin’s victories.

“We still have total power in Texas, and we must act like it by using the remaining ten weeks to restore separation of powers and limit the emergency powers that Governor-Elect Hinojosa is set to inherit,” read a social media post from state Rep. Brian Harrison (R), who called on Abbott to convene a special session of the legislature to implement the changes.

Hinojosa warned against lawmakers taking such actions.

“The people of Texas have spoken,” she said in response to the proposed plan.

Goodwin similarly argued against Republicans stripping her and the governor-elect of their executive branch powers, stating that they would be doing so “at their peril because we will have elections again in 2028.”

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $50,000 in the next 9 days. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.

author: groundxero
title: 544 Scientists and Researchers Stand with Siang Valley Anti-Dam Movement; Demand Halt to Mega Project and Release of Detained Activists
content:
“We stand with the people of the Siang Valley in their struggle to protect their river, their lands, their rights and the ability to determine their future. We recognise that the people who call this valley home must have the primary say in determining its future.”




 




Groundxero

 Desk




 




In a strong show of solidarity with the indigenous Adi communities resisting the proposed 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh, a group of 544 scientists, researchers, and concerned citizens working in the fields of nature, wildlife, society and the environment has called on the Union and state governments to immediately halt all pre-feasibility activities, withdraw additional security forces from the valley and release anti-dam protesters detained and arrested under the stringent Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA).




 




The statement, issued on November 9, 2026, comes amid growing resistance in the Siang Valley to the proposed mega-dam and reports of intensified security deployment, restrictions on people’s movement, arrests and the use of force against protesters.




 




The signatories, many of whom have worked in Arunachal Pradesh and the Eastern Himalayas, describe the Siang Valley as an ecologically irreplaceable landscape of immense biodiversity, cultural significance and traditional knowledge. Referring to an earlier statement by 114 scientists issued on June 9, 2025, they point out that 48 new species and 140 new distribution records have been documented in the valley in the past 15 years alone.




 




The statement warns that large-scale construction in an ecologically fragile and highly seismically active river system could have irreversible consequences. It emphasises that the Siang River, its forests and surrounding mountains sustain not only rich biodiversity but also the livelihoods, cultural identity and traditional knowledge systems of indigenous Adi communities.




 




The scientists express particular concern over the Arunachal Pradesh government’s continued efforts to push ahead with the project’s Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) despite sustained opposition from affected communities. They condemned the militarisation of this otherwise peaceful region, restrictions on movement, arrests and detentions of local anti-dam activists, and the use of tear gas and force against protesters. They also denounce the alleged harassment and intimidation of lawyers, journalists and others standing in solidarity of the movement.




 




Invoking the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), the signatories assert that the project must not proceed without the free, prior and informed consent of the affected indigenous communities, whose lands, livelihoods, cultural heritage and relationship with the Siang are at stake. They also stressed on the constitutional guarantees of freedom of speech, expression and peaceful assembly.




 




The statement calls on the Arunachal Pradesh and Union governments to stop all PFR-related activities, withdraw additional armed forces from the region, release those detained for participating in the movement, and initiate an open and meaningful dialogue with the affected communities.




 




The signatories affirm that the people who have protected and sustained the Siang Valley for generations must have the primary say in determining its future.




 




The full statement along with the list of signatories is published below:




 




November 9, 2026




 




We, a group of scientists, researchers, conservation practitioners and concerned citizens, many of whom have worked in Arunachal Pradesh and in the Eastern Himalaya, stand in unequivocal solidarity with the people of the Siang Valley in their opposition to the proposed 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP).




 




The Siang Valley is not merely a site for a proposed mega-infrastructure project. The Siang River, its forests and the surrounding mountains sustain extraordinary biodiversity, livelihoods, traditional knowledge systems and the cultural identity of indigenous Adi communities.




 




A statement issued by a collective of 114 scientists on 9th of June 2025, noted that the Siang is a rich living landscape of immense ecological, cultural and biological significance. In the past 15 years alone, there have been 48 new species described, as well as 140 new distribution records from the valley.




 




As scientists, researchers and citizens working in the fields of nature, wildlife, society and the environment, we recognise that the Siang Valley is an ecologically irreplaceable landscape, and much of its biodiversity and ecological complexity remains poorly understood.




 




The irreversible consequences of largescale interventions in such a fragile, extremely seismically active and biodiverse river system demand the utmost caution.




 




The people of the Siang valley have nurtured and protected these landscapes and species for generations. Their knowledge, lived experiences and concerns must be central to any decisions about their future.




 




We are deeply concerned by the Arunachal Pradesh government’s continued push to undertake the Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) for SUMP despite sustained opposition from affected communities. We are particularly saddened and alarmed by the deployment of large numbers of armed security personnel, restrictions on people’s movement, the arrest and detention of community members, and the use of tear gas and force against citizens.




 




The growing militarisation of this otherwise peaceful region is deeply disturbing and unacceptable. In a democratic country, communities have every right to question, oppose and refuse projects that they believe threaten their lands, cultures, livelihoods and futures. In keeping with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), the project must not proceed without the free, prior and informed consent (FPIC) of the affected indigenous communities, whose lands, livelihoods, cultural heritage and relationship with the Siang are at stake.




 




We also strongly condemn the harassment and intimidation of those supporting and documenting the events and the movement, including lawyers and journalists. Article 19 of the Constitution of India guarantees six fundamental freedoms, including the freedom of speech, expression and to assemble peacefully; the restrictions imposed by the state cannot be deemed as reasonable.




 




We therefore urge the Arunachal Pradesh and Union Governments to halt all PFR-related activities, withdraw the additional armed forces deployed in the region, release those detained for their participation in the movement, and engage in an open, transparent and meaningful dialogue with the affected communities, respecting their rights, agency and decisions.




 




Beyond ecological arguments, our work has taught us that protecting nature cannot be separated from respecting the people who have lived with, cared for and sustained these landscapes over generations.




 




We stand with the people of the Siang Valley in their struggle to protect their river, their lands, their rights and the ability to determine their future. We recognise that the people who call this valley home must have the primary say in determining its future.
