Given that we live in a society that promotes ignorance and superficiality, perhaps it shouldn’t be all that surprising that current day anarchist discussions of historic inter-anarchist debates usually miss the point when it comes to colonialism (and imperialism more generally.)

Anarchists do not somehow become immune to colonial society’s influence simply by making abstract and hollow declarations of opinion. Knowledge and comprehension require actual commitment and curiosity, and these are sadly rare qualities among the European, Euro-American and Euro-Canadian anarchists of today.

This article is an attempt at a brief analysis of what’s been missing in recent anarchist discussions of three historic inter-anarchist debates. The term “debates” is used here in the widest sense of a general disagreement rather than some formally-held event or correspondence. Specifically, I refer to the debates between Luigi Galleani and Ricardo Flores Magón over the Mexican Revolution, between Peter Kropotkin and Errico Malatesta on the First World War, and between Emma Goldman and Reginald Reynolds on Palestine.

In the case of Reynolds, we should note that he considered himself a fellow traveler and sympathizer of anarchism, wrote regularly for the anarchist periodicals edited by Vernon Richards, and married the socialist-turned-anarchist Ethel Mannin, but did not self-identify as an anarchist, so my phrase “inter-anarchist debate” must also be understood in the broadest sense.

The anarchist periodical Tinderbox and the anarchist website The Transmetropolitan Review (TTR) have recently invoked the Galleani-Magón debate, though without even being aware of it in the former case.

The individual who writes articles at the TTR website claimed in May of this year that the historic anarchist Partido Liberal Mexicano (PLM) made a “fateful alliance with Pascual Orozco,” the latter being a bourgeois revolutionary who, with the help of Pancho Villa, took control of Ciudad Juárez in 1911. The author makes no distinction between the on-the-ground forces of the PLM and the Junta (leadership board) of that organization, which, from Los Angeles obviously could not directly control the actions of every individual on the frontlines in Mexico, even if they had wanted to.

TTR goes on to sell the lie that at the time, “the PLM was willing to work with anyone against Madero, and they took positions in Orozco’s rebel government alongside oligarchs and hacienda owners, something which further isolated the PLM from anarchists.”

In reality, Magón and the rest of the Junta, in their periodical, Regeneración, called for violent resistance to Orozco once he took control of Juárez, denouncing him as bourgeois and openly accusing him of being on the wrong side of the revolution, specifically because he was trying to disarm other revolutionaries and was friendly with the rich.

To be clear where TTR wasn’t, the anarchists they claim the PLM isolated themselves from are specifically the Italian-American anarchists associated with the periodical, Cronaca Sovversiva (Subversive Chronicle), edited by Galleani.

TTR seems to forget for a moment that the PLM, or at least its Junta, were anarchists too, so they technically could not become isolated from themselves as individual anarchists even if they could become isolated from Italian-American anarchists. In reality, it was the Italian-American anarchists who chose to isolate themselves from the Mexican anarchists and the social revolution in Mexico as a whole, because the Italian-Americans were racist and ignorant regarding the dynamics of social revolution, particularly Indigenous, peasant and rural revolution.

Some of the Italian-Americans had traveled to Mexico to take part in the revolution but then returned home to slander it in the pages of Galleani’s periodical, much to his approval. TTR, with their false claims about bourgeois collaboration, soft-pedals the racism that the Italian-American anarchists used to justify their opposition to the PLM and their denigration of the Mexican Revolution in general. It can’t be that TTR is merely unaware of this racism, because they have already specifically mentioned it earlier in their article.

The author openly admits that in the pages of Cronaca Sovversiva, “month by month, the language grew more insulting and venomous, as well as racist.”

TTR even discuses a racist quote from Galleani, but fails to mention that this quote had already been discussed by historian Kenyon Zimmer in his 2015 book, Immigrants Against the State. Galleani, in his periodical, had preposterously claimed that a less industrial country like Mexico, populated primarily by Indigenous peoples, mestizos and Black people (of various ancestries), was less likely to engage in a social revolutionary movement than a more industrial country populated primarily by white people.

TTR, furthermore, falsely claims that “the involvement of Italian anarchists in the Mexican Revolution of 1910 is a moment in history that remains obscure not just to contemporary anarchists, but also to academic historians.” This is ironic given that TTR rarely provides citations or references for any academic (or otherwise) documentation that they draw from, and several academics have in fact written something, in various languages, about the Galleani-Magón debate, for example Zimmer, as just mentioned.

Magón’s periodical, along with other prominent anarchist periodicals of the era besides Cronaca Sovversiva, also carried the debate, so modern day anarchists have no one but themselves, their monolingualism and their lack of curiosity (or sincerity) to blame for their own lack of knowledge of anarchist history.

Prominent anarchists such as Peter Kropotkin and Voltairine De Cleyre, as well as a few Italian-American anarchists not associated with Galleani, strongly and publicly took the side of the PLM Junta, but TTR never mentions it, content to merely do their own (racist) smear campaign against the Junta, much as the Italian-American anarchists centered around Galleani’s periodical did back in the day.

Magón, in an April of 1912 issue of Regeneración, even referred to Galleani by name as being among “our enemies,” due to his part in the “smear campaign” against Mexican revolutionaries, including anarchists. But you would not have any clue about this if you were curiosity-impoverished enough to have TTR as your only source.

Aside from TTR, an anonymous contributor to the offline anarchist combat-fetishist periodical, Tinderbox, also invoked the Cronaca Sovversiva and Regeneración anarchists in an article titled History Drowned in Lethe published in the Spring of 2026 issue.

This article carries even greater irony than the writing of TTR, given that the Tinderbox contributor complains that today’s anarchists don’t reference anarchist history enough, particularly the history of the anarchists of Cronaca Sovversiva. Instead, or so we’re told, anarchists too often reference statist (or at least non-anarchist) revolutionaries in places like Rojava or Chiapas.

The author even lumps together specific organizations such as the modern Zapatistas and the defunct marxist Quebec Liberation Front with “anti-colonial struggles” as such, over-generalizing that “the relevance of these experiences to an anarchist revolutionary project is tenuous.”

An Indigenous anarchist might be surprised to discover from such an enlightened settler that their own struggle against colonialism has nothing to offer their own anarchist struggle for freedom, or vice versa, but this is of no concern to the charlatan historian who wrote the article. In fact, as we complete our reading of their article, we discover that the history of anarchism in Mexico is only worth the mere mention of some anarchists having existed there during the era of the (racist) Italian-Americans.

We find no mention of the fact that some of the anarchists in Mexico were Indigenous, or of the fact that the PLM Junta embraced the anti-colonial struggle of the Yaqui and other peoples, these being struggles that the Tinderbox writer has just told us only have a “tenuous” relation to “an anarchist revolutionary project.”

It appears that it is not so much the anarchist revolutionary project in general that the Tinderbox writer is concerned with but more so the specifically racist, white, colonialist, American anarchist project, Mexicans and Indigenous peoples within Mexico be damned, whether anarchist or not. Since the Galleani-Magón debate isn’t even mentioned, the writer obviously can’t address the racism behind it, nor the general misunderstanding of the dynamics of peasant social revolution that Kropotkin chastised the Italian-Americans of being ignorant of as well.

The Tinderbox author asks us if the revolutionary Spain of the 1930s is “really the only experience of anarchists that could nourish our imaginations,” neglecting to consider, of course, that the situation there also directly involved colonialism, specifically the colonization (and potential decolonization) of Morocco, the military conquest of which had already caused an uprising within Spain itself back in 1909.

A few North African anarchists or fellow travelers even joined the anarchist militias during the Spanish Civil War. But pay no mind. The Tinderbox writer laments a blinkered outlook on the part of others while they themself just represent more of the same.

The author even lumps together the American anarchist periodical, Man!, with the Italian-American anarchists, specifically their periodical, L’Adunata dei Refrattari, without mentioning the fact that the editor of Man!, the Romanian-born Jewish-American anarchist, Marcus Graham, specifically addressed colonialism and anti-colonialism, for example in Palestine and Ethiopia. These are precisely the anti-colonial resistance movements that the Tinderbox writer has just told us are probably irrelevant to anarchism. Meaning that Man! should have been castigated instead of included within the pantheon of acceptability.

The American-centric Tinderbox author also makes no mention of the fact that Graham contributed, during and after the Second World War, to the British anti-colonialist anarchist periodicals, War Commentary and Freedom. For the author, print anarchism only reappears on Earth with the anarchist turn taken by the writers at Fifth Estate in Michigan in the mid-1970s.

The author shows no sign of awareness that veteran Spanish-Canadian and Italian-Canadian anarchists, Federico Arcos and Attilio Bortolotti were just across the river in Windsor, and were visiting Michigan, eventually influencing the anarchists and fellow travelers there such as Fredy Perlman, who certainly can’t be accused of thinking that the relation between Indigenous peoples and the struggle against the State is merely tenuous.

Why go to all the effort of complaining about other anarchists drowning history in the fictional river Lethe when you yourself are busy drowning it in the real life rivers Detroit, Thames, Sacramento, Ebro and Rio Grande, all the while hoping that nobody hears the screams? Hopefully the Tinderbox contributor is just arrogantly ignorant and not a compulsive liar like The Transmetropolitan Review writer seems to be.

Thankfully, at least one former Tinderbox collective member subsequently wrote and posted online a modest article titled Goodnight Eurocentric Pride, responding to Tinderbox’s trash.

But unfortunately, that response provoked a response of its own, this time by a real space cadet going by the pseudonym Star Gazer, who was more than happy to ramble on at length while spreading disinformation, and again, completely ignoring the Galleani-Magón debate, the racism behind it, and, for the most part, colonialism in general.

Lest we think that they were merely racist, the space cadet also reveals themselves as sexist and ageist when they bizarrely and callously choose to exploit the subject of sex tourism in South East Asia as the bleach with which to white-wash American imperialism.

The space cadet’s argument amounts to a truly gymnastic attempt to render equivalent two distinct categories, specifically, the individual American sex tourist and the opponent of American imperialism, as if American sex tourism in South East Asia wasn’t itself an aspect of American imperialism.

Settler-imperialist anxiety can truly twist the mind, along with one’s tactical choice of argumentation. Everything the settler projects onto others they already feel guilty of themselves, whether they or their ancestors are the actual perpetrator.

The next debate, the argument between Peter Kropotkin and Errico Malatesta about the First World War, I have already addressed at length in my previous article, Anarchism and Revolutionary Defeatism. However, it’s worth noting that the debate was brought up again recently in the September of 2026 book, Constitutionalising Anarchism, by Ruth Kinna and Alex Prichard, as well as on an episode of the podcast, It Could Happen Here, released that same month. Anti-colonialism, as a crucial point of the debate, again gets the short end of the stick.

Kinna and Prichard in their new book essentially reiterate Kinna’s spurious argument from one of her previous books, 2016’s Kropotkin: Reviewing the Classical Anarchist Tradition, where she argued that “Kropotkin’s position was consistent with his conception of anarchism and he defended it in these terms,” that position being one in favor of the side of the Allies, the colonial powers of France, Belgium, Britain, Russia, Japan and later Italy, as they fought against their fellow colonial powers, Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire (not to mention Bulgaria.)

Kinna in her 2016 book, incredibly, even defends Kropoktin’s support for the Allies, all of them colonizers, by appealing to his long history of support for national liberation. Kropotkin himself was well aware that the Allies had colonies in Africa, Asia, the Pacific, and the Americas. He simply engaged in a rhetorical strategy of avoiding the matter once the war began.

Kropotkin, like Joseph Stalin after him, wanted a popular front. The colonized of the Global South would have to take a backseat to Belgian and French citizens, or a place on the front lines in the French Army of Africa, where they would be treated as second class humans at best, or cannon fodder at worst. French military recruitment even sparked several rebellions within Africa, but this is of no apparent concern to Kropotkin, or Kinna for that matter.

Kinna, with a century of hindsight in her favor, when discussing Kropotkin’s stance appears as unaware that colonialism took place on other continents and that the peoples of the colonies were deserving of liberation from European powers like France, regardless of Kropotkin’s prioritization of France and the other Allies in the heat of the moment.

“Facing up to the French failure to implement the revolutionary plan hatched in 1792, in 1914 Kropotkin held fast to the principle of national defence against oppression,” Kinna claims, failing to ask how the people of the Congo could be defended from Belgium, or how the people of Senegal could be defended from France if Kropotkin was busy urging support for the very powers that were colonizing them.

For Kropotkin, opposing Germany trumped all other concerns, at least during the war. According to Kinna, Kropotkin was right that Germany was colonizing France. But wasn’t France colonizing Africa, Asia, the Pacific and the Caribbean? Kropotkin and Kinna have no answer, at least none they want to openly declare.

Kinna, naturally, doesn’t so much as bother mentioning that opposition to the Allies’ colonialism factored into the stance that other anarchists such as Errico Malatesta, Emma Goldman and Lilian Wolfe took against Kropotkin’s euro-centric position.

Kinna references Malatesta’s article, Anarchists Have Forgotten Their Principles, but conveniently neglects to mention his specific references to the French colonization of Morocco and the Belgian colonization of the Congo, nor does she mention that Kropotkin offered no counter-argument to Malatesta on that front.

In 2026’s Constitutionalising Anarchism, Kinna and Prichard absurdly claim that “contrary to Goldman’s assertion, Kropotkin’s endorsement of the Entente’s [the Allies’] fight was an expression of a consistent antiwar stance.”

“Confusingly, Kropotkin’s support for the Entente in 1914 sprang from his conception of a martial morality,” or so we’re meant to believe, as if Africans and Asians don’t count as moral subjects.

“The war,” for Kropotkin, “was a struggle between life-affirming and life-sapping regimes” Kinna and Prichard tell us, and apparently we’re supposed to think he was right about this, even if we are among the life-sapped due to being the subjects of French, Belgian, British, Russian, Japanese or Italian colonialism.

The fact that the war didn’t end war or colonialism; that fascism and another World War followed; that Palestine still suffers today as a result of British, Soviet, American and Zionist imperialism; and that Kanaky still struggles today against French colonialism, more than century later, is all of no great importance. Defending Kropotkin’s honor, no matter the human cost, is made the primary objective.

In the topsy-turvy world of the academic, colonial empires can fight for national liberation. Support for war can be anti-war. But in the real world, this is far from the case, and the rest of us have to suffer for it.

Turning now to the recent episode of It Could Happen Here on the anarchist split over the Great War, host Andrew (of YouTube’s Andrewism fame) begins by explaining that Malatesta and Kropotkin, as well as other anarchists, “clashed intellectually over the nature of war, history, national struggle, and revolutionary change,” but Andrew also offers basically no discussion of Malatesta’s specifically anti-colonial reasoning for opposing Kropotkin’s stance on the war.

We are at least informed that the “First World War emerged from decades of imperial rivalry, colonial competition, military expansion, and competing alliance systems among Europe’s great powers.”

We are told that Malatesta wrote, contra Kropotkin that “the only war worth fighting was one of liberation, and there was no siding with national agglomerations.”

However, this could possibly lead to a misunderstanding, because Malatesta explicitly favored wars of national liberation, for example the war waged by Libyans against their Italian colonial rulers. What Malatesta opposed was wars between and among nation-states, or between and among imperialist states.

He did not oppose nations as such. After all, “nation” and “national” are not exclusively synonyms for the nation-state, or for the imperialist state for that matter. The word “nation” can also be a synonym for an oppressed people such as the Libyans, the Palestinians or the Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

Andrew at least, unlike Kinna, reads aloud the quote about Belgian colonialism in the Congo (and other incidences) from Malatesta’s Anarchists Have Forgotten Their Principles. But again, Andrew provides no commentary on it’s significance to the debate.

Andrew then brings up Kropotkin’s support for “national liberation struggles,” as if this was a point of contrast with Malatesta. The real difference, in the case of the Great War, was that Kropotkin was pretending to forget about Africa and the other continents brutalized by the colonial powers that he was busy rallying behind.

In Kropotkin’s opinion, anti-militarists advocating a general strike within a “targeted” nation were “siding with the invaders and making social revolution more difficult to carry out in the future,” Andrew explains to us.

“This is, for me,” Andrew says, “a somewhat compelling argument.”

“I feel this way about current struggle,” Andrew explains, going on to add that “while the worker has no friend in the states of the world, and I don’t think it should be framed as a matter of campism, the way we see running rampant today, it is undeniable that there are some victories and defeats that will be more or less preferable to the viability of the struggle long term.”

This, however, appears as absurd when we have knowledge of the fact that Malatesta did not disagree on that point, he only disagreed with Kropotkin regarding colonialism and militarism!

He even said as much in a response to none other than Benito Mussolini, as I discussed in my Anarchism and Revolutionary Defeatism article, and as Davide Turcato had already discussed before me in the book, Anarchism: 1914–1918, Internationalism, Anti-Militarism and War, edited by Ruth Kinna and Matthew. S Adams.

Malatesta admitted to Mussolini that he hoped particularly for a German defeat. But under no conditions would he advocate for collaboration with the Allies in order to help make it happen. Participation in the war effort would be more harmful than the benefit of a German defeat.

Andrew declares, “I am rooting against an Israeli victory anywhere,” as if Malatesta would have disagreed but Kropotkin would have concurred. The point is precisely that Kropotkin was the one who brushed aside the matter of colonialism in World War I, not Malatesta or his comrades.

Andrew states that they think Kropotkin “mischaracterized the anarchist position, or perhaps did not give them enough credit,” but it’s far from clear what Andrew means by this, given the lack of discussion of the anti-colonial aspect of Malatesta’s position.

“I share Malatesta’s criticism of the pitfalls of lesser evilism as he kinda predicted World War II,” Andrew says.

I would add that this was not just a case of “kinda,” but one of being basically correct for most intents and purposes. Malatesta wrote in Anarchists Have Forgotten Their Principles that, “after a long war, an enormous loss of life and wealth, both sides being exhausted, some kind of peace will be patched up, leaving all questions open, thus preparing for a new war more murderous than the present.”

Andrew also presents us with this very quote, by way of Matthew S. Adams’ quotation of Malatesta, rather than directly from the man himself, whose article has been freely available online for about two decades at this point, at the very least.

Andrew then quotes from the 1915 International Anarchist Anti-War Manifesto which Malatesta, Goldman and Wolfe signed, among others. That manifesto specifically drew attention to French and British colonial conquests in various parts of the Global South. But Andrew reduces this to a matter of Malatesta rejecting the argument of “the lesser evil.”

Malatesta certainly did reject that argument, but what he also rejected was the idea that colonialist-imperialist states could engage in a national liberation struggle and at the same time hold onto their colonies.

Andrew even says that they get “where Kropotkin is coming from too, as I see parallels to the situation today vis-a-vis American imperialism and the flawed actors that resist it,” as if Malatesta was a tankie or campist, and as if Kropotkin had a leg rather than a colonial subject’s throat to stand on.

Andrew explains that they “generally share Malatesta’s sentiment,” but also think that “there’s room for a more sympathetic appraisal of Kropotkin’s position.”

If there really is some middle ground between just freeing the colonies and making your colonial subjects fight for you in a war against fellow colonial powers, I’m not sure I even want to hear it. It would probably sound too much like postmodern garbage to these elderly ears of mine, and I don’t want my fellow colonized subjects’ calls for solidarity to be drowned out by a bunch of noise about poor little France and Belgium and how their loot got stolen by fellow thieves.

“It’s easy, I think, to reduce this story to Kropotkin standing alone, betraying anarchism,” Andrew claims, but I’d add that just because something’s easy doesn’t mean it’s wrong, and in fact, I’d say it really should be easy to oppose colonialism rather than support colonial powers when they’re invaded by a peer.

But I’m just a Native, what do I know? I suppose that when I’m told to line up and fight for my colonizer my question should be “how soon can I enlist” rather than “when are you gonna end your invasion of my country?”

Or else maybe I should spout some kind of waffling nonsense about how both sides of the argument for and against colonialism have a point.

Finally, we come to the 1930s Goldman-Reynolds debate on Palestine, which Anthony Zurbrugg brought up in an article published on the Anarchist Studies blog in March of 2024. This debate was only natural to resurrect in the context of the escalation of the war on Palestine that Israel launched in late 2023, and thankfully Zurbrugg’s discussion of it is less jarring than the aforementioned cases.

Zurbrugg first sketches out, though not comprehensively, various historical anarchist responses to Zionism, before honing in on the Goldman-Reynolds debate that was published in the anarchist periodical Spain and the World, edited by Vernon Richards and supported by Lilian Wolfe. Zurbrugg starts out on the wrong foot by mis-attributing editorship of the periodical to Goldman, but we can perhaps hand-wave this away as a simple mistake and lack of attention to detail.

The meat of the matter is the actual argument over Palestine and its colonization by British and Zionist forces. However, Zurbrugg partly misses the point.

Zurbrugg somehow even claims that Goldman “distinguished between Zionism which she opposed, and the rights of Jewish working people.”

However, this is difficult to believe if you actually read Goldman’s article, including the quote that Zurbrugg themself provides, where Goldman claims that the “land should belong to those who till the soil,” and that Jewish immigrants had “reclaimed wastelands and have turned them into fertile fields and blooming gardens.” This statement stands out as an early example of what’s now known as Zionist hasbara (explaining), in other words, settler colonialist propaganda, in this case building upon the colonialist theory of John Locke.

Zurbrugg describes Goldman’s response to Reynolds as merely naïve, adding that “the willingness of Jewish kibbutz members to do manual labour did not, of itself, imply a commitment to broad radical change,” and that “such tropes concealed facts: people lived on these so-called ‘wastelands’ before new settlers came in, these were not ‘empty’ lands; also, it did not follow that because settlers were making ‘wasteland’ more productive that their interests should prevail.”

Zurbrugg continues, explaining that “non-Jews were not routinely asked to join the kibbutz; they were unwelcome,” and adding that “there was little or no solidarity in joint occupation and cultivation of land by Arabs and Jews together.”

All of this is good to point out, but we are left longing for a stronger condemnation of Goldman’s reactionary Zionist response to Reynolds, all the more so since she herself frames it as anti-Zionism.

Zurbrugg does not directly discuss Goldman’s spurious accusation that Reynolds was merely opposed to Jewish immigration to Palestine, but does quote from Reynold’s response to Goldman, where he wrote, “the prime question is not whether I approve of Jewish immigration, but who shall decide on its extent,” with Reynolds adding that “at present, it is determined by a foreign government – our own [Britain] — whose decisions are enforced upon an unwilling population at the point of the bayonet.”

Reynolds correctly identifies British imperialism and its Zionist sub-contractor as the primary contradiction when it comes to Palestine in the inter-war period. Goldman, however, has attempted to apply the magician’s trick of misdirection. Zurbrugg has no commentary of their own on Reynolds’ anti-imperialist and anti-colonialist challenge, and Goldman’s failure to meet it. Zurbrugg even neglects to quote from Reynold’s specific rejection of Goldman’s Zionist and Lockean argument.

Reynolds writes, “as to the statement that ‘the land should belong to those who till the soil,’ I neither accept it nor see its relevance to Emma Goldman’s case” adding that “ideally speaking, the land should ‘belong’ in my opinion, to the whole community — since all wealth comes out of it.”

Reynolds continues, asserting that “if I accept Emma’s statement, then the land in Palestine should have belonged to the Arab peasant; and the Arab landlords had no right to sell it to Jewish immigrants who dispossessed these Arab tenants.”

“That is the only sense I can make out of Emma’s statement, unless she means that the land belongs to whoever can grab it — i.e. that it belonged first to the Arab fellaheen but now belongs to those who pushed the Arab off,” Reynolds writes, adding that “’finding is keeping’ is a good motto for conquistadores and imperialists, but not, I should have thought, for Anarchists.”

Goldman never responded to Reynold’s clear-eyed take-down of her colonialist argument, and Zurbrugg doesn’t even mention this fact, deflating any sense of the decisiveness of Reynold’s critique and its relevance to our present day.

Zurbrugg also makes no mention of the highly problematic Zionism of later anarchists such as Murray Bookchin and Sam Dolgoff, who explicitly defended the Israeli state in the 1980s, even while it was busy terrorizing Lebanon as well as Palestine. Western imperialism and its sponsorship of Israeli settler colonialism is not a factor of importance in Zurbrugg’s framing, let alone the most crucial factor.

Zurbrugg does at least mention Jewish-British anarchist Albert Meltzer’s important early article on Palestine that was published in Spain and the World’s successor, Revolt! in 1939. But even here we are provided only with Meltzer’s initial condemnation of “colonisation” (this being a direct quote from Meltzer, not a use of scare quotes) and his hopes for the “co-operation of the Arab revolutionaries throughout the Near East” with the “anti-Zionist Jewish minority.”

The crucial conclusion of Meltzer’s article is left out, that being his argument that “the struggle must be against Imperialism first, against Zionism secondly, and lastly against the bourgeois nationalist government when created,” an order of business that many present day Euro/American anarchists would sneeze at rather than embrace.

For the campist Euro/American anarchist, a Palestinian resistance organization or the Iranian government are the equivalents of the American government, just another expression of Power like any other, and American citizens have no responsibility for the history and present of Western imperialism in South West Asia, or for the conditions that such imperialism has created or exacerbated, conditions that potentially contribute to the use of authoritarian methods of organization by the resistance.

The fact that America supports imperialist and warmongering dictatorships in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates while decrying the (supposedly) same thing in Iran is of no importance to the Euro/American campist anarchist. People in Iran or Yemen have no right of resistance to Western imperialism because they come from authoritarian cultures and live under authoritarian regimes, unlike the enlightened anarchist of the West, who, not noticing the contradiction, supports a camp that includes Gulf monarchs and Israeli politicians, because the Ukrainian state needs all the weapons it can get.

In reality, Europeans and Americans must take some measure of responsibility and oppose the imperialism of their own states, even if that imperialism militarily benefits the war effort of a state they are soft on, such as Ukraine.

As Malatesta argued in his 1914 article, Our Foreign Policy, “for an anarchist, the primary enemy is the oppressor who is closest to him, and against whom he can fight more effectively.”

In North America, we are raised by colonialist-imperialist society to think that the main bad guy is whatever Global South country our masters declare to be the enemy of the week. Surely, as anti-authoritarians, we can do better than merely riding our master’s coat tails off to war.

title: Li Îzmîrê di kargehê de teqîn pêk hat: Bi kêmanî 17 karker mirin
content:
Di teqîna li Kargeha Hesin û Polayê ya HABAŞê ya navçeya Aliagaya Îzmîrê de û di şewata ku pişt re derket de, herî kêm 17 karker mirin, 1 jê giran 12 karker jî birîndar bûn.




Waliyê Îzmîrê daxuyand ku li gorî daneyên destpêkê di dema rijandina polayê şil de vînca ku bi tavanê ve mixkirî  ketiye ser ocaqê arkê û teqîn çêbûye. Kargehê jî daxuyaniyek da û got: "Di dema xebatên lênerînê yên plankirî de ku yek ji ocaqên arkê yên elektrîkê dihat kontrolkirin, qezayeke xemgîn qewimî."







#SONDAKİKA İzmir’in Aliağa ilçesinde bulunan bir demir çelik fabrikasında patlama meydana geldi. Patlamanın nedeni ve olayın detayları henüz netlik kazanmadı. https://t.co/pUzfJva2CQ


— İZMİR’İN NABZI (@izmirinnabzi) 

November 9, 2026




17 karker mirin




Walîtiya Îzmîrê di daxuyaniya xwe ya destpêkê de diyar kir ku teqîn di saet 12.00î de çêbûye, herî kêm sê kesan jiyana xwe ji dest dane û 14 kes jî birîndar bûne ku sê ji wan giran in. Walîtiyê her wiha da zanîn ku xebat ji bo rizgarkirina 10 kesên di bin xirbeyan de mane berdewam dikin.




Walîtiyê di daxuyaniya xwe ya duyem de diyar kir ku kesekî ku bi giranî birîndar bûbû rakiribûn nexweşxaneyê û du kesên din ên ku ji bin xirbeyan hatibûn derxistin jî jiyana xwe ji dest dane û hejmara miriyan derketiye şeşan.




Waliyê Îzmîrê Suleyman Elban jî dora saet 16.45an de daxuyaniyek da û diyar kir ku hejmara miriyan derketiye 10î û 15 birîndar jî li nexweşxaneyan in.




Elban diyar kir ku çar kes di bin xirbeyan de ne û xebatên lêgerîn û rizgarkirinê didomin.







Tê gotin ku di vardiyaya normal de zêdetirî 300 xebatkarî li ser wê xetê hebûn, lê ji ber guhertina qazanê ya di dema lênerînê de dora 200 xebatkar hebûne. Di wê demê de hilberîn tine bû, lê piştî alav û malzemeyên ku li xeta gaza xwezayî ketin, bu sedema teqînê.







Serokkomar û Serokê Giştî yê AKPê Recep Tayyip Erdogan piştî civîna Kabîneyê di saet 19.00an de daxuyaniyek da û diyar kir ku hejmara miriyan derketiye 16î û 13 kes birîndar in ku 2 ji wan giran in.




Wezîrê Tenduristiyê Kemal Memişoglu jî di saet 22.14an de li ser hesabê xwe yê Xê daxuyand ku karkerekî din ê rewşa wî giran bû jiyana xwe ji dest daye. Bi vî rengî hejmara karkerên di teqînê de mirin derket 17î.




*Tesîsa hilberîna hesin û polayê ya HABAŞê ya li Aliagayê, li herêma pîşesaziyê ya Bozkoy-Çakmakliyê ye. Limana HABAŞê ya li peravê Korfeza Nemrutê jî li Çakmakliyê ye û bi qasî 7 kîlometreyî dûrî tesîsa hesin û polayê ye. Di qada hilberînê ya şîrketê ya li Aliagayê de, li gel polaxane û hesinxaneyan, tesîsên hilberîna gazê, borî-tûp û enerjiyê jî hene. (Nexşe: Google Maps)




Sendîkavanê berê Dogangul: " Ev teqîneke ku ji dûr ve diyar bû dê biqewime.”




Endamê Meclîsa Şaredariya Aliagayê yê Partiya NÛ û Serokê Berê yê Şaxa Petrol Îş a Aliagayê Îbrahîm Dogangul têkildarî teqînê ji bianetê re axivî û got: "Ev teqîneke ku ji dûr ve diyar bû dê biqewime.”




Dogangul da zanîn ku li gorî agahiyên ji karkeran girtiye, hêza vîncê têr nekiriye ku potaya pola û hesinê helandî têde hilbigire. Vînc û pota wergeriyaye û pişt re şewat derketiye û tûpên oksîjenê teqiyane.




Dogangulê ku piştî teqînê çûbû herêmê, got ku di kargehên hesin û polayê de her cûre bermahî tên hilberandin, ji ber vê yekê dibe ku maddeyên cûda di nav de hebin, her weha dibe ku di nav de cebilxaneyên leşlerî jî hebin. Lêbelê Dogangul diyar kir ku agahiyên destpêkê ên ku gihîştine ber destê wî destnîşan dikin ku sedema teqînê têkçûna vîncê ye.




Dogangul bi lêv kir ku qezayên xebatê di kargehên hesin û polayê de tên asayîkirin û wiha axivî:







"Di kargehên hesin û polayê de tê gotin ku 'lingê wî jêbû, laqê wî jêbû'. Em pir fêrî van bûne. Lêbelê ev teqîn giraniya rewşê li ber çavan radixîne. Ger di dema xwe de tedbîr hatibûna girtin, gelo dê ev rewş çêbibûya? Ji bo van cûre qezayên xebatê dibêjin 'qezaya nayê dîtin'. Na, 

ev teqîneke ku ji dûr ve diyar bû dê biqewime.”

. Teqînên di kargehên hesin û polayê de 

 ji dûr ve diyar e dê biqewime.” 

û dibin sedema mirina mirovan."







Dogangul her wiha fikarên xwe anî ziman ku dibe ku hejmara miriyan piştî teqînê zêde bibe.




Daxuyaniyên Işıkhan û Gurlek




Wezîrê Xebat û Ewlehiya Civakî Vedat Işikhan di daxuyaniya li ser hesabê xwe yê medyaya civakî de got: "Ji bo lêkolîna bûyera bi êş a qewimî, ji aliyê Saziya Ewlehiya Civakî ve sermifetîşek hatiye erkdarkirin. Weke Wezaret em pêvajoyê ji nêz ve dişopînin."




Wezîrê Dadê Akın Gurlek jî da zanîn ku Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Menemenê derbarê teqînê de lêpirsîn da destpêkirin û çar dozgerên komarê hatine erkdarkirin.




Gurlek got: "Dema ku dozgerên me yên komarê û heyeta pisporan li cihê bûyerê lêkolînan dikin, xebatên lêgerîn û rizgarkirinê jî didomin da ku em bigihîjin karkerên xwe yên di bin xirbeyan de."







Zexta hilberînê, tenduristî û ewlehiya karkeran a li HABAŞê




HABAŞ yek ji mezintirîn hilberînerên hesin û polayê yên Tirkiyeyê ye. Li gorî daneyên sazûmanî yên rojane yên şîrketê, polaxaneya li tesîsa Aliagayê xwediyê kapasîteya hilberîna 4,5 milyon ton polayê şil a salane ye. Şîrket her wiha di warên gazên pîşesazî û bijîşkî, enerjî, makîneyên giran, LPG û gaza xwezayî de jî xebatan dike.




Li gorî nûçeyên Evrenselê yên ku di demên ciyawaz de derbarê HABAŞê de hatine weşandin, zexta hilberînê ya giran, kêmbûna hejmara karkeran, demên xebatê yên dirêj, lênêrînên ku hatine paşxistin û kêmasiyên ewlehiya xebatê, pirsgirêkên herî berbiçav in. Karkeran anîne ziman ku bi vardiyayên ku digihîjin 12 saetan, demên bêhndanê yên kurt û alavên kevn dixwazin em hiberînê zêdetir bikin. Ev jî şert û mercên xebatê giranir dikin.




Di serdemên ku şîrketê rekorên hilberînê û îxracatê şikandine de, karkeran anîne ziman ku ev yek bi xebata zêde, taşeronîkirin û bi kêmasiyên tedbîrên ewlehiyê hatiye bidestxistin. Li gorî gotinên karkeran, piştî mirin û birîndariyên giran jî li hin beşan hilberîn di demekî kurt de dîsa dest pê kiriye.




Di nûçeyên derbarê kargehên hesin û polayê yên li Aliagayê de ku HABAŞ jî di nav de ye, bi karkerên kêm hilberîna zêde, lênêrîn û mudaxeleyên ku di dema xebitandina makîneyan de tên kirin, kêmbûna hejmara karkerên pispor û îtiraznekirina li dijî karên xeternak wekî pirsgirêkên hevpar hatine rêzkirin.







(EMK/AY)

author: Jerome Small
title: Carroll’s royal commission: an attack on effective unionism in Victoria
content:
The Royal Commission into the Integrity of Major Public and Civil Infrastructure Construction Projects in Victoria was announced by Victoria’s Labor Premier Ben Carroll in August: his first act as the incoming premier. 

Carroll’s announcement was a response to a years-long media campaign against the CFMEU, the main construction union. It was also part of a wholesale lurch to the right by an already neoliberal Labor government. And it is a blatant attack on any idea that unions should act to raise wages. 

If proof is needed, just look at the first day of the current bloc of hearings. I attended the first day of the commission back in September and sat through the proceedings yesterday via livestream.  

Literally the main point of yesterday’s hearing was how terrible it was that the CFMEU stopped a major construction job—the Gap Road level crossing removal in Sunbury—for a day and a half in June 2022, and that this resulted in traffic controllers winning an increase in wages from the award rate (at that time $26 per hour) to around $49 per hour. 

The horror. This equates to a full-time wage of $1,862 per week, slightly above Australia’s average full-time wage of $1,835 in 2022. It’s an OK wage, though no king’s ransom. With allowances, shift and casual loading, and the plentiful overtime that construction sites run on, this can add up to a decent wage if you’re prepared to work long hours.

To listen to Chris Young, the counsel assisting the royal commission, a union winning this sort of wage for a blue-collar worker through industrial action in 2026 is a threat to all that is right in the world. So much so that two weeks of the royal commission’s rather expensive time is being devoted to investigating how this could possibly have come about, with the express intention of ensuring it never happens again. 

Young spent yesterday sifting through the circumstances leading up to this supposed affront to decency. The CFMEU had a lot going in its favour. 

Railway crossing removals happen on a tight timetable, planned up to a year in advance. The two companies doing the work—John Holland and CPB—wanted to deliver the job on time in order to secure further work. The labour market was tight in Victoria. The CFMEU had already been successful in securing enterprise agreements with most of the big companies doing this sort of work in Victoria. From the evidence led by counsel assisting, it sounds like the CFMEU judged the moment perfectly—just like any union which is serious about taking action to raise wages should, and historically has. 

Both the CFMEU and the Australian Workers’ Union (AWU) cover workers working on civil construction projects like level crossing removals, and since 2014 the CFMEU has been trying to expand its coverage at the expense of the AWU. The Victorian Labor government at that time was uninterested in helping the AWU maintain coverage over these jobs—like Gap Road—and over traffic control work in particular. 

This was a positive for the workers at Gap Road, and more broadly. The royal commission was told that Zoom Recruitment, one of the AWU-aligned labour hire companies providing traffic control at Gap Road, was operating on a long-expired enterprise agreement that paid only the legal minimum specified in the construction award. 

This is utterly consistent with the business model of the AWU for the past century or more in construction, which is to undercut the wages and condition of the CFMEU and its predecessor unions. And to their credit, for most of that time, the CFMEU and their predecessors generally ignored the AWU’s claims to coverage on “civil” infrastructure work (roads, rail, bridges and tunnels).

The commission heard yesterday that the Labor government’s largely hands-off attitude to this demarcation dispute in 2022, which effectively favoured the CFMEU over the AWU, may have been because of factional alignments within the ruling Labor Party. This is hardly a crime, or even a novel tactic in Australian union politics.  

The AWU has used exactly the same approach, of translating political clout in the Labor Party into industrial coverage (and vice-versa), for its entire existence. The conservative Shop, Distributive and Allied Union (SDA) follows the same path. The only difference is that the AWU and the SDA have an appalling record of lifting wages—in fact the SDA did the opposite, helping employers undercut legal minimums, until a path-breaking legal case in the Fair Work Commission a decade ago finally ended this multi-billion-dollar conspiracy to lower the rate of wages. No royal commission was ever called into the SDA, though. 

The cost of the CFMEU’s success in their industrial action at Gap Road was a significant focus in yesterday’s royal commission hearing. On a project with a budget of $110 million, counsel assisting estimated that the union's actions led to an extra $6 million being spent. Nearly $4 million of this was in the higher wages paid to traffic controllers. 

Given that the royal commission is costing about $1 million per week, it’s debatable whether the cost of investigating goings-on at the Gap Road project—two weeks of hearings and (at a guess) maybe the same time assembling evidence—is actually more than the extra wages paid. The Gap Road project was also delivered under budget, at $104 million, despite whatever extra cost was incurred after the CFMEU’s stop-work. Hardly the crime of the century then. 

But of course, the actual concern being aired at the royal commission was that this success in raising the rate of wages would be successful beyond Gap Road. Counsel assisting led evidence that around this time, industry sources estimated that if the CFMEU was successful in their efforts to raise the wages (from the award or near-award AWU rates to the CFMEU rates) of every single traffic controller employed over the entire pipeline of infrastructure projects in the state, the total cost might pass $400 million. It wasn’t clear from yesterday’s evidence what the total value of these projects is. 

Unions should be praised for winning higher wages on major projects. It’s bizarre, and a marker of how right-wing the whole environment is around the “big build” and the CFMEU is, that it’s at all controversial to say this. The storm of media coverage from the 

Age

, and the royal commission that is the result, reeks of class prejudice. How dare blue-collar workers without a trade get a decent living! How dare unions raise wages in a cost-of-living crisis that the media would rather us all accept is intractable! This is the real “problem” at the heart of the media storm and the royal commission.

Geoffrey Watson has admitted as much. Watson is the man who made himself famous by inventing the figure of $15 billion in extra expenses that the CFMEU had allegedly added to Victoria’s $100-billion-plus “big build” infrastructure program. In a recent interview on radio station 3AW, Watson stated of this alleged cost overrun: 

“A lot of it went into the hands of decent, hardworking people, who were getting paid at very accelerated rates. My problem with that was that too was a form of corruption in so far as it’s a misuse of public funds”.

“Conspiracy to raise the rate of wages” used to be a 

criminal offence

, punishable by two years' jail with hard labour. To take action to raise wages from $26 an hour to $49 is apparently a “misuse of public funds”, an equally reprehensible crime in the eyes of some. 

Watson is eminently qualified to know when a decent government-funded wage becomes a “misuse of public funds”. After all, this is the guy who (as the 

Australian

 newspaper 

reported

 in April 2016) “described his work at the Independent Commission Against Corruption, for which he earned up to $4,000 a day, as a ‘poorly paid living hell’”. 

It wasn’t clear from yesterday’s hearings how much money anyone else—for instance, the giant companies John Holland and CPB—was making from Gap Road. The project was effectively delivered on a “cost plus” basis, with the state government paying construction costs plus a “reasonable margin” for corporate overheads and profits. 

The implication of some figures presented yesterday was that this “reasonable margin” might be as high as 30 percent of the project’s total costs, which means the company made somewhat more than a traffic controller who had been lifted off the legal minimums. I’ll keep an eye out for evidence either way, but I won’t hold my breath—corporate profiteering from essential infrastructure construction doesn’t seem to be within the scope of the royal commission’s Gap Road investigation.

Much more of the focus in yesterday’s hearings was on the methods used by CFMEU organisers to stop work at the Gap Road site in June 2022. Rather than simply call a meeting and lead a walk-off, which might have left the union open to substantial fines, it’s alleged that union organisers used the legal cover of health and safety laws to gain access to the site and to log a series of safety breaches. While these issues were rectified, the organisers obstructed work by sitting or standing in particular parts of the site. 

Counsel assisting noted that many of these safety issues were real enough. There were 11-metre-deep holes from the piling rigs, for instance, which didn’t have a mesh cover secured and had no handrails around them. Nevertheless, the real problem, according to counsel assisting, was the CFMEU.

It’s true that rigorous enforcement of health and safety regulations can be used as an industrial tactic. This is far from ideal: it’s a lot less transparent and democratic than the approach that was commonplace when I first started in the construction industry in 1999, which was meeting on site, discussing the issues, and voting whether to stop work. The reason health and safety concerns are often used to achieve an industrial outcome is that industrial action is illegal in Australia in almost any circumstance outside a formal bargaining round, which are usually spaced four years apart. 

Management can sack union delegates, blatantly discriminate, and fail to abide by the enterprise agreement. But if a union dares to do more than file paperwork and pray for the best at Fair Work, and instead actually stops work, it faces the possibility of serious fines. 

Unions in the UK can ballot for a strike at any time in relation to 

any work dispute

. Workers in the viciously anti-union legal regime of the US have a sliver of legal space to hold an “unfair labour practice” strike when an employer wilfully violates a collective contract with the workforce. No such right exists in the legal regime introduced to Australia by Labor in the 1990s and tightened in the decades since. 

Many of the labour movement’s proudest moments—the Green Bans of the Builders Labourers Federation in the 1970s; Zelda D’Aprano chaining herself to the doors of the Industrial Court in 1971 in a protest for equal pay; the 50-day strike of Victorian nurses in 1986 that ultimately led to the world’s first enforceable nurse-patient ratios; the strikes and mass pickets that supported the Maritime Union in 1998—these and countless lesser-known disputes would never have happened if unionists had followed the preferred path of counsel assisting, and slavishly observed the laws of the day. 

One of the most offensive things about the media attacks on the CFMEU in recent years, and the royal commission, is they roll this type of legitimate and important industrial activity together with practices which should be driven out of the union movement—such as corruption and inviting criminal gangs into union structures. Socialists and other decent unionists have to reject both the corrupt and criminal tactics of some in the CFMEU 

and

 the bosses’ efforts to use these as cover to smear legitimate efforts to win wage rises and unionism in general.

Calling out the royal commission for what it is—an anti-worker disgrace—can’t mean uncritical defence of everything the leadership of the CFMEU ever did. In particular, inviting members of criminal gangs into union positions, including union delegates and health and safety reps, is a crime against principled unionism. A criminal gang is an absolutely ruthless capitalist enterprise. It’s a disgrace that such figures, some with zero industry experience, were parachuted into union roles while the Victorian CFMEU was under the leadership of John Setka. 

Writing in 2024

, when the CFMEU was first placed under the dictatorial control of an unelected, government-appointed administrator, I argued that the retreat of democracy within the CFMEU had happened over years, and was in large part the product of a siege mentality. Loyalty tests and secret deals replace organising, open debate, and frequent and open industrial action. 

A siege mentality is not an entirely irrational response when the union is under an ever-tightening legal siege, and when industrial action is criminalised. But in the long term, it’s a dead end at best, or a road to disaster at worst. 

A very different response to a siege is to try to break the siege. This would have to involve systematic organising and industrial action, involving wider forces. It would have to include a program of strikes in the finishing trades, where wages and conditions have been a basket case since the Howard government introduced its vicious anti-union Australian Building and Construction Commission in 2005, and which the current government-appointed administration has clearly done nothing to improve. 

No-one should pretend this is a simple process. Quite the contrary. Construction workers face a difficult task in winning back control of their union. Not the least of these obstacles is the flood of manufactured outrage from Carroll’s royal commission.

author: Valerie Anne
title: You Oughta Know That Alanis Morissette Is Pansexual
content:
feature image photo by Credit: NBC / Contributor via Getty Images

It’s official: 90s icon and present-day superstar Alanis Morissette is pansexual. The singer was a guest on the Handsome podcast, which is co-hosted by queer comedians Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster, and Mae Martin, and they were talking about Alanis’s penchant for a post-breakup rage anthem. Fortune Feimster jokingly asked her, “Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?” to which Alanis replied, “I’m pansexual, so yeah.”

The energy in the room was perfect. At first, everyone thought it was a joke (or perhaps that she was being…ironic), but when they clarified that Alanis was serious, they all joked that she should have led with that. You walk into a queer podcast with the queer announcement!!

Granted, this is not the first time Alanis has said she isn’t straight. She has been talking about exploring her sexuality and being attracted to women as far back as 2008, and it was apparently at least partly her idea for her character to kiss Sarah Jessica Parker’s Carrie during her Sex and the City guest spot. It’s just the first time she’s used a specific label out loud.

I considered riddling this intro with Alanis-related puns (like the joke my friend made: she’s got one pan in her pocket…) but I’ll save you the cringe. I’ll just say this news has made me even more head over feet for her.

God is a woman, and she’s also pansexual.

You Live, You Learn (About More Gay News)

Cara Delevingne sent Reneé Rapp for a loop during a prank call in an Elle interview.

Speaking of Cara Delevingne, she also was at the red carpet premiere of Club Kid talking about the movie and also the “blue tsunami” in the midterm elections.

Beanie Feldstein and her wife welcomed a baby girl into their family (Beanie already made the “beanie baby” joke so I will refrain).

Amber Glenn took the lead in her Dancing with the Stars number on Disney night, dressed in shiny white pants, flexing her impressive-as-hell back muscles, and doing the quickstep to A Star is Born from Hercules.

Queer Swedish pop star Tove Styrke returns to music after having a baby with her partner Sanna Sikborn Erixon.

Cynthia Nixon was asked who her favorite lesbian is and she said Sappho (and also gave almost-definitely-bisexual Eleanor Roosevelt a shout-out).

The wait is almost over: Netflix’s The Body drops on Wednesday, November 11.

Queer Canadian icon Jann Arden is among the recognizable names on the guest star list for Jared Keeso’s upcoming comedy I Kill the Bear, alongside other queer-adjacent faves like Melanie Scrofano, Michelle Mylett, and Tricia Helfer.

ICYMI, WNBA players Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers have actually been broken up for quite a while, but don’t worry, they’re still friends.

author: Stelinsky
title: Υπόθεση Marfin vol.3
content:
Η υπόθεση Marfin «έτρεξε» για πρώτη φορά με τις διώξεις που ασκήθηκαν το 2011, έναν χρόνο μετά τον εμπρησμό της τράπεζας Marfin στο κέντρο της Αθήνας, στην απεργία της 5ης Μάη 2010. Ο εμπρησμός οδήγησε στον θάνατο 3 από τους εργαζόμενους στην τράπεζα. Πέντε χρόνια μετά, ο σύντροφος Θ. Σίψας αθωώθηκε πανηγυρικά στο Μικτό Ορκωτό Δικαστήριο (ΜΟΔ). Λίγα χρόνια μετά, το 2021, ο φάκελος της υπόθεσης «άνοιξε» ξανά, με την αστυνομική έρευνα να μην αποδίδει καρπούς.

Στο σήμερα, η ανακίνηση της υπόθεσης Marfin για 3η φορά σηματοδοτεί το πέρασμα σε μια νέα εποχή όσον αφορά τον εγχώριο κοινωνικό-ταξικό ανταγωνισμό. Η υπόθεση ήρθε στο προσκήνιο με αφορμή την «υπόθεση της Θεσσαλονίκης»: Οι δύο υποθέσεις, με χρονική απόσταση 16 ετών, όλως τυχαίως «εξιχνιάστηκαν» την ίδια μέρα. Συγκεκριμένα στις 10 Ιουλίου εκτελείται τριπλό ένταλμα σύλληψης, και διατάσσονται κατ’ οίκον έρευνες σε 5 άτομα. Συλλαμβάνονται οι σύντροφοι Θύμιος και Κώστας, και η συντρόφισσα Ελένη, κάτοικος εξωτερικού, που μεταφέρεται στα αγγλικά κρατητήρια.

Τα στοιχεία για την υπόθεση είναι ανύπαρκτα: Από την έκθεση της Διεύθυνσης Εγκληματολογικών Ερευνών, όπου αναλύεται το οπτικοακουστικό υλικό, δεν προκύπτει ταυτοποίηση των συντροφιών ως άτομα παρόντα στο σημείο μπροστά από την τράπεζα. Μοναδικά στοιχεία η ομοιότητα κάποιων κινητών αντικειμένων, και ένα ανώνυμο e-mail, το οποίο συνέταξε η Διεύθυνση Αντιμετώπισης Οργανωμένου Εγκλήματος (ΔΑΟΕ) που πραγματοποίησε τις συλλήψεις. Η δουλειά της αστυνομίας είναι πολύ πρόχειρη: Στο mail αναφέρεται ως μέλος στο «παρεάκι» που εμπλέκεται στην υπόθεση, άτομο που ήταν στη φυλακή εκείνη την ημέρα· ακόμα, η εκπρόσωπος τύπου της ΕΛ.ΑΣ., Κωνσταντία Δημογλίδου, αναφέρει στον ΣΚΑΪ πως το επίμαχο mail είναι στα χέρια της αστυνομίας ενάμιση χρόνο, ενώ αυτό έχει ημερομηνία αποστολής 08/04/2026, δηλαδή 3 μήνες πριν τις συλλήψεις.

Οι απολογίες διεξάγονται ενώπιον της ανακρίτριας Σμαράγδας Τασούλη, και της εισαγγελέως Βαρβάρας Γνεσούλη. Τα συντρόφια αρνούνται τις κατηγορίες, υπερασπίζονται την πολιτική τους θέση, όπως και τη συμμετοχή τους στη διαδήλωση, και ζητούν να διερευνηθεί ποιος έστειλε το e-mail.

Και τα 3 συντρόφια προφυλακίζονται παρά την απουσία στοιχείων. Απορρίπτονται και οι προσφυγές τους ενάντια στην απόφαση προφυλάκισης, καθώς τα αρμόδια Συμβούλια πλημμελειοδικών επικυρώνουν τις απορριπτικές προτάσεις των αρμόδιων εισαγγελέων, του αντιεισαγγελέα πρωτοδικών Ν. Λυμπερόπουλου, και των εισαγγελέων πρωτοδικών Ε. Μαρουδά και ο. Ηλιοπούλου. Έχει ενδιαφέρον πως στα σκεπτικά των προφυλακίσεων, όπως και στις απορρίψεις των προσφυγών, υιοθετείται η συλλογιστική από το διαβιβαστικό της αστυνομίας, εμπλουτισμένη με αναφορές σε «ενδείξεις ενοχής» αλλά και σε «οργανωμένη, συλλογική και προπαρασκευασμένη δράση». Σύμφωνα με τους δικαστικούς, υπάρχει ο κίνδυνος τα συντρόφια μας να τελέσουν τα ίδια αδικήματα, μιας και «εδώ και 16 χρόνια κρύβουν επιμελώς τη δράση τους». Τι πιο λογικό άλλωστε;

Η ΔΑΟΕ, κατ’ εντολή του υπουργού ΠΡΟ.ΠΟ, Μιχάλη Χρυσοχοΐδη, έκανε τη δουλειά της. Στο μαγείρεμα παίρνει θέση και η δικαστική εξουσία, έτοιμη να το αναβαθμίσει με την –όχι και τόσο– μυστική συνταγή της. Η υπόθεση μένει στην εποπτεία της ανακρίτριας Τασούλη για τις τελικές πινελιές και το ντεκόρ.

Η Σμαράγδα Τασούλη παίζει καθοριστικό ρόλο στην υπόθεση, όπως θα δούμε παρακάτω. Η ίδια, έχοντας συμπληρώσει κάποια χρόνια προϋπηρεσίας, μέσα στο καλοκαίρι θα προαγόταν για λόγους αρχαιότητας σε πρόεδρος πρωτοδικών σε μια κενή οργανική θέση. Αρχικά η προαγωγή της εξαιρέθηκε από τον τακτικό πίνακα των προαχθέντων, όπως αυτός δημοσιεύεται επίσημα στο Φύλλο Εφημερίδας της Κυβερνήσεως (14/08/2026). Αλλά και σε δεύτερο χρόνο, παρ’ όλο που στο ΦΕΚ στις 17/09/2026 τής ανατίθεται μια θέση στο Ναύπλιο, εκείνη εξακολουθεί να μην αναλαμβάνει καθήκοντα εκεί ως πρόεδρος πρωτοδικών. Αντιθέτως, με ρητή ειδική διαταγή του Υπουργού Δικαιοσύνης παραμένει στη θέση της ανακρίτριας, έχοντας κατ’ αποκλειστικότητα την ανακριτική έρευνα για την υπόθεση Marfin, απαλλαγμένη από κάθε άλλη υπόθεση. Αυτή η τελευταία εξέλιξη επιβεβαιώνει πως η συγκεκριμένη ανακρίτρια έχει αναλάβει την ευθύνη να φέρει εις πέρας μια ειδική αποστολή, που της έχει ανατεθεί απευθείας από το Υπουργείο Δικαιοσύνης: Την ποινική αναβάθμιση της καταστολής των κοινωνικών αντιστάσεων.

Οι νέες συνταγές, λοιπόν, δεν αργούν. Το μαγειρείο καλά κρατεί: Στις αρχές του Οκτώβρη, η ανακρίτρια επιστρατεύει την 1η παράγραφο του νόμου 187Α, αυτήν περί ατομικής τρομοκρατίας.* Μέχρι πρότινος τα 3 συντρόφια κατηγορούνταν για ανθρωποκτονία κατά συρροή και από κοινού, και τα διαθέσιμα «στοιχεία» δεν επαρκούσαν για τη απόδοση κατηγοριών σύστασης οργάνωσης (εγκληματικής ή τρομοκρατικής). Με αυτή τη μεθόδευση, το κατηγορητήριο αναβαθμίζεται. Με τη σειρά του, αυτό επιφέρει επιπλέον κατηγορίες για 24 απόπειρες ανθρωποκτονίας – κατηγορίες που δεν παραγράφονται εφόσον η πράξη υπάγεται στην αντιτρομοκρατική νομοθεσία.

Το σημαντικότερο όλων, όμως, όταν έρθει η ώρα της δίκης, είναι πως τα συντρόφια μας δεν θα οδηγηθούν σε ΜΟΔ, όπως συνέβη με την πρώτη εκδίκαση της υπόθεσης (για ακριβώς τα ίδια αδικήματα, εξαιρουμένου του 187Α). Αντιθέτως, θα δικαστούν από Τριμελές Εφετείο Κακουργημάτων, που θα απαρτίζεται μόνο από επαγγελματίες δικαστές. Με αυτόν τον τρόπο, αφήνεται εκτός ο αστάθμητος παράγων των ενόρκων («λαϊκών δικαστών»), που έχουν οδηγήσει σε πανηγυρικές αθωώσεις αγωνιστών ανά τα χρόνια – όπως εξάλλου συνέβη και στην πρώτη version της υπόθεσης, με το ίδιο ακριβώς κατηγορητήριο.

Συνολικά από την πλευρά του κράτους, η ανακίνηση της υπόθεσης Marfin έρχεται ως κλείσιμο ενός ανοιχτού λογαριασμού, που βαστάει τουλάχιστον δυο δεκαετίες – λογαριασμός που άνοιξε με τη μαζικοποίηση των κοινωνικών αντιστάσεων, και την κορύφωσή της κατά την τριετία των αντιμνημονιακών ταραχών (2010-2012). Ο κατασταλτικός μηχανισμός δεν ενδιαφέρεται πραγματικά να βρει τους «ενόχους του τότε», αλλά να τρομοκρατήσει τους «συνενόχους του σήμερα» – όσες και όσους δεν έχουν πλέον πολλές επιλογές, πέρα από το να βγουν ξανά στον δρόμο, όσο η καθημερινότητα γίνεται ασφυκτική. Σε αυτόν τον κόσμο απευθύνεται η υπόθεση Marfin: Τόσο ως σκευωρία, που θα καταρρεύσει νομοτελειακά και με κρότο στις δικαστικές αίθουσες, όσο και ως αντιτρομοκρατική γκιλοτίνα που αιωρείται πάνω απ’ τον σβέρκο των επερχόμενων αντιστάσεων. Το κράτος προτείνει: «Καθίστε σπίτι, μην βρείτε κανά μπελά».

Εμείς από την πλευρά μας, αντιπροτείνουμε τη συλλογικοποίηση. Όσο οι καιροί δυσκολεύουν, όσο τα περιθώρια στενεύουν, οι μόνες διέξοδοι θα εφευρίσκονται συλλογικά.

Ένας νέος εντυπωσιακός κύκλος ταραχών απλώνεται στον πλανήτη. Η Δύση οχυρώνεται πίσω από πολεμικά σενάρια. Το δίλημμα ξεκαθαρίζει: Επανάσταση ή γενικευμένος πόλεμος!

Ατομικές αρνήσεις – συλλογικά αναχώματα. Εσείς με τις Marfin, εμείς με την 5η του Μάη!

ΟΙ ΚΟΙΝΩΝΙΚΟΙ ΑΓΩΝΕΣ ΔΕΝ ΤΡΟΜΟΚΡΑΤΟΥΝΤΑΙ

ΑΜΕΣΗ ΑΠΑΛΛΑΓΗ ΚΑΙ ΑΠΕΛΕΥΘΕΡΩΣΗ ΤΩΝ ΣΥΝΤΡΟΦΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΣΥΝΤΡΟΦΙΣΣΑΣ ΠΟΥ ΔΙΩΚΟΝΤΑΙ ΓΙΑ ΤΗ ΣΚΕΥΩΡΙΑ MARFIN

Στους παρακάτω συνδέσμους οι δημόσιες τοποθετήσεις του Θύμιου και του Κώστα

*Έχει τρομακτικό ενδιαφέρον το σκεπτικό της ανακρίτριας πάνω στο νέο κατηγορητήριο, καθώς αποτυπώνεται ευθαρσώς αυτό που τόσα χρόνια επισημαίνει για τον 187Α τόσο ο προοδευτικός νομικός κόσμος, όσο και το ευρύτερο ριζοσπαστικό κίνημα. Η αμιγώς πολιτική χρησιμότητά του γίνεται ευκρινής μέσα από την αντιστροφή της πραγματικότητας: Το ίδιο το διακύβευμα των μαζικών κοινωνικών αγώνων της εποχής μεταφέρεται στην ποινική σφαίρα, μέσα από τις –εσκεμμένα αόριστες– διατυπώσεις που παρέχει η αντιτρομοκρατική νομοθεσία. Είναι από τις λίγες φορές μάλιστα που μια δικαστική λειτουργός ψηλαφίζει την αντικειμενική υπόσταση της «τρομοκρατικής πράξης», πολιτικοποιώντας τις κινητοποιήσεις, αλλά και τις διώξεις. Στο σκεπτικό γίνονται αναφορές για την επιδίωξη η «εκδήλωση οργανωμένης και θανατηφόρας βίας, σε βάρος εργαζομένων πολιτών που δεν συμμετείχαν στην πανελλαδική απεργία, να εξαναγκάσει τους πολίτες, υπό τον φόβο ανάλογων επιθέσεων, να συμμετέχουν στις απεργιακές κινητοποιήσεις, ώστε να διασφαλιστεί η μαζικότητα αυτών και να εξαναγκαστούν οι βουλευτές της Ελληνικής Βουλής να καταψηφίσουν τα μέτρα οικονομικής και δημοσιονομικής πολιτικής που προωθούνταν (Μνημόνιο 1, μετέπειτα Ν.3845/2010)».

author: Bruce De La Cruz
title: ‘Where is the accountability?’: Nunavut’s child advocate says territory’s protection issues aren’t being addressed
content:
Another scathing report from the federal auditor general looking into Nunavut’s child protection system came as no surprise to Jane Bates, the territory’s child welfare advocate.

On Nov. 3, deputy auditor general Andrew Hayes released the latest in a series of damning reports outlining how Nunavut is failing to protect Inuit children in care of the state.

For Bates, who has already written extensively about the issue, it came as no surprise.

“These concerns have been reported on, recommendations have been made about them, and yet they remain unaddressed to the detriment of children, youth, and families,” Bates told APTN News, “which is really the fundamental issue that everyone should be really concerned about, is the lack of follow through.

“We’re not talking about buildings. We’re not talking about bicycles. We’re talking about children and youth and their families. And so it’s deeply concerning.”

Hayes’ report outlined found that “fundamental weaknesses” in Nunavut’s child welfare system and its handling of the territory’s most vulnerable “remain unresolved” in audits going back to 2011.

“When children are removed from their homes and are placed in foster care for protection, the department takes on responsibility for their safety and well being,” Hayes said at a news conference on Nov. 3. “Yet it could not consistently demonstrate that basic safeguards, intended to protect children and place them in safe environments, were being followed.”

According to the latest report, approximately 400 children and youth are in Nunavut’s foster care system; the majority are Inuit.

Hayes said his office reviewed 40 cases and found issues that go back more than a decade.

The major concerns included that Nunavut’s Department of Family Services didn’t maintain required monthly in-person contact in more than 90 per cent of the cases; only performed 52 per cent of required evaluations for home safety” and, in 75 per cent of the cases, failed to give important information about a child to caregivers.

“Where is the accountability here? And again, we’re hearing, ‘oh, yes, we accept all the recommendations and we’re going to make changes.’ Where have you been? This has been upwards of 15 years. And we shouldn’t still be having this conversation.”

One Inuk family services employee who spoke to APTN News on condition that we grant anonymity, said the lack of Inuit staffing is the biggest concern.

“There’s like 30 per cent Inuit employed by this department,” the employee said. “I think if we had an Inuk supervisor, it would make a difference. Someone who knows the culture.”

Clayton Greaves, assistant deputy minister of Family Services Wellness Division, oversees the operations for the child welfare system in Nunavut.

“When I reviewed the report, and I hear what’s happening, we accept the other general recommendations and we accept that there’s work that’s in front of us that we have to do,” he said.

Greaves emphasized the challenges in running the child welfare system and said they’re doing the best with what they have.

“When we look at the report, we have to be careful that we don’t draw the conclusion that the gaps that we see is directly related to children being harmed,” he said. “And I wanted to make sure that we’re able to emphasize that. Yes, there are challenges with our new information system. We recognize and accept, you know, the recommendation, like I said, from what the Auditor General reported.”

Auditor general funds Nunavut foster care continues to fail vulnerable children

According to Bates’ own report that was filed in September, harm is coming to children.

“In the Reviews of Critical Injuries and Deaths program, reports of sexualized violence increased significantly, from eight in 2024–2025 to 22 in 2025–2026, while the number of young people who died by suicide tragically increased to 13,” she wrote in a report tabled in the Nunavut legislature.

“Children and youth who grow up in care, there’s been numerous studies done on the trajectory for young people,” she told APTN. “The outcomes are not good for children who grow up in care. They’re away from their families. They’re away from their culture. They lose their language.

“Children have the right to grow up with their families. They have a right to be protected. These are their fundamental rights under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. And currently, in Nunavut, that is not happening.”

Bruce was thrilled to join APTN on a 10-month contract in Yellowknife, where he’s working as a video journalist. Before moving to Yellowknife, he worked in civic journalism in townships east of Ottawa, Ottawa’s AV industry as a Technician/Camera Operator, and as the On-Camera Talent of his alma mater’s Digital TV Channel (Conestoga College Digital TV), which was launched in January 2024 on Roku TV, and later Apple TV.

title: Cathy Levine - Tyrannei der Tyrannei
content:
