title: Tons of oak trees cut down on Mount Gabar
content:
Tree felling continues on the Mişarê Plain of Mount Gabar in Şırnak countryside. Logging activities, which have intensified in the region recently, have reportedly accelerated with the approach of winter on the mountain slopes facing the Eruh (Dihê) district of Siirt (Sêrt).

Footage recorded on the Mişarê Plain in Eruh showed tons of oak trees felled on different dates lined up along the roadside for transportation. The logs, stacked on top of one another, were seen stretching for hundreds of meters.

Meanwhile, the Şırnak and Siirt bar associations had previously filed criminal complaints with the chief public prosecutors’ offices, demanding an end to the tree felling in the region.

author: Unknown
title: Saki: Turkish citizens top the list of deportations from Europe
content:
Deportations across Europe have accelerated following the implementation of the new Pact on Migration and Asylum. These measures have begun to affect not only undocumented migrants but also asylum seekers and political refugees who have been granted asylum.




The adoption of the pact has been followed by an increase in deportation orders targeting Kurdish refugees in particular. Numerous Kurdish political refugees have begun to be returned to Turkey from the European countries where they reside. Refugees, including politicians, poets and writers, face trials carrying potential prison sentences of several decades under cases brought against them after their return to Turkey.




Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP Özgül Saki spoke to ANF about recent developments affecting migrants in Europe and the growing number of deportation orders.




'The price of the crisis is poverty, massacres and displacement'




Özgül Saki said that pressure on refugees had intensified following the implementation of the new Pact on Migration and Asylum on 12 June 2026. She added said: "Following its entry into force on 12 June, the Council of the European Union (EU) formally adopted a new regulation known as the Return Regulation on 1 October 2026, aimed at accelerating the deportation and return of irregular migrants who have no legal right to remain.




We must first recognize that since 2013, we have been witnessing mass migration on a scale unprecedented in previous periods. The period of conflict that began with ISIS attacks in Syria and Iraq, Israel's genocidal policies against Palestine, the escalation of tensions between Ukraine and Russia into a prolonged war, the Taliban's return to power in Afghanistan and US attacks on Iran have displaced millions of people. In my view, the underlying cause is the imperialist capitalist system's continued reliance on war as a regional strategy to resolve its own crises. The price of this crisis continues to be paid by the peoples of the region through poverty, massacres and displacement.




We are witnessing the re-emergence of colonial reflexes. Efforts to remain protected within Europe's own borders are proceeding alongside expansionist ambitions beyond them. Concepts described as 'European values,' such as human rights, democracy and equality, have lost their meaning. We are confronted with a Europe dominated by governments that regard everything as permissible in the name of 'security' and 'defense,' are turning toward fascism and envision a white Europe.




There is a widespread expectation that migration statistics will increasingly be used as a political tool, particularly amid the rise of the far right in Germany, the Netherlands and France. The prominence of 'returns,' 'border security' and 'irregular migration' in election campaigns indicates that this right-wing and fascistic trajectory will continue. As a result, a deliberate anti-migrant political agenda is being implemented through new, multilayered mechanisms of pressure on refugees."




'Restrictions begin at the border'




Özgül Saki said that, according to the Council of the European Union, the regulation adopted on 1 October expands member states' powers to carry out deportations.




Saki continued: "We have already begun to see the serious consequences of the new legislation in recent months. The coming period will bring highly unfavorable conditions both for migrants already living in European countries and for those seeking to apply for asylum.




The Council of the European Union stated that the new rules adopted on 1 October will complement the Pact on Migration and Asylum and contribute to its implementation. The regulation gives member states greater scope to carry out returns and allows for the establishment of 'return hubs' in countries outside the EU. This means that people who have been issued return decisions and are deemed to have no right to remain in the EU may be transferred to these centers under agreements or arrangements concluded with the relevant non-EU countries




Eurostat figures and recent EU data show that asylum applications across the EU have declined by approximately 24 percent. However, this decline has been achieved by deliberately making the application requirements more complicated from the outset. The aim of what the pact calls the 'accelerated asylum procedure' is to process applications at the border within a very short period. People fleeing war, poverty and violence are required to undergo identity, health and security checks within just five to seven days before they can even submit their applications. In other words, the restrictions begin at the very first stage, at the border."




'87 percent of asylum applications from Turkey are rejected'




Özgül Saki also assessed the situation regarding Turkey. Saki said: "The situation regarding Turkey is equally clear. Recent reports indicate a 40 percent decline in asylum applications from Turkey. Strict regulations and the rejection of 87 percent of applications from Turkey have played a major role in this decline. Under this 'accelerated procedure,' migrants whose applications are rejected by one country will be unable to apply to any other EU country, effectively trapping them behind both legal and physical barriers. The aim is to keep migrants outside Europe's borders. This will make migration routes more dangerous, force people to take longer journeys and increase mass deaths.




Data from the United Nations International Organization for Migration (IOM) show that the number of irregular migrants attempting to reach Europe by sea fell by 39 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the previous year. However, deaths along migration routes have increased. By mid-September, at least 2,292 migrants had died or gone missing along Mediterranean and Atlantic routes, compared with 1,999 during the same period last year. Although the number of arrivals along the route covering crossings to Italy and Malta fell by approximately 55 percent, the number of deaths rose from 844 to 996.




Meanwhile, the EU is selectively recruiting the skilled labor it needs while deporting asylum seekers it regards as a 'burden.' Through the establishment of 'talent pools,' migrants will be categorized as 'skilled' or 'unskilled,' and those selected will be brought to Europe under restrictive contractual conditions. Moreover, Frontex, the EU's border enforcement agency, is being granted powers so extensive that it will be able to intervene in the internal affairs of countries where asylum seekers are held.




Last week, we visited Uzbekistan with the Migration Subcommittee of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE PA). Uzbekistan is presented as a positive example in terms of migration policies. The Uzbek government, which has signed migration agreements with Austria and Germany, is implementing a program that could be described as a migration exchange. Training centers provide vocational education for machinists, mechanics, nurses and cooks. Those who complete their training will be employed in Germany and Austria for specified periods, according to the number of workers requested. In exchange, Uzbekistan will accept an equivalent number of migrants returned from those countries.




These agreements, which effectively risk normalizing human trafficking by bringing it within a legal framework, are becoming increasingly widespread among Balkan, Asian and European countries. The countries entering into these agreements are also signing extensive cooperation protocols with Frontex."




'Turkish citizens top the list of deportations'




Özgül Saki said that Turkish citizens ranked first among those deported from EU countries and drew attention to the fact that nationals of other countries were also being sent to Turkey.




Saki said: "According to Eurostat data, a total of 132,600 people were refused entry into the Schengen Area at the EU's external borders throughout 2025. Human rights organizations have long argued that arbitrary detention and the return of vulnerable people to dangerous countries reflect policies focused more on deterrence and pushbacks than on protecting people from persecution.




Turkish citizens rank first among those deported from EU countries and returned to third countries, with 13,405 people. An important distinction must be made here. The category 'refused entry' covers people who are denied permission to enter the EU at border crossings or airports. The category 'returned,' on the other hand, refers to people who have already crossed the border and entered the EU but are subsequently removed through an administrative decision.




Turkey ranks first not in refusals of entry at border crossings, but in actual deportations from the EU. One of the main reasons is that the EU regards Turkey as a 'safe third country.' The justification is that countries that are candidates for EU membership are automatically considered safe countries. The establishment of return hubs has also been facilitated by the removal of the requirement that migrants be sent to their country of origin or to a country with which they have a direct connection."




'Racist attacks are increasing'




Özgül Saki drew attention to the rise in racist attacks against refugees in Europe and said that anti-migrant rhetoric was becoming increasingly widespread among governments.




Saki said: "Migrants and refugees face discrimination in almost every European country. They are forced to live under the constant threat of violence and hatred in the streets, at work and in their homes. Attempts at lynching and attacks that sometimes escalate into pogroms occur in many countries, including Turkey. However, the most dangerous development in recent years is that anti-migrant sentiment has become part of official discourse, with governments adopting successive regulations that legitimize this approach.




In Turkey, operations to apprehend and deport irregular migrants have reached their highest level over the past six months, including through measures such as Mobile Migration Points. These operations, officially described as an 'all-out war against irregular migration and smuggling networks,' are being carried out under the coordination of the Ministry of Interior. However, there are serious legal problems with these operations. Monitoring reports published by Mülteci-Der in August 2026 indicate that lawyers' access to their migrant clients in removal centers has been restricted through administrative practices whose legal basis remains unclear."




'Most asylum seekers from Turkey are Kurdish'




Özgül Saki also addressed the deportation of Kurdish political refugees to Turkey, pointing to the EU's classification of Turkey as a 'safe country' as a contributing factor.




Saki said: "The safe third country designation has had a major impact. Turkey is also regarded by the EU as a safe third country. In Germany, Turkey ranks third among asylum seekers' countries of origin, after Syria and Afghanistan. The protection recognition rate for applicants from Turkey is below 10 percent. According to Pro Asyl, an independent Germany-based human rights organization defending the rights of refugees and asylum seekers forced to flee their countries, most asylum seekers from Turkey are Kurdish.




One report stated that 84 percent of Turkish citizens who applied for asylum in Germany in 2023 identified themselves as being of Kurdish origin. The German Ministry of Interior reported that the number of Turkish citizens required to leave the country had exceeded 15,000. According to data from the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF), 22,560 Turkish citizens were awaiting deportation at the end of September 2025. Turkey ranked first in this category.




As for the reasons, German authorities generally argue that there is no individually substantiated evidence of political persecution and that Kurdish identity alone is insufficient. Claims of political repression are often rejected on the grounds that they are 'not sufficiently credible or documented.' Discrimination based on Kurdish identity alone is considered insufficient to qualify for international protection.




In Norway, according to Hengaw, Sirwan Aminpour, who sought asylum in the country after participating in the Green Movement protests in 2009, was detained in January 2026 and transferred to the Trandum detention center. He faces the risk of deportation to Iran. In another case, Kurdish asylum seeker Nourzad Alimoradi, who had been waiting for eight years, was sent from Norway to Turkey and attempted suicide at Istanbul Airport. His deportation to Iran was temporarily suspended.




In the Netherlands, approximately 5,900 first-time asylum applications were submitted in the third quarter of 2026, representing a 13 percent decline compared with the previous year. Parliament approved the implementation of the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum in May 2026. The measures envisage faster and more restrictive procedures, border screening and quicker return decisions. It was also reported that the Netherlands and four other European countries were planning to send asylum seekers who had exhausted all legal remedies to a 'third country' outside the EU by the end of 2027. The Dutch Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) excluded applicants from Turkey from its pilot written hearing procedure on the grounds that their cases were too complex.




The situation facing Iranian Kurds is even more severe and has deteriorated significantly in recent months. Iran's ambassador to Iraq announced that Baghdad had agreed to expel members of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups from Iraqi Kurdistan or hand them over to Iran. Iran describes these groups as 'terrorists' and organizations acting on behalf of the United States and Israel. The war and tensions involving Iran in the region have further intensified this pressure. Tehran has also reportedly requested the extradition of 36 Kurdish opposition figures and activists from Iraq and European countries, including Germany, France, Belgium and Sweden.




Organizations such as Hengaw and Hana frequently report that Iranian Kurdish activists whose asylum applications have been rejected in Turkey face the risk of deportation to Iran. For example, the asylum application of Kurdish activist Rezgar Sheikh Jegari, who has lived in Turkey for 11 years, and his family was rejected by the United Nations Refugee Agency. Turkish migration authorities subsequently issued a second negative decision. Journalist Zanyar Aziznezhad said that he had been held in a removal center for approximately a year, beaten by guards and pressured to sign deportation documents. According to Aziznezhad, Turkey is seeking to increase deportation numbers in order to maintain EU funding.




The process of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) laying down its arms has strengthened the argument in some countries that the 'risk has decreased.' However, courts do not always accept this argument. Deportation decisions are based on two main grounds: the rejection of asylum applications due to insufficient documentation, and the classification of Turkey or Iran as 'safe' countries or countries where the level of risk has declined.




The security dimension, particularly allegations of links to the PKK and intelligence assessments by agencies such as Säpo, is especially prominent in cases involving Sweden. We witnessed a similar case in Estonia. Kurdish poet Tekin Ağacık's asylum application was rejected, and he was sent to Turkey, where he was detained at Istanbul Airport over terrorism allegations.




In cases involving Iran, the official grounds generally include rejection of asylum applications, irregular entry or residence, and concerns relating to 'public order and security.' Human rights organizations argue that such decisions violate the principle of non-refoulement, which prohibits returning people to countries where they face serious risks. These individuals face the risk of politically motivated arrest and torture in Iran."

author: bert
title: Feindbild Antifaschismus: Inflationärer Einsatz von Öffentlichkeitsfahndung
content:
Feindbild Antifaschismus: Inflationärer Einsatz von Öffentlichkeitsfahndung




Ende Oktober 2026 hat das Landeskriminalamt Baden-Württemberg eine Öffentlichkeitsfahndung gegen Antifaschist*innen gestartet, gegen die es wegen schweren Landfriedensbruchs ermittelt. Damit droht ein neuer Dammbruch, indem dieses schwer wiegende Repressionsinstrument inflationär gegen Linke eingesetzt werden könnte.

Initiiert hat die Fahndung die Kriminalpolizei Heidelberg, der das regionale Dezernat Staatsschutz – die Politische Polizei – angegliedert ist. Sie ermittelt gegen rund 40 Antifaschist*innen, die an einer körperlichen Auseinandersetzung mit Rechten am 29. August 2026 in Mannheim beteiligt gewesen sein sollen. Der konkrete Straftatbestand, der ihnen vorgeworfen wird, ist schwerer Landfriedensbruch – ein Pauschalvorwurf, der einen individuellen Tatnachweis obsolet macht und die bloße Anwesenheit in einer Gruppe verfolgt. Der Paragraf wird häufig angewandt, um nach Demonstrationen oder anderen Aktionen dutzende oder gar hunderte Aktivist*innen zu kriminalisieren.

Indem auf der Homepage des Landeskriminalamts 13 Fotos von Beschuldigten veröffentlicht wurden, ist eine neue Stufe der Repression gegen Antifaschist*innen erreicht: Nur vereinzelt wurde diese massive Maßnahme bisher im Kontext von linken Protesten eingesetzt. Dass es hier in erster Linie um Einschüchterung und Abschreckung geht, zeigte eine erste Hausdurchsuchung in diesem Verfahrenskomplex, bei der die Einsatzkräfte rabiat auftraten.

„Dass das Landeskriminalamt Baden-Württemberg die Beschuldigten an den Online-Pranger stellt, zeigt, dass im Kampf gegen Antifaschismus alle Dämme brechen“, erklärte Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe e. V. „Ob nach Blockaden, Demonstrationen und Aktionen, ob bei Öffentlichkeitsarbeit oder schlichtweg gegen antifaschistische Einrichtungen und Infrastruktur: Kaum ein Repressionsinstrument wird ausgelassen, um Aktivist*innen und die gesamte Bewegung einzuschüchtern und von weiterem Engagement abzuhalten. Umso wichtiger ist es, die Betroffenen nicht alleinzulassen, sondern im Repressionsfall solidarisch zu unterstützen. Wir sind alle Antifa!“

title: Şair Nihat Ziyalan son şiirlerinden birini Deniz Göktaş için yazdı
content:
Türkiye edebiyatının usta isimlerinden, tiyatro ve sinema oyuncusu, şair Nihat Ziyalan’ın vefatından kısa süre önce kaleme aldığı son eserlerinden biri okuyucularla buluştu. Hayatının uzun bir bölümünü Avustralya’da sürdüren ancak Türkiye ile bağını hiç koparmayan Ziyalan, geçtiğimiz yaz tutuklanarak Çorlu’daki yüksek güvenlikli cezaevinde 88 gün kalan komedyen Deniz Göktaş için bir şiir yazdı.

Ziyalan’ın imgesel bir dille ördüğü şiir, Deniz Göktaş ile açık kaynaklarda "kız arkadaşı" olarak anılan, doğaçlama, beden dili ve mizahı buluşturan "clown" (palyaço) sanatçısı Cemre Kaboğlu arasındaki ilişkiyi merkeze alıyor.

Oksijen'den Sedat Ergin'in yazısına göre; şiir, komedyen Deniz Göktaş kuyu tipi tek kişilik hücresindeyken, palyaço olan sevgilisinin Göktaş’ın giysilerini koklaya koklaya giymesi ve taklalarla sokağa atılarak önüne gelen herkesi öpüp burnunun kırmızısıyla boyamasıyla açılıyor. Bu hareketin yaydığı sıcaklığın hapishane duvarlarını aşıp Göktaş’ın hücresine ulaşması, yalıtılmış ve sese hasret hücreye kuş cıvıltılarının akmasıyla devam ediyor. Hücresinde üşümekte olan komedyen ısınırken, kuyunun dibinde ürettiği şakaları koğuşlardaki arkadaşlarına gönderiyor ve nihayetinde hapishaneyi sallayan kahkahalarla sarsılan tablo, şiirin finalindeki şu dizelerle noktalanıyor:

"vız gelir / günler aylar yıllar..."

Nihat Ziyalan, ölümünden yaklaşık bir ay önce, 7 Eylül tarihinde Sydney’de düzenlenen “Kaktüs Buluşması” adlı edebiyat etkinliğinde Aziz Nesin üzerine bir konuşma yapmış ve hitabının sonunda bu şiirini okumuştu. YouTube’da da yer alan konuşmasında, "Türkiye’de korkunç haksızlıklar oluyor… Deniz Göktaş da bana şiir yazdırdı" ifadelerini kullanan şair, eserinin iki ay sonra Sözcükler dergisinde yayımlanacağını belirtmişti.

Düzenli olarak şiirlerini yayımladığı, iki ayda bir çıkan Sözcükler dergisinin Kasım-Aralık sayısı, Nihat Ziyalan’ın bu son şiiriyle raflardaki yerini aldı. 11 Ekim’de 90 yaşında hayata veda eden şair, şiirinin yayımlandığını göremedi. Derginin yayıncısı ve yönetmeni Turgay Fişekçi, yayımlanan şiirin sonuna düştüğü notta, "İşte yayımlandı Nihat Ağabey" ifadeleriyle şaire veda etti.

bunlara karşı dik duruşlu palyaço sevgilisi

palyaço maskaralığıyla torbadan çıkarıp

şakacının üstündeyken kucaklaştığını

kuyu denen tek kişilik hücresinde Göktaş

sevdiğinin eliyle giydirildiğini hissetti

birden kuş cıvıltısı akmaya başladı

koğuşlarda yatan arkadaşlarına yolladı

title: Van'da kar yağışı ulaşımı aksattı: 97 yerleşim yerinin yolu kapandı
content:
Van — Van'da etkili olan kar yağışı nedeniyle 68 mahalle ve 29 mezra yolu, ulaşıma kapandı. Kar yağışı ve olumsuz hava koşulları nedeniyle 6 ilçede taşımalı eğitime 1 gün ara verildi.

Van ve çevresinde dün akşam saatlerinde başlayıp, gece boyunca aralıklarla etkisini sürdüren kar yağışı, hayatı olumsuz etkiledi. Van-Bahçesaray kara yolu, kar ve tipi nedeniyle ulaşıma kapatılırken; Çaldıran, Muradiye, Erciş, Gürpınar, İpekyolu ve Tuşba ilçelerinde taşımalı eğitime 1 gün ara verildi. Yoğun kar yağışı nedeniyle 68 mahalle ve 29 mezra yolu ulaşıma kapanırken, kar kalınlığı yüksek kesimlerde 20, kent merkezinde 10 santimetreyi aştı.

Kar yağışının ardından Van Büyükşehir Belediyesi ve merkez ilçe belediyelerine bağlı ekipler, karla mücadele çalışması başlattı. Ekipler, cadde ve sokaklarda kar küreme ve tuzlama çalışması yürüttü. Van Büyükşehir Belediyesi'nin kent genelindeki karla mücadele çalışmalarını bin 32 personel ve 450 iş makinesiyle sürdürdüğü belirtildi.

author: Duda Sousa
title: Agenda: maioridade penal volta à Câmara dos Deputados e Lula participa da COP31 na Turquia
content:
A redução da maioridade penal volta ao centro das discussões no Congresso Nacional esta semana. A Câmara dos Deputados terá três audiências públicas sobre o tema, entre terça e quarta-feira, 10 e 11 de novembro, enquanto avança a análise da PEC 32/2015, que propõe reduzir de 18 para 16 anos a idade de responsabilização criminal. 

O texto é relatado pelo deputado Mendonça Filho (PL-PE), que pretende apresentar seu parecer até o fim de novembro.

 A proposta tramita em comissão especial, presidida por Aluísio Mendes (Republicanos-MA). Os debates acontecem após o Senado aprovar, na semana passada, a PEC da Segurança Pública sem incluir a redução da maioridade penal na votação.




No Senado, o governo federal articula a instalação, ainda nesta semana, da comissão mista responsável por analisar a Medida Provisória que proíbe as bets no Brasil. 

Segundo o líder do governo no Congresso, senador Randolfe Rodrigues (PT-AP), a intenção é manter o texto integral da MP 1394/2026, editada por Lula em setembro

, sem abrir exceções para apostas esportivas ou jogos online, como o chamado jogo do tigrinho.




Na última quinta-feira, 5 de novembro, Randolfe afirmou que negociaria com os presidentes do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), e da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), a instalação do colegiado e a indicação de seus integrantes. O governo pretende aprovar a proposta ainda em 2026 e aponta o endividamento das famílias e os impactos das apostas na saúde pública como justificativas para a proibição. A medida já está em vigor, mas depende da aprovação do Congresso para continuar valendo.




No Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), 

o ministro Flávio Dino reúne representantes de trabalhadores, empresários e do governo, na terça-feira, 10 de novembro, para discutir os prazos de implementação do fim da escala 6×1

. A audiência de conciliação ocorre após a Confederação Nacional do Comércio (CNC) e a Confederação Nacional da Indústria (CNI) questionarem as regras de transição previstas na Emenda Constitucional 141, promulgada em outubro. As entidades empresariais defendem mais tempo para a adaptação, enquanto Dino já afirmou que a redução da jornada e a ampliação do repouso semanal não estão em negociação.




Fora de Brasília, 

o presidente Lula (PT) inicia esta semana a sua primeira viagem internacional após a reeleição, com destino à COP31, em Antália, na Turquia.

 Lula embarca na segunda-feira, 9 de novembro, e participa, quarta e quinta-feira, da cúpula de líderes da conferência climática da ONU. Na reunião, o Brasil entregará à presidência do encontro à Turquia, após sediar a COP30 em Belém. Na sexta-feira, 13 de novembro, Lula segue para as Filipinas, onde tem prevista uma visita de Estado antes de participar da Cúpula da Associação de Nações do Sudeste Asiático (Asean), marcada para os dias 14 e 15 de novembro.




Estão na agenda da semana de 9 a 13 de novembro:




DIREITOS HUMANOS







Câmara







Auxílio financeiro para famílias de pessoas com deficiência (CPD, 10/11, 13h)

: Deputados analisam projeto que prevê auxílio mensal de um salário mínimo para pais ou responsáveis por pessoas com deficiência moderada ou grave e por pessoas com doença rara incapacitante, observados critérios de renda.




Qualificação profissional para mulheres vítimas de violência (CE, 11/11, 10h):

 A comissão analisa proposta que amplia o acesso de grupos vulneráveis a programas de formação e inclusão produtiva. O PL 1692/2026 prevê prioridade para jovens em acolhimento institucional ou familiar no Pronatec e inclui mulheres em situação de violência doméstica, pessoas em situação de rua e jovens acolhidos entre os públicos prioritários do programa Acredita no Primeiro Passo.




Direitos humanos e democracia no currículo escolar (CE, 11/11, 10h):

 Os deputados analisam o PL 5275/2025, que propõe incluir no ensino fundamental e médio conteúdos sobre direitos humanos, cidadania, democracia, ética e participação popular.




Juventude, cultura e participação social (CEDES, 11/11, 17h):

 A audiência aborda o acesso de jovens negros, periféricos e indígenas à produção cultural, os impactos das plataformas digitais, a desinformação, a liberdade de expressão e as desigualdades no acesso ao esporte e ao lazer. 










STF







Violência patrimonial contra mulheres (11/11, 14h)

: A corte analisa as pautas ADPFs 1185 e 1241, que questionam a aplicação das chamadas escusas absolutórias previstas no Código Penal em casos de violência doméstica. Atualmente, essas regras podem afastar a punição de determinados crimes patrimoniais cometidos contra familiares.




Acesso policial a dados de celulares apreendidos (Julgamento virtual, 13/11):

 Ministros analisam pedidos de esclarecimento no ARE 1042075, relacionado ao Tema 977 da repercussão geral. A discussão envolve os limites para o acesso, pela polícia, a dados e mensagens armazenados em aparelhos celulares apreendidos durante investigações. 













POLÍTICA







STF







Distribuição de recursos federais aos estados (12/11, 14h30)

: Supremo realiza audiência de conciliação relacionada à ADI 5069, que discute os critérios de distribuição dos recursos do Fundo de Participação dos Estados e do Distrito Federal (FPE). A Corte prorrogou até junho de 2027 a aplicação das regras atuais e determinou a busca de uma solução negociada. 













EDUCAÇÃO







Câmara







Formação de professores para a educação inclusiva (CE, 11/11, 10h)

: Deputados analisam projeto que altera a legislação educacional para estabelecer medidas de formação continuada dos profissionais da educação voltadas à inclusão de estudantes com deficiência.




Cotas indígenas para professores da rede pública (CE, 11/11, 10h):

 Parlamentares analisam projeto que prevê a reserva de vagas para candidatos indígenas em concursos do magistério público da educação básica realizados em regiões com elevada concentração de povos indígenas. 













SAÚDE







Câmara







Saúde da mulher e atendimento oncológico (CSAUDE, 10/11, 10h)

: A audiência debate políticas de prevenção, diagnóstico e tratamento do câncer entre mulheres e reúne representantes de entidades de apoio às pacientes e convidados de órgãos como o Ministério da Saúde, o Instituto Nacional de Câncer (Inca) e a Agência Nacional de Saúde Suplementar (ANS).




Tratamento de acondroplasia pelo SUS (CPD, 10/11, 13h):

 Deputados analisam requerimento de informações ao Ministério da Saúde sobre a decisão de não incorporar a vosoritida ao Sistema Único de Saúde para o tratamento da acondroplasia, condição genética que afeta o crescimento ósseo.




Saúde mental e alimentação saudável na infância (CE, 11/11, 10h):

 A Comissão discute a criação de uma Política Nacional de Promoção do Desenvolvimento Integral da Infância e Adolescência. O projeto prevê ações voltadas à saúde mental, ao direito de brincar e à alimentação saudável.
















Agenda da semana da

 

Pública

 

é um serviço apresentado aos leitores, concebido com base nas informações dos portais da Câmara, Senado e STF

title: Gazze'de göçük altında kalan çadırlarda 5 kişi hayatını kaybetti. Arama kurtarma çalışması sürüyor
content:
Gazze Şeridi'nin orta kesiminde yer alan Deyr el-Belah kentinde yerinden edilmiş Filistinlilerin kaldığı çadırların yağış sonrası meydana gelen göçük altında kalması sonucu biri kadın, 3'ü çocuk 5 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiği bildirildi.

Gazze'deki Sivil Savunma Müdürlüğünün Sözcüsü Mahmud Basal, yaptığı açıklamada, Deyr el-Belah kentinde yerinden edilmiş Filistinlilerin kaldığı çadırların yağmurun taşıdığı kum ve kayaların altında kaldığını söyledi.

Sivil savunma ekiplerinin vatandaşların yardımıyla anında arama kurtarma çalışmalarına başladığını belirten Basal, göçükte ölü ve yaralıların olduğunu ifade etti.

Öte yandan Sivil Savunma Müdürlüğünün Telegram hesabından yapılan açıklamada da Deyr el-Belah'ta göçük altında kalan çadırların enkazından 5 vatandaşın cansız bedenine ulaşıldığı ve arama kurtarma çalışmalarının devam ettiği kaydedildi.

Bölgedeki AA muhabirinin yerel kaynaklardan edindiği bilgiye göre, göçükte yaşamını yitirenler arasında bir kadın ve 3 çocuk bulunuyor.

Gazze'deki hükümetin Medya Ofisinden dün yapılan açıklamada, Gazze Şeridi'nde 12 saat içinde 70 bin çadırın su altında kaldığı, şiddetli yağışlar nedeniyle onlarca duvarın yıkıldığı belirtilmişti.

İsrail’in Ekim 2023'ten bu yana soykırım gerçekleştirdiği Gazze'de binaların yüzde 80'den fazlası yıkıldı veya ağır hasar gördü.

Konutların büyük bölümünün kullanılamaz hale gelmesi nedeniyle Gazze nüfusunun ezici çoğunluğu derme çatma çadırlarda yaşam mücadelesi veriyor. Gazze'de kış mevsiminin bastırmasıyla birlikte yüz binlerce kişinin sığındığı çadırlar şiddetli yağışlar nedeniyle sular altında kaldı.

İsrail, ağırlaşan hava koşullarına rağmen konteyner, barınma malzemesi ve temel insani yardımların bölgeye girişini engellemeyi sürdürürken, ateşkes anlaşması kapsamındaki insani yükümlülüklerini de ihlal etmeye devam ediyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: winter oak
title: True anarchy will banish the psychopaths
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here




I wrote a 

piece

 in September about the roots of the word “anarchy” and wondered “if the deep meaning of anarchy is, in fact, our human struggle against vitaphobic, authoritarian and psychopathic forces known as archons”. [1]




The Swedish writer 

Per Shapiro

 [2] subsequently sent me a pdf of a 2014 essay by John Lamb Lash on the archons of gnostic tradition in which he likewise presents anarchy as the antidote to their domination.




In ‘

The True Anarchy of Life on Earth

‘ Lash writes of “the scheme of the Archon mind-parasites to insinuate themselves into human reality and take it over, making humans become like them, robotic, slavish, incapable of intention, discovery, or novelty”. [3]




He stresses: “To fall under the spell of the Authorities is to concede power to their false magic: under the power of deception, we deceive ourselves about what power really is and lose all sense of our own power”. [4]




In order to resist this rule we need to embrace anarchy in the 

real

 [5] sense of the word: “We cannot realize our true humanity without beating the Authorities. There is more than one way to do so, but the central and decisive way is to choose anarchy in defiance of 

any

 authority that does not demonstrate benevolence toward life in all forms… Even the word carries the essential message: an-arch, ‘against authority, against archons'”. [6]










Lash equates the gnostic version of the archons with “globalist predators and serial killers, who are one and the same breed of conniving, murderous deviants”. [7]




Wondering what makes them so different from us, and how they achieve their deception and control, he suggests: “Archons and their human counterparts gain control over humanity through a particular ‘seizure’ that operates in the back of the brain and in the field of peripheral vision simultaneously” – this involves the “reptilian brain 

in its deviant or exaggerated mode

“. [8]




“In large measure, the quasi-magical or occult power attributed to globalist perpetrators is a hoax, operating under the Wizard of Oz effect. Note that to enforce their presumed magical powers, the perpetrators need to exert enormous continual efforts of two kinds: brainwashing through the media, and threat of force through the military.




“Without a constant dual-barreled barrage, requiring the complicity of human beings to suppress and deceive their fellow creatures, their vaunted magic would quickly fade and dissipate…




“In reality, the NEWOs [New World Order psychopaths] can only sustain the 

illusion

 of magical supremacy as long as they suppress and deviate human potential, where the true magic abides: that is, 

in our species’ innate capacity for interactive magic with the animating powers of the planetary goddess

. Unless the NEWOs can suppress 

that

 capacity in a brutal manner all the time, it will naturally and spontaneously assert itself”. [9]










This is how I also see anarchy – as the life force within humankind, constantly surging forth in each new generation and trying to break out of the industrial-imperial prison in which we have been locked up for so long.




Of course, the system has to lie about what anarchy is, as Lash sets out. “The supreme moral illusion confronting humanity operates like this: those who falsely assume authority over others demand obedience to their commands 

on the claim that disobedience would result in social chaos and anarchy

.




“They claim to preserve social and moral order by rules and constraints imposed and maintained by sheer brutal force. The self-assumed authorities propagate the belief that human beings, left to their own impulses, would produce a world of disorder, conflict, and chaos.




“We are all potential terrorists in the mind of the Authorities. In our natural state of freedom and autonomy, we are dangerous to ourselves and must be curbed, leashed, and protected by a higher power. In short, the self-declared authorities claim to save humanity from the chaotic or anarchistic tendencies of human nature”. [10]




But in fact, as anarchists are always pointing out, 

normal

 human nature is not the same as that of the globalist deviants. Lash states: “The evidence that people act from innate goodness, without having to be told to do so, is strong enough, and it stands in contrast to guilt-driven action which has to be contrived and enforced from without – by threat of eternal damnation, for instance”. [11]




He is on similar territory in his analysis to Andrew M. Lobaczewski in his book 

Political Ponerology: A science on the nature of evil adjusted for political purposes

 which I wrote about in October 2025 in an essay entitled ‘

The psychopaths in power

‘. [12]










The Polish author says of such people: “They become experts in our weaknesses and sometimes effect heartless experiments. The suffering and injustice they cause inspire no guilt within them, since such reactions from others are simply a result of their being different and apply only to ‘those other’ people they perceive to be not quite conspecific”. [13]




And I was pleased to see that Lash recommends Lobaczewski’s work in his essay, explaining: “Derived from the Greek word 

poneria

 found in Gnostic writings, ponerology is the diagnosis and deconstruction of the causes and mechanisms of social evil.




“Lobaczewski uses the striking term 

pathocracy

 to describe the domination of a society by a faction of psychopathic members, estimated to be 4-5 percent of the population”. [14]




The great champion of life and humanity against the archons, in the gnostic tradition, is Sophia, the goddess of wisdom, to whom I dedicated a 

series of articles

 in 2024. [15]




The Nag Hammadi library (the “Gnostic Gospels”) consists of early Christian and gnostic texts discovered near the Upper Egyptian town of Nag Hammadi in 1945. There, in the 

Apocryphon of John

, Sophia declares of the archons: “The tree of their design is bitterness and its branches are darkened by death. Its leaves are hatred and deception, and its aroma reeks of evil (

poneria

)”. [16]










Lash writes: “Perhaps even the wisdom goddess herself did not anticipate how far the Archons would penetrate human reality and deviate the divine experiment she previsioned for the Anthropos.




“This might explain, in mythological terms, why it takes until the last minute before she catches the error and initiates her correction. 

On the Origin of the World

“In this scenario, Sophia, before she morphs into the earth, foresees a moment when the Archontic powers will be defeated, 

the moment of the consummation of their works

. In other words, their defeat comes at the moment of extreme desperation when they complete their agenda, the eleventh hour”. [17]




I, for one, am very much looking forward to the day when humankind is inspired into magical action by the life-affirming force of anarchy and the psychopathic archons are finally thrown into what Lash describes as “the gravity well (abyss) of the inanimate planetary system”! [18]

author: Brian Hioe
title: May Chin Indictment Gestures Toward Extensive Reach of Chinese United Front Work
content:
INDEPENDENT PAN-BLUE legislator Kao Chin Su Mei, also known as May Chin or Ciwas Ali, and who is an Indigenous legislator of the Atayal people, has been indicted for Chinese United Front work. According to prosecutors, Chin accepted more than 170 million NTD, which was funneled to organizations, relatives, and other bodies in order to conduct influence operations aimed at winning elections. Prosecutors are seeking 14 years for Chin, who was previously facing charges about illegally importing Chinese COVID-19 vaccines for distribution among her constituents.

The networks of these organizations were managed by her office director, Chang Chun-chieh, and legislative assistants Chen Chih-huang and Lin Yi-chun. Chang is currently under investigation for having fled overseas by boat in order to avoid arrest, with authorities conducting raids earlier this month to find the vessel on which he escaped. Chang and Chen reportedly coordinated United Front efforts, while Lin acted as an intermediary with China. Chin has been accused of using her influence as a legislator in order to influence government policy in arms sales, defense, cross-strait relations, and international relations.

For her part, Chin has denied participation in such United Front work, suggesting that she did not need Chinese support to win elections. Chin also raised questions about why she was apparently under surveillance for two decades before authorities acted on it, instead framing charges against her as politically motivated persecution by the Lai administration.

Rumors about Chin’s involvement in United Front efforts targeting Indigenous communities have been longstanding. China has long directed United Front outreach toward Indigenous communities, with the hopes that they will vote pan-Blue, as has often historically been the case. Such United Front outreach also aims to show Indigenous communities the benefits of unification with China, often by touting the supposed benefits that ethnic minority communities receive in China.

If Chin has finally been targeted by authorities, it is to be seen to what extent the KMT rallies behind her. Though Chin is a pan-Blue independent, she caucuses with the KMT and is generally understood to act in concert with the party. But it is possible that prosecutors will also take action on cases of other pan-Blue legislators who receive support from China. One notes that KMT legislative caucus leader Fu Kun-chi has faced charges of receiving campaign merchandise to be distributed among potential voters that was supplied by China. As Fu’s political network is rooted in Indigenous-heavy Hualien, it is possible that there are further ties to Chinese United Front work by him or other KMT politicians.

At the same time, it is also to be seen how the general public understands prosecution against Chin or other KMT legislators. Certainly, the public was willing to accept prosecution against former Taipei mayor Ko Wen-je on corruption charges, as well as other pan-Blue figures who have faced corruption charges, such as former Yilan magistrate Lin Zi-miao. But it remains to be seen whether they accept the validity of charges against Chin and other pan-Blue legislators implicated in United Front activity.

title: COP31 a fermî îro dest pê dike
content:
Lijneya giştî ya vekirinê ya fermî ya COP31ê, dê di saet 10.00î de li Qada EXPOyê, li Salona Lijneya Giştî ya Anadoluyê pêk were. Di lijneya giştî de Wezîrê Jîngeh, Bajarvanî û Guherîna Avhewayê Murat Kurum dê axaftina vekirinê bike.




Di çarçoveya konferansê de, bi beşdariya nûnerên nêzîkî 200 welatî, dê sernavên di rojeva avhewayê ya cîhanî de, di serî de têkoşîna li dijî guherîna avhewayê, kêmkirina emîsyonan, polîtîkayên lihevhatinê û fînansekirina avhewayê werin nîqaşkirin.



















Bermahiyên plastîk ên YEyê diherikin Tirkiyeyê: 2025 rekora dîrokî ye




3 Hezîran 2026










Mijara roja yekem a konferansê: Xurak, çandinî û tenduristî




Roja yekem a konferansê ji bo mijara "Xurak, Çandinî û Tenduristiyê" hat terxankirin. Di tevahiya rojê de, dê hêza sîstemên çandinî û xurakê li dijî guherîna avhewayê, bikaranîna bi bandor a çavkaniyên avê û bandorên qeyrana avhewayê yên li ser tenduristiya gel, di rûniştinên cihêreng de werin nirxandin.




Di çalakiya ku dê saet 11.00î de li Pavîlyona Awistralyayê ya li Herêma Şîn pêk were de, rêxistinên civaka sivîl ên ji Tirkiye û Awistiralyayê dê daxwazên xwe yên ji bo dûrketina ji sotemeniyên fosîl bînin ziman. Mazûvaniya COP31ê Tirkiye dike û serokatiya danûstandinan jî Awistiralya dike. Di vê rûniştina konferansê de nûnerên civaka sivîl ên ji herdu welatan dê bên cem hev û tê payîn ku berpirsiyariyên her du welatan ên di pêvajoya derketina ji sotemeniyên fosîl de bên gotûbêjkirin.




Di çalakiyên din ên rojê de, veguherîna enerjiyê ya edil, fînansekirina avhewayê, veguherîna torên ceyranê û erkên dewletan ên di çarçoveya hiqûqa navneteweyî ya avhewayê de dê werin nîqaşkirin.




Lûtkeya lîderan di 11ê Mijdarê de ye




Lûtkeya Lîderan a Antalyayê ku di çarçoveya COP31ê de bi beşdariya serokên dewlet û hikûmetan dê bê lidarxistin, di navbera 11-12ê Mijdarê de pêk were. Di lûtkeya ku bi mazûvaniya Serokkomar Recep Tayyip Erdogan tê lidarxistin de, tê payîn ku serokên cîhanî pêşîniyên xwe yên têkildarî têkoşîna li dijî guherîna avhewayê û sozên xwe parve bikin. 




Tê plankirin ku danûstandinên COP31ê yên ku dê du hefteyan bidomin, di 20ê Mijdarê de bi dawî bibin.




Lûtkeya avhewayê ya gelan di 14ê Mijdarê de dest pê dike




Lûtkeya Avhewayê ya Gelan ji çar aliyên cîhanê  parêzvanên edaleta avhewayê li hev kom dike.  Lûtkeya Avhewayê ya Gelan di 14ê Mijdarê de dest pê bike. Beşdarvan dê di 14ê Mijdarê Roja Çalakiya Cîhanî de bi mîtîngek vekirinê bikin.




Foruma Edaleta Avhewayê di 15ê Mijdarê de ye




Foruma Edaleta Avhewayê di çarçoveya çalakiyên ku wekî alternatîfek ji bo COP31ê tê lidarxistin. Forum dê li Antalyayê mazûvaniya ji gelek mafparêzan bike.




(Mİ/AY)

title: MED TUHAD-FED: Son iki yılda 15 hasta mahpus yaşamını yitirdi
content:
MED Tutuklu ve Hükümlü Aileleri ile Hukuki ve Dayanışma Dernekleri Federasyonu (MED TUHAD-FED), son iki yılda cezaevlerinde 15 hasta mahpusun yaşamını yitirdiğini açıkladı. Federasyon, ağır hasta mahpusların sağlık durumlarına rağmen tahliye edilmediğini belirterek Adalet Bakanlığına çağrıda bulundu.



















Hasta mahpus Tuncer Sağlam toprağa verildi




8 Kasım 2026










Mezopotamya Ajansının haberine göre, cezaevinde bulunduğu sırada ağır sağlık sorunları yaşayan ve tedavi gördüğü hastanede hayatını kaybeden Tuncer Sağlam'ın ardından federasyon temsilcileri cezaevlerindeki hak ihlallerini değerlendirdi.




MED TUHAD-FED Eşbaşkanı Kerem Canpolat ile yönetim kurulu üyeleri Mahsum Oruç ve Şafi Hayme, Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci kapsamında cezaevlerindeki koşulların iyileştirilmesi ve hasta tutukluların tahliyesi için somut adımlar atılmasını istedi.




“Cezaevlerinde yüzlerce hasta mahpus var”




Federasyon Eşbaşkanı Kerem Canpolat, devam eden siyasi sürecin toplumda umut yarattığını ancak cezaevlerindeki koşullara olumlu bir etkisinin olmadığını söyledi.




Cezaevlerinde sağlık sorunları nedeniyle günlük ihtiyaçlarını tek başına karşılayamayan yüzlerce mahpus bulunduğunu belirten Canpolat, kanser ve kronik hastalıkları olan kişilerin uygun tedavi koşullarına erişemediğini ifade etti.




Canpolat, bazı mahpusların cezaevinde kalamayacaklarına ilişkin sağlık raporlarına rağmen tahliye edilmediklerini söyledi.




Cezaevlerinde hem adli hem de siyasi mahpusların hak ihlallerine maruz kaldığını söyleyen Canpolat, devletin tutukluların yaşamını ve sağlığını koruma yükümlülüğünü hatırlattı.



















73 yaşındaki hasta tutuklu Abdullah Tırpan yaşamını yitirdi




26 Ekim 2026










“Her ölüm toplumdaki güveni zedeliyor”




Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci'nin başlamasından bu yana cezaevlerinde 15 hasta mahpusun yaşamını yitirdiğini belirten Canpolat, sağlık hakkına erişim ve tahliye uygulamalarının yeniden düzenlenmesi gerektiğini söyledi.




Canpolat, cezaevlerindeki ölümlerin toplumsal güveni de olumsuz etkilediğini belirterek sürecin ilerleyebilmesi için devletin somut adımlar atması gerektiğini ifade etti.




Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi (AİHM) kararlarının uygulanmamasını da eleştiren Canpolat, hasta tutukluların tedavilerinin cezaevi dışında, ailelerinin yanında sürdürülmesini talep etti.



















İzmir Barosu, hasta mahpus Yıldırım'ı ziyaret etti: "Zamana yayılmış idam cezası"




27 Ağustos 2026










“400 ila 500 ağır hasta mahpus bulunuyor”




MED TUHAD-FED Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Mahsum Oruç, cezaevlerinde 400 ila 500 arasında ağır hasta tutuklu bulunduğunu belirtti.




Oruç, sağlık sorunları nedeniyle cezaevinde kalamayacak durumda olan kişilerin tahliyesinin çeşitli idari ve hukuki uygulamalarla engellendiğini söyledi.




Yaklaşık dört ay önce TBMM'de kabul edilen yasal düzenlemeye işaret eden Oruç, düzenlemenin uygulanmasının çeşitli kurulların değerlendirmelerine bağlı tutulduğunu ve bu nedenle tahliyelerin gerçekleşmediğini söyledi.




Oruç, söz konusu düzenlemenin etkili biçimde uygulanması halinde Tuncer Sağlam'ın yaşamını yitirmemiş olabileceğini ifade etti.




Tuncer Sağlam'ın ölümü




Federasyon temsilcileri, Tuncer Sağlam'ın sağlık durumunun ağır olmasına rağmen tahliye edilmediğini belirtti.




Sağlam'ın avukatı tarafından 23 Eylül'de yapılan tahliye başvurusunda, vücudunda 10 santimetrelik kitle bulunduğu, damar invazyonu ve olası metastaz bulgularının tespit edildiği aktarıldı. Sağlam, 7 Kasım'da tedavi gördüğü hastanede yaşamını yitirdi.




Mahsum Oruç, Sağlam'ın yaklaşık iki yıldır cezaevinde bulunduğunu ve sağlık durumunun yetkililer tarafından bilindiğini belirterek gerekli tedavinin sağlanmadığını savundu.



















TAHLİYESİ ÜÇÜNCÜ KEZ ERTELENDİ




Hasta mahpus Mehmet Sait Yıldırım kalp krizi geçirdi




25 Ağustos 2026










“Tahliyeler için mekanizmalar oluşturulmalı”




MED TUHAD-FED Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Şafi Hayme de hasta mahpusların tahliyesi için gerekli mekanizmaların kısa sürede oluşturulabileceğini söyledi.




Hayme, ağır hasta mahpusların sağlık raporlarına rağmen tahliye edilmemesini eleştirerek Adalet Bakanlığı, Ceza ve Tevkifevleri Genel Müdürlüğü ve cezaevi yönetimlerinin sorumluluklarına dikkat çekti.




Sağlık sorunları nedeniyle günlük yaşamlarını sürdüremeyen mahpusların cezaevinde tutulmasının yaşam hakkı açısından ciddi sonuçlar doğurduğunu belirten Hayme, tedaviye erişimin sağlanmasını ve tahliye süreçlerinin hızlandırılmasını istedi.




Federasyon, hasta mahpusların sağlık durumlarının bağımsız ve etkili biçimde değerlendirilmesi, tahliyelerin önündeki engellerin kaldırılması ve tedavilerinin uygun koşullarda sürdürülmesi çağrısını yineledi.




(FY)

author: Önder Algedik
title: Seven things you must never say about COP31
content:
COP31 opened in Antalya on November 9 and its two hosts — Türkiye and Australia — have been busy.

Australia’s Labor government, despite being elected on promises to act for the climate, has approved 37 new or expanded fossil fuel projects since 2022.

Since September 2025 it has signed 19 fossil fuel agreements: 20-year liquefied natural gas (LNG) contracts, oil and gas exploration pacts with ExxonMobil, Chevron and TotalEnergies, drilling rights from Syria to Somalia, and a deal with Australia’s Woodside.

On top of those come six nuclear and mining agreements, three of them were signed in Seoul on November 3, six days before the summit opened.

One host approves the projects. The other signs the contracts. Together they will run a summit whose Action Agenda does not name coal, oil or gas even once.

Everything is going smoothly. In Türkiye, censorship helps; at least 1270 X accounts were blocked in September alone and, over the past 20 months, trustees have been appointed to 10 television channels.

So, to keep the hosts comfortable, here are seven things you must never talk about.

1. Don’t talk about fossil philanthropy

In June, the foundations of the companies that change Türkiye’s climate the most, including a refinery, car factory, coal power plant, an electricity distributor and even the operator of Antalya airport, set up “Philanthropy for Climate”. They invited environmental groups to the table. The polluters bring the money; civil society brings the legitimacy. Australians who have watched gas companies sponsor festivals and sport will know the model.

2. Don’t talk about the COP31 bill

COP31 is expected to cost close to US$2 billion. When the host agreement came before Türkiye's parliament in July, one party wrote a dissenting opinion and then abstained. Only five MPs voted “No”. An agreement that cost to the public up to US$2 billion bill passed in near silence.

COP31 is, in a sense, a rubbish summit; “Zero waste” heads its list of themes. In August, as rubbish washed up along the Mediterranean coast, the national debate was only about waste imported from Britain. Meanwhile, according to Türkiye’s statistics office, more than 10 million tonnes of waste was burned in 2024. The sky became the landfill.

4. Don't talk about the fossil deals

Has anyone at COP31 mentioned the deals Türkiye signed while preparing to host it? The energy minister posed for photos at every ceremony. A 20-year LNG contract with Mercuria. Exploration in the Black Sea and Eastern Mediterranean with ExxonMobil and TotalEnergies. A global partnership with Chevron, from Iraq to Venezuela. A stake in Kirkuk’s oil fields. Rights to drill in Syria, Libya, Somalia and Pakistan. And Woodside’s LNG.

When I counted in October, there were 14. Now there are 19.

5. Don’t talk about cities without resilience

On October 14, Istanbul, Sakarya, Kocaeli, Yalova, Muğla and Antalya went under water on the same day. The minister of urbanisation, who is also COP31 president, called it a “disaster”, blamed climate change and moved the topic onto the summit’s “Resilient Cities” theme. Were these resilient cities or cities stripped of their resilience? Between 2002 and 2021, Türkiye laid 603 million tonnes of asphalt and poured close to a billion tonnes of cement. If you must, talk only about river beds and pretend the valley slopes above them were never paved. In three days, everyone forgets.

6. Say ‘conference’, not ‘fair’

COP stands for Conference of the Parties. But it has become a Fair of the Parties. The minister announced that 1.5 million visitors are expected! That is not a venue for negotiation; it is an exhibition ground. As I argued last month, the stands will be busy and the products green. Never call it a fair. Say “climate summit”, a phrase with no actor and no action.

Say “coal phase-out”, but never mention oil. Ask for a coal exit date, which buys the government time. Don’t touch the summit’s global business partner, Koç Holding, which owns Türkiye's oil refineries. Call gas a “bridge fuel”. Australians know this one: Labor’s Future Gas Strategy says gas will be needed to 2050 and beyond.

So here are the seven things we must not talk about: Fossil philanthropy, the public bill, a country turned into a dump, fossil deals, asphalt-and-concrete cities, a summit turned trade fair, and oil and gas.

Nobody has to ban any of this, because we already don’t talk about it. We don't talk about the groups that sit at the table with fossil foundations. We don’t talk about asphalt and concrete, because their owners would come next.

We write reports about the changing climate, not about those who change it.

In Antalya there will be plenty of talk about “climate change”, with no subject and no verb. There will be no talk of 37 approvals in Canberra and 19 signatures in Ankara. No talk of three fossil fuels and two fossil infrastructures: coal, oil, gas, asphalt and concrete. Because if anyone talked about them, the conversation would arrive at the one policy both hosts share: the fossil order.

So, talk about it. In Sydney, in the Pacific and in Antalya. Thirty-seven and 19 new or expanded fossil fuel projects. Count them out loud.

[Önder Algedik is a climate researcher and activist with 350Ankara. His new book, Ya Fosil Düzen Ya Devrim (Fossil Order or Revolution), is published by İletişim.]

author: TJ Jordan and Cécile Marchand
title: How a French Oil Executive Is Working With the Trump Administration to ‘Kill’ Europe’s Methane Plan
content:
A TotalEnergies executive is working with U.S. officials to delay the implementation of new European Union methane rules, raising questions over the company’s pledges to tackle leaks of the potent greenhouse gas.




François-Régis Mouton, formerly vice-president of gas advocacy at TotalEnergies, has been representing the International Association of Oil and Gas Producers (IOGP), a London-based fossil fuel lobby group, on an assignment from the French oil giant since 2018.




Mouton has repeatedly shared and engaged with hard right, anti-renewable energy and climate science-denial content on his personal social media, a review by DeSmog and French environmental newsroom Vert found.




Mouton, who serves as IOGP’s Europe managing director, met with U.S. federal officials on at least three occasions to discuss the European Union Methane Regulation (EUMR) in the past 14 months, according to social media posts. The new framework would force oil and gas importers to meet certain standards for methane leaks in their supply chains or face big fines.




In October 2025, Mouton visited the White House to brief the National Energy Dominance Council, a pro-fossil fuel Trump administration advisory body, on how the IOGP could “work together to address and remove regulatory barriers such as…the #EUMethaneRegulation,” according to LinkedIn 

posts

 by Mouton and the council’s executive director Jarrod Agen.




This year, U.S. officials have repeatedly cited IOGP arguments for delaying the regulations after meeting with Mouton, including in a 27 April 

op-ed

 in the Financial Times by U.S. Ambassador to the EU Andrew Puzder headlined “The EU’s methane regulation could spark an energy crisis.” Puzder’s office sent an email, seen by DeSmog and Vert, to EU member states on 20 October, which similarly echoed IOGP language warning that the regulations could threaten gas supplies to Europe.




These incidents form part of a wider pattern of closed-door meetings and public statements that place Mouton in a key role in campaigns by the Trump administration and oil industry to delay the rules by at least three years, according to a DeSmog-Vert review of social media feeds, freedom of information requests, industry documents and interviews.




Mouton assumed this role despite his employer TotalEnergies and its CEO Patrick Pouyanné spending the past decade painting the company as a leader on methane action and publicly backing the EU Methane Regulation. Pouyanné is one of three top oil industry figures championing the Oil and Gas Decarbonization Charter, a voluntary initiative to curb greenhouse gas emissions from across the sector, which is due to launch a status update at the UN climate conference COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, which opens today.




By sponsoring trade groups such as the IOGP, TotalEnergies can work at arm’s length to delay, weaken and ideally defeat the regulation altogether, according to sources involved in industry discussions of the rules.




“They are coming to kill this regulation,” said one of the sources, who spoke on the condition of anonymity for fear of professional repercussions.




On Friday, the European Council — made up of heads of state or government of the EU’s 27 countries — 

endorsed

 a European Commission proposal for a one-year delay in implementing the rules, which had been due to take effect on 1 January, 2027. The Council will now have to negotiate the final decision with the 720-seat European Parliament, which has voted for a three-year delay amid the fossil fuel industry lobbying.






















 













 



















This story was published in partnership with French environmental newsroom 

Vert

 

and the 

EUobserver

.




 




 
















‘Emergency Brake’




The U.S. has been 

on track

 to eclipse Norway as Europe’s biggest supplier of natural gas — used to heat tens of millions of the continent’s homes and power industry — since the February, 2022 invasion of Ukraine prompted the bloc to seek alternatives to Russian supplies.




TotalEnergies imports more American liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Europe than any of its rivals, 

according

 to research and advocacy group Oil Change International.




Methane, the main component of natural gas, has a heating effect on earth’s atmosphere more than 80 times stronger than carbon dioxide over 20 years. Scientists say that urgent action to stop plumes of the gas 

seeping

 from the fossil fuel industry’s sprawling networks of pipelines, wellheads, storage tanks, and transport vessels represents a potential ’emergency brake’ to help slow the climate crisis.




The IOGP — whose members include oil majors ExxonMobil, Chevron, BP and Shell — says it backs methane regulation in principle but has spearheaded the industry’s calls for a three-year delay to clarify the new rules. 




Rapidly implementing the regulations in their strictest form could avoid around 80 million tonnes of methane emissions by 2050, according to a 

study

 by Berlin-based think tank DIW. This would prevent 155,000 premature deaths and produce €700 billion in climate, health and economic benefits. Delaying the rules by three years, in line with industry demands, would lead to 40,000 premature deaths and cost the EU €185 billion worth of benefits, according to the study, which was funded by the European Climate Foundation. 




The lobbying over methane is the latest sign of 

transatlantic coordination

 between the Trump administration, which has gutted climate regulations, and corporations 

opposing key aspects

 of the EU’s environmental and 

climate plans

. The U.S. government is in the process of 

weakening

 or delaying a suite of 

rules

 to reduce methane emissions from the country’s oil and gas industry.




The campaign to slow the European regulations has continued even as colossal, climate-fuelled heatwaves 

killed tens of thousands of people

 across the continent during this year’s summer of record-breaking forest fires and droughts. Meanwhile, TotalEnergies and other oil majors have raked in bumper profits off the back of soaring oil prices due to the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran.




‘Climate Crisis Is a Fraud!’




Even as climate impacts have intensified, Mouton has appeared to downplay the urgency of the crisis, including by sharing a link to a book called 

There is No Climate Apocalypse

 on his personal Facebook account in June 2025. 




In January 2026, Mouton shared an extract from a speech by U.S. President Donald Trump branding European countries deploying wind turbines as “losers”. In a subsequent Facebook post this August, Mouton said that “loads of CO2” was emitted during the Middle Ages and that current climate science was “so binary”. As of late October, Mouton was a member of three Facebook groups which are forums for questioning human-caused climate change, including one called “Climate Crisis is a Fraud!”




A post from French oil lobbyist François-Régis Mouton’s Facebook account on 29 June, 2025. (Credit: Facebook/Vert)




Mouton has also shared content by far-right French Member of the European Parliament Sarah Knafo, as well as from a Facebook page called “Zemmour TV”, which promotes the views of Eric Zemmour — a politician convicted multiple times in France for racial discrimination, making racist statements, and inciting racial and religious hatred.




Zemmour and Knafo’s party Reconquête have promised sweeping Trump-style rollbacks of climate and environmental measures if voted into power in next year’s French general election, including cancelling a planned ban on new petrol car sales and state support for wind farms. 




Screenshot of a Facebook post from French oil lobbyist François-Régis Mouton’s Facebook account on 28 October, 2026. (Credit: Facebook/Vert)




The IOGP and Mouton declined an interview request and did not respond to questions about Mouton’s personal social media activity. Mouton’s Facebook account — previously public — was in private mode the day after the interview request.




In a statement, the IOGP said it backed the EU’s climate goals and that it has “never sought to weaken the Regulation’s objective and has never called for it to be scrapped.” It was important that policymakers “draw on industry expertise when developing energy and climate legislation,” the IOGP added.




TotalEnergies said it “does not comment on the personal views or content shared on personal social media accounts by employees.”




The company did not respond to questions about lobbying by trade associations such as the IOGP and said it was calling for an approach that balanced “the implementation of the Methane Regulation with energy security.” TotalEnergies pays the IOGP between €200,000 and €500,000 in membership fees each year, according to the company’s latest disclosures. 




The U.S. Department of Energy did not respond to a request for comment.




“Europe should be defending its citizens, not importing the politics of climate denial championed by the fossil fuel lobby and the far-right,” said Laurence Tubiana, director of the European Climate Foundation, a grant-making organisation headquartered in The Hague that supports hundreds of organisations working on climate action.




‘Breath of Fresh Air’




In 2022, amid rising awareness of the devastating climate impacts of methane, Mouton told IOGP members the organisation had begun publishing industry methane emissions reporting “so we can show what we’re doing,” according to a report to members obtained by DeSmog.




“Methane is a question of credibility for gas in Europe,” said Mouton in the memo. “This issue affects our 

license to operate

” — an industry term for companies enjoying enough public support to be able to continue with business as usual despite growing fears over the climate crisis.




The EU enshrined the methane regulations into law in August, 2024, providing the legal framework for penalties to be imposed from the beginning of 2027.




With the threat of regulation now very real, Mouton and the IOGP stepped up the pressure.




Mouton’s public support for the Trump administration’s opposition to the regulations can be traced to at least September 2025, when Mouton endorsed remarks by U.S. Energy Secretary 

Chris Wright

, himself a former fracking CEO, at an event in Brussels. Mouton said Wright was a “breath of fresh air” for telling the audience that the EU Methane Regulation should be “fixed,” 

according to

 European politics site Rapporteur.




The following month, in October 2025, Mouton emerged from his meeting with Trump’s National Energy Dominance Council emphasising the importance of collaboration to “remove regulatory barriers such as…the #EUMethaneRegulation,” according to the LinkedIn 

posts

 by Mouton and Agen, the council’s executive director.




A LinkedIn post by François-Régis Mouton, Europe director, IOGP in October, 2025, telling Jarrod Agen, executive director of the U.S. National Energy Dominance Council, that the respective organisations should collaborate to “remove” the EU methane regulations. (Credit: Vert/LinkedIn)




[From Left]: François-Régis Mouton, Europe director, IOGP; Jarrod Agen, executive director of the U.S. National Energy Dominance Council; Iskren Kirilov, director of institutional relations at IOGP Europe, 23 October, 2025. (Credit: Vert/LinkedIn)




In November 2025, Brittany Kelm, a then-colleague of Agen’s at the National Energy Dominance Council, 

tagged

 Mouton and the IOGP in a LinkedIn post celebrating a vote by the European Parliament to weaken proposed flagship environmental regulations known as the 

Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive

. Kelm described the vote as a “great step forward in progress on EU regulation changes for US LNG!” before adding: “Now onto the EU Methane Reg….”




“Indeed, let’s move forward,” Mouton replied.




Mouton met with Puzder, the U.S. ambassador to the EU, in March 2026, according to an Instagram post from the ambassador’s official account. The following month, the Financial Times published the 

Puzder op-ed

 citing an IOGP-coordinated call for delays and amendments to the methane rules on the grounds they could harm European energy security.




The same month, the IOGP and FuelsEurope — another TotalEnergies-backed trade group — funded a 

study

 published by analysts Wood Mackenzie that had concluded the methane regulation “risks worsening the energy crisis” caused by the Iran war and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.




Instagram post from the U.S. Mission to the European Union, published on 19 March, 2026, after a meeting between François-Régis Mouton [Left] and Andrew Puzder. (Credit: Instagram/Vert)




In June 2026, Wright, the U.S. energy secretary, co-signed an 

open letter

 to the EU with the energy ministers of Qatar, Algeria and Nigeria asking for the methane regulation to be delayed, citing an “independent, comprehensive industry analysis” that had found “significant negative supply and price impacts are a certainty.” 




Research by the 

European Commission

 and 

Rystad Energy

, by contrast, has concluded that there are sufficient supplies of compliant gas available to fulfil Europe’s energy needs next year.




“The gas industry has consistently exaggerated the threat the EU Methane Regulation poses to Europe’s gas supply,” said Sam Leon, co-founder of climate research group DataDesk.




On 3 September, 2026, Puzder 

posted

 an IOGP open 

letter

 on X calling for a three-year delay to the new rules, signed by 22 other trade groups.




In response to questions from DeSmog, the U.S. Mission to the EU said the U.S. “supports reducing methane emissions”, but that “EU regulators have not clearly defined the compliance and verification process to allow companies to adhere to the regulation.”




Asked whether the U.S. wants to revoke the EU Methane Regulation, the Mission said this was “a decision for the EU” and “our immediate focus is a three-year delay in implementation.” It added that the U.S. administration believes “deregulation improves economic competitiveness.”




As the Trump administration has announced its own deregulation of methane at home, it has cast the moves as a boon for fossil fuel production and a way to reduce costs for U.S. businesses and consumers. In a 27 October, 2026 press release, Agen, the National Energy Dominance Council director, said the administration’s revisions of a 

U.S. rule to reduce methane leaking, venting, and flaring

 “will unleash oil and natural gas and save families and businesses $45 billion in regulatory costs.”




‘No Threat’




The IOGP, meanwhile, has been intensifying its calls for a three-year reprieve on the methane regulations.




In late September 2026, the European Commission began 

signalling

 that it may push back implementation of the rules after French President Emmanuel Macron echoed 

growing calls

 among EU member states for a year-long delay.




In early October 2026, Mouton 

said

 in an IOGP statement that a one-year delay would see the EU “return to the same problem twelve months from now.” Puzder echoed this language in the 20 October 2026 email to EU member states encouraging them to vote for a three-year delay.




“Do we really want to go through all this again next year and the year after?” Puzder said in the email. 




In parallel, the IOGP has been touting its success in keeping politicians focused on energy security — as opposed to climate action — as part of its pitch to the oil industry. In an internal presentation meant for prospective new-joiners, dated October 2026, the IOGP listed “keeping energy security at the centre of EU debates” as one of the “highlights” of its lobbying activity. The document listed “30+ targeted media placements” as part of its lobbying strategy on the methane regulations.




The European Commission declined to comment on lobbying related to the rules but said it “remains fully committed to the goals of the Methane Regulation.”




“The Commission’s own findings say the Methane Regulation poses no threat to our security of supply, yet it is about to delay it anyway because Paris, the gas industry and Washington asked loudly enough,” said Marie Toussaint, a French Green party member of the European Parliament.




‘Pushing Back’




TotalEnergies has long painted itself as an industry leader on tackling methane. The company has launched numerous voluntary methane initiatives, left the 

American Petroleum Institute

  (API) — a powerful U.S. fossil fuel lobby group — in January 2021 over its support for rolling back regulation, and publicly backs the new EU regulations. 




Pouyanné, the TotalEnergies CEO, who is one of France’s highest-profile business leaders, has suggested he can convince the American fossil fuel industry to curb emissions of the gas.




“I’ve insisted in front of everybody in the U.S…it’s a mistake today not to keep the standards on methane emissions, including in the U.S.,” Pouyanné told a TotalEnergies investor meeting in March 2025.




In a measure of its influence, TotalEnergies was the only European company present in a separate meeting that month where EU officials and a group of U.S. fossil fuel companies and lobbies including ExxonMobil and the API discussed the methane rules, according to meeting notes obtained via climate research group 

ARIA

. Ten months later, in January 2026, the API specifically named 

“pushing back”

 on the EU methane regulations among its top policy targets for this year.




TotalEnergies’ support for Mouton and the IOGP — and their coordination with the Trump administration — suggest the French oil company is intent on avoiding regulation with any teeth, climate advocates said.




“As usual, the industry prefers to do it [reduce methane leaks] on a voluntary basis — without any accountability or risk of sanctions,” said Pascoe Sabido, a researcher at Brussels-based think tank the Corporate Europe Observatory.




The post 

How a French Oil Executive Is Working With the Trump Administration to ‘Kill’ Europe’s Methane Plan

 appeared first on 

DeSmog

.
