author: Corey Larocque
title: Six months to fix foster care failures is a tall order
content:
Six months isn’t much time to fix a problem that has festered for 15 years.




But that’s the task ahead for the Government of Nunavut after the federal auditor general presented a scathing report on the state of foster care in Nunavut, pointing to “fundamental weaknesses” that have persisted for years.




Deputy auditor general Andrew Hayes presented the report titled 

Foster Care in Nunavut

 on Tuesday. It’s the fifth time the office of the auditor general — responsible for probing the effectiveness of government programs — has looked into Nunavut’s foster care since 2011.




The Family Services Department can remove children from their family homes and place them in foster care when their parents aren’t able to meet their needs or provide a safe environment.




This week’s 

report

 is a litany of failures — basic things the GN’s Family Services Department didn’t do well enough. It includes failing to do in-person checks on children once a month in 90 per cent of the files the auditor general looked at. In five cases, there was no documented contact with the child in more than a year.




Screening of foster caregivers was weak. In just 52 per cent of cases, the department completed the home studies to assess whether a new foster home was a safe environment to place a child in.




And the department didn’t provide the caregivers it relies on with adequate tools, information or financial support.
















In March, there were approximately 400 children receiving protective services, including 260 who had been removed from their family home. But the government doesn’t actually know the precise number of children in care because the department relied on a manual list instead of one generated by a software package known as Matrix that was introduced three years ago.




Premier John Main and Family Services Minister Gwen Healey Akearok held a press conference Wednesday to 

respond

 to the report. But their explanations boiled down to “we’re working on it; we’re trying to do better.”




Main called the report “upsetting” and pledged a “whole government-wide effort” to make improvements. Time will tell. The “whole-of-government” line is one that politicians use to convey a sense of urgency or that something is a priority.




“Our sincere hope is that future audits will show real improvement,” Main said.




Does the GN really need a government-wide effort? What help can the Environment Department, for example, offer in terms of fixing the foster care system? Instead of a government-wide effort, why not just get Family Services’ house in order?




Healey Akearok said her department is making progress. Workers are getting trained on the Matrix system, 97 per cent of home studies have been done and 82 per cent of annual reviews have been completed.
















“There’s still work to be done,” she said.




Hayes said Tuesday, the auditor general’s office will be back in the spring to release another report on the GN’s “quality assurance” work. Family Services pointed to the quality assurance framework it implemented to address at least four of the report’s recommendations, including calls to provide support payments to caregivers, determining if a child in care has special needs, and emphasizing to social services workers the importance of documenting care plans.




The report makes you wonder about Nunavut’s capacity to deliver bigger, more complex programs — like health care and education.




Foster care is a relatively small part of the GN’s operations. If there are so many “fundamental weaknesses” in foster care, imagine the weaknesses that must exist in other departments.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Trabajadores de las radios públicas porteñas rechazan la pre adjudicación ilegítima de sus medios
content:
Este miércoles se publicó en el boletín oficial de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires la preadjudicación de las radios públicas de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires por los próximos 5 años, a la Unión Transitoria que conforman las firmas Green Umbrella Producciones SAS y JR Comunicaciones SRL. Los trabajadores y las trabajadoras de La Once Diez (AM 1110) y La 2×4 (FM 92.7) rechazan este intento de privatización encubierta porque se trata de una acción plenamente inconstitucional e ilegal, y afirman que es urgente que la justicia se expida.







A través de un comunicado, los trabajadores y las trabajadoras afirman que el Jefe de Gobierno, Jorge Macri, incumple el mandato de la propia Constitución de la Ciudad, que en su artículo 47 garantiza la existencia de medios de comunicación propios, destinados a difundir la actividad oficial y a promover la cultura y la educación, bajo gestión estatal; y viola además el artículo 44 de la Ley de Servicios de Comunicación Audiovisual, que establece el principio de indelegabilidad de la explotación de las frecuencias asignadas a dichos servicios de comunicación audiovisual.




Los trabajadores señalan que la preadjudicación de Radio de la Ciudad (AM 1110) y La 2×4 (FM 92.7) a la Unión Transitoria, integrada por Green Umbrella Producciones SAS y JR Comunicaciones SRL, abre una serie de interrogantes sobre su idoneidad para asumir la gestión de las radios públicas.




“Incluso si dejáramos de lado la plena ilegalidad de este proceso, según la información disponible estas empresas no cuentan con antecedentes suficientes en la administración integral de emisoras ni en la gestión de medios públicos. La incorporación de actividades radiofónicas en el objeto comercial de Green Umbrella no demuestra experiencia efectiva en la operación de una radio. La trayectoria de JR Comunicaciones, en tanto, se vincula principalmente con la actividad gráfica. No tendrían entonces expertise en la gestión de medios públicos, ni podrían ser calificados como profesionales del rubro, tal como reclaman los funcionarios porteños; incumpliendo con la expectativa de que ‘un privado puede hacerlo mejor’, tal como declaró Jorge Macri al anunciar la licitación de los medios públicos de la ciudad. También plantean dudas los contratos que mantienen o mantuvieron con el gobierno porteño. En el caso de Green Umbrella, llama la atención además que uno de sus fundadores, Rodrigo Matías Morán, ocupó una banca en la Legislatura porteña en 2021 dentro del espacio Vamos Juntos, vinculado directamente al Ejecutivo de la Ciudad”, detallan.







Además, recuerdan que en una primera licitación, el gobierno porteño ya adjudicó el Canal de la Ciudad al empresario Augusto Marini, que está al frente del Grupo Cale, dueño de los streamings Carajo y Blender: “Llamativamente ahora Marini no querría avanzar con la concesión hasta que el gobierno porteño le garantice que el traspaso sea ‘sin empleados en el Canal’. Demostrando el desprecio por quienes desde hace años sostenemos y le aseguramos valor y calidad a los medios públicos de la ciudad”, afirman.




Es por todo esto que los trabajadores reiteraron su reclamo a los jueces de la Sala III de la Cámara de Apelaciones, para que den lugar a la medida cautelar que ya cuenta con dictamen favorable de la Fiscalía General de dicha cámara, donde solicitan que “se frene este intento de ceder a un privado el patrimonio del público, que es el derecho a medios estatales, que cumplan el rol social de brindar comunicación de calidad, sin ataduras comerciales ni de otro tipo”.




“La causa que iniciamos contiene en su expediente con un informe favorable del ENaCom en el que los apoderados del organismo aseguraron que la licitación se encuentra ‘en colisión con expresas previsiones legales y reglamentarias, tendientes a precaver sobre la delegación de la explotación de los medios de comunicación autorizados en su favor’”, agregan.







“Los medios públicos cumplen una función esencial para la comunicación en una sociedad democrática: informar con criterios de interés general, dar lugar y promover todas las voces, fomentar la cultura y generar espacios de interacción para y con los vecinos de la Ciudad; funciones que difícilmente puedan sostenerse bajo la lógica exclusiva de la rentabilidad comercial.




Somos las y los profesionales que desde hace 99 años hacemos llegar el Teatro Colón a todo el país; quienes desde hace 26 años hacemos sonar el Tango en todo el mundo. Las radios de la ciudad no son un negocio. Son patrimonio público. Defender los medios públicos es defender el trabajo y el derecho a una comunicación democrática, plural y de calidad”, finalizan los trabajadores y las trabajadoras de las radios públicas de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Adiós a Patricia Walsh, esa compañera que siempre estuvo en el lado correcto de la historia de nuestro pueblo
content:
Por Carlos Aznárez, Resumen Latinoamericano




Patricia, la más pequeña pero no menos importante de esa familia de patriotas revolucionarios y revolucionarias que comandaba tu padre, el montonero, el periodista, el escritor, el imprescindible. Patricia hermana querida de Viki, caída en combate en la batalla de la calle Corro. Patricia, la que nunca dejó de estar en aquellos gloriosos años 70 en que los compañeros y compañeras peleábamos por la Revolución y el Socialismo. Patricia, la que masculló su rabia el nefasto día en que los marinos genocidas intentaron secuestrar a Rodolfo, después de dar a conocer su Carta abierta a la Junta Militar, y éste resistió hasta entregar su vida para impedirlo. La misma que, ahuyentando todos los peligros, fuiste hasta el domicilio de tu padre y de su compañera Lilia, preocupada porque no tenías ninguna señal de su paradero, y sin entrar en el lugar pudiste ver los destrozos que habían hecho los milicos. Patricia, la que años después aguantó como pudo la irreparable pérdida de su hija María Eva, y ni siquiera en tan terribles circunstancias dejaste de reivindicar la vida y la lucha que la habita en todos los momentos y en cada circunstancia.




Patricia, militante de HIJOS, junto a los que peleaste por la memoria fértil de tantas y tantos madres, padres, hermanos, a los que el sistema, el de ayer y el de hoy, trata otra vez de hacer desaparecer. Patricia, la que impulsaste, desde tu cargo de diputada, y con toda la fuerza de tus principios revolucionarios, el proyecto de 

Nulidad de las Leyes de Punto Final y Obediencia Debida

, esos dos engendros que el sistema intentaba encajar con forceps en la democracia «controlada» y «dependiente».




Y por supuesto, que también fuiste periodista, psicóloga social, militante de izquierda, feminista, rebelde ante las injusticias, pero por sobre todo, digna reivindicadora de la trayectoria de tu viejo y de tu hermana, militantes montoneros, cuya memoria defendiste, no dejando que nadie se apropiara con oportunismo de la misma y del legado de sus hermosas vidas entregadas a la causa de los trabajadores y trabajadoras.




A partir de hoy no te tendremos más físicamente, pero nos acompañarán tu sonrisa compañera, tus enojos y rabietas cuando algo no salía como te lo habías imaginado, tu maravillosa pasión por darle para adelante a pesar de que -como siempre nos pasó- las derrotas parecían sumar más escalones que las victorias. Pero nunca consiguieron amilanarte todos aquellos que solo saben hablar con la voz de la violencia del poder, ni tampoco cooptarte con los cantos de sirena de falsos progresismos que tiempos después terminaban derrumbados por fuego cruzado.




Te despido compañera, y lo hago recordando ese enorme abrazo que nos dimos cuando en plena calle Arenales nos cruzamos de pura casualidad, o por esos encuentros que pacta el destino, aquel día del mes de octubre del 76. Ya había sucedido lo de la calle Corro, y por supuesto nos emocionamos hasta las lágrimas durante varios minutos, mientras repetíamos, recordando a Viki, y como una clave para seguir sobreviviendo: “LOMJE, LOMJE”. Libres o Muertos jamás esclavos.




Hasta la Victoria Siempre, compañera Patricia Walsh.

author: Danilo Arao
title: Peryodiko
content:
Photo from the Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas

Maganda ang teknolohiya kung mapapakinabangan ng karamihan.

May nagbabasa pa kaya ng peryodiko? Alam pa kaya ng kabataan ang mga katulad na salitang pahayagan at diyaryo?

Baka mas pundamental pa ang tanong: May nagbabasa pa kaya? Totoo bang wala nang masyadong kultura ng pagbuklat ng anumang nakaimprenta dahil mas gusto ng mga taong manood na lang ng bidyo?

Kung sabagay, higit pa sa peryodismo ang isyu. Analog o digital? Nobela o pelikula? Lumang midya o bagong midya? Pero saglit lang. Kailangan ba talagang mamili sa dalawa? Hindi ba puwedeng pagsabayin ang luma’t bago?

Kung gagamit ng ilang salita sa wikang Ingles, hindi ito usapin ng “conversion” kundi “convergence.” Posibleng gamitin ng lumang midya ang bagong teknolohiya para mapalakas ang mga katangian nito. At sa konteksto ng peryodismo, nagdesisyon ang maraming peryodikong gumawa ng mga website at account sa iba’t ibang social media platform.

Para sa mga peryodista, kailangang pumunta kung nasaan ang masa. Ito ang dahilan ng literal na pagbisita sa mga komunidad, lalo na sa mga liblib na lugar na tila napag-iwanan ng kabihasnan. Ito rin ang magpapaliwanag kung bakit pinapatulan pati ang TikTok sa paghuhubog ng opinyong pampubliko. Naglalaan din sila ng oras para makipagtalastasan sa social media kahit na hindi pinapansin ang mga personal na atake.

Dahil sa mabilis na pag-unlad ng teknolohiya, totoo namang lumang-luma na ang mga tinaguriang sinauna. Pero kapansin-pansin ang ebolusyon ng print para isama sa diseminasyon ng impormasyon ang teknolohiyang digital.

Gayundin ang kaso ng mga programa sa radyo dahil mayroon na silang kaakibat na teleradyo para marinig at makita ang balita, pati na ang nangyayari sa loob ng booth habang nagbobrodkast. At para naman sa mga programa sa telebisyon, uso na rin ang simultaneous live streaming.

Ngunit para sa mga lugar na mahina o walang internet signal, patuloy na namamayagpag ang lumang midya. Mas nakadepende sila sa radyo o telebisyon para sa pinakahuling balita. Nakakatulong din naman ang peryodiko para sa dagdag na pagsusuri kahit na hindi agad-agad na nakukuha ang kopya. Kaya hindi naman masyadong nahuhuli sa balita ang mga nasa liblib na lugar basta’t may mga matiyagang magsusubaybay at maghahanap ng paraan.

Maganda ang teknolohiya kung mapapakinabangan ng karamihan. Pero kung ang kalidad at bilis ng internet ay depende sa panggastos, parating mapipilitan ang mahihirap na pagtiyagaan ang mabagal na koneksiyon.

Para sa karamihang naka-prepaid na account lang sa kanilang mobile phone, mas gagamitin ang mga libreng opsiyon para ma-access ang social media accounts pero malamang na hindi maki-click ang link papunta sa buong teksto ng balitang nasa website ng mga organisasyong pang-midya. Kaya ang mangyayari, headline lang o maikling bahagi lang ng balita ang posibleng mabasa.

Anong klaseng opinyon ang mabubuo kung limitado lang ang impormasyon? Hindi ba’t mas mainam na gawing libre ang internet para sa lahat? Bakit kailangan pa kasing pagkakitaan ang teknolohiyang dapat na maging tulay para sa epektibong diseminasyon ng impormasyon?

Pero labas ng internet access, kailangan ding pangalagaan ang mga tinaguriang luma. Patuloy na kilalanin ang ambag ng print, radyo at telebisyon, lalo na ang kanilang paggamit ng teknolohiya sa gitna ng nagbabagong panahon. Hindi hiwalay ang pag-aaral ng bago sa pagkilala ng luma. Katulad ito sa pag-intindi ng kasalukuyan batay sa aral ng kasaysayan.

Uso pa ba ang peryodiko? Tandaang may mga nagbabasa pa naman. Hindi naman mawawala ang print media sa kabila ng pag-unlad ng teknolohiya. Mahalaga pa rin ang tuloy-tuloy na paglilimbag lalo na’t kinakailangan ang malalim na pagsasakonteksto.

title: Candan Yüceer YENİ Parti'den istifa etti
content:
Tekirdağ Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Candan Yüceer, YENİ Parti üyeliğinden istifa ettiğini duyurdu.




Yüceer, bugün sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, hasta olduğu dönemde düzenlenen il kongresinde kurultay delegeliği üzerinden yaşanan tartışmalara ve kendisinin delege listesine alınmamasına tepki gösterdi. "Benim aradığım yol arkadaşlığı bu değil" dedi. Şunları kaydetti:




"Bugün itibarıyla üyesi olduğum YENİ Parti'den istifa ediyorum. Ben siyaseti koltuk hesabı yapmak için yapmadım. Benim mücadelem hiçbir zaman kişisel ikbal mücadelesi olmadı. Ancak üzülerek görüyorum ki bugün bazıları kendi kişisel ikbalinin, makamının ve koltuğunun hesabına düşmüş durumda.




Son olarak benim hasta yatağında olduğum bir dönemde il kongresinde gündemin kurultay delegeliği üzerinden tartışmaya dönüştürülmesini ve bu tartışmalar nedeniyle kongrenin başlatılmamasını, şahsımın kurultay delegesi olarak dahi yazılmamasını kabul edilebilir bulmuyorum. Burada mesele bir delege listesinde kimin olup olmaması değildir.




Mesele yıllarca birlikte mücadele etmiş insanlara gösterilmesi gereken saygıdır. Mesele yol arkadaşlığı hukukudur. Mesele seçilmiş bir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanına gösterilmesi gereken siyasi nezakettir. Mesele birlikte yürüdüğümüz insanların birbirine nasıl davrandığıdır.




Benim beklediğim vefa, benim aradığım yol arkadaşlığı bu değil. Yol arkadaşlığı hukukunun bu kadar kolay çiğnendiği, kişisel çıkarların ortak değerlerin önüne geçirildiği bir anlayışın içinde yokum. Benim önceliğim de sorumluluğum da çok açık: Tekirdağ.




Benim her sabah uyandığımda düşündüğüm şey Tekirdağ’ın hangi sorununu çözeceğimiz, hangi yatırımını tamamlayacağımız, hangi projemizi hayata geçireceğimiz.




11 ilçemizde yaşayan vatandaşlarımız bizden hizmet bekliyor. Altyapı bekliyor, yol bekliyor, su bekliyor, sosyal destek bekliyor. Tekirdağ’ın kaybedecek bir günü bile yok. Benim önceliğim siyasi hesaplaşmalar değil, Tekirdağ'a hizmettir, Tekirdağ'ın bekleyen sorunları, devam eden yatırımları ve halkımıza verdiğimiz sözlerdir.




Ben enerjimi kentin geleceğine harcamayı tercih ediyorum. Bizim mücadelemizde, yolumuzda, önceliğimizde Tekirdağ’ın daha güçlü, daha adil, daha yaşanabilir bir kent olmasıdır. Ben bu göreve Tekirdağ’a hizmet etmek için geldim. Biz başımız dik, alnımız açık, hemşerilerimize karşı sorumluluğumuzun bilinciyle yolumuza devam edeceğiz. Ve bütün gücümle Tekirdağ’ıma olan sevgim ve bu güzel şehre hizmet etme sorumluluğumla Tekirdağ için çalışmaya devam edeceğim."




(HA)

author: Randi Beers
title: Jimmy Bell – The ghost of Arctic Bay
content:
At Cape Dorset in 1949, Jimmy Bell, the large, fun-loving Hudson’s Bay Co. trader, took ill. His once rotund body began to waste away until he was but a shadow of his former self. 




On arriving in Cape Dorset, his young clerk, Peter Murdoch, who had known Jimmy in Lake Harbour, barely recognized him. He described him as “a skinny-looking fellow wearing baggy clothes, his face lined and his eyes a sickly yellow.”  




Officials in Winnipeg knew in February that Jimmy’s health was “not up to its usual robust standard,” but Jimmy attributed it to “too much of his own cooking.” 




In May he sent a message to Winnipeg that admitted he required medical attention. Another message followed, in which he said he would go out to Churchill on the supply ship for a check-up. But he kept the extent of his illness from his superiors. He surmised, correctly, that if they knew his true condition, they would evacuate him to the south. 




But Peter Murdoch knew that Jimmy needed attention, much more than he could provide using the post’s medical manual. He thought that Jimmy had stomach cancer. Without Jimmy’s knowledge, Murdoch sent a telegram by radio to Winnipeg informing them of Jimmy’s condition. Too late, Jimmy realized what Murdoch had done and mustered all his strength to roar at Murdoch and express his disapproval. 




Jimmy told Murdoch, “If I have cancer I want to die in the North. I want my spirit to stay in the North. When I die my spirit is going back to Arctic Bay. That’s the place I really love most – Arctic Bay.” 




But Winnipeg had got the message. Headquarters immediately dispatched their Canso aircraft, nicknamed Polar Bear, on the long flight to Cape Dorset.
















Jimmy was evacuated to Winnipeg on July 2. He was operated on at Winnipeg General Hospital a few days later, but doctors concluded that there was nothing more they could do for him. His mother and a brother were sent for and reached his bedside on the last day of August. Jimmy Bell died on Sept. 12 and was buried in Brookside Cemetery, in Winnipeg. He was only 43.




The inscription on his pink granite headstone ends with: “Here we leave our loved one sleeping.” 




But Jimmy wasn’t sleeping. He was restless. And, as he had promised, his spirit returned to Arctic Bay — or so it appeared.




Jimmy had a dear friend there. Amarualik was a leader among the Inuit and had worked for the Hudson’s Bay Co. for many years. Jimmy and Amarualik were close, and Jimmy had had a child with Amarualik’s daughter, Kautaq. That girl, Tapisa (now Tapisa Hughes of Arctic Bay) was the youngest of three daughters that Jimmy had with Inuit women.




When he died, the Hudson’s Bay Co. manager’s residence in Arctic Bay became the scene of strange occurrences. Residents and visitors heard footsteps in the storeroom, but there was no one there. Cups rattled in the cupboards and dishes rattled in the sink. But no one present had disturbed them. Doors mysteriously opened. The building was haunted.




Jimmy had returned to Arctic Bay to be near his old friend, Amarualik.
















It’s noteworthy that many of Jimmy’s manifestations happened in the kitchen of the residence, because Jimmy, in life, had apparently been obsessed with the neatness of his kitchen. Len Budgell, a lifelong Hudson’s Bay Co. employee, recalled that Jimmy was a bachelor and that “he liked things just so. If you did the dishes at night and hung the tea towel up, and it wasn’t the way Jimmy would have hung it up, in the morning you would find it neatly rearranged to Jimmy’s preference.” 




When the rattling of dishes became too loud, some company managers were known to shout, “Leave the bloody dishes alone, Jimmy.” 




That would generally result in a short burst of fierce rattling — Jimmy was clearly displeased — before silence would settle in. 




Soon after Eric Mitchell arrived in Arctic Bay as manager, he experienced a number of “curious, though disturbing incidents.” Footsteps were heard on the creaky floorboards of the attic night after night until one night he shouted, “Quit it!” 




One night he awoke to find all the doors of the house wide open. When he told Amarualik about these events, the old Inuk replied nonchalantly, “That’s just Jimmy Bell wandering around. Don’t worry about it; he’s just waiting for me to join him.” 
















The disturbances in Arctic Bay were no secret. They became part of Baffin Island lore. Word of the haunted staff house reached Winnipeg where some officials laughed it off. 




But one winter in the 1960s, company officials visited Arctic Bay and overnighted at the staff house. They wanted to investigate the reports of Jimmy’s ghost. Footsteps were said to have been heard on the roof, and so, on a windless night, they put a ladder up and spread flour on the roof, then waited. Sure enough, footsteps were heard again on the roof. But a physical check showed the flour undisturbed.




Amarualik passed away on June 28, 1967. The disturbances ceased at that time. Jimmy Bell’s friend had finally joined him, and Jimmy was finally at peace. 




Taissumani is an occasional column that recalls events of historical interest. Kenn Harper is a historian and writer who lived in the Arctic for over 50 years. He is the author of 

Give Me Winter, Give Me Dogs: Knud Rasmussen and the Fifth Thule Expedition

, and 

Thou Shalt Do No Murder

, among other books. Feedback? Send your comments and questions to kennharper@hotmail.com.

author: La Zarzamora
title: Lanzamiento de Black Onions, un listado de sitios web anarquistas y antiautoritarios con extensión .onion
content:
Publicado originalmente en Montréal Contre-information

Nos complace anunciar el lanzamiento de Black Onions, una nueva iniciativa que tiene como objetivo ofrecer una lista estable y actualizada periódicamente de sitios anarquistas y antiautoritarios con extensión .onion. Los sitios .onion son sitios web accesibles a través del navegador Tor mediante direcciones que terminan en «.onion».

En los últimos meses, algunos gobiernos han atacado las infraestructuras de comunicación de nuestros movimientos con renovado vigor; buena prueba de ello son la conferencia internacional sobre el «terrorismo de extrema izquierda» celebrada en Estados Unidos en julio, así como la inclusión del proveedor de servicios de alojamiento militante italiano Autistici/Inventati en una lista de sanciones relacionadas con el terrorismo a finales de agosto.

Para bien o para mal, la comunicación pública de nuestros movimientos tiene lugar en gran medida en Internet, lo que la hace vulnerable a los mecanismos tecnológicos de censura. A diferencia de los sitios web convencionales, los sitios .onion son menos vulnerables a la censura, ya que no utilizan nombres de dominio y permiten ocultar la ubicación del servidor, del mismo modo que el navegador Tor oculta tu propia ubicación al visitar el sitio. Consideramos que los sitios .onion son nuestra mejor baza para seguir comunicándonos en línea dentro del movimiento anarquista, especialmente si los intentos de censura se intensifican en el futuro.

El problema recurrente de los sitios .onion es que sus direcciones, compuestas por 56 caracteres aleatorios, son imposibles de memorizar. Black Onions tiene como objetivo resolver este problema. Te recomendamos guardar en los marcadores del navegador Tor, o en un archivo en tu ordenador, las direcciones .onion que utilizas habitualmente; pero si necesitas una dirección que aún no has guardado, ¡encuéntrala en Black Onions!

Accede a Black Onions a través de cualquiera de las siguientes direcciones:

– blackonions.gd – blackonions.li – blackonions.st – (próximamente, una dirección .onion)

Para establecer una base de confianza en esta nueva iniciativa, los siguientes proyectos anarquistas han avalado nuestra propuesta mediante declaraciones firmadas con PGP: Act For Freedom Now!, un proyecto de contrainformación activo desde 2008 , y el No Trace Project, un proyecto contra la represión activo desde 2021.

¡Utiliza sitios .onion! ¡Resiste a la censura!

author: groundxero
title: Amid Ongoing Siang Protests, In-Principle Forest Clearance Nod to Naying Hydroelectric Project; Over One Lakh Trees to Be Felled
content:
The recommendation for in-principle forest clearance for the 1,000-MW Naying Hydroelectric Project in Arunachal Pradesh comes amid escalating protests against large dam projects in the Siang river basin. 

With 470.8 hectares of forest land set to be diverted, compensatory afforestation proposed 1,700 kilometres away in Madhya Pradesh, and landowners rejecting NEEPCO’s compensation offer, the 

Naying 

project on the Siyom River raises serious questions about ecological destruction, and the social cost of hydropower expansion 

in a region where indigenous communities are increasingly resisting such projects that threaten their forests, rivers and ancestral lands.




 




Groundxero

 

Desk




 




Amid growing opposition and resistance to the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh, another major hydroelectric project in the Siang river basin has moved closer to implementation. On October 23, 2026, the Forest Advisory Committee (FAC) of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 

recommended in-principle forest clearance

 for the 1,000-MW Naying Hydroelectric Project on the Siyom River (Yomgo River), a major tributary of the Siang.




 




The FAC recommendation permits the diversion of 470.8 hectares of unclassed forest land for the project, which will require the felling of approximately 1,04,036 trees. The FAC has categorised the project area as a “high conservation value zone”. The clearance comes despite persistent objections from project-affected communities, unresolved disputes over land compensation and allegations of procedural irregularities in the environmental clearance process.




 




The Naying project, being developed by the North Eastern Electric Power Corporation (NEEPCO), is a run-of-the-river scheme with peaking power generation capability. Proposed on the Siyom (Yomgo) River, a right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra, the project extends across parts of Shi-Yomi and Siang districts, both bordering China. With an estimated investment of Rs 11,835 crore, it involves the construction of a 108-metre-high concrete gravity dam over an area of approximately 470 hectares.




 




The project was conceived more than a decade ago and received the Central Electricity Authority’s concurrence in 2013. Its progress remained stalled for years because of environmental and social concerns, particularly the large-scale diversion of forest land. The Union Environment Ministry’s Expert Appraisal Committee recommended environmental clearance in June 2026, and the project received conditional environmental clearance in July. The conditions included safeguards relating to compensatory afforestation, wildlife conservation, air and noise pollution monitoring, and waste management. A mandatory public hearing was subsequently held at Yapik village in Shi-Yomi district.




 




Construction is expected to begin around 2028, with commissioning targeted for 2032.




 




Landowners reject NEEPCO’s compensation offer




 




The successive clearance procedures of the project have intensified opposition among affected landowners. Twelve villages are expected to be affected, and grievances over compensation have developed into a major source of conflict between local communities and NEEPCO.




 




The dispute reached a deadlock in September 2026, when NEEPCO proposed compensation of just Rs 130 per square metre for land and forest resources during an administrative meeting in Yapik village. The Naying Hydroelectric Project Land Owner Welfare Committee (NHEPLOWC), led by its chairman, Taya Yabu, rejected the offer, describing it as a gross undervaluation of ancestral land.




 




The landowners pointed out that compensation rates for comparable infrastructure projects in other districts of Arunachal Pradesh ranged between Rs 3,000 and Rs 5,000 per square metre. They demanded that the same standard be applied to the Naying project.




 




On September 23, landowners from seven affected villages met at Yapik and formally decided to suspend all cooperation with NEEPCO until their demands concerning compensation and land rights were addressed.




 




The nine-point memorandum submitted by the Land Owner Welfare Committee also raised objections to unauthorised tree cutting and clear-felling within designated local forest areas without the required final clearances and compliance procedures.




 




Questions over the environmental public hearing




 




The landowners’ opposition is not confined to monetary compensation. They have also raised serious questions about the transparency and legality of the environmental clearance process.




 




During the mandatory public hearing, affected landowners submitted a memorandum detailing their objections and concerns relating to the environment and local livelihoods. However, the welfare committee alleges that the Arunachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board (APSPCB) failed to provide a formal action-taken report or respond to the objections submitted by the community.




 




The committee has further alleged that the official minutes and records of the public hearing were withheld from the public. This, it argues, prevented project-affected families from verifying whether their objections and concerns had been properly recorded before the government proceeded with subsequent declarations and land acquisition notices.




 




Following these alleged procedural violations, local landowners convened meetings in Yapik village and adopted resolutions warning of peaceful protests and total non-cooperation if the state government failed to arrange a formal hearing to address their grievances in a transparent manner.




 




The refusal of seven villages to cooperate with NEEPCO represents a significant challenge to the project’s implementation. It also raises a fundamental question: can a project claiming to serve the public interest proceed legitimately when the people whose land and forests it will consume are contesting the terms of acquisition and the very procedures through which it has secured approval?




 




A forest lost here, trees to be planted 1,700 kilometres away




 




One of the most troubling aspects of the Naying project is the nature of its proposed compensatory afforestation.




 




Under the compensatory afforestation framework, project developers are required to arrange tree planting on an equivalent or, in this case, double the area of forest land diverted for non-forest purposes. Accordingly, NEEPCO must undertake compensatory afforestation over 942 hectares.




 




However, the planting is not proposed in the Siyom river basin or even in Arunachal Pradesh. According to the project’s environmental assessment, the compensatory afforestation is to be carried out on degraded forest land spread across 18 districts of Madhya Pradesh, approximately 1,700 kilometres away from the project site.




 




The FAC has stipulated that the 942 hectares must constitute a single contiguous patch rather than being divided into smaller, scattered plots.




 




This arrangement exposes a fundamental flaw in the compensatory afforestation model. A natural forest is not simply a collection of trees that can be replaced by planting saplings somewhere else. It is a complex ecological system shaped by its geography, soil, water, climate, biodiversity and the relationship between local communities and their surroundings.




 




The forests of Arunachal Pradesh, particularly those classified as having high conservation value, sustain distinctive ecosystems and provide habitats for diverse wildlife. Planting trees in a different geographical and ecological region cannot recreate the biodiversity, ecological functions or livelihood relationships of the forests being destroyed.




 




The problem is further compounded by the lack of transparency and accountability in the implementation of compensatory afforestation programmes. Studies and audits have repeatedly raised concerns about the survival of planted saplings, the use of limited varieties of fast-growing species, inadequate monitoring and the exclusion of local communities from long-term maintenance.




 




A comprehensive Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audit report examining nationwide greening and afforestation initiatives highlighted severe implementation failures. The 

audit reportedly

 found that forest-cover expansion fell substantially short of targets. The cited figures indicate that forest cover increased by only 0.03 million hectares against a target of 1.4 million hectares over a decade, while 70 per cent of sampled afforestation sites showed no noticeable improvement in greening.




 




Such shortcomings make it difficult to accept compensatory afforestation as an adequate ecological response to the destruction of an existing natural forest.




 




In the case of Naying, the contradiction is particularly stark: more than one lakh trees are to be felled in a high conservation value forest zone in Arunachal Pradesh, while the legally mandated afforestation is to take place thousands of kilometres away in another state, in a completely different ecological landscape.




 




Naying and the larger battle over the Siang river basin




 




The Naying Hydroelectric Project is not an isolated case. It is one of at least four hydroelectric projects planned in the Siang river basin, with the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project being the largest and the most contentious.




 




The cumulative impact of these projects on the river system, forests, biodiversity and indigenous communities remains a major concern. The local opposition to the Upper Siang (SUMP) project has already developed into a statewide wider people’s movement involving the indigenous Adi community, residents of villages along the river, student and youth organisations, cultural activists and the larger civil society. Communities fear that the massive project could submerge dozens of ancestral villages and irreversibly alter their relationship with the river and surrounding forests.




 




In late October and early November 2026, protests against the Upper Siang project escalated, resulting in demonstrations and strikes, the state responded by use of force to suppress the protests, anti-dam activists were detained in Itanagar and New Delhi, and the deployment of central paramilitary forces, including the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and the Rapid Action Force (RAF). The use of the draconian Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against anti-dam activists has further intensified people’s anger and intensified the opposition to the project.




 




The growing resistance to both the Naying and Upper Siang projects reflects a deeper conflict between the state and the indigenous communities over the future of Arunachal Pradesh’s rivers, forests and ancestral lands.




 




For the people living in these river valleys, land and forests are not merely economic assets to be acquired through compensation packages. They are integral to their livelihoods, cultural identities, community life and relationship with their ancestral lands.




 




The Naying project has already exposed the design of an environmental clearance process that move forwards even as affected communities contest compensation, question the transparency of public hearings and refuse cooperation.




 




The key issue is therefore not simply whether NEEPCO will meet the official conditions attached to the project’s clearances. It is whether the destruction of a high conservation value forest and the disruption of lives of the indigenous communities can be justified in the name of expanding electricity generation and national security, while the indigenous communities who bear the environmental and social costs have no meaningful say in determining the future of their ancestral land, forests and rivers.

title: İşte Meydan İşte Sahne Sergisi ziyarete açıldı
content:
Ankara – 1961 yılında kurulan, kurulduğu dönem Ankara’nın tek tiyatrosu olan Meydan Sahnesi’ni anlatan ve Sibel Durak’ın hazırladığı ‘İşte Meydan İşte Sahne Sergisi’ 22 Kasım’a kadar ziyarete açık olacak.

Açılışta konuşan Ankara Tabib Odası’ndan( diyelim çalışanı yerine) Sibel Durak, “Sergideki bütün materyal arşiv malzemesidir. Sahaf ve müzayedelerden, kendi çabam ve olanaklarım ile topladığım malzemelerden oluşuyor. Yaklaşık 3 yıldır topluyorum. Aynı zamanda sergide, Uğur Kavas’ın verdiği Aceleci Kalp, Köşe Kapmaca ve Karaların Memetleri oyunlarının fotoğrafları yer alıyor” dedi.

Meydan Sahnesi’nin, tiyatronun altın çağında kurulduğunu dile getiren Durak, ”Sahne, 1961 yılında kuruluyor ve başarılı işlere imza atıyor. O dönem biletler satışa çıktığı gibi bitiyor. Meydan Sahnesi, açılan tiyatro kursları ve oyunları sayesinde çok fazla oyuncunun tiyatroya başlamasına olanak sağlamıştır. 80’lere kadar 20’ye yakın yeni tiyatro kurulmuş ve tiyatroların yaygınlaşmasında önemli rolü olmuştur. Ayrıca bu dönem telif ücreti ödeyemedikleri için Adalet Ağaoğlu tiyatro oyunlarının çevirisini yaparak destek vermiştir” şeklinde konuştu.

Serginin kuruluş sürecinde yaşananlara değinen Durak, “Meydan Sahnesi ile ilgili çok fazla kişiye ulaşamadım. Sergiyi hazırladıktan sonra bazı insanlarla görüşme fırsatı buldum. Tiyatro, 1972-73 sezonunda kapanmış ve 50 yıldan fazla bir süre geçmiş. Sergide, çalışmamım devamı için kullanmamı istedikleri materyalleri paylaşan olursa sergide kullanmak isterim” ifadelerini kullandı.

Devlet Tiyatrosu’nun zamanında çok iyi seyirci yetiştirdiğini söyleyen Durak, ”Meydan Sahnesi gibi özel tiyatrolar da bunun üzerine koyarak kültürün devamını sağlamıştır. Ankara seyircisi başkadır denir, çünkü bir kültür yaratılmıştır” dedi.

Meydan Sahnesi’nde oynanan oyunların kendine has tarzı olduğunu dile getiren Durak, “Genelde komedi, polisiye oyunlar oynanmış. Bulabildiğim oyun isimlerini yazdım. Tiyatroyla ilgilenen bir kişi sergiyi gördükten sonra ‘bu oyun da vardı’ diyebilir. Bu da talep doğrultusunda oyunların yeniden sahnelenmesine olanak sağlayabilir. Bu sayede o dönem verilen emek, mücadele ve cesaret insanları harekete geçirebilir. Fakat ne yazık ki bu dönemde tiyatroların durumu iç açıcı değil. Yeterli destek görmüyorlar ve vergiler çok ağır. Bu da tiyatro kültürünü olumsuz etkiliyor” açıklamalarında bulundu. Açıklamalarında bulundu demeyelim dedi veya şeklinde konuştu diyelim

Ayrıca arşivlerin önemine vurgu yapan Durak, “1-2 istisna kitap dışında tiyatro tarihi ile ilgili tarih kitaplarında bile çok fazla bilgi yok. Yoklukların içinde önemli emekler verildiğini hatırlatmak istedim, amacım buydu. Aynı zamanda elinde arşivi olanlara da, ellerindeki arşivi nasıl kullanabilecekleri konusunda fikir vermeyi amaçladım. Rahmi M. Koç Müzesi’nin de sergi salonunu tahsis ettiği bir iş birliği oldu” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Martyrs of Kurdistan’s Freedom Struggle commemorated in Sine
content:
Following the HPG’s announcement of the identities of nine guerrillas from Rojhilatê Kurdistan who fell as martyrs in the freedom struggle in previous years, a memorial event was held in the city of Sanandaj (Sine).







During the commemoration, the Martyrs’ Families Committee and Peace Mothers carried photographs of the fallen guerrillas and repeatedly chanted the slogan “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs never die).







 







At the event, organised by the Martyrs’ Families Committee and the Peace Mothers, it was stated that the martyrs had become symbols of unity among all parts of Kurdistan.







It was also emphasised that the martyrs of the freedom struggle, from Kobanê, Shengal, Amed, Qamishlo and Hewraman to Sine, had set an example of defending humanity against ISIS.




At the end of the ceremony, the Martyrs’ Families Committee of Rojhilatê Kurdistan extended its condolences to the people of Sine and the patriotic people of Kurdistan. The committee also reiterated that the martyrs of Rojhilatê Kurdistan are martyrs of the entire Kurdish people.

author: Unknown
title: Laura Quagliuolo: Öcalan's freedom is key to lasting peace
content:
The Call for Peace and a Democratic Society issued by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025 brought discussions on a democratic solution to the Kurdish question into a new phase. International calls for Öcalan's freedom and the implementation of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) ruling on the "right to hope" also continue. Demands for Turkey to fulfill its obligations under the supervision of the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers are increasingly coming to the fore.




Italian feminist activist, writer and member of the Rete Jin women's solidarity network Laura Quagliuolo spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the importance of Öcalan's freedom for a democratic solution, the failure to implement ECtHR rulings and the role of women in building peace.




Efforts to find a democratic solution to the Kurdish question have continued since the call issued by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025. How do you assess the process at its current stage? What do you think are the fundamental conditions that must be met to achieve lasting peace?




I think the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey has not yet been realized. We have not reached that point yet, primarily because Abdullah Öcalan is not free. I believe Öcalan's freedom is a very important condition for the Kurdish people to achieve freedom and for their existence to be recognized. The Kurdish people can no longer be ignored. As you know, Abdullah Öcalan's call was extremely clear and powerful. The guerrillas came down from the mountains and laid down their weapons. Their weapons were burned in a ceremony. This was an enormously significant step toward peace.




However, the Kurdish people must also be recognized. Their language, traditions, culture and way of life must be recognized. They can no longer be subjected to oppression, as the Turkish state has done in the past and continues to do today. Therefore, the most important issue, first and foremost, is the freedom of Abdullah Öcalan and the many other comrades who remain imprisoned under various circumstances.




Abdullah Öcalan's situation is particularly serious and troubling. Because after nearly 28 years of imprisonment, they must acknowledge that he has always been someone who has taken steps toward peace in the Middle East. Another condition is recognizing that the Kurdish people, and not only the Kurds but other peoples as well, are working and living according to the principles that emerge from Abdullah Öcalan's paradigm. This must be recognized because it represents hope not only for Turkey but for the entire Middle East and, if I may say so, for the whole world.




As you mentioned, despite the ongoing process, there has been no fundamental change in the legal status or prison conditions of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan. This remains one of the Kurdish side's most fundamental demands. Do you believe lasting peace can genuinely be built without securing the conditions necessary for Öcalan's freedom and participation in the process?




As I said before, Öcalan's freedom must be guaranteed. He must have the freedom to speak to the people, to his own people. It is not only a matter of allowing him to participate in meetings. Conditions must also be established in which he can express his views and be heard by everyone. Because, in my opinion, he is a man of peace. He is also someone who can help guide this peace process in the right direction. But they cannot continue to keep him imprisoned like this. They need to take steps, and serious ones at that.




The ECtHR ruled against Turkey in 2014 over the aggravated life sentence imposed on Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan without the possibility of release. However, more than 12 years later, the ruling has still not been fully implemented. How should this position be interpreted? What concrete steps do you expect from the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers at its meeting in December?




You know, Europe constantly talks about peace and many other things. But in reality, Europe is not genuinely committed to achieving peace, whether in the Middle East, in the war between Russia and Ukraine, or anywhere else. They talk, but they have done nothing in the face of the genocide in Palestine. That is the situation in Europe. They speak and then fall silent. What remains after their speeches is silence. That is exactly what happened 12 years ago. You know, the court, all those rulings and everything else... The court ruled against the Turkish state over this imprisonment. But afterward, they were not consistent in ensuring that their own decisions were respected. They are doing nothing to secure the implementation of their rulings or to compel Turkey to comply with them.




They simply left the matter there. They announced their decisions and then allowed Turkey to do whatever it wanted. Throughout all these years, the Turkish state has clearly demonstrated its intentions and what it really wants to do: stop the peace process, obstruct it, oppress the Kurdish people and seize control of their municipalities. You know, they have done everything they could to silence all of this. Europe, meanwhile, has done very little. Neither Europe as a whole, nor the Commission or other institutions, nor individual states have taken meaningful action. They have remained truly silent. Therefore, this silence sends a message to the Turkish state, to Erdoğan and to others: You can do whatever you want.




Democratic confederalism offers hope for the whole world




I think what they need to understand is this: If they want peace not only in Turkey and Syria but throughout the Middle East, they must support the work being carried out by the Kurdish people in every part of Kurdistan. They must support the building of a different society, the inclusion of women in social life and all these efforts.




Yes, I am talking about democratic confederalism. This model is being implemented almost everywhere, although at different levels. Particularly in Syria, and even in Turkey. Because when I visited Bakur, or Northern Kurdistan, about ten years ago, I saw with my own eyes that democratic confederalism was already being practiced in some form in areas where Kurdish mayors had been elected. That is how I see it.




You recently joined hundreds of individuals and organizations in signing an international appeal demanding the implementation of the right to hope for Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan. What significance do you think this international solidarity and mobilization has for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question?




Yes, as I said earlier, I believe that the struggle for Abdullah Öcalan's freedom is extremely important for the situation in that region. Moreover, as I have already mentioned, its significance extends far beyond that region. Because Abdullah Öcalan addresses everyone in his writings, not only the people living in that region. Therefore, the presence of someone like him is extremely important.




He does not really want to be a leader in the conventional sense. He wants to be a guide. Having such a guide, being able to speak with him and ensuring that he can participate in important decision-making discussions would be truly significant. And, unless I am mistaken, I believe the Kurdish people want the same thing. I think this is one of the conditions the Kurdish people want to see fulfilled so that they can genuinely achieve peace and work together with the national institutions of Turkey, Syria or other countries.




Kurdish women have played an important role in the struggle for peace, democracy and women's rights for many years. As a feminist activist who has been involved in this struggle for decades, how do you assess women's role in the current peace process? Why is their participation so important for building genuine and lasting peace?




This is one of the fundamental issues facing the entire world. You know, women have always been a driving force for peace, and a very powerful one. They have always played a very important role in holding society together, speaking about peace and preserving social cohesion. This is extremely important. We have also seen how important women's role in society is in North and East Syria. Women played, and continue to play, an extremely important role in maintaining peace, preventing violence, stopping violence and attacks against women, and keeping society together.




Therefore, this is very important not only there but everywhere. It is their concern, but it is also the concern of those of us living in Europe and of people throughout the world. Women are struggling for this as well.




Finally, what role should the European Union and the international community play in supporting this peace process? What message would you like to convey to the European public regarding the freedom of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan and a solution to the Kurdish question?




My message is that they should listen to what Abdullah Öcalan says, read what he writes and understand what he expects from the international community. I think the current Pope has also understood this. I mean, if you read his latest encyclical, it almost seems as though he has read Öcalan too. You can see this in what he says about peace, society, women, young people and many other issues.




Therefore, I believe the international community, particularly those who have a say in decision-making, need to read and listen. Because today, throughout the world, we are talking much more about war than peace. This is truly devastating. All the promises made after the Second World War have, in a sense, been swept aside. Human rights, peace, dialogue and all those values have been abandoned.




And for what? For the militarization of society, the struggle to control resources, attempts to dominate territories and conflicts between opposing sides. It is society that suffers the consequences of all this.




That is why they must first listen, read and then make their assessments. Once they have done so, they must also be prepared to take steps to secure Abdullah Öcalan's freedom and put peace processes into practice.

title: KJK: The time for self-defence is now!
content:
The Coordination of the Kurdistan Women’s Community (KJK) issued a written statement ahead of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Emphasising the importance of strengthening women's organisation and unity against male-dominated violence, the KJK stated that the Peace and Democratic Society Process would create new opportunities for women's free participation and their struggle for freedom.




The statement said: "Violence against women has never before been carried out with such depth and systematic intensity. Male-dominated violence, which has reached horrific levels and permeates every month, every day and every moment of the year, has made it imperative to say ‘enough is enough’. In this regard, effective results can only be achieved if we, as women, unite in organised struggle against femicide, the destruction of life, society and nature perpetrated by capitalist modernity — the representative of our era's murderous system of domination — and its derivatives, which inject these forms of destruction into every cell of life.




Against a culture of violence embedded in every aspect of social life, we, as women, need plans and projects that establish a multidimensional perspective of struggle, ranging from transforming the organisation of everyday life and relationships to building alternative structures for a free life. At a time when violence has become a culture and a way of life, the process of democratic integration initiated by Rêber Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] brings all peoples and oppressed groups together within a framework of interconnectedness, while opening up new horizons of struggle for all the oppressed, particularly women."




The statement added: "With the development of the Peace and Democracy Process, our women's liberation perspective and the seeds of an alternative life will grow much stronger. One of the fundamental objectives of the Peace and Democratic Society Process is to pave the way for women's democratic and free participation. Through this process, the ground will also be created for a more comprehensive and profound struggle against violence targeting women, as well as all attitudes that marginalise and objectify women in every sphere of life. The Democracy and Peace Process will therefore also be a process through which women's freedom, their understanding of liberation and their fundamental human rights can be advanced in every sphere of life.




This year, we approach the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on 25 November with a new, comprehensive and profound perspective. We respond by strengthening women's unity in Kurdistan, the Middle East and across the world, and by advancing their collective struggle. Let us transform 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, into an even stronger expression of women's solidarity, unity and struggle than in previous years."




The statement continued: "The reality of 25 November places upon women's movements, above all, the duty and responsibility to organise through women's own collective wisdom and to democratise society under women's leadership. For this reason, everyone — particularly women comrades — must strengthen and expand their organisation with every step they take, successfully carrying this march towards freedom into cities, villages, streets, neighbourhoods, factories, schools, homes and the lives of individuals. The male-dominated system, which is the gravedigger of society and women, operates strategically and politically at global, regional and local levels. If it implements its agenda multidimensionally at every moment of life, then we, as women's movements, must also wage a multidimensional struggle everywhere and at all times, based on a strategy and politics of women's liberation.




We can develop our existence by expanding our world of meaning through struggle, organisation and the power of self-defence. On this basis, we can change and transform society and men, and create a world in which it is possible to breathe freely. In this way, the tradition of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, whose roots go back to the Mirabal sisters and extend to Sakine Cansız, will open the doors to a world free from violence.




Let us strengthen our organised, collective women's struggle under the slogan 'through women's organization against violence, the time for self-defence is now!' to overcome violence and lay the foundations of a new life alongside women struggling for freedom, equality and justice. Let us speak with one voice and one heart on 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, and make the 21st century an era of women's liberation."

title: KNK warns of division in South Kurdistan and calls on KDP and PUK to engage in dialogue
content:
The Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) has warned of further divisions among Kurdish institutions amid the escalating government crisis in South Kurdistan. Following the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan’s (PUK) announcement that it would withdraw from the regional government and its threat to establish parallel administrative structures in Sulaymaniyah, the KNK called on the two dominant parties in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), the KDP and PUK, to resume negotiations without delay. It stressed that political power struggles must no longer be conducted at the expense of the population and the region’s constitutionally guaranteed autonomy.




The latest escalation was triggered by Wednesday’s election of a new parliamentary leadership in Hewlêr (Erbil). After nearly two years of political deadlock, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), together with smaller parties and minority representatives, pushed ahead with the parliamentary session. The PUK and several opposition parties boycotted the vote because no agreement had been reached on the future distribution of power. With 52 of the 100 members of parliament participating, the session barely secured the required majority. KDP politician Vala Fareed was elected speaker of parliament.




PUK leader Bafel Talabanî subsequently declared that his party would recognize neither the parliamentary session nor any government formed as a result of it. He announced the party’s withdrawal from the existing regional government and threatened to establish separate government and administrative offices in Sulaymaniyah if the KDP continued on its current course. As a result, the dispute now concerns not only the formation of a government, which has been deadlocked since the October 2024 elections, but also the unity of South Kurdistan’s political institutions.




KNK offers to mediate between the parties




In its statement, the KNK described the developments as a serious threat to regional stability. It warned that the ongoing disputes were already disrupting public life and jeopardizing the political achievements of the Kurdish population.




The organization recalled that it had repeatedly held talks with the parties involved since the parliamentary elections in October 2024 and urged them to form a government without delay. The KNK said it had also expressed its willingness to mediate between the KDP and PUK. According to the organization, the latest escalation made reaching a political agreement all the more urgent.




“The leaderships of the KDP and PUK, together with all political forces, must engage in comprehensive dialogue as soon as possible and with the necessary sense of responsibility to reach a national and patriotic understanding,” the statement said.




The KNK called on the parties to subordinate their interests in political power to a shared political responsibility. The priorities, it stressed, must be ensuring a functioning government, strengthening institutions, upholding the rule of law, and addressing the needs of the population. Civil society organizations and other social groups should also participate in efforts to find a solution, it added.




National unity as a prerequisite for stability




Through its offer of mediation, the KNK aims to prevent political divisions between Hewlêr and Sulaymaniyah from becoming further entrenched. The congress warned that the autonomous rights of the Kurdistan Region would be particularly at risk if the rival parties extended their dispute into state institutions.




Preserving these achievements, it emphasized, must take precedence over party-political interests. The KNK therefore reaffirmed its willingness to exhaust all possibilities for bringing the KDP and PUK closer together.




“The path to national unity is the only way to overcome the existing differences and ensure peace and stability for our people,” the statement concluded.

author: Freedom Editor
title: The Whistles of Minneapolis
content:
How blowing a whistle to stop ICE raids opens up a challenge to the techno-fascists

The tools of state authoritarianism are changing fast. Swarms of drones levelling Gaza and mapping European airports; “flock” street cameras and cyber surveillance webs cataloguing everyone that moves through the major cities or uses a cell phone; state-directed bot armies using deep fake video and memes to alter people’s interior psyches.

A large part of the USA’s economic growth over the last few years has been the ever-larger digital surveillance and weapons industries, with Palantir and Amazon Web Services allowing governments to create vast databases of citizens’ lives, with ominous results. Digital and AI technologies have well-begun acting as accelerants of the domination and exhaustion of workers and the Earth’s ecologies. Commentators and scholars increasingly warn of geopolitical parallels with the twentieth century’s most wicked son, fascism.

Only this time the fash are equipped with expansive digital technologies of war, policing, surveillance, and propaganda.

But anti-fascist movements have begun to adapt, inventing organic technologies as new forms of counter-power. For example, when Trump sent Immigration Control and Enforcement (ICE), newly formed as a MAGA federal militia, to Minnesota to abduct, detain, and deport people of colour, organisers responded by mass 3-D printing a simple but effective technology: whistles. In Minneapolis, a longstanding hub of leftist organising, protesters wear these whistles as they take to the streets to disrupt ICE operations.

For more than a year, these same organisers and protestors have watched ICE agents on their city raids. Using encrypted cell phones to communicate to each other in Signal loops, they try to warn neighbours before the agents arrive. Thousands monitor the Signal loops for word of a raid, waiting for the moment to run out of their homes, blowing their anti-ICE whistles, so that all within earshot can try to flee the raids if they feel at risk. They are joined as community self-defence councils and more underground crews, with memberships in the tens of thousands. With some undocumented families hesitant to even leave their homes for fear of being disappeared by a federal sweep at the bus stops and outside of schools, mutual aid networks organise transportation networks to help their neighbours arrive at their workplaces and schools undetected.

The community councils have innovated on the road blockade to create what they call “filter blockades” across their neighbourhood streets, designed to allow neighbours to pass freely but prevent the passage of federal agents. Community defence crews counter-surveil federal authorities, setting up outside ICE’s headquarters at the Fort Snelling, a federal compound at the confluence of the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers that flow down through the North Woods and Western prairies. One hundred and fifty years ago, the United States Army forcibly marched thousands of Dakota Peoples into a concentration camp at the fort. Hundreds of Dakota prisoners died their first winter there, murdered, frozen to death, and starved. Now, federal forces carry out new forms of domination from the fort, part of what the federal government claims as their “unorganised territory” – lands never incorporated into any state or Native American government and thus under the direct control of the presidency through the Department of the Interior.

In Minneapolis’ Whittier neighbourhood, dissenters briefly raised an autonomous zone blockade at the site of the ICE murder of Alex Pretti, a nurse turned community defender. This is the same patch of concrete that, during the George Floyd uprisings, nurtured an epicenter of intense Black Lives Matter anti-police organising. From May 2020 until more than a year later, liberationists controlled a block of the neighbourhood as a police-free zone. Along the edge of Fort Snelling, an infrastructure that was and remains, as Nick Estes has called it, an infrastructure of U.S. power to genocide Indigenous people and Dakota people, organisers with First Nations United have started a Land Back protest and prayer camp on the land that was taken from their families more than a century ago. For these liberationists, only re-territorialising the land as Indigenous Land can end the cycles of history of white nationalist federal state detention and murder that have been perpetrated on the site.

These abolitionist tactics of not letting federal agents do their work uphold and make possible liberation struggles of many kinds. As it is practiced in the streets, self-defence against ICE becomes a logic against white nationalism because ICE targets people of colour, whom they construct to be the “illegals” of the global diaspora (no one is illegal). The uprisings also express logics of opposition to capitalism, because multinational capital seeks to restrict people’s freedoms of movement and mobilisation, not least across nation-state borders, to exploit the unevenness of global labour markets created by colonialism, imperialism, and unequal exchange. As the Trump administration labels those participating “antifa”, and formally declares them members of a domestic terrorist organisation, these people become revolutionaries in the eyes of the increasingly fascist state, willing or not.

Blowing a whistle to stop ICE raids opens up a challenge to the techno-fascists. So do the very low-tech efforts to help transport and harbour people targeted by the USA federal government for deportation. Still more organic technologies like these are needed to mount a serious rejection of the fash and the truly enormous amounts of energy the digital technologies of militarism and the consumer economy now demand. AI data centres will within the decade consume as much electricity as the nation of India. They will also consume vast amounts of freshwater. All this comes in an already destabilised climate with shrinking freshwater supplies worldwide. Day Zero, the moment when a major city runs out of fresh water, is already nearly here in Mexico City, Chennai, and Tehran. Los Angeles planners are working hard to continue expanding their ever-declining water sources, building new infrastructure to draw down water from ever more distant watersheds.

Fash power is partly techno-power, raising the need for struggles to create new organic technologies to uphold life free from domination and with a collective equality between human communities and broader communities of living beings. But any ecological politics that aims to respect human life, decarbonise and detoxify economies, and stop biological extinctions, must do so by countering far-right and capitalist structures. To “melt” ICE and stop the polar ice-caps from melting are but two components of the same struggle: to degrow the planetary economy so that it will not dominate planetary life.

This article was first published in Catalan

title: Erdoğan'dan Aliyev'e ‘kardeşim’ mektubu: Ankara-Bakü geriliminin gölgesinde kutlama
content:
AKP’li Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Azerbaycan’ın 8 Kasım Zafer Günü’nün altıncı yıl dönümü dolayısıyla Azerbaycan Cumhurbaşkanı İlham Aliyev’e mektup gönderdi. Azerbaycan Cumhurbaşkanlığı’nın internet sitesinde 7 Kasım’da yayımlanan mektubun “Sayın Cumhurbaşkanı, aziz kardeşim” sözleriyle başlaması dikkat çekti.

Türkiye ile Azerbaycan arasındaki ilişkilere de değinen Erdoğan, Şuşa Beyannamesi ile en üst seviyeye taşınan “Bir millet, iki devlet” anlayışını vurguladı.

Erdoğan, iki ülkenin hem ikili ilişkilerde hem de uluslararası alanda yakın iş birliği ve dayanışma içinde çalışmayı sürdüreceğine inandığını belirtti.

Erdoğan’ın mektubu, Azerbaycan’da yaşanan başörtüsü tartışmasının ardından Ankara ile Bakü arasında ortaya çıkan gerilimin gölgesinde geldi.

Tartışmanın ardından başta eski Cumhurbaşkanı Danışmanı Oktay Saral olmak üzere AKP’li isimler Azerbaycan yönetimine yönelik sert açıklamalarda bulunmuştu. Azerbaycan yönetimi bazı isimlere ülkeye giriş yasağı getirirken, Saral tepkilerin ardından görevinden alınmıştı.

Gerilimin sürdüğü dönemde Azerbaycan Cumhurbaşkanı Aliyev, Ankara’da düzenlenen Türk Devletleri Teşkilatı Zirvesi’ne katılmamıştı. Aliyev’e yakınlığıyla bilinen APA haber ajansında yayımlanan bir yazıda da AKP iktidarına yönelik ağır suçlamalara yer verilmişti.

Erdoğan, daha önce Güney Kore dönüşünde gazetecilere yaptığı açıklamada 8 Kasım’da Azerbaycan’ı ziyaret etmeyi planladığını söylemişti.

Aliyev’e gönderilen mektup, iki ülke arasındaki ilişkilerde yaşanan gerilimin ardından Ankara’nın yakın iş birliği ve dayanışma mesajını yeniden öne çıkardığı bir adım olarak değerlendirildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Barış Akademisyenlerinin 215 dosyası Danıştay’da bekliyor
content:
Barış Akademisyenleri, 2016–2018 yılları arasında olağanüstü hal (OHAL) döneminde çıkarılan kanun hükmünde kararnamelerle (KHK) kamu görevinden ihraç edilen akademisyenlerin açtığı davalardaki güncel durumu paylaştı.




İhraçların üzerinden 10 yıl geçerken, akademisyenlerin açtığı davaların önemli bir bölümü halen bölge idare mahkemeleri, Danıştay, Danıştay İdari Dava Daireleri Kurulu (İDDK) ve Anayasa Mahkemesi (AYM) aşamalarında bulunuyor.




10 OHAL KHK’siyle 406 Barış Akademisyeni kamu görevinden ihraç edilmişti.




OHAL Komisyonu 385 başvuruyu reddetti







İhraçların ardından başvuruların ilk adresi, 2017’de kurulan OHAL İşlemleri İnceleme Komisyonu oldu.




Komisyon, Barış Akademisyenlerinin 385 başvurusunu reddetti. Komisyon ret kararlarını 2021’in sonunda açıkladı ve ancak bu tarihten sonra idare mahkemelerine başvuru yapılabildi.




Barış Akademisyenleri bu nedenle yargıya erişimin yaklaşık beş yıl boyunca engellendiğini belirtti.




İdare mahkemelerinde 190 ret, 173 kabul kararı




Komisyon kararlarının ardından idare mahkemelerinde toplam 384 dava açıldı.




Bunlardan 190’ında akademisyenlerin başvurusu reddedilirken, 173 davada kabul kararı verildi. Paylaşılan verilere göre 21 davaya ilişkin bilgi ise eksik.




İlk derece mahkemelerinin kararları daha sonra bölge idare mahkemelerine (BİM) taşındı.




BİM aşamasında 155 dosyada istinaf başvuruları davacı lehine kabul edildi ya da karar davacı lehine kaldırıldı. 130 dosyada ise süreç davacı aleyhine sonuçlandı.




78 dava hakkında henüz karar verilmedi.




23 akademisyenin göreve iadesi kesinleşti




Davaların Danıştay 5. Dairesi’ndeki aşamasında ise şimdiye kadar 23 dosyada akademisyenler lehine verilen kararlar onandı. Böylece bu davalarda göreve iadeler kesinleşti.




Beş davada akademisyenler aleyhine verilen kararlar onandı. Bu dosyalarda bir sonraki hukuki aşama Anayasa Mahkemesi’ne bireysel başvuru.




Danıştay ayrıca bir davada akademisyen aleyhine bozma kararı verdi. Bölge idare mahkemesinin kararından farklı olan dosya yeniden BİM’de görüşülüyor.




41 davada ise Danıştay akademisyenler lehine bozma kararı verdi. Bu dosyalar da bölge idare mahkemelerine geri gönderildi.




Bu 41 dosyanın dokuzunda BİM önceki, davacı aleyhine kararında ısrar etti. Bu davaların bir sonraki aşaması Danıştay İdari Dava Daireleri Kurulu olacak.




215 dosyada henüz karar yok




Danıştay 5. Dairesi önündeki 215 davada ise 6 Kasım itibarıyla henüz karar verilmedi.




Dokuz dava Danıştay İdari Dava Daireleri Kurulu aşamasında bulunurken, akademisyenler aleyhine kesinleşen kararlarla ilgili beş başvuru da Anayasa Mahkemesi aşamasında.

title: Süper Lig'in 11. hafta maçı: Kocaelispor deplasmanda Eyüpspor'u 2-0 yendi
content:
Kocaelispor, deplasmanda Eyüpspor'u 2-0 yendi.

5. dakikada Kocaelispor öne geçti. Sissoho'nun ceza yayının sol çaprazından şutunda, kaleci Moldovan meşin yuvarlağı çeldi. Dönen topu altıpas çizgisinin gerisinde önünde bulan Agyei'nin vuruşunda, meşin yuvarlak ağlarla buluştu: 0-1.

12. dakikada Baku'nun pasında ceza yayının gerisinde topla buluşan Uğur Kaan Yıldız'ın vuruşunda meşin yuvarlak, Eyüpspor savunmasına çarpıp kaleye yöneldi. Kaleci Moldovan, meşin yuvarlağı önledi.

22. dakikada Massanga'nın pasında topla buluşan Boutobba, Kocaelisporlu Berkan Kutlu'dan sıyrıldıktan sonra ceza sahasının sağ çaprazından şutunu çekti. Kaleci Serhat Öztaşdelen, meşin yuvarlağı önledi.

28. dakikada Kocaelispor farkı 2'ye çıkardı. Tayfur Bingöl'ün uzun pasında sol kanatta topla buluşan Baku, ceza sahasının sol tarafındaki Rivas'a meşin yuvarlağı aktardı. Bu oyuncunun pasında ceza yayında topla buluşan Berkan Kutlu'nun bekletmeden vuruşunda, meşin yuvarlak kalecinin solundan ağlarla buluştu: 0-2.

Kocaelispor, karşılaşmanın ilk yarısını 2-0 üstün tamamladı.

55. dakikada Uğur Kaan Yıldız'ın sağ kanattan kullandığı serbest vuruşta ceza yayının içerisinde topla buluşan Sissoho'nun bekletmeden şutunda, meşin yuvarlak az farkla üstten auta gitti.

67. dakikada Raux Yao'nun pasında savunmanın arkasına sarkan Abdullahi, kaleci Serhat'tan sıyrıldıktan sonra ceza sahasının sağ çaprazından vuruşunu yaptı. Kocaelisporlu Emir Ortakaya, kaleci Serhat'ın müdahalesine rağmen kaleye yönelen topa müdahale ederek golü önledi.

90+1. dakikada paslaşılarak kullanılan kornerde sağ kanatta topla buluşan Sadia, arka direğe doğru ortasını açtı. Bu noktada bulunan Yusuf Barası'nın kafa vuruşunda, meşin yuvarlak üstten auta çıktı.

Kocaelispor, müsabakadan 2-0'lık galibiyetle ayrıldı.

title: Düzce'de av tüfeğiyle vurulan 16 yaşındaki çocuk öldü
content:
Fotoğraf: Tima Miroshnichenko/Pexels

Düzce'nin Gümüşova ilçesinde 16 yaşındaki Ahmet K., çıkan tartışmada av tüfeğiyle vurularak hayatını kaybetti.

Olay, Gümüşova ilçesine bağlı Yongalık köyünde meydana geldi. Edinilen bilgiye göre, Ahmet K. (16) ile A.İ.U. (17) arasında henüz belirlenemeyen bir nedenle tartışma çıktı.

Tartışmanın köy dışındaki orman yolunda kavgaya dönüşmesi üzerine A.İ.U., yanında bulunan av tüfeğiyle Ahmet K.'ye ateş ederek olay yerinden kaçtı.

İhbar üzerine bölgeye sevk edilen polis ekipleri, Ahmet K.'yi yerde hareketsiz halde buldu. Olay yerine gelen sağlık ekipleri, çocuğun yaşamını yitirdiğini belirledi.

Ahmet K.'nin cenazesi, otopsi işlemleri için Düzce Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi Eğitim Araştırma ve Uygulama Hastanesi morguna kaldırıldı.

Olayın ardından kaçan 17 yaşındaki A.İ.U. ise polis ekipleri tarafından gözaltına alındı.
