Παράλληλα, οι βασικές ανάγκες όσων κατοίκων έχουν καταφέρει να παραμείνουν στην περιοχή υποτιμώνται διαρκώς, με παραδείγματα όπως οι ελάχιστες θέσεις στους βρεφονηπιακούς σταθμούς της γειτονιάς, οι ελλείψεις στα σχολεία κ.α. Πλάι στην διαρκή υποτίμηση των κατοίκων, έρχεται και η καταστολή όσων αγωνίζονται στα Εξάρχεια. Το γκλοπ του μπάτσου πάει μαζί με την επένδυση του επιχειρηματία και στην περίπτωση των Εξαρχείων, με τις αστυνομικές δυνάμεις να έχουν στρατοπεδεύσει στην περιοχή, να χτυπούν βάναυσα τις διαδηλώσεις που γίνονται ή καταλήγουν στα Εξάρχεια, να εγκλωβίζουν κόσμο σε μαγαζιά, να συλλαμβάνουν αδιακρίτως και να γεμίζουν με χημικά την περιοχή. Η καταστολή αυτή, βέβαια, έχει περάσει από το επίπεδο των αγωνιστικών κινητοποιήσεων, στο επίπεδο της καθημερινότητας των κατοίκων της γειτονιάς, με τα σεξιστικά και χυδαία σχόλια των μπάτσων να δίνουν και να παίρνουν, με τις διμοιρίες να σουλατσάρουν δίπλα σε δημοτικά σχολεία, με μπάτσους να εγκλωβίζουν 100αδες ανθρώπους σε μαγαζιά, με επιθέσεις με δακρυγόνα σε παιδικές εκδηλώσεις. Μπροστά στους τουρίστες και τα αφεντικά, οι μπάτσοι είναι σούζα, διασφαλίζοντας τα συμφέροντα και την ομαλότητα της καλοπέρασης τους επιβεβαιώνοντας το διαχρονικό σύνθημα: στους πλούσιους υπηρέτης και στους φτωχούς νταής, αυτή είναι η ξεφτίλα του να ‘σαι ματατζής.




Πλατεία – Στρέφης – Πολυτεχνείο: Τα Εξάρχεια δεν μπαίνουν σε μουσείο




Τρία κομβικά για την αγωνιστική ιστορία της γειτονιάς σημεία – ορόσημα των Εξαρχείων βρίσκονται στα νύχια του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου, υπό αστυνομική κατοχή: η πλατεία Εξαρχείων, ο λόφος του Στρέφη και το Πολυτεχνείο. Στην πλατεία Εξαρχείων έχει γίνει πλέον ξεκάθαρη με όλους τους τρόπους η πολιτική σκοπιμότητα της κατασκευής μετρό. Το μετρό ήρθε για να εδραιώσει την στρατοπέδευση των μπάτσων στην πλατεία Eξαρχείων, ως συνέχεια της πάγιας αστικής στρατηγικής -σε συνέχεια του σπρωξίματος της ναρκοπιάτσας τα προηγούμενα χρόνια- με στόχο να ξεκόψει την πλατεία από τον χαρακτήρα της πολιτικοποίησης και της αγωνιστικότητας που είχε για δεκαετίες. Αυτό γίνεται ακόμη πιο εμφανές εδώ και έναν και πλέον χρόνο όπου οι εργασίες έχουν σταματήσει ενώ το έργο έχει κριθεί ακατάλληλο για αυτό το σημείο, και παράλληλα οι μπάτσοι, οι λαμαρίνες και η μεγαλοκατασκευαστική της ΑΒΑΞ παραμένουν στην πλατεία, με την τελευταία να έχει χρυσοπληρωθεί για ένα «δημόσιο» έργο το οποίο δεν εκτελείται.




Ταυτόχρονα στον λόφο του Στρέφη, έναν χώρο όπου η απαγόρευση για την διοργάνωση πολιτικών εκδηλώσεων και κινήσεων οικονομικής ενίσχυσης είχε αρχίσει να επιχειρείται να επιβληθεί ήδη από το 2018, έχει γίνει κανονικότητα η στρατοπέδευση των δυνάμεων καταστολής. Ο πραγματικός τους ρόλος στην εξάλειψη της εγκληματικότητας έχει αποδειχθεί καθ’ όλους αυτούς του μήνες με την αρμονική τους συνύπαρξη με τα κυκλώματα ναρκεμπορίου που λυμαίνονταν τον λόφο του Στρέφη και τα ξεκαθαρίσματα λογαριασμών μεταξύ ντιλεράδων που λάμβαναν χώρο λίγα μέτρα παρακάτω. Ο παρασιτικός τους ρόλος αποδεικνύεται καθημερινά: από τα φασιστικά συνθήματα που γράφουν, από τον τραμπουκισμό των επισκεπτών του λόφου, ακόμη και παιδιών, από τις προσαγωγές που κάνουν κάθε λίγο και λιγάκι. Και στον λόφο του Στρέφη, αφού η εργολαβική εταιρεία της prodea ανέλαβε την ανάπλαση του, αφήνοντας τον σε πολύ χειρότερη κατάσταση απ’ ότι τον παρέλαβε και εισπράττοντας παράλληλα εκατομμύρια, αποτέλεσε το προεόρτιο για την μόνιμη εγκατάσταση της συμμορίας της ΕΛ.ΑΣ, η οποία εξακολουθεί να λυμαίνεται ακόμη τον λόφο. Την ίδια στιγμή, η δημοτική αρχή υπό τον «προοδευτικό» μανδύα παίζει τον βρώμικο ρόλο της μιλώντας για «κοινωνική ειρήνη» στον λόφο και παράλληλα ψάχνει εναγωνίως μισθωτή για το αυθαίρετο του Εξωστρεφή, ώστε να εδραιωθεί και σ’ αυτό το σημείο η καπιταλιστική κερδοφορία με την απαραίτητη αστυνομική παρουσία που θα εξασφαλίσει με την βία την κοινωνική ειρήνη.




Τα Εξάρχεια έχουν ιστορία και η ιστορία γράφεται από όσους αγωνίζονται




Οι υφιστάμενοι συσχετισμοί δύναμης που έχουν διαμορφωθεί στα Εξάρχεια δεν είναι ούτε μη αναστρέψιμοι ούτε το τέλος της ιστορίας. Η καταστολή πάντοτε επιχειρούσε να πάρει το πάνω χέρι στα Εξάρχεια. Η διαφορά με τις παλαιότερες εποχές είναι ότι η απάντηση σε μια «μπούκα» σε ένα μαγαζί και η προσαγωγή 50 ατόμων, σήμαινε ότι την επομένη 500 θα βρίσκονταν στον δρόμο για αυτούς. Η διαφορά είναι ότι μια περιπολία Δέλτα θα έτρωγε επιθέσεις σύσσωμα από τον κόσμο που βρισκόταν στα Εξάρχεια ανά δύο στενά. Στο χέρι μας είναι να ξαναγυρίσουμε τους συσχετισμούς δύναμης προς το μέρος των αγωνιζόμενων, στο χέρι μας είναι να σπείρουμε πάνω στο έδαφος της κοινωνικής αλληλεγγύης και των αναρχικών ερεισμάτων που έχουν χτιστεί μέσα σε δεκαετίες στα Εξάρχεια, και όχι να τα αφήνουμε έρμαιο στα μεγαλοαρπακτικά του κεφαλαίου. Με έναν αγώνα με συνέχεια, στρατηγική και μαχητικότητα που δεν θα εγκλωβίζεται στην αυτοαναφορικότητα και τις παθογένειες των μικροηγεμονισμών της παλαιάς εποχής. Με έναν αγώνα που σε πρώτο και ενεργό ρόλο θα έχει τον πραγματικό κόσμο των Εξαρχείων, αυτών που πλήττονται πρώτα και κύρια από την σημερινή συνθήκη στην γειτονιά.




Στηρίζουμε την πορεία πορείας μνήμης και συνέχειας του αγώνα των Εξαρχείων




Σάββατο 6/11 στις 21:00 στην πλατεία Εξαρχείων







Ανοιχτή 

Συνέλευση για την υπεράσπιση του Λόφου Στρέφη




ΠΛΑΤΕΙΑ ΣΤΡΕΦΗ ΠΟΛΥΤΕΧΝΕΙΟ – ΤΑ ΕΞΑΡΧΕΙΑ ΔΕΝ ΜΠΑΙΝΟΥΝ ΣΕ ΜΟΥΣΕΙΟ




ΠΑΡΑΣΚΕΥΗ, 6/11, ΠΕΖΟΔΡΟΜΟΣ ΘΕΜΙΣΤΟΚΛΕΟΥΣ




Τα ξημερώματα της 9ης Αυγούστου 2022 η πλατεία Εξαρχείων γέμισε με μπάτσους που διώχνανε τον κόσμο που άραζε εκεί. Δημιούργησαν μια περίμετρο και ευθύς εμφανίστηκαν εργάτες που άρχισαν να στήνουν τις λαμαρίνες οι οποίες βρίσκονται ακόμα εκεί μέχρι σήμερα. Όσοι/ες/α ήμασταν εκεί θυμόμαστε τις σκηνές: ΜΑΤ να σπρώχνουν γείτονισσες και να τις πετάνε σπρέι δακρυγόνου, εκεί ήταν και η Μαριάννα και ο Κυριάκος. Πλήθος κόσμου να φωνάζουμε και να βρίζουμε μπάτσους και να βγάζουμε συνθήματα για ρουφιάνους-εργάτες που μας παίρνουν την πλατεία, εκεί ήταν και ο Χρηστάρας. Δάκρια βουβά πόνου για το τι μας μέλλει, δάκρυα κοφτερά οργής για το τι θα τους κάνουμε και πώς θα μας το πληρώσουν, εκεί ήταν και η Δέσποινα.




Εκείνη ήταν η μέρα Χ για τη γειτονιά. Η εκκένωση της πλατείας και η φρουριοποίηση της ήταν κομβικό σημείο για όλους/ες/α μας καθώς αυτή η κίνηση του κράτους άλλαξε πολύ τις δυναμικές της γειτονιάς. Όχι μόνο χάσαμε τον τόπο συγκέντρωσής μας, τον χώρο όπου μπορούσαμε να αράζουμε χωρίς να καταναλώνουμε, το σημείο συνάντησης μας, αλλά στη θέση του μπήκαν λαμαρίνες και ένστολοι μπάτσοι να το φυλάνε, να μας τραμπουκίζουν, να μας επιτίθενται. Για ένα δήθεν συγκοινωνικό έργο, που από την αρχή ξέραμε πως αποσκοπούσε αποκλειστικά στην καταστροφή της πλατείας και του πολιτικού χαρακτήρα της γειτονιάς, στον εξευγενισμό της, στην αύξηση των αξιών των ακινήτων και στην εξασφάλιση υπερκερδών των επενδυτών, ενταγμένο στο γενικότερο σχέδιο για το κέντρο της Αθήνας.




Και δεν είναι τυχαία μια ανάπλαση στο κέντρο των Εξαρχείων, τη γειτονιά που κάθε λογής Πλεύρηδες, φασίστες και νεοδημοκράτες πολιτικοί έχουν ήδη από τα 90ς βάλει στο στόχαστρο για την «πάταξη της ανομίας», την πολιτική δηλαδή απονέκρωση μιας γειτονιάς που ιστορικά συσσώρευε τις αντιστάσεις της νεολαίας και αποτέλεσε τον τόπο εξέγερσης που εγκαινίασε συμβολικά την ίδια τη Μεταπολίτευση. Τα Εξάρχεια είναι ο τόπος αμέτρητων εξεγερτικών στιγμών, στιγμών που χαράκτηκαν στην ιστορία της σύγχρονης αγωνιζόμενης κοινωνίας, όπως το Πολυτεχνείο του 1973, η δολοφονία του Μιχάλη Καλτεζά το 1985, το Πολυτεχνείο του 1995, η εξέγερση που ακολούθησε την κρατική δολοφονία του Γρηγορόπουλου, φεμινιστικές πορείες και περιπολίες, πορείες ενάντια στην Ευρώπη φρούριο και άλλα πόσα. Ταυτόχρονα είναι και τόπος όπου συλλογικές διεργασίες παίρναμε τη ζωή μας στα χέρια μας ανοίγοντας καταλήψεις για τη στέγαση και την πολιτική οργάνωση, ικανοποιώντας τις ανάγκες μας συλλογικά.




Πάνω σε αυτό το νήμα όσες/α/οι δραστηριοποιούμαστε στη γειτονιά βρεθήκαμε να προστατεύουμε την πλατεία κάνοντας εκεί συνελεύσεις, περιφρουρήσεις όλο το βράδυ για την αποτροπή της άλωσής της, φτιάξαμε παιδική χαρά για τη νέα γενιά Εξαρχειωτόπουλων, φυτεύσαμε και βάψαμε την πλατεία, διοργανώσαμε πολιτικές εκδηλώσεις και συναυλίες που έφεραν χιλιάδες ανθρώπους στην πλατεία. Και όλα αυτά ανατράπηκαν ένα χάραμα με την στρατοπέδευση μπάτσων και την εγκατάσταση του εργοταξίου στην πλατεία.




Ο φράχτης υψώθηκε από 3 στα 5 μέτρα, ξηλώθηκε η παιδική χαρά, ξηλώθηκαν τα παγκάκια, έδιωξαν το άγαλμα με τους 3 έρωτες της πλατείας και κόπηκαν όλα τα δέντρα. Αν και αντιστάσεις και επιθέσεις υπήρχαν και συνεχίζουν, ο πόνος που έχουμε βιώσει βλέποντας το ξεριζωμό της γειτονιάς μας δεν είναι αμελητέος. Συνεχίζουμε όμως να αγωνιζόμαστε για τις καλύτερες μέρες που θα έρθουν, τις λαμαρίνες τις ρίξαμε ήδη δύο φορές, τους μπάτσους δεν τους φοβόμαστε πια και είναι επιτακτικό να διεκδικήσουμε ολόκληρη τη γειτονιά ξανά.




Σκατά λοιπόν σε μπάτσους και αναπλάσεις!




Στηρίζουμε την συγκέντρωση υπεράσπισης της πλατείας Εξαρχείων με το πολιτικό μας υλικό και καλούμε κι εμείς στην πορεία ιστορικής μνήμης και συνέχειας του αγώνα των Εξαρχείων

 την Παρασκευή 6/11, από τις 7.30μμ!

title: I think the left completely failed to form an effective covid-safety strategy.
content:
queeranarchism

:

chronicbitchsyndrome

:

queeranarchism

:

I think the left completely failed to form an effective covid-safety strategy. 

First they failed by putting far too little effort into winning systematic changes (access to health care, access to paid sick leave, ventilation of work- and public spaces, etc) and putting most of the focus on individual behaviors that they could judge individuals for (vaccines and above all masking). 

Their second failure was to then primarily rely on punitive pressure and scolding people to achieve that behavior. Which meant that this strategy only kind of worked a little when they had enough people to keep up that pressure. The moment that pressure wasn’t enough anymore, most people stopped masking because they’d only even done it because of external pressure. 

This left us with nothing. No systematic changes and no group safety. 

At that point, the third failure was to change nothing once it became abundantly clear that these tactics weren’t working. People wrote comics and long reads and video essays about the lack of solidarity of people who stopped masking, and while there was truth there, that didn’t change anything. 

Yet at no point did people take stock, re-assess and change strategy. To this day people are just doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results. In fact, people seem to just double down. Where they talked about a range of safety measures in the past they’ve switched to only talking about masking. Where they used a range of tactics in the past, they’ve switched to only scolding. 

And when you challenge them, the response is something like “But I am right, this is unjust, so people 

should

 change when I tell them it is unjust”. But that’s not a strategy. Creating societal change doesn’t require being right, it requires having an effective plan on how to actually achieve real change. 

And I don’t have a full draft of what would make an effective strategy. I think unions could play a big role in achieving things paid sick leave and proper ventilation. But I don’t have all the answers either. I think there needs to be an acknowledgement that what’s currently happening isn’t working, and that a new strategy is long overdue.

ventilation and air filtration are the most important, and its exhausting to be constantly screaming this from the rooftops every day.

organizers have the power to make community events covid-safer and accessible for the at-risk disabled via two simple tracks: hold events outside, and purchase air purifiers to run at indoor events. (advertise on your literature that the air at your indoor events will be purified, otherwise disabled people will assume it’s not and we can’t come.)

stand-alone air purifiers run from around $200 to the $1000 range, depending on size and efficiency, and purchasing a single one should be doable for a fundraising event and/or collective purchase by most organizations with more than a handful of organizers (at least, in north america and europe, which is unfortunately the only economies i have knowledge about organizing within and so is all i am talking about right now).

the things that do not work, as said above, are guilting, shaming, or bullying individuals into taking individual mitigations. this does not make your community space safe for disabled individuals. on top of that, if you are indoors, requiring masks doesn’t make it safe for us anyway unless you are also purifying the air. mask-required events in poorly ventilated indoor areas without filtration end up mostly serving groups of abled people and people who are otherwise not at high risk from viral infections, who are well meaning, but failing to achieve what this accommodation should be targeting.

this has been something i have been agitating for locally for over two years now, to very little avail, because i am fighting against a veritable nonprofit industrial complex pushing the “guilt people for not masking and do nothing else” party line. there isn’t even any publicly available educational literature locally on why masking does and doesn’t work and why air filtration is a significantly more useful accommodation. i am doing my best to compile some information into a database, but designing effective propaganda is outside of my wheelhouse, and it feels like a losing battle at times.

Gonna reblog this version again because this gets reply it. 

Everyone else: please stop focussing on the ‘scolding’ part. We don’t need a kinder, more persuasive covid activism that focuses only on making individual people wear masks. This post was never about tone. 

We need 

strategies 

to achieve 

systematic changes

 of our 

material conditions

. Changes that will be 

continuously effective

 regardless of peoples continued commitment to covid-safety and when we have a strategy we need 

action at the local level

 to to put those changes into action. 

Go pressure your city council to demand mandatory ventilation in stores. Start a fundraiser for ventilation in your anarchist community center. Organize in your union for paid sick leave and work-from-home-when-you-have-a-cold guidelines. Go forth and change the material conditions of safety.

title: Peter Gelderloos: Breathing Room
content:
Woodcut by Frans Masereel







from Peter Gelderloos’ substack page, 

Suviving Leviathan

, 05/11/2026







Breathing Room




from the apocalyptic, fascistic Right to the insufficient, hypocritical, quietly genocidal Left




In the recent elections in Brasil, one of the largest countries in the Global South, leftwing darling Lula beat Flavio Bolsonaro, the fascistic dynast supported by the country’s plantation owner class. In Israel, the extreme Right lost the elections to the far Right (not a typo). And in the US, a “blue wave” has given the Democrats an ample margin of control in both chambers of Congress as well as a strong majority of governorships (for non-US readers, for whatever weird-ass reason related to our especially amnesiac, isolationist culture, in the US blue is the color of the Left and red is the color of the Right). In once Republican-held or toss-up states like Texas, North Carolina, and New Jersey, Democratic candidates won by double digits while conservatives won in what were, until yesterday, solidly Republican states like Florida or Louisiana by only 1 or 2%.







A high level Republican operative connected to Trump admitted to the press that these elections were just “too big to rig,” casually acknowledging how common it is to redraw electoral maps or send the precise vote-counting machines to the friendly districts and low quality, high-failure-rate machines to the unfriendly districts, in order to win an extra percentage point and tip elections.




Brasil




In Brasil, where former far Right president Jair Bolsonaro serves a sentence of house arrest in his mansion for launching a failed coup attempt after he lost the 2022 elections, his son Flavio Bolsonaro carried the first round of the elections in early October but failed to attain a majority. In the second round, held October 25

th

, voters turned to the Left and re-elected the incumbent, Lula, off the Workers’ Party. Wealthy investors punished the country for their vote, with the Brasilian stock market taking a plunge after the election even though Lula is a very business-friendly politician who has overseen a large deal of growth and “development” in the Brasilian economy. In practice that means he promotes oil drilling and mining in the Amazon, he subsidizes the intertwined beef-soy industry causing so much destruction in the south and west of the country, and he also supports manufacture and higher tech industry.







Brasil’s stock market index, with the big crash on the right-hand side occurring on October 25.







If Bolsonaro’s son Flavio had won this past 25

th

 of October, the death squads that work for the ranchers, soy plantation owners, miners, loggers, or directly for the state, would have had free rein. Several of my friends and many of the 

Indigenous

, 

African diasporic

, and lower class mestizo or white people 

I met last year

, people at the forefront of 

rural

 and 

urban struggles

 against the ongoing violence of colonial capitalism and 

for a better world

, would have been at greater risk of getting murdered for their resistance. For sure, a lot of people are breathing a very valid sigh of relief. But they’re not naïve about the meaning of the leftwing victory.




[Some of those links above go to 

Antimidia

 videos in Portuguese. Before pressing play, scroll down to “Legendas” and you’ll see buttons for English subtitles.]




As one friend put it, “

If Bolsonaro wins, they kill us; if Lula wins, they let us die.

” A second friend referred to a “mono-polarization” in which there are not two competing poles, just a single pole, “the extreme Right, which pulls everything into its proximity.”




Another friend described the following:







“Bolsonarismo already won. I don’t say that just because the Congress and Senate are controlled by fascists, I’m referring to Lula’s campaign replicating the methods of communication that are very close to fascism (including the name “Lula’s Army”). A few days ago on TV, Lula openly defended lowering the age at which children can be tried as adults (in order to appease the Right) and other similar things. Every time there is a “vote against fascism” which includes the attempt to also convince the Right or “center right,” the pendulum moves to the right.




“After the conservative reaction to 

the 2013 revolt

, some people (like the author Paulo Arantes) said that we were living in a situation with a horizon of diminishing expectations, without a view towards amplifying the struggles and the capacity to dream of a new world. It seems to me that now it’s worse: not only are they [the Left] slamming on the breaks, but the vital energy to struggle was channeled into the methods of the enemy.




“Perhaps what most calls my attention is how the argument for a “struggle for national sovereignty” was adopted in a terrible way. To combat Trump’s intervention pushing for a brutal extractivism to get so-called rare earth minerals, it is affirmed that [these lands and resources] are exclusively Brasilian, as though the problem were only who gets to destroy the Earth and not the destruction itself.”







And a fourth friend shared with a fair amount of alarm and heartbreak over how Lula’s campaign capitalized on the fear of Bolsonaro to break the sense of autonomy of a great many people in one of the strongest, most radical anticolonial and anticapitalist projects in the territories occupied by the Brasilian state. It even got so bad that some comrades accused those who refused to vote of secretly being Bolsonaro supporters.













This quote is from a message they sent me just before the election: “We’ll keep fighting, whoever wins. But here the possible re-election of Lula is referred to as a defeat of Bolsonarismo, and it’s nothing of the kind.”







They also recommended some texts, 

this one is an academic article

 in English, Portuguese, and Spanish about the People’s Web, an anticolonial “land back” network of communities based on direct action, mutual aid, and autonomy, and these two, which are in Spanish, address “

What Do They Mean When They Say Sovereignty?

” and “

Lands Without Borders, Owners, and Flags in Brasil and Argentina

.”







Friends, strangers, comrades, neighbors: we have been making this mistake for too fucking long. Literally millions of us have died in this struggle. We have to get smarter than binary thinking. 

If we can only consider two different options for our world, both of them are Death.

 Fuck antifascism, fuck anti-imperialism, and fuck the democrats, liberals, and Marxists who manipulate those concepts, if all they come to mean is that we have to support a slightly gentler form of colonialism, of white supremacy, of ecocide, of patriarchy. The slower path to Hell still takes you to Hell and, look around folks! We’ve arrived. False pragmatism and the extremely simple-minded strategy of “you have to vote for A because B is worse” have failed us catastrophically. Why on earth would we keep using a strategy that has brought us to this hellscape?




Other worlds are possible, they are already and still alive here in the cracks of the present system, and we desperately need to remember them, imagine them, believe in them, commit to them, and fight for them.




Israel




Let’s turn to the Israeli elections as a great example of the problem of supporting the lesser evil.




For Netanyahu and his colleagues, Arabic people voting in Israel is an existential “emergency.”




In Israel, 11 parties won seats in the Knesset. Nine of those parties are rightwing. The two leftwing parties won only 6% of the vote. And one of those parties (Democrats) isn’t even anti-genocide – they want to stop the ongoing wars and land theft but not necessarily to reverse the land theft and ethnic cleansing Israel is based on. The other, the Joint List, is led by Palestinians who have never been allowed to join the Israeli government. This was, truly, an election between the extreme Right and the far Right. The Opposition coalition won 48 seats in the Knesset, 40 of which are divided amongst three rightwing parties, and 8 of which belong to the only Israeli leftwing party. (Yep! That means that of the Israeli [non-Arabic] part of the electorate, less than 8% vote for the Left, and the rest vote for the far Right or extreme Right.)




The primary campaign promise of the Opposition coalition, led by Gadi Eisenkot’s Yasher party, was to remove Netanyahu from power, not because of all his wars and genocide, but because he’s not doing a great job at those wars and genocide. Polling consistently shows that 

the vast majority of Israelis

 are 

in favor of the genocide

 and 

the wars against Lebanon, Syria, and Iran

, but majorities were 

upset with Netanyahu

 that his government did not 

win the release of the prisoners held by Hamas

 quickly enough and that the methods being used by West Bank settlers 

might lead to more sanctions

 and a loss of support from “the international community” (Europe and the US). Also, many are miffed that *Haredi or Ultra-Orthodox Jews have 

historically been exempted

 from obligatory military service; they want all Israeli citizens to participate in the military. Others are upset with the fact that Netanyahu is avoiding a prison sentence by staying in office. He got convicted, not for war crimes, but for a pretty clear case of corruption.




*(Haredi make up a significant number of the 800,000 settlers living illegally—but with the full support of the state—in the West Bank and East Jerusalem on recently stolen land, and the political parties representing them are a part of Netanyahu’s coalition. To be clear, the Ultra-Orthodox are often the vanguard of the genocide as they attack, burn, plunder, and murder in the West Bank, they just don’t put on a uniform to do it. 

The number of West Bank settlers has roughly doubled in the last 20 years

.)




The second major promise made by the Opposition was to maintain the official, white supremacist tradition in Israeli politics and not to let any Arabic-led party into the government. Since Netanyahu’s party, Likud, still got the most votes (though they lost 9 seats in the Knesset and their ultra-nationalist allies lost a cumulative 5 seats), the only way for the Opposition to keep both of those promises is to rule with a minority coalition that does not include the two Palestinian-led parties but relies on their votes for investiture and critical legislation, which means a really solid practice of compromise. That shouldn’t be so difficult. Both of those parties have said they would do whatever it takes to get rid of Netanyahu and stop some of the more extreme new settlement projects in the West Bank.




That shouldn’t be too hard a compromise. After all, the rightwing Opposition wants to get rid of Netanyahu, and they’re okay with stopping some settlement projects since those empower their political competitors in the Orthodox camp and could hurt their economy by leading to more sanctions. The only thing that could stop them from winning control of the government is their own racism. So… I give them a 50/50 shot, at best. 

Recent polls support that kind of pessimism.

: incredibly few Israelis believe any land should be given back to the Palestinians* or that recently built settlements should be dismantled. They don’t believe the settlements are wrong, but 50% said the policy of land theft and construction in the West Bank should be “adjusted to avoid sanctions escalation and international isolation”. Amongst Netanyahu’s bloc, however, a solid majority said “the government should continue the policy ‘whatever the price’.” 52% of those polled said they could accept sanctions on individual settlers who were especially violent, but 63% opposed international sanctions being placed on goods coming from illegal settlements (“illegal,” in the media, referring to Palestinian lands stolen since the Oslo accords of 1993, not all the land stolen before that). With very few exceptions, most Israelis only oppose the daily violence of settlers in the West Bank if it might hurt them personally. As 

The Guardian

 put it: “The poll suggests that the more people feel they will be damaged personally, the more they oppose the settlement policy.”




[*Some Israeli politicians do support giving desert lands, much of it the traditional territory of Bedouins, to Palestinians as a non-consensual exchange to permanently take over more fertile Palestinian lands.]







The bullet and the ballot to keep Palestinians down. Invaders vote at an official polling station set up in the West Bank.







Here’s more detail from other polls. 

In May 2024

, after 7 months of the war on Gaza, only 4% of Israelis thought the country’s assault had gone too far, half thought Israel should directly govern Gaza after the war, and only 8% thought that the people of Gaza should be allowed to choose their own government. By that point, 

Israel had directly killed over 35,000 Palestinians in Gaza

, not counting increased deaths from disease or hunger, they had seriously injured 80,000, and forced 1.7 million out of their homes – completely destroying most of the homes along with all the belongings in them. Over 90% of Israelis thought that was the right thing to do. Actually, that’s incorrect. Half the Israelis polled thought the genocide “had not gone far enough”.




Another year of genocide didn’t soften that view. In August 2025, a poll carried out by an Israeli organization found that 76% of Israelis believed that “

there are no innocents in Gaza

,” tacitly approving of the mass murder of children and noncombatants. The poll was conducted “amid rising racist attacks against Palestinians in occupied territories and Palestinian citizens of Israel.”




An August 2026 poll found that the Israeli public supported the wars against Iran, Lebanon, and Syria, but were “

dissatisfied with the results

,” namely the failure to achieve regime-change in Iran and the slowdowns (so-called ceasefires that the Israeli military violates multiple times every day) in the invasions of Lebanon and Syria. A March 2026 poll published by the 

Times of Israel

 found that 

78% of Israelis supported the war against Iran

 (which at that point had killed at least 1,500 Iranian civilians and an unknown number of Iranian soldiers). Even half of Israelis who identified themselves as leftwing supported the war.







Actually, this isn’t Lebanon, it’s “Greater Israel.”







In conclusion, elections, democracy, and the Left won’t stop Israel’s genocide and ongoing wars because:







the vast majority of Israelis are pro-genocide




even the Left is pro-genocide and half of the Left is pro-war




the Israeli leftwing party only got 6% of the vote, which was a huge gain for them.







Surviving Leviathan with Peter Gelderloos is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.Subscribe




The US




The sweeping victory of the Democrats in yesterday’s election illustrates a point I was trying to make in “

The Right’s Rollercoaster to Hell

.” By huffing the fumes of their own ideology of power too deeply, by zealously attacking anyone they perceive as a threat to the established order, the Right frequently damage the basis of their own power. And, at least in the anglosphere, the Right have not had intelligent strategists since the days of Margaret Thatcher and Henry Kissinger. Since then, they’ve just been getting dumber and dumber.




Many people have gotten furious with the rightwing attacks: people who need abortions, people who need access to healthcare, trans folks who want to be treated like people, Black folks who need an end to centuries of lynching, exclusion, and exploitation, Muslims sick of being portrayed as terrorists and invaders, latinas and African immigrants who were being attacked regardless of their status, and all the people who don’t belong to those groups but have loved ones who are, or all those who oppose bigotry and oppression on principle. (Basically, all those whom moderate Democrats refer to as fringe groups or the “woke.”




Then there’s the fact that the stupidity of the Trump regime was wrecking the US economy. While the billionaires keep raking it in, the dollar has lost about 9% of the value it had at the beginning of 2024, 

real wages have been stagnating or falling

, 

underemployment is high

, 

groceries have been getting more expensive

, 

food insecurity, electricity, and gas prices are all going up

, 

rent has increased 44% since 2019

 and 

mortgage rates are almost three times as high

 as they were in 2021. Obviously, all those things are much harder on working class and lower income people, while the rich don’t even notice the price of gas and groceries.




So again, it’s no surprise that most people wanted a big change. This map, showing how far to the left or right the vote went compared with 2024, is a pretty clear illustration.







Three short red arrows showing the districts that shifted a little to the right. Hundreds of long blue arrows showing all the districts that moved far to the left.










Incidentally, the US stock market

 surged 

after the leftwing victory. Remember how the opposite occurred in Brasil? The market has no

 invisible hand

, and there’s no cutthroat, mercenary competition intrinsic to human nature. It’s evil rich fuckers who want Brasil to maintain itself as a plantation for the global economy, where the millionaire landowners and mine owners can easily pay cops or paramilitaries to murder labor organizers or Indigenous people who might get in the way of their investments. The very same banks, corporate execs, and multimillionaire or billionaire investors want the US to maintain a more complex economy with a huge market to import goods from around the world alongside a well educated class of researchers who can be subsidized to develop pharmaceutical, chemical, alternative energy, and computing technologies that will result in trillions of dollars of profits. But a poorer population and major cuts to research subsidies can’t sustain that kind of economy. Clearly, the State is more powerful than capitalists on their own and the capitalists don’t always get their first choice, but they’ll make do with their second. They’ll profit in Brasil under Lula, and they’re happy that things in the US are turning around but if the most powerful government in the world goes too far Left or too far Right or just too far stupid, the capitalists will take their investments elsewhere and a new coalition of powerful states will arise to uphold the global order once NATO can’t hack it. They’re already in the wings, preparing. But maybe there’s another sort of change that could happen…







With a solid majority in Congress, the Democrats will get the opportunity to pass a budget next year that they could use to defund ICE, end military aid to Israel, and restore money to public education, scientific research, and social services related to healthcare, food poverty, and support for disabled people. They can also investigate corruption in the Trump administration, ICE conspiracies to murder or otherwise violate the rights of immigrants and rapid response people, and other instances of law breaking by government officials. And if they don’t fuck it up, they’ll probably win the presidency and keep a congressional majority in 2028.




What’s more, 

progressive candidates swept a number of elections

, including in toss-up states and districts, disproving the rhetoric of the Party establishment that more voters will support moderates and leftwing candidates can’t win competitive elections. That means there’s a possibility for the party as a whole to support more progressive policies by 2028, though of course the 

New York Times

 is scrounging for any statistical manipulation or talking head or can claim the elections were a vindication of the moderate Democrats, CNN is offering AIPAC a free platform to spread Islamophobia and reinforce the idea that responsible politicians have to support Israel’s genocide, and every person or institution with power and money to the left of Hitler is trying to reinforce the idea that Jeffries and Schumer are the best possible leaders of the Party, in the hopes of preserving a pro-police, pro-deportation, pro-billionaire, pro-AI, pro-Israel agenda.




So what do all these results mean for some important questions? What kinds of changes might we expect from the electoral victories of the Left?




—




Possible







The most recent right-wing wave that has seen governments across the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Asia shift to the Right may break, at least for now.










More marginalized and lower class populations will probably get access to government-funded resources.




Some workplace protections, environmental regulations, and rights to healthcare will be expanded or restored.




The repression against anticolonial and anticapitalist movements might shift to softer tactics.




The war against Iran might end, for now.







As a low-income person who relies on government assistance for healthcare, with a lethal (but fortunately very slow-moving) cancer caused by environmental toxins, who generally works jobs that involve dangerous or unhealthy conditions and few to no benefits, and who participates in movements constantly subjected to surveillance and repression, and with beloved friends who experience more brutal forms of repression that I don’t, I’m happy for all of these things. They make a difference. But is that difference enough?




—




Not Gonna Happen







We won’t be freed of the obligation to work for bosses in jobs that are often humiliating, unhealthy, and unsafe.




Poverty won’t disappear.




We won’t be allowed to have an unalienated relationship with our homes and the land: housing will continue to be designed as a way to enrich the wealthy and preserve our dependence on them, and land will continue to be treated as property.




Prisons and police won’t disappear, and the routine torture and brutality they produce will continue.




Political repression of anarchists, autonomous movements, and Indigenous communities fighting to get their land back won’t end, and when the Left is in power those facing repression will receive less solidarity and more isolation.




No historical form of oppression like white supremacy or patriarchy will disappear; they will continue to operate through and intensify systemic features like work, poverty, housing, policing, and repression.




Israel will not stop the genocide against Palestinians.




Indigenous peoples around the world will not be allowed to have autonomy over their land and culture.




Governments and corporations from Europe, North America, and South and East Asia will not stop sponsoring wars, genocide, slave labor, and deadly mining and plantation industries across sub-Saharan Africa.




Greenhouse gas emissions reductions will not happen fast enough to avert the acceleration of the worst mass death and mass extinction events in human history. Many years, there will be no emissions reductions at all.




Real emissions reductions, when they do occur, will be based on energy technologies that prioritize economic growth and cause a huge boom in land theft, toxic mining, death squads, and habitat destruction.




Other forms of ecocide and extractivism like industrial agriculture will continue to kill the soil, destroy the forests and wetlands, abuse workers, brutalize hundreds of millions of non-human animals, and drive ongoing land theft and genocide against Indigenous peoples.




The list only continues…







These elections have won us a little bit of breathing room, nothing more. The only way to create the kinds of change we need for survival is through waves of revolution that destroy, abolish, transform, and heal all the vestiges of that trinity of evil – capitalism, colonialism, and the State.




Those three forces are inseparable. They can’t be reformed, and none of them can be abolished while leaving the others intact. Only the State has ever existed without the other two but the emergence of colonial capitalism transformed all the various state models in the world into the modern state, which has proven unable to abolish capitalism no matter how many red flags it waves.




We have an extremely low chance of helping to launch these waves of revolution, sticking to it, adapting, overcoming, and winning, and if we do succeed it’s a labor that requires generations. And yet, it’s a bet we need to take, because there’s a 100% chance of immense suffering and death under the present system. There’s a 0% chance of reforming this system into something good through the methods of change it offers us, like elections. And, of the dozens of authoritarian Left revolutions that have succeeded in their strategy of seizing state power, exactly 0 have abolished capitalism, oppressive hierarchies, poverty, wars, or ecocidal ways of living.




How about we give a chance to the methods and traditions of struggle that have always predicted that would be the outcome of electoral reform or revolutionary states? How about we give a chance to the methods and traditions of struggle that have always rejected colonial society and fought for a world of 

ecocentric communities

 organized through 

rooted networks

 and mutual aid?

author: Kate Sharpley
title: We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years : Travels of a Protest Poem
content:
As ‘We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years’ this poem is possibly the most widely reprinted item from Freedom.

In September 1893 the London anarchist newspaper Freedom : A Journal of Anarchist Communism published a poem called ‘A Humble Reminder : To the Propertied Classes’, credited to ‘N.’[1] It’s an anti-capitalist protest, lamenting the ‘workers’ dead’ whose deaths enriched those ‘propertied classes’. It rails at the rich ‘We have fed you all for a thousand years, / And you hail us still unfed’. I do not know who ‘N.’ was, though they seem to be connected to the Freedom milieu. Freedom had published another poem by them, ‘The Pet Voter’, in August 1892.[2] Max Nettlau used the same initial when writing in Freedom in June 1891; the Fabian socialist Edith Nesbit had a poem ‘A Word For The Children’ in Freedom in February 1891 (‘The right to give help is your own, / The right to claim it theirs.’) Neither seems a convincing candidate for the authorship of this poem. The Kipling connection

‘N.’ introduced their poem by saying it was ‘slightly altered from Rudyard Kipling’s Ode in praise of English Enterprise.’ That’s a reference to Kipling’s ‘Song of the Dead’ published four months earlier in The English Illustrated Magazine (May 1893). ‘N.’s address to the propertied classes ‘For if blood be the price of England’s wealth, / Good God, we ha’ paid in full’ rewrites Kipling’s address to the sea ‘If blood be the price of admiralty, / Lord God, we ha’ paid in full!’.[3] The ‘Humble Reminder’ changes Kipling’s poem – but leans heavily upon it. Mark Leier said ‘strictly speaking the poem is not a parody of Kipling’s poem but a re-working of the words based on the original verse and meter.’[4] It reminds me of Utah Philips’ comment on IWW songmaking: ‘The Wobblies liked to steal the hymn tunes ‘cos they were pretty and change the words so they made more sense.’[5]

The connection to Kipling persisted. He was credited in many of the reprints (inevitable, perhaps, given that the author remained unknown and their debt to Kipling was clear). There were even articles discussing what it would mean if the poem were by Kipling.[6] Reprinted and recited

Once printed, it was always possible for the poem to reappear, and this one spread beyond the anarchist press, becoming a standard of labour movement papers. The title often changed, varying from ‘The Cry of Toil’ to ‘The Capitalist’. Just as the connection to Kipling is sometimes there and sometimes not, the text varies between the poetic ‘ha’’ to the everyday ‘have’.

Apparently a version was published in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania in 1895.[7] The Portland anarchist newspaper The Firebrand reprinted the poem (anonymously) as ‘The Workers Outcry’ in 1897.[8] Changes had been made to Americanise the text: instead of pounds the third line talks of ‘there’s never a dollar of all your wealth’.

Sometimes you can read about the poem’s life off the printed page. In May 1897 Miss Olive Keep recited ‘We have fed you all for a thousand years’ at a gathering of the Socialist Labor Party. [9]. In August 1899, The Carpenter, a union journal for ‘Carpenters, Stair Builders, Machine Wood Workers, Planing Mill Men, and Kindred Interests’ reprinted the ‘Firebrand version’ (with credit).[10] In 1904 the poem reappeared as ‘The Price of England’s Wealth’ in Glasgow’s The Voice of Labour.[11] This version talks of ‘sovereigns’ rather than ‘pounds’ or ‘dollars’ but there are other changes: I can’t tell if it’s rewritten from the Freedom or Firebrand version.

The anarchist journal Mother Earth (‘published every 15th of the month’) reprinted ‘The Cry of Toil’ (credited to Kipling) in April 1908.[12] On April 18, 1908 it appeared in the IWW’s Industrial Union Bulletin (also credited to Kipling).[13] Once the poem was reprinted in the IWW songbook, and was later put to music (‘about 1916’ by Rudolf von Liebich), it was firmly established as a classic of working class protest.

In November 1913 strikers in Auckland used a line from the poem on their banner during the 1913 Waterfront Strike: ‘If blood be the price of your cursed wealth, good God we have bought it fair’.[14] It’s not often we get the names of people who helped circulate the text but ‘Gordon’ suggested it (as ‘The Workers’ Answer’) in the 1917 compilation New songs for Butte Mining Camp.[15]

As ‘We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years’ this poem is possibly the most widely reprinted item from Freedom. In March 1969 it was reprinted (from the IWW songbook, credited to an ‘unknown proletarian’) on the front of the third issue of the Bulletin of the Anarchist Black Cross. The band Palm Ghosts released a version in August 2026. Questions remain: Who was N? How did it get into Mother Earth? If anyone sees any evidence, please let us know. Notes

1, https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/qrfmk0 2, https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/31zfks 3, See https://www.kiplingsociety.co.uk/poem/poems_dead.htm 4, ‘Kipling Gets a Red Card,’ Labour/Le Travail n.31 (Spring 1993), 163-8. 5, Utah Phillips, intro to ‘Dump the Bosses Off Your Back’ on his album We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years (1983). 6, See ‘The New Kipling’ in Brisbane’s Daily Standard Saturday 2 May 1914. https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/178878885 7, ‘The Cry of Labor’, Mar 24, 1895 in the Sunday News. Not seen, reference from: https://weneverforget.org/hellraisers-journal-from-the-spokane-industrial-worker-cry-of-toilwe-have-fed-you-all-for-a-thousand-years/ 8, The Firebrand : For Burning Away Of The Cobwebs of Ignorance and Superstition, March 7 1897. https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/v41r69 9, The times (Washington [D.C.]), May 3, 1897 https://www.loc.gov/resource/sn85054468/1897-05-03/ed-1/ 10, https://archive.org/details/carpenter19unit/mode/2up? Page 7 11, https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/nk9c3s 12, https://archive.org/details/mother-earth/Mother%20Earth%20v03n02%20%281908-04%29%20%28-covers%20Harvard%20DSR%29/ 13, https://archive.org/details/v2n08-apr-18-1908-iub/mode/2up?q=%22we+have+fed+you+all+for+a+thousand+years%22 14, https://natlib.govt.nz/records/22878480 15, https://archive.org/details/newsongsforbutte00unse/

author: anred
title: ¡Presente, ahora y siempre! Falleció Elsa Pavón, la primera Abuela de Plaza de Mayo que recuperó a su nieta secuestrada por la dictadura
content:
Confundadora de Abuelas de Mayo y referente histórica en la lucha por los derechos humanos, fue sostén de generaciones en la lucha contra los crímenes cometidos durante la última dictadura genocida.

 Por 

Valeria Jasper, para La Izquierda Diario.







A poco de cumplir 90 años, 

Elsa Pavón

 falleció en la madrugada de este jueves.




En 1978 secuestraron a su hija, 

Mónica Grinspon

, a su yerno 

Claudio Logares

 (ambos militantes de Montoneros), y a 

Paula

, la hija de ambos, en Montevideo. Son víctimas del 

Plan Cóndor

. Allí comenzó la búsqueda y la lucha que 

Elsa

 ya no abandonaría nunca.




Elsa

 fue la primera 

Abuela de Plaza de Mayo

 que recuperaró a su nieta 

Paula

 por vía judicial y genética, en junio de 1984. Para reconocerle su verdadera identidad, el Poder Judicial tardó once años. Había sido apropiada con 23 meses de vida.




Te puede interesar: 

Elsa Pavón: “Mi hija, mi yerno y mi nieta desaparecieron en el marco del Plan Cóndor”




Elsa

 era la presidenta de la 

Asociación Anahí

, la organización que fundo 

“Chicha” Mariani

 en 1996. En agosto pasado, cuando se cumplieron 50 años de la desaparición de 

Clara Anahí Mariani Teruggi

, la nieta de 

Chicha

 que sigue desaparecida, 

Elsa

 estuvo presente junto a su nieta 

Paula

.










 


































Ver esta publicación en Instagram






































































 




Una publicación compartida por Casa Mariani Teruggi (@casamarianiteruggi)
















En esta 

convesación con Myriam Bregman

, 

Elsa

 sostuvo de forma categórica cómo 

el dolor a ella no la destruyó, sino que la construyó

.




Con las banderas en alto exigiendo 

Memoria, Verdad y Justicia

, despedimos a la querida 

Elsa

, abrazando a su nieta 

Paula

, amigos y compañeros de lucha.










 


































Ver esta publicación en Instagram






































































 




Una publicación compartida por Myriam Bregman (@myriambregman)

author: Mong Palatino
title: The thrill of group bike rides
content:
Bikers have been bonded by the daily commute or the frequent group rides, and this ritual of biking together can be turned into an advocacy action. This should not be a surprise since the tribe of bikers who regularly ride together suffers from the same grave inefficiencies that plague our roads and communities.

Biking brings calm and exhilaration at the same time, and these feelings are amplified during a group ride.

Planning a group ride takes time and patience, and it is deservedly celebrated when it happens.

It is usually done for leisure, a chill time with fellow bikers. It can be a training session for a scheduled race. Or it can become the power of many if organized to promote a cause.

Whatever the intent that pedals the ride, it is necessary to have trust, coordination, and the unity to move forward in one direction.

Safety measures are learned, relearned, enforced, and adopted during the ride. Newbies take cues from fellow riders, hand signals are introduced, and road rules that apply to cyclists are highlighted in real time. The grounding experience allows bikers to map out routes, rediscover a place from a new perspective, and become familiar with the local scenery. If field trips immerse travelers in history and the tourism value of a town or institution, a group bike tour provides the same allure and they cover even the remote corners that cars and buses cannot reach. A bike tour always offers new ways of seeing and experiencing the peripheries in our communities.

The group ride is an educative activity for all – riders, motorists, commuters, and pedestrians. It makes the bikers more visible, and this is deliberate. A lone biker wishes to be seen for his or her safety, a group ride ensures it and compels the people on the road to acknowledge the space reserved for cyclists. And if a protected bike lane is missing, the bikers crowding the street effectively become the mobile barrier that serves as a reminder not just of the presence of two-wheeled vehicles but also the right of others (non-car drivers) to use the taxpayer-funded road infrastructure.

This is the principle guiding critical mass rides which have become a global movement. An intentional biking of the many to normalize the idea of biking, encourage people to go out and bike, and destigmatize the use of roads by bikers. It is through these collective efforts that a community of bikers is formed. Bikers sharing the joy of biking and pedaling together to remove the perils of the supposedly mundane human act of travelling on a non-motorized vehicle.

There is no single community of bikers, and the diversity of these networks highlights the power that can be harnessed to deliver a message to broader segments in society. Bikers have been bonded by the daily commute or the frequent group rides, and this ritual of biking together can be turned into an advocacy action. This should not be a surprise since the tribe of bikers who regularly ride together suffers from the same grave inefficiencies that plague our roads and communities. They all see, hear, and experience the same daily evils of bad governance that propel citizens to speak out and mobilize.

Imagine a long line of bikers occupying a road, this scene repeated several times until it becomes normal. It is an attempt to rewire our perceptions of what a car-dominated street should look like. Then imagine this determined group of citizens on the move who by their mere presence reveal the glaring inadequacies in urban planning. They can be rallied to challenge car centrism and its morbid manifestations in policymaking, public works, traffic regulations, and toxic road mindset and habits.

The potential of tapping bikers to be active advocates of sociopolitical causes is confirmed by their actual participation in protest actions against controversial issues from the flood corruption scandal in 2025 to Pax Silica this year. Frequent bike rides have been organized to raise public awareness of pressing social concerns such as the critical conditions of rivers, coastal habitats, and watersheds. Both young and old bikers have shown enthusiastic participation in rides that explore historical landmarks and celebrate the opening of parks and green spaces.

Biking alone will not change the world, but it is a brave individual defiance of the norms in our motorized megapolis. Every pedal is a plea for consideration, recognition, and basic kindness. Biking together provides greater visibility and faster pace in the demand for reforms. It is popularly argued that biking is the closest thing to experiencing the freedom of flying. We can add that biking together allows us to feel the possibility of moving things, places, ourselves, and society closer towards a destination in the future that we will define.

title: Lotte contro il carovita: in Campania nasce il gruppo Le Donne del Vallo di Diano
content:
Ecco una breve intervista con il neonato gruppo 

Le Donne del Vallo di Diano 

andata in onda sulle libere frequenze di 

Blackout

. 




Siamo in Campania, più precisamente in provincia di Salerno. Il contesto è quello delle mobilitazioni degli auto trasportatori: è in questi presidi che prendono parola anche diverse giovani mamme, sul tema del carovita, del lavoro, ma anche dei diritti che vengono loro sottratti e che rivendicano, come quello alla sanità pubblica ed accessibile. 




Mariagrazia ci racconta di come hanno deciso di continuare ad organizzarsi insieme ed attraversare altre piazze come lo sciopero del 30 ottobre. Ci parla delle testimonianze che stanno raccogliendo e delle reti che intendono tessere per sostenere i produttori del territorio.

author: anred
title: Francia en huelga: un malestar que cruza generaciones
content:
Sindicatos de trabajadores y de estudiantes, chalecos amarillos, convergieron en una jornada de huelga tras cinco semanas de movilización masivas que desafían las respuestas del gobierno de Macron. Actualmente, tres generaciones convergen en un mismo espacio, ya no privado, sino público, para expresar un descontento social articulado contra la cultura del trabajo precarizado y el consumo asfixiante. Los jóvenes ven su futuro hipotecado antes de empezar; los adultos, su presente consumido por el costo de vida y la carga impositiva; los jubilados, agotados tras una vida laboral, se enfrentan a reformas que recortan o postergan lo que legítimamente les corresponde. En el plano comunicacional, existe un contraste directo entre la narrativa oficial del Ministerio del Interior, que califica las marchas como jornadas transcurridas «sin problemas», y el registro de la ciudadanía. Cientos de registros audiovisuales difundidos por los propios manifestantes muestran cómo la intervención de las fuerzas policiales y de la gendarmería, en los momentos de dispersión, suele actuar como detonante de los enfrentamientos.

 Por Mario Daniel Villagra desde Francia, para Red Eco Alternativo.







(Mario Daniel Villagra desde Francia – Red Eco Alternativo) Francia – Las manifestaciones continúan, se intensifican, se organizan y pasan de la espontaneidad a la conciencia, pese a los intentos del gobierno de Emmanuel Macron de controlarlas, desviarlas y generar desinformación. Docentes hartos de las malas condiciones de trabajo y estudiantes secundarios, que se pusieron a la cabeza de un movimiento de imaginación y cólera, empujan desde hace semanas una protesta que hoy, 5 de noviembre, suma a estudiantes y trabajadores: el motor de todo pasado, presente y futuro. Según el sindicato SNES-FSU, el 52 % del personal de colegios y liceos está en huelga.




Actualmente, tres generaciones convergen en un mismo espacio, ya no privado, sino público, para expresar un descontento social articulado contra la cultura del trabajo precarizado y el consumo asfixiante. Los jóvenes ven su futuro hipotecado antes de empezar; los adultos, su presente consumido por el costo de vida y la carga impositiva; los jubilados, agotados tras una vida laboral, se enfrentan a reformas que recortan o postergan lo que legítimamente les corresponde.En el plano comunicacional, existe un contraste directo entre la narrativa oficial del Ministerio del Interior, que califica las marchas como jornadas transcurridas «sin problemas», y el registro de la ciudadanía. Cientos de registros audiovisuales difundidos por los propios manifestantes muestran cómo la intervención de las fuerzas policiales y de la gendarmería, en los momentos de dispersión, suele actuar como detonante de los enfrentamientos.




Las causas estructurales de la protesta




No sería justo atomizar el análisis y decir que esto es algo de actualidad. Hay hechos que indican que, desde hace una década, existe una presidencia atravesada por una retórica del diálogo, pero con falta de escucha y de canales de participación ciudadana reales.Las movilizaciones actuales no son un hecho aislado, sino la acumulación de un largo ciclo de conflictividad durante los mandatos de Macron. En esa cronología podemos enumerar la revuelta de los Gilets Jaunes (Chalecos Amarillos) en 2018-2019; las protestas masivas de 2023 contra la reforma de las pensiones, impuesta mediante el artículo 49.3 de la Constitución, que permite adoptar un texto sin votación parlamentaria; y, claro, la actualidad, con el descontento por el encarecimiento de la vida y el malestar en el sistema educativo y universitario, donde se denuncian el deterioro de la infraestructura escolar, la falta de reemplazo de docentes y la necesidad de mejores condiciones de trabajo y estudio.Es lógico mencionar también el factor económico, entre causas propias del gobierno y ajenas a él: la subida del precio de los combustibles, impulsada por la inestabilidad geopolítica en Oriente Medio, ha reducido severamente el poder adquisitivo.




El frente de estudiantes secundarios y la respuesta del Ejecutivo




A finales de octubre, tras una consulta que reunió más de 100.000 contribuciones de casi 3.000 liceos, el gobierno, con el primer ministro Sébastien Lecornu a la cabeza, presentó un paquete de medidas: un tope de 28 alumnos por clase (el primer año del liceo), 500 puestos docentes adicionales, 1.000 millones de euros para renovar las universidades, becas indexadas a la inflación desde 2027 y el reemplazo de 

Parcoursup

, la plataforma de acceso a la educación superior, en 2028. A eso se suma la creación de 15.000 nuevas plazas en educación superior hasta 2028, que el sindicato Unión Étudiante contrapone a las 10.000 que, según sus cifras, se suprimieron el año anterior.La posición estudiantil fue rechazar las medidas por considerarlas paliativos insuficientes que no abordan problemas estructurales como la crisis habitacional juvenil, la saturación del sistema universitario y la precariedad laboral. Los estudiantes reclaman, de hecho, 250.000 plazas.El malestar es transversal a varias generaciones, y la confluencia social entre estudiantes y trabajadores está inclinando la opinión pública respecto de la agenda gubernamental y las urgencias económicas de la población. Algunos analistas sostienen que lo que ha hecho Macron es volver inentendible la política, y lo respaldan con hechos de su mandato. Recordemos las elecciones de 2024: el Nuevo Frente Popular fue la fuerza con más diputados (182 de 577), aunque sin mayoría absoluta, y el primer ministro designado por Macron no provino de esa coalición.La huelga de hoy, convocada por un amplio frente intersindical al que se unen sindicatos del sector privado, aúna las fuerzas de los estudiantes secundarios y universitarios y de los trabajadores, del transporte a los puertos: una clara muestra de que la indignación social se organiza.En la Francia actual, como un espejo social contemporáneo, se desarrolla una suerte de «nueva novela francesa», donde ya no es la mesa, el espacio interior de la casa, el lugar para las reuniones y los debates, sino la calle, las explanadas de los edificios educativos. Falta que se organicen más las discusiones de los asalariados en una nueva agenda, y que se comience a construir un poder popular.

da

imporre divieti e prescrizioni sui percorsi dei cortei

content:
Il 31 ottobre scorso anche la Germania ha visto una mobilitazione diffusa in oltre trenta città, da Berlino a Francoforte, partecipata da giovani e giovanissimi, contro la guerra e il carovita. 




da 

Radio Blackout




L’onda delle proteste in Francia si è estesa anche alla vicina Germania, Paese rappresentativo di una profonda crisi sociale e produttiva oltre ad essere capofila di un’Unione Europea votata alla riconversione bellica e al riarmo. 




Un’emersione spontanea, a tratti al di fuori delle dimensioni classiche della politica dei movimenti, e che assume caratteristiche simili a quel che si sta esprimendo in Europa pur mantenendo una continuità con le attivazioni recenti in Germania, come quella contro la leva obbligatoria e, per altri versi, la vittoria elettorale della Linke a Berlino.
