title: Midterm USA: come sta la seggiola di Trump?
content:
A due anni dall’inizio del secondo mandato di Trump il tempo delle elezioni del Midterm è stato raggiunto in modo da rinnovare il Congresso intero e un terzo del Senato, come indicato dalla Costituzione statunitense. Trump è stato sconfitto in entrambi i casi, con i Dem vincitori in 22 Stati, di cui 5 precedentemente in mano repubblicana, e che ora contano 228 seggi alla Camera e 54 al Senato (dati parziali allo stato della scrittura dell’articolo).




Due anni passati anche troppo velocemente: intensificazione delle operazioni dell’ICE (con i conseguenti sommovimenti come a 

Minneapolis

), stati di emergenza di carattere politico emanati in diversi Stati, guerra (persa) all’Iran, ruolo di principale sponsor del genocidio in Palestina, richiesta agli Stati Nato di aumentare la spesa militare senza sborsare un centesimo, guerra commerciale alla Cina (e non solo), aumento vertiginoso del debito, ma anche corruzione e aumento dei profitti per la famiglia di Trump, lo scandalo di Epstein… In poche parole, una fattuale caduta del soft power americano.




STRATEGIE 




Entrambi i partiti hanno messo in atto delle strategie per giocarsi la riconferma o il ribaltamento dei rapporti governativi tra Camere (in particolare il Senato) e la Casa Bianca. Il rischio di un ribaltamento in favore dei Dem era nell’aria e in questo senso la priorità da parte del GOP era quella di concentrarsi sul mantenere il controllo sul Senato, in particolare sul difendere i seggi contesi e cruciali in Stati come Texas, Ohio, Kansas, Maine e Alaska per garantire l’approvazione delle nomine giudiziarie e dei funzionari federali anche in caso di governo diviso. Ma non è andata come sperato, infatti alcuni di questi Stati hanno visto una vittoria Dem inaspettata come nel caso del Kansas che non eleggeva un democratico dal 1932.  D’altro canto la strategia del Partito Democratico ha puntato ad affermarsi come l’unico contrappeso istituzionale e di controllo nei confronti del secondo mandato di Trump. Il tema centrale ruota intorno all’economia domestica: i Democratici imputano direttamente alla Casa Bianca l’aumento del costo della vita, del carburante e dell’inflazione, dipingendo i dazi protezionistici come “tasse sui consumatori” e denunciando i tagli ai servizi sanitari (medicina di base e sussidi ACA). Sul piano internazionale, attaccano i rischi di escalation bellica nei conflitti esteri ed evidenziano presunti conflitti di interesse dell’amministrazione, promettendo di usare la maggioranza al Congresso per avviare commissioni di inchiesta e vigilanza.




L’ultimo elemento da considerare è un andamento particolare degli ultimi anni relativo ai Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) che si sono trasformati da movimento di nicchia a forza capace di influenzare gli equilibri della sinistra americana. Sfruttando il malcontento della cosiddetta Gen Z e Millennials su disuguaglianze e costo della vita, i DSA hanno canalizzato l’attivismo giovanile portando istanze radicali nelle istituzioni. I risultati di ciò si sono visti: nel macro l’elezione a sindaco di Mamdani a New York, seguito da oltre 250 membri dei DSA in diverse altre posizioni (minori) in più di 40 Stati.




Fino ad ora i DSA sono stati forti principalmente nei grandi centri urbani abitati, tuttavia dalla campagna elettorale emerge un altro fenomeno: la retorica alternativa all’establishment, impostata sulle condizioni di vita e di riproduzione delle persone, sta permettendo le prime penetrazioni nelle zone 

rurals

 più prossime alle città; forse ancora in minoranza, ma tuttavia rimane un fenomeno interessante. 




La loro strategia per le 

Midterms

 si è basata sul condizionamento interno al Partito Democratico: sfidando i candidati moderati alle primarie nei collegi urbani, l’organizzazione impone temi chiave come sanità pubblica, diritto alla casa e tutela dei lavoratori. Questo spinge l’agenda dem verso sinistra, garantendo altresì un’alta affluenza di elettori militanti. Questo soggetto introduce un discorso che significa la dialettica alto-basso non più nei termini di establishment-popolo, bensì con fattori nuovi più prossimi ad una dialettica di classe. Si tratta di una formazione con istanze social democratiche e improntate alla redistribuzione della ricchezza con particolare attenzione al tema delle “minoranze” e di soggettività che intendono essere protagonisti di un nuovo scenario politico statunitense a venire.




Per concludere l’analisi sugli attori in campo, una posta in palio porta i nomi e i cognomi dei tecno-capitalisti, ovvero i baroni della ristrutturazione capitalistica in atto. Le Big Tech finanziano a rubinetti aperti le candidature repubblicane. Tra i maggiori donatori si è distinto il fondatore di Tesla, che ha investito 446 milioni di dollari del suo patrimonio personale. Anche la campagna dei democratici ha visto somme esorbitanti per sponsorizzare i candidati, il totale di questi investimenti ha raggiunto il record mai visto, arrivando a sfiorare i 12 miliardi di dollari in totale per la spesa elettorale. Il legame tra Repubblicani e grandi capitali delle Big Tech si è rivelata un’arma a doppio taglio per Trump, infatti da un lato la crescente opposizione ai data center e, dall’altro, l’onda lunga dello scandalo degli Epstein Files hanno avuto un ruolo di primo piano nell’erosione del consenso. Un esempio è il caso di Talarico che in Texas ha vinto, riuscendo a espugnare una roccaforte dei repubblicani con una campagna basata sul confronto aperto e diretto con la schizofrenia capitalistica di Musk. Se si guarda ai finanziatori delle rispettive campagne elettorali per il midterm, Musk risulta fra i maggiori donatori insieme ad altri miliardari americani per il fronte repubblicano, mentre continuano ad essere i maggiori finanziatori per il fronte dem Soros e Bloomberg. A questo si aggiunge il fenomeno delle micro donazioni che hanno sostenuto i candidati più radicali premiati appunto per le loro posizioni. Questo non significa che la sfera di influenza della Silicon Valley sia da sminuire d’ora in avanti, anzi, il ruolo dei grandi capitali legati alle Big Tech continua ad essere un elemento di primo piano nel direzionare la Grand Strategy americana.




Va detto che le contraddizioni interne al partito democratico non si risolvono con questa tornata elettorale, ma anzi si intensificano. Fra queste la presenza dentro il partito in maniera maggioritaria, di tutta una fetta di 

deep state

 che ha come orizzonte comune quello della guerra e del dominio imperialista, che ha disegnato e preparato le guerre che oggi imperversano lo scenario globale, dall’Ucraina all’Iran passando per la Palestina e i sanguinosissimi e più che mai ignorati conflitti africani. Oggi, come sostiene Jeffrey Sachs, economista e professore alla Columbia University, in una sua recente intervista, il punto è che il popolo americano abbia più che altro voluto punire Trump e i repubblicani, piuttosto che sostenere il disegno Dem in senso generale, ad eccezion fatta per le politiche portate dai candidati DSA e da altri come Talarico che hanno spinto su una retorica fortemente contrappositiva e improntata alla richiesta di welfare e protezione sociale. Probabilmente, una futura vittoria alle prossime elezioni presidenziali da parte dei democratici, passerà da un imbuto: o queste rivendicazioni verranno assimilate da una parte dell’establishment dem e si potranno rappresentare in maniera credibile come il “Partito della pace” oppure si tratterà dell’ennesimo caso in cui tutto cambia per non cambiare niente. 




COMPOSIZIONE DEL VOTO







La geografia del voto e gli itinerari degli eletti sono elementi interessanti da guardare. Ancora una volta assistiamo a una faglia generazionale e demografica. Sembra che a erodere le roccaforti repubblicane sia stata una forte immissione di componenti giovanili che attraversano territori rurali, tradizionalmente più schierati a destra. La campagna repubblicana si è focalizzata sui temi della sicurezza nazionale, in particolare per quel che riguarda il confine Sud con il Messico e l’espulsione di massa dei migranti con gli interventi dell’ICE, e della difesa della politica economica protezionistica, sempre in chiave di re-industrializzazione, ma non ha sortito effetti positivi su questa componente, anzi. Il trend più esplicitamente invertito è quello che riguarda i latinos che, se nel 2024 erano stati determinanti per la vittoria di Trump, oggi proprio a fronte delle politiche apertamente persecutorie e razziste hanno fatto pesare l’ago della bilancia da un’altra parte. Un altro elemento che ha probabilmente giocato in questo è la modifica di Roe contro Wade che ha conferito la competenza sul diritto all’aborto ai singoli Stati Federali, cancellando quindi il diritto costituzionale. Questo è visibile anche dai risultati dei referendum costituzionali abbinati alle elezioni. Sui giornali si legge di diversi primati dal punto di vista dei candidati, e soprattutto delle candidate, elette. La prima donna ispanica, la prima donna palestinese, la prima donna indigena, la prima afroamericana. Si potrebbero trovare mille cause e variabili che hanno portato a questi risultati ma ciò che vorremmo focalizzare è una questione, ossia quella materiale. Se le analisi mainstream nostrane calcano la mano sul fatto che a premiare questi profili sia stata la “politica delle identità” tradizionale negli Usa, lo fanno per non dare risalto alla capacità di queste attiviste di intrecciare le direttrici di genere e di razza con la questione di classe. Aver saputo ricollegare i fili dell’impalcatura storica in cui questi architravi dello sfruttamento spingono per la divisione dei subalterni ai bisogni materiali insoddisfatti che le persone sperimentano in maniera trasversale a causa della guerra e della crisi sociale, significa assumere un ruolo politico che poi viene riconosciuto. Questo evidenzia l’enorme potenziale che possono sprigionare movimenti femministi e antirazzisti se riescono ad oltrepassare gli steccati imposti dall’alto. 




GUERRA E CAROVITA 







E’ evidente per tutti, anche per lo stesso Trump, che ad aver avuto un ruolo di primo piano nell’andamento di queste elezioni sia stata la guerra all’Iran, o meglio, gli effetti di questa. Su Fox News il presidente ha dichiarato “La gente è d’accordo con quello che sto facendo sull’Iran, ma probabilmente non era disposta ad accettare la conseguenza a breve termine di pagare di più per la benzina. Lo capisco, ma non lo condivido”, forse centrando il cuore della questione. La crisi economica e le condizioni materiali erodono il bacino di consenso che, prima di questa tornata, era stato convinto dall’ideologia MAGA. La crisi in cui versano gli USA sul piano interno, inasprita dal proliferare di progetti devastanti per il territorio e per chi lo abita (soprattutto localizzati in quei territori in cui c’è spazio per installare enormi gigafactory di dati in barba agli insediamenti dei residenti nelle zone rurali, ci sono addirittura dei casi in cui Musk ha tentato di comprare direttamente le case di chi protesta contro i suoi data center) e gli aumenti dei prezzi della benzina (gli abitanti degli USA utilizzano più del doppio rispetto agli europei le automobili) iniziano a minare le idee-forza mobilitate da Trump e, in generale, dalla leadership americana che ne hanno garantito la vittoria. Un processo che è iniziato ben prima di questo giro di metà mandato e che si traduce in una crisi dei valori dell’egemonia americana alla base della necessità di una guerra permanente ma al contempo occasione per approfondirne le contraddizioni. Possiamo forse dire che il peggioramento delle condizioni materiali porterà a un indebolimento dell’american dream anche dall’interno? 




E poi Gaza. L’enormità della portata umana, storica, etica, morale, filosofica che il genocidio ha giocato sul realismo capitalista e l’Occidente come espressione della “modernità” non poteva che essere un elemento fondamentale in questa tornata elettorale. Il sostegno esplicito delle lobby israeliane ha punito chiunque se ne fosse avvalso portandole addirittura a dichiarare di voler nascondere in futuro chi vorranno finanziare per tutelare gli interessi sionisti. 




Sono interessanti anche le dichiarazioni di Teheran che legge il voto USA come un no alla guerra in Iran e che quindi sostiene il popolo americano. «I crimini contro l’umanità a Gaza, l’adesione cieca agli interessi dell’illegittimo regime israeliano e la guerra infinita contro l’Iran hanno inflitto al partito repubblicano la più grave sconfitta nella storia delle elezioni Usa» E’ quanto ha scritto su X Mehdi Tabatabaei, vice capo del dipartimento per le comunicazioni dell’Ufficio della presidenza iraniana. Dall’altro lato occorre fare una distinzione tra i fronti: se l’Iran ha buon gioco a sottolineare che il voto USA è un voto contro la guerra scatenata da Trump e Netanyahu sul suo territorio, diverso è lo sguardo della Russia di Putin. Il viceministro degli Esteri russo, Serghei Ryabkov, all’agenzia Ria Novosti, ha dichiarato: “Aspettiamo i risultati definitivi. L’approccio di base del Partito Democratico nei confronti della Russia è estremamente negativo. Non c’è nulla di nuovo in questo”. Che ci sembra faccia emergere con una certa lucidità l’altro tema profondo da sollevare. I democratici sono noti per essere cavalieri dell’esportazione della democrazia nel mondo e guerrafondai nella storia dell’America che conosciamo. L’ordine liberale prevede una solida, duratura, infrangibile egemonia a guida statunitense e trova eco nei suoi omologhi alle nostre latitudini ed è fuor di dubbio che questo si debba tradurre con la necessità della guerra per garantirla e mantenerla. La differenza tra Grand Strategy repubblicana e democratica risiede forse nella narrazione con cui si può condire la stessa intenzione: guerra aperta ma subdolamente legittimata dall’esigenza dei popoli del resto del mondo di venire salvati, democratizzati, liberati dagli Stati Uniti e su questo il Medio Oriente ne sa qualcosa. 




Questo piano non si gioca su un livello ideologico ma strettamente materiale, ora più che mai forse. Prima di tutto l’insensatezza della guerra che deve pur essere combattuta da qualcuno in carne ed ossa. Dai territori della base MAGA che oggi hanno visto un’inversione di tendenza proviene il materiale umano che deve essere impiegato nell’esercito, un elemento che se si consolida creerà una rigidità importante alle proiezioni esterne della politica americana sia essa repubblicana o democratica. E poi, quali dovrebbero essere i margini per attuare un programma realmente socialista o redistributivo come sembrano evocare alcuni di questi punti? In uno stato di guerra permanente dove si prendono le risorse materiali per attuare programmi di questo tipo senza mettere in discussione le necessità della fabbrica della guerra? Inoltre, in uno scenario in cui molti analisti stanno delineando un orizzonte in cui la bolla finanziaria causata dall’intelligenza artificiale potrà scoppiare causando effetti ben peggiori della crisi dei mutui Subprime, quali vie d’uscita per uno Stato basato sul debito? Il debito americano ha superato i 40 mila miliardi di dollari e il 70% è detenuto da soggetti interni come fondi pensione, banche e assicurazioni. Come scrive Fabio Mini in un 

articolo di Sinistrainrete

, “il debito è come la guerra: è una macchina che continua a marciare e consumare finché c’è fiducia.” Oggi vediamo che la fiducia nei confronti della guerra voluta dagli USA di Trump sta venendo meno, anche all’interno dei suoi confini. Ciò interroga profondamente il modo di produzione capitalistico indipendentemente dall’alternarsi nella dimensione istituzionale di tattiche politiche formalmente diverse ma tutte interne all’ordine imperialista. 




BISOGNI DI CLASSE E NUOVA CREDIBILITA’ DELL’ARENA ISTITUZIONALE? 







Quindi siamo all’alba dell’implosione del mondo MAGA? Difficile dirlo ora, sicuramente ci sono tutti i presupposti e sono molte le fratture che l’esperienza di governo ha esacerbato fino a portare all’allontanamento di molti dei suoi fondatori. 




Anche se la domanda è importante e merita analisi molto meno frettolose delle consolatorie conclusioni liberal, forse la questione più profonda è un’altra. Le condizioni materiali della classe quindi anche la sua lotta, nelle forme più variegate e spurie, si affermano nuovamente e definitivamente come motori e variabili imprescindibili della politica americana e di riflesso occidentale? La questione non è tanto quanto il MAGA stia implodendo ma quanto i democratici, o meglio alcuni loro pezzi, abbiano appreso la lezione che quel movimento si è portata appresso spaccando e sconvolgendo la concezione che tutti avevano di cosa fosse la politica. Dal 2016 il MAGA ha in qualche modo reso chiaro a tutti che la politica è “cattiva”, è principalmente scontro a partire da posizioni inconciliabili se non attraverso la mediazione violenta dello “Stato”. Nelle sue contraddizioni enormi questo fenomeno sociale variegato, ha risettato la politica americana su di un altro livello che ora viene praticato proficuamente da un grosso pezzo della politica democratica. La scommessa di Trump di spostare il livello dello scontro in una guerra civile orizzontale fra i vari settori di classe si è per ora tradotta in un fallimento, il proiettare la sua soluzione sull’imposizione militare al resto dell’impero ne ha approfondito la caduta. 




A spostare l’asse però sono stati anche i movimenti sociali di opposizione alle politiche adottate dai MAGA una volta al governo, rimettendo al centro la questione della sanità, della difesa dei lavoratori soprattutto dalle politiche di disciplinamento razziste praticate dall’ICE contro i migranti e le donne. Anche se la narrazione alle nostre latitudini vorrebbe raccontarci che ora il pallino della partita starebbe tornando nella dimensione elettorale e istituzionale, che la democrazia è salva, che 

funziona

; è invece quanto mai vero che il baricentro capace di direzionare i prossimi avvenimenti rimanga in basso e quindi alla portata dei movimenti. Va letto come elemento di questo quadro anche un nuovo rapporto alla politica che si è espresso nella campagna dei nuovi leaders democratici, un processo da leggere quasi come una sorta di movimento dal basso che poggia effettivamente su un’articolazione e una base sociale che si è attivata, si è organizzata e ha contribuito fisicamente e virtualmente ad essa. In parte il successo è dato dalle considerazioni fatte in precedenza e al tipo di profilo che è stato scelto per rappresentare istanze presenti nella società americana, dall’altro è dato dal rapporto che si è andato a costruire tra virtuale e cittadini singoli e organizzazioni di base inserite nel tessuto sociale. Un dato che porta in nuce un’inversione di tendenza in quanto fino ad ora a dimostrare questa capacità di radicamento e di appoggio a reti sociali esistenti anche al di fuori delle metropoli è stato appannaggio dei conservatori. Non si tratta di un movimento in senso stretto, incompatibile o non integrabile alla dinamica istituzionale, ma potrebbe rivelarsi una spia di una ripoliticizzazione di massa non scontata. 




Ciò che ci deve interessare oggi non è tanto la tenuta della democrazia americana o dell’equilibrio istituzionale. Ciò che ci deve interessare è la riorganizzazione del capitale e, in quanto rapporto sociale, delle classi in lotta. Quali organizzazioni dal basso si stanno dando in risposta a carovita e guerra, quali spazi si aprono e come si traduce in forma di scontro dal basso verso l’alto la crisi dell’impero anche al suo interno? Come sempre gli scenari che possono aprirsi alle nostre latitudini sono influenzati da ciò che accade negli USA, proprio perché l’Europa rimane una periferia dell’impero a loro guida. Se vediamo una ripresa di senso del far politica in maniera attiva e che metta al centro le condizioni di vita e di riproduzione di essa, non è altro che una boccata d’aria e una possibilità in più per continuare ad approfondire le fratture di questa fase storica.

author: Peter C. Gøtzsche, MD
title: Winning Norwegian Lawsuits about Forced Drugging with Antipsychotics
content:
I

t is very difficult to win lawsuits about psychiatric malpractice, particularly about forced drugging with antipsychotics.

1

 One reason is, as lawyer Jim Gottstein, has observed in Alaska,

2

 and which I have also seen on several occasions, that psychiatrists routinely misrepresent the evidence in court: About how ill their patients are; what wonders they can achieve with antipsychotics; and saying that the patients have tolerated them well, which the patients disagree with.

3




When I studied 30 consecutive cases from Denmark

3

 and 30 consecutive cases from Alaska,

4

 where the patients had appealed forced treatment orders, I found that the legal procedures were a sham where the patients were defenceless, and that the law had been violated in every single case.




Another reason why lawsuits are difficult to win is that judges have so much respect for authority that they didn’t care the least when I, other expert witnesses, and lawyers for the plaintiffs like Gottstein demonstrated in court that professors of psychiatry and other experts were lying.

1,2,5




A third reason why it is so difficult to obtain justice is that Ombudsman and Supreme Court decisions are consistently being ignored.

1

 In Norway, the Ombudsman concluded in 2018 that forced treatment with an antipsychotic in a concrete case had violated the law.

6

 The law stipulates that forced drugging can be used when, with “high probability, it can lead to recovery or significant improvement in the patient’s condition, or if the patient avoids a significant worsening of the disease.” Referring to science, the Ombudsman noted that the probability of achieving the intended improvement is very low.




Despite the Ombudsman’s ruling, the unethical practice just continued. It is therefore very significant, also in an international context, that four court cases in Norway—three of them related to antipsychotics—were recently won.




In 2024, I was an expert witness in a lawsuit against the Norwegian State at the Oslo District Court.

5

 It was lost because of an incompetent judge, but the Court of Appeal, which corresponds to the Superior Court in other countries, ruled in 2026 that the human rights were violated when Inger-Mari Eidsvik was subjected to forced treatment with antipsychotics and in a case of solitary confinement.




It had been very difficult to get there. Inger-Mari’s lawyers had been fighting 

pro bono

 for over three years for the right to sue the state for multiple violations of the European Convention on Human Rights, the UN conventions, and the Norwegian Constitution. After having lost in two inferior courts, they won at the Supreme Court and were allowed to go ahead with the first case ever to challenge coercive treatment in psychiatry.




I describe here three other Norwegian cases. I met the three women involved at the Mad in Norway film festival in September 2026 where my filmmaker and I showed our documentary, “The Illusion of Psychiatry.”

7

 My account is based on court documents and personal information.







Helen Wesnes




Helen’s story is so gruesome that it is hard to believe that this could happen in a civilised country. She was sexually assaulted in her late teens and struggled with insomnia and nightmares. In the end, she agreed to a two-week stay at a psychiatric hospital, which a psychologist had suggested.




Two weeks turned into nine years. Helen spent nine years continuously in Reinsvoll Hospital from 2000 when she was only 20 years old. NINE YEARS!




Then, from 2009 to 2015, she stayed at an assisted living residence where she was subjected to forced medication. In total, she was under forced treatment for 15 years.




From day one, she was put on an antidepressant, and shortly thereafter she also received antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, an antiepileptic, a stimulant, and lithium. She was misdiagnosed with hebephrenic schizophrenia, but lithium doesn’t work for schizophrenia.

8,9

 It was also medical malpractice to treat Helen with Leponex (clozapine) and Abilify (aripiprazole) simultaneously. National

10

 and international guidelines recommend against using two antipsychotics at the same time and there are very good reasons for this. The benefit is not increased by increasing the dose

11

 but the risk of death from these highly toxic drugs is of course dose-related.

12




Leponex is a particularly toxic drug, which is not more effective than other antipsychotics,

8

 and, according to an expert testifying in court, it should never have been used. It is not a first-line drug but was initiated without any consultation with other clinicians.




Moreover, antipsychotics have no effect on traumas, and they caused extensive harms. Helen suffered from drooling, incontinence, substantial weight gain, mental dullness, cognitive decline, low blood pressure, and syncope.




Initially, she received psychotherapy, which proved beneficial. But when her therapist was transferred to another department, it was discontinued and her condition deteriorated markedly. The expert considered that if Helen had received psychotherapy instead of antipsychotics, she would likely have been well after a year instead of her spending 15 years under unbearable conditions.




In 2001, Helen informed her psychiatrists that she had been sexually assaulted and that this had caused her mental health challenges. Nevertheless, no assessment or treatment for trauma was initiated and she was deprived of her freedom for 15 years.




Helen’s fight for justice started in 2016 and it isn’t over yet. At first, the Norwegian System of Patient Injury Compensation (NPE) and the Patient Injury Board concluded that she was not entitled to compensation because she had not sustained an injury resulting from a failure, inadequate treatment, or negligent treatment.




In 2022, Helen filed a writ of summons against the State asking for compensation because of her suffering resulting from violation of fundamental human rights. Shortly before the case was due to go to trial, the proceedings were halted because Helen and her lawyer found out that the NPE had failed to obtain the nursing records from Reinsvoll Hospital. As a result, NPE reopened the case, and, without going to court, Helen was awarded NOK 7,790,000 in 2024 for loss of earnings and permanent injury from the treatment, as well as NOK 33,207 to cover legal costs.




Helen’s lawyer took legal action against NPE because they disagreed with the NPE’s assessment of the extent of her loss of earnings, as well as the severity of the physical and psychological harm she suffered because of the treatment. That part of the case is scheduled to be heard by the District Court in February 2027.




In 2026, the District Court awarded Helen NOK 4,500,000 as compensation due to violation of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR)

13

 articles 3, 5 and 8, plus NOK 1,179,375 in legal costs. The part of the case against the Norwegian State concerning a claim for compensation for lost income is still being considered by the District Court. Conversely, the State appealed the verdict in September 2026 to the Superior Court claiming that the District Court failed in assessing the evidence and in the way it used the law.




I don’t think the State will prevail, as the case is very clear. The District Court’s verdict is unusually harsh. The assessment and diagnosis of Helen did not live up to medical standards—it was not even possible to trace how the first diagnosis, schizoaffective disorder, was reached. Senior Consultant Jan Wollenberg apparently did not consult with other clinicians who knew Helen better than he did to discuss his diagnosis.




The diagnosis of hebephrenic schizophrenia was also wrong, and the Court ruled it was unjustified to use forced treatment because Helen did not suffer from a serious psychiatric disorder. However, in just three years, she was mechanically restrained 67 times with belts for a total of 153 hours.




Helen was subjected to medical treatment in violation of Article 3 of the ECHR (Prohibition of torture) and to unlawful deprivation of liberty, in violation of Article 5 (Right to liberty and security).




The way Helen was treated was extremely inhumane and unprofessional. When the nurses suspected that she was hiding tablets or spat them out, it was decided that she would be observed for 30 minutes after receiving her medication, to ensure she took it. The staff even checked her oral cavity to confirm that it had been swallowed.




Helen suffered from tremors caused by the antipsychotics and the staff observed that when she tried to take photographs, it took a long time to get the camera into focus because her hands shook so severely. The verdict noted that she, incidentally, is an exceptionally good photographer.




Tests of Helen’s serum levels revealed very high concentrations of medication. Nevertheless, no adjustments were made to the dosage even though it was clear that she was a slow metaboliser. This was serious medical malpractice. Evaluations and dose adjustments were carried out to a very limited extent despite the fact that she experienced serious harms and showed very few signs of improvement. The court found that this constituted degrading treatment and was a violation of Article 3 (Prohibition of torture).




Helen was denied contact with the outside world to such an extent that it constituted a violation of Article 3, or alternatively Article 8 (Right to respect for private and family life). No one at the ward was allowed to talk to her about difficult topics, which is terribly inhumane and reduces the chance of recovery because having relationships are very important for recovery.

8

 Her primary contact person instructed her to put all painful thoughts and feelings into an imaginary box.




Helen had nothing to occupy her time and was only permitted to use photography equipment and a PC for short periods. Restrictions were also placed on her ability to keep a diary or write other texts, which made it difficult for her to engage in correspondence. She was allowed to write only for short periods during the day, and she could only receive visits from her family for 30 minutes, with staff present, which resulted in their conversations being largely superficial.




Allegedly, the rationale for the restrictions was that she became agitated by too much stimulation. I am convinced that the little contact she had with other people reminded her of what life was about before she ended up in a psychiatric ward and that it was therefore a natural reaction that she became “agitated” afterwards. Most people would have reacted the same way.




Helen was not permitted to have a mobile phone and was allowed to use a computer and photography equipment for only one hour (30 minutes per shift). On one Christmas Eve, she could visit her parents’ home for an hour and a half, accompanied by staff. When her grandmother died, she was permitted to attend the church service for the funeral but was not allowed to join the family gathering that followed. Helen’s mother was instructed to avoid physical contact with her daughter and was not permitted to massage her.




In 2005, Helen was forbidden to use photography and recording equipment within the ward or on the hospital grounds, which was particularly demeaning because photography was a passion for her and she was always careful regarding what she chose to photograph.




The restrictions constituted an interference with Helen’s right to family life, in violation of Article 8, and considered as a whole, including her inability to write freely, the restrictions also constituted degrading treatment under Article 3, which is about torture.




During the court case, Helen declined to grant a general waiver of the duty of confidentiality for staff at Reinsvoll. The State argued that since she had failed to fulfil her duty to provide information, any uncertainty regarding the evidence must be resolved to her detriment.




However, Helen had said that the State could conduct interviews with current or former employees at Reinsvoll, if she herself was present, which the State deemed unacceptable.




The reason why Helen declined to grant a general waiver is that she distrusted the authorities, which she had all the reason in the world to do given her experiences.




On two occasions, Helen was subjected to violence by fellow patients. The failure to prevent the violence and the insufficient follow-up care she received after the incidents constituted a violation of Article 3, or, alternatively, Article 8. On one occasion, a fellow patient struck her repeatedly—completely unprovoked—and grabbed her by the throat. This was in the ward’s common areas, at a time when no staff were present. Helen feared for her life and found the incident deeply traumatic. A psychiatrist described the event as extremely serious, noting that the outcome could have been dire had no one intervened.




There were plans to reduce Helen’s Leponex dosage but due to increasing agitation triggered by another attack by a patient during hospital activities it was decided to halt the tapering process. Thus, Helen was punished twice, and the follow-up care she received following these two incidents—or rather the lack thereof—was poorly documented. She was not permitted to speak with anyone about the attacks.




Helen was drugged till 2014. She fought for a long time to have the Leponex dosage reduced because she had become severely ill from its harms. However, she was only allowed very minor dose reductions. In the end, she withdrew from Leponex herself, very quickly, in a few steps, and came off the medication within a few months. During the tapering, she developed severe insomnia and needed to go to Reinsvoll Hospital for help. It was only then that the medical staff realised she had been misdiagnosed and subjected to inappropriate treatment.




The hospital discontinued the remaining medications more or less cold turkey, over a period of only 10-14 days, after which she was sent home. This was serious medical malpractice. Withdrawal symptoms include akathisia, which increases the risk of suicide markedly.

8

 Helen became extremely ill and was hospitalised with severe withdrawal symptoms that lasted several months.




Hilde Marie Rekstad 




Marie suffered from depression and anxiety and got the diagnosis atypical bipolar disorder. Much later, she questioned the diagnosis because she didn’t feel bipolar and it was made without adequate assessment.




Her psychiatrists never asked her how she was doing or why she was depressed. They interpreted it as a biological disorder because her paternal grandfather had been diagnosed sometime in the 1940s. Marie did not dare tell them that her marriage was unhappy because she was afraid of losing her children. The erroneous biomedical interpretation had major consequences both for her and her children.




Marie received electroshocks and large amounts of antidepressants, antipsychotics, lithium, antiepileptics and benzodiazepines and became intoxicated. When she complained about this, her psychiatrists refused to examine her and said she did not have insight into her disease. One of the kidneys and the parathyroid glands were affected but she was sent home from the hospital in very bad shape.




She saved her life by fleeing abroad and by not telling anyone that she was a psychiatric patient, which had the result that she was properly examined.




She received large doses of lithium for 14 years and developed kidney damage, which is a well-known harm and a reason why serum concentrations of lithium should be measured regularly. However, her general practitioner had forgotten about her and therefore hadn’t done this. Marie complained to the Norwegian System of Patient Injury Compensation (NPE).




They rejected her complaint. Unnamed sources have revealed that this authority has been instructed to reject virtually all claims about economic compensation for medical malpractice. This could very well be true because, if the authority took the complaints seriously and awarded compensation when it was justified, the number of complaints and awards would explode because malpractice is very common in psychiatry.

2,8




The arguments from the authority were unconvincing and Marie’s lawyer appealed the verdict, as he found errors both in the way the law had been used and in the assessment of the evidence. In 2016, the verdict was rejected by the County Governor (Fylkesmannen) who concluded that the general practitioner had violated the law and had not lived up to the expected professional standard.




Marie came on disability pension and lost 14 years to psychiatry. But after she decided to come off the drugs, she got her life back and started working again. She wrote a moving book about her experiences.

14




In 2021, Marie received NOK 3,287,454 for loss of income, NOK 15,000 for injuries, and NOK 31,969 for legal costs from the NPE.




Helena Münster




In May 2026, the District Court ruled that the requirements for continued compulsory mental health care were not met for Helena’s 29-year-old son.




Her son was diagnosed with ADHD in 2008 but both he and his mother believe that he has Asperger’s syndrome, currently called autism spectrum disorder. In 2021, he underwent an assessment at Akershus University Hospital, which concluded that he, with a “high probability” had autism spectrum disorder. However, in March 2026, the same hospital concluded that he did not meet the criteria for this diagnosis. They gave him the diagnosis hebephrenic schizophrenia and started treatment with Leponex.




Because his psychotic symptoms were substance-induced, there was uncertainty regarding the diagnosis, but the Court found it likely that he had autism spectrum disorder. The Court noted that symptoms and characteristics specific to schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders can overlap and that individuals with autism spectrum disorders have an increased risk of developing psychotic symptoms.




The Court also noted that he was not medication-free during the observation period and he used psychoactive substances, amphetamines and cocaine, which supported the Court’s view about uncertainty regarding the diagnosis.




Indeed. I have argued that it should be made illegal to diagnose people while they are under influence of psychoactive substances because it is impossible to know if what is being observed are just harms of the drugs or some serious mental disorder.




The Court considered it uncertain whether his symptoms were of such nature and extent that they constituted a serious mental disorder within the meaning of the law and could justify forced treatment.




Furthermore, no improvement had been observed due to the compulsory treatment; on the contrary, as his mother and maternal grandmother explained in court, his condition had worsened significantly. He had become listless, slept a great deal, was depressed, and had gained a substantial amount of weight. His family explained that he previously took an interest in exercise, but that he was now devoid of energy, passive, depressed, and apathetic, and that his life lacked any meaningful content. He himself stated that, during his stay at Akershus, he had resorted to substance use in order to manage daily activities, such as getting out of bed and showering.




The Court found that the use of coercion could not continue and that compulsory treatment was clearly not the best solution for him. He found the coercion highly distressing; had lost trust in the system; was physically severely affected by drug harms; and experienced a loss of autonomy, which prevented him from engaging in meaningful activities such as exercise, walking in nature, and having contact with his family.




The Court considered that the dubious diagnosis, hebephrenic schizophrenia, prevented him from receiving the appropriate help—namely, cognitive behavioural therapy. The Court agreed that treatment with Leponex had left him so devoid of energy that he felt compelled to resort to substance use just to manage ordinary daily activities.




The State’s arguments were pathetic. They asserted that he had hebephrenic schizophrenia, even though substance abuse can cause psychosis, and claimed that he had improved on Leponex, according to the clinician in charge, ignoring that clinicians have a huge conflict of interest when asked if a patient has improved on their toxic drugs.




Helena told me that her son’s psychiatrist who was responsible for the compulsory treatment had said that he had observed a positive effect from the antipsychotics, and even though Helena had repeatedly cried out about how destructive the drugs had been, he had continued to maintain his position.




Like this psychiatrist, the State also resorted to wishful thinking, “There must be scope for further improvement,” and postulated that little weight could be given to Helen’s son’s own account because he lacked insight into his illness and also lacked the capacity to consent.




He surely had the capacity to consent. He was well-informed about medications, wanted to be helped, and had a reasonably realistic understanding of his situation.




The Court did not agree that a significant improvement had occurred or that there was evidence to suggest a potential for further improvement. He had been treated for 2-3 months, without any significant improvement having been demonstrated.




His poor level of functioning was reinforced by his demeanour in court. He fell asleep while sitting in the courtroom and had to leave the proceedings to sleep in his car. During his testimony, he appeared emotionally blunted and disengaged.




He had been treated with antipsychotic medication over a long period without any significant positive effect being demonstrated, and several different types of antipsychotics had been tried, each type used for a relatively short duration.




It is bad medicine to switch drugs because there is no evidence that it is beneficial. In psychiatry, switching to another drug from the same class, adding another drug from the same class, or adding a drug from another class, does not result in better outcomes.

15




Conclusions




I think my account speaks for itself. We look back in horror at the mistreatment of psychiatric patients in the asylums in the last century, e.g. with insulin coma therapy, lobotomy, shock therapy with electricity or drugs causing horrible fractures, deep sleep lasting for days or weeks, and electric shocks and emetics against homosexuality.




What few realise is that in 50-100 years from now, people will look back in horror and will not understand why we allowed psychiatrists to kill many of their patients with drugs that provided no meaningful benefit and caused permanent brain damage in many of them.

2,8




Antipsychotics are so toxic that they double mortality.

16

 Psychiatry is the only medical specialty where the doctors can kill their patients with a drug, which the patients begged them not to use, with impunity.




Shouldn’t we leave a better legacy than this?




We must push for additional lawsuits to make psychiatry less harmful than it currently is. I am proud of the four brave Norwegian women who challenged a deeply unjust and inhumane system with tremendous power at its disposal and won.




***

author: Natália Perez
title: Tsunami azul nas midterms: será o fim da era Trump? – com Tatiana Vargas-Maia
content:
A vitória democrata nas eleições de meio de mandato indica tendências de mudança para a disputa presidencial de 2028 e revela uma certa vitalidade democrática nos Estados Unidos. É o que afirma Tatiana Vargas-Maia, convidada do Pauta Pública desta semana. O episódio discute o resultado das midterms, divulgados na última terça-feira, 3 de novembro, e seus possíveis impactos no cenário político norte americano.




Na conversa com Andrea Dip, a cientista política e professora de Economia e Relações Internacionais da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul, Tatiana Vargas-Maia propõe uma reflexão sobre o que muda, de fato, nos dois anos que restam do mandato de Trump. A entrevistada também analisa o que esse recado das urnas pode significar para a extrema direita no resto do mundo e para o Brasil, que acaba de sair de uma eleição em que a relação com os Estados Unidos também esteve em jogo.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: The Philippines’ ‘solar surge’ leaves many Filipinos behind
content:
Workers install solar panels on the roof of a home in the Philippine capital, Manila. Amid the continued energy crisis from the Gulf conflict, customer inquiries and weekly rooftop solar installations have been rising in the country (Image form Anton L Delgado / Associated Press / Alamy)

Amid increasing energy prices, Filipinos are turning to solar – but upfront costs mean it remains out of reach for those who most need savings

Fidds Salvador Badilles, a doctor in Las Piñas, a city just south of the Philippines’ capital Manila, transitioned to solar power and electric vehicles to offset rising costs from the energy crisis. In June, her family installed a 12.6-kilowatt, 20-panel system, as well as a 12-kilowatt solar hybrid inverter and 32-kilowatt-hour batteries.

“We are saving so much already on gas and monthly electric consumption,” Badilles tells Dialogue Earth. Her family now saves PHP 20,000 (USD 315) each month for a system that cost them PHP 700,000 (around USD 11,000), she notes: “Even air conditioning [for the whole day] is not a problem anymore.”

Jovi Solomon, a café owner in Bataan province, installed a 40-kilowatt (KW) solar panel system to offset her business’s electricity costs, setting her back PHP 880,000. She says this allows her to save PHP 10,000 a month on her power bill.

Interest in solar power has surged as Filipinos grapple with skyrocketing electricity rates that have worsened since the Gulf conflict began in late February. However, the trend has also highlighted the stark gap between those who can afford solar options and those who are priced out.

A Reuters report from June 2026 indicated that the Philippines imported USD 407 million worth of solar panels from China between March and May, a year-on-year increase of 145%. It estimates that the median Filipino household now spends around 12% of its monthly income on electricity.

Residential installations – solar panels that are below 100 KW or are registered under the Philippines Net-Metering Program – make up around 245 megawatts (MW) of the country’s 1,846-MW solar capacity, according to 2025 data from the Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities. While the majority of that capacity is from utility-scale installations (projects above 1 MW), residential installations have outpaced commercial installations (projects above 100 KW).

A survey of 20 solar companies in April by clean energy non-profit New Energy Nexus said that customer inquiries were up by an average of 582%. Weekly rooftop installations rose 170% on average from before the energy crisis began, it noted.

Alnie Demoral, Asia energy analyst at the think-tank Ember, says that with the Philippines’ largest electricity provider Meralco’s rates at around PHP 14.5 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) in June, “a household rooftop system now pays for itself in about three years”. The utility’s rates have since risen to nearly PHP 15.1 per kWh, a 16% increase from January.

“Our earlier estimate of roughly 1,300 MW of rooftop solar by April is likely conservative today,” she says.

While updated official figures have yet to be released, “every indicator we’ve seen since May points to Filipinos adopting rooftop solar faster than ever”, Demoral adds.

A single solar panel unit capable of powering direct current devices like lights and mobile devices could cost PHP 4,000-6,000 (USD 63-94) each, according to John Mark Napao, an electrical engineer and founder of Solar Hope, a non-profit that provides off-grid electrification to rural and Indigenous communities through solar power.

That amount is a considerable fraction of the national average minimum wage of PHP 510 a day or PHP 11,100 a month as of April, as aggregated by the Ibon Foundation, a think-tank. A solar power system with an inverter – needed to run appliances such as air conditioners and refrigerators – would cost much more. For example, a basic, 630-watt-peak grid-tie solar system from Solaric, which is connected to the utility grid, starts at PHP 114,000.

Sheryl Estella, program manager at New Energy Nexus Philippines, says that while the non-profit has been observing strong consumer interest in solar, this does not necessarily translate into actual installations.

“The upfront cost of a solar PV [photovoltaic] system can represent several years of electricity expenses for a household, making the initial investment difficult for many families to absorb,” Estella notes.

“For many lower-income households, the issue is not whether solar can save [them] money over its lifetime, but whether they can afford the initial investment or qualify for financing in the first place,” she adds.

This reality is especially felt by the country’s urban poor, according to Orly Gallano, president of SM-ZOTO, a federation of organisations serving such communities within Metro Manila and its surrounding areas.

“Most of the jobs in these communities earn a monthly minimum wage of about 15,000 pesos (USD 235)… these are construction workers, industry workers, vendors,” Gallano says. He notes that his own electric bill takes up around 10-20% of his monthly SM-ZOTO salary.

Gallano says he saw the cost-saving benefits of solar power when SM-ZOTO installed a 5-KW solar system in their office, where they set up mobile charging stations for the community. Since then, the office’s monthly bill of PHP 16,000 has gone down nearly half, to PHP 9,000, he notes. The team was able to install the panels by partnering with the Center for Energy, Ecology, and Development, an advocacy organisation, with funding from the New Zealand embassy.

“If you’re an ordinary citizen and you don’t earn that much, [solar power is] a big expense initially,” he notes. “But later on… your electric bill will go down… in other words, this is an investment.”

Gallano plans to eventually transition to solar at home, after putting his dependents through school, he adds.

Angel Cruz, a freelance massage therapist and hairdresser living in the northern part of Metro Manila, says her meagre income leaves her with just PHP 5,000 after expenses.

The electricity bill for the apartment she shares with her parents and three children reaches PHP 7,000-8,000 each month. It covers just two fans, a television, a rice cooker, charging of their portable devices, lights, and an air conditioner that runs nightly to help manage her father’s hypertension.

While her parents chip in from time to time to help pay for power, a solar panel system with inverters and batteries is “not something we can afford anytime soon”, she notes.

Private banks in the Philippines offer solar installation loans, but requirements such as continuous employment, income thresholds and tax returns are likely to disenfranchise low-income, contractual and informally employed workers.

The government offers loan facilities via its savings and mutual fund agency, Pag-IBIG, that members can use to finance solar systems. However, these schemes also require individuals to have contributed to their savings for two years, as well as proof of income. Meanwhile, state programmes such as the Ginhawa Solar Energy Loan are only available to government workers and pensioners.

Jasmine May Sabado, a senior energy transition campaigner for People of Asia for Climate Solutions, notes that these loan grants are based on an individual’s credit history, which presents hurdles for those with poor credit. She suggested that allowing longer-term loan repayment can help cushion the impact of upfront costs.

“Accessibility does not easily extend to the poorest and most vulnerable communities who can benefit the most from solar rooftop systems,” according to Gerry Arances, lead convenor of the Power for People Coalition. “This is where government action remains sorely wanting, especially in the context of the energy crisis.”

He says the government should allocate resources towards solar rooftop panels for the country’s poorest communities and areas, to provide both an immediate reprieve and long-term solution to energy shocks. Arances adds that the government must encourage local supply chain development and offer tax rebates for solar panels and parts to improve product affordability.

“We especially emphasize the necessity of integrating solar power into socialized program frameworks to benefit poor and underserved communities and sectors for whom loan facilities would not be an option,” he says.

Demoral says that mechanisms for affordable financing already exist, with government loans already available or set to launch. But “the gap is in the implementation, on how quickly these programs are rolled out, how easy it is for households and small businesses to apply, and how quickly applications are approved”, she stresses.

Sabado says that local governments should pass solar-ready ordinances that are responsive to their local contexts. Such laws require new buildings or major renovations to include infrastructure that can accommodate solar systems. These will make the process of applying to use such power easier for households and entities, she notes.

Sabado adds that applications to set up net-metering can take months, despite government efforts to fast-track the process. Individual households also have difficulty acquiring permits for solar installations due to several documents being required, such as a lot title, tax declaration and proof of ownership.

Demoral says the Department of Energy’s recent decision allowing “micro-solar systems” of up to 1 KW to be installed without a building permit or environmental certificate showed promise in making the process less cumbersome for smaller households.

“It opens the door to plug-and-play systems of just one or two panels, at a fraction of the cost of a full rooftop installation,” she notes. “Households that could never afford a full system can now start small.”

The energy department did not respond to Dialogue Earth’s requests for comment.

“Government has an important role in creating the conditions that make affordable and renewable energy more accessible to Filipinos,” Estella says. This doesn’t just mean setting renewable energy targets, but also reducing barriers that consumers and installers face, she notes.

According to Estella, the government needs to simplify permitting and net-metering procedures, establish clear technical standards, and ensure consistent implementation.

She adds that it is important to strengthen the local solar industry through skills development, quality standards and support for qualified manufacturers.

“This can expand access, improve service quality, and help build a more competitive market,” she says. “Ultimately, widening access requires making renewable energy easier to adopt, easier to finance, and safer and more reliable to integrate into the electricity system.”

author: Freedom Editor
title: East London is anti-fascist
content:
Join us in Altab Ali Park on Saturday midday for a collective display of solidarity against the far right

On Saturday 31 October, neo-nazi thugs decided the best thing they could do with their day was take a trip to Freedom Bookshop in Whitechapel, and threaten and attack the volunteers and visitors to the shop.

The 15 or so masked up men filmed themselves spouting nonsense about “degenerate books” and making Hitler salutes. The volunteer locked the shop, a passerby confronted them and half the group fled. The man defended himself and was punched once before the rest of the group made their escape down Aldgate East tube.

Since then our heart has been warmed by the many expressions of solidarity.

As our friends from Plan C wrote, Freedom was attacked because it represents a history of anti-fascist resistance in East London.

Whilst this has happened to Freedom now, this concerns all of us. Let this be the catalyst to rally together.

Against fascist intimidation it is especially important to prioritise coming together, strengthening our existing networks, and organising for the sake of our community.

Join us in Altab Ali Park on Saturday midday for a collective display of solidarity against the far right.

author: Benji
title: Grossdemo gegen Tönnies
content:
Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Wir demonstrieren am 21.11. in Kellinghusen

Ihr seid wütend auf Tönnies? Wir auch! Wir haben 

dokumentiert

, was Schweine bei Tönnies wirklich erleiden müssen. Wir haben bei Tönnies in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert. Doch Tönnies tötet weiter. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal groß auf und demonstrieren an dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: Kellinghusen.




Bist du dabei?




Samstag, 21.11.2026

14:00 – 17:00 Uhr

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Hintergrundinfos




Rideshare-Tool

Damit möglichst viele Menschen zur Demo gegen Tönnies kommen, wollen wir euch bei der Planung eurer Anreise unterstützen. Daher haben wir ein cleveres Rideshare-Tool entwickelt, mit dem ihr Fahrgemeinschaften bilden könnt. So wird die Anreise für euch günstiger, einfacher und spaßiger.




Jetzt einsteigen!

Warum demonstrieren wir?

Anlass für die Großdemo am 21. November ist unsere aktuelle Veröffentlichung „Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies“. Tönnies ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie. Als Marktführer tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen Schweine. Unsere Aufdeckung zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf der Tiere in der CO₂-Anlage. Die Schweine schreien vor Angst und versuchen zu fliehen.




Was wir bisher getan haben

Gewalt im Schlachthof aufgedeckt

Verstöße dokumentiert

Tönnies angezeigt

Eine große Welle an Presseberichten ausgelöst

Zahlreiche Interviews geführt

Eine politische und gesellschaftliche Debatte angestoßen

Bei der Tönnies-Zentrale in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert

Hintergrundinfos

Und jetzt?

Die Gewalt im Schlachthaus geht unvermindert weiter! Wir sind wütend. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal ganz groß auf, bündeln unsere Kräfte an einem Termin und demonstrieren gemeinsam mit euch an genau dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: 

Kellinghusen!




Unsere Forderung: Der Betrieb muss schließen!




Ablauf und Programm

14:00 Uhr: Auftakt


Wir starten mit einer Auftaktkundgebung mit Redebeiträgen auf dem Unteren Marktplatz.

Demozug


Als großer und lauter Demozug ziehen wir mit Schildern, Bannern und Fahnen durch Kellinghusen, skandieren lautstark und setzen ein starkes Zeichen.

Zwischenstopp am Schlachthof


Die Demoroute führt uns bis zum Schlachthof. Dort gibt es weitere Redebeiträge.

Abschlusskundgebung


Gemeinsam laufen wir zurück zum Unteren Marktplatz, wo die Demo nach einer Abschlusskundgebung endet.

So kannst du mithelfen

Du willst mithelfen, dass die Demo richtig groß wird? Dann unterstütze uns bei der Mobilisierung: Bring deine Freund*innen mit zur Demo, teile unseren 

Content auf Social Media

 oder poste selbst unser Sharepic:




Demoregeln

Bitte beachtet unsere allgemeinen Demohinweise, damit sich alle wohlfühlen. Danke für euer Verständnis und eure Mithilfe!




1. Antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch

Einen Ansatz, die Ausbeutung der Tiere zu reformieren und somit im Grundsatz beizubehalten, verfolgen wir nicht. Unsere Forderungen sind grundsätzlich antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch. Wir bitten deshalb ausdrücklich darum, auf der Demo vermeintliche „Zwischenschritte“ oder „Reformen“ (z. B. Biofleischkonsum oder Verbesserung der Haltungsbedingungen) nicht als Ziel zu kommunizieren.

2. Kein Platz für Menschenfeindlichkeit

ARIWA lehnt alle Formen allgemeiner und gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit (wie zum Beispiel Ableismus, Antisemitismus, Homo- und Trans*feindlichkeit, Rassismus oder Sexismus) sowie verschwörungsideologische Denkmuster ab. Personen mit solchen Hintergründen sind bei der Demo ausdrücklich nicht erwünscht. Mehr Infos: 

ariwa.org/selbstverstaendnis

3. Keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs

Bitte tragt nach Möglichkeit keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs und achtet darauf, dass sie auch nicht so aussieht. Denn Produkte wie Kunstpelz oder Kunstleder können missverstanden werden und für Außenstehende einen falschen Eindruck erwecken.

4. Keine Partei- oder Religionswerbung

Parteiwerbung, Werbung für religiöse Gruppierungen sowie Holocaust-Vergleiche sind nicht erwünscht.

5. Bitte keine Tiere mitbringen

Aufgrund von Lärm, Hitze und Enge bitten wir euch, keine Tiere mit zur Demo zu bringen.

Sharepic downloaden




Der Beitrag 

Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

 erschien zuerst auf 

ARIWA

title: Talebanî: Em ji hikûmetê vedikişin
content:
Bafil Talebanî ragihand ku ew îtiraf bi civîna Parlamentoya Herêma Kurdistanê nakin û daxwaz ji PDKê kir ku dawî li tevgera hêzê bîne û got: “Em ji vê hikûmetê vedikişin.”




Piştî civîna Meclisa Rêveberiya Yekitiya Niştîmanî Kurdistan (YNK) Bafil Talebanî peyameke vîdeoyî weşand.




Bafil Talebanî ragihand ku wan gelek caran li Hewlêrê bi berpirsan re hevdîtin pêk anîne û got:







“Her carê ku pêşketin çêbûye di hevdîtinan de têk çûye, parlamento li hev neciviyane. Lê belê di nav PDKê de hatiye isbatkirin ku nizanin hikûmraniyê bikin, me berê gotibû tişteke wiha bibe, em îtiraf pênakin.”




“Îro rêveberiya YNKê desthilat da min û em radigihînin ku em îtiraf bi vê civînê nakin. Ev hikûmet têk çûye. Lewma biryara me ew e ku em ji vê hikûmetê vekişin. Em ji her qurbaniyê re amade ne. Em bi çareserkirina pirsgirêka Rojava û pêvajoya aştiyê û birayên xwe yên li Rojhilat ve mijûlin.




Peyameke min ji we re heye; we biryareke neheq da. Ez ji we re dibêjim, gel netirsînin. Dest ji liv û tevgera hêzê berdin, Em civînê û hikûmeta ku dê di encama vê civînê de were avakirin nas nakin. Ez ji wan dixwazim ku me neçar nekin ku bertek nîşan bidin. Ew çi postê li Hewlêrê destnîşan bikin, em ê li Silêmaniyê destnîşan bikin.”







Krîza avakirina hikûmetê du sal in berdewam dike




Li Herêma Kurdistanê ya Federal a Îraqê, hilbijartinên parlamentoyê di 20ê Cotmeha 2024an de pêk hat. Lêbelê ji wê rojê ve parlamentoyê deriyên xwe venekirine û hikûmet jî nehatiye ava kirin. Her çend di navbera PDK û YNKê de ji bo avakirina hikûmetê gelek civîn hatibin kirin jî, heta niha tu lihevkirineke zelal derneketine holê.




Di hilbijartina Cotmeha 2024an de kursiyên ku partiyan bi dest xistibûn ev in:




PDK: 39




YNK: 23




Nifşê Nû: 15




Yekgirtû: 7




Komele: 3




Helwest: 4




Bereya Gel: 2




Goran: 1




Hevpeymana Herêma Kurdistan: 1




Pêkhateyan: 5

author: Jillian C. York
title: When the Watchdogs Are Silenced: India's Crackdown on Those Documenting Online Censorship
content:
On November 3, our colleagues at the Software Freedom Law Center, India (SFLC.in) 

received notifications

 from X that the Delhi Police had issued takedown requests targeting 42 URLs. Among the accounts and posts targeted were those belonging to 

SFLC.in

, the 

Internet Freedom Foundation

 (IFF), and X account @geoblockedindia, as well as posts documenting legal notices and instances of online censorship.

 




Takedown requests targeting SFLC.in and other digital rights groups threaten not only their work, but the public’s ability to know when and how online speech is being restricted.

 




The requests cite grounds including hate speech, alleged defamation of the Hindu nationalist organization 

Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh

 (RSS), and concerns relating to safety and security. But the context in which these requests have emerged is particularly troubling: they target organizations and individuals whose work involves documenting restrictions on online expression and making those restrictions visible to the public.

 




In other words, the organizations being targeted are among those trying to tell the public when and how its speech is being censored.

 




SFLC.in is one of India's most important digital rights organizations and promotes innovation and open access to knowledge by helping developers make great free and open-source software, protects privacy and civil liberties for Indians by educating and providing free legal advice, and helps policymakers make informed and just decisions about use of technology. In 2025, we recognized their work with an 

EFF Award

 for Defending Digital Freedoms.

 




IFF

 (the Internet Freedom Foundation) is another of EFF's close allies in India. Like EFF, IFF combines advocacy campaigns and strategic litigation to advance digital rights. They write frequently about internet shutdowns and have filed several lawsuits contesting them.

 




Among SFLC.in's initiatives is its

 

Free Speech Tracker

, which documents instances of online censorship, content restrictions, and account takedowns in India. In a country where government orders to restrict online content are often opaque, this work is absolutely essential.

 

 

Recent legal notices object to the tracker itself, as well as the organization’s documentation of restricted content and geo-blocked material. The allegations against SFLC.in include claims that it is "continuously opposing government directions" and publicly circulating information about restricted content, thereby undermining measures taken in the name of national security and public order.

 




But documenting government censorship is not the same as undermining public safety. Reporting that content has been restricted is not an endorsement of that content, nor does it constitute an attempt to circumvent the law. It is an exercise in transparency and accountability, and one that allows journalists, researchers, civil society organizations, and the public to understand how governments exercise their power over the information landscape.

 




Censorship thrives in the absence of transparency

 




The use of legal complaints and platform takedown mechanisms against organizations documenting censorship creates a particularly troubling dynamic. When those who monitor restrictions on expression are threatened with having their accounts or reporting removed, the result is a chilling effect that extends far beyond the immediate targets. Other organizations or journalists may think twice before documenting controversial takedowns or challenging government orders, and the public loses access to an independent record of decisions that affect its ability to speak and access information online.

 




There is also an important role here for platforms like X. Platforms 

must be transparent

 about the requests they receive, provide meaningful notice to affected users, and ensure that any restrictions are subject to appropriate scrutiny and avenues for appeal. When governments seek to restrict speech, platforms have a responsibility to avoid becoming opaque intermediaries through which censorship is quietly carried out.

 




These developments are part of a broader pattern of pressure on independent civil society organizations working to defend freedom of expression and access to information in India. Digital rights groups play an indispensable role in documenting the effects of government policies, identifying patterns of censorship, and challenging restrictions that undermine fundamental rights. Their ability to do so independently is not a peripheral concern; it is a cornerstone of a healthy democratic society.

 




The right to freedom of expression includes the right to scrutinize the exercise of government power. That includes the right to document censorship, question the reasons given for it, and make that information available to the public. 

 




EFF stands in solidarity with SFLC.in, the Internet Freedom Foundation, @geoblockedindia, and all those working to document and challenge restrictions on online expression in India. We urge the authorities in India to respect the rights of digital rights organizations to conduct their work without intimidation or retaliation, and to ensure that any restrictions on online expression comply with international human rights standards.

Αφίσες/Καλέσματα των εκδηλώσεων:




Καταστολή και κοινοτισμός” – 

Στέκι Μεταναστ(ρι)ών




Α

νοιχτή συνέλευση αλληλεγγύης στα Προσφυγικά







Εκδήλωση και συζήτηση με θέμα “Καταστολή και Κοινοτισμός”. Θα συμμετέχουν δια ζώσης, η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών, η Κίνηση Χειραφέτησης Αναπήρων Μηδενική Ανοχή, η Επιτροπή Αγώνα Μεγάλης Παναγιάς και η Αυτόνομη Παρέμβαση Εστιακών.




Την προηγούμενη περίοδο η συνέλευσή μας, μαζί και με άλλες συλλογικότητες και ανθρώπους της Θεσσαλονίκης συντόνισε και προσπάθησε να δώσει ορμή και περιεχόμενο στον αγώνα αλληλεγγύης στα Προσφυγικά, όπως αυτός εξελίχθηκε στην πόλη μας. Το σκεπτικό μας, όπως το βάζαμε και στον δημόσιο λόγο μας, ήταν πως στα Προσφυγικά βρίσκουν έρεισμα όλοι οι αγώνες, γιατί όλοι οι αγώνες πηγάζουν και παίρνουν μορφή στην συλλογική ζωή των από τα κάτω. Μετά την πρώτη νίκη που κατάφερε ο αγώνας αυτός και με την επιθυμία να ανοίξουμε μία σειρά εκδηλώσεων για την αυτοοργάνωση πάνω στις βασικές συλλογικές μας ανάγκες, αποφασίσαμε να πραγματοποιήσουμε αυτήν την εκδήλωση. Στην κοινοτική συγκρότηση και την κοινωνική αυτοοργάνωση εντοπίζουμε την προοπτική συλλογικής επιβίωσης και αξιοπρεπούς ζωής μέσα στην συνθήκη εντεινόμενης καταστολής και μαζικής εξόντωσης που ζούμε σε πλανητικό επίπεδο.




Από τον κοινωνικό αγώνα των εστιακών ενάντια στην πλήρη υποβάθμιση του μοναδικού χώρου με στοιχεία κοινωνικής κατοικίας στην Θεσσαλονίκη, την κινηματική απάντηση σε μισαναπηρικές δολοφονίες και των εγκλεισμό των αναπήρων, την αντίσταση και την πολύμορφη καταστολή της Μεγάλης Παναγίας, ενός ολόκληρου χωριού, και το κοινωνικό μέτωπο που χτίστηκε με αιχμή τις απεργίες πείνας για την υπεράσπιση της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών, οι συμμετέχουσες συλλογικότητες εκφράζουν μια μεγάλη βεντάλια της αντίστασης των από τα κάτω, με μακρόχρονη εμπειρία απέναντι σε ευρύτατους μηχανισμούς και μεθόδους καταστολής.




Η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών έχει ξεκινήσει περιοδεία σε διάφορες γεωγραφίες στην ελλάδα και το εξωτερικό με τίτλο “Οι αγώνες νικούν όταν συναντιούνται”, με σκοπό τη σύνδεση και την ενδυνάμωση των αγώνων σε κάθε τοπικότητα. Θα παρουσιαστούν τα σκεπτικά και η θεμελίωση του αγώνα, τα μέσα που επιλέχθηκαν, ο απολογισμός της έκβασής του, καθώς και η προοπτική και οι προτάσεις για την επόμενη μέρα τόσο για την Κοινότητα όσο και ευρύτερα για το κίνημα και την κοινωνία.




Καλούμε τον κόσμο της πόλης να έρθει στην εκδήλωση και να συμμετέχει με τοποθετήσεις στην κουβέντα που θα ακολουθήσει.

Μέσα από τις ρωγμές τους σάπιου κόσμου τους ανοίγουμε δρόμους ελευθερίας




Το κύμα μαθητικών/φοιτητικών κινητοποιήσεων που εξαπλώνεται στη Γαλλία αποτελεί έκφραση της συσσωρευμένης κοινωνικής οργής απέναντι σε ένα σύστημα που θυσιάζει τις ανάγκες της νεολαίας στον βωμό των κρατικών και οικονομικών συμφερόντων. Οι καταλήψεις σχολείων, οι διαδηλώσεις και οι απεργιακές κινητοποιήσεις δεν περιορίζονται στην αντίδραση για τις περικοπές στην εκπαίδευση, αλλά αμφισβητούν συνολικά τις συνθήκες μέσα στις οποίες καλούνται οι νέοι να ζήσουν και να διαμορφώσουν το μέλλον τους. Η αλληλεγγύη εκπαιδευτικών, φοιτητών, εργαζομένων, αλληλέγγυων, μπορεί να μετατρέψει τις επιμέρους αντιστάσεις σε ένα ευρύτερο κίνημα ενάντια στην εκμετάλλευση και την καταπίεση. Οι συνελεύσεις, οι καταλήψεις και οι συλλογικές πρωτοβουλίες αλληλοβοήθειας δημιουργούν χώρους αυτοοργάνωσης, όπου οι άνθρωποι παίρνουν τις αποφάσεις στα χέρια τους, χωρίς να αναθέτουν τις διεκδικήσεις τους σε θεσμικούς εκπροσώπους. […] Η ιστορία των κοινωνικών αγώνων υπενθυμίζει πως καμία κατάκτηση δεν χαρίστηκε από τα πάνω. Η συλλογική δράση μπορεί να ανατρέψει όσα παρουσιάζονται ως αναπόφευκτα, όταν οι άνθρωποι οργανώνονται, συλλογικοποιούν τις αντιστάσεις τους και αγωνίζονται για να ζουν ελεύθερα χωρίς να υποτάσσονται στις επιταγές του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου.

ΒΑΡΒΑΡΙΚΗ ΚΛΗΡΟΝΟΜΙΑ

– 

Μια ιστορία για την κατάληψη Villa Βαρβάρα και το κίνημα των 90s στη Θεσσαλονίκη




Το αυτοοργανωμένο – αντιεμπορευματικό ντοκιμαντέρ Βαρβαρική Κληρονομιά είναι η απόπειρα καταγραφής μιας ιστορίας για την κατάληψη Villa Βαρβάρα και το κίνημα της Θεσσαλονίκης στα 90s. Η δημιουργία του βασίστηκε πάνω σε 17 συνεντεύξεις συντρόφων και συντροφισσών που δραστηριοποιούνταν στο κίνημα εκείνη την περίοδο και στην έρευνα πάνω στο αντίστοιχο αρχειακό υλικό (βίντεο, φωτογραφίες, αφίσες, κείμενα, έντυπα). Στόχος του είναι να μοιραστεί εργαλεία έρευνας και καταγραφής της ιστορίας με το κίνημα και να παρακινήσει για αντίστοιχες απόπειρες στο μέλλον.




Η έκδοση Βαρβαρική Κληρονομιά βασίζεται στις απομαγνητοφωνήσεις των συνεντεύξεων που έλαβαν χώρα για τη δημιουργία του αυτοοργανωμένου, αντιεμπορευματικού ντοκιμαντέρ “Βαρβαρική Κληρονομιά – Μια ιστορία για την κατάληψη Villa Βαρβάρα και το κίνημα των ’90s στη Θεσσαλονίκη”. Μια συλλογική δημιουργία του κινηματογραφικού crew της κατάληψης Φάμπρικα Υφανέτ, των αρουραίων των αρχείων και καταληψιών της Villa Βαρβάρα.

Συζήτηση για την “ειρήνη” του συστήματος και την άνοδο της ακροδεξιάς – Κοινωνικός χώρος Ven, seremos

 




“Ο πόλεμος τους σκοτώνει ό,τι άφησε όρθιο η ειρήνη τους…” έγραφε ο Μπέρτολτ Μπρεχτ




Με αυτό το σύνθημα πραγματοποιήσαμε φέτος το 23ο αντιρατσιστικό φεστιβάλ




Είναι αλήθεια πως ζούμε σε μια εποχή όπου ο πόλεμος παύει να αποτελεί εξαίρεση και μετατρέπεται σε μια διαρκή συνθήκη. Από την Παλαιστίνη και τη συνεχιζόμενη γενοκτονία στη Γάζα μέχρι τους πολέμους και τις στρατιωτικές επεμβάσεις που απλώνονται στη Μέση Ανατολή, Κούβα, Βενεζουέλα ολόκληρες κοινωνίες πληρώνουν με νεκρούς, εκτοπισμό, πείνα και καταστροφή.




Οι μεγάλες «δημοκρατίες» πολεμούν, και εξολοθρεύουν απροκάλυπτα με στόχο την ενίσχυση της ισχύος τους. Η ΕΕ φουλάρει τις πολεμικές μηχανές της με 800δις και με τις ζωές μας, για να αναγεννηθεί ο καπιταλισμός επενδύοντας στα μελλοντικά προϊόντα θανάτου. Οι στρατιωτικοί προϋπολογισμοί εκτοξεύονται, σε βάρος των κοινωνικών δαπανών, ενώ η πολεμική βιομηχανία καλείται να αυξήσει με ταχύτητα την παραγωγή της. Αλλά όποιος προετοιμάζεται για πόλεμο, τον θέλει.




Από την άλλη η “ειρήνη” τους είναι τo γκρίζο κύμα της ακροδεξιάς και φασισμού που πριμοδοτείται από την αστική πολιτική. Οι μηχανισμοί εξουσίας ανακατευθύνουν την οργή σ’ αυτούς και αυτές που δεν έχουν τίποτα, που ζουν αποκλεισμένες. Με κοινά στοιχεία τον ρατσισμό, τον εθνικισμό, την λευκή υπεροχή και την πατριαρχία, η ακροδεξιά έχει κανονικοποιηθεί.




Η “ειρήνη” τους δολοφόνησε 35.000 ανθρώπους από το 2014 μέχρι σήμερα, στη Μεσόγειο και στα κλειστά σύνορα της ΕΕ-φρούριο.




Η “ειρήνη” τους βάζει το κέρδος πάνω από την ανθρώπινη ζωή: όπως στα Τέμπη, στην Βιολάντα κά.




201 καταγεγραμμένοι θάνατοι το 2025 και 14.000 εργατικά ατυχήματα.




Η “ειρήνη” τους μετράει 15 γυναικοκτονίες μέσα στο 2026, ομοφοβικές και τρασφοβικές επιθέσεις, εξορίζει και δολοφονεί κάθε μη ¨κανονικό¨ σώμα.




Η “ειρήνη” στερεί σε ανθρώπους το δικαίωμα στη στέγη και υποβαθμίζει το σύστημα υγείας.




Η “ειρήνη” τους δίνει μισθό που δεν βγάζει το μήνα, νομοθετεί 13ωρα δουλειάς και εργασιακό μεσαίωνα.




Η “ειρήνη” τους είναι μια τεράστια υφαρπαγή πόρων (γη, νερό, δάση κλπ), διαρκείς περιφράξεις και περιβαλλοντική καταστροφή, αποτέλεσμα του αχαλίνωτου καπιταλισμού




Τι μπορούμε να κάνουμε για να αναχαιτίσουμε την πορεία προς τον πόλεμο και την προώθηση της Άκρας Δεξιάς από το αστικό μπλοκ εξουσίας ;




Διαφαίνεται κάποια ελπίδα από την εξέγερση της νέας γενιάς στην Γαλλία, Ισπανία, Πορτογαλία, Ιταλία, Γερμανία, Ελβετία, Αλβανία, Σερβία κά




Αυτά τα ερωτήματα θα μας απασχολήσουν στην εκδήλωση συζήτηση, που δεν καταφέραμε να κάνουμε στο 23ο αντιρατσιστικό φεστιβάλ και προγραμματίσαμε εκ νέου.




Την Παρασκευή 6 Νοεμβρίου στις 20.00 στον Κοινωνικό χώρο ven, seremos συζητάμε με την Λαμπρινή Θωμά, δημοσιογράφο και τον Δημήτρη Καλτσώνη , καθηγητή θεωρίας κράτους και δικαίου στο Πάντειο Πανεπιστήμιο
