Rêxistinê di raporê de da zanîn ku cezayê bidarvekirinê li 2 girtiyên Kurd hatiye birîn û li 21 kesan jî bi giştî 67 sal û 15 roj cezayê girtîgehê û 10 sal cezayê taloqkirî yê girtîgehê hatiye birîn. Her wiha ji bo kesekî ji wan cezayê 31 qamçiyan jî hat dayîn.



















HENGAW: Îranê di meha Îlonê de herî kêm 68 kes darve kirine




5 Cotmeh 2026










Ev amar dema ku Îran ji ber çewisandina xwînî ya xwenîşandanên li dijî hikûmetê yên ku Kanûna Pêşîn a 2025an dest pê kiribûn, bi zexteke mezin a civaka navneteweyî re rû bi rû ye.




Mîsyona lêkolînê ya Neteweyên Yekbûyî (NY) di rapora xwe ya meha Îlonê de diyar kiribû ku rayedarên Îranê komkujî, desteserkirinên bêsedem û şkence pêk anîne û hinek binpêkirin dikevin çarçoveya tawanên li dijî mirovahiyê.




Pisporên Neteweyên Yekbûyî her wiha bal kişand ser zêdebûna zextên li ser kêmneteweyan û bi taybetî Kurd û Belûçan.



















HRANA: Îranê di meha Hezîranê de 127 kes darve kirin




24 Hezîran 2026










8 jin û 6 zarok hatin desteserkirin




Li gorî agahiyên Hengawê, di nav 64 Kurdên ku ji aliyê hêzên ewlehiyê yên Îranê ve hatine desteserkirin de 8 jin û 6 zarok hene.




Hejmara herî zêde ya desteserkirinê bi 27 kesan li bajarê Sineyê û bi 25 kesan li bajarê Urmiyeyê hat tomarkirin.




Li bajarê Îlamê 8 kes û li Kirmaşanê 2 kes hatin desteserkirin, li Tehran û bajarê Xorasana Bakur jî kesek hat desteserkirin.



















Li Îranê di 3 salan de 2 hezar û 910 kes hatine darve kirin




18 Îlon 2025










Li gorî raporên Hengawê, rayedarên Îranê di meha Cotmehê de li seranserê welêt herî kêm 85 girtî darve kirine ku ev rêje li gorî meha Îlonê bi rêjeya ji sedî 25an zêdebûnekê nîşan dide.




Ji 124 bûyerên desteserkirinê yên li seranserê welêt, 64 kes ji wan Kurd bûn.




Hengawê ragihand ku ji 5 girtiyên Kurd ên hatine bidarvekirin 2 kes bi tohmetên pêwendîdarî madeyên hişbir û 3 kes jî bi tohmeta kuştina bi zanebûn hatine mehkûmkirin.




Cezayê bidarvekirinê yê Werîşe Mûradiyê




Di nav kesên ku cezayê bidarvekirinê li wan hatiye birîn de girtiya siyasî ya Kurd a ji bajarê Sineyê Werîşe Mûradî jî heye.




Li gorî Tora Mafên Mirovan a Kurdistanê (KHRN), piştî ku Dadgeha Bilind a Îranê biryara berê betal kir, Şaxa 15emîn a Dadgeha Şoreşa Îslamî ya Tehranê di nîvê meha Çiriya Pêşîn de careke din cezayê bidarvekirinê li Mûradiyê birî.




Mûradî bi tohmeta "endamtiya komeke serhildêr a bi çek" hat mehkûmkirin.




Êrişên li ser kolberan û kuştina jinan




Hengawê her wiha ragihand ku li nêzîkî bajarê Baneyê pasdarên sînor ên Îranê gule li kolberê Kurd Elî Meşhûrî reşandin û ew birîndar kir.




Kolber ew xebatkarên sînor in ku ji bo debara xwe li ser xetên çiyayî yên Rojhilatê Kurdistanê kel û pelan vediguhêzin.




Rêxistinê di meha Cotmehê de kuştina 4 jinên Kurd jî belge kir ku yek ji wan bi hinceta "namûsê" hatiye kuştin.



















Rêxistina Mafên Mirovan a Îranê: Li Îranê her roj 6 kes tên darvekirin




27 Çile 2025










Di raporteke din a Hengawê ya li ser mafên jinan de hat destnîşankirin ku di heman mehê de li seranserê Îranê herî kêm 23 jin hatine kuştin, 16 çalakvanên jin hatine desteserkirin û herî kêm 8 ji wan Kurd bûn.




Hengawê meha Îlonê ragihandibû ku 5 girtiyên Kurd hatine bidarvekirin, 70 kes hatine desteserkirin û cezayê bidarvekirin an girtîgehê li 13 kesan hatiye birîn.




Tora Mafên Mirovan a Kurdistanê (KHRN) jî di raporeke din a vê hefteyê de diyar kir ku di meha Cotmehê de herî kêm 2 bidarvekirin, 44 desteserkirin û girtin rû dane û cezayê bidarvekirin an girtîgehê li 5 kesan hatiye birîn.



















Îran: Di nav 5 mehan de bi tohmetên siyasî herî kêm 59 kes hatin darvekirin




11 Îlon 2026













Di sala 2025an de herî kêm 48 jin hatin darvekirin




Rêxistina Mafê Mirovan ya Îranê (Iran Human Rights- IHR) û platforma Li Dijî Cezayên Darvekirinê Em Tev bi Hevre ne (Ensemble contre la peine de mort) têkildarî darvekirinên li Îranê raporeke hevpar weşandibûn.




Li gorî raporê di sala 2025an de hejmara darvekirinan li gorî sala berê wî ji sedî 68 zêde bûye û gihîştiye 1639 kesan.




Her weha li gorî vê hejmarê rojane herî kêm 4 kes hatine 

darvekirin

. Ji sala 1989an û vir ve cara yekem ewqas kes tên darvekirin.




Li gorî heman raporê di sala 2025an de 48 jin hatine darvekirin ku ev hejmar di 20 salên dawî de hejmara herî zêde ye.




Rêxistinên mafên mirovan dibêjin ku darvekirin ji bo zextên siyasî û kontrola civakî têne bikaranîn. Rêveberê IHRê diyar kir ku rayedar hewl didin bi avakirina atmosfera tirsê xwepêşandanan bitepisînin. Rêxistina Efûyê ya Navneteweyî, jî diyar dike ku 

Îran

 li gorî nifûsa xwe yek ji wan welatan e ku hejmara herî zêde ya darvekirinan lê tê sepandin.







*Çavkanî: Rûdaw, HENGAW, KHRN

title: Peymana Mekeyê li Parlamentoya hat pejirandin
content:
Parlamentoyê, pêşnûmeyasaya têkildarî erêkirina Peymana Hevbeş a Parastinê ya Mekeyê pejirand. Ev peyman di navbera Tirkiye, Pakistan û Erebistana Siûdiyê de hatibû îmzekirin.




Peymana ku di navbera Tirkiye, Pakistan û Siûdiyê de hatibû îmzekirin di Lijneya Giştî ya Parlamentoyê de bi 277 dengên erê li hemberî 118 dengên na hat pejirandin.




Peyman avakirina "mekanîzmaya hevbeş a parastin û ewlehiyê" ya di navbera her sê welatan de pêşbînî dike. Li gorî vê peymanê, êrişeke çekdarî ya derve ya li ser aliyekî wekî ku li dijî hemû aliyan hatiye kirin tê hesibandin.




Peyman her wiha pêşbînî dike ku alî ji bo parastina serwerî, serxwebûn û yekparçeyiya axa hevdû hevkariyê bi pêş bixin û li hemberî gefên muhtemel bi hev re gavan bavêjin.




Derbarê peymanê de




Tirkiye, Erebistana Siûdiyê û Pakistanê di Tebaxê de Peymana Hevbeş a Parastinê ya Mekeyê îmze kiribûn.




Peyman ji 16 madeyan pêk tê û ji aliyê Serokkomarê Tirkiyeyê Recep Tayyîp Erdogan, Şazadeyê Erebistana Siûdiyê Mihemed Bîn Selman û Serokwezîrê Pakistanê Şehbaz Şerîf ve hatiye îmzekirin.




Di nava vê peymanê de madeyên krîtîk cih digirin. Li gorî peymanê, êrişa li ser her endamê vê hevalbendiyê dê wekî êrişa li ser her du welatên din jî bê dîtin.




Rayedar radigihînin ku Peymana Mekeyê bi temamî ji bo armancên parastinê ye û ti welatî nake armanc.




Her sê welat di çarçoveya "mafê parastina rewa" yê madeya 51ê ya Peymannameya Neteweyên Yekbûyî (NY) de piştgiriyê didin welatê ku rastî êrişê hatiye. Di vê piştgiriyê de derfet û şiyanên leşkerî jî cih digirin.




Herî

 

kêm ji bo

 

10

 

salan

 

e




Alî piştî ketina meriyetê heta 10 salên ewil nikarin ji peymanê derkevin.




Piştî 10 salan jî tenê bi agahdarkirineke nivîskî ya herî kêm 3 mehan berê, dê karibin mafê xwe yê vekişînê bi kar bînin.

author: ROAPE
title: What does Zambia’s Hakainde Hichilema tell us about democracy in Africa today?
content:
Perhaps the strongest hangover from colonialism is the relative lack of consent garnered by the ruling parties: the notion of them gaining “hegemony on a 

shoestring

” in a context where rulers’ goals are to keep labour costs as low as possible in order to expand profits of exports. The strategy depended upon indirect rulers defined by “traditions” (flexible and changing) and regions and required brokerage among shifting alliances. Lacking the ideological means of gaining consent via domination of media and civil society institutions, rulers resort to state violence and intimidation.




In 2021 Hichilema inherited a state structure that had, according to 

Amnesty International

, over the previous decade undertaken a “systematic crackdown on the right to freedom of expression”, criminalizing peaceful dissent and forcing the closure of independent media outlets. One consequence is that there are no reliable sources of information on the current political crisis. What fails to make international news is any analysis of the prominent regional and ethnolinguistic divisions that animate street-level politics. There is also no analysis of the striking absence of any clear differences in ideological or policy orientations between parties. The currently jailed opposition leader Brian Mundubile heads a coalition formed for the sole purpose of getting UPND out of power while contestation rests largely on respective judgements of character and regional and ethno-linguistic criteria. Questions revolved around 

who

 gets to govern – rather than 

why

 they should govern. Youtube and Facebook searches for elections information do not yield much more than pastors and self-appointed “prophets”, prophesizing elections results rather than actual political analysis.




The campaign period leading up to the national election on August 13

th

 was marred by street violence among 

political supporters

, backed up with intimidation of opposition supporters by police and military. International observers have documented instances of voter intimidation, assaults, abductions, and arrest of hundreds of opposition supporters. Even worse has been the loss of life. A day after the election, security forces killed opposition member,Mutotwe Kafwaya, a former cabinet minister, and Lovemore Chishima, a polling agent. The UN Special Rapporteur, Gina Romero, has called for immediate international scrutiny. The EU parliament passed a near 

unanimous resolution

 condemning the killings and the increase in political repression since the election and calling for an independent and impartial investigation. Hichilema has also cancelled the passports of at least six critics of his government, who include a 

prominent academic

. When he was in opposition, Hichilema was a victim of the same repression he is inflicting on those who oppose his government.




For Tonga, Ila and Lenje ethnic groups (collectively referred to as ‘Bantu Botatwe’),  a stronghold of the ruling UPND, and where Hakainde and the rest of Southern Province belong, his election victory in 2021 was the culmination of a 75-year struggle of supporting opposition candidates who called for liberal nationalism. This dates back to 1951 when Hakainde’s fellow southerner, Harry Nkumbula launched the Northern Rhodesian African Congress (later renamed as African National Congress). With Nkumbula being eclipsed by Kenneth Kaunda and the United National Independence Party (UNIP) throughout the independence struggle, he remained the primary opposition figure until the banning of the opposition parties in 1973. Since then, Southern and Western regions had maintained deep grievances. With the UPND in power, today these grievances find expression through periodical street battles involving loyal cadres, most of who are lumpenproletarian, against their opposition counterparts. Unemployed and in poverty, these cadres hope for hand-outs in exchange for political support. Ruling party cadres are often the ones who kickstart the political disturbances targeting the opposition, which include disrupting campaign rallies. Thereafter, the police and military, join in, ostensibly to restore order by cancelling the opposition rallies altogether, which ultimately benefit the party in power. This dynamic also led to the suspension of the 2026 election ballot counting in some areas.




Back to Nkumbula, his politics continue to be misunderstood despite a brilliant 

biography

 by Giacomo Macola that dispels much of the popular mythology that fuels animosity towards Tonga-speaking peoples. To understand some of the ethnolinguistic (read: “tribalist”) tensions in Zambia it is helpful to know some of the colonial history.




Early in the industrial-era conquest of “Northern Rhodesia”, portions of what is today Zambia’s Southern Province were the site of the earliest and highest concentrations of Christian missionary settlements. Prior to their arrival, cattle-rearing Tonga-speaking peoples on the “plateau” portions of the province were being preyed upon by neighbouring warring groups. Unlike many Bantu-speaking peoples, the Tonga had not reorganized their societies to support military self-defence, (nor did they elect chiefs with political power). Thus, they appreciated the relative calm brought by British rule.




Missionaries established schools and popularized the use of the ox-drawn plow. With their knowledge of English, Tonga peoples were quick to occupy roles as civil servants within the colonial state, and after. Large portions of their land were cleared and given to white settlers, but rather than burdening themselves with resentments, Tonga farmers emulated these settlers. They adopted the dominant crops of maize and tobacco production (which they had to sell at prices below what the white settlers would garner). Their cattle herds grew rapidly, especially among those with access to grazing on the nutrient-rich Kafue floodplains. Cattle were both wealth and traction to pull plows, leading to a cycle of accumulation. By the time of independence in 1964, many were wealthy enough to buy large-scale farms from white populations departing to the racist bastions of Southern Rhodesia and South Africa. Other large private-titled plots were subdivided and sold to endogenous farmers, sometimes with low-interest, state-guaranteed loans.




By independence, most Tonga farmers had adopted key tenets of liberal democratic ideology including the belief that employers provide “opportunity” rather than exploitation. They were taught to approach “farming as a business” long before it became a mantra of the World Bank, AGRA and dominant development NGOs. They wanted an impartial state that would nurture indigenous capitalists.




Although they maintained an oppositional force in the first decades of independence, the plateau part of Southern Province benefitted from loans, an agricultural marketing board providing inputs, and a ministry of agriculture and veterinary department offering extension services, all while a growing urban population maintained a steady market for maize, sunflower, milk and livestock. They also had family members occupying positions as civil servants, whose savings could be invested back into their farms.  This broke down during an economic downturn in the 1980s and since then, many Southerners have lamented what they perceive as a dysfunctional state, rife with corruption, and benefitting specific regions and ethnolinguistic groups, especially the Bemba of the country’s northern region. There are some parallels with the experiences of the Lozi, in Western Province, whose Litunga (king), from 1889, sought recognition from the British Monarchy through treaties, as a strategy of bolstering themselves from predation by the Makololo, and internal pretenders. Yet, in the post-independence era, their political power eroded, leading to a shared sense of marginalization in the national project.




Two structural differences in political mobilization in the North and East are larger migrant labour populations, who became an industrial (often unionized) proletariat, and that chiefs have held greater ability to mobilize electoral support.  This differs from an organizational context in which Southern Province farmers are disadvantaged by geographic distance. Thus, to some degree, they have a harder time representing themselves (paraphrasing Marx’s Eighteenth Brumaire). Their work disperses them




In this context, Tonga farmers have repeatedly sought a saviour figure, and Hichilema  was their perfect organic intellectual so long as they didn’t look too closely. He was like them. He had succeeded in finance and in industrial cattle finishing (buying adult animals, fattening them in stockyards and re-selling). What they overlooked, however, was the degree to which he represents international capitalist interests that have bought out many of the large-scale farms gradually lost by Tonga peoples throughout the perpetual structural-adjustment, neoliberal era.




According to the neoliberal theory behind Structural Adjustment Programs imposed in the 1990s, an overburdening state was holding back the entrepreneurial capitalist class. In practice, it was the opposite. Without the state, Tonga farmers faced 

devastating loses

 that included widespread livestock epidemics, in turn contributing to periods of regional famine in the late 1990s and early 2000s.




From the perspective of other ethnolinguistic groups of the North and East, the Tonga are often resented for their seeming over-representation in positions within the state apparatus, banks and large corporations. Some Tonga farmers also bring ecologically destructive agricultural practices into the north (often led by tobacco, kiln dried alongside deforestation for cropping). In many instances this coincides with the displacement of previous inhabitants that did not adhere to capitalist property rights.  With limited and distorting evidence, anti-Tonga sentiment is mobilized by some factions who have understandable grievances in an economy that works for so few.




If one looks at a 

voting map

 of the recent election results, they will see it split down the middle. While Hakainde succeeded in Central and Copperbelt, the margins of victory were much tighter, owing to the fact these provinces have greater diversity and large populations of Tonga within them.




The majority of Zambians oppose ethnic chauvinism (“tribalism”), but when there are no recognisable differences in political platforms, ethnicity and region is all that remains. HH foments these grievances when he publicly stated, in 2025, his preparedness to tactically 

“squeeze the throat”

 of his opponents. This talk emboldened thuggish behaviour from UPND cadres, before HH then prevented his predecessor, Edgar Lungu from leaving the country for medical care, resulting in his untimely death in June of that year. In the weeks before the election, numerous videos were posted on X and Tik Tok, of UPND cadres angrily miming a slash of the throat, suggesting that was coming for Mundubile.




The admiration Hakainde has attracted from international leaders and business interests is comparable to people like Macky Sall in Senegal, or Rwanda’s Paul Kagame. They are initially heralded as technocratic liberals who can wield gentlemanly liberal discourses. They can supposedly govern through reason and don’t need the blunt force and the carceral machinery of the state to succeed. They are seen as potentially neutral, managerial arbiters that will govern in national interest. And not steal. In these cases, we see that once in office, there are structural features of the neocolonial African state that pull them into old patterns and reveal the shallowness of the electoral discourse.




Many such features derive from the limited space for endogenous capital accumulation in economies that have incorporated Africans in subordinate ways. Neoliberalism deepened the dependence of African countries upon primary commodity exports. International capital dominates mineral extraction and construction of key infrastructure, and it has thoroughly (if unevenly) 

penetrated

 the agrarian economy. Attempts at building domestic linkages in the extractive sector through local content legislation are 

muted

, in part due to the ineffectuality of the state.




Among the limited spheres left for indigenous capital are transport and petty mercantilism. As these sectors are saturated with competition, profit margins are low. Beyond this, dominant fractions of the indigenous ruling class fight for control over the state apparatus, which can offer the prospects of infrastructure contracts that can be dispersed in a clientelist fashion and provide kickbacks to politicians. This is a cut-throat game. As 

Brian Mutambo

 has carefully outlined, prominent UPND tactician, Siawan explains to their cadres that the stakes of losing are that the opposition will do to Hakainde what he has done to Lungu.




Bankers

 like HH because he paid down debt and restructured loans with the IMF (yet again), bringing down inflation. He has also, however, imposed new mining laws that legislated gradual increases in 

local content

 laws, in effort to expand the sphere of indigenous accumulation. And, he re-instituted free primary and secondary education and dedicated funds to building schools, training and hiring teachers and expanding universities. The latter should be celebrated as a return to the post-independence norm before IMF Structural Adjustment brutally decimated public services. Yet, the reality for most Zambians is that while they are better educated, they are dissatisfied with the 

state of the economy

 amidst 

high unemployment

. They have been subjected to decades of structural adjustment, that has only brought rising levels of 

poverty

. According to the UN, the share of GDP from labour, comprising wages and social protection transfers, decreased from 48.2% in 2004 to 26.5% in 2025. It has halved. Admittedly, this data is skewed by the fact annual copper exports tripled over this period, alongside rising productivity. The benefits flow upward and out.




In the 1990s the Washington consensus institutions demanded conditionalities of multi-party democracy. Today, the US president shows that it is by no means necessary. Tanzania’s recent experience of 

post-election violence

 shows Hakainde what he can get away with. We know who else he looks to for guidance, as in 

April 2025

, speaking at the American Jewish Congress Global Forum 2025, Hakainde stated that he shares democratic values with the US and Israel. In November 2025, following the hosting of the Israeli AGRI-Tech Summit in Livingstone, southern Zambia, he agreed to a “shared commitment to deepening economic and technological partnerships” with 

Israel

 and sought “investments cooperation in key sectors such as energy, agriculture, precision irrigation, and technology”.




Numerous African governments are embracing such an alliance with Israel. In the Zambian case, it is a concerning indication of the underlying capitalist agrarian model, built on erasure and enclosure alongside the severe disregard for basic rights of assembly, expression, resistance and even existence. What Hakainde is adopting coincides with the enabling of a populist escalation of street-level violence that resembles that of Israeli settlers (admittedly in a much milder form). The risk of this current moment in Zambia is that the existing political divisions could split the country in two. HH’s behavior should not be normalized. The EU, UN and Amnesty International calls should be taken very seriously by any country wishing to uphold the possibility for civilian, democratic rule in Zambia and elsewhere.




(The opinions expressed in this piece are the author’s own and do not represent those of Carleton University or any other employer or affiliation. The author is also grateful to Alexander Caramento for comments on an earlier draft).


The post 

What does Zambia’s Hakainde Hichilema tell us about democracy in Africa today?

 appeared first on 

ROAPE

author: Willy Mutunga
title: Book Review: From Mau Mau to Ruto-Must-Go: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism
content:
I recently read a review of the book, 

From MAU MAU to RUTO-MUST-GO: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism,

 

by Teddy Odira, a young lawyer in Nairobi who published in The Platform for Law, Justice, and Society. I shared the review with one of the co-editors of the book, Shiraz Durrani, and asked him what he thought. This is was his response via a WhatsApp text:




It’s a brilliant review, I think. He understands the undercurrents that the book explores and identifies key issues, like land, that have driven resistance. He also sees resistance as an on-going, incomplete struggle. Very well done!




What is well said by another is mine. In this review, I want to glorify the work of the artist movements in Kenya for breathing life into the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, particularly 

Article 33

 that decrees freedom of expression. This freedom of expression has limitations. It is the freedom of artistic creativity that is glorified in two of the articles in the book. They glorify cartoonists and Social Justice Theatre (SJCCTT). Freedom of artistic creativity in Kenya is valued by others, including the two mentioned. The others include: poets, spoken word artists, graffiti artists, songwriters, singers, comedians, filmmakers, and others. Freedom of artistic creativity has been a radical site of struggle in the implementation of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. Freedom of expression under the Constitution has been the subject of a recently published scholarly work.




This Constitution has been described as progressive and transformative because of the process of its making, its texts on objectives, purpose, and vision to reform, by non-reformist reforms, which maintain the status quo in Kenya. While the ruling elite find the Constitution inconvenient and abstract, these sites of struggle have used provisions of the Constitution to craft political demands, breathe life into these sites through uprising, robust public participation, mass action, and public interest litigation. The quest for an authentic patriotic alternative political leadership is a continuous struggle anchored in these constitutional sites of struggle that the ruling elite has refused to implement. It is argued that such an alternative political leadership that is authentic and patriotic will implement the Constitution by consolidating gains made, and rescuing the weaknesses that are encountered during the process of its implementation.




Glorification




A: In Praise of Cartoonists: Ruo Kimani-Ruo




Ruo Kimani-Ruo praises the cartoonists in words that should not be paraphrased:







…, 

there has emerged an unprecedented form of political cartoons artwork which has been launched in Kenya with sizzling, scorching, blistering cartoon editorials and other graphics and caricatures of public figures that express the artists’ opinions, with celebrated cartoon artists Celeste and Maddo

 

being joined by Yoko and others-all freely and fearlessly expressing their opinions on public issues and the individuals in government and thereby shedding light on the public mood on issues.…










With these political cartoons, the artists have had a field day and typically combined artistic skills, hyperbole and satire to question authority. The cartoons have drawn attention to, among other things, corruption, electoral inequalities, political abductions and other social ills including violence- and the Consolidated Fund at Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) where billions of shillings are being ‘siphoned and stashed in offshore accounts in the West; and suspicions of embezzlement.







The genius of the cartoonists that I have encountered over decades lies in the interpretation of their work for the powers that be, and the citizens themselves. They are always armed with many interpretations of their cartoons. They use those interpretations to either stay safe when confronted by elites and their machinery of violence, or to mobilize the citizens around the key messages. They invariably keep their mouths shut and let their work engage both the enemy and the friend. Their work requires great critical thinking, taking ideological and political positions in breathing life into the provisions of the Constitution to energize non-reformist reforms.




B: In Praise of Theatre Artists:

 

Zachary J Patterson




Zachary J Pattern glorifies the Social Justice Centres Travelling Theatre (SJCTT) in the following paragraphs:







Interactive scenes show an all-too familiar tale of the oppressed and their oppressors-the spectators become ‘spect-actors’. It is a brilliant way of renewing hope, inspiring the imagination and reviving resistance

…. 










Inspired by communist playwright Bertolt Brecht’s notion of art as tool that can help shape our social conditions, members of SJCTT approach their performance as active participants of the class struggle. The provocative thespians of SJCTT use common language rooted in local knowledge to cut through the apolitical noise and disrupt the established order, exhibiting a clear political perspective drawn from Marxist political theory. Shaped by their surrounding social conditions and informed by historical and contemporary realities, SJCTT deploys techniques of Augusto Boal’s Theatre of the Oppressed to analyze social problems and address the factors of the oppression.










…Their performances are shaped both by appreciation for Kenya’s history of resistance and their shared experiences, resulting in programs rich with historical knowledge and relevance to contemporary issues.










…Inspired by Boal and Brecht, [Ezra] Brain suggests that the nature of political theatre is to disrupt, present a coherent political perspective, and challenge dominant narratives and discourses…From a Marxist perspective, in order for the theatre to be political, it must go beyond entertainment and awareness-building by offering the people a way forward. Performing among community members in Nairobi’s informal settlements, SJCTT introduce[s] unruly protagonists to encourage dialogue amongst the spectators and educate them to consider active participation in politics-which could change their lives for the better.







SJCTT needs to be put in the historical trajectory of links and continuities of revolutionary struggles. Before SJCTT was the University of Nairobi Travelling Theatre (UNTT), and the Kamirithu outdoor theatre that performed Ngugi wa Mirii and Ngugi wa Thiong’o’s play Ngaahika Ndeenda/I Will Marry When I Want. Both performances were projects of the underground movement, the December Twelfth Movement (DTM). Ngugi wa Thiong’o was a member of one of the DTM’s underground cells. The (UNTT) staged various radical plays in high schools all over Kenya. The cast was invariably radical University students from the radical departments in the (UNTT), namely Literature, Law, Political Science, Economics, Sociology, and Religious Studies. We should not forget the Mau Mau’s Kenya Land and Freedom Army’s (KLFA) poems and songs. This Liberation Army still remains the most revolutionary beacon of Kenyan class struggles. These poems and songs were compiled, edited, and translated from the Gikuyu language into English by Maina Wa Kinyatti. As recently as 10-13 September 2026, some of the cast in SJCTT performed at the Kenya National Theatre, Ngugi wa Thiong’o’s   Matigari ma Njiruungi. Ndungi Githuku was the lead actor. He is also the leader of the Field Marshal Band, known for its revolutionary poems and songs.




In Lieu of Conclusion: 

From Mau Mau To Ruto-Must-Go

 

demystified




As I have stated above, the Mau Mau War of Liberation remains the greatest and the main beacon of our revolution. The working peoples of Kenya took up arms to challenge the might of the British Empire. Independence after 78 years of occupation, oppression, and exploitation was a revolution, albeit an ordinary one compared to the great revolutions of the 20th Century. Even those two great revolutions of the 20th Century went through links and continuities of ordinary revolutions.




The attributes of a leader who is a comprador in chief, and the glaring personification of the elite in power is President Museveni. I believe Mahmood Mamdani has interrogated and historicized this issue in the case of Museveni. The outsourcing of the Ugandan Army in Somalia, South Sudan, and the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are clear examples of a leader of an elite that can second-guess the interests of imperialism and implement its interests. Although Mamdani does not discuss cultural imperialism in Uganda, it is clear Museveni has supported the demands of cultural imperialists in the US and Europe in their quest to get the Parliament of Uganda to enact the draconian Anti-homosexuality Act. The fundamentalist Christian Right in the US and Europe argues that they want to save Africans from the decadence of Western values! Indeed, they say this when they are very ignorant of African values that tolerate and accommodate sexual orientation. These cultural imperialists have always described African values as Satanic. 




President Ruto is the personification of a collective comprador bourgeoisie, a class that has crucial ingredients in the economic, social, cultural, theological, and political spheres. In a country that has deep divisions on ethnicity, individualization of this class could be seen to be against a particular community and thereby enrich the strategies of ethnic divisions by the same comprador class. The entire comprador bourgeoisie has to be historicized and interrogated so that its ingredients are understood. If there is to be personification, it must be to identify the various components of the class and their various respective leaderships. And the link between the comprador bourgeoisie and the imperialist bourgeoisie has to be understood. I believe the Malcolm Xian metaphor of the house niggers is still apt. Indeed, Kenya and the rest of Africa are slave plantations; the ruling elites are a den of house niggers, and the masters of the plantation are the imperialism of the Triad (US, Europe, Japan), including other countries that are in the orbit of imperialism and have interests in Africa, such as China and Russia. President Ruto and the comprador bourgeoisie he leads have supported continuing to allow military bases in Kenya without the participation of Kenyans, that is decreed by the supreme law, the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. He has sent the police to Haiti in defiance of a court order on the issue. The West still pontificates about democracy and the rule of law, but does not comply with our supreme law, finding it abstract and inconvenient, a hallmark of hypocrisy, racism, perfidy, and double standards.




The burning political question in Africa, in my opinion, is the quest for an authentic and patriotic alternative political leaderships. To be such a leadership, it must be at a minimum, anti-imperialist and anti-comprador. It must be a leadership that loves the working people. It must run to the people of Africa for support when it faces the wrath of imperialism. Such leadership has to embrace people-to-people revolutionary Pan-Africanism that includes the African diaspora as the basis of the liberation of Africa. It must be a leadership that understands the status quo of the planet which is unsustainable, unacceptable, and undesirable, and that has to be overthrown. The growing consciousness of global citizens towards identifying the common enemy of the planet we wish to see must be reinforced and supported in this century through a global solidarity against militarism, ecological degradation, sexism, homophobia, domination, exploitation, oppression, and a planet that puts profits before people. Such leadership should participate in the ongoing debates of a socialist planet. These debates seek a consensus on the socialist paradigm that will liberate the planet by interrogating the socialist experiments in the Soviet Union, China, North Korea, Cuba, Vietnam, and other countries where the revolutionary paradigm has been enacted through liberation wars and movements. That project is absolutely critical to identifying what socialist gains have been made, and the exposed weaknesses can be the basis for further discussion that could consolidate a revolutionary theory for implementation.




–




This article was first published in 

Pambazuka News

.

Book Review: From Mau Mau to Ruto-Must-Go: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism

 first appeared on 

The Elephant

author: Jana Hoger
title: Update: Polizeihund bei Demo misshandelt – Staatsanwaltschaft stellt Ermittlungen ein
content:
Symbolbild







Bei einer Demonstration gegen den AfD-Parteitag am 11. Januar 2025 in Riesa kam es zu 

gewaltsamen Einsätzen

 der sogenannten Polizeihunde. Wir von PETA Deutschland kritisieren dies scharf, erstatten Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen und fordern, dass der Einsatz von Polizeihunden endlich beendet wird. Erfahren Sie hier, was bei der Demonstration vorgefallen ist und warum Gewalt gegen „Polizeihunde“ kein Einzelfall ist.




Update vom 7. November 2026




Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden stellt Verfahren ein




Nachdem im Januar 2026 ein Video für einen medialen Aufschrei sorgte, das zeigt, wie ein sogenannter 

Polizeihund

 bei einer Demonstration gewaltsam gegen einen Demonstranten eingesetzt wurde, erstatteten wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen.




Im August 2026 wurde bekannt, dass die Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden in dem Fall nicht weiter ermittelt – angesichts des traurigen Videos mit absurden Begründungen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft erklärt diese Entscheidung in dem Einstellungsbescheid damit, dass ein „Verstoß gegen das Tierschutzgesetz […] nur vorliegen [würde], wenn man einem Tier ohne vernünftigen Grund aus Rohheit erhebliche Schmerzen zufügen würde.“ Der im Video dokumentierte Umgang des Beamten mit dem Hund sei keine „Rohheit“ im Sinne des Tierschutzgesetzes, da die ergriffene „Maßnahme […] zum Aufrechterhalten der öffentlichen Sicherheit und Ordnung erforderlich war […]“ und der Hund „nur kurz eingesetzt“ worden sei.




Die Staatsanwaltschaft begründet die Entscheidung darüber hinaus damit, dass „Diensthunde […] legal bei der Polizei als Hilfsmittel auch in Stresssituationen eingesetzt […]“ werden. Die Tiere würden dabei automatisch Belastungssituationen ausgesetzt. Die Interessen und das Wohl der Hunde rückten jedoch im Verhältnis zu den polizeilichen Interessen der Gefahrenabwehr in den Hintergrund, da die „Diensthunde“ zu diesem Zwecke ausgebildet würden. Der den Hunden zugeschriebene „Nutzen“ rechtfertigt laut Ansicht der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden, dass die Tiere bewusst in Gefahrensituationen gezwungen werden.




PETA kritisiert Entscheidung der Staatsanwaltschaft: Gesetz erlaubt Gewalt gegen Diensthunde




Die Einstellung unserer Anzeige ist ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, dass das Gesetz die „Diensthunde“ nicht vor einem gewaltsamen Umgang und Missbrauch schützt. Hunde sind keine Einsatzmittel, sondern fühlende Lebewesen, die einen respektvollen, liebevollen Umgang verdient haben – nicht die missbräuchliche Verwendung  als Waffe oder Schutzschild.




Wir vertreten die Ansicht, dass moderne Polizeiarbeit ohne Tiere auskommt und fordern daher Politik und Behörden auf, „Diensthunde“ zu verbieten.







Originaltext vom 13. Januar 2025




Gewalt gegen Polizeihunde bei einem Einsatz gegen Demonstranten in Riesa




Videos von der Demonstration zeigen deutlich wie gewaltvoll einige Diensthundeführer:innen mit den „Polizeihunden“ umgehen. Einer der 

Hunde

 wurde von einem der Beamten am Hals gepackt und gegen eine Leitplanke und einen Demonstranten gedrückt. Dadurch sollte der Hund offensichtlich dazu gebracht werden, den Demonstranten zu beißen. Der Hund zeigte hierbei unübersehbare 

Anzeichen

 von massivem Stress, Überforderung und Meideverhalten. Ein weiterer völlig überdrehter Hund verbiss sich in den Arm eines anderen Polizisten.





https://www.instagram.com/p/DExO_Z1Mcvv/?hl=de





PETA erstattet Strafanzeige und fordert den Einsatz von Polizeihunden zu beenden




Dieser gewaltsame Umgang der Einsatzkräfte mit den Hunden ist tierschutzwidrig. Hunde sind nicht dazu da, für die Arbeit der Polizei ausgenutzt zu werden. Wir fordern deshalb, den Einsatz von Hunden bei der Polizei endlich einzustellen. Zudem erstatten wir bei der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden Zweigstelle Meißen Strafanzeige gegen den verantwortlichen Polizisten. Ferat Kocak, Abgeordneter der Linken war als parlamentarischer Beobachter vor Ort und hat sich bereit erklärt in der Strafanzeige als Zeuge aufzutreten.




„Die aktuellen Aufnahmen aus Riesa zeigen eindeutig, dass Hunde bei Polizeieinsätzen nichts zu suchen haben. Wir hoffen, dass es den betroffenen Hunden gut geht und sie keine körperlichen Schäden von dieser grausamen Behandlung davontragen. Die Psyche der Hunde leidet nach solch einem Einsatz ganz sicher. Hunde sind von Natur aus freundliche, soziale Lebewesen. Durch gewaltsame Trainingsmethoden werden sie bei der Polizei ‚scharf gemacht‘ und zu einer Art Waffe konditioniert – gegen ihren Willen. Ihre Treue zur Bezugsperson wird dabei schamlos ausgenutzt. Das ist unethisch und muss aufhören. Gute Polizeiarbeit kommt ohne Tiere aus. Dieser Einsatz in Riesa muss Konsequenzen haben.“

Jana Hoger, Tierpsychologin mit Schwerpunkt Hund und Fachreferentin bei PETA Deutschland




Gewalt gegen „Polizeihunde“ ist kein Einzelfall




Bei der Ausbildung von „Polizeihunden“ kommt es standardmäßig zur Anwendung von Gewalt. Durch Zwang und 

Schläge

 sollen die Hunde „scharf“ gemacht werden. Auch bei den Einsätzen kommt es immer wieder zu Vorfällen, bei denen Hunde verletzt und teilweise lebensbedrohlichen Situationen ausgesetzt werden. Die Tiere leiden unter extremem Stress, sodass auch unbeteiligte Menschen versehentlich von den Hunden angegriffen werden. Wenn die Hunde gerade nicht bei einem Einsatz sind, verbringen die eigentlich geselligen Tiere oftmals ihr Leben eingesperrt in Zwingern ohne ausreichend soziale Kontakte.




Sogenannte Polizeihunde können ihren natürlichen Bedürfnissen nicht nachgehen – sie werden für menschliche Zwecke ausgenutzt und instrumentalisiert. Die Hunde, die nicht mehr für die „Arbeit“ geeignet sind, erwartet oft eine ungewisse Zukunft.




Fordern Sie den Einsatz von Hunden zu beenden




Bitte unterstützen Sie uns, die Tierquälerei zu beenden und appellieren Sie in einer höflichen E-Mail an die folgenden verantwortlichen Stellen, den Einsatz von Hunden für den Polizeidienst in Sachsen abzuschaffen:







Sächsischer Innenminister Armin Schuster unter 

info@smi.sachsen.de




Beschwerdestelle der sächsischen Polizei unter 

beschwerdestelle-polizei@sk.sachsen.de

 oder 

info@sk.sachsen.de

PETA Deutschland e.V.

author: Maira Escardovelli
title: PEC da Segurança Pública leva “populismo penal” para a Constituição, aponta professor
content:
Apesar de representar um avanço na construção de uma estrutura institucional mais integrada entre as forças de segurança, a PEC da Segurança Pública, aprovada na última terça-feira, 3 de novembro, pelo Senado Federal, uma das principais apostas do governo federal, incorporou termos que reforçam o “populismo penal”, considerando a inserção na Constituição Federal do aumento de penas e a criação de novos tipos penais. A avaliação feita à 

Agência Pública

 é de Rodrigo Ghiringhelli de Azevedo, professor de Direito da Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul (PUCRS) e membro do Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública.
















Rodrigo de Azevedo aponta avanço institucional com a aprovação da emenda constitucional, mas vê trechos da proposta como “contraditórios” ao artigo 5° da Carta Magna




Na visão de Azevedo, os mecanismos de endurecimento penal previstos na Emenda à Constituição aprovada “reforçam um caminho que o Brasil já vem trilhando”, com uma “opinião pública punitivista” que demanda maior segurança. Para o professor, essas medidas, inclusive, são consideradas “contraditórias” em relação ao artigo 5º da Constituição, que estabelece a presunção de inocência e a individualização da pena, o que poderia resultar em um questionamento da própria constitucionalidade de dispositivos previstos no texto. O professor reconhece, porém, que essa “dimensão mais negativa” do texto não “inviabiliza os avanços do ponto de vista do arranjo institucional da segurança pública” conquistado com a emenda constitucional.




Foi em abril de 2025 que o governo federal, por meio do Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, enviou a primeira versão da PEC à Câmara dos Deputados. A matéria ganhou a relatoria do deputado federal Mendonça Filho (União Brasil-PE), que modificou o texto, adicionando normas mais punitivistas e retirando o objetivo inicial da matéria, que era o de coordenar a atuação das forças da União, estados e municípios, Polícia Federal, Polícia Rodoviária Federal, Polícias Estaduais e Guardas Municipais. À época, passou a tramitar o PL Antifacção, também enviado pela pasta da Justiça, que teve relatoria do deputado Guilherme Derrite (PP-SP).




“Nós já estávamos num momento eleitoral, em que deputados como o Derrite e o Mendonça Filho claramente estavam com o objetivo de se aproveitar da agenda parlamentar de reformas de matéria penal e de segurança pública para obter dividendos eleitorais. Por isso, eu digo que se estabeleceu uma competição entre eles para verificar qual era o mais duro no combate ao crime, do ponto de vista dessas medidas de aumento de pena, do enriquecimento da execução penal, que não tem uma eficácia comprovada”, explica Azevedo.




Para o professor, essas medidas defendidas pelos deputados, “pelo contrário, vão produzir um aumento do superencarceramento, da superlotação carcerária e, portanto, do ambiente propício para o crescimento das facções criminosas, mas que agradam a uma [parcela da] opinião pública”.




A aprovação da PEC foi colocada como condição para que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criasse o Ministério da Segurança Pública, uma de suas propostas de campanha desde a eleição de 2022. Sobre a nova pasta, Azevedo aprova a sua criação e afirma que ela terá um “papel político importante de coordenação da reestruturação” do que foi proposto na matéria.




Destaca, também, a importância de que a direção do Ministério tenha “capacidade política para construir com os governadores”, principalmente os de oposição, para que a questão não se torne um “entrave” para a implementação do sistema de segurança pública.




Entre as ações destacadas pelo professor que devem ser implementadas pelo novo Ministério estão a reestruturação da Polícia Federal (PF) e da Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF). Com a ampliação da estrutura da PRF permitida pelo novo texto, os governadores poderão acioná-la em casos de calamidade pública, como uma força de policiamento ostensivo, além de apoio para os sistemas penitenciários estaduais e na estrutura dos presídios federais de segurança máxima.




Quando o texto da PEC foi enviado ao Congresso Nacional pelo Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, houve muita resistência dos governadores e a matéria mudou na Câmara. Mas a proposta ainda prevê a integração da União com os Estados. Com a aprovação, como ficará essa articulação?




O texto original dava à União o papel de coordenação do Sistema Único de Segurança Pública (SUSP). Esse termo incomodou os governadores e isso foi uma contaminação do debate pelo contexto eleitoral, de polarização política. Essa contrariedade vem de governos ligados ao bolsonarismo, que queriam evitar justamente que o governo federal assumisse o papel de maior protagonismo. O que foi feito, e não acho que seja algo tão grave, foi tirar a expressão de “coordenação”, e se passou a trabalhar com a ideia de integração, no sentido de cooperação. Para que isso aconteça, o governo federal vai ter que manter o papel de indução de políticas, de financiamento, inclusive, das políticas de segurança, tanto dos municípios quanto dos estados. Isso, de alguma forma, é um papel de coordenação.




Por exemplo, se uma prefeitura quiser implementar políticas de prevenção ao crime e quiser obter recursos do Fundo Nacional de Segurança Pública, provavelmente vai passar por um encaminhamento de um projeto para que seja aprovado e para que o governo federal possa repassar esses recursos. Então, o governo federal vai ter que estabelecer os critérios para isso, como também os mecanismos de formação da segurança pública de uma forma mais unificada. A ideia, inclusive, é a criação de uma escola nacional de formação. Todas essas coisas passam por um papel mais importante e mais protagonista da União, e a PEC, embora não tenha dito expressamente que significa uma coordenação, na prática, não impede que a União desempenhe esse papel de principal ator, nesse contexto de uma maior integração entre União, estados e municípios.




O senhor vê possibilidade dessa coordenação acontecer efetivamente, considerando que em 2027 teremos a maioria dos estados governados por políticos de oposição ao governo federal e até de extrema direita?




É uma dificuldade na política, mas isso não impede uma atuação mais integrada. A ideia da PEC, do Sistema Único de Segurança Pública, é replicar o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). Tratando-se de um sistema único, de uma política pública, o que nós precisamos é de algo que não dependa de qual é o governo e de qual é a sua ideologia, que esteja pautado por princípios que sejam não de governo, mas de Estado. E que garantam aquilo que a PEC, de alguma forma, incorpora. [Incluindo] a necessidade de controle da atividade judicial, mas também de uma formação qualificada e toda uma série de outros requisitos que tanto estão na PEC quanto na lei do SUSP, que já estabeleceu quais seriam esses critérios e como se dá essa articulação entre os diferentes entes federativos.




A questão é colocar isso em funcionamento. Eu acredito que esse é o grande ponto positivo de fato da PEC: ela legitima a atuação mais protagonista do governo federal, prevê também o fortalecimento do Fundo Nacional de Segurança Pública e do Fundo Nacional Penitenciário. Essa é uma ferramenta de governança que vai permitir que mesmo que os governos sejam de oposição ao governo federal, eles acabem tendo tanto interesse quanto a necessidade de participarem das instâncias de governança do SUSP para que possam obter também esses recursos.




Como se daria essa integração, na prática?




A partir desse fortalecimento da integração e da coordenação dos esforços, é muito importante, por exemplo, que se passe a obrigar os estados a seguirem certos parâmetros entre os quais a utilização de câmeras corporais em atividades de policiamento ostensivo. Não haveria mais, digamos, como recusar a utilização. Pelo contrário, agora nós podemos estabelecer, como já tem acontecido, diretrizes nacionais de como essa utilização precisa ocorrer. A ideia de uma padronização de atuação é o que se pretende a partir dessa ideia de uma integração, onde o governo federal, evidentemente, vai cumprir um papel fundamental.




E é importante que seja um governo comprometido, inclusive com a democracia, porque, quando se trata de segurança pública e a atuação das polícias, esse é um elemento chave para que a gente possa reconhecer a existência de um Estado Democrático de Direito. Não é só votar e ser votado, também é como a segurança pública é exercida, como ela é colocada em prática e como se dá essa relação do cidadão com a polícia, que em critérios e padrões democráticos deve ocorrer sempre dentro da lei e dos direitos e garantias fundamentais.




Há alguma questão que a PEC deixou de lado e poderia ser fundamental para solucionar os problemas nacionais da segurança pública?




A PEC é o que era necessário para que haja um arranjo institucional mais articulado, mais integrado, mais coordenado. Parece-me que ela realmente representa um avanço. Mas, claro, toda lei não é algo que funcione de forma abstrata. Agora é preciso colocar em prática justamente todas essas reestruturações institucionais, começando pela criação do Ministério, passando pela organização da Polícia Federal, a articulação também dos municípios, que poderão converter as suas guardas municipais em polícias.




Pelo menos, agora, nós temos uma estrutura que permite que tudo isso seja colocado em prática. Todas as demais questões que a PEC incorporou, que eu acho que são muito negativas, elas apenas reforçam um caminho que o Brasil já vem trilhando, que é o do populismo penal, que é o aumento de penas, a utilização dessas reformas de forma demagógica, buscando ganhar apoio eleitoral. Isso passa tanto pela criação de novos tipos penais, quanto também de medidas, digamos, espetaculares, com algum apoio social, como redução da maioridade penal e a castração química de estupradores.




Coisas que a gente sabe que não tem nem evidências de que funcionem, mas que acabam agregando uma opinião pública punitivista, que demanda maior segurança. É muito negativo que os mecanismos de endurecimento penal estejam agora na Constituição. Eles são, na minha opinião, até bastante contraditórios em relação, por exemplo, ao artigo 5º da Constituição. Me parece até que se poderia questionar a própria constitucionalidade de algum desses dispositivos, o que é algo realmente muito complexo, porque há uma reforma constitucional que coloca na Constituição essas coisas. Mas, de qualquer maneira, digamos que essa dimensão mais negativa daquilo que foi aprovado, não inviabiliza os avanços do ponto de vista do arranjo institucional da segurança pública a partir de agora.




Como o senhor analisa a criação do Ministério de Segurança?




Eu sou um defensor da criação desse Ministério. Todas as políticas públicas de responsabilidade da União têm ministérios próprios. A segurança pública é uma política pública central na atual agenda política do Brasil, especialmente porque a criminalidade organizada atingiu níveis que precisam ser enfrentados de forma articulada pela União, Estados e Municípios. Então, esse é o principal papel desse Ministério.




Ele terá que ordenar os esforços do governo federal nessa área, o que envolve especialmente a reestruturação da Polícia Federal e da Polícia Rodoviária Federal, a Escola Nacional de Formação, a questão do sistema penitenciário que também vai ficar, pelo que tem sido discutido, no âmbito do Ministério da Segurança Pública. Isso envolve tanto o apoio para os sistemas penitenciários estaduais, quanto a garantia da estrutura dos presídios federais de segurança máxima.




Além disso, me parece muito importante também que o ministro [dessa nova pasta] seja alguém que, além de capacidade gerencial, tenha capacidade política para construir com os governadores. [Dessa forma] o fato de que há vários governadores de oposição não acabe sendo um entrave para que esse sistema de segurança pública seja implementado. É preciso ter capacidade de articulação com o órgão que reúne os secretários estaduais de segurança pública de todos os estados, os comandos e chefias de polícia.




A PEC prevê alguma mudança na atuação da Polícia Federal? 




Em relação à Polícia Federal, não há grandes alterações. A PEC torna explícito o fato de que a Polícia Federal tem como competência atuar em casos que envolvem crime organizado, facções criminais, milícias e que sejam de âmbito interestadual ou internacional, mas isso já estava na lei, agora coloca-se na Constituição.




E na Polícia Rodoviária Federal?




A alteração mais importante é a da Polícia Rodoviária Federal, porque ela amplia a sua competência de atuação para além das rodovias federais, chegando às hidrovias e ferrovias. Além disso, a PEC prevê que a PRF, a pedido dos governadores, possa ser convocada para atuar em contextos de calamidade e emergência. Ela consolida um papel de polícia ostensiva federal, o que a PF não é, já que ela é uma polícia judiciária e investigativa. Por essa ampliação, a Polícia Rodoviária Federal acaba assumindo um papel que é um pouco o papel que a Força Nacional de Segurança vinha cumprindo.

title: Di lêpirsîna fonê de Wezîra berê ya AKPî Kaya hat girtin
content:
Di çarçoveya lêpirsîna fonê de ku ji aliyê Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Stenbolê ve tê meşandin, Cîgira Serokê Giştî a berê ya AKPê û Wezîra berê Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya hat girtin. Hevjînê wê İlyas Kaya û Serokê berê yê Lijneya Bazara Pişkan (SPK) İbrahim Omer Gonul bi şertê kontrola adlî serbest hatin berdan.




Serdozgeriyê di lêpirsîna fonê de Kaya bi mebesta “endamtiya rêxistina ku ji bo sûckirinê hatî avakirin” û “li dijî derketina Qanûna Bazara Pişkan” bi daxwaza girtinê sewqî Dadgeha Aştî û Cezê ya Nobedar kiribû.



















Di çarçoveya lêpirsîna fonê de 14 kes hatin girtin




24 Îlon 2026










Dozgeriyê ji bo hevjînê Kayayê İlyas Kaya û Serokê berê yê SPKê İbrahim Omer Gonul jî daxwaza tedbîra kontrola adlî ya ku qedexeya derketina derveyî welat û erka îmzeyê dihewîne kiribû.




Kesên navborî di saetên sibehê yên 5ê Mijdarê de li Dadgeha Stenbolê cara duyemîn weke gumanbar îfade dan. Piştî karûbarên dozgeriyê yên ku derdora saet 20.00an de bi dawî bûn, di saet 22.40an de ji bo Fatma Betul Sayan Kayayê daxwaza girtinê hat kirin.




163 milyon lîre veberhênan, zêdetirî 2 milyar lîreyî dahata firotinê




Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya

 û hevjînê wê İlyas Kaya piştî ku di Nîsana 2026an de veberhênanî li pişken Ozata Denizcilikê kiribûn, di Mijdarê de jî tam beriya ku krîza fonê derkeve holê, bi firotina van pişkan ketibûn rojevê.




Li gorî daneyên darayî yên ku di çarçoveya lêpirsînê de ji bo raya giştî hatine parvekirin, 

Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya

 û hevjînê wê İlyas Kaya bi tevahî 163 milyon û 46 hezar lîre li pişkên Ozatayê Denizcilikê razandibûn û piştî nêzîkî çar mehan ev hîse ango pişk bi buhayê 2 milyar û 170 milyon lîreyî ji dest derxistibûn. Cudahiya di navbera her du kiryaran de nêzîkî 2 milyar lîreyî bû.



















Di lêpirsîna fonan de 7 kes hatin desteserkirin




28 Îlon 2026










Piştî ku ev îdia di raya giştî de bûn rojev, Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya ji erka xwe ya Cîgirya Serokê Giştî ê AKPê vekişiyabû.




Serdozgeriyê di 29ê Îlonê de ji bo meqamên peywendîdar serlêdan kiribû da ku mal û milkên jin û mêrên Kayayê bên cemidandin. Paşê nêzîkî 1 milyar û 860 milyon lîre ji wê dahata ku bi dest xistibûn, derbasî hesabê ku ji aliyê Fona Sîgorteya Hesabên Tesarûfê (TMSF) ve hatibû diyarkirin kiribûn. Hatibû ragihandin ku pereye sereke û faîza nêzîkî 310 milyon lîreyî nehatiye vegerandin.




Di lêpirsînê de 433 gumanbar hene




Di dosyeya ku ji aliyê Buroya Lêpirsîna Sûcên Fihêlkirin û Finansmana Terorê ya Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Stenbolê ve tê meşandin de, gelek danûstendinên bazara pişkan û şîrketên têkildar tên lêkolînkirin.




Li gorî amarên ku Wezîrê Dadê Akın Gurlek di 3yê Mijdarê de eşkere kirin, di lêpirsînê de 433 gumanbar cih digirin. Ji van kesan 112 kes girtî ne, 186 kes jî bi şertê kontrola adlî hatine berdan. 38 kesên ku biryara girtina wan heye jî fîrar in.

author: groundxero
title: Bernie Sanders: Winning the Midterms Is Not Enough. Here’s What We Must Do
content:
The American people understand that the economy today is rigged and that we cannot continue the ‘same old, same old’ establishment politics and establishment policies.




 




Bernie Sanders




Nov 05, 2026




Common Dreams




 




On Tuesday, Trump told us to vote as if he were on the ballot. And that is exactly what the American people did.




 




Together, we stood up to 

authoritarianism

 and a president who does not believe in the Constitution or the 

rule of law

. And we won.




 




With Democratic control over the Senate and the House, we will now—finally—be able to hold 

Donald Trump

 accountable.




 




The American people have had enough. They are demanding real change and bold policies that will dramatically improve their lives.




 




That is a big deal. But as important as it is, it is not enough. We have got to do more.




 




Whether we like it or not, we are living in an unprecedented moment in American history where our country faces extraordinary crises. We cannot and must not run away from them when Democrats assume power in January.




 




These crises must be dealt with.




 




It is no secret that in the 

United States

 and all over the world, people are giving up on 

democracy

. Now, why is that?




 




And the answer is that—all over the world, not just in America—working families are struggling to put food on the table and pay for basic necessities while the very richest people become much richer. And, throughout our country and in many other countries, ordinary people are saying, ‘Does their government even know that they exist?’ Or are elected officials too busy worrying about the needs of the rich and the powerful?




 




This is an American issue, but, in fact, an international issue.




 




And in my view, the American people have had enough. They are demanding real change and bold policies that will dramatically improve their lives.




 




In the richest country on Earth, the American people want a government that stands for working families, not billionaire campaign contributors. And that is not just 

Bernie Sanders

 talking.




 




According to a recent AP poll, 80% of registered voters want either “complete and total upheaval” or “substantial change” in how this country is run. And that includes 97% of Democrats, 90% of independents, and 58% of 

Republicans

.




 




In other words, the American people understand that the economy today is rigged and that we cannot continue the ‘same old, same old’ establishment politics and establishment policies.




 




The American people want change. Real change. And the midterm election confirms just that.




 




Let me give you some examples of what I mean and the issues that we have got to deal with.




 




In our country today, income and 

wealth inequality

 has reached unprecedented levels. The top 1% now owns more wealth than the bottom 93%. One man, 

Elon Musk

, owns more wealth than the bottom 53% of American households. In my view, that is insane. And I think that’s how most Americans feel.




 




Democrats, when they gain control, in January, of the House and the Senate, cannot ignore this grotesque 

inequality

. We must take on the greed of the very, very rich and their incredible wealth.




 




We must enact a 5% wealth tax on billionaires so that we can provide every working-class family in the country, a family of four, with a $12,000 direct payment.




 




And that means a Democratic Congress must pass a wealth tax on billionaires.




 




At a time when billionaires pay a lower effective tax rate than truck drivers or nurses, we must enact a 5% wealth tax on billionaires so that we can provide every working-class family in the country, a family of four, with a $12,000 direct payment. In other words, if you’re a working-class family of four, that’s $3,000 for every man, woman, and child—$12,000.




 




Furthermore, with that tax on billionaires, we can build 7 million units of low-income and 

affordable housing

, we can make public colleges and universities tuition-free, and we can provide universal free child care for 13 million 

children

. That is what a wealth tax on billionaires can do.




 




But taxing the oligarchs means more than just taking on their wealth. 

It means ending their stranglehold over our political system.




 




Elon Musk

 and his billionaire friends have poured a record-breaking $2 billion into the recent election. That is absurd.




 




The American people want Congress to overturn 

Citizens United

, abolish 

super PACs

, and establish public funding of elections. Democracy must mean one person, one vote, not billionaires buying elections.




 




But it’s not just massive income and wealth inequality that we have to deal with or a corrupt 

campaign finance

 system.




 




In America today—as everybody knows, and I get the same response wherever I go in this country—everybody understands that our 

healthcare

 system is broken. It is dysfunctional. And it is wildly expensive.




 




We spend almost twice as much per person on healthcare as any other major country. Yet, despite that huge expenditure, more than 90 million Americans are uninsured or underinsured. Over half a million people go bankrupt each year because of medical debt. We pay the highest prescription 

drug prices

 in the world. And tragically, more than 60,000 Americans die unnecessarily every year because they cannot afford medical care.




 




How cruel is that?




 




Yes, we must repeal the $1 trillion in cuts Trump made to 

Medicaid

 and the 

Affordable Care Act

 to prevent 15 million Americans from losing their healthcare. Yes, we must restore ACA tax credits to stop the outrageous premium spikes for 20 million Americans, but that is nowhere near enough. Healthcare must be considered as a human right, not a privilege. That means passing 

Medicare for all

 legislation now supported by 66% of the American people.




 




As an immediate first step, Democrats must lower the 

Medicare

 eligibility age from 65 down to 55, expand Medicare to cover dental, vision, and hearing, and guarantee universal healthcare coverage for every child from birth through age 19. All of this can be accomplished with 51 votes in the Senate, through the reconciliation process.




 




But it’s not just income and wealth inequality that we have to deal with, or a corrupt campaign finance system or a dysfunctional healthcare system. We must deal with artificial intelligence—the most transformational 

technology

 in the history of humanity.




 




In America today, 

big tech

 oligarchs are spending trillions of dollars on 

artificial intelligence

 and robotics with virtually no regulation.




 




Democrats must enact a national moratorium on AI data centers, must pause advanced AI development and ban superintelligence.




 




This revolutionary technology will transform the lives of every man, woman, and child in our country and around the world. Left unchecked, AI and robotics will destroy tens of millions of jobs, devastate our children’s mental health, eviscerate our 

privacy

 rights, drive up electricity rates, strain 

water

 supplies, and transform warfare.




 




If AI becomes smarter than human beings and escapes human control, it will also pose an existential threat to the very existence of humanity. We cannot allow a handful of big tech billionaires to become even richer and more powerful by ramming this dangerous technology down our throats.




 




Democrats must enact a national moratorium on AI data centers, must pause advanced AI development and ban superintelligence.




 




And by the way, I might mention that in the election, in dozens of communities throughout our country, citizens voted for a moratorium on the construction of data centers. In other words, a moratorium on data centers is exactly what the American people want.




 




But my friends, it is not just 

oligarchy

, a corrupt campaign finance system, a broken healthcare system, and uncontrolled AI.




 




In America today, while the very rich get richer, 60% of our people live paycheck to paycheck and millions work long, long hours for incredibly low wages. That must change.




 




A job must lift people out of 

poverty

, not keep them in it.




 




The $7.25-an-hour federal 

minimum wage

 is a 

starvation

 wage. Democrats must raise it to a living wage of at least $20-an-hour and make it easier for 

workers

 to form 

unions

 by passing the PRO Act. A job must lift people out of poverty, not keep them in it.




 




Further, in our country today, one-third of our seniors are struggling economically, and more than 20% are trying to survive on less than $15,000 a year. Nearly half of older Americans have no retirement savings and no idea how they will retire with a shred of dignity. Meanwhile, Elon Musk pays the same amount into 

Social Security

 as someone earning $184,600 a year. That is absurd.




 




By applying the Social Security payroll tax to all income above $250,000, including capital gains and dividends, we could increase benefits by $2,400 a year, lift millions of seniors out of poverty, improve cost of living adjustments, and keep Social Security solvent for generations without raising taxes on the bottom 91% of Americans.




 




We must also restore the traditional pension plans corporate America took away so that every worker can count on a guaranteed income in retirement.




 




That is what a Democratic Congress must do.




 




Let me be clear. In America today, we spend more on the military than the next six nations combined. Despite massive waste, fraud, and abuse, the 

Pentagon

 has repeatedly failed independent audits and cannot account for trillions of dollars in spending. Adding insult to injury, Trump has dragged us into an illegal and unconstitutional war in Iran that will cost hundreds of billions of dollars.




 




We must end this disastrous war.




 




We must cut off all funding for the genocidal government in Israel.




 




And we must substantially reduce 

military spending

.




 




Instead of pouring $1.1 trillion into a bloated Pentagon and never-ending wars, a Democratic Congress must build the best public education system in the world with no teacher earning less than $60,000 a year.




 




We are fighting to give hope to the American people—to allow them to understand that their government can work for them, can address the crises that they face, and will pay attention to the needs of the men, women and children in our country who are struggling, and not just the very, very wealthy campaign contributors.




 




And let me touch on one more subject that Democrats must deal with.




 




Since Trump took office, ICE agents have shot American citizens in cold blood, have broken down doors to arrest people, and have sent five-year-old children to detention centers. These actions are not only immoral and disgraceful, they are unconstitutional.




 




Democrats must immediately rein in the $75 billion Republicans gave Trump to fund his domestic army. Instead of ICE agents terrorizing communities throughout the country, we must finally move to comprehensive 

immigration

 reform and a path toward citizenship for the undocumented.




 




Let’s be clear: All of the policies I have just discussed—and more that I have not mentioned—are not radical.




 




They are precisely what a strong majority of the American people want.




 




So we are in a moment in American history where a lot of folks are losing faith in democracy. They are struggling every day just to stay alive while, at the same time, billionaires have more money than they can spend in a thousand lifetimes and are getting richer and richer all of the time.




 




What we are talking about now is not only the need to fight for economic justice.




 




We are fighting to give hope to the American people—to allow them to understand that their government can work for them, can address the crises that they face, and will pay attention to the needs of the men, women and children in our country who are struggling, and not just the very, very wealthy campaign contributors.




 




That is, in my view, what Democrats have got to do when they assume power in January.




 




We can do it. We must do it.




 




And I look forward to working with all of you to make sure that it happens.




 







Bernie Sanders

 (I-Vt.) was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2006 after serving 16 years in the House of Representatives. Sanders ran to become the Democratic Party presidential nominee in both 2016 and 2020 and remains the longest-serving independent member of Congress in American history.




 




This article is republished from 

Common Dreams

 under a Creative Commons license. Read the original 

article

title: Lilia Folt - On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness
content:
Author

: Lilia Folt

Title

: On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness

Date

: September 27

th

, 2026

Notes

: Originally published in 

Dissonant Times

, a grassroots journalism and counter-info project from the Willamette Valley of Oregon.

Source

: Dissonant Times, Retrieved on 11/5/2026 from https://dissonanttimes.org/anarchic-reflections-on-anti-surveillance-mindfulness/




 Surveillance has become a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in America. Cameras watch us from businesses and homes, from bus stops, from cars, from traffic lights. Bluetooth trackers ping our smartphones as we pass by, mapping our movements. The phones themselves illuminate our paths through society by continuously pinging cell towers, providing our cell providers our location data, information that is only a subpoena away, if that. In countless ways, we’ve been made to both passively accept and actively participate in our own surveillance. This vast complex of surveillance doesn’t just gather information about us, it also shapes our behaviors, temperaments, and ways of moving through the world. Surveillance molds us down to the level of subjective, sensory, embodied experience. At that same level we can begin to shake off its hold on us and reclaim ourselves. For that, I am offering a practice I’m calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness,” a form of walking meditation that builds mindful awareness of surveillance cameras. This practice, if taken up consistently, opens onto a broader project of transforming our relationship to the places we live in, a project that itself naturally blossoms into materially transforming public space, as self expands to world in the moment-by-moment practice of mindfulness. 




Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness




 Readers may or may not be familiar with the Panopticon. Designed by 18

th

 century English liberal Jeremy Bentham, the Panopticon was a model for an institutional building designed so that a single prison guard can watch all the inmates from a central watch tower. The inmates, meanwhile, cannot tell whether or not they are being watched, and therefore could be watched at any moment. To quote Bentham: 







 The more constantly the persons to be inspected are under the eyes of the persons who should inspect them, the more perfectly will the purpose of the establishment have been attained. (...) This being impossible, the next thing to be wished for is, that, at every instant, seeing reason to believe as much, and not being able to satisfy himself to the contrary, he should 

conceive

 himself to be so. 







 A lot has changed since the 1700’s, but the disciplinary paradigm of surveillance has remained the same. If anything, it has expanded beyond specific institutions to encompass much of society. 




 There are cameras everywhere, and we are being watched, and while we are aware of this, we tend to see it as normal and unremarkable, an inevitability we must resign ourselves to. Consciousness of being surveilled fades into the background, becoming a constant assumption of being watched that we internalize. This surveillance consciousness is running us all the more effectively because it is not distinct, because it is 

un

conscious. That is why the first step in anti-surveillance mindfulness is becoming conscious of surveillance. 







 Mindfulness is at the same time a means and an end, the seed and the fruit. When we practice mindfulness in order to build up concentration, mindfulness is a seed. But mindfulness itself is the life of awareness: the presence of mindfulness means the presence of life, and therefore mindfulness is also the fruit. — Thích Nhất Hạnh, 

The Miracle of Mindfulness







 “Mindfulness” is a practice originating in various sects of Buddhism. The mindfulness practices and concepts I’m familiar with have largely been within the school of Zen Buddhism

[1]

. 




 The classic mindfulness practice is watching the breath, and that is a great starting point. Take a breath in, the air entering through your nose, your stomach and chest softly expanding as you inhale. Then exhale through the mouth, the stomach and chest settling back down, gently exhaling for a little longer than your inhale. Repeat this several times, deepening your breaths slightly. From there, start to check in with your body. Notice how it feels to be sitting down, or to be standing if you are standing; notice how it feels to be holding this piece of paper, holding your phone, or looking at your computer, however it is that you are reading this. 




 The practice I am calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness” is a walking meditation, or a meditation performed however it is you get around. While walking or rolling on the sidewalk, first get in touch with your breath, as above. Then, begin to notice your surroundings: the buildings, the sky, the trees, the people, the sounds. Make note of the cameras that you see while walking around, on businesses, or Ring cameras on houses, cameras too on bus stops. Tesla cars all have cameras. Look at what angles these cameras are pointed in, if you can figure out where they’re pointing—on some of the dome-shaped cameras, this isn’t clear. Notice when you are in view of these various cameras; notice when you are not in view of cameras. 




 With this practice, surveillance goes from being a taken-for-granted, constant background of your subjectivity, to a distinct phenomenon that you are consciously aware of. When it fades into the background, it becomes a part of you—putting it into your conscious awareness makes it once again separate from you and your being.
