title: K. C. Sinclair - Proudhon, Slavery, and the American Civil War
content:
Author

: K. C. Sinclair

Title

: Proudhon, Slavery, and the American Civil War

Date

: November 2026

Source

: Retrieved on November 5, 2026 from 

historykeepshappening.wordpress.com




 In a passing remark made by the renowned historian of anarchism, Paul Avrich, in his 1988 book, 

Anarchist Portraits

 (pg.20), we are told that the infamous French anarchist, Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, did not support the side of the North (otherwise known as the Union) in the American Civil War. 




 Avrich, uncharacteristically, provided no source for this, as if it was already common knowledge, neglecting to clarify whether Proudhon opposed both sides of the war, or perhaps worse, supported the South. He also left us hanging as to whether he’d gleaned this information from Proudhon’s own words in French, from secondary sources in English, or from both. Not much of Proudhon’s work had been translated into English at the time, but perhaps Avrich accessed the French documentation. The subject in the chapter in question was not Proudhon but instead a passionate supporter of the North, the Russian anarchist Mikhail Bakunin, and Proudhon was only mentioned as a point of contrast, so perhaps this is the simplest explanation for Avrich’s failure to provide a citation. 




 Whether Avrich knew it or not, the subject of Proudhon’s position on the war had already been addressed by the presumably non-anarchist musician and writer, Thomas A. Sancton, in his 1979 academic journal article, 

The Myth of French Worker Support

 

for the North in the American Civil War

.

 Decades later, in 2021, Sancton greatly expanded that article with his book, 

Sweet Land of Liberty: America in the Mind of the French Left, 1848-1871

. 




 In the 1979 article, Sancton referenced both published works and private letters of Proudhon’s in order to show that if the French anarchist had opposed both sides of the war, for different reasons, he still more strongly opposed the North than the South. Sancton, unfortunately quoted Proudhon out of chronological order and without translation, so I have rearranged and translated those quotes for the purposes of this article. 




 Proudhon, in a September 1862 letter to Gustave Chaudey asked, “we have no faith in the North’s philanthropy; we do not accept that the Federal Constitution prevents secession; …. what’s more, the forces of the North are suffering one setback after another; England, Belgium, and France — consumed by poverty — call for cotton; and if the imperial [French] government, by a stroke of good luck links the two issues of Mexico and the Confederates, restoring relations between Europe and New Orleans, will you still attack it on that front?” 




 Proudhon refers here to the 

Second Franco-Mexican War

. Imperialist France had invaded Mexico in early 1862, a few months after the American Civil War began. 




 Sancton doesn’t provide his own analysis of this particular quote beyond noting that it proves that Proudhon’s anti-Yankee sentiment was not isolated to his published works. But, for our part, we can note that Proudhon, for an anarchist, sounds oddly defensive about both the government of the American secessionists and that of his own French Empire, particularly given that the defense of slavery was very much the South’s reason for seccession. 




 Proudhon, in a letter to (Lucien?) Jottrand in October of 1864, wrote, “I am not, I admit, a friend of the Anglo-Saxons, and I believe that few people are fond of them. Also, I deplored the policy of our emperor, who could have, if he had wanted… obtained from the South the promise of emancipation for the blacks, and intervening then as an interested party in the present war, would have, at the time I am writing to you, brought those in the North to their senses.” 




 Again, Sancton does not comment on the specifics of Proudhon’s words here, only elaborating to the extent of pointing out that Proudhon had some influence on the French labour movement, even if he was not its official spokesman. We, on the other hand, can note that Proudhon’s opposition to the North is clearly stronger than his opposition to the South, and that he was strangely naive about the South’s willingness to part with slavery. 




 In his 1865 book, 

On the Political Capacity of the Working Classes

,

 Proudhon even commented publicly on the war. Sancton uses an extended quotation from that book, the translation here being taken from the one done by Shawn P. Wilbur, while the truncations are Sancton’s. 




 “As I write,” Proudhon explained, “[…] the United States of the North also claims to retain in the Union, by force, the United States of the South, calling them traitors and rebels, neither more nor less than if the old Union were a monarchy and Mr. Lincoln an emperor. It is clear, however […] leaving aside the question of slavery, the war waged against the South by the North is unjust […] in which case the Americans will do well to erase from their platforms in the future the words of political liberty, republic, democracy, confederation and even Union. Already they are beginning to deny on the other side of the Atlantic the rights of States, which means the federative principle […]” 




 Once more, Sancton provides no commentary, but we can see that Proudhon’s naivety reached truly astonishing heights as he preposterously abstracted away from the question of slavery and even accused the North of having started the war, despite the South having both seceded and fired first, and the North not making moves to abolish slavery until the war was well underway. Incredibly, in Proudhon’s formulation, states’ rights and the abstract federative principle take precedence over the rights of enslaved people. Naturally, he does not even bother trying to explain how a people can properly exercise their right to federation while still being enslaved by others. 




...

content:

Subtitle

: An interview by Millennials are Killing Capitalism

Welcome to Millennials Are Killing Capitalism. This is Jay. In this episode we had the rare opportunity to interview a spokesperson from a direct action group that has targeted Toll Holdings, in australia. The campaign has engaged in a range of sabotage, vandalism, and disruptive actions, including sledgehammering windows, cutting internet cables, blockading roads and in an international port entrance, they have also slashed lines and cut valves to disable vehicles, covered facilities inside and out with paint and foul liquids, and sabotaged infrastructure such as signal boxes used by Toll. In this discussion we asked them about the development of the antizionist movement in australia after October 7

th

 

2023, and asked about how their group settled on its target, prepared their campaign, and selected the tactics they wanted to use in it. As our guest raises the spirit of adventure they see as necessary to take meaningful direct action to confront the genocidal war machine, I also asked them what they think about allegations of adventurism that can be levied from the left at those who take such action. Because this campaign is heavily under threat by the State, we agreed to some additional security measures in this conversation. The voice you hear is not the actual voice of the person we interviewed; the original interview was transcribed and then converted to audio using text-to-voice generator. Just as an editorial disclaimer from me amid heightened attacks on various forms of speech, I just want to say as a platform we are not advocating that people engage in any form of illegal activity. Having said that we do understand the greatest crime that humanity has recognized, the crime of genocide, is still ongoing. There are moral, ethical, and even legal imperatives that people are engaging in order to try to stop that crime from continuing to unfold. This interview is to hear from those who are taking direct action to hold genocide and War crimes. These actions have been threatened with severe repression, and many who take these forms of action do face repression. We see it as a journalistic responsibility to ensure that people hear from those who are willing to take action to stop genocide. We know that their voices will be marginalized by most media platforms out there. It is also very important that people show up and support political prisoners if we are ever to build a movement that is capable of confronting the machinery of genocide and imperialism. We will include links to the Death to Toll campaign website, and other interviews with their spokespeople in the show description.










First of all welcome to Millennials are Killing Capitalism, it’s great that we are able to do this interview to talk about the work that you’re doing in so-called australia, or that region in the world. It’s not an area that we get to cover as often as we should, and that’s typical of us US-brained people that you know, we tend to be quite US-centric. Or maybe focusing on areas like Palestine, and Iran, and Lebanon, where we’ve seen some of the hot elements of this war in its most direct forms. But we do want to highlight different ways that people in different places are resisting the genocide of Palestinians, and this broader campaign to undermine the sovereignty of the entire West Asian region as we see it. And your campaign is one that was brought to my attention by some friends of the platform. And it’s really important that people are able to hear from you.




 A: Thanks so much. Really happy to be here. 




So to start, could you talk a little bit about the anti-zionist or pro-Palestine movement in so-called australia. Obviously I’m saying so-called because like the United States, Australia is another settler colony historically. Give me some of the lay of the land, what that has looked like over the last however many years you want — and share what inspired this campaign we are discussing today.




 A: Yeah, so there’s obviously been activism in solidarity with Palestine for a long time in Australia, but I would say that post-Al Aqsa Flood, there was this moment of intensity where, for a minute, it felt like everything changed. And it felt like things had changed in a bad way because of the horror of the genocide and the urgency that that engendered. But I think that one thing that also changed was the sense that, like, honour and agency had been returned to colonized people, in a way. You’d be familiar with the sort of humanitarian thing of like, all these poor people, they’re suffering but the idea of colonized people fighting back. Of colonizers running for their lives. And of the possibilities of what this world can look like just being blown open, like, suddenly I felt and I think many others felt that this was something which was opened up by Al Aqsa Flood. And of course, when possibilities are opened up, you know, the possibility of resistance is opened up. And then at the same time, where you have resistance you have counter-insurgency. 




...

author: CNT Villaverde Alto - Comarcal Sur de Madrid
title: 7 de noviembre: De la Huelga Indefinida a la Huelga General
content:
El próximo 

7 de noviembre

, Villaverde se convertirá en el punto de encuentro de las luchas que nos llevan atravesando estas semanas. A través del barrio, caminaremos de la Huelga Indefinida a la Huelga General de la mano de compañeras y amigas.




Arrancaremos el día, a las 

12:30

, de la mano del Comité de Huelga de Villaverde, el 

espacio unitario

 en el que vecinas y organizaciones de la zona estamos trabajando desde el común para construir la Huelga General del 11, con un pasacalles que recorrerá el barrio, 

partiendo del parque El Cruce para llegar a la Plaza de Ágata

, justo en frente del Ateneo Libertario de Villaverde.




Será allí, en la que es nuestra casa, donde el Sindicato abrirá sus puertas para continuar con la jornada. A las 

15:00

, la 

Sección Sindical de CNT Educación Pública CAM

 habrá preparado una gran paellada popular, con el objetivo de 

destinar sus beneficios a la caja de resistencia

 que sostiene su Huelga Indefinida. Y es que, precisamente, de esta lucha histórica emprendida ya hace cuatro semanas nos hablarán también las compañeras aprovechando el espacio colectivo: las que comen juntas, conspiran juntas. Será la oportunidad para aprender, de primera mano, acerca de la experiencia de organización colectiva y desde la base, de lucha y resistencia que están llevando a cabo las compañeras.




Después, extenderemos el hilo colectivo que en la jornada conectará la Huelga Indefinida con la Huelga General para continuar construyendo entre todas una jornada verdaderamente combativa para pararlo todo. Las compas del Comité de Huelga de Villaverde organizarán, a las 

17:00

, también en el Ateneo Libertario de Villaverde, un 

taller de pancartas

 con el que extender la agitación del 11N.




Y, tras esto, como broche de oro, cerraremos las jornadas con una fiesta a cargo de la 

Plataforma Queremos FP

, otra de las organizaciones convocantes de la Huelga Indefinida de Educación en la CAM en la que nuestro Sindicato tiene representación. Las compañeras de FP organizarán una 

pinchada de DJ a partir de las 19:00

, acompañada de 

bebida y picoteo

 con el objetivo de seguir reforzando la herramienta de lucha que es la caja de resistencia.




Con estas jornadas, CNT Comarcal Sur y las organizaciones convocantes aspiramos a 

tejer un espacio colectivo

 que estreche lazos entre las luchas que estamos emprendiendo. Esperamos que se conviertan en un momento de trabajo y de ocio militante, de acumulación de fuerzas para las convocatorias inminentes, así como de refuerzo para las que ya están en marcha. 

Esperamos contar con vecinas, afiliadas, militantes y amigas

; extender la voz y la agitación para salir aún más fortalecidas.




Porque sola no puedes, pero con compañeras sí. El próximo 7 de noviembre nos encontraremos con la convicción de que 

vamos a ganar la Huelga Indefinida

 y con la determinación de que 

el 11N se convierta en un día histórico

 para la lucha de nuestra clase.




¡Que no falte nadie!

author: CNT Colmenar Viejo
title: 8 de noviembre. Cuando Sale el Sol
content:
Ópera prima de nuestra compañera Elena Martínez, se 

preestreno en el Centro de Humanidades en el municipio de la Cabrera

 los días 8 y 9 de enero de 2016 como homenaje a la sierra de Madrid y posteriormente se 

estrenó en Madrid

 en el marco del 

Festival Ellas Crean

. Cuando Sale el Sol es un documental colaborativo sobre la dramática realidad de los desahucios.




Durante su recorrido entre 2016 y 2017, fue seleccionado en círculos alternativos como el Teatro del Barrio, en Alternativa Film Festival de Medellín y en el Festival de Málaga fuera de la selección oficial, además de distintos municipios de la sierra norte de Madrid.




Entre los años 2008 y 2014 se produjeron en España más de 500.000 desalojos. En un contexto social de casi cinco millones de personas sin trabajo, las Plataformas de Afectados por la Hipoteca, el movimiento 15M y la propia sociedad civil, consiguieron parar numerosos desahucios y organizar alternativas reales de cambio.




Cuando Sale el Sol pone el acento en las emociones y la lucha de personas y colectivos, traduciéndose en un documental colectivo que construye utopías y rinde homenaje a la solidaridad y al apoyo mutuo. Es también la suma de las miradas de periodistas independientes cuyo trabajo libre y honesto defiende la libertad de expresión, el derecho a la información y a una vivienda digna para todas.




Este próximo 

domingo 8 de noviembre

, asistiremos a la 

concentración organizada por la PAH SN (Plataforma de Afectadas de la Sierra Norte de Madrid)

 convocada 

a las 12 h en la Plaza del Pueblo de Colmenar Viejo

.




Después nos vamos a  juntar 

en el local del sindicato CNT Colmenar Viejo a las 14:30 h para una comida popular (apúntate escribiendo a 

colmenarviejo@cnt.es

 antes del viernes), y sobre las 17 h se proyectará el documental

 

Cuando Sale el Sol.

 Aunque se refiere a los desahucios de hipoteca de la época, sigue estando por desgracia de rabiosa actualidad siendo un grito por el derecho a la vivienda, señalando la increíble herramienta que supone la solidaridad y el apoyo mutuo para conquistar imposibles.

Cuando Sale el Sol

Sindicato de Colmenar Viejo

.

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Trump out! | Progressive groups launch 12 days of protest
content:
Photo by Emman Capones/Pinoy Weekly

We don’t want this lunatic to come to our country. He is a mass murderer who has initiated wars around the world, led by and benefiting the US.

Progressive groups launch 12 days of protest as the visit of US President Donald Trump to the Philippines approaches.

“Trump is not welcome here in the Philippines, he is not welcome anywhere in the world,” said International League of Peoples’ Struggles-Philippines Secretary General Arnold Padilla in a press conference on Wednesday, November 4.

Trump is scheduled to visit the Philippines on November 16 to sign the Pax Silica initiative also in time for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

“Under the banner of Trump Out, we shall hold daily actions ranging from rallies, indoor assemblies, public forums, pickets, concerts, teach-ins, camp-outs, and vigils aimed to express the Filipino people’s strong objection to Trump’s visit,” Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) Chairperson Teddy Casiño said.

Casiño added in Filipino, “Trump represents the largest imperialist power, which sows war, terror, oppression, and plunder across the world. This includes military aggression against Iran, support for genocide, the imposition of economic sanctions and intervention in Venezuela, Cuba, and other countries; military escalation in the Philippines and across the Asia-Pacific; and brutal repression of immigrants and critics within his own country.”

For Ana Marie Nemenzo of the Network Opposed to Pax Silica, Trump should be declared as persona non grata and barred from entering the country.

“We don’t want this lunatic to come to our country. He is a mass murderer who has initiated wars around the world, led by and benefiting the US. This shows that imperialism remains very much alive and must be opposed because it poses a major threat to the planet and endangers the lives of ordinary people around the world,” she added.

Nemenzo said the Philippines has not been truly free. She said since the so-called independence in 1946, the Americans have kept the Philippines tied to the U.S. economy. She also criticized the presence of soldiers and its equipment in the country and urged the public to join the movement to drive U.S. military forces out of the country.

Nemenzo also added that Pax Silica will only further tie the Philippines “to an economic framework that primarily benefits powerful countries seeking access to our critical resources.”

“We know that the Philippines is among the most vulnerable countries. The loss of people’s livelihoods must be a paramount concern,” she added, saying that her organization, Women’s Health is one in the campaign against Pax Silica.

For Pastor Allan Sarte, secretary general of Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association, Trump is the number one enabler of (then Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu that killed 70,000 citizens of Gaza, more than 20,000 of which are children. “We cannot in conscience welcome Trump in the Philippines,” he said.

Not only the Filipinos are rejecting Trump, Bayan said the glaring defeat of Trump’s party in the U.S. midterm elections is a powerful boost to the Trump Out campaign.

“The Democratic Party’s landslide victory, wresting control of both Houses of Congress and defeating Republicans even in traditional strongholds like Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina, is a resounding repudiation of Trump and his rule,” the group said in a statement.

The group said the results of the election is a reflection of the growing disgust and rejection by the American people of Trump’s corrupt, authoritarian, war mongering, racist, anti-immigrant and over all anti-people policies. “They show that even in his own country, Trump faces mounting opposition to his disastrous leadership,” Bayan said.

The group expressed their solidarity with the American people who are resisting Trump’s attacks on their democratic rights, livelihoods, and welfare.

“They see through his collusion with his big corporate backers to enrich himself. They oppose his war on Iran and belligerence towards other countries’ sovereignty,” Bayan said. (RVO)

author: Unknown
title: Ji ber nûçeya girtina rojnameger Yelis Ayazê, li dijî bianetê lêpirsîn hat vekirin
content:
Rêvebirê Karên Nivîsan ê Berpirsiyar ê bianetê Vecih Cuzdan, ji ber nûçeya ku di 18ê Gulana 2026an de li ser girtina rojnamevan Yelis Ayazê hatibû weşandin, di çarçoveya lêpirsîna ku ji aliyê Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Aydinê ve tê meşandin de duh li Stenbolê îfade da.




Lêpirsîn li ser giliya Parlementera AKPê ya Aydinê Seda Saribaşê hatiye destpêkirin ku navê wê di nûçeyê de derbas dibû.




Cuzdan tevî parêzera xwe Deniz Yazgan çû Amîriya Buroya Ewlehiyê ya Rêvebiriya Emniyeta Navçeya Maltepeyê.




Cuzdan di çarçoveya xala 217/A ya Qanûna Cezayê Tirkan(TCK) de bi sûcê “

bi zanayî agahiyên xapînok di nav gel de belav kiriye

” û di çarçoveya xala 123an a TCKê de bi sûcê “

aramiya kesan têk daye

” hat tohmetbarkirin.




Hat hînbûn ku di çarçoveya lêpirsînê de dê Rêveberê Giştî ê Weşanê ê bianetê Murat İnceoglu jî îfadeyê bide.




Cuzdan: Nûçe li ser girtina rojnamevanekê ye




Cuzdan sûcdarî qebûl nekirin û diyar kir ku nûçeyê behsa girtina rojnamevan Yelis Ayazê ya ji ber xebatên wê yên rojnamevaniyê û bertekên rêxistinên pîşeyî yên çapemeniyê kiriye:







“Bûyera ku tê îdiakirin di dibistanê de qewimiye, ji bo nîşandayîna ku ev girtin li ser kîjan nûçeyan hatiye girtin, hatiye veguhastin. Di sernavê de bi eşkereyî hatiye gotin ku ev îdiayek e. Di nûçeyê de hem cih daye daxuyaniya Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Aydinê ya ku gotibû îdia ne rast in, hem jî daxuyaniya ku Ayazê ji girtîgehê şandibû.




Têkildarî serlêdanên CÎMERê û wêneyan, hemû agahî bi destnîşankirina çavkaniyên wan hatine veguhastin. Mebesta bingehîn a vê weşanê agahdarkirina civakê ye di barê girtina rojnamevanekê û helwestên li dijî vê girtinê de. Zev e ku mebesta vê nûçeyê ti carî belavkirina tirs, fikar an panîkê di nav civakê de nehatiye meşandin.”







Yazgan: Girtina rojnamevanekê raya giştî eleqedar dike




Parêzerê Cuzdan, Deniz Yazganê jî di îfadeya xwe de diyar kir ku di nûçeyê de vegotina derbarê dibistanê de di sernav û xala destpêkê (spot) de bi awayê “îdia” hatiye nîşandan. Bi bîr xist ku daxuyaniya Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Aydinê ya ku îdiayan red dike jî di nava metnê de cih girtiye.




Yazganê anî ziman ku gotinên di nivîsa Ayazê ya ku ji girtîgehê şandibû de bi eşkereyî ji bo xwe nîvîsiye û got: “Destnîşankirina serlêdanên CÎMERê an jî belavkirina wêneyan nayê wê wateyê ku bûyera li dibistanê hatiye îsbatkirin; ev her du mijar ji hev cuda ne. bianet.orgê tu carî ev îdia wekî rastiyeke ku bi xwe lêkolîn kiriye û derxistiye holê pêşkêş nekiriye.”




Yazgan diyar kir ku heke berevajiyê vê yekê were îdiakirin, divê bê destnîşankirin ka ew îdia dispêre kîjan îfadeya di nûçeyê de:







“Mijara nûçeyê biryara girtinê ye, di nava xwe de daxuyaniya dijber dihewîne û bertekên rêxistinên pîşeyî yên çapemeniyê radigihîne; ev hemû nîşan didin ku ev weşan bi armanca agahdarkirina raya giştî hatiye kirin. Girtina rojnamevanekê ji ber xebatên wê yên nûçegihaniyê û bandora bendeke cezayî ya li ser çapemeniyê, bi xwe re mijarên ku eleqeya wan bi berjewendiya raya giştî re heye tînin.”







Yazganê her wiha daxwaz kir ku bê diyarkirin giliya sûc di kîjan dîrokê de ketiye qeydan. Yazganê heyama çar mehan a vekirina dozê ya ku di maddeya 26an a Qanûna Çapemeniyê de cih digire bi bîr xist. Yazganê diyar kir ku ji bo vekirina doza giştî gumaneke (şubhe) bes tune ye û daxwaz kir ku derbarê Cuzdan de biryara neşopandinê bê dayin.




Mijara nûçeyê girtina Ayazê bû




Nûçeya bianetê ya ku bû mijara lêpirsînê, di 18ê Gulanê de bi sernavê “Rojnamevana ku îdiaya ‘Kurê parlementerê AKPî bi çekê çû dibistanê’ nivîsî sê roj in girtî ye” hatibû weşandin.




Di nûçeyê de hatibû aşkerekirin ku xwediyê Rojnameya Aydinpostê Yelis Ayaz, piştî ku îdiayên derbarê kurê parlementerekî de ku bi çekê çûye dibistanê kiribû nûçe, di çarçoveya xala 217/A ya TCKyê de hatiye girtin.




Di nûçeyê de her wiha cih dabûn wê nivîsa ku Ayazê ji nava girtîgehê nivîsîbû.




(HA/AY)

author: Odessa Bishop-McMurray
title: “If they won’t give us a future, we will build one right here” - why the French revolt should inspire high-schoolers everywhere
content:
As one of the organisers of the upcoming nationwide 

Students Say No to Hanson

 demonstration on 12 November, I’ve had to endure a lot of inanity from the media and the right. Amongst snide remarks about the stages of brain development and warnings of the mortal dangers of missing two periods of class, one accusation keeps coming up: that we’re plotting to bring “French-style riots” to Australian cities. 

Right-wing journalists seized on an Instagram post we made on 11 October, conveying the inspiration we draw from French student protesters fighting government austerity and the far right. 

Cue an avalanche of hysterical headlines and news segments: The Murdoch-owned Adelaide 

Advertiser

 warned readers to brace for “walkouts ‘inspired’ by violent French protests”. Pauline Hanson went on Brisbane’s 4BC Radio to rip into us: 

“...They are saying they are inspired by what’s going on in France. What? The 

looting

? The 

burning

? The 

destruction

? They’re 

inspired

 by that?”

Well, we’re not sorry for being inspired by French students. Everyone who wants to see a better world should identify with their struggle. 

Young people everywhere are facing a dire future, and revolt is rightly spreading. It’s clear even to some in the establishment that what’s happening in France is part of a global wave of protest with deep roots. As former UK Prime Minister Gordon Brown wrote this week in 

The Guardian

: “A global youthquake is happening. Promises we made young people have been broken—and they know it.”

Both far-right governments and “sensible centrists” are taking us on the same trajectory: more racism, more militarism, and more austerity. 

When states aren’t attempting to re-introduce conscription, as in Germany, they’re funnelling billions into the military-industrial complex while schools crumble. In France, students endure classrooms infested with cockroaches, mould and overcrowding, sometimes numbering 35 students to a class. 

We’ll likely never be able to afford secure housing or sufficient healthcare. We’ve watched politicians choose fossil fuel companies over the habitability of our planet. For many of us, the establishment’s unanimous endorsement of Israel’s genocide in Gaza was the final nail in the coffin.

It’s obvious that the journalists’ and politicians’ pearl-clutching about a few broken Parisian shop windows is a means of avoiding discussion of these issues. And their condemnation of violence rings hollow when they decline to comment on the vastly greater violence that the system inflicts on people daily. 

There’s the violence that is inherent in running such an unequal society. French youth linger without a future in the slums while the richest 500 families own nearly half the country. Schools and hospitals in France are crumbling, but the latest budget announcement includes 54 billion euros in further cuts to public spending. The police systematically brutalise Black and Arab working-class migrants. The high-profile killing of 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk, which sparked a nationwide revolt in 2023, is part of a long history of racialised policing. 

When these injustices generate resistance, there’s one public service the government can guarantee: the bludgeoning of protestors, tear gas, and potentially lethal stun grenades; exploding a student’s hand, breaking another’s jaw and leaving two 16-year-olds blinded for life. 

This is an inherent admission that the ruling class has no genuine plan to improve society. They just want resignation from ordinary people, and when that fails, tear gas is their backup plan.

But French students have shown that resignation gets us nowhere; Our power comes from the streets, and that’s a lesson the ruling class desperately does not want students to learn.

Already, France has shown small glimpses of how these movements can win real gains. While still hoping to crush the movement, the government has already been forced to make concessions. They’ve announced plans to cap class sizes, hire more teachers, and create more university places. This is a tiny fraction of what the movement is demanding, but it proves a timeless truth: a month of rebellion can win more change than decades of asking nicely.

A grassroots student movement in Serbia just ended the 14-year rule of the repressive Vučić regime. In Brazil, thousands of students flocked to the streets to successfully halt the advance of far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.

It seems like young people are doing a lot of the heavy lifting in confronting the far right, authoritarianism and inequality. This is definitely the case in Australia, where the establishment has spent the entire year cringing and simpering in front of One Nation. It’s taken groups like High School Anti-Capitalists to call demonstrations and try to put up a fight. 

We’re ready to take on Pauline Hanson again on 12 November because we want to see her politics driven to the fringes of society. More than that, because we have a vision of a future that is free of all inequality and oppression. 

Join us - we owe it to ourselves and to the brave students across the world fighting alongside us.

Speaking outside her blockaded school in the Parisian suburb of Saint-Denis, a 16-year-old protester captured the hope that students all around the world carry: 

"They spend all day telling us who we are, what we can wear, and what we are allowed to hope for. But out here on the pavement, next to my classmates, they can't define us anymore. We are writing our own history now. If they won't give us a future, we will build one right here."

title: Луиджи Фаббри - Анархическая Организация
content:
Автор

: Луиджи Фаббри

Название

: Анархическая Организация

Подзаголовок

: Доклад, представленный Итальянскому Анархическому Конгрессу в Риме (16-20 июня 1907) и Международному Анархическому Конгрессу в Амстердаме (24-31 августа 1907).

Дата

: 1907

Дополнительная информация

: Текст был разделен на 11 частей, только первая часть изначально была с названием. Названия для остальных частей придумал переводчик.




ПРЕДВАРИТЕЛЬНОЕ ЗАМЕЧАНИЕ




 В качестве заключения к следующему докладу об 

индивидуальном и коллективном действии в анархическом движении

, представленному 

Первому Итальянскому анархическому конгрессу

, состоявшемуся в Риме с 16 по 20 июня сего года (1907), была предложена эта резолюция: 




 «

Конгресс,




принимая во внимание, что в борьбе против организованных сил капитализма и правительств необходимо единство анархических сил,




выражает пожелание, чтобы это единство становилось всё сильнее и обширнее на основе солидарности и сознательного участия всех индивидуальных воль;




вследствие чего полагает, что анархисты, уже согласные не только в идеях, но и в методах борьбы, объединят свои силы, повсеместно создавая группы и затем связывая эти группы между собой, при естественном сохранении автономии личности в группах и автономии групп в их объединениях;




заявляет, что, считая необходимым это объединение сил для коллективного действия, столь же необходимым остаётся и индивидуальное действие в его наиболее сознательных проявлениях, со стороны каждого соответственно его силам

». 




 Конгресс единогласно, за исключением одного голоса, одобрил эту резолюцию теоретического характера; и принял, что касается Италии, следующее постановление практического характера: 




 «

Конгресс рекомендует товарищам из разных местностей безотлагательное формирование групп, чтобы иметь возможность в кратчайший срок приступить к образованию

 

Итальянского Анархического Социалистического Альянса

 

на началах полнейшей автономии, поручив уже существующим группам подготовительную работу

». 




 Представляя тот же теоретический и тактический доклад «Международному анархическому конгрессу» в Амстердаме, я надеюсь, что там будут приняты идентичные и ещё более точные резолюции, – и что вскоре от теоретических утверждений мы перейдем в область фактов к созданию Международной Анархической Ассоциации. 




 Да здравствует Либертарный Интернационал! 




 Рим, 20 августа 1907. 







ЛУИДЖИ ФАББРИ







I. Вступление




Товарищи

. 













 Уже много лет анархическое движение, – начавшееся столь блистательно внутри 

Интернационала

, – бьётся в неразрешимом кризисе, и это происходит прежде всего из-за недостатка доброй воли среди нас. 




 Мы, анархисты, должны признаться, если нас никогда не устрашали преследования, обрушивающиеся на нас извне, то мы всегда имели проклятый страх перед неким призраком, который сами же создали. Прежде всего мы смирились с тем, чтобы быть жертвами всех безумцев, всех чудаков, всех тех, кто впадает в крайности, которые под предлогом логики претендовали не только на то, чтобы оправдывать всё то, что находили непристойным и низким у буржуа, но и на то, чтобы препятствовать и разрушать всякую работу по восстановлению движения, которую пытались предпринять другие товарищи, постоянно выставляя напоказ призрак идейной непоследовательности. 




 Анархическая идея имеет своей первой основой индивидуальную свободу; но те, кто стал бы утверждать, что индивидуальная свобода при анархии бесконечна и абсолютна, были бы утопистами в самом смехотворном смысле этого слова, ибо бесконечное и абсолютное – это абстрактные понятия, это умственные построения, не имеющие возможности практического осуществления. Ныне же, напротив, всегда во имя индивидуальной свободы некоторые анархисты, в зависимости от того, что им нравится, либо провозглашают право делать что угодно и даже посягать на свободу и право других, либо объявляют непоследовательным любую попытку революционного осуществления анархии и организации для пропаганды. 




 Здесь мы намерены заняться возражениями, которые выдвигаются против идеи организации. 




II. Организация и пропаганда




 Обычно говорят, что организация – это метод, а не цель; это ошибка. Принцип организации следует пропагандировать не только потому, что, организуясь сегодня, мы можем лучше подготовить революцию, но и потому, что принцип организации сам по себе является одним из главных постулатов анархической доктрины. 




 В буржуазном обществе, где государство и церковь берут на себя сверху задачу держать вместе сообщество, чтобы эксплуатировать его в своих интересах, и где индивидуальная воля поглощается и часто уничтожается общественным механизмом, который претендует на то, чтобы брать на себя заботу обо всём вместо него и регулировать жизнь индивидов от рождения до смерти, – в этом обществе, где организация монополизирована государством и капитализмом, единственно мыслимая организация – это организация для борьбы против угнетения и эксплуатации. 




 Но общество, провозглашаемое анархистами, в котором не будет ни «провиденциальных»

[1]

 людей, ни учреждений, и которое будет основано на участии всех индивидов в производстве и в объединении, потребует, чтобы организация была распространена на всех, вплоть до последнего индивида и чтобы каждый добровольно участвовал в общей гармонии. И поскольку это участие каждого должно быть самостоятельным, добровольным, свободным, чтобы, при отсутствии принуждения, никто не пренебрегал долгом солидарности, необходимо, чтобы сначала было распространено сознание необходимости организации, так чтобы организовываться означало удовлетворять истинную материальную и моральную потребность. Вот почему, по нашему мнению, пропаганда организации должна вестись непрерывно, так же как и пропаганда всех других постулатов анархического идеала.

author: Sagar Sanyal
title: Emergency and autocracy in Modi’s India
content:
The far-right government in India led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been increasingly repressive and anti-democratic over recent months. Commentators are asking if the country is in the grip of an ‘

undeclared Emergency

’, a reference to the 1975-77 period of ‘Emergency rule’ by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in which activists and trade unionists were simply rounded up and jailed. 

The current repression is a response to the student and youth protests that erupted in the capital, New Delhi, in late July. They were sparked by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), a satirical movement that began on social media a couple of months earlier. The scale and intensity of the protests surprised the regime, as did the mocking anti-Modi tenor of popular chants. While the protest demand was for the resignation of the education minister over exam leaks, the protesters were motivated by visceral opposition to Modi, who has ruled since 2014. The police lashed out using the sort of 

force

 that they typically use in repressed regions like Kashmir. Police fired pellet guns, used nail-studded batons and sexually assaulted women protesters. 

Despite the repression, tens of thousands mobilised daily for five days—high school and university students, middle-class and working-class youth. Not only in Delhi, but in dozens of cities around the country. Alongside clips of police brutality circulating on social media, there are clips of youth chasing police off the streets with their sheer numbers and bravado. There are clips of cheeky middle-class youth approaching police who are away from the heat of the action to ask mocking questions like “Dear Mr. Officer, are you planning to tear gas protesters today?” The government is tracking down incriminating and embarrassing recordings of those events and asking social media platforms to 

remove them

.

Public opinion has turned strongly against Modi’s repression. Among the Hindi-speaking, middle-class, upper-caste Hindus who have been the most secure vote base of the BJP, parents now saw their own children being beaten—just for demanding a fair opportunity in college exams! Ultimately, the administration conceded the protest demand to sack the education minister, a humiliating 

defeat

 for Modi. It gave the lie to the “unstoppable strongman” image of him so carefully crafted by pro-Modi big media. 

Less than three months after the July protests, a new protest movement gripped the nation. It demands the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner of India, Gyanesh Kumar, who has been highly partisan to Modi and his 

Hindu nationalist

 Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and, according to some parties, rigged state elections in Bihar (May 2025) and West Bengal (April 2026). In West Bengal, the BJP won for the first time due in part to the chief election commissioner disqualifying millions of names from the eligible voters list. Deletions disproportionately targeted Muslims, who are an ideological enemy of Hindu nationalists, and who were also an important vote base of the party the BJP displaced—the Trinamool Congress (TMC). 

Following a late September 

expose,

 which revealed that the chief election commissioner had overruled the protestations of even his fellow election commissioners, the CJP and left student groups took up vote-rigging as a national campaign to channel the energy from the July student movement. Demands for the chief election commissioner to resign have been taken up by all opponents of the BJP. 

When a large protest was called for 

10 October

, the state responded by locking down New Delhi. Around 40,000 paramilitary and police laid siege to a sizeable area around the “designated protest site” of Jantar Mantar in the centre of the city. They blocked roads and shut down local internet mobile services (India is 

among the worst

 states for this). They closed over 40 metro train stations in Delhi and stopped over 200 inter-city trains from reaching Delhi. They threatened activists in their homes on the night before the march, this coming on top of regular arbitrary detention of prominent leaders of the protest movement (from the CJP and the left parties). 

Undeterred

, protestors appeared in their tens of thousands and were again met with batons and tear gas, and thousands were detained.

Sizeable protests have continued sporadically since 10 October, some called by the CJP or student organizations of the left, 

others

 by major opposition parties. The cause has received expressions of 

support

 from the Samyukta Kisan Morcha (United Farmers’ Front), an umbrella organization of farmers’ unions that emerged in 2020 in opposition to 

Modi’s Farm Laws

, as well as from trade union federations.  

Many see the 10 October crackdown in Delhi as a sign that the Modi regime fears being toppled. Speculation is rife that India will have its own version of the “Gen Z” protests that ousted governments in neighbouring Nepal (2025), Bangladesh (2024) and Sri Lanka (2022). BJP politicians denounce the protests as a plot by foreign powers to destabilise Indian society and bring about regime change. 

The Modi administration appears backed into a corner. To sack the election commissioner would be tantamount to accepting that several state elections over the past year have been 

rigged

. 

*****

What explains the rage of students and youth? Among young college graduates, 

unemployment

 is at 40 percent. The shrinking size of the public sector means there are fewer jobs for graduates. Promises of jobs in corporate management or in professional and white-collar careers in a handful of headline-grabbing sectors like IT have turned out to be a pipe dream for most, given the large pool of unemployed graduates. 

College graduates are not outliers in the wider economy. Since 2014, when the Modi government took power, it has marketed India as a fast-growing economy with jobs for all and rising incomes for the masses. Yet growing numbers of youth feel that reality does not match state propaganda. Not just young people. The 

middle class

 of India has seen stagnating incomes during Modi’s rule, while the working class faces a 

crisis of underemployment

 that has built up over a quarter-century of neoliberalism.

As Indian capitalists see it, the economy needs major “restructuring”. Private investment needs a shot in the arm. There are too many inefficient’ labour-intensive small enterprises, which ought to make way for big capital-intensive enterprises. Capital resources must be moved from producing for ordinary Indian households to producing for export or building infrastructure to attract foreign investment - especially in military, strategic and high-tech sectors. Wages must be held down. Yet all these measures will further reduce the number of jobs, reduce wages and take national resources away from the goods and services that ordinary households consume. 

The July and October waves of protest in India are an elemental upsurge that carries the potential to make major social changes. Even more so if the protesters can combine forces with workers, who undertook a wave of wildcat 

strikes

 earlier this year, and with farmers' unions who expect a renewed fight against Modi over recent US-India trade agreements which threaten their livelihoods.

What comes of this latent potential depends on its political leadership. There are both moderate and radical sections of the movement. For now, it appears the momentum of protest has been channelled onto a moderate path. Opposition parties, predominantly moderate, see an opportunity to “ride the tiger” of popular upsurge to dislodge the BJP from power. The largest such party is the Congress party, which anchors the “INDIA bloc” of parties that oppose the BJP and aspire to form a coalition government. This bloc of parties organised the most recent large rally, on November 1 in New Delhi, rather than the CJP or the left student groups associated with the explosive protests in July and early October. 

Besides Congress, several parties with a provincial or sub-national presence are also important. They represent blocs of provincial capital that have distinct interests to the capitalists who dominate national policy. They have sizeable vote bases among castes and communities special to their province. The Samajwadi Party, for instance, is a big presence in the most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, currently governed by a BJP firebrand but facing elections in the early months of 2027. The TMC was entrenched in West Bengal until its loss to the BJP this year. These parties are keen to reform the election commission to ensure their own survival against the BJP. However, like the BJP, they too want to rule in favour of the capitalist class and are loath to address the deeper economic grievances fuelling the upsurge.

The protest movement has also spurred mainstream discussion of Hindu nationalist forces beyond the Modi administration. The Indian far-right is bigger than Modi and his immediate crew. It is highly organised and ideological. At its centre lies the 

RSS

, a disciplined, cadre-based Hindu supremacist organization created in the 1920s, which explicitly drew on the fascism of Mussolini and Hitler. The RSS does not contest elections but is the controlling force behind the BJP. Modi has been an RSS man since childhood. Around the RSS are various vigilante groups. Under the Modi government, RSS men have been increasingly inserted into the state bureaucracy, judiciary, the police and armed forces, university leaderships, and, of course, the election commission. In BJP-ruled states, Hindu nationalist vigilante groups have developed working relations with police. These groups routinely 

lynch

 and beat Muslims without police interference. 

It would be one thing to remove from the helm of the state Modi and his right-hand man Amit Shah, the Home Minister. But that would leave intact a state machinery peppered with ideologically cohered and well-connected right-wingers. They are practised in suppressing democracy and pushing Hindu supremacy in league with vigilantes. 

In recent weeks, speeches by Congress leader Gandhi have targeted not only Modi and the BJP but also the RSS and its supreme leader Mohan Bhagwat. This plays well for a progressive audience, who have long been alarmed by the growing threat of the RSS. However, if the attacks on the RSS go beyond rhetoric and have the effect of encouraging efforts to clean out the state machinery of notorious RSS personnel, it is possible this will open space for more radical sections of the protesters to revive and take momentum back from the moderates.

It remains to be seen what will be gained out of the youth upsurges of July and early October. Some lessons are already apparent. The explosive power of discontented youth could place on the back foot a Modi regime that has seemed unstoppable. Indian progressives had despaired for years about the steady erosion of democracy and bemoaned the failure of the mainstream opposition parties to resist. Today, there is hope.

title: Killing King Abacus - Notizen zu einer neuen Analyse der Institutionen der Herrschaft
content:

Mehr Kontakt Material Sticker, Plakate, etc.

Es ist kaum 65 Jahre her, da war es absolut üblich, in der anarchistischen Literatur Analysen der Institutionen zu lesen, in denen sich die verschiedenen Formen der Herrschaft manifestierten. Wenn man beispielsweise über die Unterdrückung der Frauen schrieb, dann wurden die Familie und die Ehe untersucht und bloßgestellt. Wenn die Unterdrückung von Vergnügen und der Freude des Lebens zur Diskussion stand, dann wurden Religion und Gesetz ins Visier genommen. Der institutionelle Rahmen, in dem sich diese Gesellschaft abspielt wurde als Quelle der Ausbeutung, Herrschaft und Entfremdung wahrgenommen.

Es scheint so, als wäre dieser institutionelle Rahmen in jüngerer Zeit größtenteils vergessen worden zu sein. Von den verschiedenen Institutionen, in die unser entfremdetes kreatives Potenzial zu unserem Nachteil akkumuliert wurde, scheinen nur noch der Staat und das Kapital (und gelegentlich die Technologie) in einem bedeutenden Ausmaß Erwähnung zu finden und selbst diese werden häufig mehr als Geisteszustände, denn als konkrete soziale Institutionen behandelt. So entdecken wir beispielsweise, dass Anarchist*innen gegen Staatlichkeit (was auch immer das sein soll) sind, anstatt gegen den Staat. Auf diese Weise kann etwa ein Bookchin behaupten, gegen Staatlichkeit zu sein, während er den altertümlichen griechischen Stadt-Staat als Modell für seine demokratisierte Version der „Anarchie“ bewirbt.

Jede andere Form der Unterdrückung wird ebenfalls zu einem „-ismus“ (Rassismus, Sexismus, usw.) oder schlimmerem (Homophobie impliziert beispielsweise eine psychologische Störung, die einer Behandlung bedarf, anstatt einer sozialen Repression, die nach Revolte verlangt). Natürlich verleugnen wir nicht die Realitäten der Ideologien der Bigotterie und ihrer Durchdringung der Gedanken und Gefühle der Ausgebeuteten und Unterdrückten. Aber ohne ein Verständnis des institutionellen Rahmens der Unterdrückung und Herrschaft ist es nicht möglich zu verstehen, wie die herrschende Klasse diese Ideologien dazu nutzt, diejenigen zu spalten, die sie ausbeutet.

Selbst die anscheinend Radikalsten (weil ihre Rhetorik am extremsten ist) innerhalb des anarchistischen Millieus entgehen dem nicht. Die von primitivistischen und antizivilisatorischen Kreisen kommende Kritik richtet ihre verbalen Angriffe allzu häufig gegen eine nebulöse, schlecht definierte Zivilisation. Gewiss klingt „Für die Zerstörung der Zivilisation“ radikal. Meiner eigenen Definition gemäß stimme ich damit sogar überein. Aber meiner Definition nach ist Zivilisation nicht irgendeine nebulöse, weitestgehend mentale Kategorie, die dem Rationalismus oder dem westlichen Denken oder welcher unerwünschten Denkweise auch immer entspringt; sie ist ein Netzwerk konkreter sozialer Institutionen, die ich in meinem Alltag konfrontiere: Staat, Wirtschaft, Religion, die Familie, technologische Systeme, und so weiter, allesamt sehr reale Entitäten, die nicht von Gedankenspielen beseitigt werden werden.

Und genau hier tappt die derzeitige Tendenz in eine Falle. Wenn eine Analyse des institutionellen Rahmens der Unterdrückung, Ausbeutung, Herrschaft und Entfremdung vergessen wird, dann tritt Therapie an die Stelle von Revolution. Wir sind dann gezwungen, uns mit den pathetischen, weinerlichen Geständnissen eines Chris Crass zu beschäftigen oder auch der schlechten Popkultur-Psychologie der Autor*innen des Textes „Stick it to the Manarchy“ (wobei schon der Gebrauch eines Begriffs wie „manarchy“ ein sicheres Zeichen dafür ist, dass jemand nichts hörenswertes zu sagen hat), die versuchen ihren „Sexismus“, „Rassismus“, „Homophobie“ und „Klassismus“ abzulegen, die nicht länger irgendwelche Ideologien der Bigotterie sind, sondern niedere mentale Krankheiten, unter denen die selbsternannten „Privilegierten“ aller Klassen leiden.

Jede*r ernsthafte revolutionäre Anarchist*in muss sehen, dass das nur eine weitere List der Feiglinge und jener ist, die ein Interesse an der Aufrechterhaltung der herrschenden Ordnung haben, die eigentliche Entscheidung darüber, auf wessen Seite sie im Kampf gegen diese Gesellschaft stehen, aufzuschieben. Diejenigen von uns, die es mit der Zerstörung der gegenwärtigen Welt ernst meinen, um unsere Leben selbst zu gestalten, haben keine Zeit für diese selbstgerechten Gedankenspielereien, die so sehr an Selbsthilfegruppen erinnern („Mein Name ist … und ich bin süchtig nach meiner eigenen Unterdrückung.“). Unsere Aufgabe liegt vor uns: Die Institutionen aufzudecken und anzugreifen, die uns unsere Leben gestohlen haben und uns in diesem Prozess unsere eigenen Leben wiederanzueignen. Welche kleinen Versatzstücke einer unterdrückerischen Mentalität diesen Prozess auch immer überleben, mit denen lässt sich auch dann ein Umgang finden, wenn wir diese Aufgabe erst einmal bewältigt haben.
