author: Harriet Williamson
title: Google UK Signs ‘Sweetheart Deal’ With Employer-Friendly Union
content:
Google UK has been accused of signing a “sweetheart deal” with an employer-friendly union to undermine workers’ ability to organise within the tech company. 




Google 

signed an access agreement with Prospect union on Monday

 to make inroads among its 7,000 UK workers – excluding DeepMind staff – after 

new rights for unions to access workplaces

 in Britain came into force last week.




However, critics say Prospect lacks a strong record of organising with Google employees – known as Googlers – in the UK. The two largest and most active unions in Google UK are Unite and the Communication Workers’ Union (CWU) via their United Tech and Allied Workers (UTAW) branch. 




Prospect was granted access to the Google UK workforce over Unite and the CWU, despite the latter two unions applying for access as soon as formally possible. This means Prospect can now 

communicate with non-unionised workers

 and encourage them to join. 




In a joint Unite and CWU statement to members seen by Novara Media, the two unions warned that Prospect’s agreement with Google is only for “occasional meetings and an internal page, falling far short of the legal minimum requested by your unions”. 




A Google UK software engineer and UTAW rep, speaking to Novara Media on the condition of anonymity due to fear of professional reprisals, called the deal “a huge slap in the face for me and all UTAW and Unite organisers in Google”.  




The software engineer said: “We have worked diligently over the past few years to represent our fellow Googlers’ needs through collective action. We fought to keep as many jobs as possible during redundancies, we demonstrated against Google’s military contracts, and we demanded a stronger, worker-led regulation on Google and DeepMind’s AI direction. 




“For all of our fastidious work, our request for a right as basic as access has been ignored and given to Prospect, a union with laughably low membership in Google which has not participated in a single one of our aforementioned struggles.”




Unite and the CWU are asking why Prospect, which has not engaged in member-led unionising activity at Google, was granted access so quickly and alleging that the Prospect deal was pre-planned because Prospect may be considered a “tamer” or more employer-friendly union.




The Google software engineer added: “This conduct by Google is an insidious way to undermine worker organisation while veiling themselves in the guise of a benevolent, pro-union company. It is telling that this deal was conducted by Google UK’s current senior labour relations consultant, Philip Bickerstaffe, an ex-national officer at Prospect.”




Bickerstaffe worked at Prospect as a national officer from 2004 to 2011, according to his LinkedIn profile, before going on to roles with BT, Boeing, Amazon and Google. 




The Prospect-Google deal follows 

a similar agreement

 between Prospect and Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and Whatsapp. Meta employs roughly 5,000 people in the UK. 




Right of access to workplaces in the UK – even where employers are hostile to trade unions organising onsite – was included in the Employment Rights Act 2025, and came into force on 30 October. 




Unite and the CWU say they put in an access request at the stroke of midnight on 30 October, and received a formal acknowledgement from Google on 3 November, which said their request would be considered and responded to “within the appropriate time frame”.




Employers then have 15 days to respond and a further 25 days to negotiate. The Prospect deal was announced on 2 November, suggesting that little, if any, time was spent negotiating the terms of the deal, which has added to the impression that the deal is favourable to the employer.




Unite, the CWU and Prospect are all members of the Trade Union Congress (TUC), which means they must 

respect the principle

 that a union shouldn’t organise at a workplace where another union already has the majority of workers as members or is actively engaged in significant organising activity. 




Unite and the CWU say Prospect has violated this national cross-union agreement by signing the access deal with Google UK. 




A Prospect spokesperson said: “These allegations are false and seem designed to undermine union organising at Google. Our access agreement with Google was agreed in accordance with the TUC principles and does not include Google DeepMind where other unions are making a recognition bid.” 




A spokesperson from Google UK said: “To comply with new UK workplace legislation, we have established a structured access agreement with Prospect union for Google’s UK employees, but not including Google DeepMind. This step builds on our established work with internal employee representative groups, allowing us to fulfill these new requirements while preserving the respectful, direct dialogue our culture is built on.” 




Unite and the CWU have assured members that they are escalating the matter through the appropriate channels.

author: Erin Reed
title: Republicans Spent Nearly $200 Million on Ads Attacking Trans People — and Lost
content:
The election was a stunning rebuke of anti-transgender politics, and Democrats should take note moving forward.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

By now, you have likely seen the results of the 2026 midterms: a wave election for Democrats the likes of which we have not seen in years. Republicans and their allies spent nearly $200 million on anti-transgender ads alone, bankrolled in part by billionaires like Elon Musk. Virtually every Democrat in a highly contested race was the target of these kinds of ads. And what did it buy the Republican Party? An earth-shattering loss, and a stunning rebuke of anti-transgender politics.

A blue Texas in the face of the biggest anti-trans ad spend of any race this cycle … a victory in Michigan from a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate who forcefully defended trans people at every step of the race … a western Montana smokejumper who will go to Congress after telling voters the government has “no business sticking its nose into our personal lives” when it comes to transgender health care and sports … and an Alabama trans Democrat who won her race running on bread-and-butter issues in a conservative district in the Huntsville suburbs. These are just a small handful of the dozens of races we will remember as proof that anti-trans politics simply no longer works for the Republican Party, and that Democrats need never fear such attacks again.

I started writing about anti-transgender politics back in 2022 after the extreme efforts of Texas Gov. Greg Abbott and Attorney General Ken Paxton to sweep the state for transgender kids. In that dark time, they ordered child abuse investigations into the parents of transgender youth, and many of those families fled the state. Now, not only does James Talarico win in the face of ads built around him saying “God is nonbinary,” but Gina Hinojosa, who waved a trans flag on the Texas House floor after Democrats ran out the clock on a sports ban in 2021, wins the governorship. Vikki Goodwin wins the lieutenant governorship after being endorsed by Equality Texas and after voting no on every anti-trans bill that reached the House floor. And more than that, it appears the Texas House is going to go to Democrats for the first time since 2003. The dark era of horrific anti-trans targeting of trans Texans is over, and there is hope that one day, some of the trans people who fled may get to return to the state, despite the millions Elon Musk poured into Texas trying to prevent it.

The positive results for transgender people were not limited to Texas — they were seen across the board. If you were a Democratic consultant who believed that you had to moderate on transgender issues to win an election, the results in places like Montana’s 1st Congressional District make it clear that such capitulation is not necessary in the slightest. Smokejumper Sam Forstag, a Democrat running in a stubbornly Republican House district, won his election handily. When asked whether he supports transgender participation in sports or gender-affirming care for transgender youth, his answer was that the government has no place banning any of it, and that the issue is an attempt to distract voters while Republicans “pick our pockets.” Trump campaigned in Montana for Aaron Flint, his opponent, who ran anti-trans ads. It wasn’t enough. Western Montana will have a Democratic congressman who supports transgender people, and he won one of the toughest races in the country handily.

Several Democrats who championed transgender people won in major swing races, and the most notable was probably Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed. El-Sayed was the target of millions in anti-transgender ads on one side, and drew the ire of centrist Democrats on the other for not moderating on many progressive causes, including transgender people. When asked in a hostile CBS “60 Minutes” interview about trans people and other “social cultural issues,” his response was that “a failure to show up and fight for that right is a failure to show up and fight for your own.” Then, when asked specifically about schools, he called the fight over what kids learn in school a manufactured “cultural flash point.” It cost him nothing in a state Trump won in 2024. El-Sayed won Michigan’s U.S. Senate race by about 6 points as of the early morning hours.

It was also a big night for transgender candidates. Washington state will have the first out Black transgender woman elected to a state legislature in Jaelynn Scott, and Michigan will have a trans woman legislator as well in Joanna Whaley. But perhaps the most stunning result when it comes to transgender people winning their elections was Allison Montgomery, who won in a relatively conservative suburban Huntsville, Alabama, district. She ran on bread-and-butter economic issues. In 2022, the last time the seat was on the ballot, Republican Phillip Rigsby won it by 16 points. Now, she has beaten Rigsby by more than 6 points, a major swing for any Democrat, much less a trans Democrat running in Alabama. “I know the headlines tomorrow are gonna be provocative and catchy, but let’s focus on the most important part of this victory: we showed that a truly grassroots campaign that stands on its policies and its principles has a real shot in Alabama. We the people are tired of attempts to distract us with culture war issues, whether we’re in a minority group or not,” she posted to her campaign site after her victory.

The victories for transgender people didn’t stop there. Of 160 races being tracked by Erin In The Morning with transgender implications, 107 races went for the side supportive of transgender people while 53 went for the side that was not supportive. These races range from school board fights such as the Wake County board of Education going to trans-supportive candidates in North Carolina, to Wisconsin likely carrying a Democratic trifecta, allowing for real protections for transgender people to pass in the state. Meanwhile, candidates like Peggy Flanagan win in Minnesota, even after drawing the ire of Republicans for wearing a Protect trans kids t-shirt with a knife on it. In Mississippi, anti-transgender ads failed against the Democratic candidate for US Senate, who was within striking distance as of this morning. And even in Tennessee, there were victories against anti-transgender politics to be found: Victoria Broderick, a LGBTQ+ woman who has made supportive statements about transgender people, is likely to win her election against Scott DesJarlais in what was supposed to be a safe Republican Seat. “Any politician talking about men in women’s sports is a lazy politician,” Broderick said in the leadup to the election. “They are deflecting from questions about the war in Iran, the gas crisis and what is going on in our country.”

The results were not unanimously good for transgender people. Some anti-transgender democrats such as Josh Turek won, though their influence will be diluted in a party that sent many pro-transgender Democrats from swing states as well. Meanwhile, Anti-trans ballot measures look likely to pass in Colorado and Washington, although the forced outing measure in Washington is trailing, and the same was true in Arizona. But even in these results, the anti-trans side was winning by only 52-48 in Colorado and 57-43 in Arizona and Washington as of the early morning, with plenty of votes left to count. No longer can Republicans claim that even trans sports, the issue they have pegged as the most polarizing of trans-related issues, is an “80-20 issue.” Given the razor-thin margins in Colorado and the incredibly protective state courts in Washington and Colorado, it seems likely that these measures will end up in court, where they could be overturned or defanged. And in some states, transgender people won on ballot measures, such as Vermont, where gender identity will be enshrined in the state constitution, only the third state to do so.

Now, Democrats will hold significant power in state legislatures and nationwide, and they can present a real check on Trump’s power, including his attacks on transgender people. They may be able to stymie Trump’s trans military ban, or use the budget process to hinder the investigations of hospitals and schools that support transgender people. They can ensure that no new national anti-trans policy makes its way into budgets or law. The congressional bathroom ban will likely fall soon, and multiple states could pass protective legislation for transgender people that they could not before. And all of this happened in a national environment where Republicans put more effort into anti-transgender attacks than ever before, only to suffer one of the most devastating results any party has seen in a generation. The election was a stunning rebuke of anti-transgender politics, and Democrats should take note moving forward: it costs nothing to defend transgender people, and it may even lead Republicans to waste their time and money attacking us for virtually no gain.

This piece was republished with permission from Erin In The Morning.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Illegal Iran War Helps Boost Oil CEOs’ Personal Fortunes by Millions
content:
The CEO of Shell is among oil bosses who have raked in millions of pounds as the value of their shareholdings soared amid the illegal US war on Iran.




Wael Sawan saw his shares in Shell gain £4.7m since the US and Israel first attacked the country in late February, 

research by Greenpeace

 shows. 




He cashed out £1.3m worth of shares on 22 May, the day before Donald Trump said a deal to cease hostilities had almost been reached. 




Bosses from TotalEnergies, Harbour Energy and Equinor also raked in millions as oil prices surged due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a major global transport route for oil and natural gas.




North Sea oil CEOs have added a total of £19m to their personal fortunes via share price increases since the war began, Greenpeace said.




The windfalls come as 

oil giants report a bumper set of financial results whilst

 households in the UK and across the world struggle with rising energy bills.




Equinor CEO Anders Opedal has seen his shares rise by £1.03m amid the war, while TotalEnergies’s Patrick Pouyanné enjoyed an £8.4m boost to his shareholdings, selling £3.1m in shares and savings one month after the war began. 




“Cashing out millions in personal shares while the market drives millions of people into energy poverty – all while their companies’ operations supercharge climate breakdown – is crisis profiteering at its most cynical,” said Rudy Schulkind, political campaigner at Greenpeace UK.




Equinor and Shell were recently granted permission by Andy Burnham’s government to start new drilling in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea. Both are also set to benefit in the event that Rosebank oil field is approved.




Oil companies in the US have earned more than $130bn in profits during the war, according to 

an analysis last week

 from the New York Times. 




Trump’s decision to capitulate to Israel and attack Iran appears to have lost him a lot of support –  and is believed to have played a key role in the Republicans’ resounding defeat in the midterms on Tuesday. 




The US president campaigned on an anti-war platform while promising to lower people’s bills.

author: Mary Stuart
title: AI Needed to Produce More Gas to Power More AI, Tech Firm Cohere Says
content:
Oil and gas companies need to integrate AI into their operations so that they can extract more fossil fuels—which can then be used to power more AI.




That is the pitch that Canada’s leading AI company, Cohere, is making to the oil and gas industry, even as its CEO Aidan Gomez argues publicly that it is important for the tech industry to be aligned with “environmental goals.”




“As energy demand surges globally, driven in part by the explosive growth of AI data centers, oil and gas companies face significantly new operational, market, and environmental pressures,” explains a 

Cohere e-book

 from 2025 that advertises the AI company’s services to the fossil fuel sector. “AI has the potential to change the industry’s trajectory quickly, thereby better equipping it to address the growing supply-demand imbalance.”




An 

X post

 from the Toronto-based Cohere in early 2025 claimed that “AI-driven analytics optimize drilling, leading to more efficient resource extraction,” while predicting that “the oil and gas market for AI & ML [machine learning] is projected to surpass $4.9 billion by 2034, with GenAI playing a pivotal role in this growth.”




Using 

AI to increase the production of fossil fuels

, which are then used to power the explosive growth of AI data centres, might seem like a strategy designed mostly to increase profits for fossil fuel and tech companies. 




But that’s not the way Gomez is pitching Cohere to Canadians. He 

promises

 his company will deliver huge societal benefits, including bringing “down the cost of living for the average Canadian” and developing “cures for different diseases and ailments.”




Variations of Cohere’s fossil fuel-forward business model have been adopted across the industry by Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and other tech giants, according to Paris Marx, tech critic and author of the new book 

Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires

.




“It feels like another example of just how intertwined the fossil fuel industry and the tech industry have become since the advent of generative AI taking off,” Marx told DeSmog in an interview. “There were relationships between them in the past, but now it’s just fully out in the open how simpatico their interests are, because more data centres means more fossil fuel demand”.




Cohere did not respond to DeSmog’s request for comment.







Subscribe to Desmog




Get the weekly intelligence you need to hold polluters accountable
















Email Address







Sign Up










Send me intelligence from:







All




US/Global team




UK/Europe team

























‘Playbook for Oil and Gas’




In mid-September, 10,000 people gathered in Montréal for Canada’s largest AI conference. One of the most anticipated speakers that day was Gomez, who in 2023 was 

named by Time

 as one of the 100 most influential people in the world working in AI.




Cohere, the company he co-founded in 2019, recently received a funding commitment of $1.6 billion from 

Mark Carney’s Liberal government

, helping bring its valuation to nearly 

$36 billion

, and making it Canada’s most valuable AI firm and a significant player in the global industry. Gomez spoke on multiple occasions at the 

ALL IN conference

 from September 16-17, where he described AI as a nation-building technology for Canada.




“I think Canadians are strategic. And if we look at where we are right now in our geopolitical situation, we need to gain leverage on the world stage. That is frankly the project for our country. If we want to remain sovereign, if we want remain an independent country, we need leverage on a global stage. This is a place where we can win,” he said. 




Gomez also assured attendees that data centres “can be completely in line with environmental goals,” adding that “with the type of energy that goes into these data centres, we need to make sure that it’s clean.” 




Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez at the ALL IN conference in Montréal, September 2026. Credit: Mary Stuart




Cohere has in some cases prioritized renewable energy for its computing power, as it will be operating its AI models through a 

Bell data centre

 in Merritt, BC, that is powered by hydroelectricity.




Nevertheless, the vast majority of new data centres proposals in Canada involve fossil fuels. Canada’s federal government 

has previously identified 15.5 gigawatts

 of new gas capacity planned for data centres, which could cause an increase of somewhere between 33 to 63 megatonnes of annual greenhouse gas emissions.




While Gomez promoted the use of clean energy on stage, his company is trying to secure contracts with fossil fuel companies, including to help boost their production and refining capacity. 




Cohere

’s 2025

 

e-book

 makes the case for “creating an AI-empowered oil and gas company”. It details “how energy sector leaders can harness generative AI— including agentic AI systems — to transform the oil and gas value chain, spanning upstream exploration and production to midstream logistics, downstream refining, and services.”




Examples include helping to “identify the ideal drilling locations”, supporting pipeline monitoring and leak detection, and taking care of transportation logistics. The book offers the example of Shell using AI to improve efficiency in deep-sea exploration, “boosting offshore oil output”.




DeSmog 

recently reported

 on a new study that found AI could increase global energy-related carbon dioxide emissions by between 1.2 and 4.8 percent, largely from improving productivity in fossil fuel production. Large fossil fuel companies, like 

Chevron

, 

Equinor

, 

ExxonMobil

, and 

Shell

 are already integrating AI into their operations.




Cohere argues in its e-book that fossil fuel companies are well-positioned to meet the massive electricity requirements of new data centres. “AI offers a transformative leap — a way to help the sector meet surging energy demand,” it argues.




The explosive growth of AI data centre proposals can in turn “provide markets” for the oil and gas industry, 

according to

 

an internal strategy document

 prepared for the Clerk of the Privy Council, one of the top advisors to Prime Minister Carney.




Global AI Player




Gomez isn’t the only Canadian CEO attempting to portray AI as environmentally sustainable. Mirko Bibic, CEO of Bell Canada, said at the ALL IN conference that his company is developing AI with “Canadian environmental stewardship”. Bibic explained that Bell’s data centres will use closed loop cooling systems, and that the company is going to “use best-in-class building practices to minimize the emissions”.




The conference took place on the heels of 

Bell’s announcement

 to expand an AI hub in Saskatchewan by 900 megawatts, which will be 

powered by gas

.




“Bell is committed to building AI infrastructure responsibly,” the company said in response to questions from DeSmog, adding that the Saskatchewan proposal “will be subject to the provincial environmental impact assessment process.” 




Cohere is the 

only Canadian company

 that develops large language models (LLMs), which it does for governments, companies, and other enterprise users rather than consumers.




The company recently finalized a merger with German AI company Aleph Alpha, a move that Cohere says will allow it to compete directly with OpenAI and other tech giants in certain markets. “We are now the largest AI company outside the United States and China,” 

Gomez said in late October

, following the news of the company’s $36 billion valuation. 




“We need this technology,” 

Prime Minister Carney said

 in announcing his government’s investment in Cohere’s latest funding round. “That’s why this company’s growth has been so extraordinary. It is in all our interests for Cohere to succeed, and now all Canadians will have a share in that success.”




But Cohere’s products will specifically create “greater profitability” for the oil and gas industry—at least according to the AI company’s promotional materials.




“The question is no longer if generative and agentic AI will reshape the oil and gas sector, but rather how quickly organizations will position themselves to benefit,” Cohere’s e-book argues.




The publication ends with a quote from Vicki Hollub, CEO of the U.S. oil company Occidental Petroleum: “Technologies … like AI will determine whether we stagnate — or surge forward.”




The post 

AI Needed to Produce More Gas to Power More AI, Tech Firm Cohere Says

 appeared first on 

DeSmog

.

author: La Zarzamora
title: Lulén y Max, dos jóvenes trans llevan año y medio encarcelados por defenderse de su agresor
content:
Lulen y Max son una pareja de dos personas trans condenados por intento de homicidio agravado con tentativa hacia el padre adoptivo de uno de ellos.

Los hechos habrían ocurrido en febrero del 2025 cuando ambos jóvenes se reúnen en la casa del padre de Lulen “Willian Watts” en Córdoba, con el motivo de buscar algunas reliquias de su abuela quién había fallecido recientemente.

El contexto de la familia adoptiva de Lulen es clave para entender los hechos, ya que desde su adolescencia se vio enfrentado a la violencia psicológica y física que perpetuaba el padre hacia la madre; a la homofobia del padre por su orientación sexual y posteriormente por su transición de género.

El día de los hechos como era recurrente hubo una discusión. Lulen y Max se defienden golpeando a Willian Watts hasta que un vecino escucha gritos, interrumpe la pelea y llama a la policía. Watts se encontraba inconsciente por una supuesta asfixia, pero queda vivo y sin lesiones. Desde ese día en febrero del 2025 Lulen y Max se encuentran secuestrados, presos en la cárcel de Córdoba.

La fiscalía les condenó a 12 años y seis meses de cárcel por intento de homicidio agravado con tentativa, primero por el vinculo familiar, segundo por alevosía y tercero por una supuesta teoría de premeditación (tentativa).

Sin duda ha habido diferentes vulneraciones desde el sistema judicial en su totalidad, ya que no dan ninguna relevancia a los hechos de violencia consecutiva y daños previos ejercidos por Willian Watts, tampoco otorgan valor al transodio y sostienen una hipótesis de película sin entender la legítima defensa y el malestar que puede llevar a una persona a defenderse.

En palabras de su red de apoyo:

“A pesar de que cayeron casi todos los agravantes que pidió el fiscal, la condena es insólita en su dureza y no se tuvieron en cuenta las circunstancias atenuantes que pidió la defensa; la de años de abuso y violencia psicológica hacia Lulén por parte de su padre.”

“Aún transitando el dolor y la bronca, estamos dispuestos a seguir a la próxima instancia judicial para lograr un mejor resultado. Seguiremos con actividades para terminar de juntar el dinero para terminar de pagar la defensa y vamos a sostener y abrir la campaña de libertad para Lulén y Max. Porque no aceptamos este fallo y no dejaremos que todo lo que se presenció quede impune.”

“Las vidas Trans importan, y ningún fiscal transodiante ni menos un tribunal discriminatorio nos van a parar o amedrentar.”

author: David Corn
title: A ressaca eleitoral de Trump
content:
É como se os eleitores norte-americanos, depois de uma longa noite de farra, tivessem acordado de ressaca, arrependidos das decisões da noite anterior.




Com os democratas conquistando com facilidade ampla maioria na Câmara dos Representantes (equivalente à Câmara dos Deputados no Brasil) e assumindo o controle do Senado, o eleitorado enviou uma mensagem clara: está cansado de Donald Trump. Em vários estados, os republicanos sofreram uma derrota histórica. Foi um tsunami azul, a cor do Partido Democrata.




Na Carolina do Sul, a democrata Annie Andrews obteve uma vitória surpreendente sobre Darline Graham na disputa pela cadeira no Senado, anteriormente ocupada pelo irmão de Graham. No Texas, o deputado estadual democrata James Talarico derrotou o procurador-geral republicano Ken Paxton na disputa por uma vaga no Senado, enquanto a deputada estadual Gina Hinajosa venceu o governador republicano Greg Abbott. Ela será a primeira governadora latina do estado, onde um democrata não vence o Senado desde 1988.




Na Geórgia, o senador democrata Jon Ossoff foi reeleito com facilidade, e a ex-prefeita de Atlanta Keisha Lance Bottoms foi eleita governadora por ampla margem de votos. 

Ela será a primeira mulher negra a comandar um estado na história dos Estados Unidos.




Os candidatos democratas ao Senado também venceram nos estados republicanos do Meio-Oeste do país, Iowa e Kansas. Já em Ohio, a democrata Amy Acton derrotou Vivek Ramaswamy na disputa pelo governo estadual. Na Flórida, deputados democratas que eram alvos do 

redesenho eleitoral

 feito pelos republicanos nos distritos do estado sobreviveram à disputa. 




Em todo o país, os democratas derrotaram com ampla margem os candidatos republicanos à Câmara em distritos nos quais Trump havia vencido por dois dígitos nas eleições de 2024.




À medida que as notícias desastrosas para Trump e o Partido Republicano se acumulavam, o presidente fez uma série de posts nas redes sociais reclamando da rede de televisão Fox News. Enquanto isso, assessores da Casa Branca tentavam freneticamente lembrar aos jornalistas que Trump não era candidato naquela eleição. Mas há alguns dias, Trump 

disse

: “Peço a todos que finjam que meu nome está na cédula”.




Esses resultados sinalizam que a política repugnante de Trump — baseada em mentiras, enganos, divisão, preconceito, tribalismo, ódio e demagogia, plenamente abraçada pelo Partido Republicano — já não encontra eco na maioria dos americanos. Seus discursos estridentes, nos quais acusa os democratas de serem comunistas que odeiam os EUA, de quererem impor cirurgias de transição de gênero a crianças e de destruir o país, não conseguiram desviar a atenção da maioria dos eleitores. 




As realidades escancaradas do segundo governo Trump são preços elevados, a guerra no Irã — mal conduzida e com objetivos equivocados —, uma cruzada cruel de deportações em massa, uma política econômica errática e improdutiva, corrupção descarada e em larga escala, autoritarismo crescente e doses generosas de caos.  




As eleições de 2026 estabelecem um claro padrão.

 Os eleitores podem cair na conversa de Trump quando ele é candidato, ataca as elites que estão no poder e faz grandes promessas (como a de uma “era de ouro” para os EUA). Mas, na hora de avaliar seu desempenho na Casa Branca, a aprovação desaparece. 




Em 2016 e 2024, ele teve uma boa performance como aspirante à Presidência, desempenhando o papel de herói nacionalista e grande outsider que poderia enfrentar o sistema, confrontar as elites, provocar os liberais e garantir prosperidade. 

Essa encenação — vendida com a convicção de um vigarista e a empolgação de um anunciador de circo — funcionou.




No entanto, Trump na Presidência não impressiona, e suas ações na Casa Branca provocam reações contrárias. Em 2018, os eleitores se voltaram contra ele, e os democratas conquistaram a Câmara dos Representantes. Em 2020, enquanto Trump administrava mal a pandemia de Covid-19, os eleitores o tiraram do poder e entregaram o comando a Joe Biden. Os democratas mantiveram o controle da Câmara e conquistaram a maioria no Senado.




As eleições de meio de mandato de 2026 seguem a mesma tendência. Depois de quase dois anos de crises, autocracia, brutalidade, corrupção, políticas plutocráticas e todo tipo de excentricidade, os eleitores rejeitaram pela terceira vez uma presidência de Trump. 

Isso significa que o republicano nunca recebeu uma avaliação positiva de seu desempenho por parte do eleitorado.




Estas eleições de meio de mandato foram as eleições do dia seguinte. Como mostram os índices de aprovação de Trump, em queda vertiginosa, os eleitores vinham alimentando um profundo arrependimento pela escolha que fizeram. Trump percorreu o país pedindo aos cidadãos que votassem como se seu nome estivesse na cédula. E foi exatamente o que eles fizeram. 




Ele conduziu seu Partido Republicano ao fracasso. Nem mesmo sua tentativa de manipular as regras eleitorais por meio de um redesenho racista dos distritos de votação dos estados conseguiu salvá-lo e seus seguidores fanáticos do Partido Republicano.




Os presidentes dos EUA costumam sofrer derrotas expressivas nas eleições de meio de mandato (levam uma “surra”, como definiu Barack Obama em 2010). Mas, desta vez, foram as próprias decisões e ações de Trump — a guerra no Irã, as 

tarifas

, a criação de uma força policial secreta para prender moradores que respeitam a lei, a destruição de setores fundamentais do governo federal, a devastação dos sistemas públicos de saúde e de pesquisa médica do país, a campanha megalomaníaca para colocar seu nome no Kennedy Center e em outras instituições, entre outras medidas — que fizeram sua impopularidade ultrapassar em muito a tendência histórica.




Trump fez isso consigo mesmo e com seu partido. 

Esta eleição foi um sonoro não ao ICE, à guerra comercial com o Canadá, à aproximação com Vladimir Putin, ao retrocesso democrático

 e à tentativa de tomar a Groenlândia.




Os últimos dias da campanha foram marcados por inúmeros sinais das feridas que Trump provocou em si mesmo. Ele fez um discurso absolutamente bizarro (até para seus padrões) diante do espelho d’água em frente ao Lincoln Memorial, no coração de Washington D.C., no qual se gabou de sua suposta vitória sobre as algas que povoaram a piscina durante uma reforma controversa promovida por seu governo. (Quantos americanos se importavam com isso?) 




Em seus últimos comícios de campanha — realizados em estados republicanos onde, surpreendentemente, os candidatos do partido pareciam vulneráveis —, 

Trump continuou afirmando que a economia estava ótima, fez comentários sobre as bundas das pessoas e disparou declarações islamofóbicas.

 Muitas vezes, divagava de forma desconexa e emitia sons que não chegavam a formar palavras. Não parecia estar bem.




Ao longo da campanha, o presidente dos EUA praticamente não tomou nenhuma medida para responder às preocupações de eleitores que não fossem seguidores do MAGA (“Make America Great Again”, seu movimento político), a não ser oferecer o falso suborno de US$ 5 mil a todos os adultos americanos.




Trump não tinha nada a dizer sobre a crise do custo de vida e chegou a negar que ela existisse, enquanto os democratas, com razão, insistiam repetidamente no tema. Também não abordou a alta dos gastos com saúde e moradia. O republicano argumentou ainda que o valor mais caro da gasolina era um pequeno preço a se pagar pela guerra no Irã, que aparentemente ele não consegue encerrar. 




Durante a campanha, ele fez ainda promessas vazias sobre a redução dos preços dos combustíveis e 

apostou no ódio, demonizando os democratas como radicais e excêntricos antiamericanos.

 Disse que drenaria o “pântano” de Washington, D.C. (em referência ao combate ao 

establishment

 político e ao fim dos malfeitos no governo). Em vez disso, explodiu os diques e deixou o esgoto da corrupção invadir a Casa Branca.




Trump se transformou em um espetáculo de variedades cruel e grotesco. Isso pode funcionar para um candidato, mas não para um presidente.




O vice-presidente JD Vance, sua versão em miniatura, também aderiu à onda de ódio. Em um comício do republicano Vivek Ramaswamy, candidato derrotado ao governo do estado de Ohio e responsável pela 

propaganda mais desprezível

 da campanha eleitoral, Vance bradou: 




“Vi a notícia de que existem comunidades ilegais de imigrantes ilegais somalis que estão se coordenando para inundar as urnas e abafar o seu voto… Queremos que as eleições americanas pertençam aos cidadãos americanos. Enviem uma mensagem votando em Vivek para governador.”




Não havia notícia alguma nesse sentido. Vance estava simplesmente explorando o racismo, talvez como uma prévia de sua campanha presidencial de 2028.




Trump e seu partido despejaram toneladas de desinformação e de porcaria sobre os eleitores americanos. E Elon Musk gastou (na verdade, desperdiçou) quase meio bilhão de dólares para apoiar candidatos republicanos e atacar democratas, com boa parte desse dinheiro destinada ao Texas, para ajudar Ken Paxton, procurador-geral do estado e candidato derrotado ao Senado.




Mas nem mesmo o dinheiro vindo de Marte foi capaz de salvar os republicanos do colapso provocado por Trump. Menos de dois anos após sua volta ao governo, a maioria dos norte-americanos deseja uma mudança de rumo. Eles gostariam de acreditar que a última eleição nunca aconteceu. Mas aconteceu. E muitos danos já foram causados.




Parar de cavar é o primeiro passo para sair do buraco. Este passo já foi dado. Mas a bagunça continua, assim como Trump, ferido, furioso e pronto para provocar ainda mais estragos. A faxina depois da ressaca não termina com esta eleição. Ela está apenas começando.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Providence Becomes Largest US City to Divest From Israel in Historic Vote
content:
The ordinance passed by 75 percent after a months-long grassroots campaign.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

On Tuesday, voters in Providence, Rhode Island, overwhelmingly passed an ordinance requiring the city to divest from companies that enable genocide, apartheid, and human rights violations.

The ordinance is the Palestine solidarity movement’s first binding municipal divestment law passed through popular vote in the U.S. — and makes Providence the largest U.S. city to vote to divest from Israel.

The ordinance, listed on Providence’s ballot as Question 7, passed by 74.99 percent. It calls on the city to “divest from countries and companies profiting from genocide, apartheid, ethnic cleansing and prolonged military occupation,” and became a ballot question due to a sustained, popular campaign led by the Providence for Palestine Coalition over the past year.

“Millions of dollars in Providence city funds are invested in companies facilitating and profiting from the Israeli genocide in Gaza, apartheid system in the occupied West Bank, and ongoing assault on Lebanon and Iran,” Jewish Voice for Peace-Rhode Island explained in a press release. “In addition, Providence has a 20-year history of investing millions in Israel Bonds, which function as direct, no-strings-attached loans to the Israeli government and military.”

Jackie Goldman, a Jewish Voice for Peace organizer and city councilor elect, told Truthout that the ordinance is “the first constituent-led ballot initiative, which is both unique and replicable.”

“It was regular people who said, ‘we are going to create this ordinance, we are going to get enough signatures to get this on the ballot, we are not waiting for our elected officials to do something, we are going to do that work ourselves to make it happen,’” Goldman said.

Goldman said that the ballot initiative evolved from a campaign led by Jewish Voice for Peace-Rhode Island to push Providence to divest from Israel Bonds. When allied city councilors introduced a similar divestment ordinance, it stalled out due to opposition from the outgoing mayor, Democrat Brett Smiley, who is a staunch supporter of Israel.

Goldman is also the first openly trans person to be elected to the Providence City Council. Speaking on the phone with Truthout while canvassing on Tuesday, Goldman repeatedly turned to speak to local residents and explain the importance of Question 7, both in English and in Spanish.

“As it was stalling out, we said, ‘how do we take this into our own hands, and get this on the ballot?’” Goldman said. “And so we talked with some of the folks from Pittsburgh who had done a ballot referendum, and also looked through the various rules in the Providence city charter, and decided to go the ballot initiative way.” Organizers also looked to the example of Somerville, Massachusetts, the first U.S. city to vote to divest from Israel last year.

In Providence, residents must collect 1,000 signatures to put an ordinance before city council — if the council does not pass the ordinance, it can be put on the ballot by collecting around 5,000 additional signatures. The Providence for Palestine coalition — which includes Jewish Voice for Peace-RI, the Democratic Socialists of America-RI, AFT Local 6516, American Muslims for Palestine MA/RI, and Reclaim RI — decided to go to the ballot rather than lobby council members, and ended up collecting over 10,000 signatures, more than double those required.

Adit Sabnis, a graduate student organizer at Brown University in AFT Local 6516, said that organizers at Brown and within Jewish Voice for Peace had “tried to find ways of divesting,” but “our leaders weren’t listening.” So they asked, “how can we take this power and put it into our own hands? How can we make the decision on this, rather than outsourcing it to them?” The coalition decided that “if the leaders won’t listen to us, we’re going to take it straight to the people.”

“What I think is unique is that I have not seen a lot of constituent-led ballot initiatives to try to fundamentally change how cities work. That being said, I know that a lot of city charters have mechanisms like this that will allow for [people in various cities across the U.S.] to be able to do direct democracy,” Goldman said.

“This is so important for the fact that we are in this moment where our elected officials are so often bought by corporate power” or otherwise facing pressure to ignore popular will, Goldman added.

While the outgoing mayor was a staunch supporter of Israel, the primaries brought forward several democratic socialist candidates for council, as well as for mayor. Sabnis explained that the divestment coalition coordinated with the David Morales mayoral campaign to canvass citywide. Throughout the process, the coalition “tried to find ways where we could bring regular people like us to show that we can really make a difference.”

Morales, a democratic socialist, won the election and will now become Providence’s youngest mayor, at age 28.

“This time, we have a majority city council as well as a mayor who are on board with divesting, which means that we will actually enforce this legislation,” Goldman said.

The local divestment campaign dovetailed with a citywide mobilization for rent stabilization, both policy priorities that the outgoing mayor blocked from becoming law and that the wave of progressive candidates made central to their platforms.

“I think it is very clear that the people of Providence want something new and want something different,” Goldman said. “While divestment and some of the issues like rent stabilization are maybe separate, it is similar in that a lot of people are not happy with how the status quo is going.”

The divestment initiative has energized the campaigns of local candidates, strengthened Providence’s organizing movements, and demonstrated that there are ways to mobilize for change beyond electing individuals, Goldman added.

Activists in Providence have managed to connect local struggles with Palestine solidarity organizing. Palestinian community organizer and American Muslims for Palestine member Reem Said-Awad told Truthout that the coalition tied the fight for Palestine to Black Lives Matter and the struggle against Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Over the past three years, more mainstream mobilizations in Providence like No Kings also began speaking about Palestine, she said.

“Things do change, if you are persistent,” Said-Awad said. “Even though we don’t have as many people on the streets right now, people are actively doing things behind the scenes. Awareness is there. Now it’s time for action.”

Sabnis said that the campaign for divestment has been met with an outpouring of support from Providence residents.

“Based on our leaders and politicians, it was very easy over the last two or three years to be very hopeless, and feel like we couldn’t do anything about [the genocide in Gaza],” Sabnis said. “I think the number one thing we saw when we started going out in the community and collecting these signatures is that people were so happy and so thankful that we were organizing around this, but also just thrilled that they could actually do something meaningful for Palestine.”

“So often in the U.S., we’re told that the only way to make our voices heard is to ask elected leaders, and to beg them to abide by some semblance of a moral code,” Sabnis went on. “And so the fact that 10,000 people in Providence, if not more, could … take it all into their own hands, and say, ‘we’re going to reclaim our power. We’re no longer going to ask our leaders to do it if they’re not going to listen to us’ — to me, I think it’s emblematic of how democracy should be.”

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. As Trump attempts to silence dissenting voices, we have no choice but to ask for your help.

We are fundraising today to fund our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: CMI Argentina
title: El rechazo a Trump y el gran triunfo demócrata en ambas cámaras
content:
La oposición tendrá mayoría en el Congreso en los dos últimos años de su gobierno.




Demócratas celebran en Arizona




Por Beverly Fanon-Clay y Mirko Trudeau




El Partido Demócrata consiguió una gran victoria en las elecciones de medio mandato celebradas el martes en Estados Unidos, obteniendo mayorías en las dos cámaras, según las proyecciones, por lo que los dos últimos años del gobierno del presidente Donald Trump serán con un Congreso completamente adverso a sus intereses.




Donald Trump, el 2 de noviembre, en Washington: ¿triste, solitario, final?




La narrativa del presidente estadounidense «elegido por Dios» se ha hecho añicos ante realidades mucho más mundanas: pagar las facturas, llenar el depósito del coche y hacer la compra. La derrota histórica ha venido desde dentro, por lo que aún ha sido más dolorosa. Cinco grandes feudos republicanos y cruciales para el control del Senado le han dado la espalda al presidente estadounidense: Carolina del Norte, Carolina del Sur, Texas, Iowa y Kansas se han teñido de azul.




Los votantes estadounidenses eligieron a su primera gobernadora negra, su primer senador abiertamente gay, el primer senador musulmán y la primera gobernadora indígena en unas elecciones de medio mandato que reflejan un liderazgo cada vez más diverso. Fue una gran reprimenda contra el odio y la división», señaló Bill Shiebler, director de estrategia de la organización no gubernamental State Voices.




Tan importante como la magnitud de la debacle es la responsabilidad por la misma, en la medida en que Trump se empeñó en que los comicios fueran un referendo sobre su persona. A principios de año, nada sugería que los demócratas pudieran hacerse con la mayoría del Congreso; de hecho, todavía en mayo 59 por ciento de los adultos tenían una opinión desfavorable de dicho partido.




Los analistas señalan cuatro factores centrales del resultado electoral: la injerencia de Trump en los procesos internos de los republicanos, en los que impuso a candidatos contra el criterio de las militancias locales, la agresión criminal contra Irán, que rompió la promesa de no meter al país en más guerras interminables en el extranjero que, a su vez, desató una ola inflacionaria y la inhumana e indiscriminada cacería desatada contra los migrantes, sin importar su estatus legal, que enajenó al trumpismo el voto latino, crucial para sus victorias anteriores.




La mejor muestra de este cambio de preferencias entre los descendientes de latinoamericanos se encuentra en Texas, donde James Talarico y Gina Hinojosa aplastaron a sus contrincantes conservadores por márgenes que nadie anticipó en la carrera senatorial y por la gubernatura. En Florida, la ultraderecha estuvo muy cerca de perder su bastión ante proyectos liberales.




James Talarico ofrece un discurso en Austin tras convertirse en el primer senador demócrata elegido por Texas en 38 años




Quizás la principal lección de la derrota rotunda de los republicanos y Donald Trump, para Estados Unidos y el resto del mundo, es que la democracia vive en el país que acaba de celebrar los 250 años de su fundación. No es una lección menor, y ni siquiera era seguro que sucediese dada la aversión de Trump hacia la separación de poderes y su sistemática impugnación del legítimo proceso electoral. .




El partido azul ha recuperado el control del Senado y de la Cámara de Representantes después de imponerse en bastiones republicanos donde las encuestas ni siquiera les daban posibilidades. Uno de los triunfos de la noche es el de Texas, donde Gina Hinojosa se convierte en la primera gobernadora hispana tras derrotar al (ex) todopoderoso Greg Abbott.




En Míchigan, el demócrata Abdul El-Sayed ganó las elecciones al Senado y se ha convertido en el primer musulmán en la Cámara alta. Los republicanos han mantenido el escaño en el Senado por Florida, con el triunfo de Ashley Moody, y Byron Donalds será el primer gobernador negro de ese Estado, que se consolida como principal enclave conservador. “Estoy un poco sorprendido. Pensé que lo haríamos mejor”, ha comentado Trump. Tras admitir la derrota, ha dicho que aceptará los resultados.




El demócrata Xavier Becerra convierte en el primer gobernador de origen latino al frente del Gobierno de California en más de 150 años. «Qué gran noche para ser californiano. Qué gran noche para ser estadounidense, para ser hijo de inmigrantes de la Unión, para estar de pie en la victoria junto a todos vosotros», ha afirmado en su discurso de celebración en Sacramento.




El demócrata Xavier Becerra junto a su esposa Carolina Reyes en Sacramento




La derrota del partido que está en el gobierno en las elecciones de medio término es lo usual en la política estadounidense, en la que el electorado suele castigar al mandatario de turno, pero la caída republicana del martes fue muy importante, lo que seguramente traerá un replanteo interno, más allá de lo que pueda hacer Trump. La contundente victoria de los demócratas se apoyó en varios factores que ya estaban pesando en la ciudadanía a la hora de evaluar al gobierno del magnate republicano, pero lo que más pesó fue la marcha actual de la economía.




El control de las dos cámaras por los demócratas azuza la incertidumbre sobre el auge de la inteligencia artificial. El mercado está analizando si la ola azul implicará una desaceleración de la fuerte apuesta por la IA que están haciendo las empresas tecnológicas, mientras valora un potencial frenazo en la construcción de centros de datos en EE UU, donde los demócratas han vencido en estados clave gracias a una campaña que ha tenido en el punto de mira la fuerte expansión de estas instalaciones.




El precio al alza de la nafta y del diésel, que en este último caso se traslada además a los precios de muchísimos productos, viene generando en todos los estados del país un incremento del costo de vida. Esto sumado al rechazo a la guerra con Irán fueron los factores que pesaron con fuerza a la hora de la votación.




Además, particularmente entre la ciudadanía estadounidense de origen hispano, las cacerías promovidas por el gobierno a través de los agentes del Servicio de Control de Inmigración y Aduanas (ICE, por sus siglas en inglés), también generaron un alejamiento del voto latino por los republicanos.







«Estoy absolutamente dispuesto a aceptar estos resultados», ha afirmado Trump en una entrevista con The New York Times, en la que también ha afirmado que «está dispuesto a trabajar» con los demócratas para llegar a acuerdos en la Cámara de Representantes. «No me presentaba como candidato y, si lo hubiera hecho, ¡habríamos ganado por goleada!», fue la primera reacción del presidente estadounidense al avance del escrutinio. Intenta eludir así su responsabilidad en los resultados de las midterms a medida que se van conociendo los datos de los comicios, convertidos en un plebiscito a su gestión.




Una de las victorias más resonantes de los demócratas se dio en el estado de Texas, un bastión tradicional de los republicanos. Allí, el pastor presbiteriano James Talarico, de 37 años, derrotó de manera contundente a su adversario republicano, el fiscal general del estado, Ken Paxton, un candidato polémico, sobre quien pesan muchas acusaciones de corrupción, pero que tenía el apoyo decidido de Trump.




Talarico, que logró aproximadamente el 60% de los votos, principalmente gracias al apoyo masivo que tuvo en las principales ciudades del estado, Austin, Dallas y Houston, será el primer senador demócrata texano desde 1988, lo que da cuenta de la relevancia de este triunfo.







“Este es un mandato para realizar un cambio grande. Esta noche es el inicio del fin de la era de Trump; mañana empezamos a construir el mejor mundo que seguirá”, declaró el diputado demócrata Greg Casar, presidente del caucus progresista del Congreso.La frase de la jornada fue “ola azul” (el color del Partido Demócrata), otros usaron “tsunami” o “sismo” para calificar la culminación de la elección intermedia.




Antes del cierre de las casillas de votación, Trump había asegurado a CBS News: “yo tengo el poder definitivo; se llama veto”, y afirmó que la Suprema Corte le otorgó “tremendos poderes” sobre agencias federales sin importar quién controle el Congreso. Hasta ahora nadie ha impedido al magnate continuar desestabilizando a su propio país y al resto del planeta. Sin lugar a dudas, el resultado reflejó un repudio a la agenda de Trump.




Pero no todo fueron buenas noticias para la cúpula demócrata ya que varios de los candidatos que ganaron no comparten el consenso del liderazgo centrista de su partido. “Esto se trata del pueblo contra los milmillonarios”, declaró Talarico, quien ahora es el primer demócrata en ganar una curul en el Senado federal por Texas desde 1988. Candidatos al Senado en Maine, Michigan y Florida también definieron sus contiendas como luchas contra los milmillonarios y sus intentos de “comprar” esta democracia, algo que no comparte el liderazgo que acepta donaciones de los ricos.




Confrontado por una alta tasa de desaprobación el año pasado, Trump presionó a Texas y Florida para manipular sus mapas electorales y elegir a otros cinco republicanos más. Pero en ambos estados, esos esfuerzos parecieron fracasar por completo, con casi todas esas curules que habían sido dibujadas para republicanos acabando en manos demócratas. Al irse revelando los resultados de esta noche, el presidente comentó a The New York Times que “absolutamente estoy dispuesto” a aceptar los resultados de la elección. “Bueno, estoy esperando trabajar con ellos (los demócratas). Probablemente resolveremos algo”.




Beverly Fanon-Clay y Mirko Trudeau son periodistas estadounidenses del Centro Latinoamericano de Análisis Estratégico (CLAE)







Fuente: 

https://estrategia.la/2026/11/04/el-rechazo-a-trump-y-el-gran-triunfo-democrata-en-ambas-camaras/




La entrada 

El rechazo a Trump y el gran triunfo demócrata en ambas cámaras

 se publicó primero en 

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

.

author: Mag
title: Nach zehn Jahren Kampf: Angleichung an den Tarifvertrag der Länder bei Berliner Assistenzbetrieben
content:
Dossier




„Nach der fünften Verhandlungsrunde zwischen ver.di und den beiden größten Berliner Assistenzbetrieben ambulante dienste e.V. und Neue Lebenswege GmbH wurde am 16. Mai 2019 eine Tarifeinigung erzielt. Mehr als 1000 Mitarbeiter/innen in der persönlichen Assistenz wird jetzt die Angleichung an den Tarifertrag der Länder (TVL) ermöglicht. (…) Die Tarifparteien konnten sich nun auf die Entgeltgruppe 5 des TVL einigen. (…) Auch alle anderen Mitarbeiter/inn/en sollen in die Entgeltordnung des TVL überführt werden. (…) Die Tarifeinigung wurde mit einem Refinanzierungsvorbehalt versehen, welcher noch von Verhandlungen mit dem Berliner Senat und den Pflegekassen abhängt…”

 

Pressemitteilung von ver.di Berlin-Brandenburg vom 24. Mai 2019

 

 sowie Hintergründe und dazu:







Finanzierung Persönlicher Assistenz bis Mitte 2027 verlängert – jetzt braucht es dauerhafte Sicherheit im Koalitionsvertrag 

 


„

Schon seit mehreren Jahren kämpfen Menschen mit Assistenzbedarf und deren Beschäftigten für ein langfristige Sicherung ihrer Finanzierung. Zuletzt war diese durch eine Fachliche Weisung der Sozialsenatorin bis Ende 2026 abgesichert worden. Diese Weisung ist nun bis Mitte 2027 verlängert worden.


ver.di Berlin-Brandenburg begrüßt die Entscheidung von Sozialsenatorin Cansel Kiziltepe. Damit konnte kurzfristig verhindert werden, dass die bestehende Regelung ausläuft und für Beschäftigte, Arbeitgeber*innen und Menschen mit Assistenzbedarf erhebliche Unsicherheiten entstehen. Gemeinsam mit der Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Arbeitgeber*innen mit persönlicher Assistenz (AAPA e. V.) hatte sich ver.di für eine schnelle Lösung eingesetzt. Die Verlängerung verschafft nun Zeit, um die noch offenen Fragen zur Refinanzierung zu klären. Insbesondere die vollständige Anerkennung und Refinanzierung des geltenden Tarifvertrags bleibt dabei zentral.


Die jetzt gefundene Übergangslösung darf allerdings keine dauerhafte Unsicherheit verlängern. ver.di erwartet, dass die Gespräche mit der Senatsverwaltung zeitnah fortgesetzt werden

…“ 

Pressemitteilung vom 4.11.2026 beim ver.di-Landesbezirk Berlin-Brandenburg

 




Unwürdige Blockade auf Kosten behinderter Menschen endlich beenden: Erneut protestierten Arbeitgeber:innen und ihre Assistenzen in Berlin für gerechte Bezahlung 







Behinderte Arbeitgeber in Berlin wollen mehr zahlen




„

Am Dienstag forderten Arbeitgeber mit Behinderung und ihre Assistenzen eine gerechte Bezahlung. Auch zu einer Besetzung sind sie wieder bereit.




»Ich hätte mich eigentlich gerne woanders mit dir getroffen«, sagt Tabea Michel zu Saskia Class. »Irgendwo, wo man sich netter unterhalten kann.« Die Flure des Landesamts für Gesundheit und Soziales (Lageso) sind zwar kein einladender Ort für ein Gespräch unter Freundinnen, aber die beiden Frauen sind am Dienstag für etwas anderes vor Ort. Gemeinsam mit knapp 30 anderen Personen statten sie der Abteilung Persönliche Assistenz im siebten Stock einen »unbefristeten Besuch« ab, wie es im Aufruf des Berliner Bündnisses für ein selbstbestimmtes Leben heißt. Mit der Besetzung möchten sie erreichen, was bereits im Dezember 2025 im Berliner Abgeordnetenhaus beschlossen wurde: eine gerechte Bezahlung für persönliche Assistenzkräfte.


»Es tut natürlich weh, wenn man weiß, woanders könnte man für dieselbe Arbeitsleistung mehr Geld verdienen«, sagt Tim. Er ist seit elf Jahren als persönlicher Assistent für Menschen mit Behinderung tätig, wird allerdings anders als seine Kolleg*innen, die bei Assistenzdiensten angestellt sind, nicht nach der tariflich festgelegten Entgeltgruppe 5 bezahlt. (…)


»Es gibt gar keinen Geduldsfaden mehr, der reißen kann«, zitiert Michael Theben seine Mitstreiter*innen. Im November 2025 besetzten Arbeitgeber*innen und ihre Assistent*innen über 24 Stunden die Senatssozialverwaltung, bis Senatorin Cansel Kiziltepe (SPD) ins Gespräch mit der Finanzverwaltung trat. Die Gleichbezahlung ab dem Jahr 2026 wurde auch im Abgeordnetenhaus beschlossen. Eine fachliche Weisung der Senatorin ging laut dem Bündnis für ein selbstbestimmtes Leben Ende März beim Lageso ein, wurde aber noch nicht umgesetzt. Nach den vielen Verzögerungen und Vertröstungen heißt es am Dienstag aus der Menge: »Ohne eine schriftliche Zusage gehen wir hier nicht raus.«

…“ 

Artikel von Hannah Blumberg vom 19.05.2026 in ND online

 




Unwürdige Blockade auf Kosten behinderter Menschen endlich beenden




„… 

ver.di Berlin-Brandenburg kritisiert die bis heute ausbleibende Umsetzung der entsprechenden Fachlichen Weisung in aller Schärfe.




Nach Informationen, die ver.di vorliegen wurde die entsprechende Fachliche Weisung bereits am 31. März 2026 an das Landesamt für Gesundheit und Soziales (LAGeSo) übermittelt. Dennoch wurde die notwendige Umsetzung bis heute nicht vollzogen. Damit werden höhere Löhne für Persönliche Assistentinnen im Arbeitgeberinnen-Modell nach Entgeltgruppe 5 (EG 5) weiterhin verhindert. Die Blockadehaltung der beteiligten Stellen führt dazu, dass behinderte Menschen und ihre Persönlichen Assistent*innen weiterhin benachteiligt werden. Ein demokratisch gefasster Beschluss des Berliner Abgeordnetenhauses darf jedoch nicht durch Untätigkeit in nachgeordneten Verwaltungen ausgehebelt werden

…“ 

Pressemitteilung vom 18.05.2026 vom ver.di-Landesbezirk Berlin-Brandenburg

 










»Die Situation ist zermürbend, es geht um unser Leben, es ist existenziell«: Persönliche Assistenz und das Warten auf den Berliner Senat




„

Persönliche Assistenzen und Menschen mit Behinderung wollen, dass die Senatssozialverwaltung ihre Versprechen einlöst




Gleicher Lohn für gleiche Arbeit – dafür kämpfen Menschen mit Behinderung und ihre persönlichen Assistent*innen in Berlin schon lange. Im Dezember hatten sie endlich Erfolg: Die Berliner Abgeordneten ergänzten den Entwurf des Haushalts für 2026 und 2027 um den Hinweis, dass die Assistenzkräfte genauso viel Geld erhalten sollen wie ihre nach Tarifvertrag bezahlten Kolleg*innen. Doch für die konkrete Umsetzung muss die Senatssozialverwaltung unter Senatorin Cansel Kiziltepe (SPD) eine fachliche Weisung erlassen. Dass das noch nicht geschehen ist, führt zu großer Verunsicherung bei den Arbeitgeber*innen und den Assistenzkräften.




»Die Situation ist zermürbend, es geht um unser Leben, es ist existenziell«, sagt Jules Butzek zu »nd«. Butzek ist Teil der Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Arbeitgeber*innen mit Persönlicher Assistenz. Zusammen mit anderen Arbeitgeber*innen und den Assistent*innen besetzte Butzek im November 24 Stunden lang das Gebäude der Sozialverwaltung, um eine angemessene Bezahlung der Assistenzkräfte durchzusetzen. Dass trotz aller Anstrengungen und dem Beschluss der Abgeordneten immer noch keine Klarheit über die Entlohnung der Assistent*innen in diesem Jahr besteht, ärgert Butzek. »Es besteht eine große Unsicherheit für alle, das Lageso handelt total unteschiedlich.« (…)


Neben der Höhe der Entlohnung ist es den Arbeitgeber*innen wichtig, dass in der neuen Weisung die Reglementierungen bezüglich der Budgetbegleitung, Einarbeitung, Teambesprechungen und Kalkulation der Krankentage zurückgenommen werden, sagt Butzek. »Der individuelle Bedarf ist entscheidend.« So stellt es auch die Bundesarbeitsgemeinschaft dar: »Das Persönliche Budget ist so zu bemessen, dass der individuell festgestellte Bedarf und die erforderliche Beratung und Unterstützung erfolgen kann. Demzufolge verbieten sich pauschale Vorgaben bezüglich Budgetassistenz, Einarbeitung und Dienstbesprechungen.«

“ 

Artikel von Lola Zeller vom 02.02.2026 in ND online

 

 („Arbeitgeber mit Behinderung warten auf den Berliner Senat“)




Gleicher Lohn für Persönliche Assistenz in Berlin: Abgeordnetenhaus sichert Arbeitgebermodell ab, fachliche Weisung muss allerdings schnell folgen




„

Selbstbestimmtes Leben produzieren – Erfolg nach zehn Jahren Kampf: In der Persönlichen Assistenz in Berlin gilt jetzt der Tarifvertrag der Länder




“Bei den Assistenzbetrieben Neue Lebenswege GmbH und ambulante dienste e.V. in Berlin mit zusammen etwa tausend Beschäftigten ist es im April und Mai gelungen, zwei der ersten Haustarifverträge in der Persönlichen Assistenz durchzusetzen – mit beinahe vollständiger Angleichung an den Tarifvertrag der Länder (TVL). Violetta Bock sprach mit KLAUS DRECHSEL, Tarifkommissionsmitglied bei ambulante dienste (ad), über die Ergebnisse und wie sie im Laufe von zehn Jahren dorthin kamen. (…) [Wie sind die Arbeitsbedingungen?] Im Tarifprozess haben wir um den schwierigen Teil der Arbeitsbedingungen eine Klammer gemacht. Das Grundproblem bei ad sind die Nullstundenarbeitsverträge. Da hat der Gesetzgeber mittlerweile nachgebessert, indem laut Teilzeit- und Befristungsgesetz nun automatisch zwanzig Wochenstunden vereinbart sind, wenn keine Stundenzahl eingetragen ist. Unser Arbeitgeber unterläuft das mit Zehn-Stunden-Verträgen. Dann gibt es im Konzept der Persönlichen Assistenz die Wahlfreiheit: einE AssistenznehmerIn kann sich aussuchen, wer bei ihm die Dienstleistung erbringt. Das ist nachvollziehbar, begründet für die Assistentin aber eine prekäre Situation, etwa wenn sie oder er in Ungnade fällt und dann plötzlich ihr Monatseinkommen verliert. [Was habt ihr erreicht?] Das gesamte materielle Volumen des TVL ist jetzt wirksam: Zuschläge, Zulagen, Jahressonderzahlungen, Urlaubsanspruch, Zusatzurlaubsanspruch, Wechselschichtzulagen. Nicht alle, aber ziemlich viele aus verschiedenen Funktionsgruppen haben durch eine andere Entgeltgruppe eine Aufwertung erfahren. Die AssistentInnen waren in der Gehaltsgruppe 3 und sind jetzt in der Gehaltsgruppe 5. Nur bei den Überstunden haben wir eine Sonderregelung getroffen. Das hat mit der spezifischen Struktur unseres Betriebes zu tun. Geschätzt haben wir jetzt also 300 bis 500 Euro mehr im Monat. Das ist ein ganz schön dicker Brocken und entsprechend groß ist die Freude. Unser Ergebnis strahlt definitiv positiv aus, nicht nur in Berlin, sondern auch bundesweit findet es in diesem Feld Beachtung, insbesondere die Entgeltgruppe 5. Was es als relevante Größe sonst noch in Berlin gibt, ist das Arbeitgebermodell über das persönliche Budget. Die Beschäftigten in diesem Modell haben noch die Gruppe 3, sie haben keine Tarifbindung und damit auch nicht bestimmte Zulagen. Dort gibt es nun Bemühungen in Richtung Gleichstellung. [Ihr habt zwei Haustarifverträge gemeinsam durchgesetzt?] Wir haben in Berlin eine gemeinsame Betriebsgruppe in der Persönlichen Assistenz. Die Tarifkommissionen, die im August 2018 gewählt wurden, sind getrennt. Die Tarifverhandlungen wurden im wesentlichen gemeinsam geführt. Zum Schluss war bei der Lebenswege GmbH der Prozess schwieriger, so dass es dort noch ein paar separate Verhandlungen gab. Grundsätzlich war unser Herangehen als Beschäftigte: Zusammen sind wir stärker, das hat sich auch die ganze Zeit als roter Faden durchgezogen…“

Das wurde am Dienstagabend auf einer vom Verdi- Landesbezirk organisierten Diskussionsveranstaltung deutlich. Für Enttäuschung sorgte die kurzfristige Absage des Vorstands der AOK Nordost, Frank Michalek – von ihm war eine Aussage zur Refinanzierung des Tarifvertrags erhofft worden. Sozialsenatorin Elke Breitenbach (Linke) und Gesundheitssenatorin Dilek Kalayci (SPD) bedachten die Beschäftigten für ihren Kampf um einen Tarifvertrag mit Lob und Glückwünschen. Auf die Frage eines persönlichen Assistenten, ob der Senat die Finanzierungslücke übernehmen würde, wenn die Krankenkasse weiter auf Zeit spielen, wollten die Senatorinnen allerdings keine konkreten Zusagen geben. Verdi-Gewerkschaftssekretär Max Bitzer rief in einer engagierten Rede die AssistenznehmerInnen auf, ihre Leuchtturmfunktion wahrzunehmen und weitere Beschäftigte zum Kampf für Tarifverträge zu motivieren. Am 10. Oktober ist eine Kundgebung vor dem Sitz der AOK Nord geplant. Damit soll der Druck auf die Krankenkasse erhöht werden, sich einer Refinanzierung des Tarifvertrags nicht in den Weg zu stellen, damit der Tarifvertrag endlich in Kraft treten kann

.“ 

Bericht vom 5.9.2019 von und bei Peter Nowak

 

 von der Podiumsdiskussion am Dienstag, 3. September 2019 in Berlin: „Persönliche Assistenz stärken, Tarifverträge sind zu refinanzieren“:










Podiumsdiskussion am Dienstag, 3. September 2019 in Berlin: „Persönliche Assistenz stärken, Tarifverträge sind zu refinanzieren“  


„

Seit dem 16. Mai 2019 warten die mehr als 1.000 persönlichen Assistent/inn/en für Menschen mit Behinderungen von Ambulante Dienste e.V. und Neue Lebenswege GmbH auf die Umsetzung des im Mai von den Tarifparteien unterschriebenen Tarifvertrages. Der Tarifvertrag wurde unter Refinanzierungsvorbehalt gestellt, und die Vergütungsverhandlungen mit den Pflegekassen und dem Senat lassen auf sich warten. Deshalb lädt ver.di zu einer Podiumsdiskussion am Dienstag, dem 03. September 2019, in der Zeit von 19:00 Uhr bis 20:30 Uhr. Die Senatorin für Integration, Arbeit und Soziales Elke Breitenbach und die Senatorin für Gesundheit, Pflege und Gleichstellung, Dilek Kalayci werden sprechen. Der Vorstand der AOK-Nordost, Frank Michalak wurde eingeladen. Weiter werden für die Geschäftsführungen Uta Wehde, für die Assistenznehmer/innen Hans Werner Fuhlroth und für die Tarifkommissionen Michael Teumer und Jan Lensing sprechen. Moderieren wird die Geschäftsführerin des Vereins demokratische Ärzte Dr. Nadja Rakowitz. Im Fokus stehen die Fragen der Anerkennung der persönlichen Assistenz für Menschen mit Behinderungen, der Tarifautonomie und der Umsetzung von Tarifverträgen bei Freien Trägern in Berlin

…“

author: La Zarzamora
title: Indignación ante ataque a Mujeres Trans en Palermo en medio de oleada fascista en Argentina
content:
A una semana de la marcha del orgullo, la noche del sábado 31 de octubre, un grupo de entre 50 y 60 jóvenes y adolescentes varones se organizaron a través de un grupo de Whasapp para atacar, agredir y violentar en masa a trabajadoras sexuales Trans y Travestis que se encontraban en Los Bosques de Palermo.

Llegaron llenos de ira, violencia y rabia, arriba de sus bicicletas, denostando a las travestis por su trabajo; usando palos con clavos, piedras, tirándoles vidrios y conos de tránsito. Y no se quedaron ahí, para mayor crueldad, uno de ellos, mientras corrían detrás de las mujeres, fue grabando y registrando todo lo ocurrido para después subirlo a redes sociales. En el video mencionaban con total naturalidad e impunidad la idea de ‘’ir a cazar travas’’ alcanzando más de 700.000 vistas, con comentarios transódicos, mofándose y celebrando el hecho.

Muchas de las mujeres que fueron atacadas por este grupo de adolescentes se encuentran con heridas, golpes y el trauma de haber vivido este despreciable hecho. Para la comunidad travesti de Argentina esto no es más que un resultado o consecuencia de los naturalizados discursos de odio hacia la comunidad LGBTIQ+, ya que baja ni más ni menos que desde la presidencia de Argentina.

Como ejemplo el discurso de Milei en el 2025 World Economic Forum, en el que niega la existencia Trans, mencionando que serían ‘’hombres disfrazados de mujer’’. Además, menciona algunos casos de violencia dentro de la comunidad de personas condenadas para generalizar hechos delictivos para toda la comunidad: ‘’porque en sus versiones más extremas la ideología de género constituye lisa y llanamente abuso infantil: son pedófilos’’, estableció, generalizando y denostando a toda una comunidad con su transodio presidencial.

Mientras tanto y en paralelo el mismo presidente apoya y avala al Estado genocida de Israel, haciéndole alabanzas a pesar de que han matado a miles de niñeces, han violado mujeres, infancias y destruido a todo un territorio.

Además es amigo de Trump quien está relacionado al ‘’Caso Epstein’’ donde un grupo de hombres violaba y asesinaba a mujeres en una isla.

Milei ha instalado la naturalización del odio hacia las personas Trans, mujeres, homosexuales y fomentando el odio hacia toda la comunidad, por lo que esto no sería más que los resultados de los discursos fascistas y totalitarios clásicos frente a la realidad, imponiendo una idea de lo ‘’bueno’’ y lo ‘’malo’’, e instalando en el imaginario la idea de que unas personas son mejores que otras, o que unas pueden estar por encima de otras.

Igual que en el patriarcado más antiguo, que parece antiguo, pero es más actual que nunca, las cacerías existen, las violaciones en manada o el aumento de los femicidios a mujeres, Travestis y Mujeres Trans, tan solo en octubre en el mismo país se registraron 39 femicidios en 31 días.

Por lo mismo dentro de la comunidad LGBT+ existe un repudio total ante lo ocurrido y ante el Estado y su funcionamiento histórico que es en desmedro de las comunidades excluidas, disidencias y animales.

También llaman a la organización y a cuidarse en colectividades para enfrentar y defenderse de la violencia cotidiana.
