Interestingly, Most reflects on propaganda activities as a whole, among other things, in his thoughts on “Labor Day,” which he understands as “the day of agitation par excellence in the spirit of the social revolution”—and has quite precise ideas about how it should be used for propaganda purposes, rather than “a day of rest imposed at the workers’ expense, on which they are permitted to go for a walk with the express permission of the police” (Most 2006Bj: 92) . He also reflects on anarchist publications, their dissemination, and their propagandistic impact (Most 2006Bv: 184–188, Most 2006Bw: 189f.).

[6] Their own organizational concepts arise from resistance to the global order of domination, as exemplified by the Zapatistas, whose 1994 uprising is regarded as a milestone for more recent emancipatory social movements (Graeber 2009a: xiii–xvii) . Consensus-based, direct-democratic, and autonomous forms of organization are thus present worldwide as starting points for alternative forms of society (Graeber 2007e: 329ff.) and, for example, consensus-based decision-making is by no means extraordinary, but rather “typical of societies where there would be no way to compel a minority to agree with a majority decision; either because there is no state with a monopoly on coercive force, or because the state has no interest in or does not tend to intervene in local decision-making” (ibid.: 341). Elections, on the other hand, according to Graeber, create marginalized minorities, thereby causing humiliation and hatred and destroying the community. Instead, we must see ourselves as capable agents and constitute ourselves as such in order to take action: “To begin to free ourselves, the first thing we need to do is to see ourselves again as historical actors, as people who can make a difference in the course of world events. This is exactly what the militarization of history is trying to take away” (Graeber 2011: 383). By “militarization of history,” Graeber means, in this context, the authoritarian political enforcement of neoliberal capitalism, which, through bureaucratic apparatuses, creates a sense of hopelessness regarding alternative futures (ibid.: 382).

[7] Slavoj Žižek, on the other hand, assesses the potential of emancipatory social movements quite differently. He regards the activism cultivated within these movements as illusory or, in a sense, as part of the dominant order of power. He writes: “If one responds to a call to action today, this action does not take place in a vacuum, but within the hegemonic ideological coordination [...]. Nevertheless, it is precisely this form of activity that serves as a perfect example of interpassivity—of doing certain things not to achieve something, but to prevent anything from actually happening, to prevent anything fundamental from changing” (Žižek 2002: 18f.).

[8] Bookchin noted as early as 20 years before Graeber that there was “the danger that the revolutionary project might lose its identity, its capacity for self-definition, and its sense of direction.” Today we are not only witnessing a loss of revolutionary acumen, but also experiencing an inability to define what is really meant by the term ‘revolutionary change’ and by concepts such as ‘capitalism’“ (Bookchin 1990: 123). Drawing on the New Left, which emerged in the early 1960s, he reflects on the recurring dynamic between the expansion of autonomy and the containment of social movements, noting that the “concept of ‘participatory democracy’ to describe grassroots control over all aspects of life—not just political ones—became very fashionable. [... The] New Left, and to a considerable extent the counterculture that emerged alongside it, had a strong anti-parliamentary orientation that often bordered on total anarchism” (ibid.: 141).

[9] Most thus takes issue with Marxism, which he describes as a quasi-religious doctrine; he regards it as “unscientific ” and outdated, declares the application of scientific thinking to history to be inadmissible, and, above all, criticizes the theory of impoverishment—widespread in his time—which he argues leads to fatalism and serves to contain an autonomous labor movement (Most 2006Bk: 104–107). The Social Democrats, he argues, are “trapped in prejudice” (Most 2006Bm: 209–216). “In the ‘century in which we live,’ are the views heard in the circles of the organized proletariat dogmas; are the parties and corporations of the working class churches? If that is the case, then of course we must feel like ‘heretics’ [...]” (Most 2006At: 165).

[10] One might ask, then, why he so vehemently insists on the necessity of a violent overthrow in opposition to those he calls “noble anarchists” (Most 2006Bp: 131–134). One might speculate that desire is the father of thought when Most believes that the concentration of capital in large corporations (“trustism”)—and thus the intensification of class antagonism—is a lever for social revolution (Most 2006Bo: 127–130)—a revolution that is by no means hindered by the emergence of a new middle class but, on the contrary, is rather promoted and spurred on to “fighting spirit” (Most 2006Bq: 135ff.). He is wrong on both counts and evidently clings to conventional models that must be considered outdated at this point. Even if it does not apply in this case, his (vulgar-Marxist) derivation of the necessity of social revolution from the mode of production and social structure is interesting.

[11] Giuseppe Ciancabilla attempts to master this balancing act; unlike most other individualist anarchists and insurrectionists, he does not reject political struggle but, on the contrary, addresses it in its only possible form: as a consistent revolutionary struggle. In doing so, he opposes the principle of authority in any form under the conditions of an authoritarian society. By “politics,” he means the struggle against government and the state (Ciancabilla 1899).

title: “Vatandaşın hakkı olan 615 milyon doları BYD’den tahsil edin”
content:
Yeni Parti Zonguldak Milletvekili Deniz Yavuzyılmaz, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, BYD’ye sağlanan yatırım teşviklerini ve vergi muafiyetlerini gündeme taşıdı.

BYD’ye sağlanan vergi muafiyetleri nedeniyle kamunun 615 milyon doların üzerinde kayba uğradığını iddia eden Yavuzyılmaz, “AKP’nin, Çinli otomotiv devi BYD’ye 615 milyon dolar vergi kıyağı yaptığını tespit ettik! Peki nasıl? 5 Temmuz 2024’te; Ticaret Bakanlığı, BYD’ye yapacağı kıyaklara giden yolun taşlarını döşemeye başlıyor. Yatırım teşvik belgesi kapsamında yapılan ithalatı ek gümrük vergilerinden muaf tutuyor. Üç gün sonra 8 Temmuz 2024’te; BYD ile Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanlığı arasında, 1 milyar dolarlık yatırım taahhüdü üzerinden bir ‘yatırım anlaşması’ imzalanıyor. Ancak süreç boyunca: BYD ile imzalanan yatırım anlaşmasının detayları kamuoyundan gizleniyor” dedi.

BYD’ye verilen teşvik belgesinin sır gibi saklandığını söyleyen Yavuzyılmaz, “10 Haziran 2026’da; BYD, Türkiye’de yapmayı taahhüt ettiği Manisa yatırımı için takvim bulunmadığını ve projeyi askıya aldığını açıklıyor. Peki BYD, yatırım anlaşmanın imzalandığı Temmuz 2024’ten, yatırımı askıya aldığı Haziran 2026’ya kadar ne yaptı? İmtiyazlı şekilde, devasa vergi indirimi avantajlarıyla Türkiye’de tam 59.168 adet araç sattı. AKP eliyle, otomotiv sektöründeki adil rekabet ortamı paramparça edildi. Sonuç: Vergi kaybı tutarı 615 milyon dolar! Güncel kurla yaklaşık 30 milyar lira! Nasıl hesapladım? Ticaret Bakanlığı’nın BYD’ye sağladığı vergisiz ithalat hakkı kapsamında; Araç başı gümrük öncesi fiyat ortalama 11.500 dolar alındığında; Gümrük vergisi, ek vergi muafiyeti ve bu muafiyetlerin ÖTV ile KDV matrahlarına zincirleme etkisi hesaplandığında toplam vergi kaybı 615 milyon doları aşıyor” ifadelerini kullandı.

Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanı Mehmet Fatih Kacır’a çağrıda bulunan Yavuzyılmaz, “Ya BYD’nin taahhüt ettiği fabrikayı derhal kurdurun ya da teşvik belgesini iptal edip sağlanan tüm destekleri derhal geri alın. Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat’a: Çin menşeili araç vergilerinden BYD’yi muaf tutan düzenlemeleri hemen yürürlükten kaldırın. Zamanaşımı süresi dolmadan, devletin ve vatandaşın hakkı olan 615 milyon doları faiziyle birlikte BYD’den tahsil edin” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: St’át’imc Chiefs Council challenges Ottawa’s pipeline plans in court
content:
A group of First Nations in British Columbia announced they have filed a federal court application for a judicial review of the federal government’s decision to fast-track the proposed Pacific Link oil pipeline between Alberta and BC as a “project of national interest.” In a press conference held in Richmond B.C. this morning, members of the St’át’imc Chiefs Council — representing eleven Nations of the St’át’imc people (also known as Lilloee) —decried what they called a lack of consultation and stressed the need for the courts to slow the developmental process.

Chief Bonnie Adolph of the Sekw’el’was (Cayoose Creek) First Nation began by outlining threats to the salmon upon which her people rely. She said that when her community wrote to the Major Projects Office asking to be consulted about listing the project under the Build Canada Act, they were told since their land was not on the proposed pipeline route, the Crown would not consult with them.

“When we told the Major Projects Office their narrow geographic approach failed to account for downstream, interconnected and cumulative environmental risks to our inherent St’át’imc title and rights,” Adolph said, “We were told that we could send comments like any member of the public, but not as a First Nation whom the Crown had a legal [duty] to consult. This is not lawful, this is not constitutional, this is not consistent with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous People.”

The salmon central to the lives of St’át’imc people are all over the waters threatened by an oil spill from the pipeline, said Chief Travis Peters from N’Quatqua (Anderson Lake) First Nation.

“The salmon we rely upon travel the Fraser Estuary and the Fraser River twice,” he explained. “Once, as juveniles heading out to the ocean, and [again] as adults returning home to spawn. There are salmon in the river system almost all year. The idea of the construction of new crude oil infrastructure in the heart of the Fraser River Estuary on unstable soil is terrifying.

“What happens if there’s an earthquake? What happens if the pipeline leaks? What happens if the tankers run aground?”

Peters noted that 100 First Nations signed the 2010 Save the Fraser Declaration, but “if anything, the health of the Fraser River salmon has only worsened since 2010. The cumulative impacts of climate change and development have become more severe.”

Chief Justin Kane from Ts’kw’aylaxw First Nation (formerly Pavilion Indian Band), who is also Chair for the St’át’imc Chiefs Council, said the Chiefs Council filed for a judicial review because the federal court failed to meet its constitutional duties to St’át’imc.

“We know this project could have serious, potentially catastrophic risks for our fishing rights and way of life,” he told media. “Salmon is part of who we are. It’s part of our identity. And we have the right to understand what those risks are and to be immediately consulted about whether they are actually working.”

The federal government forced the Chiefs’ hands, Kane said, by insisting that the only question is how — and not if — the project will go ahead.

“If this decision is not challenged in court,” Kane argued, “it sets a dangerous precedent all Canadians should be concerned about. It is foolhardy for the government to try to push through a project at breakneck speed without proper assessment and consultation. Canada is attempting to circumvent its own laws, and ours.”

He said Ottawa has said it would consult with First Nations later, despite the fact that the project is moving ahead.

“Because the Pacific Link is listed under the Building Canada Act,” he said, “the Act says it must be granted a conditional document that is deemed to be all environmental approvals for the project. How can the future of consultation be meaningful if the decision is already made?”

Hugh Braker is a member of Tseshaht First Nation on Vancouver Island as well as of the First Nations Summit Political Executive.

In his statement to media, Braker noted that Mark Carney has said repeatedly that taking action to protect against climate change is “a moral duty.”

“Those were his words,” Braker said. “And what’s he doing about it? He’s building a pipeline. Probably the worst thing he could do. Our prime minister wears a coat of hypocrisy. And he has to realize that. He has to realize that things like life expectancy are going down because of climate change.”

Braker added that First Nations have already issued a climate-change document (the BC First Nations Climate Strategy and Action Plan) that the province of British Columbia has adopted.

“But here comes the pipeline,” Braker said. “So really, there needs to be a solid answer from the prime minister, why he said that everyone has a moral duty when it comes to climate change, but he apparently is exempt. I need to hear from him why that is.”

BC Assembly of First Nations Regional Chief Terry Teegee noted the importance of speaking up not only about the Pacific Link pipeline, but also Bill C-39, Bill C-5, the Building Canada Act and the Building Canada Strong Act.

“I had the opportunity to present to the many Senators our concerns of an untenable review process of one project, one review, one year,” Teegee said. “It bypasses the meaning of what consultation is, the meaning of the United Nations Declaration Act and free, prior and informed consent. This project being pre-approved does not meet the standard of not only a free, prior and informed consent, but the minimum standard of consultation.”

In the near future, Teegee predicted, conflict between First Nations and the federal government will escalate.

“And it’s not just First Nations,” he said. “It’s the unions that I’ve seen that are developing a war room. It’s the youth that are raising their voices about climate change. It’s many of our First Nations here in British Columbia that are concerned about not only the environment, but also the minimum standards of the [provincial] Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, and also the United Nations Declaration Act federally.”

Grand Chief Stewart Phillip (Sylix Nation) of the Union of BC Indian Chiefs decried political and social attitudes dismissive of Indigenous rights and title.

“Canadians and British Columbians absolutely refuse to recognize our rights,” he said, “our rights that are international in nature, that are enshrined in the Constitution and have been upheld by the Supreme Court of Canada on so many different occasions. Yet Canadians still have this backward, ignorant notion that somehow that’s not important, that’s not real.”

Phillip framed the Pacific Link as a project created in partnership between Prime Minister Carney and Alberta premier Danielle Smith.

“It’s the same pipeline that we fought with Enbridge and Kinder Morgan,” he argued, “just a different location. So again, my fundamental basic message to the corporations is buyers beware when you invest in British Columbia, because we’re not standing down. We’re not stepping back. We have the colour of right on our side inherently, constitutionally and legally. And we’ll be back in the courtrooms again.”

Jesse joined APTN as a producer after 16 years as a print and web journalist. During seven of those years, he covered the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee for community newsmagazine The Nation. Jesse’s writing on Indigenous issues has also appeared in Canadian Geographic, the Toronto Star, the Rover, The Eastern Door, Metro, and the Huffington Post.

author: Jake Johnson
title: Mamdani Threatens Trump Admin With Legal Action Over ICE’s Use of Parking Lots
content:
Agents’ use of city parking lots to stage raids amounted to “unlawful commandeering” of public property, he asserted.

Agents’ use of city parking lots to stage raids amounted to “unlawful commandeering” of public property, he asserted.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday threatened the Trump administration with legal action over federal immigration agents’ use of city parking lots to stage raids, which the Democratic elected official said amounted to “unlawful commandeering” of public property.

“This use of city property in furtherance of federal immigration enforcement is unauthorized and is therefore illegal, endangers city residents, and sows fear among those who seek to access city property,” Mamdani wrote in a letter addressed to U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) acting director, David Venturella.

Mamdani’s letter notes that ICE agents have “reportedly parked their vehicles and conducted meetings in several city-owned, unstaffed parking lots” — including ones near a park and a city-run preschool.

“ICE has not secured any authorization from the city to use these lots for immigration enforcement. To be clear: the city does not authorize ICE using its property in this manner,” Mamdani wrote. “Parking lots connected to city parks are reserved for the safe use and enjoyment of New Yorkers and visitors who wish to use our parks. Use of these lots for other purposes, including ICE’s reported use of these lots, amounts to unauthorized activity on City property. Accordingly, you must immediately issue guidance to your agents prohibiting them from using any City lots to stage or conduct enforcement operations.”

Mamdani’s letter comes weeks after a plainclothes ICE agent shot a Dominican immigrant in the Bronx while his 5-year-old son was in the car, infuriating community members and intensifying pressure on the mayor to do everything in his power to remove the rogue agency from New York City.

“We know that ICE is rotten to its core,” Mamdani said after the shooting. The mayor has called on President Donald Trump to end all ICE operations in New York City and has demanded abolition of the agency, saying it is “making a mockery of what law and order is supposed to be.”

In mid-October, Mamdani and more than 100 other elected New York officials called on private parking lot owners to bar ICE agents from using their property.

“In solidarity with immigrant New Yorkers and in our shared commitment to the city we love, we ask that you do not rent, lend, or otherwise make your property available to ICE as a staging area for its enforcement operations,” reads the October 16 letter. “Make it known to ICE that it is not authorized to use your garages and lots.”

author: Unknown
title: VOLVAC patronu adını gizleyerek işçi arıyor
content:
Barış Salık [email protected] Murat Uysal [email protected]

İstanbul – Tuzla’daki VOLVAC Paketleme ve Gıda Makinaları Fabrikasının önünde kurulan çadırda direniş 8. gününe girdi. DİSK/Birleşik Metal-İş’e üye oldukları için işten çıkarılan 35 işçi fabrika kapısında bekliyor. Bu işçiler, üretimde çalışanların tamamı. Fabrikada üretim yok. İşçilerin anlattığına göre şirket yeni işçi aramak için ilan açtı. İlanlarda fabrikanın adresi birebir yer alıyor ama şirketin adı geçmiyor. İşçilerin aktardığına göre fabrikanın önünde ilk günden bu yana yaklaşık 100 polis bekliyor.

İşçi Yıldıray örgütlenme fikrinin nasıl olgunlaştığını şöyle anlattı: “Bir iş arkadaşımız vardı, işini de iyi yapan biriydi. Sebepsiz yere 25/2 ile işten atıldı. Biz zaten bir süredir içeride koşulların kötüleştiğini konuşuyorduk. Bir gün toplu bir şekilde cuma namazına giderken cami yolunda ‘Sendikaya üye olalım’ diye bir fikir geliştirdik. Ardından hızla örgütlenmeye başladık. İçeride birkaç kişi hariç herkes örgütlendi.”

İş Kanunu’nun 25/II maddesi, işverene “Ahlak ve iyi niyet kurallarına uymayan haller” gerekçesiyle işçiyi bildirimsiz ve tazminatsız çıkarma imkanı veriyor.

Eylül ayında örgütlenmesini tamamlayan işçiler yetki başvurusu yaptı. Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığının yetki tespit yazısı 15 Ekim’de geldi. Yıldıray, sonrasında yaşananları şöyle aktardı: “Yetkinin ardından patron Birleşik Metal-İş genel başkanıyla görüştü. Görüşme olumlu geçse de daha sonra çalıştığı avukatı değiştirdi. Hemen ardından da birimlerinde şef ve sorumlu olan, ben dahil 5 arkadaşı işten attı.” Atılan 5 işçi 26 Ekim Pazartesi sabahı fabrika kapısının önünde direnişe başladı. İçeride çalışmaya devam eden işçiler de arkadaşlarına sahip çıktı. Yıldıray şöyle anlattı: “Bu işten atmayla beraber çalışmaya devam eden arkadaşlarımız içeride eylemler yaptı. Biz kapı önüne çadır kurmuştuk, aralarda gelip bize destek oldular, sloganlar attılar. Geçtiğimiz cuma günü de içerideki 30 arkadaşımızı işten attılar. Şimdi 35 kişi burada mücadelemizi sürdürüyoruz.”

Yıldıray, işten atmalar karşısında devletin tutumunu da sorguluyor: “Burada içimizden biri bıçaklansa, bir saldırıya uğrasa polis gelmeyecek. Mesele patronun güvenliği olduğunda burada birikiyor. Bu kolluk kimi koruyor şimdi? İlk günden beri 100 polis bizim başımızı bekliyor, daha doğrusu patronun malını bekliyor. Oysa biz anayasal hakkımızı kullandık. Madde ne diyor? İşçi istediği sendikaya üye olabilir diyor. Eğer öyleyse patron bizi işten atarak suç işliyor, kanuna karşı geliyor. Ama bu kanunu koruyan kanunların da olması lazım. İşçiler işten atılırken patrona ‘Bunları niye işten atıyorsun?’ diye soracak devlet lazım.”

Anayasa’nın 51. maddesi, çalışanlara önceden izin almaksızın sendikalara üye olma hakkı tanıyor. 6356 sayılı Sendikalar ve Toplu İş Sözleşmesi Kanunu da sendika üyeliği nedeniyle işten çıkarmayı yasaklıyor. Birleşik Metal-İş İstanbul 1 No’lu Şube Başkanı Can Emrah Ülgü de geçen hafta patronlara danışmanlık yapan avukatlık bürolarına dikkat çekmişti. Ülgü’ye göre bu bürolar süreci sendikasızlaştırma üzerine kuruyor ve patronlara yol haritası sunuyor.

VOLVAC, gıda paketleme makineleri üretiyor ve ağırlıklı olarak ihracata çalışıyor. Şirket, tanıtımında ABD, Rusya, Çin ve Almanya dahil 42’den fazla ülkeye satış yaptığını söylüyor. Sendikaya göre siparişler yoğun. Ancak üretimde çalışan işçilerin tamamı atıldığı için fabrikada üretim durmuş durumda. İçeride yalnızca sekreterlik, insan kaynakları ve satış bölümlerinde çalışanlar kaldı.

İşçiler, daha bir hafta öncesine kadar siparişler yetişsin diye enselerinde boza pişiren patronun şimdi ne yaptığını merak ediyor.

Sorunun yanıtına dair bir ipucu bir iş ilanından geldi. İşçilerin anlattığına göre şirket yeni işçi arıyor. İlanda fabrikanın adresi birebir yer alıyor ama şirketin adı geçmiyor.

İş ilanları örneklerinden birkaçı

İş ilanları örneklerinden birkaçı

Mücadelelerini sürdüreceklerini söyleyen Yıldıray, sendikalaştıkları için işten atılan tüm işçilerle dayanışma içinde olduklarını vurguladı.

Yılbaşından bu yana sendikal örgütlenme sürecinde işten atılan işçiler arasında başka örnekler de var:

Mersin Limanında Özgüneş Lojistik’ten 185 TÜMTİS üyesi

İzmir Aliağa’da Smart Solar’dan 85 Enerji-Sen üyesi

Bolu’da Domino Tekstil’den 60 işçi

Bursagaz’dan 22 Enerji-Sen üyesi

Ankara Polatlı’da Panelsan işçileri. Direnen işçilerin üzerine tır sürülmüştü.

author: Joshua Davis
title: Federal Government Is Targeting Officials Who Are Trying to Hold ICE Accountable
content:
Since January, the House Judiciary Committee and Department of Justice have targeted 65 state and local officials.

Since January, the House Judiciary Committee and Department of Justice have targeted 65 state and local officials.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

In the months leading up to the 2026 midterm elections, congressional Republicans and federal prosecutors have targeted dozens of local officials in cities and counties across the country that have adopted some sanctuary policies. The investigations have increasingly focused on prosecutors and law enforcement officers, many of whom have publicly announced plans to go after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents who commit crimes in their jurisdictions or refuse demands to cooperate with federal immigration policing.

In total, 65 officials in 16 states have been targeted since January, according to a review of documents released by the House Judiciary Committee and the Department of Justice (DOJ), as well as interviews with senior officials who have direct knowledge of individual investigations. The House Judiciary Committee has issued subpoenas and other demands for testimony, documents, and records to more than 40 officials, 15 of them local prosecutors. Alongside that, the DOJ has initiated investigations into 50 local or state officials since 2025, including five involving local prosecutors. In all, 17 local prosecutors have been swept up in House Judiciary or DOJ investigations and lawsuits related to immigration policies.

House Judiciary Committee Chair Rep. Jim Jordan said in a recent report that “Democrats’ open-borders policies at the federal level and sanctuary policies at the state and local level allow millions of illegal aliens to pour into the country and ensure that criminal aliens, after encountered by local law enforcement, are released back into American communities,” echoing language the committee has commonly used in its investigations.

Many experts describe these investigations as unprecedented, and view the move as retaliation against local officials who refuse to cooperate with federal immigration agents or threaten legal action against ICE officers.

“These [prosecutors] are being intentionally intimidated by congressional and federal authorities,” said Mona Sahaf, the director of the Reshaping Prosecution initiative at the Vera Institute of Justice. “The use of [the] DOJ to target perceived political opponents is new. It’s busting norms, and it’s highly dangerous.”

The targeting of local prosecutors appears to be a matter of policy in the second Trump administration. “Sanctuary Jurisdictions Directives” issued by the attorney general’s office on February 5, 2025, held that the DOJ Civil Rights Division should “identify state and local laws, policies, and practices that facilitate violations of federal immigration laws or impede lawful federal immigration operations,” and “where appropriate, take legal action to challenge such laws, policies, or practices.”

The DOJ, in a June 18 press release announcing an investigation into local officials in Philadelphia — including District Attorney Larry Krasner — concerning a policy prohibiting federal agents from wearing masks, said that its “series of lawsuits brought by the Civil Division” targeted “illegal policies designed to thwart federal law enforcement across the country.”

Rebecca Roiphe, the Joseph Solomon Distinguished Professor of Law at New York Law School, said the investigations into local prosecutors represented “a wholesale abandonment” of the principle of separation between the DOJ and the political branches of government. “This administration has pretty openly suggested that it is normal and appropriate and even laudable for the political branches to have some degree of control over the Department of Justice,” she said.

Referring to the DOJ investigations, Roiphe said, “The bottom line is that these federal prosecutions can end up threatening local prosecutors to fall in line with federal priorities, and that’s illegitimate in our system.”

These overlapping investigations, reports, and the DOJ directives follow the Heritage Foundation’s Project 2025 threat to “initiate legal action against” prosecutors who refuse to adhere to the priorities of the Trump administration. For many of the targeted prosecutors, the political influence has become impossible to ignore.

Among the targeted is Parisa Dehghani-Tafti, the top prosecutor in Arlington, Virginia, who drew the ire of Representative Jordan’s committee on multiple occasions, including when she declined to charge an activist who handed out flyers containing the home address of Deputy White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, citing concerns over First Amendment-protected free speech.

In a July 1 letter to Dehghani-Tafti, Jordan described Dehghani-Tafti’s decision not to charge as “politically-motivated actions in a case involving a far-left agitator’s disturbing campaign to threaten, harass, and dox a senior White House official and his family” and accused her office of having “sanctuary policies that prioritize illegal and criminal aliens over American citizens.”

Dehghani-Tafti, who characterized the House Judiciary actions as “pathetic,” denies any wrongdoing and suggests that these investigations are the result of her political opponents’ inability to defeat her electorally.

“They can’t beat us at the polls, and so they’re being undemocratic about it and trying to undermine the voters,” she told Truthout.

In total, Jordan and the House Judiciary Committee have issued three letters and a subpoena to Dehghani-Tafti, in addition to writing an interim report on her in September, which was largely based on a July closed-door deposition. Following the report, the DOJ Civil Rights Division informed Dehghani-Tafti that she was under investigation following a referral from the House Judiciary, according to a senior official with direct knowledge of the investigation.

“None of this is normal,” Dehghani-Tafti said. “What they’re doing is taking mechanisms that are designed to uphold the rule of law and perverting them. And that is not normal, except for authoritarians.”

Dehghani-Tafti was not the only Northern Virginia prosecutor to be on the receiving end of both House Judiciary and DOJ investigations. The top prosecutor for Fairfax County, Virginia, Steve Descano, similarly received three letters and a subpoena, and was the subject of an interim report from Jordan’s committee. The report, “Fairfax County, Virginia: The Dangerous Consequences of Sanctuary Policies,” claims that a 2019 campaign promise to make “charging and plea decisions that limit or avoid immigration consequences” is discriminatory and violates federal law. The report goes on to accuse Descano’s office of “efforts to erase national borders and undermine immigration enforcement.”

Descano declined to comment for this story, citing the ongoing investigations. His chief of staff, Laura Birnbaum, directed Truthout to prior official statements issued by his office, including an October 20 response to the House Judiciary report. “This ‘report’ is nothing more than recycled Republican talking points put out weeks before the midterm elections as a desperate attempt to distract from widely anticipated Republican losses,” wrote Birnbaum.

Responding to the DOJ investigation, Descano’s office released a statement in May that accused the Trump administration “of misusing the Justice Department to launch partisan attacks.”

Both Dehghani-Tafti and Descano belong to a small coalition of prosecutors from cities across the U.S. that declared an intention to prosecute federal agents who commit crimes in their cities. The alliance — the Fight Against Federal Overreach — which intentionally takes its name from the slang acronym FAFO, formed in January in part as a response to the deadly ICE shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minneapolis that same month. Less than a year later, nearly half of the group’s founding members have found themselves under investigation by the DOJ.

“No other administration has ever done things like this,”said Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, who has been a target of DOJ investigators.

Moriarty, whose jurisdiction includes Minneapolis, made national headlines in January when she announced a state-level investigation into the shooting of Good by ICE agent Jonathan Ross. Just days later, the DOJ subpoenaed four Minnesota officials, including Gov. Tim Walz and Attorney General Keith Ellison, as part of an investigation into whether they impeded federal immigration agents during “Operation Metro Surge.” News reports initially incorrectly named Moriarty among the officials who received a subpoena, though it was later revealed that she did not receive one. Moriarty told Truthout she believes that her name was released intentionally by government officials to intimidate her.

Viewed in isolation, these actions may appear to be singular responses during an exceptional political moment, but taken together, the data suggest a wider attempt to punish officials who try to thwart federal immigration policies.

“The story is there — if you speak up and work to hold police accountable, we will come after you,” said Sahaf, referring to the House Judiciary and DOJ investigations. Sahaf, a former DOJ trial attorney, warned that should local prosecutors fear becoming a political target for investigating federal agents and police, “we’ll have no one … to deter this kind of conduct from happening again.”

Clarissa Delgado contributed additional reporting for this article.

title: Eisenhower’ın dünya küresi Pentagon'da taşınırken nasıl kırıldı?
content:
Pentagon’un koridorlarından birinde 1930’lardan kalma, çapı 75 santimi geçen bir dünya küresi duruyor. Amerikan ordusu bu küreyi seksen yılı aşkın süredir kuşaktan kuşağa koruyor. Yaygın inanışa göre General Dwight Eisenhower, 1942’de savaş planlarını hazırlarken kürenin başında çalıştı. Yanındaki plakette bunun yalnızca popüler teori olduğu yazıyorsa da efsane plaketten daha güçlü görünüyor.

Bu yılın başında Amerikan Fox News kanalının eski sabah programı sunucusu, bugünün Savunma Bakanı Pete Hegseth küreyi makam odasında görmek istedi. Böyle eserleri normalde ordunun askeri tarih uzmanları taşıyor. Ancak o günlerde hükümet kapanmıştı ve uzmanlar zorunlu izindeydi. Bakanın ekibi beklemedi. Şubat ayında küreyi kendileri kaldırmaya çalıştılar ve düşürdüler. Küre, oyma ahşap ayağının içindeki metal eksenden koptu ve alt tarafında, tam Antarktika’nın üzerinde yarık açıldı.

Olay aylarca gizli kaldı. Washington Post, ekim ayında fotoğraflarla ortaya çıkarınca Pentagon önce kazaların olabileceğini, kimsenin yaralanmadığını ve kürenin tamir edildiğini söyledi. Ardından düşenin replika olduğunu öne sürdü. NBC News ise üç yetkilinin anlatımına ve fotoğrafa dayanarak kırılanın orijinal küre olduğunu doğruladı. Düşürenler için orijinal ya da replika fark etmeyebilir, sonuçta boya ve alçıydı. Oysa bazı eşyalar döneminin bütün hafızasını taşırlar.

Eisenhower o küreyi döndürdüğünde dünya savaştaydı. Washington’da savaş planlarının başındaydı. İki yıl sonra Normandiya çıkarmasını yönetecekti. Savaşın ardından Avrupa’nın ortasına demir perde indi ve dünya iki kampa bölündü.

Türkiye savaşa fiilen girmemişti fakat perdenin tam ucundaydı ve güvenlik kaygısı her şeyin önündeydi. Savaş boyunca tarafsız kalan ülke, barışta kendini yalnız buldu. 1947’de Truman Doktrini’yle Amerikan yardımı geldi, ardından Marshall Planı’nın traktörleri köy yollarına çıktı. Zorlanan Batı kapısını Kore Savaşı açtı. 1950’de Meclise bile danışılmadan Kore’ye gönderilen Türk tugayı, Kunuri’de ve sonrasında ağır kayıplar verdi. Bu bedel Batı’nın Türkiye’ye bakışını değiştirdi. Karara karşı çıkan Barışseverler Cemiyeti üyeleriyse tutuklanıp yargılandı.

Eisenhower o yıllarda yeniden üniforma giymişti. Aralık 1950’de NATO’nun ilk Avrupa başkomutanı oldu ve ittifakın askeri karargahını Paris yakınlarında kurdu. Türkiye 18 Şubat 1952’de onun komutasındaki ittifaka katıldı, Başkomutan Eisenhower üyeliği yerinde mühürlemek için Ankara’ya kadar geldi. Küreyi döndüren el, Türkiye’nin yerini de haritada işaretlemişti.

Eisenhower Ankara’ya ikinci kez 6 Aralık 1959’da, bu kez ABD başkanı olarak geldi. Türkiye’yi görevdeyken ziyaret eden ilk Amerikan başkanıydı. Cumhurbaşkanı Celal Bayar onu Esenboğa’da karşıladı. Eisenhower Anıtkabir’e çelenk bıraktı, ardından Bayar, Başbakan Adnan Menderes ve Dışişleri Bakanı Fatin Rüştü Zorlu ile Çankaya’da görüştü. Ankara Üniversitesi ona fahri doktora verdi, caddeler el sallayan kalabalıklarla doldu. Ertesi sabah Karaçi’ye uçarken Türk halkına olağanüstü karşılama için teşekkür etti.

Ancak ziyaretin ardından yapılan görüşmelerden Türk hükümetinin umduğu büyük ekonomik yardım çıkmadı. Eisenhower’ı uğurlayan liderlerin iktidarı yalnızca beş ay daha sürdü. 27 Mayıs 1960’ta ordu yönetime el koydu, bir yıl sonra Menderes ve Zorlu İmralı’da idam edildi.

Eisenhower ocak 1961’de, görevi devretmeden önce Beyaz Saray’dan Amerikalılara veda konuşmasını yaptı. Normandiya’yı yönetmiş beş yıldızlı general, ülkesini kendi kurduğu makineye karşı uyardı: Devasa ordunun büyük silah sanayisiyle iç içe geçmesi Amerikan tarihinde yeniydi ve oluşan askeri-sanayi kompleksinin haksız nüfuz kazanmasına karşı uyanık olunmalıydı. Yeni gücü dizginleme görevini de uyanık yurttaşlara bıraktı.

Pentagon’daki küre şimdi tamir ediliyor. Kırığı onarılınca yeniden ayağına oturtulacak ve dönebilecek. Ama Antarktika’nın üzerindeki iz, dikkatli bakan gözlerden kaçmayacak.

İttifaklar kuşaklar boyunca, sabırla ve uzmanların eliyle taşınır. Kore’de dökülen kanla, Ankara sokaklarında sallanan ellerle örülür. Eisenhower savaştan sonra bakanlığın adının savaştan savunmaya çevrilmesini desteklemişti, savaşı en iyi bilen general, barışın adını seçmişti. Bugün onun küresini odasına isteyen bakan ise adı yeniden savaş yapmaya çalışıyor.

Pentagon, küre olayını önemsiz olmayan bir haber diye geçiştirdi. Bakan küreyi istedi ama Eisenhower’ın sözlerine hiç kulak vermedi. Türkiyeli biri olarak bu kazayı izlerken aklıma bir soru takılıyor: Ortak tarihin ağırlığını taşıyamayan eller, bugünün sayısız perdeyle bölünmüş dünyasını nasıl taşıyacak?

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Dilovası işçi katliamı davasında 5. duruşma bugün
content:
Dilovası’nda 3'ü çocuk 7 işçinin yaşamını yitirdiği yangına ilişkin davanın beşinci duruşması bugün Kandıra Ceza İnfaz Kurumları Kampüsü’ndeki duruşma salonunda görülecek. 23 sanığın yargılandığı davada 10 sanık tutuklu, 1 sanık ise firari. Aileler, yalnızca imalathanenin patronlarının değil, yıllarca ruhsatsız faaliyete ve denetimsizliğe göz yuman kamu görevlileri ile diğer tüm sorumluların da hesap vermesini istiyor.

Kocaeli’nin Dilovası ilçesinde 8 Kasım 2025’te Ravive Kozmetik’e ait parfüm dolum imalathanesinde çıkan yangında üçü çocuk 7 işçi yaşamını yitirdi. Yangında Hanım Gülek, Esma Gikan, Şengül Yılmaz, Tuncay Yıldız, Tuğba Taşdemir, Nisa Taşdemir ve Cansu Esatoğlu hayatını kaybetti, 6 işçi yaralandı.

Yangının ardından açılan davada ilk duruşma mart ayında görülmüştü. Şirket yetkililerinin yargılandığı dosyaya daha sonra kamu görevlileri hakkında açılan dava da birleştirildi. Böylece sanık sayısı 23’e yükseldi. Eylül ayında görülen dördüncü duruşma itibarıyla 10 sanık tutuklu, 1 sanık firari olarak yargılanıyor.

Davada Ravive Kozmetik yetkilileri İsmail ve Altay Ali Oransal ile ortak üretim yaptığı öne sürülen şirketin yetkilileri Aleyna Oransal ve Gökberk Güngör hakkında “olası kastla öldürme” suçundan ceza isteniyor.

İşyerinin faaliyetinin sürmesine ilişkin denetim ve görevleri bulunan belediye görevlileri hakkında ise “bilinçli taksirle birden fazla kişinin ölümüne neden olma” suçlamasıyla dava açıldı. Böylece davanın önemli başlıklarından birini, yangına ilişkin sorumluluğun yalnızca işyerinin patronlarıyla sınırlı tutulup tutulmayacağı oluşturuyor.

Aileler ise imalathanenin yıllarca faaliyet göstermesinde rolü bulunan kamu kurumlarının ve görevlilerinin sorumluluğunun da ortaya çıkarılmasını istiyor.

Kamu görevlileri hakkındaki dosyanın ana davayla birleşmesiyle birlikte Dilovası Belediyesi’nin denetim sorumluluğu da yargılamanın konusu haline geldi. AKP yönetimindeki Dilovası Belediyesi’nin görevlileri hakkında açılan davada, ruhsatsız çalışan imalathanenin faaliyetinin neden durdurulmadığı ve denetim görevlerinin nasıl yerine getirildiği tartışılıyor.

Ailelerin aktardığı bilgilere göre imalathanenin ruhsatsız çalıştığı yangından kısa süre önce zabıta tarafından tespit edilmişti. Buna karşın işyerinin faaliyetinin sürdüğü, daha önce de farklı kamu kurumlarına şikâyetler yapıldığı belirtildi. Aileler, bu nedenle sorumluluğun yalnızca belediye görevlileriyle de sınırlı tutulmamasını istiyor.

Ailelerin itirazı, yangının yalnızca işyerindeki eksiklikler üzerinden değerlendirilmesine karşı çıkıyor. Ruhsatsız imalathanenin yıllarca çalışmasına izin veren, yapılan şikâyetleri karşılıksız bırakan ve denetim görevini yerine getirmeyen bütün kurum ve kişilerin sorumluluğunun araştırılmasını talep ediyor. Belediye görevlilerinin yanı sıra bakanlıklar, denetim kurumları ve diğer kamu görevlilerinin de yargılama kapsamına alınması gerektiğini vurguyor. Aileler ayrıca imalathaneye iş veren şirketler ile işyerindeki çalışma koşullarından sorumlu olan diğer kişi ve kuruluşların da soruşturulmasını istiyor.

Davanın ilk duruşması mart ayında Kandıra Cezaevi Yerleşkesi’ndeki salonda görüldü. Mahkeme, tutuklu sanıkların durumunu ve dosyadaki delilleri değerlendirdi. Mayıs ayında görülen ikinci duruşmada, daha önce imalathanede çalışmış 17 yaşındaki bir işçi tanık olarak dinlendi. Tanık, 15 yaşında işe başladığını ve sigortasız çalıştırıldığını anlattı. Aynı duruşmada bazı sanıkların tutukluluk durumları ve dosyadaki deliller değerlendirildi.

Temmuz ayında görülen üçüncü duruşmada ise tutuklu sanıkların telefon ve bilgisayarlarındaki dijital materyallerin incelenmesi gündeme geldi. Mahkeme, bazı sanıkların tutukluluklarının devamına karar verdi ve duruşmayı eylül ayına erteledi.

Eylül ayında görülen dördüncü duruşmada ise belediye görevlileri hakkındaki dosyanın ana dosyayla birleşmesinin ardından kamu görevlilerinin sorumluluğu da yargılamada daha geniş biçimde ele alındı. Mahkeme, Dilovası Belediyesi Zabıta Müdür Vekili Nizamettin Balcı ile eski Zabıta Müdür Vekili Cengiz Taşdemir’in yeniden tutuklanmasına, dört belediye görevlisinin ise adli kontrol şartıyla tahliye edilmesine karar verdi.

Bugünkü beşinci duruşma, yangının birinci yılının dolmasına günler kala görülecek. Aileler, davanın imalathanenin patronları ve birkaç belediye görevlisiyle sınırlı kalmamasını; yangının meydana gelmesine uzanan denetimsizlik zincirinde sorumluluğu bulunan herkesin yargılanmasını istiyor.

Aileler, 3 Kasım’daki duruşmanın yanı sıra 8 Kasım’da, katliamın birinci yılında yapılacak anmaya da çağrı yaptı. Davanın tüm sorumluları kapsayacak biçimde genişletilmesini isteyen aileler, “Bütün sorumlulardan hesap sorulana kadar mücadelemizi sürdüreceğiz” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Varto-Karlıova'da JES direnişi: Bilirkişi keşfine yüzlerce köylü katıldı
content:
Muş'un Varto/Gimgim ve Bingöl'ün Karlıova/Kanireş ilçeleri arasındaki köylerde planlanan jeotermal enerji santrali projesine karşı açılan davada, Bingöl İdare Mahkemesi'nin görevlendirdiği bilirkişi heyeti 2 Kasım Pazartesi günü proje alanında inceleme yaptı. Keşif, aylardır projeye karşı çıkan köylülerin ve ekoloji örgütlerinin katılımıyla gerçekleştirildi.




Heyet, sondaj kuyularının açılması planlanan Licik, Çermî ve Şorik köylerinde incelemelerde bulunduktan sonra Varto'nun Xwarik (Çalıdere) köyüne geçti. Buradaki keşfi yüzlerce köylü izledi.




Xwarik'te yüzlerce kişi keşif heyetini bekledi







Xwarik'te keşif heyetini bekleyen köylüler/Fotoğraf: MA







Bilirkişi heyeti Karlıova'daki incelemelerini sürdürürken Varto'nun Xwarik köyünde farklı kentlerden gelen ekoloji savunucuları, siyasi parti ve demokratik kitle örgütü temsilcileri, “Varto yeşildir yeşil kalacak” ve “Direne direne kazanacağız” sloganlarıyla projeyi protesto etti.




DEM Parti Muş Milletvekili Sümeyye Boz, köylülerin yalnızca doğal çevrelerini değil, geçim kaynaklarını ve geleceklerini savunduklarını söyledi. Jeotermal projenin suya, toprağa ve hayvancılığa zarar vereceğini savunan Boz, halkın rızası olmadan verilen izinlere karşı çıktı.







“Biz burada geçim kaynaklarımızı da yaşam kaynaklarımızı da geleceğimizi de savunuyoruz” diyen Boz, köylülerin taleplerinin dikkate alınmasını istedi ve “Zafer Varto halkının olacak” dedi.







DEM Parti İzmir Milletvekili İbrahim Akın ise enerji yatırımlarının çevresel sonuçlarıyla hükümetlerin iklim politikaları arasındaki çelişkiye dikkat çekti. Akın, COP31 hazırlıklarına değinerek iklim değişikliğiyle mücadele iddiasında bulunan yönetimlerin bir yandan ekolojik yıkıma yol açabilecek projelere izin vermesini eleştirdi.




Akın, bu politikaları “sahte yeşil politikalar” olarak nitelendirerek yaşam alanlarını koruma mücadelesinin sürdürülmesi gerektiğini söyledi.




Varto Belediye Eşbaşkanları Gıyasettin Aydemir ve Gülbahar Kaya da köylülerin mücadelesini desteklediklerini belirterek ilçenin doğal varlıklarını korumakta kararlı olduklarını açıkladı.




İncelemelere DEM Parti milletvekilleri İbrahim Akın ve Sümeyye Boz'un yanı sıra baro temsilcileri, avukatlar ve ekoloji örgütleri de katıldı.




180 günü aşan çadır nöbetinden bilirkişi keşfine




ABD merkezli IGNIS H2 Enerji Üretim AŞ'nin geliştirmek istediği projeye karşı köylüler nisanda Bingöl İdare Mahkemesi'nde dava açtı. Varto'nun Xwarik köyünde 3 Mayıs'ta başlatılan çadır nöbeti ise 180 günü geride bıraktı.



















Muş'un Xwarik köylüleri mera savunmasında: JES projesine direnişin 180. günü




31 Ekim 2026










Köylüler, jeotermal sondajların yeraltı su kaynaklarını, tarım alanlarını, meraları ve hayvancılığa dayanan geçim kaynaklarını olumsuz etkilemesinden kaygılı. Bölgenin aktif fay hatları üzerindeki konumu da itirazların başlıca gerekçeleri arasında.




Bingöl İdare Mahkemesi, 21 Temmuz'daki ara kararıyla bilirkişilere 13 ayrı başlıkta soru yönelterek keşif yapılmasını istedi. İlk olarak 8 Ekim'de yapılması planlanan keşif, heyette yeterli uzmanlığa sahip bir jeofizik mühendisi bulunması talebiyle yapılan itirazın ardından 2 Kasım'a ertelendi.




Avukatlardan fay hattı ve eksik rapor uyarısı




Keşfin ardından açıklama yapan davanın avukatı Barış Yıldırım, bölgedeki fay hatlarına dikkat çekerek projenin hayata geçirilmesinin yaşam hakkı açısından ciddi riskler doğuracağını savundu.




Yıldırım, şirketin proje için ilgili kurumlardan alınması gereken raporları tamamlamadığını ileri sürdü. Türkiye'nin taraf olduğu uluslararası sözleşmelerin de dikkate alınması gerektiğini belirtti.




Muş Barosu Başkanı Kadir Karaçelik, köylülerin aylardır sürdürdüğü mücadeleye destek vererek şöyle konuştu:







“Umut ediyorum ki mantıklı bir şekilde değerlendirilir yasal organlar tarafından. Gimgim halkının yaşam çığlığına ses verilir.”







Van Barosundan avukat Rojhat Özgökçe de hukuki sürecin yanı sıra köylülerin mücadelesinin önemine dikkat çekti:







“Bir şeyler dönüşecekse, sizin direnişiniz sayesinde dönüşecektir.”







DEM Parti Muş Milletvekili Sümeyye Boz ise mahkemelerin halkın yaşam hakkını gözeten bir karar vermesini umduklarını belirterek mücadeleyi sürdüreceklerini söyledi.




Davanın konusu çevresel değerlendirme kararları




Davanın esasını jeotermal kaynak arama faaliyetlerine ilişkin çevresel değerlendirme kararlarının hukuka uygun olup olmadığı oluşturuyor.




İnsan Hakları Derneği Ekoloji ve Yaşam Hakkı Komisyonu da keşif öncesinde yaptığı açıklamada, Çalıdere, Kantarkaya ve Ilıpınar çevresindeki projelerin yalnızca enerji üretimi ve ekonomik getiri açısından değil, halk sağlığı, ekolojik denge ve gelecek kuşakların yaşam hakkı bakımından değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini belirtti.




Bilirkişi heyetinin incelemelerini tamamlamasıyla davada yeni bir aşamaya geçildi. Ancak rapor henüz açıklanmadı. Projenin fay hatları, su kaynakları ve tarım alanları üzerindeki etkilerine ilişkin itirazlar, bilirkişilerin bilimsel değerlendirmesi ve mahkemenin kararıyla ele alınacak.




Köylülerin aylardır sürdürdüğü nöbetin ardından yapılan keşif, projenin geleceğine ilişkin yargısal sürecin önemli aşamalarından biri oldu.




(AEK)

Moves by the Trump administration may be emboldening churches to jump into state proposition fights.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

On November 3, Virginians will vote on two ballot initiatives that have become the center of a well-resourced campaign led by Catholic Bishop Michael Burbidge.

This campaign is urging congregants to vote “no” on two ballot measures. Ballot Question 1 would affirm abortion access as a constitutional right in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Ballot Question 2 would repeal a 2006 same-sex marriage ban that defines marriage as between one man and one woman. Burbidge, who leads Virginia’s Arlington Diocese, which says it has 432,000 registered parishioners, is using his position to call on Catholic parishioners to vote against abortion access and marriage equality for all Virginians and to urge others to do the same.

This campaign has deployed the resources of the church, including church bulletins and guest speakers to preach against the ballot initiatives. The Archdiocese of Arlington itself hosts the CatholicsVoteNo.com website, which states that the church is “not partisan” while condemning the supposed “many evils and unintended consequences” of the initiatives, and even assailing surrogacy.

That website also features a “pledge to vote no,” and details how followers can get involved in opposing the ballot measures, from hosting registration drives to reaching out to their specific pastor for directions on community outreach. Burbidge’s identified goal is to convince the nearly 700,000 confirmed Catholics across the state to vote “no” on these amendments, a figure that could be decisive in making the initiatives fail.

For decades, the IRS forbade places of worship from endorsing or opposing political candidates as tax-exempt organizations. However, Donald Trump’s IRS has recently engaged in efforts to roll back what’s known as the “Johnson Amendment,” a tax provision that has been in place for more than 70 years that bars tax-exempt nonprofits from endorsing or opposing political candidates. That move was struck down in the courts, but it is currently under appeal in the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. In the meantime, the IRS has issued new guidance on the Johnson Amendment, seemingly giving tax-exempt places of worship enough legal wiggle room to engage in political campaigning directly to parishioners without jeopardizing their status. Beyond that, there is no legal bar on nonprofits engaging on public policy issues, including on referenda, as with the documented role of the Mormon Church in opposing marriage equality via Proposition 8 in California in 2008.

If Virginia is any indication, the Trump administration’s efforts to lift limits on churches directly backing political candidates may be emboldening churches that may have previously stayed out of state proposition fights to jump in strongly, using the hierarchy and wide reach of a religious institution to tell adherents how to vote. For years, Catholic Church leadership in the U.S. has wrestled with controversy and pressure to deny holy communion to believers in public office who vote to protect access to abortion. This includes Burbidge, who used his post to uphold a ban from a San Francisco archbishop denying Speaker Nancy Pelosi communion in the Arlington diocese because of her support as a representative for abortion access and, in 2022, he publicly called on Joe Biden to “repent” for his support of abortion health care.

In this coming election in Virginia, as a leader within the Catholic Church, Bishop Burbidge is using the resources contributed by his congregation to call on parishioners to vote in support of his anti-LGBTQ, anti-abortion agenda. Meanwhile, the majority of Catholics in the U.S. support marriage equality and access to abortion health care.

Burbidge has close ties to Leonard Leo and his more than $1 billion network of groups, which includes the Marble Freedom Trust and Rule of Law Trust. Leo’s network helped capture the U.S. Supreme Court that overturned Roe v. Wade and now is being marshaled to capture other key democratic institutions, from state courts, to the media, to the entertainment industry, to push Leo’s regressive agenda. The Leo-funded network has played a significant role in almost every abortion-related state ballot initiative in recent years, and has recently become a major donor of a national anti-abortion coordination group.

Burbidge has direct financial ties to Leo. Since 2022, the Arlington Diocese that Burbidge heads has received $2.45 million from the Sacred Spaces Foundation, where Leo is listed as the foundation’s director, president, and treasurer. In 2023, Leo used the nonprofit to buy a church near his home in Northeast Harbor, Maine, for $2.7 million. The Sacred Spaces Foundation took in $13.9 million from the Knights of Columbus Charitable Fund between 2022 and 2024.

The two serve on the Catholic University Board of Trustees together, and Burbidge has long been involved with March for Life — an anti-abortion movement tied to Leo and his public relations firm CRC Advisors, and funded extensively by the Leo-tied Knights of Columbus. In 2025, Burbidge spoke at Life Fest, an event sponsored by the Knights of Columbus, which also has ties to Leo through billionaire hedge funder Sean Fieler, who has used Knights of Columbus as a donor-advised fund (DAF) to move money to groups to keep his role more secret. Fieler is an anti-abortion, anti-LGBTQ activist who has praised Leo as a person who has influenced how he wields his financial power.

The day before early voting began in Virginia, Burbidge organized a webinar titled “Know Exactly What You’re Voting On” in support of his “Catholics Vote No” campaign. The webinar was co-hosted by the Life Leadership Conference, which was created in January 2025 and infused with $30 million through the Pro-Life Venture Fund, according to right-wing media that referred to the fund by name but failed to provide additional details about how it operates. These reports also pointed to anti-abortion activists Robbie George, Raymond Ruddy, and Leonard Leo (likely via the almost $900 million trust Leo controls) as the backers of this new venture determined to further erode reproductive rights at the federal and state levels. (It is unclear what type of legal entity the fund is, as it is not registered as a PAC and tax forms have yet to be filed for the entity.)

Ken Cuccinelli — the former Virginia attorney general and former Trump appointee — also spoke at St. Raymond of Peñafort Catholic Church, a parish within Burbidge’s diocese, on October 1, 2026, telling congregants why they should vote “no” on Ballot Questions 1 and 2. While this event was not publicized as a “Catholics Vote No” campaign event, Burbidge is Cuccinelli’s bishop, and St. Raymond has been promoting the “no” campaign to its parishioners in its weekly bulletins.

Cuccinelli also has ties to Leonard Leo. He is a frequent speaker at events organized by the Federalist Society, a dark money networking group of right-wing lawyers that serves as a pipeline to power for high-profile lawyers, judges, and more. Leo helps lead the Federalist Society as co-chair of its board. The Heritage Foundation’s so-called Election Transparency Initiative, headed by Cuccinelli, is listed as a coalition partner of the Only Citizens Vote Coalition, which has received funding from the Leo-tied 85 Fund. Cuccinelli also authored a chapter in the Trump 2.0 playbook, Project 2025. Many of the contributors to that playbook received funding from Leo’s network.

Burbidge released his January 2025 pastoral letter on Roe v. Wade’s anniversary, in which he attacked in vitro fertilization (IVF), calling the treatment “a grave moral injustice,” although he has been notably silent on the injustices of those who have died as a result of oppressive abortion bans. Burbidge also claims without evidence that IVF harms “the sacred love of husband and wife” and that children born through donors and surrogates don’t have as strong of a bond with their parents, even though studies have shown that parent-adolescent relationships of children born via IVF are either the same or more positive statistically than those conceived without IVF. He describes the IVF industry as the “Wild West” because it supposedly “lacks basic health and safety regulations,” even though it is one of the “most heavily regulated procedures in American medicine,” according to the American Society of Reproductive Medicine.

Burbidge has held leadership positions with the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB), which includes serving as the chair of USCCB’s Committee on Pro-Life Activities from 2022 to 2024. USCCB is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit group created in 1946 as a vehicle for Catholic Bishops in the U.S.

USCCB has joined the fight to eliminate abortion access, presenting abortion as going against the values of the Catholic Church. In August 2026, the group launched a “prayer and action to stop the spread of abortion pills” campaign against telehealth and abortion pills including mifepristone. USCCB has spread disinformation about the abortion pill, a medication that has repeatedly been proven safe by experts, and urged parishioners to spread its claims. It also asked those committed to its cause to participate in a pressure campaign against pharmacies, distributors, and pharmaceutical companies to keep them from continuing to help people in the U.S. receive the abortion health care they want or need.

USCCB is not required (and opts not to) publicly report its revenue and expenses. However, tax filings of other groups show millions in revenue annually from an array of Catholic charities as well as DAFs. These DAFs include one belonging to the Leo-tied Knights of Columbus, which has given USCCB more than $1.3 million.

This November, Virginia will be a testing ground for the power of religious institutions to pressure their congregants — mobilizing the hierarchy and marshalling the resources everyday Virginians fund — to vote for a regressive agenda. Only Virginians can decide if the freedom to control their own bodies and destinies — and to marry the people they love — can be taken away.

title: Stevens Endorsed Rogers Right After He Touted His Support of Abortion Bans
content:
Mike Rogers once co-sponsored a federal bill that would ban abortions from the point of conception.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Rep. Haley Stevens’s (D-Michigan) surprise endorsement of Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers for Senate over Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday came amid renewed attention on Rogers’s anti-abortion views after he bragged about his stance in an appearance on a conservative radio show last week.

Last Thursday, as the Detroit Metro Times noted, Rogers touted his stances against abortion and trans rights.

“Is it safe to say that we don’t have to worry about you joining Democrats when it comes to things like … supporting gender mutilation surgery for minors, abortion through all nine months of pregnancy for any reason whatsoever?” Dutko said, overexaggerating stances on both issues. “Can we feel confident as evangelical Christians that you’re going to be on our side on some of these social issues?”

“You don’t even have to think about it twice. I’ve been very open about all of those issues — including, for the time I was in Congress, having a 100 percent pro-life rating. I am actually the guy who will stop trangender mutilation of our kids with these trangender surgeries,” Rogers said.

Rogers said the members of his family “are all conservative Christians. This is the only way that I know how to be.”

The clip was posted by Democrats and El-Sayed, who criticized the stance and highlighted Rogers’s history of backing extreme anti-abortion legislation.

“A vote for Mike Rogers is a vote for a national abortion ban,” said El-Sayed in a post on social media.

As Reproductive Freedom for All pointed out on Sunday, Rogers voted for a national abortion ban that would prohibit abortions past 20 weeks as a House member in 2013, and has even cosponsored radically dangerous bills to ban all abortions from the point of conception. Additionally, Rogers said in 2010 that he thinks abortion “should be legal only to prevent the death of the mother” — meaning that he doesn’t support exclusions for rape, incest, or when continuing pregnancy could harm the pregnant person or the fetus.

Rogers’s campaign responded to those posting about the clip by saying that he’s against a national ban. In a post on social media on Saturday, he highlighted a clip in which he said that “Michigan voters have already decided the issue, and I respect that decision” and that he “won’t do anything to change it.”

Abortion rights advocates were skeptical. “Nothing can erase Mike Rogers’ votes or make him any less dangerous to our reproductive freedom,” said Reproductive Freedom for All President and CEO Mini Timmaraju in a statement after Stevens’s announcement on Sunday.

Timmaraju also condemned Stevens for backing Rogers. “Haley Stevens is giving cover to a politician who spent his career trying to ban abortion and was still bragging about that record just days ago,” Timmaraju said.

Stevens has previously touted her support for abortion rights, including during her primary campaign this year. In a speech on the House floor in 2023, she pledged to the women of her state that she would “return to the House of Representatives and seek to enshrine your rights into law” and combat the overturn of Roe v. Wade. “I will not stop until we enshrine women’s rights into the law of this land,” she said.

On the campaign trail for her House seat in 2022, Stevens had suggested that her opponent, incumbent Rep. Andy Levin, was not as committed to abortion rights as she was because he is a man.

On Sunday, however, Levin pointed out that Stevens’s view on abortion was compromised by conservative super PACs that were backing her campaign at the time. Stevens’s ascendancy that year was buoyed by a $5.4 million injection into her campaign by the pro-Israel lobby, including AIPAC, which wanted Levin ousted over his criticism of Israel’s occupation of Palestine.

That year was “the summer of the Dobbs decision, and ultimately voters placed their trust in a ‘pro-choice’ woman who promised to protect their reproductive freedoms,” wrote Levin in a thread on X. “Our campaign pointed out time and again how Democrats should not welcome outsized spending by Super PACS that support anti-choice, MAGA insurrectionists into our primaries, and today we see the logical conclusion of those alliances.”

author: Erin Reed
title: El-Sayed Didn’t Fall for Anti-Trans “Gotcha” Moment in “60 Minutes” Interview
content:
If he can win a highly contested seat, it will be a clear case that embracing anti-trans views is not required to win.

If he can win a highly contested seat, it will be a clear case that embracing anti-trans views is not required to win.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan, has long been a vocal ally to transgender people. In the 2026 midterms, he has not wavered in that support, despite the hundreds of millions of dollars in attack ads, much of which has been focused on transgender people, that have poured into this year’s elections from the Republican Party and, even at times, from the Democratic Party as well. Rather than capitulate to those ads, as some Democrats have done, El-Sayed has defended transgender people outright, on sports, on education and on health care. That was certainly true in his 60 Minutes interview released Sunday, in which Ross Douthat, the conservative columnist Bari Weiss brought to the program this summer, pressed him multiple times on his support for transgender people.

Douthat, the interviewer, started with a question as to whether El-Sayed’s faith puts him in conflict with “a very socially liberal and culturally liberal party,” listing “abortion, same-sex marriage, transgenderism [sic]” as issues on which “a lot of Muslims, like a lot of Christians,” hold conservative positions. Notably, “transgenderism” is a far-right term used to frame transgender people as an ideology rather than a class of people. In doing so, those who use it seek to paint transgender people’s existence as a matter of faith or belief rather than a fundamental characteristic of a person. In its most extreme form, the claim is that gender itself does not exist.

El-Sayed then rejected the premise that his faith puts him in conflict with the values of a secular liberal society, pointing instead to the importance of standing for all people’s rights: “I believe in rights. And even though somebody might use rights that you don’t understand, you never mean to use yourself, you still got to show up and fight for those rights. And that’s the thing about this moment. I think it is a responsibility for us to stand up against the risk of government making incursions on any of our rights, to build the kind of continuum, the kind of coalition where any of us and all of us who have our rights at risk are standing up and fighting for all of our rights. And I think this is an important responsibility. So in conversations with folks in the Muslim community, conversations with folks in the LGBTQ community, the point I always make is to say, listen, I don’t care whether or not you will ever use a right that you were fighting for, understand that a failure to show up and fight for that right is a failure to show up and fight for your own.”

Douthat attempted to pin El-Sayed down on transgender people, asking: “What about the rights of parents to control over their children’s education? Because a lot of places where there’s tension between Islam and Muslim voters and what I’m calling cultural liberalism are around issues like what is taught in school, what happens with transgender kids on sports teams, and so on, right? Like these are places where rights are in conflict, right? What do you think happens there?”

El-Sayed forcefully rejected it, pointing out that it is unrealistic to expect that kids will not learn about transgender people in the age of the internet: “The notion somehow that you are going to prevent your child from being exposed to something that you may find disagreeable, and that that is going to be because of school, is so profoundly outdated, because of course you have all the information and they have all the information. So here’s the thing about it. I think it’s really important for us to recognize that the free flow of information is actually a beautiful thing. It’s really important, and the most important thing you can do is not try to protect a person from seeing a thing. It’s about trying to make sure that as you coach your kid through the world, that you are engaging with them and saying, here’s what I believe, here’s what you may see in the world, you get to make your choices about who you’re going to be in the world.”

He then pivoted, as many other Democrats have, to the argument that Republicans are trying to make the issue into a cultural flash point to distract voters from the cost of gas, groceries and medical care.

Watch the entire exchange here (Start at 41:16):

This is far from the only time that El-Sayed has stood up for transgender people. In August, Fox News’ Jesse Watters asked El-Sayed whether he supported “sex changes for minors,” and he responded that “the government shouldn’t tell you what kind of health care you should have, and if you’re a minor, that’s between you and your doctor and your parents.” Then, a few weeks later, a Michigan State student asked his position on gender-affirming care, and he replied, “I don’t think the government gets to have a say about what health care is provided in what circumstances and why.” Despite running in a state like Michigan, which voted for Trump in 2024, El-Sayed has refused to sacrifice transgender people in his attempt to win a Senate seat for Democrats, and it appears to be working: El-Sayed is surging ahead in the polls, with the New York Times/Siena poll released Sunday finding him ahead of Republican Mike Rogers, 53 percent to 42 percent.

El-Sayed’s answer has set off a firestorm on the right. Katie Pavlich of NewsNation posted on X that El-Sayed wants your child to see photos of male genitalia. Nancy Mace, whose claim to fame is her push to ban the first transgender member of Congress from the Capitol’s bathrooms, simply posted “OH MY GOD!” Riley Gaines went on Fox News to denounce El-Sayed, and Rogers himself posted the clip. None of it has led El-Sayed to retract his answers or soften his support for transgender people.

El-Sayed’s race will be one of the most important to watch on election night. If he can win a highly contested seat despite the anti-transgender Republican money spent against him and the attacks from the right-leaning wing of his own party, it will be a clear case that embracing anti-trans views is not required to win swing states and swing districts across the United States. His approach stands in sharp contrast to that of Josh Turek in Iowa, who has called for a federal funding ban on gender-affirming care, or Marcy Kaptur in Ohio, who said in an ad that she “voted with Republicans to keep transgender ideology out of our schools.” EITM will be tracking every race with transgender implications on election night, and you can follow our election guide here.
