title: "Jülide Kural Yalnız Değildir”: Kadınlar imzaya çağırdı
content:
Sanatçı Kadir İnanır’ın yaşamını yitirmesinin ardından Jülide Kural’a yönelik cinsiyetçi saldırılar ve hakaretlere karşı “Jülide Kural Yalnız Değildir” başlıklı dayanışma kampanyası başlatıldı. Kampanyayı başlatan kadınlar, Kural’la dayanışma göstermek için herkesi imza vermeye çağırdı.







Kampanyaya imza ile destek vermek için

 burayı 

tıklayabilirsiniz.







Kampanya metninde, Jülide Kural’ın özel yaşamının kamuoyu önünde sorgulanmasına ve itibarsızlaştırılmaya çalışılmasına tepki gösterildi.




Bir kadının saygınlığının medeni durumuna bağlı olmadığının vurgulandığı metinde, Kural’ın yalnızca Kadir İnanır’ın hayat arkadaşı olmadığı, kendi emeği, birikimi ve sanatçı kimliğiyle toplumsal yaşamda yer edindiği belirtildi.




Kural’ın hayat arkadaşını kaybettiği ve yas tuttuğu bir dönemde saldırılara maruz bırakılmasına dikkat çekilen açıklamada, yasın kişisel bir süreç olduğu ve kimsenin bir başkasının nerede, nasıl ve ne kadar süreyle yas tutacağına karar veremeyeceği ifade edildi.




İnsanların kişilik haklarını ve mahremiyetini hiçe sayan, dedikoduları ve doğruluğu bilinmeyen iddiaları toplumsal linçe dönüştüren anlayışın kınandığı metinde, Kadir İnanır’ın anısına ve Jülide Kural’ın yasına saygı gösterilmesi istendi.




Kampanya metninin sonunda imzacı kadınlar, Jülide Kural’la dayanışma içinde olduklarını belirterek herkesi kişilik haklarına, özel yaşamın mahremiyetine ve Kural’ın yasına saygı göstermeye çağırdı.



















25 KASIM'A GİDERKEN




Jülide Kural: Tanık Olduğum Şiddet Korkusuzluğu Öğretti  




19 Kasım 2019










İmzaya çağrı metninin tamamı şöyle:




" Jülide Kural Yalnız Değildir!




Sanatçı Kadir İnanır'ın yaşamını yitirmesinin ardından, sanatçı Jülide Kural'a yönelik sürdürülen cinsiyetçi saldırıları ve hakaretleri kabul etmiyoruz.




Bir kadının özel yaşamının kamuoyu önünde sorgulanmasını ve kendisinin itibarsızlaştırılmaya çalışılmasını reddediyoruz.




Hiçbir kadının saygınlığı medeni durumuna bağlı değildir. Jülide Kural, yalnızca Kadir İnanır'ın hayat arkadaşı değil; kendi emeği, birikimi ve sanatçı kimliğiyle toplumsal yaşamda yer edinmiş bir kadındır.




Üstelik bütün bunlar, hayat arkadaşını kaybetmiş bir kadının yas tuttuğu günlerde yaşanıyor. Yas, herkesin kendi hissettiği biçiminde ve kendi iç zamanında yaşadığı insani bir süreçtir. Bir insanın nerede, nasıl ve ne kadar süreyle yas tutacağına başkaları karar veremez. Yas tuttuğu günlerde bir kadını kendisini savunmak zorunda bırakmak kabul edilemez bir hoyratlıktır.




İnsanların kişilik haklarını ve mahremiyetini kamuoyu önünde hiçe sayan, dedikoduları ve doğruluğu bilinmeyen iddiaları dolaşıma sokarak bunları toplumsal linçe dönüştüren anlayışı kınıyoruz.




Yaşamını yitiren bir sanatçının anısına ve hayat arkadaşının yasına gösterilmesi gereken saygının, özel yaşamları üzerinden yürütülen tartışmalarla gölgelenmesini kabul etmiyoruz.




Biz aşağıda imzası bulunan kadınlar, Jülide Kural'la dayanışma içinde olduğumuzu ifade ediyor; herkesi kişilik haklarına, özel yaşamın mahremiyetine, Kadir İnanır'ın anısına ve Jülide Kural'ın yasına saygı göstermeye davet ediyoruz."



















“BEN ROSA LUXEMBURG” 




Sahnede iki devrimci kadın: Jülide mi? Rosa mı? 




10 Aralık 2022













Ne olmuştu?




Oyuncu Kadir İnanır’ın 26 Haziran 2026’da yaşamını yitirmesinin ardından sanatçı Jülide Kural’a İnanır’ın yeğeni Levent İnanır miras hakkı üzerinden sözlü saldırdı.




Kural’ın özel yaşamı, İnanır’la birlikteliği ve yas süreci de kamuoyunun gündemine taşındı.




Kadir İnanır’ın 2022 yılında noter huzurunda hazırlattığı vasiyetnamesinde mal varlığını uzun yıllardır birlikte olduğu Jülide Kural’a bıraktığı ortaya çıktı. Vasiyetin açıklanmasının ardından İnanır’ın yeğeni Levent İnanır, dayısının sağlık sorunları nedeniyle vasiyetnameyi hazırladığı sırada irade sorunu yaşadığını öne sürerek hukuki yollara başvuracaklarını söyledi.




Jülide Kural, T24’ten Sibel Yükler’e yaptığı açıklamada hem miras iddialarına hem de kendisine yönelik söylemlere yanıt verdi. İnanır’ın büyük bir servete sahip olduğu iddiasının doğru olmadığını belirten Kural, mal varlığının birlikte yaşadıkları ev, üç eski otomobil ve bankadaki bir miktar birikimden ibaret olduğunu söyledi.




Kural, İnanır’la evlenmemelerinin kendi tercihi olduğunu belirterek birlikteliklerinin hukuki bir statüden değil, sevgi, güven ve ortak yaşam iradesinden beslendiğini söyledi. Kendisinin bağımsız bir kadın olarak emeği ve kişiliğiyle var olduğunu vurgulayan Kural, gerçek dışı iddialar ve kişilik haklarına yönelik saldırılar karşısında hukuki süreç başlatacağını duyurdu.




Yas tutma biçimi de tartışma konusu yapıldı




Levent İnanır’ın, Jülide Kural’ın Kadir İnanır’ın ölümünden bir hafta sonra Bodrum’a tatile gittiği yönündeki açıklamaları da tartışmalara neden oldu. Kural ise bu iddiayı reddederek İnanır’ın mezarıyla ilgilenmek için üç hafta İstanbul’da kaldığını, ardından Bodrum’a tatil için değil, yaşadığı sağlık sorunları nedeniyle psikolojik destek almak amacıyla gittiğini açıkladı.




Kural, kendisi hakkında yapılan rencide edici açıklamalar ve hakaretler nedeniyle hukuki süreç başlatacağını da söyledi.




Müjde Ar’dan Jülide Kural’a destek




Tartışmalara sanatçı Müjde Ar da tepki gösterdi. T24’ten gazeteci Sibel Yükler’e konuşan Ar, Kadir İnanır ile Jülide Kural’ın 20 yılı aşkın birlikteliklerine tanıklık ettiğini belirterek Kural’a yönelik saldırılara karşı çıktı.




Ar, “Jülide Kural korkunç bir şekilde kadına şiddet sarmalının içine düşürüldü. Kadınlar olarak onun daha fazla incinmesine müsaade etmeyeceğiz” dedi. Ar, kamuoyunu Kural’ın maruz kaldığı saldırıların meşrulaştırılmasına izin vermemeye çağırdı.







(EMK)

Bulgaristan'da düzenlenen cumhurbaşkanlığı seçimlerinde mevcut Cumhurbaşkanı Iliana Yotova ve cumhurbaşkanı yardımcısı adayı Kiril Valchev'in seçimi kazandığı bildirildi.

Bulgaristan basınında yayımlanan gayriresmi sonuçlara göre, yerel saatle 20.00'de sona eren oy verme işleminin ardından açıklanan iki ayrı sandık çıkış anketinde Yotova'nın oy oranı yaklaşık yüzde 51 olarak ölçüldü.

Seçim sonuçlarına ilişkin ilk veriler sandık çıkış anketlerine dayanırken, Yotova ve Valchev'in zaferi Bulgaristan basınında geniş yer buldu.

Kesin sonuçların açıklanmasıyla seçim sürecinin resmen tamamlanması bekleniyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: FMF Staff
title: Deporting Afghans to the Taliban by Way of Pakistan Is a Betrayal That Gets the United States Nothing
content:
The Trump administration is reportedly preparing to put more than 150 Afghans on a flight to Pakistan, where they would then be transferred across the border into Taliban-ruled Afghanistan. AfghanEvac, a coalition advocating for Afghan allies, says some of those facing removal are the brothers and sons of men who served alongside U.S. forces. The first flight could leave as early as Monday, just one day before Election Day in the United States.

Because the United States cannot deport people directly to Afghanistan, it lacks official diplomatic relations with the Taliban regime; the plan routes them through Pakistan. Call it what it is: a deportation to the Taliban with a layover. Officials reportedly told The New York Times that the removal is, in effect, to Afghanistan, and detainees have been told the same. Pakistan’s role is to carry out the handoff.

What the layover adds is risk. Afghans would be moved through a third country and beyond any oversight, and placed in the hands of authorities who have no obligation to protect them. From there, they could be pushed across the border to a regime they fled and one that would seek to harm them. These are the people who escaped Taliban rule after August 15, 2021.

Pakistan is not safe for Afghans. Since 2023, the Pakistani government has expelled over 2.4 million Afghan refugees back to Afghanistan as relations with the Taliban have deteriorated. Earlier this year, Pakistani officials ordered law enforcement agencies nationwide to arrest Afghans without valid visas. This is part of a years-long campaign of forced returns that has sent millions of Afghans back to a country where many face homelessness and unemployment. Many of those Afghan refugees were born and raised in Pakistan.

The Taliban’s “amnesty” is empty words. It is not a guarantee of safety.

On its first day back in power in August 2021, the Taliban announced a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and the former republic government of Afghanistan. That promise was never kept. The United Nations has documented reports of extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detentions, and other abuses. The families of former U.S. partners have particular reason to fear for their safety.

The policy to return Afghans to Afghanistan also lends credibility to the Taliban.

When the United States sends people into Taliban-controlled Afghanistan, even through a middleman, it implies that returning is safe. It suggests that the United States is willing to rely on the assurances of a regime that has repeatedly broken its promises and violated fundamental rights. Deporting Afghans in this way serves the Taliban’s desire to be treated as a legitimate government and to establish normal relations with the Trump administration.

The Trump administration advanced a similar narrative last year in May, when it ended temporary protections for Afghans, claiming that “Afghanistan has had an improved security situation” despite clear evidence to the contrary.

Cooperating, even indirectly, with a regime that has barred half the population of Afghanistan – girls and women – from education and public life, and has violated every international and national law gains the United States nothing in return. It is neither smart nor logical. It would not serve the U.S. now or in the future. It adds to the humiliation of how the U.S. withdrew from Afghanistan and handed the country back to the Taliban, a terrorist group it fought for 20 years.

The United States gains nothing from this policy. It loses far more.

The cost of this policy lands on American credibility. The United States asked Afghans to translate, guard, drive, gather intelligence, cook, clean, implement the many projects, and fight beside its forces, and promised to stand by them. Abandoning those allies, or their families, breaks that promise and abandons its obligation to protect people who are in harm’s way because they supported the U.S. mission.

The damage goes beyond Afghanistan. Future partners in any other conflict will remember how the United States treated those who stood with it. This is not border security. These individuals have already undergone vetting. It does not make Americans safer. It uses federal resources to send people toward danger, and abandons those who trusted the United States.

63% of Americans do not want Afghans to be deported.

A bipartisan national poll by AfghanEvac and HIAS, designed and run by Lake Research Partners and The Tarrance Group, found that 84 percent of likely 2026 voters say America should keep its promise to Afghan wartime allies. By more than two to one, voters oppose deporting hundreds of Afghan refugees who assisted U.S. forces to third countries where they have no connection, and 63 percent oppose deporting Afghan allies to such countries. Seventy-six percent support restoring protection programs for Afghans whose resettlement cases were already approved. Support for admitting Afghan allies rises from 52 percent to 72 percent once voters learn who these partners are.

Call your Member of Congress and your two senators. The Capitol switchboard is (202) 224-3121. Ask the operator to connect you with your Member’s office. Ask them to:

Publicly oppose this deportation flight and press the administration to halt removals of Afghans from the U.S.

Ask them to sign the discharge petition for the bipartisan Afghanistan TPS Act, which would protect Afghans already in the U.S.

Keep the promises made to Afghans who stood with us.

A simple script: I’m a constituent. I’m calling to ask [Member’s name] to oppose deporting Afghans to the Taliban through Pakistan and to protect Afghans who are already in the United States. Keeping our word to our allies is not only the right thing to do, it’s also a smart thing to do. We must deliver on our promise.

The United States made a promise. For 20 years, Afghan allies delivered, risking their lives and putting their families in danger in support of the U.S. mission in Afghanistan. The American people continue to stand with the Afghans who are already in the U.S. They believe it’s the right thing to honor its commitments. Deporting Afghans is not a sound policy, does not advance U.S. interests, and will only undermine America’s credibility.

For more on Afghan deportation, follow AfghanEvac here and here.

Source: AfghanEvac; the New York Times; Amu TV; USCIS.

St. Paul, MN – Looking closely at court filings around the “Minnesota 15” prosecution has revealed vast patterns of surveillance by federal agents, in Minnesota and beyond. We took a closer look at the summer’s largest set of filings, 30 main exhibits and several subsequent ones, to map out just how undercover operations, 

facial recognition

We did an in-depth

. Covering hundreds of pages of evidence, it’s around 100 minutes long. While it is an almost overwhelming level of detail, it is worth checking out to get a glimpse at both the breadth and the depth of how this campaign worked.
















Watch the full report on

The prosecution of the Minnesota 15

ICE in Minnesota: 2025-2026




Minnesota 15 Coverage







Federal prosecutor Brian W. Lynch, who 

marched masked at the January 6 riot in Washington, DC,

Kieran F. Knutson, the president of Communication Workers of America Local 7250, told Unicorn Riot that the surveillance which targeted his union’s finances was part of an effort to “map out the resistance to ICE”:







“In my opinion the federal investigations should be seen as both an attack on and an effort to map out the resistance to ICE in Minnesota including the trade unions.




The Feds have a broad understanding of the different facets of the resistance and they have used these investigations as a means to map out the specific organizations, influential organizers, and networks of solidarity and collaborative activity.




The release of documents shows that this is not limited to investigating incidents involving ICE agents and protesters but is expansive to include unions and community groups that sponsored and organized the January 23rd Day of Truth & Freedom with No Work, No School, and No Shopping, including their finances.




This investigation started concurrent with the launching of Operation Metro Surge revealing its purpose as a counter-insurgency operation to, in the words of Commander Greg Bovino, ‘pacify this place’.




The unions – as a part of the active resistance to the illegal and deadly ICE operation – are an important target for the Federal government.”




Kieran F. Knutson, President CWA Local 7250







Federal Reserve wire transfer systems searched for CWA union, Sunrise Movement, and other data between January 1, 2023 and March 29, 2026.







Anti-Left Campaign Centered on Minnesota




Ali Winston in Wired pointed out that 

ICE is running one of the largest anti-left surveillance campaigns in U.S. history

, and Minnesota is at the heart of it. By his count, 115 ICE-HSI agents were involved in the Minnesota 15 case, including several high-profile agents from other states. He also found a 

spinoff surveillance campaign in Chicago

 in April 2026.




As Winston noted, Unicorn Riot’s previous 

exposure of the confidential ICE-HSI Undercover Operations Handbook

Attorneys for the Minnesota 15 filed documents showing that Operation Keyhole was a “certified undercover” (CUC) operation. On September 9, this forced 

Minnesota U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen to disclose Keyhole has been in effect since late 2008

As of June 2026, five investigations including Whipple Shield were being supplied under Keyhole, according to Rosen. The point of including Operation Whipple Shield and Puppet Master in Keyhole was to enable “the use of CUC Keyhole funds to provide investigative support, such as funding the deployment of personnel and the acquisition of necessary equipment,” according to Rosen.







An ICE undercover management flow chart originally uncovered by Unicorn Riot and

author: CMI Argentina
title: La IA es un nuevo transtorno para Estados Unidos
content:
Trump espera contrarrestar sus fracasos económicos con la IA. Pero se acrecientan los indicios de sobreinversión y estallido de la burbuja bursátil que alimenta esa innovación. La euforia digital agrava la desigualdad, el quebranto fiscal, el rebrote inflacionario y el declive del dólar. Profundiza el declive de Estados Unidos y afecta a una economía desindustrializada. La élite de Washington carece de fórmulas para lidiar con el creciente avance de China.







Por Claudio Katz (1)




Trump ha concentrado en la Inteligencia Artificial todas las expectativas económicas de Estados Unidos. El crecimiento del PIB está impulsado casi exclusivamente por el gasto en esa tecnología, el mercado de valores opera en torno al puñado de empresas que controlan esas acciones y casi toda la inversión se localiza en ese sector. El universo restante de la producción, el consumo y el comercio ha quedado sujeto al devenir de la IA. Como en todas las apuestas riesgosas y extremas que despliega, Trump juega todas sus cartas al éxito de esa innovación digital.




Se apoya en la oleada de tecno-optimismo que motorizan los auspiciantes de la nueva tecnología y proclama que la IA traccionará el crecimiento, con nuevos puestos de trabajo calificados, incremento de la productividad y aceleración del desarrollo con asistencia automatizada.




Un inspirador de este clima proclama que la nueva tecnología es sinónimo de progreso, abundancia y bienestar, si se reafirma el pleno funcionamiento del mercado, sin regulaciones, ni restricciones de ningún tipo 

(2)

. Otros entusiastas auguran un festival de empleo junto a la IA 

(3)

 y varias afamadas consultoras pronostican expansión y bonanza por esa invención 

(4)

.




Trump concibe además a la IA como un instrumento para doblegar a China, multiplicar el belicismo y recomponer la supremacía mundial de Estados Unidos. Pretende también utilizarla para instaurar un estado policial y criminalizar a los opositores 

(5)

.




Esa innovación es vista, en los hechos, como el gran contrapeso a las adversidades que afronta el magnate. Los aranceles, sanciones y amenazas monetarias que desplegó Trump en el 2025 tuvieron resultados tan desfavorables como el viraje bélico del 2026, que ha desembocado en el fulminante fracaso de la guerra contra Irán. ¿La nueva apuesta revertirá esos fallidos? ¿Permitirá contrarrestar el declive imperial de Estados Unidos? Existen numerosas razones para postular una respuesta negativa a esos interrogantes.




Acciones de IA en septiembre pasado. Foto: MICHAEL M. SANTIAGO – GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA




Sobreinversión a la vista




Estados Unidos no está en condiciones de utilizar en su ámbito productivo los vertiginosos avances que desenvuelve con la Inteligencia Artificial. A diferencia de lo ocurrido con otras revoluciones tecnológicas del siglo XX, el declive de su industria le impide ese aprovechamiento.




La primera potencia afronta una aguda regresión industrial, con estancamiento de la productividad e imparable pérdida de competitividad frente a China. En la dura batalla por bajar costos, aumentar ventas y conquistar mercados, Estados Unidos tiende a quedar relegado.




Los abanderados de la IA prometen superar esa adversidad con la innovación más revolucionaria de la centuria en curso. Pero omiten que el exponencial desarrollo de ese sector se consuma en frontal contraposición con el resto de la economía. Avanza capturando todos los recursos requeridos para el resurgimiento de la industria, sin ofrecer ningún indicio de retroalimentación ulterior de beneficios para el universo fabril.




Los paladines de la IA auguran ese impacto positivo, cuando la nueva tecnología sea incorporada a las empresas, con el consiguiente incremento de la productividad, las ganancias y el crecimiento del PBI. Pero no existe hasta ahora el menor indicio de proximidad de esa secuencia.




Entre 2005 y 2019, el crecimiento medio de la productividad en Estados Unidos giró en torno al 1,5 % anual y aumentó al 2,5 % desde finales de 2022 por el uso de la tecnología ya existente 

(6)

. El efecto la IA aún no se avizora por la lentitud, las dificultades y las prevenciones que suscita su aplicación y las estimaciones sobre sus efectos positivos son muy cautelosas 

(7)

.




Lo que por el contrario prevalece como dato muy visible es el descomunal exceso de inversión, que incentiva el niño mimado del capitalismo norteamericano. Esas tasas de absorción de capital aumentan al 20% anual, es decir a un nivel sin precedentes en el pasado.




Las mega compañías tecnológicas (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon) comprometen sumas insólitas de 725.000 millones de dólares en 2026, para construir la infraestructura de la IA. Son montos que superan ampliamente lo invertido en la construcción ferroviaria del siglo XIX o en todas las secuencias de la revolución digital de las últimas dos décadas (computadoras, chips, redes, Internet). Cuando, cómo y de qué forma impactaría esa inversión en la producción es un interrogante irresuelto.




Las empresas tienen previsto invertir en IA cerca de 10,3 billones de dólares hasta 2032, que deberán financiar con enormes deudas puesto que ningún calculo estima ingresos futuros de ese orden. Esa cifra equivale a una inversión en proporción al PBI que triplica los porcentuales de las cinco revoluciones tecnológicas precedentes 

(8)

.




Igualmente, muchos esperan que los modelos de la IA generen una demanda acorde a la mega inversión en curso, pero no aportan ninguna evaluación de beneficios amoldados a semejante expectativa. Es muy visible la brecha que separa el descomunal aumento de la inversión, con los negocios que permitirían ese desarrollo. Esa desconexión multiplica los diagnósticos de sobreinversión y el consiguiente divorcio entre el capital canalizado hacia la IA y la rentabilidad esperada por esa apuesta.




Si se toma en cuenta lo ocurrido con las revoluciones tecnológicas del pasado, el aumento de la productividad derivada de una innovación radical se consuma al cabo de varias crisis. Esas convulsiones desvalorizan gran parte del capital absorbido por el nuevo sector, antes de inaugurar el esperado despegue.




Las estimaciones más corrientes sugieren brechas de una o dos décadas entre la invención de la nueva tecnología y su conversión en innovación incorporada al circuito productivo. La repetición de esa secuencia implicaría un escenario de crisis próximas y demorados efectos benévolos. Pero las perspectivas son más sombrías para la IA por las monumentales dudas que rodean a su implementación económica.




Hasta ahora, las empresas no saben cómo utilizarla de la manera efectiva en su actividad corriente y los proveedores del nuevo instrumento no se atreven a traspasar el costo real de ese servicio a sus clientes o consumidores. Invierten cifras gigantescas en mejorar la IA sin exigir remuneraciones acordes a ese gasto. La sobreinversión no solo se verifica en esas brechas. También se corrobora en la preocupación por la pérdida de empleos que suscitará la aplicación de la IA, con el consiguiente impacto negativo de ese recorte sobre los ingresos, los mercados y finalmente los propios beneficios.







El atractivo inmediato que ofrece la IA para los capitalistas es el reemplazo del personal calificado por alguna operación automatizada de menor costo. Pero tanto la escala como las consecuencias de esa sustitución, incrementan los temores en un efecto económico nocivo por su introducción.




La sobreinversión suele desencadenar estallidos, cuando los participantes de ese proceso perciben que han comprometido sumas de capital desconectadas de la valorización factible. Ese punto crítico comienza a aflorar en varios indicios del termómetro financiero.




Burbuja sin control




La principal señal de la sobreinversión en IA es la burbuja financiera que está generando esa innovación en Wall Street. Induce una montaña de especulación nunca vista en el mayor mercado bursátil del mundo. Desde hace una década las acciones de las mega empresas digitales (Nvidia, Alphabet-Google, Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta-Facebook, Tesla) concentran el grueso de las compras y acaparaban un tercio del valor del principal índice de ese mercado.




El logo de Nvidia en la fachada de su sede de Santa Clara.Justin Sullivan/Getty Images




Como las nuevas estrellas de la IA se han embarcado en monumentales inversiones para construir Centros de Datos, semiconductores e infraestructuras de hardware, los montos en juego superan todo lo imaginado. En la oferta pública para reunir dinero, SpaceX capturó el volumen más grande de la historia. OpenAI y Anthropic se aprestan a lograr resultados parecidos, engrosando la capitalización de esas empresas con cifras inéditas. Mientras nadie sabe cuál será el rendimiento futuro de su actividad, las tres compañías exhiben por ahora significativas pérdidas 

(9)

.




A medida que recolectan fondos, los dueños de esas compañías acrecientan sus fortunas a una escala que enmudece a cualquier mortal. Elon Musk se ha convertido en el primer billonario de la historia y acumula por sí mismo riquezas superiores al 46% más pobre de la humanidad (3800 millones de personas) 

(10)

. Junto a sus pares de la plutocracia digital pretende seguir juntando dinero a la espera que la burbuja nunca explote. Pero ese quimérico objetivo jamás fue alcanzado con ninguna innovación. La codicia de los capitalistas desemboca invariablemente en estallido financiero.




La burbuja de la IA se alimenta, además, con una explosiva modalidad de financiamiento circular y cruzado entre las propias empresas, que torna imposible distinguir los ingresos reales de los movimientos contables que engrosan las valuaciones. Los participantes de este circuito (denominados hiperescaladores) alimentan a su vez esa ficción, con préstamos y emisiones de deuda por doquier que inflan aún más las cotizaciones. La velocidad de ese engrosamiento va muy por delante de los indicadores de algún retorno acorde 

(11)

.




La alocada euforia en curso está personificada en Ellon Musk y su empresa SpaceX, que sin ninguna perspectiva científica creíble recoleta fondos para colonizar Marte. Las acciones de su empresa ya cotizan 350 veces por encima del importe que generarían sus futuros beneficios.




El imparable éxito de sus negocios lo ha convertido en la encarnación de todos los ensueños del capitalismo y ese atractivo explica el poder de arrastre, que ejerce sobre pequeños inversores cegados por el libertarismo ultraliberal. Ese espejismo es muy ilustrativo del clima imperante en torno a la IA 

(12)

.




Para montar la burbuja en curso, la plutocracia digital ha reforzado las estrechas relaciones que forjó desde su nacimiento con los popes de Wall Street. Esos financistas lucran con los jugosos márgenes de toda la intermediación en curso.




Pero los tecno-millonarios afinaron también sus conexiones con el nuevo bloque de Fondos de Inversión, Hedge Funds y Cryptomonedas, que gana fortunas inflando el valor de los activos del mundo digital 

(13)

. Ese entrelazamiento potencia las señales de alerta que emiten los economistas del establishment frente a la tormenta que se avecina.




Esa calamidad es incluso advertida por los propios gestores de la burbuja, que se cubren las espaldas tramitando un rescate estatal parecido al socorro que recibieron los grandes bancos en el 2008. Las firmas tecnológicas se perciben a sí mismas como perdurables gigantes que toda la sociedad debería sostener.




El CEO de OpenAI, Sam Altman, tiene en mente ese auxilio, cuando propicia la creación de un fondo financiero público “para que los ciudadanos puedan participar de los beneficios de la IA”. Ese organismo sería el puente para el gran socorro, si la burbuja desemboca en un generalizado colapso financiero 

(14)

.




Tal como ocurrió en el 2008, el alcance internacional de ese estallido está a la vista, en la enorme participación de capitales de todo origen en la fiebre de la IA. En algunos casos -como Corea del Sur- esa tensión ya se avizora por la gran exposición de las firmas de chips, memorias y semiconductores. En otros países -como Arabia Saudita, los Emiratos Árabes Unidos o Kuwait- se han montado gigantescos fondos soberanos para financiar la nueva tecnología 

(15)

. Como las mega empresas digitales de Estados Unidos han emitido deuda en todo el mundo, el temblor de su emprendimiento estrella haría trastabillar a todo el planeta.




La IA es una innovación radical con inciertas potencialidades productivas, que irrumpe en una economía afectada por décadas de financiarización. Los grandes capitalistas de Estados Unidos han contrarrestado sus declinantes ganancias en la producción, con elevadas remuneraciones en las finanzas. La sobreinversión en el ámbito digital realimenta esa hipertrofia financiera y la vulnerabilidad de todas las operaciones con capitales ficticios que acosan a la primera potencia.




Wall Street




Lo ocurrido hace dos décadas con la burbuja de acciones puntocom es el antecedente tranquilizador que exhiben los involucrados en la actual ruleta digital. Ese trastorno -que antecedió a la masiva introducción de Internet y los teléfonos celulares- fue un típico desplome de Wall Street de limitadas consecuencias. Condujo a la remodelación del sector, depurando a las firmas perdedoras y afianzando a las empresas que han comandado el auge posterior.


Pero la escala de capitales en juego en esta oportunidad y sus interconexiones globales auguran una tensión de otro porte. Esa dimensión obedece a su empalme con otro espectro de tensiones en varios ámbitos de la economía estadounidense.




Desigualdad, endeudamiento e inflación




La sobreinversión y las burbujas financieras que acompañan a la IA interactúan con otros desequilibrios reforzando su intensidad. Ese agravamiento es muy visible en el plano de la desigualdad, que al cabo de una larga preeminencia del neoliberalismo se ha transformado en la desgracia mayúscula de la sociedad norteamericana.




Esa inequidad es potenciada por la tecno-plutocracia del Silicon Valley. Desde ese epicentro digital se ha empoderado la nueva élite de mil millonarios, que sintetiza y personifica Elon Musk. Ese ídolo de la ultraderecha exhibe su billonaria fortuna, despreciando la solidaridad humana y naturalizando la despiada lógica del capitalismo. Como todos los súper ricos de la era actual, encarna la brutalidad que sostiene a ese sistema 

(16)

.




Elon Musk, nazi.




La plutocracia digital exacerba la desigualdad que en las últimas décadas ha corroído a los Estados Unidos. Mientras que en 1980 la proporción del ingreso nacional en manos del 1% más rico era la mitad que la del 50% más pobre, en la actualidad duplica ese porcentual 

(17)

.




En Estados Unidos se localiza gran parte del 1% de ultra millonarios que detenta el 45% de la riqueza global. Tan solo en 2024 la fortuna conjunta de esa élite creció tres veces más rápido que en 2023. Los acaudalados de las firmas tecnológicas conforman el segmento más privilegiado de ese minúsculo grupo. Su exuberante patrimonio consolida la estructura dualizada de la economía estadounidense, asentada en el alto crecimiento de los servicios digitales y el sostenido estancamiento del grueso de la actividad productiva. Esa desigualdad acentúa la baja competitividad de una economía obstruida por la creciente masa de consumidores endeudados y empobrecidos.




Pero la interacción de la IA con los desequilibrios de la economía estadounidense es más explosiva en lo inmediato en el terreno de la deuda pública. Los multimillonarios fondos que alimentan la burbuja tecnológica en Wall Street, compiten con la financiación de un pasivo estatal que se agiganta día a día.




Ya no está en juego la típica competencia de rentabilidad entre dos inversiones, sino una inédita tensión entre desequilibrios mayúsculos que se potencian mutuamente. La magnitud de los capitales capturados por el sector digital es tan descomunal, como el descontrolado volumen del endeudamiento público.




Esas cajas sin fondo rivalizan por la absorción del ahorro mundial. Por un lado, las firmas tecnológicas han captado en el curso del 2026 más de 220.000 millones de dólares. Por otra parte, el bache fiscal que Estados Unidos necesita financiar se ha duplicado desde el 2017 y exige un monto de pago de intereses superior a los gastos del Pentágono. Debe lidiar con un stock de la deuda federal que ya superó los 40 billones de dólares 

(18)

.




Estas múltiples demandas de dinero irrumpen cuando ha concluido la etapa del dinero barato, que inauguró el rescate de los bancos y prolongó la pandemia. Frente al atractivo de la burbuja digital, los acreedores de la deuda pública reclaman mayor remuneración a su financiación de ese pasivo. Esta exigencia genera el sostenido aumento de la tasa de interés, que Trump pretendía reducir para sostener el nivel de actividad de la alicaída economía estadounidense.




President Donald Trump tours the Federal Reserve alongside Fed Chair Jerome Powell and Sen. Tim Scott (R-SC), Thursday, July 24, 2025. (Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok)




Esa financiación crecientemente encarecida de los Bonos del Tesoro es una bomba de tiempo, con esquirlas en todas las direcciones. Por un lado, torna más gravosos los préstamos internos de ese país y, por otra parte, tensa las relaciones con los acreedores extranjeros. Esos tenedores foráneos poseen cerca de un tercio de los bonos del Tesoro y tienden a retraer sus compras frente a la evidente insolvencia de su deudor.




Estados Unidos depende desde hace décadas de la colocación de sus títulos en el mundo, pero está ingresando en un círculo vicioso de costosas refinanciaciones y peligrosos manejos especulativos. Mientras la remuneración de ese pasivo se ubica en el nivel más alto desde 2007, su administrador Scott Bessent improvisa cotidianas recompras de títulos, manejos de plazos y diferencias de tasas, para preservar la fidelidad de los inquietos acreedores de esa carga.


Para colmo de males, debe recurrir al rescate del principal tenedor de esos títulos que es Japón, un país agobiado por el estancamiento, el endeudamiento y una pérdida de competitividad superior al socio norteamericano 

(19)

.




Las operaciones de socorro mutuo entre ambas potencias incluyeron durante mucho tiempo mecanismos de especulación, para lucrar con las diferencias de tasas y paridades monetaria entre el yen y el dólar. Pero ese 

carry trade

 se ha tornado insostenible 

(20)

. Por esa razón, los periódicos temblores en la Bolsa de Tokio encienden todas las alarmas del sistema financiero mundial, revitalizando el fantasma del 2008. Todos saben que ese desmoronamiento fue provocado y contenido con el mismo festival de deuda pública que impera en la actualidad.




Además, la inflación que generó ese auxilio al comienzo de la década, vuelve a reaparecer con fogoneros de otra índole y efectos del mismo tipo. Por un lado, la improvisación proteccionista de Trump introdujo un desorden arancelario que encareció la economía estadounidense y, por otra parte, el incremento del precio del petróleo que disparó la guerra del Golfo, ya impacta sobre todas las cadenas de valor. Esa presión inflacionaria induce a incrementar las tasas de interés, obstruyendo en forma adicional el intento trumpista de sostener el débil crecimiento del PBI estadounidense.




Esa combinación de adversidades afecta finalmente al reinado del dólar como moneda mundial, acelerando la tendencia a su reemplazo por otras divisas, en las transacciones corrientes entre potencias de peso 

(21)

. China, Rusia y los BRICS Plus afianzan ese giro en una dinámica de creciente desdolarización, que corroe el pilar de la dominación imperial norteamericana 

(22)

.




La IA es la única apuesta económica actual de la elite estadounidense para lidiar con tantas desventuras. Suponen que el liderazgo en esa tecnología permitirá contrarrestar la adversidades comerciales, financieras y productivas que afronta la potencia en declive. Pero no registran cómo el desarrollo de ese instrumento multiplica todos los desequilibrios. La IA no preserva el poder de Estados Unidos. Al contrario: socava por múltiples vías la continuidad de ese predominio.




Desesperación frente a China




La exasperación que provoca el vertiginoso avance de China en el terreno digital ilustra el desconcierto que reina entre las élites norteamericanas. Hasta hace muy poco tiempo consideraban que ese universo les pertenecía sin ningún rival a la vista. Pero la constante progresión de Beijing en las últimas décadas ha devenido en un proceso arrollador en los últimos años.




Xi Jinping al asumir un nuevo mandato el 18 de octubre de 2022.




El despunte comenzó con la creación de Alibaba -una empresa de comercio electrónico que desafió a las plataformas occidentales -y con el afianzamiento de Baidu, “el Google chino” que ya opera como segundo motor de búsqueda del mundo. En 2018 emergió Tencent como una firma especializada en la industria del entretenimiento, que capturó la cima mundial en el campo de los videojuegos. Posteriormente se consolidó WeChat (la análoga a WhatsApp) como la red social más popular y utilizada por el impresionante número de ciudadanos chinos.




Esos vertiginosos desenvolvimientos partieron de la transferencia de tecnología que impuso el coloso asiático a los inversores estadounidenses de emprendimientos digitales. Esas firmas aceptaron la exigencia china en su incontenible búsqueda de ganancias, permitiendo la copia inicial de sus mercancías. Posteriormente no pudieron contener la mejora y remodelación de sus productos por parte de las nacientes empresas orientales, que terminaron escalando hasta convertirse en imparables competidores. Consiguieron la delantera en esa carrera, primero con las nuevas comunicaciones por redes 5G y posteriormente con los dispositivos celulares Huawei. Ahora, las firmas chinas rivalizan en todos los campos del universo digital 

(23)

.




Ese salto de emparejar a disputar primacía ya no se limita a las grandes innovaciones como las tecnologías verdes de las turbinas eólicas, los paneles solares, los coches eléctricos y los trenes de alta velocidad, sino que involucra también las actividades del Big Data.




En todos los casos capturan las invenciones de su rival, transformándolas en innovaciones más eficientes, China ganó los titulares del planeta con el impactante logro de DeepSeek. Desarrolló una aplicación de Inteligencia Artificial que ofrece innumerables ventajas sobre el modelo rival del ChatGPT de OpenAI.




DeepSeek introdujo un buscador interactivo que realiza las mismas acciones de su competidor a un costo significativamente inferior. Desenvuelve el mismo entrenamiento, con una erogación equivalente al 10 % de lo invertido por su contendiente. Esa diferencia se traduce en una brecha semejante en el cobro del servicio. Lo que ChatGPT ofrece por 15 dólares, DeepSeek lo comercializa a tan sólo 0,14 dólares.







Además, el modelo chino funciona con procedimientos de código abierto, que permiten a cualquier persona examinarlo, modificarlo y adaptarlo a sus necesidades, en contraposición al restrictivo esquema del antagonista norteamericano. Por esa sustancial diferencia la aplicación china desató de inmediato un furor de descargas.




Esta misma receta se extendió ahora al Kimi K3 de la empresa Moonshot AI, que superó en desempeño a Claude Fable 5 de Anthropic y al GPT 5.6 Sol de OpenAI. Ese modelo es 112 veces más barato por cada millón de tokens (un barril de inteligencia).




Un token cuesta 56 dólares con Anthropic, 26 dólares con OpenAI, 1,50 dólares con Meta, 1 dólar con xAI y Google, y 0,50 dólares con los modelos chinos. Esta nueva cachetada provocó un cisma en la plutocracia de IA, puesto que muchas voces reconocen que el camino de desenvolvimiento elegido por Estados Unidos es muy costoso y poco redituable 

(24)

.




Varios gobernantes norteamericanos intentaron contener con sanciones el avance de su rival, prohibiendo por ejemplo la exportación a China de los procesadores más avanzados. Pero provocaron un efecto contrario al buscado, al incentivar la investigación y fabricación local de esos insumos y su posterior venta a precios sustancialmente más bajos.




DeepSeek afrontó, por ejemplo, las restricciones impuestas por Washington utilizando otro tipo de semiconductores y terminó elaborando un producto exitoso. Ese mismo boomerang se verificó con Huawei, que se ha consagrado en el ámbito mundial del 5G, luego de neutralizar las infructuosas puniciones que motorizó Estados Unidos para asfixiar su compañía. Los castigos afectaron más al agresor que al agredido.







Otro ejemplo en la misma secuencia se verifica en la fabricación de los circuitos integrados más avanzados, donde la empresa SAETG empieza a competir con Nvidia, acortando la brecha tecnológica en un terreno donde China afrontaba gran retraso y dependencia externa.




Con ese avance, mejora su posicionamiento en las tres instancias de la cadena de valor de la IA: los insumos para los microprocesadores (tierras raras, minerales críticos), el entrenamiento de las plataformas y el emplazamiento de los Centros de Datos 

(25)

. Hasta ahora, Estados Unidos conserva ventajas en la frontera tecnológica y en el cómputo, mientras China reduce esas distancias y logra un mejor posicionamiento en eficiencia, integración industrial y escala.




En la disputa por quién llegará primero (que podría denominarse la “carrera Sputnik”), Estados Unidos conserva ventajas importantes en segmentos decisivos. Pero en el propósito de integrar esa tecnología a la economía real (“momento Shenzhen”), la supremacía china salta a la vista 

(26)

.




Además, para algunas empresas estadounidenses (como Nvidia), China sigue siendo un enorme mercado potencial que intenta conservar, evitando que ambos países desenvuelvan trayectorias tecnológicas totalmente contrapuesta 

(27)

.




Pero la confrontación se ha desatado y China reafirma en el campo digital, la mayor productividad y competitividad que exhibe en todos los terrenos de la actividad económica. La confirmación más impactante de esa ventaja, es el creciente uso por parte de las propias empresas norteamericanas de los instrumentos digitales elaborados por compañías orientales. El establishment de Washington afronta con estupefacción esa adversidad, sin encontrar algún camino para revertirla.




La expectativa en un próximo y largo estancamiento de China -semejante al que afecta a Japón- no se ha corroborado. El gigante asiático mantiene una gran distancia con las economías que languidecen por envejecimiento de la población, desempleo estructural o transición demográfica. Tampoco padece el agotamiento de los ingresos medios, el declive de la productividad o la primacía del despilfarro financiero.




Esa variedad de infortunios -presagiada por la crema de los economistas convencionales- no se ha verificado en el competidor asiático. El motor estatal del crecimiento continúa operando, se multiplican los resultados de las inversiones que orientan la economía y se afianza el resguardo de las reservas acumuladas para lidiar con los contratiempos.




El fracaso del intento trumpista de socavar la locomotora asiática con aranceles se verifica en la continuada expansión de la Ruta de la Seda. China ya concertó convenios con 148 países y acuerdos bilaterales con 102 contrapartes. Es el mayor socio comercial de 120 naciones países y comanda la gestación de un bloque económico alternativo en torno a los BRICS.




En el terreno digital es particularmente evidente el contraste, entre el estrecho horizonte de ganancias de corto plazo que guía a la oligarquía tecnológica estadounidense, y la apuesta de largo plazo de su contraparte china. La plutocracia que rodea a Trump hace valer sus exigencias al Estado, con el mismo despliegue poder que en otra época exhibía la industria pesada o los bancos. Conforma un lobby que se sumó al líder Republicano, luego de archivar sus tradicionales preferencias por el globalismo de los Demócratas. Moldea a su servicio todas las medidas que dicta el Congreso, concreta el Ejecutivo y convalidan los jueces.




Por el contrario, los barones del sector tecnológico privado de China (Alibaba, Tencent, Ant Group, Didi), siguen los lineamientos que impone la conducción del Partido Comunista, con la misma disciplina que anteriormente Huawei o SMIC aceptaron las normas de esa dirigencia. La arquitectura regulatoria para la IA generativa que China estableció en el 2023, le permite regular determinados aspectos y acelerar otras aristas del mismo campo, en función de una estrategia que acota y subordina la gravitación de la rentabilidad inmediata 

(28)

.




La diferencia sustancial entre ambas potencias no se ubica en la personalidad de Trump y Xi Jinping o en el perfil de los dos países, sino en la estructura social y el manejo del Estado.




En China hay importantes clases capitalistas que especulan con sus fortunas y explotan a los trabajadores. Pero esos grupos no controlan el poder estatal y ese límite explica la capacidad y autonomía que detenta la dirigencia política, para orientar la economía. Trump carece de fórmulas para lidiar con esa desventaja que desborda todas sus intenciones y proyectos. Esta adversidad acentúa los desequilibrios de todo el modelo de capitalismo digital que analizaremos en el próximo texto.

author: Omar Hassan
title: Ben Carroll’s ‘new direction’ for Victoria is towards the big end of town
content:
In his first statement released following the ousting of Jacinta Allan, Victorian Premier Ben Carroll promised “a new direction” for Victoria. So far, it’s been the longitudinal equivalent of prostrating yourself at the feet of the bosses and hoping for a better ride in the media. And it doesn’t feel that new.

Granted, Carroll came to office more determined than Allan to concede to each and every one of the right-wing attacks on the Labor government. He has distanced himself from the Big Build, and immediately announced a royal commission into the CFMEU, the key demand of the bosses and right wing who see an opportunity to strike a blow against unionism.

Carroll has also announced a softening of the land tax changes introduced by former premier Daniel Andrews, one of the few progressive taxation policies introduced in recent years. This is a signal to business and the wealthy that a Carroll government will not be expecting them to make sacrifices to reduce the state’s debt. 

But on many other issues, Carroll is more of the same. Crime is an example. The capitalist media’s constant focus on incidents of anti-social behaviour has created the impression that Victorians are living in an era of unprecedented violence and crime. Yet the crime rate is 

roughly the same

 as it was a decade ago, according to data drawn from the Victorian Crime Statistics Agency. 

Nevertheless, Caroll has announced a “zero tolerance” approach to crime, involving “less bail, more jail”. Not satisfied with their draconian “adult time for adult crime” laws introduced by Allan which target children as young as 13, Labor has promised a review aimed at legislating harsher sentences for young offenders. His government has also committed $150 million in new funding for expanded police and PSO numbers. The latter are being empowered to patrol in wider areas, including shopping malls.

Police are also being given the right to frisk people for knives anywhere at any time, despite a 2022 Griffith University review into a similar law in Queensland finding that there was “

no evidence

” that it deterred knife carrying or led to a reduction in violent offending. What the policy will definitely achieve is to expand the systematic harassment of youths from poor and migrant backgrounds.

To the extent there are real issues with anti-social behaviour and crime, much of it is driven by poverty, the housing crisis and lack of social services. According to the Council for Homeless Persons (CHP), the homeless population rose by 24 percent in the five years to 2021, the last census for which data is available. The perpetrators of this invisible crime are the developers and the banks, but most of all the Labor government, which is responsible for Victoria having the lowest proportion of public and community housing in Australia. The CHP also reported that the Victorian government slashed spending on social housing by 9 percent in the 2024–25 budget, despite having the largest number of people seeking emergency housing support. 

The Labor government is also demolishing every public housing tower in the city to make way for private development on lucrative inner-city land. The residents of these buildings have largely been dispersed to the outer suburbs, where housing is cheaper and services are woefully inadequate. 

In a similar vein, the government has failed to address the ballooning numbers of people seeking support in dealing with drug and alcohol problems. In May, the Victorian Alcohol and Drug Association reported there were 5,122 Victorians on daily waitlists for drug treatment services, a 115 percent increase since the pandemic. These are people who are actively seeking support, but 40 percent had not even been assessed. 

Insofar as there is youth crime, it can’t be separated from the conditions of life for many young people, and in particular the condition of schools. Too many, especially those in poor areas, are not adequately resourced, particularly when it comes to assisting students with special needs. It is a disgrace that we still lack full-time professional social workers and counsellors in every public school, and that it is incredibly difficult to get funding for support staff in classrooms without a disability diagnosis. The government prefers to lock kids up rather than support them to get an education.

Faced with these issues, the obvious answer is to increase funding to assist people in acute situations to find shelter, health care, job and educational opportunities and financial assistance. 

There are a handful of measures that aim to sweeten the otherwise bitter pill. The establishment of ten public, walk-in dental clinics across the state is one. The proposal to cap fees for toll roads and public transport fees to $30 a day is another. While superficially attractive, this is essentially a $300 million a year taxpayer subsidy to Metro and the toll companies—socialists call for both to be renationalised without compensation. Labor has also promised to provide free abortion care on demand, a relatively cheap and very overdue measure, likely to cost just $7.5 million a year. None of this will fundamentally address cost-of-living issues for working-class people. 

Wage rises, which 

would

 make a significant difference to the standard of living of hundreds of thousands of Victorians, are not on offer from this government. Teachers, health workers and doctors have been denied their pay demands by the Carroll government, and it has maintained the 3 percent wage cap for public sector workers, which is well below the rate of inflation. 

Overall, Labor’s response to the surge in support for One Nation and growing support for the Liberals has been to attempt to curry favour with the bosses while throwing some crumbs at its base. The capitalist establishment is far from convinced, and is clearly all-in on a Liberal victory come November. Yet the effect of Carroll’s approach means that whoever wins, Victorian workers face an extended period of reactionary law and order policies, declining living standards and reduced investment into public services.

author: Editors
title: Turmoil in world politics: we have to rise to the challenges
content:
“It was the best of times, it was the worst of times ... it was the spring of hope, it was the winter of despair.” The famous opening words of Charles Dickens novel, 

A Tale of Two Cities,

 set in the Great French Revolution could equally apply to France and much of Europe today.

The best of times and spring of hope—the vibrant, months-long school student mobilisations and blockades that have drawn hundreds of thousands of French workers and university students onto the streets in solidarity. All in the face of savage police violence unleashed by President Emmanuel Macron’s government of the supposed moderate liberal centre.

Eventually, after weeks of foot-dragging, trade union leaders called a general strike for 5 November—a vital step forward and test for the rebellion.

It is not just France. A wave of protest inspired by the French students has swept Europe from Belgium to Portugal to Italy, where students and workers have long endured similar attacks on living standards and democratic rights, the rise of militarism and threatening fascist forces.

Spain has also been gripped by revolt over the cost of living and housing crisis sparked by the eviction of 87-year-old woman Maricarmen Abascal. The general strike called for 11 November is set to be the largest in Spain in the 50 years since the fall of General Franco’s fascist government.

But it’s also the worst of times—reflected in the scale of support for far-right forces internationally.

The majority of the French population sympathises with the protestors’ grievances over the cost-of-living, cuts to public services and education funding. Yet polls indicate Marine Le Pen of the fascist National Rally is set to decisively win April’s presidential elections. Le Pen leads the left’s Jean-Luc Melenchon 69 percent to 31 percent. 

Large sections of the capitalist class and its middle-class supporters are rallying behind National Rally as the “party of order” to crush resistance not just from unruly students but organised workers and impose harsh austerity measures to boost profits.

Similarly in Spain, the right-wing People’s Party backed by the fascist Vox seems set to defeat the discredited centre-left government in the 29 November elections on a program of wage cuts, mass public sector sackings and attacks on democratic rights.

Then there is Brazil. An inspiring wave of protests led by young people transformed the course of the elections ensuring the defeat of the far right’s Flavio Bolsonaro. Yet the increasingly violent far right shows no sign of being curbed. Ruling in the interests of Brazil’s capitalist class, Lula da Silva’s Workers Party disillusioned swathes of workers and the poor preparing the ground for the far right. And a re-elected Lula is not about to change course and mobilise workers in mass strike action to challenge the rich and powerful.

Politics worldwide has become much more polarised, the product of decades of neo-liberal attacks on workers’ living standards and increasingly authoritarian rule undermining the hold of parties of the centre-left and centre-right. The pattern is uneven, but in many countries it is the far right that so far has been the main beneficiary of the growing discontent.

From Spain to France to Germany to Australia, the traditional reformist parties have utterly failed to defend workers’ interests and ward off the far-right threat. It is vital that the militant socialist left and the broader working-class movement is rebuilt to meet these challenges. And there are important opportunities to do just that.

There is a much greater opening for Marxist, working-class politics than in previous waves of protests over the last few decades. In Spain, for example, the 2011 movement of the squares provoked by the 2008 Global Financial Crisis was posed as a citizens’ movement that was neither left nor right. There was pronounced hostility to the involvement of socialist organisations and trade unions.

This time around, the movement is much more posed as a movement of the left centred on working-class demands with the involvement of revolutionary organisations welcomed. Mass strike action by workers is rightly seen as vital for the movement going forward.

In France, it was students from the poorest working-class suburbs that initiated the rebellion and the party most associated with the rebellion is Melenchon’s left-wing La France Insoumise (LFI). 

But half-way house left reformist operations like Melenchon’s LFI or the Left Party in Germany, which do not want to overthrow capitalism, are not up to the tasks that the situation demands. The LFI to its credit defends the student protests but does not intervene as an organised force in the movement to take it forwards, nor does it galvanise its hundreds of thousands of supporters to agitate in the unions for strikes that go beyond a simple one-day affair.

Australia has lagged behind developments in Europe. But here too we see increasing discontent with the mainstream parties and the rapid rise in support for Pauline Hanson’s One Nation. In Victoria, we are set to see the election of a hard right Liberal government, backed by One Nation, out to implement a raft of austerity measures attacking workers.

Our side needs to rise to the challenge. This serious situation demands both concerted mass resistance and the building of a revolutionary socialist movement that is determined to take the struggle against capitalism all the way.

author: Alma Torlakovic
title: Western Sydney residents in revolt after being kept in the dark over data centre
content:
In their rush to appease big tech billionaires and open up Australia as a destination for hyperscale data centres, Labor governments at all levels have demonstrated how little respect they have for the people living in their so-called “safe seats”. This is most obvious in the diverse communities of Western Sydney, where the state government has rushed to approve a dozen of these polluting, energy-intensive monstrosities.

Labor has relied on the same blueprint for each recent approval: declare the data centre as a “state significant development”, don’t let the residents know and hope that nobody checks the website for the development proposals. They have gone as far as overselling the projects on behalf of the companies, claiming that they will create jobs for the community, downplaying the hazards involved or regurgitating the idea that these are not much different from a storage warehouse.

This strategy has backfired in Guildford in Sydney’s western suburbs, where a community campaign is brewing over the state government’s approval of a $1.1 billion hyperscale data centre right next to a sports field and homes. Residents are outraged that they've been left in the dark about the 7.2-hectare data centre that will cause 24/7 noise, raise energy bills, emit carcinogenic fumes, lower people's house prices and have a huge impact on water usage and carbon emissions. We are determined to stop it, as other communities have.

An information session organised by Cumberland City Council on 24 October to address the growing community backlash to the project turned into an angry row as 100 local residents turned on council officials, the mayor and local Labor MP, Julia Finn. Residents accused them of leaving them in the dark about the project, with most only learning of the 68-megawatt data centre plans in their neighbourhood during the past fortnight. Finn, who claimed that letters had been sent to residents, was booed down by angry constituents who said that no such thing had happened.

Robyn Hann, who is spearheading the action group to stop the data centre build, said:

“We went to the [council] information session hoping to learn more and have our concerns addressed regarding health, water, pollution, 24/7 noise, house prices and other issues. Instead, we got smoke and mirrors … I felt we were completely ignored.”

One woman summed it up, telling the meeting that she had lived in the area and worked hard for 30 years to pay off her home and build a life, only to be blindsided by this project.

Western Sydney residents are sick and tired of being taken for granted by the Labour Party and being the dumping ground for polluting industries. I have published a 

petition

 to demand that the Cumberland City Council and the NSW government put an immediate stop to this project. It has already gathered over 4,000 signatures. 

Goodman Group, the company behind the proposed data centre, recently had to withdraw plans to build a data centre in Lane Cove following community opposition. Gregory Goodman, CEO of Goodman Group, has added a $20 million penthouse in Double Bay to his suite of multi-million-dollar mansions in upmarket Woollahra. He’s certainly not building a data centre next to any of his luxury properties.

Since the initial council information session, community pressure has forced the council to adopt a more moderate stance. It says that it will explore legal avenues to challenge the development. At federal level, sensing widespread hostility to mega data centres, the Albanese government has announced plans to ban them in residential areas in city suburbs. But these regulations will not apply to existing approvals. 

And we cannot leave things in the hands of the politicians and bureaucrats because the law is stacked in favour of big business. We must continue to pressure the state government and local Labor member. 

A community forum on 26 October organised by independent councillor Ahmed Ouf to oppose the project drew 200 people at Guildford Leagues Club. A similar number showed up to the council meeting on 28 October to register their opposition to the proposal.

NSW Socialists have played a central role in this campaign. We have doorknocked thousands of homes in the area, gathering signatures for the petition, talking to local residents.

The NSW government and Julia Finn could intervene to stop this project if they wanted. But they’re more interested in appeasing tech billionaires. That’s just one more reason we plan to take this fight to the next state election and vote Finn out.

Alma Torlakovic

 is the NSW Socialists candidate for Western Sydney’s Granville in the upcoming 2027 state election.

author: Tom Sullivan
title: Mass protests defeat the far right in Brazil, but Lula is no way forward
content:
With the winds in Latin America blowing decisively towards the far right over recent years, voters went to the polls in the continent’s most important country, Brazil, in October. The Workers’ Party (PT), led by long-time leader and incumbent president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, lost in the first round, but achieved a remarkable turnaround in the second round.

Lula, as he is popularly known, was running against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, Lula’s predecessor. Jair is currently serving a 27-year sentence for an attempted coup after he lost the 2022 election. During his term he oversaw the deaths of over 700,000 people during the pandemic and is a close ally of President Trump. 

In the first round, Flavio Bolsonaro won 47 percent against Lula’s 45 percent. The right also took control of Congress.

The PT’s first-round loss shows how much support the PT has lost among its traditional base. The outgoing Lula administration was committed to a fiscal framework of zero budget deficits, resulting in caps on public spending and wages. It also allowed further oil exploration of the Amazon. During the campaign, Lula gave ground to the right's tough-on-crime platform, indicating his support for lowering the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16.

The PT’s poor performance in the first round makes its turnaround in the second round even more impressive. Over the three weeks, the PT’s vote increased by over ten million, giving the party 52 percent of the vote. Facing criminal allegations of money laundering, Bolsonaro fled to Miami.

The key factor in the sharp jump in the PT vote was the huge rallies that spread across the country between the two rounds of voting. The day after the first round, students at the Federal University in Rio de Janeiro held an assembly that turned into a rally, spilling out onto the streets. Social media and WhatsApp groups exploded with calls for demonstrations. On 7 October, the National Union of Students called demonstrations in several major cities that saw tens of thousands come out. 

These initial demonstrations were about mobilising to defeat the far right, defending public education, and fighting to reduce the work week to five days from six, a demand that Lula’s government has resisted. Although backing for the PT’s re-election was present, it received much less emphasis. One slogan was: “No to the father, no to the son.”

By 9 October, even small cities were holding assemblies and demonstrations. In Ponta Grossa, a city of around 350,000, university and high school students held an assembly of over a thousand people, promoted as “students against fascism”. It decided on an action plan that included leafleting and door knocking. Similar scenes played out at universities across the country.

“The first few days after the election were like a frenzy”, said Veronica O’Kelly, a national leader of the socialist group Revolucão Socialista. She continued,

“WhatsApp groups promoted rallies across the country. Students led demonstrations out of the universities into the streets. Their demands were immediately far beyond anything the PT was offering. This is what kicked off the mass demonstrations that came over the following weeks.” 

On the first weekend after the first round over one million joined marches in Sao Paolo and Rio de Janeiro under the slogan “The class is in the streets”. Lula was a prominent feature of the rallies, standing on top of a bus in Sao Paolo, surrounded by throngs of people. In other cities, hundreds of thousands joined marches. 

But students remained the driving force. On 14 October, the student union at the University of Brasilia held a demonstration of over 50,000 in the capital under the slogan “Bolsonaro never again and end the 6x1 now,” referring to the six-day work week.

The fact that the rallies raised major economic demands alongside support for the PT put pressure on Lula not just to offer promises after the second round but to take immediate action. On 14 October, Congress passed a constitutional amendment reducing the work week from six days to five with no loss of salary. This was a monumental victory for the Brazilian working class that the movement imposed on not just the PT but the entire ruling class. The measure passed the Senate 75 to 1, with even Bolsonaro’s party voting for it.

Another notable point of the election was several strong results for the left. Several far-left organisations inside the Party for Socialism and Liberation (PSOL), the main party to the left of the PT, formed the Radical Left Caucus, which included several prominent figures like Thiago Avila, a leader of the Sumud Flotilla for Gaza, and other current PSOL MPs. Their platform included a series of pro-working class economic reforms such as the nationalisation of public utilities. Six members of the Caucus, running as PSOL candidates, were elected or re-elected. The combined vote for Radical Left Caucus candidates exceeded two million, showing political space exists to the left of the PT if candidates embrace a more left-wing platform.

Brazil’s election shows that the far-right’s seemingly unstoppable rise to power can be halted. What stopped it was not the capitulatory reformism of leaders like Lula. It was the power of ordinary people, mobilising and organising in the streets, universities and workplaces.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Endangered Eastern Grass Owl Habitat Threatened by Shalun Science Park
content:
ENVIRONMENTALISTS HAVE warned of the potential displacement of the Eastern grass owl as a result of the construction of the Shalun Science Park.

The Eastern grass owl is a critically endangered species in Taiwan, with its habitat including Tainan, Chiayi, Kaohsiung, and Pingtung, and it is Taiwan’s only owl species that nests in grasslands. After much effort by environmentalists to rebuild its habitat on the Dadu Mountain Plateau, the Eastern grass owl was found to have returned to central Taiwan earlier this year. It is thought that the Eastern grass owl disappeared from central Taiwan in the 1960s.

Environmentalists voiced concerns about the owl’s habitat at the second-stage environmental impact review, whose scoping session concluded on October 12th. The planned development zones “Parking 1” and “Industrial 1-2” would threaten the habitat of the Eastern grass owl, in that the current area is considered top-tier nesting grounds for the owl. As such, developers were urged to create habitats for the Eastern grass owl before construction. The Kaohsiung Science Park has been cited as an example of where development has already displaced the Eastern grass owl.

Science parks consume vast amounts of water and electricity. Nevertheless, it is common for local politicians to call for their development, with the view that this brings tech jobs to local populations. Likewise, with Taiwan increasingly central to the AI boom, in terms of providing the world with its supply of necessary semiconductors, this has led to a demand for facilities to keep up the pace–including not only semiconductor fabs themselves, but the facilities they need to keep running, such as power supply. And yet, as seen with the Eastern grass owl, this threatens the local environment.

Indeed, this proves another way in which the AI boom is reshaping Taiwan. While environmental destruction is commonplace with AI development, mostly along the lines of data centers and manufacturing, this can also occur with land acquisition–sometimes infringing on labor rights.

The relocation of Kuai Kuai from its current Taoyuan factory to Hsinchu, which is too far for the existing workers to commute, is due to the land the factory sits on being sold to a semiconductor company. Kuai Kuai’s owners were accused by striking workers, then, of having potentially acquired the land in order to sell it to semiconductor manufacturers, given that it is lucrative real estate. It is possible that land grabs by the semiconductor industry will become increasingly common in Taiwan, something that poses a risk not only to labor but also to the environment. This is to be seen.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Rosario: familias del noroeste de la ciudad se movilizaron por obras para no volver a inundarse
content:
Vecinos y vecinas del barrio Empalme Graneros, ubicado en la zona noroeste de Rosario, se manifestaron para exigir al gobierno provincial que avance con las obras necesarias para evitar nuevas inundaciones. El barrio sufrió 17 inundaciones a lo largo de su historia y sus habitantes advierten que todavía esperan soluciones definitivas.










Escuchar/descargar el reporte de Aire Libre de Rosario




La inundación más trágica y recordada ocurrió en abril de 1986, cuando el barrio permaneció bajo el agua durante tres días y cerca de 80 mil vecinos y vecinas resultaron perjudicados.




En diálogo con Aire Libre, Osvaldo “Lalín” Ortolani, presidente de la vecinal Empalme y referente de la organización Nunca Más Inundaciones (NuMaIn), explicó que una de las obras principales es la construcción de un conducto pluvial, cuyos estudios están realizados desde hace 12 años. Además, señaló que el gobierno provincial cuenta desde hace una década con los estudios necesarios para construir cinco represas.




“Hay una obra que se tiene que hacer, hace 12 años que hay estudios, es un conducto y es lo más importante de todo. En el mientras tanto, este gobierno provincial desde hace 10 años tiene los estudios y todo hecho para hacer cinco represas”, afirmó.




Ante la falta de avances, los vecinos plantean que, si el gobierno provincial no puede realizar el conducto, comience al menos por la construcción de una represa.




“No queremos mantas y colchones, queremos soluciones”, remarcó Ortolani.




El referente barrial también advirtió sobre la responsabilidad de las autoridades provinciales ante la posibilidad de que se repita una inundación de la magnitud de la ocurrida hace 40 años.




“Esto es un mensaje para los que tienen el poder de decisión. Si hay una desgracia no va a ser El Niño, va a ser la negligencia, la ineptitud, la irresponsabilidad de los que pueden hacer cosas y no lo hacen”, sostuvo.




Ortolani cuestionó, además, las intervenciones que se están realizando en otros canales de la zona, al considerar que no resuelven el problema de Empalme Graneros. En ese sentido, denunció que las obras anunciadas no garantizan que el agua deje de afectar al barrio y reclamó que se prioricen las soluciones que necesitan sus habitantes.




Los vecinos y vecinas volverán a reunirse el próximo miércoles para continuar analizando la situación y sostener el reclamo por las obras de infraestructura que permitan prevenir nuevas inundaciones.







Fuente: 

https://agencia.farco.org.ar/2026/10/29/rosario-familias-del-noroeste-de-la-ciudad-se-movilizaron-por-obras-para-no-volver-a-inundarse/
