You may have heard of her: Aradia, daughter of Diana, the Roman moon goddess, and Lucifer, the personification of the morning star. Siblings in this particular tale, they create and birth Aradia with the sole purpose of sending her to earth to help liberate Italian peasants from the crushing weight of the ruling class. The lore says she was meant to teach witchcraft and sorcery to the disempowered resistance, so they could utilize the teachings to rise up and win the class war. To poison the powerful. To bind them and their oppressive deeds from causing further harm.

At least this is what Charles Godfrey Leland relayed in his slim, influential 1899 book, Aradia: Or The Gospel of the Witches.

“And thou shalt be the first witches known;

And thou shalt be the first of all i’ the world:

And thou shalt teach the art of poisoning;

Of poisoning those who are the great lords of all;

Yea, thou shalt make them die in their palaces;

And thou shalt bind the oppressor’s soul (with power)”

The book itself includes invocations, spells, tales of Aradia’s origins, and claims of a secret witch society who had a long, unbroken lineage of practicing folk magic and pre-Christian spiritual and healing traditions throughout Italy. In the book, followers of Aradia are instructed to gather in groups and have monthly naked meetings in forests during the full moon in honor of Diana until “…the last of your oppressors shall be dead.”

“If I were just to look at the book itself without the modern view, I would say Aradia is an initiator, she is someone who elevates people who are really not just disenfranchised, but slaves; enslaved in their souls, enslaved in their bodies,” says Dr. A.D. Manns, cultural historian and author of Aradia's Hidden Hand: The Untold Life of Roma Lister (Hexen Press, 2025). “And through her intervention, she's bringing these subjugated peoples to another level, allowing them to gain a certain degree of mastery.”

It is thrilling to consider; not a savior coming to rescue everyone, but rather a divine ally of sorts arriving with the power of organizing with the people and providing them with more tools to fight.

Poison those in power. Cast spells. Achieve collective freedom.

A woman named Maddalena (sometimes known as Margherita or Maddalena Talenti) was Leland’s paid informant who collected, and provided Leland with, information detailing Aradia’s origin story as the symbol of resistance and uprising she is portrayed as in Aradia. Maddalena herself claimed she was a link in the unbroken lineage Leland described in the book, a Tuscan and Etruscan witch, a role she said was passed down to her through generations.

Reception of the book has been complicated. It has been discussed, critiqued, praised, referenced, evaluated. It even influenced the modern witchcraft and neo-pagan revivals in the mid-1900’s. Wicca has roots in Leland’s Aradia, too; Gerald Gardner was deeply inspired by the book and adopted much of what he read and wove it into spells and rituals for his Gardnerian Witchcraft teachings. Doreen Valiente’s Charge of the Goddess, which is an influential piece of Gardnerian Wicca’s Book of Shadows, was also heavily inspired by Aradia’s modern lore. And Stregheria, or Italian American witchcraft, which was popularized by Raven Grimassi’s work, can also follow its threads back to Aradia. Tales of everyday people being taught to fight back against oppression is a strong and enduring theme that has led these spiritual traditions to carry on, growing in popularity even more so in the rapidly tilting times we are in today.

Aradia book cover (Wikicommons image)

Born in Pennsylvania in 1824, Charles Godfrey Leland was somewhat of an armchair anthropologist and self-taught journalist, with a law degree and an education dabbling in languages and poetry. He fought in the French Revolution of 1848 and had a keen interest in the arts, founding and directing the Public School of Industrial Art in Philadelphia in 1880, an institution that taught crafts to the disadvantaged children of the city.

Aside from his eclectic education and an interesting assortment of career paths, Leland is probably known best today as a Folklorist; he traveled extensively and took a special interest in the Roma of Europe, Native Americans, Irish Travelers, and other marginalized and oppressed people, writing books and magazine articles about them; some of Leland’s perspectives and writings are fairly problematic, with stereotyped perspectives on the cultures he studied, especially in regard to the Roma. It can be assumed that some of this seeped through in Aradia.

He attributed his varied interests in everything from the occult to the arts and law—and as a Union soldier who fought at the Battle of Gettysburg—to an incident he claimed happened while still a newborn. In her biography of Leland, his niece Elizabeth Robins Pennell writes that Leland often shared a story of his Dutch nurse performing a ritual on him in the family’s attic, which included candles, a bible, a key, a knife, salt and even some money to set him on his path to becoming “a scholar and a wizard.”

Again, because of his eclectic interests and experiences, it might have been difficult for Leland to be objective about his research, particularly in regards to Aradia and Italian witchcraft. How Leland acquired the information he used for Aradia: Or The Gospel of the Witches, was tricky, at best.

Dr. Sabina Magliocco is a professor emeritus of anthropology at UBC Vancouver and is a scholar of religion (including modern pagan religions) with expertise including folklore studies, witchcraft and magic. She’s conducted in depth research about the origins of Aradia’s lore and agrees that when it comes to Leland’s interests in marginalized people and their world view, he had a romantic perspective of the people and lore he wrote about.

“It's very likely that [Maddalena] Talenti knew this and that she shaped her legends and the material she gave him to suit what she thought that he would want to hear,” says Magliocco. “So where does that leave us? Certainly, in the book Aradia, there's a lot of stuff that is probably elaborated or invented. However, there's a good chance that a figure called Aradia existed in Italian folklore.”

One point that is important to consider in Maddalena’s information gathering and sharing, though, is the context of what was happening in Italy during the time she provided it to Leland.

19th Century Italian Peasant Broom Vendor (Library of Congress public domain)

The Italian peninsula was on shaky, tumultuous grounds in the 1800’s.

Though a considerable win for the ruling class, the Risorgimento—the unification of Italy in 1861—was a failure for millions of laborers and other impoverished people, and did not deliver the promise of stability. Instead, it carved out a deepening divide between the poor and the ruling class. As Antonio Gramsci wrote in his Prison Notebooks, it was a “passive revolution that wasn’t a revolution at all.” It ignored the needs or input of the working people and pushed Italy toward a tipping point, exasperating the already dire circumstances for millions of people. Many argue that this failed revolution paved the way and opened the door for fascism to barge into the country decades later.

Instead, the Risorgimento brought with it the expansion of the wealthy class purchasing and privatizing large swaths of land, rapidly swallowing up communal agricultural spaces that many relied on to feed their families. A loss of roughly two million hectares (five million acres) of forest accompanied the vanishing of the beni comuni (common lands), with private landowners quickly clearcutting trees to plant crops. Peasant farmers became sharecroppers, with their labor exploited on now-private property, and the rapid deforestation contributed to erosion that, in turn, resulted in poor crops for at least two years in the early 1870’s. Poor crop yields on leased land meant debt owed to landowners by peasant sharecroppers, sometimes for years. And to add to the misery, waves of disease swept through Italy over and over again.

Malaria created one health crisis in the mid 1800’s, with 15-20 thousand people dying per year. Next came numerous cholera outbreaks, which killed roughly 113,000-15,000 people in the 1860’s and another 50,000 in 1880.

The ruling class—including doctors and members of the clergy—believed that because the poor were the most impacted by the disease, they were responsible for spreading it. As such, they needed to extinguish all peasant revolts and sent the military to poor rural and urban communities to enforce order, sometimes violently. The troops brought cholera along with them. And the strict military actions of enforcing fumigation and other forms of intense disease-fighting tactics led to anger and more uprisings in poverty-stricken Italy. This oppression created further animosity and distrust toward the wealthy and religious classes.

The first major wave of cholera was also accompanied by a grain tax in 1868, by the Italian minister of finance, Quintino Sella, who was subsequently labeled "starver of the people."

The Grist Tax, which was catastrophic for the peasantry, was meant to remedy the severe deficit the country was facing because of excessive military spending, both in battling various entities in the fight for unification, and by oppressing peasant uprisings. Because the main food staple of the poor was bread—and they were already suffering from devastating epidemics—this struck another detrimental blow to the people, creating increased agitation to fuel the anger growing across the peninsula.

As many struggled to survive under these brutal circumstances, seeds of revolution also spread through the new nation. The movement of the Sovversivo (the subversives working to overthrow authority) spread from the peasants in the countryside to the poverty stricken in the cities and back again, winding its way down every alley and field of crops. The perseverance and inspiration of these revolutionaries is carried on in international class struggles today.

Depiction of Silcilian repression by Neapolitan government 1848 (Creative Commons)

In the south, braccianti (day laborers) began fighting back by keeping some of the harvested crops for their families and using other, more passive “weapons of the weak” to resist. Some destroyed land deeds and otherwise sabotaged landlords around the country.

In the north, whispers of resistance were heard from women working long, backbreaking hours in the rice fields. This is where many claim the first versions of Bella Ciao were sung as the women lamented their ruthless working conditions and rebelled—through song—against greedy landowners.

While the Risorgimento was still in early stages of development, Propaganda of the Deed was first outlined in 1857 by Italian Socialist Carlo Pisacane (shortly before leading a raid to free prisoners in Ponza, and his subsequent death in June of that year). The 1870’s saw a surge in anarchist thought throughout Southern Europe, and in Italy in particular. The infamous revolutionary framework of Propaganda of the Deed, which advocates direct action against the ruling class establishment, became inspiration for anarchists fighting against the bourgeoisie during the years surrounding the Risorgimento; the framework was even endorsed at the 1881 International Anarchist Congress in London. The hope was that if the people could take bold revolutionary direct actions against the oppressor class, the rest of the exploited population would follow suit, leading to collective liberation. As Pisacane once famously said, "ideas spring from deeds and not the other way around; the people will not be free until they are educated, but they will be well educated once free."

While working in dire situations and dealing with extreme hunger, peasants continued to revolt. And although they were continuously met with violent oppression, they continued to rise up.

There is more, and I could go on, but life was brutal, and the ruling class continuously dealt blows against the masses, keeping their boots and bibles pressed down on the necks of the people. It was in the trenches of this social and political upheaval, a time when people were likely desperate for a figure like Aradia to offer some empowered hope and encouraged resistance, that the her story made its way into Charles Godfrey Leland’s hands.

“The people with power, they don't need magic. They have capital and they can exploit people with that capital,” says Magliocco. “The people who need magic are the people who don't have access to any means for making their vision of what they want to come true. The only thing they have is appealing to supernatural powers or trying to use those supernatural powers themselves to get something.”

19th century drawing of a Cimaruta amulet used in Italy against the evil eye (Wikicommons)

Italy was once rich with folk magic (much of which carries on in one form of another today). The folk magic practitioners—the herbal healers, makers of modest protection charms and rituals for humans and livestock alike, detectors of the Malocchio, or evil eye—were mostly peasants and used their folk healing practices to improve conditions in everyday life.

The witch hunts in Italy during the 16th and 17th centuries—though not nearly as deadly as neighboring countries of Germany where up to 30,000 were killed over several centuries (Italy, by comparison saw between 400-2,500 deaths), led much of these folk practices to be extinguished or widely adapted and merged with the church through the use of Catholic saints after the earlier witch hunts in Italy.

The last witch hunts ended a century before the height of the fairly popular spiritualist movement, which, unlike Italian folk magic, centered seances, mediumship or communicating with the dead, spirit table-tipping and spirit photos, and mostly appealed to the more privileged middle and upper classes. The table-tippers in the Spiritualist movement lived comfortable lives and were safe in practicing this form of magic.

"The History of Witches and Wizards" (creative Commons)

Among the spiritualists in Italy, was an English-born woman named Roma Lister, who in some ways maneuvered the thin veil between the world of peasant folk magic and the showy world of entertainment Spiritualism. She may have also contributed to Aradia’s story alongside Maddalena.

Leland met Lister around 1892, and the two remained close friends until his death in 1903. He was drawn to her intellect and to her charismatic personality, and to her connection to the spiritualist and folklore community in Italy.

Manns says that a memoir written by Countess Walburga Paget, an English-German aristocrat in Florence who often hosted artists, politicians, and occultists at her home, recounts spending time with Lister in Florence. She recounted that Lister would bring her tarot cards and crystal balls and share stories of witchcraft. Manns also points out that Lister had experience summoning spirits and had a spiritualist and theosophical perspective on things, and wrote about witchcraft and Italian folklore in her own memoirs.

Beyond her prominence and experience in the spiritualist community, Roma Lister was a friend of—or at least well acquainted with—Maddalena.

“She definitely knew Maddalena. And according to Leland, Maddalena taught Roma Lister different magical things; not just card reading, but also, as he calls it, different forms of the black art,” says Manns. “And there’s a moment where Leland is with Maddalena, and Maddalena is doing a ceremony, and she's demonstrating a ritual, and he says that Roma Lister's there taking notes.”

Maddalena of Florence (public domain image)

If we think outside of the box, it isn’t out of the question to assume that Lister had assisted Maddalena in formulating the Aradia information presented to Leland. It’s also worth considering–again, maybe further outside of the box– that Roma Lister may have drawn on her experience as a spiritualist and channeled Aradia’s story. Or in the very least, as suggested by Manns, that there was some magic at play during the creation of the book.

“Even if you remove the idea of evocation, the fact that maybe she summoned parts of it,” says Manns. “You could still say that there's an interesting relationship in the way in which material is being transferred to Leland, who's basically the editor; he is being influenced by the two of them and the things that they're doing and what they're describing.”

Again, Leland was fascinated by witchcraft and very likely had a vision of what it looked like, especially given the wildly imaginative ideas that people had of witches in the centuries leading up to Leland’s time in Italy. And Maddalena, Roma Lister, and perhaps others he had met at the time fit the profile, which he mentions vaguely, and in passing, in his introduction to Aradia, fed him what he longed for.

“If you imagine the philosophers, the alchemists of the Middle Ages, they had an idea of what the philosopher stone should look like,” says Manns. “And in a way it's like Leland has this idea of what witchcraft should look like, and then that's what ends up surfacing in Aradia.”

Still, there is evidence that a figure like Aradia existed at some point in Italian folklore. Maybe just not the exact version we leftist witches have adopted as our own.

“We're not really talking here about historical fact. We're talking about a sacred narrative. So it's a little bit like saying, ‘Is there any evidence that Zeus exists?’ Well, that's kind of not the point,” says Magliocco. “Aradia is a real figure, but this idea that she's the daughter of Diana and Lucifer and that she came to earth to teach political resistance to Italian peasants, this is pretty much developed by Leland or by Leland's interlocutor.”

Magliocco spent time collecting legends in Sardinia in the 1980’s. During her research, she heard tales of a figure called s'Araja (s'Araja means the Araja, and Araja is a version of the Italian word Aradia). In Sardinian folklore, there are two versions of s’Araja.

“s'Araja justa generally rewards good behavior or gender appropriate behavior on the part of young women who had spun and woven enough for their dowry, “says Magliocco. “s'Araja dimoniu leads a raid of spirits of the dead that ride through the sky at night and they make a lot of noise and they can, in some cases, indicate who will die within the year.”

Magliocco says that at some point these figures were introduced into Sardinia, most likely during the period of Pisan and Genoese occupation in the 12th and 13th century. This, according to Magliocco, means that in Italy in the 12th and 13th century, there was a figure called Aradia. She points to versions of the name Aradia associated with central and northern Italian versions of La Befana, “the good Italian witch who visits children on the eve of the epiphany, and again, rewards good little children with sweets and candy and punishes naughty children by leaving them coal.”

Illustration of La Befana (public domain image)

“This is part of a whole body of folklore about supernatural women who fly through the sky, who have some kind of sense of justice, and that existed in Italy, certainly from the high Middle Ages,” she says. “And sometimes they lead a raid of spirits of the dead.”

These legends match an early medieval legend about Herodias, a biblical figure and earlier version of the Aradia we know today: Herodias was the mother of Salome, who had demanded the head of John the Baptist, and whose punishment for his death was to dance through the air eternally without rest. Salome and Herodias eventually merge into one figure over time, possibly, as Magliocco says, because it was Roman custom for the women in one family to be known by the name of that particular family.

“Now we've got this wicked figure who is punished by wandering through the air and she begins to merge with other legends because this is what legendary material does” says Magliocco. “If you work with any contemporary legend material like aliens or Bigfoot or any of that stuff, these stories start to mush into one another.”

Herodias and Salome with the Head of John The Baptist (public domain image)

Aradia continues changing and growing today, and the hunger for her—or at least the archetype of her—seems to be spreading, as well. She validates the peasants’ recognition that the systems they were told were unchangeable and that insisted their oppressive circumstances were fated, were lies. Aradia offering the people the power to unshackle themselves from the harms of the ruling class was a gift.

Destroy the system in which the overlords wield absolute control. Bring them to their knees right in their own homes.

“If we go back to the art of poisoning, these secret acts to exert your power in even the darkest of situations, the fact that you can be literally a slave or in a horrible situation, and there's a sliver of hope, and then you are extricating yourself from that situation,” says Manns. “I think that's really compelling.”

We may never know for certain the exact origin of the modern telling of Aradia as an answer to peasant disempowerment. The written manuscript Leland claimed to receive from Maddalena, Il Vangelo delle Streghe, disappeared shortly before Aradia was published. And does it really matter? Do we need evidence of her legitimacy? Folktales can and do indeed morph and evolve over time to reflect social conditions, to integrate the narrative with the circumstance of the time. We don’t always settle with one political or world view, we don’t all stay with the same career throughout our lives. The needs of our communities are fluid, and we often have to step back, readjust, and reprioritize our roles to fit those needs. If we can change and grow and adapt to the changes in the world, can’t our deities do the same?

As my friend Phoenix LeFae points out in a piece she wrote for The New Aradia: A Witch’s Handbook to Magical Resistance anthology, “The more we call on Aradia, the stronger she gets—for what you feed with words and deeds grows. We cannot know the details of her origins, yet we can see what she has become and what she is becoming: a Goddess of witchcraft, power, and resistance.”

Words are indeed powerful. Deeds even moreso.

“We are once again in a period in which there are huge wealth disparities. And not unlike the peasants that Leland wrote about, we have a system in which wealth has been concentrated in the hands of very few billionaires,” says Magliocco. “Everyday people, even middle-class people who maybe grew up to expect a different kind of way of living, are struggling. Folks are struggling to pay for food, for housing. Aradia becomes a symbol of everything that leftist witches want to achieve. In other words, we want to achieve a more just world through magic.”

Salvator Rosa, "Witches Sabbath." (Wikicommons image)

What inspiration can we find from Aradia while fighting back against our modern ruling class, those who have shown us time and time again that they are certainly not—not now or ever—coming to save us? Who have, in fact, created the very conditions we live under today? We give them power with our votes, we give them power with our passivity.

Witches and others in the margins have provided care and protection outside of the system as long as societies have existed; midwives and healers and weavers and ritualists and community organizers and other sovversiva had (and still have) immense power. We can continue working or infiltrating in the shadows, poisoning the overlords (metaphorically?), creating class solidarity, sharing knowledge and skills and building a true resistance, remembering that all we have is each other and we need to start acting like it.

Manns points to resistance fighters against Nazis in France, the subversion of using underhanded subterfuge within corporations—whatever we do, the key is to organize ourselves outside of the religious and political tyranny.

“Aradia says: you can wield this sorcery. I'm giving you the knowledge, but you're not sitting there like you can't do anything by yourself and somebody's pulling you up into the heavens,” says Manns. “Aradia is the initiator, she is showing you these secrets, and then you take that and act accordingly.”

"Ye who are poor suffer with hunger keen,

And toil in wretchedness, and suffer too

Full oft imprisonment; yet with it all

Ye have a soul, and for your sufferings

Ye shall be happy in the other world,

But ill the fate of all who do ye wrong!"

Ill the fate of all who do ye wrong. So mote it be.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Kapatid seeks probe of jail reservation commercialization
content:
New Bilibid Prison. Screengrab from Google Earth

“We mean protecting 366.7 hectares of public land so it can be transformed into a modern, humanized center for custody, legal aid, and reformation.”

Political prisoners’ support group Kapatid urged Congress to investigate plans to commercialize the New Bilibid Prison (NBP) reservation in Muntinlupa City, warning that the proposed closure of the facility could displace not only inmates but also long-time residents living within its grounds.

Kapatid received reports that some residents got three eviction notices and that hearings were underway. The group called on Congress to include the affected communities in its proposed legislative inquiry and to ensure their welfare and protection.

Kapatid also launched its “Protect Bilibid Lands” campaign, calling for the preservation of the entire NBP reservation as a permanent national correctional center and an immediate halt to plans to close the facility by 2028 and convert its grounds into a commercial real estate venture.

The group urged both chambers of Congress to investigate Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) Director General Gregorio Catapang Jr. ‘s reported moves to commercialize 366.7 hectares of public land identified under Proclamation No. 1159. The area is 52.79% larger than the 240-hectare Bonifacio Global City and is projected to generate P1 billion to P2 billion in annual lease revenues.

“When we say ‘Protect Bilibid Lands,’ we do not mean preserving a broken, corrupt prison system. We mean protecting 366.7 hectares of public land so it can be transformed into a modern, humanized center for custody, legal aid, and reformation,” said Fides Lim, Kapatid spokesperson. “Amid widespread corruption scandals and the lack of accountability, a congressional inquiry is urgently needed to compel full transparency since mass transfers are being used as a pretext for decongestion to empty prime public land for commercial profit.”

Kapatid said that retaining NBP as a national correctional center is necessary to keep prisoners near their families and support their rehabilitation.

Citing BuCor data, the group said that 12,878 of the 21,129 persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) at NBP, or nearly 61%, came from the National Capital Region, CALABARZON and Central Luzon.

The NCR accounted for 5,998 prisoners, or 28.39% of the population, followed by CALABARZON with 4,199 or 19.87%, and Central Luzon with 2,681 or 12.69 percent. Including Bicol’s 2,028 prisoners, Kapatid said that 14,906 PDLs, or 70.55% of the total, came from these four contiguous Luzon regions.

“Retaining NBP ensures that 6 out of every 10 inmates remain near their families for regular visitations which are clinically proven to improve mental health and rehabilitation success,” Lim said.

She also cited Rule 59 of the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners, known as the Nelson Mandela Rules which calls for prisoners to be allocated to facilities close to their homes or places of social rehabilitation.

Kapatid warned that transferring prisoners to remote penal colonies would increase travel expenses for low-income families and weaken the family support networks needed during rehabilitation.

The group also cautioned that mass transfers could merely shift overcrowding to other facilities. It cited occupancy rates of 541% at Iwahig Prison and Penal Farm, 504% at Leyte Regional Prison, and 399% at San Ramon Prison in Zamboanga City.

KAPATID further cited 6,538 prisoner deaths across BuCor facilities from 2020 to 2025, warning that separating vulnerable prisoners from their families could worsen the prison health crisis.

The group said that the proposed commercialization must be assessed against Republic Act No. 10575, or the Bureau of Corrections Act of 2013 which establishes BuCor’s responsibilities for the safekeeping and reformation of national prisoners and provides for standard correctional facilities, including hospitals and visiting areas.

Kapatid maintained that decongestion should address systemic problems in the criminal justice system rather than rely on the transfer of prisoners to distant penal colonies.

“Real decongestion requires judicial efficiency and structural reforms, including clearing administrative backlogs that force prisoners who have fully served their sentences to resort to costly habeas corpus petitions for release; releasing elderly and very ill prisoners on humanitarian grounds; and ending the drug war that fuels extreme prison overcrowding,” Lim said.

The group’s campaign builds on a petition submitted to the Department of Justice on July 24 signed by 45 political prisoners at NBP, including 12 senior citizens and 18 people with medical conditions.

The petition opposed forced mass transfers to distant penal colonies and called for human rights safeguards, including prior formal notice and written consent from PDLs.

Kapatid said that preserving the NBP reservation does not mean maintaining the existing prison system unchanged, but transforming the public land into a modern correctional facility that upholds human dignity, access to legal assistance and rehabilitation.

The group called on Congress to investigate the proposed land conversion, ensure transparency in decisions involving public property, and protect both prisoners and long-time residents who could be affected by the planned closure and commercialization of the reservation. (DAA)

author: Unknown
title: Warzone Distro - A is for Nihilism
content:
Author

: Warzone Distro

Title

: A is for Nihilism

Date

: 2017/09/08 04:28

Source

: Retrieved on 01/17/2026 from https://warzonedistro.noblogs.org/post/2017/09/08/a-is-for-nihilism/







“We’re all animals prescribed medication in the form of artificiality. Moral values, roles and “higher purposes” are socially constructed and assigned to us to reinforce social control. Individualist anarchy contradicts the homogeny of civilized order. Our animality is imprisoned by an institutional society that enforces its order through domesticated membership. Beneath all of the socially constructed identities, roles, conditioning and subservience we crave anarchy-acting and experiencing life out of bounds, above and beyond indoctrinated captivity. When we undress all of these assignments and refuse the medication of civilized order we are naked, wild and unique. Life opens up as a playground, and like within a self-aware dream in which we decide to have fun, it becomes a playground of limitless potential. In a self-aware dream, we know we must hurry and have fun before we awake. Life is a dream in which we must hurry and play before we wake up dead.”

 

 — Blitz Molotov







Introduction




 Nihilism comes from the Latin nihil, meaning “nothing”. As a philosophical position, nihilism involves rejecting certain existence claims. Two prominent forms of nihilism are existential nihilism, whch rejects claims that human life is meaningful, and moral nihilism, which rejects claims that human actions can be right or wrong. Other forms include epistemological nihilism, mereological nihilism, and political nihilism. As with any other philosophical label, there is diversity within nihilism and disagreement over what counts as nihilism. Labels with some overlap include existentialism, absurdism, fatalism, and pessimism. Some people embrace nihilistic conclusions as a philosophical matter, while other people relate to nihilistic themes more as a matter of intuition, personal experience, or personal expression. With that said, this zine does not represent any “official” definition, nor a new program or political ideology. Instead it merely presents some common anarchist-nihilist ideas which encourage an anti-political critique of all social control and order, in favor of individual empowerment, anarchy and insurrection. 




A

 is for Anarchy beyond (the nostalgic captivity of) leftism.




Critiquing the Left










 Critiquing civilization as the logic, institutions, and physical apparatus of domestication, control, and domination. 










 A critique of communism, socialism, and all other left ideologies as they merely seek to redistribute the exploitations of the earth more evenly among classes of humans without addressing the destructive relationship between mass society and the earth. 










 Understanding that an attack upon capitalism that fails to target civilization can never abolish the institutionalized coercion that fuels society. 










 Critiquing the Left as nebulous, anachronistic, distracting, a failure & at key points a counterproductive force historically (“the left wing of capital”). 










 Critiquing Reductionism (Only particular aspects of the social struggle are included in leftist organizations. Other aspects are ignored, invalidated or respressed, leading to further and further compartmentalization of the struggle. Which in turn facilitates manipulation by elites and their eventual transformation into purely reformist lobbying societies with all generalized, radical critique emptied out.) 










 Critiquing Leftist activists for political careerism, celebrity culture, self-righteousness, privilege politics, vanguardism & martyrdom. 










 Critiquing Specialization or Professionalism (Those most involved in the day-to-day operation of the organization are selected — or self-selected — to perform increasingly specialized roles within the organization, often leading to an official division between leaders and led, with gradations of power and influence introduced in the form of intermediary roles in the evolving organizational hierarchy.) 










 Critiquing the tendency of Leftists to insulate themselves in academia, scenes & cliques while also attempting to opportunistically manage struggles. 










 Critiquing collectivism, the subordination of the individual to the group. Critiquing the ideology of collective responsibility (a critique that does not mean the refusal of social or class analysis, but rather that removes the moral judgment from such analysis, and refuses the dangerous practice of blaming individuals for activities that have been done in the name of, or that have been attributed to, a social category of which they are said to be a part, but about which they had no choice — e.g., “Jew”, “gypsy”, “male”, “white”, etc.) 










N

 is for moral nihilism







“And if I call myself an individualist anarchist, an iconoclast and a nihilist, it is precisely because I believe that in these adjectives there is the highest and most complete expression of my willful and reckless individuality that, like an overflowing river, wants to expand, impetuously sweeping away dikes and hedges, until it crashes into a granite boulder, shattering and breaking up in its turn. I do not renounce life. I exalt and sing it.”

 

 — Renzo Novatore

author: Brian Hioe
title: Migrant Rights Remain Unheard Ahead of Election
content:
THE KUAI KUAI STRIKE that came to an end earlier this month involved migrant workers being led across picket lines by labor brokers. Migrant workers were instructed to say on video that they were willing to work, unlike striking Kuai Kuai workers.

The strike by workers at iconic snack Kuai Kuai’s Zhongli factory came to an end after five days earlier this month. Kuai Kuai is an iconic snack best known for a superstition that keeping bags of it near machinery keeps them running smoothly. Kuai Kuai operates one factory in Taoyuan, but 130 out of 155 union members voted in favor of a strike after the company decided to relocate to Hsinchu.

The two sites are 39 kilometers from each other, meaning that the move is untenable for many workers. Workers were only informed of the land scale on September 1st. The factory has operated in Zhongli since 1968, and 1/3rd of workers at Kuai Kuai have worked there for more than thirty years, despite the fact that their wages are near minimum wage.

Workers have accused the San-Ti Group that owns Kuai Kuai of perhaps having only acquired the company with an eye on selling its land to Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc. Originally, Kuai Kuai workers were only offered a 5% pay increase and verbal assurances that they would be relocated to the new factory. It is to be seen if acquiring land to sell it to technology companies is a tactic increasingly adopted in corporate acquisitions going forward.

The incident of labor brokers bringing migrant workers across the picket line then highlights when migrant workers are pitted against domestic Taiwanese workers by their employers. In particular, one notes that this may become an increasingly common feature of protests going forward, in which employers aim to leverage splits between blue-collar migrant workers and domestic workers.

Indeed, this would sometimes be taking advantage of periodic waves of backlash against migrant workers.

Migrant worker groups recently demonstrated outside of the Ministry of Health and Welfare earlier this month, calling for being allowed to exercise their rights to maternity leave, as well as having days off. Instead of having work shifts, sometimes migrant workers are expected to work around the clock, sometimes even needing to hire other migrant workers to fill in.

On the same day, employers’ groups demonstrated outside of the Ministry of Labor, criticizing the government for not taking enough action about workers who have absconded from the job, what is framed as too long of a wait between replacing caregivers, and when migrant workers are pregnant and cannot work. Though this was framed as defending the interests of people with disabilities who require caregivers, the attempt is also to weaken migrant rights, so that they are less able to defend their labor rights, and are not made to work around the clock–as if they were robots, rather than human beings.

author: ACG
title: SOLIDARITY WITH ALL ANTI-WAR PRISONERS IN RUSSIA & DRAFT DODGERS IN UKRAINE
content:
Beneath is the text of the leaflet distributed outside both the Russian and Ukrainian embassies in London by members of the Anarchist Communist Group and the Network of Anarchist Internationalists (NAI) on Saturday October 31st







For the past five years, the warring states of Ukraine and Russia have been sending the working class to die on the battlefields, killing civilians across the war zone and destroying critical infrastructure with missiles and drones. European states are arming Ukraine, helping to keep the war of the trenches going on indefinitely—a war that has already lasted longer than WWI—in order to lay the groundwork for the revitalisation of their declining industry by shifting it more and more toward a war economy. The endless war, financed by loans from Europe and the USA, allows states to carry out their ideological, bureaucratic and technical “defensive” restructuring, as well as the broader restructuring of production, at a time when the US is pulling back from funding the war in the region and the whole planet is beginning to smell of gunpowder. The loans under the Rearm Europe arms program and the record ‘defence’ budgets being pushed by Europe point with certainty toward war austerity, in other words an even harsher exploitation of the working class, as its future wages are put up as collateral for current spending. In 2025, global military spending reached $2.887 trillion, the highest level ever recorded by SIPRI, while Europe increased its military spending by 14% in a single year. European military spending reached an average of 3.2% of GDP, up from 2.8% in 2024.




The Death Camp that is Ukraine, hemmed in on all sides, built jointly by Russia on the one hand and the USA and Europe on the other, plays a key role in spreading militarisation throughout European societies: expanding the arms industry, increasing military spending, intensifying and generalising conscription, recruiting men and, to

some extent, women into the armed forces with the lure of a career, and repressing those who refuse to take part.




Within this process, desertion and draft resistance movements play an important role in undermining the ideology of national unity and the state’s ability to keep mobilising entire populations for war. This is why the widespread draft resistance and desertion in Ukraine and Russia—300,000 deserters and 2,000,000 draft dodgers in the former, and more than 75,000 deserters and 260,000 draft dodgers as early as September 2022 in the latter—is so significant and deserves the support of the antiwar movement. The stories of violence and imprisonment suffered by those resisting mobilization on both sides of the front show what the militarisation of society means

in practice, and what it costs to refuse to fight for the state and the bosses.




In Russia, which has recently entered a phase of silent mass mobilisation, deserters—most of them forcibly recruited through coercion and blackmail—are being summarily executed on the spot by their own commanders (zeroing out). Along the borders of Ukraine, men trapped inside the country by martial law—which prevents them from leaving for safer countries—are trying to cross frozen mountains and rivers to escape

mobilisation. Some freeze to death; others drown. Those forced to remain in the country are left at the mercy of the TRCs, a special military unit that rounds up men from the streets, their workplaces, public transport stops, cafés and outside schools. They are thrown into vans and taken to the front in a practice that has become known

as busification’. Those who physically resist busification or take part in armed resistance inside training centers end up facing crushing prison sentences. When an army lifer is killed in such an incident, the sentence is life imprisonment.




Bogdan Koshel, 27, was drafted in Kyiv in June 2025. After contemplating suicide, he eventually turned his weapon on the military bastards who were training him and was sentenced to life in prison on June 9, 2026, for the deaths of two of them. Twenty three-year-old Oleg Gavrilov and five others arrested under martial law for

“obstructing mobilization” during the July 8, 2026 uprising in a neighborhood of Lviv against a busification operation are being prosecuted for assault against police officers. Twenty-seven-year-old Ukrainian Trotskyist Bogdan Syrotiuk was sentenced to 15 years in prison not for any physical attack or act of resistance, but simply for expressing antiwar views in articles published on the World Socialist Website. These are only a few of the hundreds who have disappeared into state cells, with no solidarity network to support them. Even legal defense by independent lawyers has become difficult, since they risk being subjected to busification the moment they

appear in court, or becoming targets of beatings.




Women who defend men against busification and run social-media groups documenting TRC checkpoints are also targeted by uniformed thugs, cops and far right paramilitaries. Those who support men trying to escape busification are beaten by cops, pepper-sprayed and otherwise assaulted; after their arrest, they can receive

five-year suspended sentences and be placed under supervision. Angela Gurena was sentenced to five years in prison without suspension for posting a TikTok video showing soldiers rounding up men during a busification operation.




Even civilians are thrown into so-called “penal colonies,” a soviet holdover in the prison system, because they are accused of alleged—and perhaps, in some cases, actual— “collaborationism” with the Russian administration in the formerly occupied territories. At “Penal Colony” No. 86 in Vinnytsia, alleged “collaborators” went on hunger strike on August 5 and again on September 11, protesting the brutal conditions of their detention, including torture and 12-hour forced labor.




Across Ukraine, 620 incidents of armed and/or unarmed resistance to busification and 272 attacks on TRCs have been recorded since the beginning of 2026.




On the other side of the front, in Russia, more than 20,000 people have been arrested for antiwar actions since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Some were arrested for antiwar graffiti, others for setting fire to military recruitment offices, and others for sabotaging railway lines carrying military

supplies to the front. More than 40 people had already been sentenced by the end of Russian proletarians who hit military recruitment offices with Molotov cocktails or sabotage railway lines are not always motivated exclusively by anti-militarist or antiwar convictions. In many cases they are anti-regime or motivated by pro-Ukrainian sentiments. However, even when such actions are done out of solidarity with the Ukrainian population, from pacifist or internationalist anarchist or communist convictions, they are still prosecuted as terrorism or as collaboration ‘with the enemy’.




In any case, those involved face heavy sentences and vindictive treatment inside the prisons where they are held.




The case of the ‘Chita anarchists’ is a telling example. Aleksandr Snezhkov and Lyubov Lizunova, two young people who wrote an antiwar slogan and set up an antiwar group on Telegram, were convicted as terrorists. Aleksandr was sentenced to 11 years in prison, while 17-year-old Lyubov was sent to a juvenile penal colony far from where herfamily lives. The anarchist Alexey Rozhkov was sentenced to 16 years in prison for throwing a Molotov cocktail at a military recruitment office, which, much to our regret,

caused minor damage.




Some men in Russia who took a stand against the war have lost their lives. Among them was 43-year-old anarchist pacifist Dmitry Kuznetsov, who died after being beaten and tortured in prison, and 20-year-old conscript Seryozha Gridin, who died by suicide in February 2023 at a military base near Moscow rather than fight in Ukraine. In a note, he wrote: “I decided to die here, in my homeland, without foreign blood on

my hands.”




Imprisoned Russian activists are calling for contact with the internationalist antiwar movement. Through their relatives and lawyers, they have made clear that they can endure prison, but not isolation. Contact addresses for reaching them are available through Solidarity Zone and the Anarchist Black Cross.

author: Unknown
title: Kuruluş amacından uzaklaşan bir yapı: Altın Portakal’ın gölgesinde Film Forum tartışmaları
content:
Bu yıl 63. kez sinemaseverlerle buluşan Antalya Altın Portakal Film Festivali, yalnızca perdelere yansıyan yapımlarla değil, festivalin endüstri ayağı olan Antalya Film Forum’da yaşanan krizler ve tartışmalı süreçlerle de gündeme damgasını vurdu. Adayların açıklanmasının ardından başvuru videolarının izlenmediğinin ortaya çıkması, yönetmeliğe aykırı yapımların seçkiye dahil edilmesi ve jüri süreçlerindeki şeffaflık eksikliği sinemaseverler açısından büyük yankı uyandırdı. Bu sürecin arka planını, Antalya Altın Portakal Film Festivalini, Antalya Film Forumunu ve süreci Yönetmen Umut Beşkırma ve Yönetmen Erinç Durlanık ile konuştuk.

Bu yılki Antalya Film Forumu, başvuru ve değerlendirme aşamalarında yaşanan skandallarla sinemacıların tepkisini çekti. Sürecin fitilini ateşleyen isimlerden biri olan Yönetmen Erinç Durlanık, yaşananları adım adım aktararak sistemin nasıl tıkanmış olduğunu gözler önüne serdi. Geçtiğimiz yıl da projeyle festivale katıldığını belirten Durlanık, Vimeo üzerinden yaptığı takiplerde projesine ait başvuru videolarının sıfır izlenmeyle bırakıldığını fark ettiğini söyledi.

Benzer bir durumun bu yıl da yinelendiğini vurgulayan Durlanık, başvuru havuzunda yer alan 167 projenin çok kısa bir sürede nasıl değerlendirildiği sorusunu gündeme getirdi. Projelerin 3 dakikalık tanıtım videolarının ön jüri tarafından açılıp izlenmediğini, dijital izleme sayaçlarının sıfır gösterdiğini belirten Durlanık, yapılan eleştiri yorumlarının ise festival yönetimi tarafından sistemden silindiğini ifade etti. Yaşanan bu güven sarsıcı gelişmelerin ardından sinemacıların bir araya gelerek ortak bir bildiri hazırladığını belirten Durlanık, sürecin arkasındaki yapısal sorunlara dikkat çekti.

Durlanık, yaşananları şöyle anlattı: “3 dakikalık videonun bile izlenmemiş olması, değerlendirmenin ne kadar güvenilir ve adil olduğuna dair büyük bir soru işareti yaratıyor. Daha sonra yönetmeliğe aykırı şekilde, daha önceden uzun metrajı çekilmiş bir projenin seçildiğini fark ettik. Ön jüri üyelerinin bile projeleri izlemediklerini açıkça beyan ettiği, değerlendirme kriterlerinin tamamen belirsiz olduğu bir fiyaskoyla karşı karşıya kaldık.”

Antalya Film Forumunun sinemacılar için yeni ortak yapım olanaklarının önünü açan ve projelerin tartışılabileceği buluşma noktaları olması gerektiğini belirten Yönetmen Umut Beşkırma da bu yılki sürecin ruhuna dair eleştirilerini yöneltti. Geçmişteki uygulamalar ile bugünkü tabloyu kıyaslayan Beşkırma, Forumun kuruluş amacından oldukça uzaklaştığını belirtti.

Umut Beşkırma, Film Forum süreçlerine ilişkin “Geçmişte Zeynep Atakan’ın yürüttüğü dönemde sunumlar akredite izleyicilere açık yapılıyordu. Böylece projeler yalnızca jüri üyelerine değil, sektördeki diğer sinemacılara da ulaşabiliyordu. Bu yıl ise sunumlar kapalı oturumlarda gerçekleşti. Finalistler, adeta hastanede randevu sırası bekler gibi, kendilerine ayrılan saatte içeri girip sunumlarını yaptılar ve çıktılar. Bir sinema buluşmasından çok, sınava giriyormuşuz hissi veren bir süreçti.”

Beşkırma, katılımcıların birbirleriyle tanışabileceği sosyal ortamların, kokteyllerin veya yemeklerin dahi düzenlenmediğini, hatta katılımcılara yaka kartı bile verilmediğini vurguladı. Aynı platformda finalist olan diğer sinemacılarla dahi tanışma fırsatı bulamadıklarını ifade eden Beşkırma, projelerin özgürce konuşulabileceği ve yeni ilişkilerin kurulabileceği bir atmosferin tamamen ortadan kaldırıldığını dile getirdi.

İki yönetmenin paylaştığı bu tablolar, Türkiye’de bağımsız sinema üretmenin zaten son derece zor olduğu ekonomik ve kültürel koşullarda sinemacılar üzerinde derin bir psikolojik ve mesleki tahribat yaratıyor. Üretimin zaten kısıtlı imkanlarla yürütüldüğü bu koşullarda, destek mekanizmalarının kapalı kapılar ardında yürütülmesi, torpil ve kayırmacılık iddialarını beraberinde getiriyor.

Sinemacıların önünü açacak, onlara nefes aldıracak alanların birer birer daraltılması meselesi üzerine konuşan Umut Beşkırma, sinema desteklerinin ve festival platformlarının şeffaflıktan uzaklaşmasının Türkiye sinemasının geleceği açısından son derece kaygı verici olduğunu belirtti. Üretim koşullarının bu denli ağır olduğu bir iklimde, sinemacıların emeklerinin karşılığını alamamasının yanı sıra en temel organizasyon ve misafirperverlik koşullarında bile sorunlarla karşılaşmasının kabul edilemez olduğunu vurguladı.

Erinç Durlanık ise sürecin şeffaf yürütülmemesine ve en somut itirazların dahi görmezden gelinmesine ilişkin, “Gerçek ortadayken ve yanlışlar bu kadar net kanıtlanmışken hâlâ bunun yok sayılması, hiçbir düzeltme yapılmadan işin oldubittiye getirilmesi sinemacıların hevesini kırıyor. İnsanlar buraya bir kez başvurabiliyor. Bu hakkın bu şekilde heba edilmesi büyük bir haksızlık” dedi.

Antalya Film Forumundaki tartışmaların yanı sıra, bu yılki Antalya Altın Portakal Film Festivalinin genel seyri ve ulusal yarışma seçkisi de sinemacılar tarafından eleştiri oklarının hedefi oldu. Festivalin genel atmosferini ve organizasyon aksaklıklarını değerlendiren Umut Beşkırma, festivalin ulusal yarışma seçkisini oldukça zayıf bulduğunu dile getirdi.

Beşkırma, festival izlenimlerini ise şöyle aktardı: “İzlediğim filmlerin önemli bir bölümünün sinemasal nitelik açısından beklentilerimin altında kaldığını söyleyebilirim. Bunun dışında festivalin organizasyonunda da birtakım aksaklıklar yaşandı. Özellikle ulusal yarışma gösterimlerinde filmlerin arka arkaya programlanması, her gösterimden sonra salonun boşaltılıp seyircilerin yeniden içeri alınması ciddi yığılmalara neden oldu. Bu da seyir deneyimini olumsuz etkileyen bir durumdu.”

Festivallerin genel durumu ve sinemacıların emeklerinin karşılığı meselesini daha geniş bir perspektiften değerlendiren Umut Beşkırma, Türkiye’deki film festivallerinin zaman zaman popüler kültürün tuzağına düştüğüne dikkat çekti.

Örnek olarak bu yılki ulusal yarışma jürisinde yer alan Meryem Uzerli ve Fatih Artman’ın konumunu gösteren Beşkırma, “Her ikisinin de televizyon dünyasında başarılı oyunculuk kariyerleri olabilir, buna herhangi bir itirazım yok. Ancak Türkiye’nin en önemli film festivallerinden birinin ulusal yarışmasında jüri üyeliği yapacak ölçüde sinemasal birikime sahip olduklarını düşünmüyorum. Mesele televizyon oyuncularının festivallerde yer alması değil; sinemasal birikim ve yetkinlik yerine popülerliğin belirleyici bir ölçüte dönüşmesi” diye konuştu.

Festivallerin asıl sorumluluğunun popüler isimler üzerinden görünürlük kazanmak değil, sinemayı ve sinemacıları görünür kılmak olması gerektiğini vurgulayan Beşkırma, bağımsız sinemanın zaten zor olan üretim koşullarında festivallerin bu tutumunun alanı daha da daralttığını belirterek sözlerini noktaladı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Altın Portakal'da filmler vardı, tartışmalar da…
content:
Antalya Altın Portakal Film Festivali geride kaldı. Filmler gösterildi, ödüller sahiplerini buldu, sinemacılar ve izleyiciler bir araya geldi. Ancak festivalin ardından yalnızca filmler ve ödüller değil, organizasyon sürecinde alınan kararlar da tartışılıyor.

Festival boyunca özellikle uluslararası seçkiyi takip etme fırsatı buldum. Farklı coğrafyalardan, farklı anlatım biçimlerinden ve sinema dillerinden filmleri bir araya getiren seçkiyi oldukça başarılı buldum. Filmlerin temaları, ele aldıkları toplumsal meseleler ve sinemasal yaklaşımları festivalin ufuk açıcı tarafını oluşturdu. Uluslararası seçkinin, izleyiciyi farklı hikayelerle ve dünyalarla buluşturması Altın Portakal’ın en değerli yanlarından biriydi. Bu açıdan festivalin sinemaseverlere sunduğu programın hakkını da teslim etmek gerekiyor.

Bu yıl festivalin gündeme gelen başlıklarından biri, sinema projelerine destek sunan Antalya Film Forumun değerlendirme süreciydi. Foruma başvuran 18 sinemacı, ön değerlendirmelerde eşit koşulların sağlanmadığını belirtip ortak bir bildiri yayımladı. Başvuru materyallerinin incelenmediği, değerlendirme ölçütlerinin ortaklaştırılmadığı ve yönetmeliğe uygun olmayan bir projenin finalistler arasında yer aldığı yönündeki itirazlar, destek mekanizmasının işleyişini tartışmaya açtı.

Festival yönetimi bazı eksiklikleri kabul ederken kayırma iddialarını reddetti. Ancak özellikle bağımsız sinemacılar ve ilk filmini gerçekleştirmek isteyen yönetmenler açısından önemli bir destek mekanizması olan Film Forumda değerlendirme ölçütlerinin açık ve denetlenebilir olması gerekiyor. Çünkü bu tür platformlar yalnızca finansman değil, sinemacıların üretim ve görünürlük olanakları açısından da belirleyici.

Altın Portakal’ın tartışmalı geçmişinde 2014’te Reyan Tuvi’nin Yeryüzü Aşkın Yüzü Oluncaya Dek belgeselinin yarışma dışı bırakılması ve 2023’te Kanun Hükmü belgeseli etrafında yaşanan kriz sonucunda festivalin iptal edilmesi önemli yer tutuyor.

2014’te Gezi direnişini konu alan belgeselin yarışmadan çıkarılmasına tepki gösteren yönetmenler filmlerini çekmişti. 2023’te ise Kanun Hükmü belgeselinin seçkiden çıkarılması ve sonrasında yaşanan gelişmeler festivalin iptaliyle sonuçlanmıştı.

Festivalin dikkat çeken kararlarından biri de basının açılış ve kapanış törenlerinde yer almamasıydı. Açılış töreninde Onur Ödülü alan Menderes Samancılar, ödülünü basın emekçilerine adadı ve özgür basının önemini vurguladı. Ancak gazeteciler Samancılar’ın konuşmasını salonda dinleyemedi. Konuşmaya ilişkin haberler, sonradan sosyal medyaya düşen görüntü ve içerikler üzerinden hazırlanabildi.

Gazetecilerin bir töreni yerinde takip edememesi ve haberini sosyal medyaya düşen içeriklerle yapmak zorunda kalması, basının etkinliklerden dışlanmasının somut bir sonucu. Gazeteciliğin kamusal denetim ve doğru bilgiye erişim işlevinin giderek daha fazla baskı altında olduğu günümüzde, basına alan açılması her zamankinden daha önemli. Tam da gazeteciliğe en çok sahip çıkılması gereken bir dönemde, kültür-sanat etkinliklerinin basını dışarıda bırakması tepki çekti.

Festivalin bir diğer kararı, fiziksel katalog ve festival gazetesi baskılarının kaldırılmasıydı. Festival Direktörü Deniz Yavuz, Sinefil Atak’a verdiği söyleşide bu yıl fiziksel katalog ve festival gazetesi basılmadığını belirtti. Yavuz, kararı festivalin karbon ayak izini azaltmaya yönelik çalışmalar kapsamında değerlendirirken konaklama, ulaşım, atık yönetimi ve kağıt tüketiminin ölçüleceğini, sonuçların gelecek yılın verileriyle karşılaştırılacağını anlattı.

Kağıt tüketimini azaltmak ve çevresel etkileri ölçmek önemli bir hedef. Ancak festival gazetesi ve katalogların kaldırılmasının tasarruf olarak da sunulması, kültürel belleğin ve bilgiye erişimin nasıl korunacağı sorusunu beraberinde getiriyor. Festival gazetesi yalnızca bir yayın değil; söyleşilerin, yönetmenlerin değerlendirmelerinin ve festivalin bir bellek aracı. Sürdürülebilirlik politikalarının kültürel erişimi ve kamusal hafızayı gözeterek yürütülmesi gerekiyor. Ancak festivalin 136 milyon TL’lik bütçesi düşünüldüğünde festival gazetesi dijital ortamda hazırlanıp okurlara sunulabilirdi; böylece hem kağıt tüketimi azaltılabilir hem de Altın Portakal’ın kültürel belleğine katkı sağlanabilirdi.

Antalya Altın Portakal Film Festivali, bütün bu tartışmaların yanı sıra sinemanın farklı alanlarından üretimleri izleyiciyle buluşturması, yeni projelere alan açması ve sinema emekçilerini bir araya getirmesi bakımından da önemli bir buluşma oldu.

Bununla birlikte festivalin gerçekleşmesi için emek veren çalışanları, teknik ekipleri, gönüllüleri, sinema emekçilerini ve organizasyonun farklı aşamalarında görev alan herkesi de unutmamak gerekiyor. Filmlerin izleyiciyle buluşmasını sağlayan, yoğun bir çalışma sürecini yürüten ve sinemanın bir araya getirici gücüne katkıda bulunan tüm emekçilere teşekkür etmek gerekiyor.

Altın Portakal’ın geleceği açısından beklenti, bu emeğin sanatsal özgürlük, şeffaflık ve basın özgürlüğü ilkeleriyle birlikte büyümesi. Çünkü bir festivalin niteliğini yalnızca gösterdiği filmler ve dağıttığı ödüller değil, nasıl bir kültür ortamı yarattığı da belirliyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Hayatım yollarda eriyor
content:
Fotoğraf: Mesut Baylav/Evrensel

Küçükken ailecek metroya bineceğimiz anı sabırsızlıkla beklerdim. Mahalleden çıkıp hareket halinde olmak bana büyük bir heyecan verirdi. Ancak büyüdükçe o büyü tamamen kayboldu. Şafak vakti minibüs yakalamaya çalışmak, dakikalarca otobüs beklemek ya da Marmaray’ı kaçırıp on dakika sonrakini dert etmek hiç de eğlenceli değilmiş.

Artık o eski heyecanın yerini derin bir yorgunluk aldı. Fark ettim ki eve pestilim çıkmış şekilde dönmemin sebebi sadece işim değil, tüm bu çileli gidiş-gelişlerimmiş. Yolun en zor kısmı, metroya adım attığım an başlıyor. Vagon kapış kapış; oturabilmek köşe kapmaca, ayakta kalmak ise yüzlerce insanla o sıkış tıkışlıkta hayatta kalma mücadelesi. Kötü kokular, son ses video izleyenler, ağlayan çocuklar... Hepsi ayrı bir sınav.

En çok da insanları izlerken içim burkuluyor. Kıt kanaat bir maaş için kendini harap eden, ayakta uyuyan o kalabalığı görünce derin bir üzüntü duyuyorum. Ne yapmalı, bu çark nasıl kırılır bilemiyorum.

Gün batımını otobüs camından izlerken akılda hep aynı sorular: “Bu akşam ne yemek yapsam?”, “Sabah kaçta kalkarsam yetişirim?” Hayatımızın büyük bölümünün yollarda erimesi hiç adil değil.

Yine de yaşamaya devam etmek zorundayız. Sevmesek de, usansak da kendimizi var edebilmek için o metrolara katlanıyor, bir sonraki güne uyanıyoruz. Galiba hayatın gerçeği de bu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: infolibre
title: Στάχτη η έδρα της ελβετικής εταιρείας που κατασκευάζει τα όπλα LBD της γαλλικής αστυνομίας
content:
Σε απάντηση στους σοβαρούς τραυματισμούς που προκλήθηκαν από τα όπλα LBD  που χρησιμοποιούνται από την αστυνομία και τη χωροφυλακή στη Γαλλία, ακτιβιστές επιτέθηκαν στα κεντρικά γραφεία της Brügger & Thomet στην Ελβετία σε ένδειξη συμπαράστασης στις διαμαρτυρίες των νέων σε όλη την Ευρώπη. Οι κεντρικές εγκαταστάσεις της εταιρείας στη Βέρνη τυλίχτηκαν στις φλόγες τη νύχτα της 28ης προς την 29η Οκτωβρίου. Πρόκειται για μια εταιρεία με σημαντικά οικονομικά οφέλη από την προμήθεια οπλισμού στις γαλλικές δυνάμεις ασφαλείας. Στα προϊόντα της περιλαμβάνονται τα όπλα που εκτοξεύουν πλαστικές σφαίρες και από τότε που η αστυνομία άρχισε να τα χρησιμοποιεί, τουλάχιστον 70 άτομα έχουν τυφλωθεί στη Γαλλία.




Οι εικόνες που δημοσιεύτηκαν στα μέσα ενημέρωσης δείχνουν ένα κτίριο με μαυρισμένη πρόσοψη, απανθρακωμένο πίσω από τους φράχτες του και με τα παράθυρά του να έχουν γίνει κομμάτια. Η εφημερίδα «24 

Heures

», με χαρακτηριστικό τίτλο «Κατασκευαστής όπλων καταστράφηκε από τις φλόγες», επικαλούμενη την τοπική αστυνομία, αναφέρει ότι «οι συνθήκες και τα αίτια της έναρξης της πυρκαγιάς αποτελούν επί του παρόντος αντικείμενο έρευνας».

author: Unknown
title: 24 kentten Ankara’ya ‘barış nöbeti’ yolculuğu: Savaşın kazananı yoktur, anaların gözyaşının rengi birdir
content:
Elif Ekin Saltık [email protected]

1 Ekim 2024 tarihinde TBMM yeni yasama yılı açılışında MHP Lideri Devlet Bahçeli’nin DEM Parti sıralarına giderek tokalaşmasıyla fiilen başlayan sürecin üzerinden iki yıl geçti. Geçen iki yılda sürecin ağır aksak ilerlemesi, verilen sözlerin tutulmaması ve adımların yetersiz kalması üzerine Barış Anneleri alanlara çıkıyor. Devletin somut ve kalıcı adımlar atması talebiyle 1 Kasım Pazar günü Diyarbakır başta olmak üzere 23 kentten Ankara’ya doğru yola çıkacak olan anneler, barışın tesisi için kararlılıklarını bir kez daha vurguluyor.

2 Kasım sabahı Ankara’ya ulaşacak olan Barış Anneleri, ilk olarak Meclis Parkı’nda kitlesel bir basın açıklaması düzenleyecek. Açıklamanın ardından Kurtuluş Parkı’na geçilerek 2 Kasım’ı 3 Kasım’a bağlayan gece boyunca “barış nöbeti” tutulacak. Eylemin ikinci gününde ise TBMM’deki siyasi partilerin grup toplantılarına katılım sağlanacak, parti heyetleri, Adalet Bakanlığı ve Cumhurbaşkanlığı yetkilileriyle doğrudan görüşmeler gerçekleştirilecek.

Yolculuk öncesinde gazetemiz Evrensel’e konuşan Barış Anneleri Hatice Yaşar ve Yıldız Doğanay, hem iki yıllık sürecin değerlendirmesini yaptı hem de Ankara’da dile getirecekleri talepleri paylaştı.

Kendisinin gerilla, şehit annesi olduğunu vurgulayarak söze başlayan Barış Annesi Hatice Yaşar, iki yıldır cenazelerin gelmediğini ancak sürecin amaca uygun biçimde ilerletilmediğini kaydetti: “Biz barıştan başka bir şey istemiyoruz. İki yıldır cenazeler gelmiyor, biz bu sürecin iyiye gitmesini, barışa evrilmesini istiyoruz. Ancak iki yıldır somut tek bir adım dahi atılmadı. Sürecin başında Sayın Öcalan da ifade etmişti, ilk adım olarak hasta tutukluların serbest bırakılması gerekiyordu. Yüzlerce hasta mahpus var ama iki yıldır ne bir hasta tutuklu bırakıldı ne de bir tahliye gerçekleşti. Aksine, 30-33 yıldır zindanda olan, cezasını tamamen bitirmiş insanlara ‘Pişmanım de, seni öyle bırakalım’ dayatması yapılıyor. 30 yılını cezaevinde geçiren bir insana ‘pişmanım’ dedirtmeye çalışmak nasıl bir anlayıştır? Nerede görüldü böyle bir şey?”

Cezaevlerindeki tecrit ve kısıtlamaların kaldırılmasını, kapıların açılmasını isteyen Yaşar, iktidara şöyle seslendi: “Bizim tek talebimiz barıştır. Adalet Bakanlığı, Cumhurbaşkanlığı, cumhurbaşkanı yardımcısı kim varsa, bu sürecin iktidar kanadındaki muhataplarıyla görüşmek istiyoruz. Süreç tıkanmıştır, bu tıkanıklığın önü açılmalı, Sayın Öcalan’ın statüsü ve fiziki özgürlüğü sağlanmalı, zindanların kapısı açılmalıdır. Artık yeter, biz bu yükü taşıyamıyoruz. Buradan asker ve polis annelerine de sesleniyorum: Biz nasıl barış diyorsak onlar da ellerini elimize versinler, el ele verelim ve bu barışı birlikte inşa edelim.”

Barış Anneleri Hatice Yaşar ve Yıldız Doğanay

Barış Anneleri Hatice Yaşar ve Yıldız Doğanay

Evlatlarını savaşta kaybettiğini ve bir anne olarak başka hiçbir canın yitip gitmesine tahammülünün kalmadığını belirten Barış Annesi Yıldız Doğanay ise savaşın insani ve ekonomik yıkımına dikkat çekti: “Ben bir anne olarak konuşuyorum, evlatlarımı yitirdim. Artık üçüncü, dördüncü evladımı veya başka bir evladı kaybetmek istemiyorum. Sadece kendim için değil, binlerce Kürt ve Türk annesi için konuşuyorum. Asker, polis annelerine çağrı yapıyorum: Gelin ellerinizi elimize verin. Bizim evlatlarımız şehit düşerken nasıl canımız yanıyorsa, asker ve polis şehit olduğunda da bizim yüreğimiz aynı şekilde yanıyor. Annelerin gözyaşının rengi aynıdır. Türk, Kürt, Arap fark etmez, ananın yürek acısı birdir. Biz kimsenin ölmesini istemiyoruz, bu savaşın önü kesilmeli ve onurlu bir barış kurulmalıdır.”

50 yıldır süren savaşta ortamında ‘Biri galip geldi, biri mağlup oldu’ denemeyeceğini belirten Doğanay sözlerini şöyle tamamladı: “Savaşta kazanmak diye bir şey yoktur. Savaş ölümdür, gözyaşıdır, yok oluştur. Ülkenin ekonomisi, kaynağı savaşa, silahlara ve operasyonlara harcanıyor, oysa bu kaynaklarla ülke imar edilebilir, insanlar refaha kavuşabilirdi. Biz hiçbir evladımızın ölümünü kabul etmiyoruz. Barış, barış, ısrarla barış diyoruz.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Kurdish doctoral student imprisoned in Iran
content:
Matin Faramarzpour, a Kurdish cultural activist and doctoral student in philosophy at the University of Tabriz, has been sent to Mahabad Prison to serve a six-month sentence for “propaganda against the state”.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Faramarzpour, who is from Mahabad, was arrested on 28 October after appearing in response to a summons at the Enforcement of Judgements Office of the city’s Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office, and transferred to prison.




On 8 July, security forces violently arrested Faramarzpour in Mahabad’s Sheikh Shaltout Park, and he was provisionally released on bail several weeks later.




Branch One of the Islamic Revolutionary Court of Mahabad subsequently sentenced him to six months in prison on charges of “propaganda against the state.”

title: Sancar: Abdullah Öcalan has moved to the new facility built on Imrali
content:
Mithat Sancar, a member of the Imrali Delegation of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), made remarks on current developments during an interview with Medya Haber TV.




Stating that the Peace and Democratic Society Process had experienced a slowdown over the past two months, Sancar said that following the steps taken by the Kurdish Movement, the delegation needed to visit Imrali. He explained that the committee tasked with working with Abdullah Öcalan was the Peace and Politicisation Committee, emphasising that Öcalan's coordination was essential for the process to advance.




Saying that the process could not move forward through one-sided expectations and demands, Sancar stressed that the state needed to abandon its rigid stance in order to overcome the main obstacles.




“The move that will resolve the main deadlock will come from Mr Öcalan. I do not believe there is an issue that cannot be overcome, but for it to be resolved, the state must move away from its persistent and rigid approach,” he said.




Stating that Öcalan's aim was to unite the Kurds as a political subject, Sancar added: “Mr Öcalan has moved to the new facility built on Imrali. His agreement to move there should lead to an acceleration of the process.”

author: labor4pal
title: Dockworkers Global Strike to Halt Militarization of Ports (Countercurrents)
content:
Dockworkers on this International Day of Action, October 30 objecting to the “militarization” of European and Mediterranean ports today held strikes across the region bringing cargo handling to a halt at 111 ports. Striking workers, activists along with several hundred students shut down the Port of Trieste for more than an hour while rallying on numerous issues. Across Europe 40 other port blockades halted operations as workers protested in France, Greece, the Basque Country, Turkey, and Morocco in North Africa under the rubric “Ports for Peace – Jobs with Dignity.”

The port blockades, described as one of the largest coordinated international strikes in history is intended to send the message that workers refuse to participate in warfare and genocide by disrupting the military logistics networks and to end the use of commercial ports as “instruments of the military machine.” In compliance with the May 2026 Istanbul Declaration published by unions at over 35 European ports, they are demanding “that port facilities not be used to transport weapons destined for war zones nor be transformed into military bases serving NATO, the United States, or the European Union” with a special focus on “the genocide against the Palestinian people and the US-Israeli war of aggression in the Middle East and against Iran.”

In Italy, the grassroots 100,000-member strong Unione Sindacale di Base (USB) along with four other unions organized the general strike and called for all sectors of the country to participate in support of their blocking military shipments to Israel for its genocide in Gaza.

The unions have declared bluntly that “We do not load death. We do not transport bullets, bombs, and missiles so children can be killed. Workers will not pay for the war economy, inflation, armaments, and the profits of the monopolies.” They have also expressed “Full solidarity with the peoples of Cuba, Venezuela and Sudan.”

Other issues to be resolved revolve around worker safety, cargo transparency, decent wages, reduced working hours, fair pension provisions, and a stop to the implementation of the “highly automated port.” This concept is being promoted by internation shipping and container transport companies, which would require fewer union workers in favor of “semi-automated crane systems, driverless transport vehicles and automated container storage planning to increase efficiency and simplify processes.”

The morning blockade at the Port of Trieste saw operations come to a halt as 5,000 people flooded into the main entry point of the normally busy port as a heavy police presence stood nearby. Before departing on a march across the city, the crowd heard from several speakers on a variety of issues, including “housing expenses and soaring rents – increases in energy costs and household utility bills,” along with the inflationary impact of escalating fuel prices. All issues which resonate with working-class people from across Europe and around the world.

Other topics broached by speakers were the continual erosion of public worker’s salaries due to high inflation and increased energy costs and the government’s preference, in claiming that there are no available funds, while spending public funds on “armaments rather than essential services.” Additionally, there were calls for an end to fossil fuels and in ending military propaganda in school curriculum.

To illustrate the issue of misplaced spending the Unione Sindacale Italiana (USI) handed out a broadsheet showing the cost of various military armament and how many new schools and hospitals could be constructed instead, for the equivalent of the billions of Euros being spent by the government. As an example, one Eurofighter jet aircraft could fully fund 25 schools and two hospitals. An obscene misuse of public funds that was reflected in numerous handmade signs carried by protesters.

After rallying, the crowd marched across the city carrying signs along with Palestinian and union flags while chanting loudly and clapping to, “Siamo tutti antifascisti” (we are all anti-fascists) and in calling for an end to the Genocide in Gaza.
