author: Mitchell Plitnick
title: As US and Israel Plot Iran Escalation, Regional Powers Scramble to Avert It
content:
Saudi, Pakistani, and Turkish leaders met with Iranian officials in Tehran, signaling their reticence to renew the war.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The first of two elections that many believe are the final bell before all out war is resumed against Iran is now complete. Although it seems likely that the efforts to cobble together a governing coalition in Israel, if that is even possible, will take weeks, the American midterms are expected to be the last milestone before the United States and Israel launch a massive attack on Iran.

There is no doubt that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is almost bursting with anticipation of the bloodshed to come. Donald Trump, as always, seems unsure of how to proceed, but seems very uncomfortable with the situation as it stands, while also being unwilling to make the concessions necessary to end this futile, destructive war he started for no good reason.

Iran can do little to deter an American attack, if that is what Trump decides to do. But it can retaliate with devastating consequences, which will be felt by its Gulf Arab neighbors, Israel, and the global economy.

That is why the countries of the newly created Mecca Pact — Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Türkiye — took the dramatic step of meeting Iranian officials in Tehran.

Iran trumpeted the meeting as demonstrating the seriousness with which the Sunni Muslim states take the Islamic Republic, meeting in the Iranian capital rather than in a third country.

Saudi Arabia said the meeting was aimed at mediating between the United States and Iran, but there is no evidence the United States had any part in the planning of this meeting. Indeed, the indications are the opposite; one purpose of the confab was to establish regional dialogue specifically on security matters.

Participants included Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff Field Marshall Asim Munir, Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish Director of National Intelligence Ibrahim Kalin. They met with Iran’s Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei.

The fact that the meeting included leaders of the countries’ respective militaries indicates that the description of the meeting — that it was to deal with regional security — is likely accurate.

And, while little has been made public about the substance of the meeting, it also seems fair to say that there was little progress that could have been made on the major issues—the war with U.S. and the ongoing battles between Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni Ansar Allah.

Regarding Ansar Allah, Saudi Arabia was feeling Iran out to see if they would intervene with the Yemeni fighters whom the Saudis have been unable to defeat.

But Iran doesn’t have much reason to do so. While they could benefit from pulling the Saudis away from the American war effort, the compromises Tehran would have to make are far too great.

Reports out of Israel state that the Saudis offered Ansar Allah $1 billion for a ceasefire. But the Yemeni group will not budge on its understandable demand that Saudi Arabia drop its air blockade of Yemen.

This is not an issue Iran can try to mediate. If they try to get Ansar Allah to compromise on the air blockade, it undermines their argument that the United States must end its sea blockade of Iran.

Iran supports Ansar Allah’s cause, but if they thought they could get concessions from the Saudis on the kingdom’s support for American military efforts, Ansar Allah might find it reasonable to agree to a temporary ceasefire to help their ally.

But they cannot compromise on the air blockade, nor would Iran want them to. As long as Saudi Arabia maintains its efforts to block air traffic in Yemen, they can’t buy their way out of Ansar Allah attacks.

On the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, the Saudis are very worried, as are all the countries of the Gulf and their neighbors. They should be, given that Trump has warned the Gulf states to get ready for a “short, intense military campaign.” Considering that the war started on February 27 was supposed to end in just a few days, or weeks at most, no one is counting on the “short” part. But it is likely to be intense, and that intensity will be felt in Iran and the Gulf Arab states.

The problem for Iran is that its interlocutors can do little to turn Trump’s mind. Even Saudi Arabia, which is in a terrible position right now if the war restarts, has few options outside of registering its reservations with Trump, which it surely has already done.

Türkiye and Pakistan have even less leverage over Trump’s decisions. If he is reckless enough to risk the consequences of restarting the war with Iran, what can they do to stop him?

And those consequences are potentially very dire.

Iran has made it clear that it intends to target data centers, AI hubs, and underwater fiber networks that are the backbone of the internet in addition to oil infrastructure. No one doubts they have the capability of doing so.

The amount of damage that can be inflicted on the world dwarfs anything we’ve seen until now.

That has produced fear among the Gulf states, but it has also produced tension between them and Iran. Gulf states are angry at Iran for targeting them in response to American attacks, but Iran is aggravated because the Gulf states have cooperated with Washington.

This double-edged sword was visible this week when Qatar submitted a proposal for a ceasefire and a path back to negotiations, including reciprocal but revocable steps each side could take, presumably offering each side the assurances they needed to proceed.

But at the same time, Qatar publicly supported the call for Iran to allow international traffic through the Strait of Hormuz unconditionally. That did nothing to help the case for Qatar’s proposal, which Iran eventually dismissed as a collection of random ideas rather than a serious proposal and which Trump ignored.

Vice President JD Vance, who has quietly been opposing the resumption of large-scale fighting, tried reaching out via a letter to Rezaei, but the letter reportedly offered no immediate relief from any of the pressures the U.S. is putting on Iran while demanding that any talks include the nuclear issue, which Iran insists be left to be discussed after its minimal terms are met. In other words, it was just Vance delivering Trump’s unacceptable terms in nicer language.

If that wasn’t enough to make the Vance letter a non-starter, the fact that Vance’s earlier efforts were routinely contradicted by Trump soon after empties the vice president of any credibility, even if Tehran believes he is personally sincere in his desire to avoid another round of full-scale fighting.

This leaves only one hope: that Trump, in his eternally mercurial and indecisive way, will back away from what will be a devastating conflict.

One unknown is how much Trump understands about the danger that an Iranian response presents and how certain it is that a devastating response will be coming.

Trump’s threat of a “short intense” attack would seem to imply that he is being led to believe that the United States can overwhelm Iran with devastating force. Of course, that is exactly what he tried in February, and it failed dismally. Outside of insanity, does he have any reason to think that the same action would produce a different result this time?

It could be that what the U.S. and Israel are planning is a multi-phase attack.

American planners may think the weakness of their initial strike was that they targeted Iranian leadership while devastating large areas of civilian and military infrastructure, believing that this would lead to the collapse of the Iranian government. When that failed, there was no plan B.

It may be that the idea this time is to simply start with doing as much damage to Iranian infrastructure as they can, then pinpoint where the response is coming from and take out those missile and drone launchers.

That is consistent with what Senator Chris Murphy is warning about when he says that what the Trump administration is planning is “insane.”

“It will lead to devastating escalation, and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law. There’s been open reporting as to what we may be planning and the civilian infrastructure that we may be targeting,” Murphy said. “They’ve been asked by the president to develop a plan. Whether they believe it will work or not, I do not know. But the plan that they have developed will lead, in my view, to a prolongment and an escalation of this war that will be devastating for our security interests.”

The result, then, would be one of two things. If the U.S.-Israeli attack is successful, the Gulf states will suffer significant damage, but they can recover and, theoretically, come out with a weakened Iran. But that would mean that what failed in February magically works in November, and there is no evidence to support that expectation.

The other, far more likely scenario is that Iran continues to weather American and Israeli attacks and responds by devastating the Gulf states, further demolishing American positions, and inflicting a far greater degree of damage on Israel than they have in the past.

In that scenario, Gulf oil and civilian infrastructure could be damaged beyond repair. Moreover, given the region’s inherent instability — governed as it is mostly by iron-fisted dictators ruling over states of mixed and often clashing ethnicities drawn up by colonial map-makers — such a scenario could well mean the end of one or more of the Gulf states.

It is that scenario that the Mecca Pact countries are trying to avert.

They are not fools; they knew there was little that Iran could do to change the strategic playing field. Instead, they hoped that sending their top security leaders to Tehran would signal to Washington how concerned they were. They understood that the meeting, by its very existence, would give Iran a diplomatic win and, more importantly, would show that the Mecca Pact is intended to forge a new regional security system that will want to work with Iran, potentially even including it in the group someday.

The Mecca Pact countries, as well as Iran, hope that this message of the region’s strong desire to avert the oncoming catastrophe will convince Trump to back off.

Meanwhile, in Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu is even more incentivized to see the war roar back to life. With the election process in deadlock, he needs to move swiftly, before the opposition can make the case to the public that they are better suited to defeat Iran than Netanyahu.

He needs the war to make it more difficult to replace him, and he will push hard for it. He has already tried to provoke Iran into an act that would have restarted the major fighting before Trump was ready. He will surely try again before too long.

author: Victoria Valenzuela
title: Incarcerated LA Youth Fought for the Right to Hug Their Parents — and Won
content:
Having enshrined youths’ right to hug parents during visits behind bars, activists are pushing for decarceration.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Mercedes Maradiaga sat across from her 19-year-old son in the Los Padrinos Juvenile Hall in Los Angeles in complete devastation. Her son had at that point been incarcerated at the prison for two years and she had visited him every weekend. But that day in September 2024 was especially hard because it was their first visit since he had been beaten by officers earlier that week in a space in the jail where there were no cameras. The guards had jumped on and kicked him, and he needed surgery for a torn ACL. All she wanted was to give him a hug and reassure him that she was there. However, because of the no-contact visit policies at Los Padrinos, she was unable to give him that comfort.

Even during birthdays and holidays, they weren’t allowed to embrace. The boy endured the jail’s horrible living conditions — including rat infestations and flooded toilets — but couldn’t hug his mom for a moment of escape.

“I couldn’t even let him know I’m here just with the little hug,” Maradiaga said. “It would have meant everything to him. It was sad, and I did that for four years.”

Los Padrinos had reopened a year earlier in 2023, after being shut down in 2019 due to conditions that violated the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) standards, including abuses by staff. Six officers were criminally charged with assault and child abuse for using pepper spray on several teenage girls. Reports also cited a decreasing youth population as a factor for closure, yet staff claimed to feel “outnumbered.” When Los Padrinos closed, youth were shuffled to another facility called Central Juvenile Hall — and then in 2023, that facility was closed down due to similar issues. Los Padrinos reopened, and just months later, the abuses restarted. In 2025, 30 officers were criminally charged by the California Attorney General with child endangerment and abuse, conspiracy, and battery for encouraging “gladiator fights” that pit youth against each other.

Olivia Shields, a justice transformation policy coordinator at Urban Peace Institute, described the constant closing and reopening of BSCC facilities as a “cycle of noncompliance.” Shields said the Los Angeles County Probation Department has ultimately failed with these maneuvers to address the core issue: unmet youth needs — which won’t be addressed through incarceration but through coordinated care in the form of individualized, robust support systems and resources.

“Rather than decarcerate these populations of young people and find community-based alternatives or step-downs for as many of them as possible, they basically shift the youth around from facility to facility to avoid noncompliance,” Shields said.

Long before the closing of Los Padrinos in 2019, the facility had a bad reputation among Angelenos. Maradiaga recalled hearing disturbing stories about the facility in the ’80s when she was a kid.

“I think it needs to be shut down,” Maradiaga said. “I think that there needs to be a better way for the youth. I don’t think locking them away from their family is the answer.”

Barred From Basic Human Contact

When Ilana Parach, executive director and co-founder of Hoops 4 Justice, went inside Los Padrinos with a basketball and mentorship program, she quickly learned about what youth were facing inside. She felt it was important to give them a platform to express their needs directly, so she pivoted to working with them on legislation.

“They made a list of specific programs they wanted — resources for their families, reentry support,” Parach said. “At the bottom of that list, they wrote, ‘We want to hug our moms.’”

Incarcerated youth directly told her that one parent who hugged her son during a visit on his birthday then had her visit terminated and future visits suspended for two weeks. She said another youth was incarcerated for three years and had no choice but to watch his mother cry during the visits because she couldn’t hug him.

Contact visitation policies vary across California and are often left at the discretion of correctional officers. Parach said youth and staff both told her that Los Padrinos stopped allowing contact visits after the pandemic. Parach said that during meetings of the board of supervisors, she heard officers citing staffing shortages, financial issues, and concerns about drugs as reasons for disallowing contact visits. Still, visitors have to go through extensive screening when they come through a facility, including going through body scanners, sniffing by drug dogs, and X-ray scanners for their belongings.

“How could a young person’s parent bring in those drugs into a facility when they cannot even hug their loved one,” said Emily Zamora, policy and campaign coordinator at Youth Justice Coalition, an abolitionist organization that empowers impacted youth to dismantle the system.

Parach knew it wasn’t right that the youth weren’t allowed to embrace their family members, so she brought elected officials in to hear their stories. One of the elected officials who visited was California Assemblymember Isaac Bryan, who later introduced the Hug Act, the bill authored by the youth. Gov. Gavin Newsom signed it into law on September 27. The newly passed law will make it a right for all youth in juvenile detention centers to hug their parents, no longer leaving it at the discretion of the probation department that oversees the youth facilities.

Parach said it is important to center young people and amplify their voices.

“I think that they have to keep the kids at the center of the decisions,” Parach said. “Not just figuratively, but I think youth literally have to continue to provide direct input because they’re the ones that understand their needs the most, and making decisions about them without them is a detriment to all of us.”

Many youth advocates, youth, and families say the Hug Act was long overdue.

“It’s really devastating that it has taken up to this point towards this becoming legislation … for young people to be able to hug their loved ones,” Zamora said. “But the fact that this has been like something that hasn’t been around is honestly inhumane.”

Now, some of the organizers who had pushed to make the Hug Act a reality are continuing their longer struggle: shutting down dangerous facilities like Los Padrinos, and decarcerating youth out of the system altogether.

Shields said it’s inhumane not to allow young people who are going through the worst experience in their lives to hug their loved ones and experience the kind of comfort that they and their loved ones desperately need in these moments. And beyond that, incarcerated youth have been shuffled around various facilities as they have opened and closed and reopened.

Shields said that after Los Padrinos reopened in 2023, “It was just pure chaos. Because this was like a dilapidated facility that hadn’t been used in years, and it hadn’t been updated in any way, shape, or form, and then you’re just putting a bunch of young people there.”

“Detention is not a place where young people will have their needs met … It’s not something that we can reform our way out of.”

“Detention is not a place where young people will have their needs met,” Shields said. “The culture of probation and the culture of the way that they’re treating young people … is so deeply entrenched. It’s not something that we can reform our way out of.”

Justice advocates in Los Angeles have been calling out the youth incarceration system for years. In 2022, their campaign to put pressure on the Los Angeles Board of Supervisors resulted in the creation of the Department of Youth Development (DYD) to transition to a care-first approach. Shields said DYD is a county-run entity, which involves navigating tough bureaucratic barriers. The department and the work that they are building is new, requiring constant tending and resources from the board, as well as work to stay rooted in the vision and strategy of youth and community advocates.

Shields and Zamora believe in community-based care and alternatives to incarceration, rather than youth detention. They are also proponents of credible messenger programs in which someone from an organization connects youth to resources and opportunities both while they are incarcerated and after they return home so they have a support system when they leave, with the ultimate aim of decarceration.

“A lot of the young people that we work with will talk about why a credible messenger was so much more impactful for them than a probation officer and being incarcerated,” Shields said.

Zamora said detained youth have told her about many cases of medical neglect in Los Padrinos. In one case that her organization highlighted at the time, she says a young person drank bleach to get the attention of staff and finally get seen by a nurse. She said she also heard about a teenager in Los Padrinos who didn’t get to hug their parent before the parent passed away because of the no-contact visiting policy. Additionally, she has heard a lot about overdoses in the facility. She said Los Padrinos should have stayed closed given its huge track record of corruption and abuse.

The Youth Justice Coalition operates in a space that previously operated as the David V. Kenyon Juvenile Justice Center courthouse, where youth were detained and often given long sentences. Zamora said the transformation of the building from a punitive space into a place where youth find community and empowerment, as well as a garden and high school for system-impacted youth, gives her hope for what abolition can look like.

“This space is such a testament to what it looks like to shut down facilities that do not serve our communities and do not serve our young people … so that we could support these young people in being who they can be under the conditions that they deserve,” Zamora said.

Shields said there is a coalition of youth justice organizations in Los Angeles that will continue drawing attention to the conditions inside, showing up to the BSCC and board of supervisors’ meetings, and amplifying what they have been hearing from young people about how egregious those conditions are.

“We can’t incarcerate our way out of lack of safety,” Shields said, adding that instead we must find “a way to not reform but transform the youth justice system so that it really is rooted in love, care, healing, and a different form of accountability.”

title: Народная Самооборона - Имеет ли марксизм научную основу? Анархистская критика диалектики
content:
Автор

: Народная Самооборона

Название

: Имеет ли марксизм научную основу? Анархистская критика диалектики

Дата

: 2010е

Дополнительная информация

: НС признана террористами/экстремистами и так далее

Источник

: веб архив




 Примечание публикатора: 




Статья была откопана из веб-архива одной анархистской организации 2010-х годов. Содержание ее кажется весьма глубоким. Видно, что автор хорошо разбирается в марксизме и в философии. Автор ее, очевидно, анархист. Цель работы – не оставить камня на камне от одного из столпов марксизма – диалектическом методе. Несмотря на критический тон всей статьи, автор предлагает, что особенно ценно, некоторые ориентиры при построении настоящей современной революционной теории.




Приятного чтения!













 Первая статья из нашего цикла о марксизме, посвящена диалектическому материализму. Каждая политическая теория основана на каких-либо философских, социологических или экономических теориях. Основа марксизма – диалектика. Диалектика является ключевой теорией в марксизме – именно её зовут “научным методом”, и именно на ней построена вся система марксизма, включая экономическую и политическую теорию. Поскольку марксисты агрессивно-навязчиво рекламируют диалектику как “научную теорию”, противопоставляя её “ненаучному анархизму”, мы написали большую статью с разбором диалектики, действительного научного метода, применяемого в научном сообществе (как ни странно, ничего общего с диалектикой не имеющего) и метода, применяемого основоположником анархо-коммунизма Петром Кропоткиным. 




1. Диалектический материализм.




 Философская основа марксизма представляет из себя критическое развитие Марксом и Энгельсом идей немецких философов – диалектики Гегеля и материализма Фейербаха. Соединив диалектику и материализм и критически развив их, марксисты назвали свою теорию диалектическим материализмом. 




2. Диалектика




 Диалектика – это философская система, выдвигающая несколько “всеобщих законов развития”, применимых абсолютно ко всему – к природе и социуму, к истории и математике, к литературе и экономике, к живой природе и неживой… Диалектика в современном виде была разработана в начале XIX века немецким философом Гегелем. Гегель, являясь страстным сторонником идеалистического подхода полагал, что весь мир является лишь сознанием. Доказать эту точку зрения при помощи логики представлялось абсолютно невозможным, а потому Гегель был вынужден отказаться от обычной логики, и создать собственный метод, с помощью которого было бы можно обосновать, что наш мир является Абсолютным Разумом. Сама логика, говорит Гегель, является идеальным способом познания мира… но он доступен только Абсолютному Разуму, обладающему всей полнотой знания. Субъективному человеческому разуму, однако, в деле познания вселенной логика не поможет, мы не сможем понять вселенную посредством обычной логики. Потому Гегель применяет для познания Абсолютного Разума диалектику. При этом он предупреждает, что диалектический метод не должен применяться в обычной жизни, где подходят правила логики. Диалектический метод применяется им для познания вопросов основ бытия в его идеалистической манере. Марксизм, однако, переняв диалектику, перевернул это положение, и объявил о применимости диалектики во всех сферах бытия и сознания. То есть, по сути, инструмент, который самим создателем предполагался не для реальной жизни, но для абстрактных изолированных размышлений о некоем Абсолютном Разуме, охватывающем всё сущее, был перенят марксистами с отрицанием идеалистических выводов диалектики, и применим к реальной жизни. Это подобно тому, как некий теолог использовал бы Библию для познания бога, но атеисты, отрицающие само существования бога переняли бы Библию для познания сущности бутерброда с колбасой. 




 То есть с самого начала диалектика являлась антинаучным инструментом. В науке, если факты не соответствуют теории, отвергается теория. Гегель же поступил наоборот, и когда теория не сошлась с фактами, он изобрёл такой метод, который бы доказал, что его теория сходится с фактами. Это подобно тому, как если бы Гегель утверждал, что огонь является жидкостью. Однако это утверждение противоречит фактам. И вместо того, чтобы отказаться от своего утверждения, Гегель отказывается от научных методов, от общеупотребительных терминов, и заменяет их такими методами, так изменяет термины, и так произвольно подбирает их, что на выходе в рамках его рассуждения огонь становится жидким. В реальной жизни огонь от этого жидким не становится, но если в рассуждениях теперь всё сходится – значит, огонь жидкий. Аналогичным образом Гегель доказывал свою точку зрения о том, что наш мир является сознанием. Маркс и Энгельс с его точкой зрения были не согласны, и не разделяли положение о том, что наш мир – сознание. Однако инструмент доказательства Гегеля они сочли необычайно удобным, и решили взять его на вооружение. Вооружившись методом Гегеля, они начали доказывать совершенно противоположное тому, что доказывал сам Гегель. Казалось бы, уже одно это должно вызывать вопросы насчёт применяемого метода и его “научности”. Ведь если из одного метода вытекают два взаимоисключающих утверждения, то значит что-то с этим методом не так. Но это аргумент для обычной логики, а диалектика её отрицает. 




 Суть диалектики сводится к тому, что весь мир представляет собой единый процесс, постоянно развивающийся и никогда не пребывающий в некоем застывшем состоянии. Из чего очевидно, что нельзя представить некое абсолютное, идеальное состояние, как это делают многие утописты. И, соответственно, рассматривать человеческую историю, те или иные её события или политические или экономические системы, нужно не как застывшую систему в вакууме, но как развивающуюся систему, как процесс. Ничего не остаётся неизменным – всё в этом мире развивается в соответствии с внутренними “универсальными законами развития”, и в сочетании со всеми прочими процессами. Каждое явление развивается не в себе самом, но во взаимодействии со всеми прочими явлениями. И это вполне верное предположение, с которым трудно не согласиться – все происходящие процессы влияют друг на друга, и через друг друга – на все прочие. Не существует абсолютно замкнутых процессов в себе, всё взаимосвязано, и рассматривать отдельное явление нужно не “в вакууме”, но во взаимодействии с остальным миром.

author: Evan Vorpahl
title: Billionaires Captured Ohio’s Supreme Court. Now They Want a Fully GOP Court.
content:
Ohio’s state court election has been a circus of corporate and dark money campaigning.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Since mid-October, two right-wing super PACs have spent untold sums on ads portraying two of the four candidates running for seats on the Ohio Supreme Court as soft on crime. This campaign against judicial candidates supported by Democrats is a tried-and-true element of the attack playbook for special interests seeking to undermine judges that might hold corporations accountable.

One of the groups, called First Principles PAC, is a core part of Leonard Leo’s $1 billion+ dark money court capture operation. The other PAC, Ohioans for a Healthy Economy Action (OHE Action), is affiliated with the Ohio Chamber of Commerce and has been funded by billionaires Dick Uihlein, Jimmy Haslam, and Vivek Ramaswamy. The two targets of the ads, Jennifer Brunner, the lone Democrat on the Ohio Supreme Court, and appellate court judge Marilyn Zayas, are running against Republicans Colleen O’Donnell and Dan Hawkins respectively.

Ohio’s spring judicial primaries showcased hyper-partisan campaigning, which has now carried into the general election: Hawkins and O’Donnell have also campaigned alongside the Donald Trump-backed gubernatorial candidate Ramaswamy. Ramaswamy and his campaign for governor have been heavily criticized for spending millions on ads featuring the estranged mother of his opponent, Amy Acton, calling her daughter a “liar.” That woman has not seen her daughter for 47 years since she lost custody of her children after siding with Acton’s stepfather, who was indicted for raping Acton starting when she was 10 years old.

Meanwhile, last month, Republican Ohio Supreme Court Justice Dan Hawkins appeared at a banquet hosted by the Ohio Christian Alliance. At that event, he lamented the supposedly “rogue, liberal judges” derailing Trump’s agenda. He also emphasized that he and the other Republican justices “understand the importance of what it is to be a conservative justice … We need to make sure we maintain this strong conservative majority on the Ohio Supreme Court … together we can make sure Ohio’s Supreme Court stays in strong conservative hands.” That “conservative” court has wielded judicial power in distinctly un-conservative ways, overturning or ignoring recent legal precedents to help Republicans redraw voting maps and rewriting parts of a state ballot measure in ways that tipped the scales in favor of opponents of reproductive rights.

The stark partisanship in the election of Ohio judges is the product of decades of work by billionaires and right-wing operatives to open the floodgates of dark money influence in the state. It’s also a direct result of Republicans insisting on putting political party labels on judicial candidates in 2021. A main tactic in this campaign, pushed by corporate interests and the network of Leonard Leo, the architect of the right-wing capture of the U.S. Supreme Court, has been to manipulate how judges are selected. With a now 6 to 1 right-wing majority, Ohio may be this far right campaign’s largest state court capture success story.

It didn’t have to be this way. A century ago, widespread partisan corruption in elections led Americans to demand a change in how judges were selected. This culminated in the “Missouri Plan” and other related merit-based selection systems in many states. These procedures, which focus on experience and merit rather than partisanship for the selection of officials who are supposed to act as neutral arbiters, have acted as guardrails to insulate judicial power from party loyalty.

Although Ohio did not change its judicial selection process to a merit-based system, the state passed a law in 1911 mandating nonpartisan ballots for the selection of judges, a move that helps support judicial integrity by protecting the ideal that candidates be elected for their dedication to fairly interpreting the law, rather than loyalty to a political party or donors. (A year later, in 1912, the legislature passed a law allowing for partisan primaries, but general elections remained nonpartisan until 2021.)

Over the years, as big money began to seep into judicial elections, Ohio courts grappled with the conflicts of interest that political spending in judicial races inevitably brings. In 2006, The New York Times reported on Ohio’s weak recusal practices and a perceived correlation between campaign contributions and judicial decisions: “[J]ustices routinely sat on cases after receiving campaign contributions from the parties involved or from groups that filed supporting briefs. On average, they voted in favor of contributors 70 percent of the time.” Then-Justice Paul Pfeifer, a Republican, told the Times, “Everyone interested in contributing has very specific interests … They mean to be buying a vote.”

Between 2018 and 2020, Ohioans voted to narrow the right-wing majority on the Ohio Supreme Court from 7-0 to 4-3, despite millions in outside spending from groups affiliated with the Ohio Chamber of Commerce and other right-wing groups. Following those losses, the Republican-controlled legislature passed SB 80, which added partisan labels to general elections for high-level judicial races. The bill was introduced by Republican State Sen. Theresa Gavarone, who has worked closely with Leo’s network and other right-wing dark money groups.

In 2026, Gavarone was twice named a “policy champion” by the American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC), a corporate bill mill that pairs state legislators with special interest groups and corporate lobbyists to endorse regressive bills or policies. ALEC legislators then try to get these “model” bills made into law in their state, without revealing the role of ALEC or the special interests they may have secretly voted with to adopt those bills behind closed doors.

Gavarone’s award was for her work advancing voter suppression legislation pushed at ALEC’s pay-to-play conference by the Honest Elections Project (HEP), a Leonard Leo group that is a six-figure funder of ALEC. HEP is the alias of one of Leo’s core groups and its bills make it harder for Americans to vote.

Gavarone has also worked behind the scenes with fossil fuel billionaire Charles Koch’s Americans for Prosperity to craft other electoral legislation in Ohio. This year, Gavarone and Republican State Sen. Jane Timken (more on the Timken family later) co-sponsored legislation to put an amendment on the ballot to enshrine voter ID restrictions in the state constitution that make it harder for Ohioans to vote. Voter ID is one of many tactics for legislators peddling debunked voter fraud disinformation.

A number of people with ties to the Federalist Society, which Leo co-chairs, and other right-wing groups also testified in the legislature in favor of the bill, including Chris Bonneau, a longtime advocate of partisan judicial elections for the Federalist Society, and Robert Alt, an active member of the Federalist Society who helms The Buckeye Institute, part of the State Policy Network of groups closely tied to ALEC. The Buckeye Institute has operated in tandem with many Leo-tied groups, filing coordinated amicus briefs in high-profile cases before the U.S. Supreme Court. Travis Taylor of the dark money Foundation for Government Accountability (FGA) also testified. FGA is notorious for its recent widespread lobbying effort to relax child labor laws.

The Republican-gerrymandered state legislature passed Gavarone’s bill to add party labels to judicial candidates in general elections, which Republican Gov. Mike DeWine signed into law. The Ohio Chamber of Commerce hailed it as a major “policy victory.”

Justice Jennifer Brunner filed a lawsuit seeking to strike down that law, arguing that it “placed the appellate level judges and the justices of Ohio in positions to be viewed by the public as partisan.” She also noted that the measure “imposes a partisan check on the decisions of non-partisan trial judges.” In other words, placing partisan labels next to judicial candidates could cause the public to view judgeships as political positions dedicated to furthering the agenda of a political party, rather than viewing judges as independent arbiters of the law. On October 14, 2026, ahead of heated state supreme court elections, a federal district court judge rejected Brunner’s lawsuit.

In 2022, spending in Ohio’s first partisan judicial elections after the passage of SB 80 skyrocketed to $21 million, the most expensive judicial election in state history. Groups tied to the Ohio Chamber as well the Republican State Leadership Committee, a 527 nonprofit group that has received millions from the core groups tied to Leo, have accounted for a large share of that spending. Republicans swept the 2022 and 2024 supreme court elections, and they are seeking to take unanimous control of the court this November.

As the Ohio Supreme Court has become more and more partisan, it has also grown increasingly emboldened.

As the Ohio Supreme Court has become more and more partisan, it has also grown increasingly emboldened.

In April 2026, five Republican justices on the court struck down the state’s 70-year ban on judges making political endorsements. The ruling was even a bridge too far for fellow Republican Justice Pat Fischer, the lone dissent, who pointed out that the majority ignored precedent and procedure and invented a question within the case to enable themselves to make partisan political endorsements despite neither party in the case raising that question. Fischer also noted that the decision threatens the court’s impartiality and the public’s confidence in the court’s credibility. Notably, the Ohio Code of Judicial Conduct has long barred such endorsements, stating “[a] judge or judicial candidate shall not engage in political or campaign activity that is inconsistent with the independence, integrity, or impartiality of the judiciary.” (Justice Brunner had recused herself from the case.)

The effect of the ruling was almost immediately evident. Republican Fifth District Court of Appeals Judge Andrew King ran an ad in the Ohio Supreme Court primary bragging that he was “the pro-Trump constitutional conservative for [Ohio] Supreme Court.” And Republican Supreme Court Justice Dan Hawkins has been on the campaign trail with Ramaswamy, who gave $50,000 to OHE Action in 2024, as it was running ads supporting Hawkins.

The extreme partisanship on display in Ohio is a direct result of the right-wing’s long-term campaign to make it harder to hold corporations and billionaires accountable.

The extreme partisanship on display in Ohio is a direct result of the right-wing’s long-term campaign to make it harder to hold corporations and billionaires accountable.

Changes to state tort or injury laws are protecting corporations from accountability at the expense of everyday people by making it much harder for consumers to sue for damages. The Ohio legislature passed a massive tort reform package in 1996 that was heavily backed by the U.S Chamber of Commerce and its Ohio state affiliate. When the Ohio Supreme Court found it unconstitutional three years later, the Chamber launched a scorched-earth campaign against Justice Alice Robie Resnick. A Chamber-tied front group called Citizens for a Strong Ohio spent $4.2 million on misleading ads targeting Resnick’s reelection campaign, and later spent years fighting to hide its funders.

Meanwhile, attorneys and legal “experts” tied to the Leo-led Federalist Society and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce have urged the Ohio legislature to continue shielding corporations from accountability. They have also pushed back against citizens seeking to protect their ability to sue for damages incurred from environmental hazards like lead paint and asbestos.

A few recent rulings by the captured court illuminate just how far it is willing to go to promote the anti-consumer agenda of its corporate and billionaire benefactors. In the 2024 “boneless wings” case, a 4-3 Republican majority ruled against Ohioan Michael Berkheimer, who was seeking compensation for the lifelong harms he has suffered after a nearly one-and-a-half-inch bone was lodged in his esophagus and became infected after he ate “boneless” wings. The Republican-dominated court ruled absurdly in that case that the restaurant was not liable because “boneless” referred to a cooking style, rather than the actual lack of bones in the chicken.

In another glaring example, in 2025, a 6-1 Republican majority on the court rejected additional damages to the widow of a worker who died by asphyxiation when he walked into an elevator control room at a TimkenSteel plant that had filled with nitrogen gas. Despite the business’s alleged history of safety violations, the court ruled against the widow collecting damages beyond her husband’s death benefits of $800 a week, because nitrogen gas is not legally “toxic,” even though it causes death if it displaces the oxygen humans need to stay alive. Justice Brunner, the lone dissent, wrote that the decision “[flew] in the face of reason.”

Besides the generically pro-corporate ruling, the decision specifically favored the politically connected Timken family, which owns TimkenSteel. The Timkens have been described as Ohio Republican royalty. The family has contributed heavily to Republicans in the state, including candidates for the Ohio Supreme Court such as Dan Hawkins.

Timken money has also supported former justice Judith French, who in 2014 told voters point-blank:

The Ohio Supreme Court is the backstop for all those other votes you are going to cast. Whatever the governor does, whatever your state representative, your state senator does, whatever they do, we are the ones that will decide whether it is constitutional; we decide whether it’s lawful. We decide what it means, and we decide how to implement it in a given case. So, forget all those other votes if you don’t keep the Ohio Supreme Court conservative.

The Timken Company Good Government Fund and Republican State Sen. Jane Timken, who is married to the former CEO and board president of TimkenSteel (now Metallus Inc.), also contributed $11,000 collectively to the campaigns of three of the justices who presided over the case. A spokesperson for the court asserted that the justices are under no obligation to recuse unless they deem themselves to have a conflict.

Months after the TimkenSteel decision, a bill was proposed to increase the non-economic damages cap in personal injury lawsuits. (Ohio law limits non-economic damages to $250,000.) Ohioans for a Healthy Economy, the Ohio Chamber group currently running attack ads against Democratic judicial candidates Brunner and Zayas, ran ads against the bill this spring.

In Ohio and across the country, corporate and far right interests are pouring money into efforts to change how judges are selected, politicizing the bench through partisan labels, and currying favor with campaign donations. The eroding independence of state courts will continue to have devastating effects on everyday Americans — unless citizens fight back and insist on stronger recusal standards, stronger anti-corruption and campaign finance disclosure rules, strict limits on political spending, and a process for selecting state judges based on merit, not money.

Lisa Graves, True North’s executive director, and Deputy Executive Director Alyssa Bowen contributed to this story.

title: Tahincioğlu: Pressure and access bans on the press are a wake-up call
content:
Pressure on the opposition press has increased under the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government, particularly over the past two years. The government has begun using various methods of repression against media outlets it considers critical of its policies.




Access to the website and social media accounts of T24, one of Turkey's most widely read news websites, has been blocked. A trustee was appointed to HALK TV, while the websites and social media accounts of Kurdish media outlets such as Mezopotamya Agency, Jinnews and Yeni Yaşam have frequently faced access restrictions.




Data released by the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) for September 2026 showed that access to 3,492 pieces of online and digital media content had been blocked. During the same period, access restrictions were imposed on 15 news websites, while four websites were shut down.




Journalist Gökçer Tahincioğlu, a representative of T24, assessed the reasons behind the pressure on the press and its impact on journalism.




‘A government that has largely lost its narrative’




Tahincioğlu said that the government had largely lost its political narrative and stressed that the pressure on the press could not be attributed to a single cause. He added: "I don't think there is just one reason. If you look at the course of politics, you see a scattered and fragmented opposition, another opposition force facing obstacles to carrying out its role, and yet another opposition structure whose position in the elections remains uncertain. 




If you look at it from the perspective of a government that has largely lost its narrative and is experiencing economic difficulties at their most severe, you can also understand this opposition landscape. It would not be wrong to say that pressure on the media has increased as an extension of this fragmented political structure. Today, we are in an environment that is different even from the 2023 elections, one in which we feel pressure much more intensely. The media is not exempt from this pressure. On the contrary, it is among the most visible targets."




‘This is a turning point’




Tahincioğlu also addressed the access ban imposed on T24, describing the decision as a turning point for independent media. He said: "Given everything that has happened, it may not be entirely accurate to say that T24 is being singled out with particular persistence. However, completely blocking access to one of Turkey's leading independent news websites, especially on the basis of incomprehensible justifications that do not constitute offences under the law and even contain factual errors, after the website had already been targeted, is difficult to understand. But leaving aside whether it makes sense, it is possible to say that this marks a turning point. At the same time, this process serves as a warning, an alarm bell for independent media."




Tahincioğlu stated that government pressure had placed more than 95 percent of the media under the control of circles close to the government, pointing out that the public's right to access news was becoming increasingly restricted. He added: "Until recently, we were saying that 95 percent of the media was under the control of circles close to the government and that these outlets, far from going beyond the limits imposed on them, were voluntarily working to legitimise the government's criticised practices.




Today, those limits have narrowed even further. This also means that people are being deprived of news and must make extraordinary efforts to access information. Yet news should be information that reaches people and circulates freely. It should not be something people have to struggle to obtain. Of course, this environment is extremely advantageous for the government."




‘The divisions are deep and are not just a problem of today’




Tahincioğlu also assessed how different sections of society respond to the pressure on Kurdish media, saying that attitudes on this issue had not changed. He said: "I don't think this picture has changed. Those who criticise the repression continue to criticise it, while those who defend it as justified continue to do so, either openly or through their silence. Some people might be told, 'Look, now it has happened to you too,' but we can also say that these same people only regard what happens to them as a problem. Unfortunately, these divisions are very deep and are not just a problem of today."




Tahincioğlu pointed out that some sections of society consider the pressure on Kurdish media justified and said: "A large proportion of these actions are regarded as justified. Yet, at a time when efforts are being made to establish peace, perhaps everyone should reflect on these issues as well. However, there are deep divisions and deeply rooted habits. Abandoning these habits and looking at things from a different perspective is not easy. But without understanding and being understood, the chances of these processes succeeding are already very low." 




‘The problem goes far beyond the strength and influence of professional organisations’




Gökçer Tahincioğlu also addressed the position of press organisations and trade unions, stressing that professional organisations should be assessed individually rather than treated as a homogeneous group. He added: "We should not regard professional organisations as such a homogeneous group. However, the organisations that genuinely do their jobs properly, as we understand them, also have limited strength and influence. In an environment where most of the media operates within this structure, you cannot expect these organisations to have considerable strength or influence.mIn this respect, I think some professional organisations are being treated unfairly.




At this point, responsibility also falls, to some extent, on the public and political actors. When journalists have been reduced to such small numbers, both in terms of their presence and the platforms available to them, and journalism has been pushed so far into a corner, I do not think it is fair to criticise those who continue struggling. Unfortunately, the problem goes far beyond the strength and influence of professional organisations."

author: Unknown
title: Women’s conference in Ankara: There can be no peace without justice
content:
The “Women Discuss the Future Side by Side” conference, organized at the initiative of 80 women, including journalists, writers, academics, politicians, and activists, began in Ankara on. Saturday.




Following the opening speech, the conference continued with musical performances by İlkay Akkaya, Feryal Öney, Nurcan Değirmenci, and Selda Öztürk. More than 500 women from different cities are attending the conference.




Hikmet Kılınç, the mother of İpek Er, who died after being sexually assaulted and driven to suicide by Turkish specialist sergeant Musa Orhan in Siirt, is also among the participants. Showing her daughter’s belongings, photographs, and locks of hair, Hikmet Kılınç said, “I want justice for my daughter.”




The conference, consisting of three sessions, started with its first session, titled “Freedoms, democracy, justice, and equal citizenship.” Speakers at the opening session included politicians Gültan Kışanak and Zeynep Altıok Akatlı, Feride Eralp of the ‘I Need Peace Women’s Initiative’, writer Hidayet Şefkatli Tuksal, and political scientist Füsun Üstel.




Füsun Üstel: What we need is equal citizenship




Füsun Üstel drew attention to the legal reforms outlined in the fourth section of the report submitted by the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) to the parliamentary commission as part of the ongoing peace process in Turkey.




Üstel stated: “What is being discussed here is a transitional legal framework. A wide range of demands are being put forward. These include equal citizenship for Alevis, addressing their demands in the context of freedom of belief, introducing certain amendments to the Political Parties Law and the Election Law, amending Article 42 of the Constitution, which governs the right to education, to enable the use of the mother tongue both in education and in various areas of public life, and finally, Article 66, which defines citizenship.




The demand for equal citizenship is based on a conception of citizenship that rests on a neutral and impartial relationship between the state and the individual. Citizenship, as we know, actually reflects an inherent tension. It is a status that both includes and excludes. Citizenship is a concept with both internal and external boundaries. In fact, it conceals existing inequalities.




The demand for equal citizenship alone is not enough. In an environment where rights and freedoms are being curtailed, public spaces are increasingly shrinking, and various forms of exclusion are being created, is equal citizenship sufficient? What we actually need is equal citizenship plus rights.”




Füsun Üstel pointed out that the demand for equal citizenship must also be critically examined from the perspective of women. She continued: “What does equal citizenship mean for women? Is the concept of equal citizenship broad enough to include women? Behind equal citizenship lie masculine norms, patriarchal structures, and hierarchies. At the local level, we are facing a major backlash against women. At the global level, we are also witnessing an alliance of right-wing, conservative, and authoritarian regimes against women. Therefore, we must not be content with the demand for equal citizenship alone. We can bring these issues to the forefront by discussing them as part of building peace and a democratic society.”




Gültan Kışanak: Freedom does not come with permission




Speaking after, Gültan Kışanak stated the following:




“Freedom is something that begins and ends with us. Freedom is not a space that opens up with the permission of those in power or of men. If you do not take action yourself, it will never happen. We cannot achieve equal citizenship without dismantling the patriarchal, capitalist, and colonialist system.




When it comes to equal citizenship, simply putting race, class, and gender into words is not enough. We have often discussed how the Kurdish question also stems from our inability to become ‘us.’ We believe that differences have points of intersection and that, by developing policies on this common ground, we can build our shared future. We will succeed.”




Hidayet Şefkatli Tuksal: We should focus more on what unites us than what divides us




Feminist writer Hidayet Şefkatli Tuksal emphasized that the women’s movement and the Kurdish women’s movement have been struggling together against policies of repression and violence targeting women in Turkey.




“We constantly say that we all come from different backgrounds. Instead of talking about our differences, we should emphasize what we have in common. We need to come together more often to learn from one another and discuss what we can do together,” she said.




Feride Eralp: There can be no peace without justice




Feride Eralp, a member of the ‘I Need Peace Women’s Initiative’, emphasized that genuine peace cannot be achieved without justice and equal citizenship.




Addressing İpek Er’s mother, Eralp said: “We are speaking here while looking at İpek Er’s photograph. Without justice, peace would mean that the violence of war continues to be inflicted on women’s bodies in everyday life. War is not just about weapons.”




Drawing attention to the relationship between domestic violence against women and state policies, Eralp continued: “It is no coincidence that the concepts of family, population, and security have been closely linked ever since the concept of citizenship emerged. Why is the declining population growth rate a cause for concern in Turkey? Because the supply of cheap labor will decrease. For example, there is talk of the Mecca Agreement. What will Turkey be able to offer Saudi Arabia, or how will it be able to claim, ‘I have NATO’s second-largest army’? Another reason is that the elderly population requiring care will increase. In a country like Turkey, women are expected to care for elderly family members within the household.”




Zeynep Altook Akatli: We must shape politics through the language of peace




Politician Zeynep Altıok Akatlı stated:




“I believe that we can grow by engaging with aspects of one another that we have not seen and ideas that we do not agree with, and that these differences can also teach us something.




As we speak about peace and embrace it with the same conviction, I want to address the language we adopt. Even in debates within the opposition itself, we see the influence of the government’s violent language and rhetoric. I want to talk about how a culture of violence has engulfed the culture of peace, making us forget that peace is itself a culture.




To truly internalize peace and the concept of equal citizenship, we must know, learn about, and keep alive the memory of the suffering that society has endured from the past to the present.




Being a woman in a patriarchal society is difficult. But when identities such as being a woman, being Kurdish, being Alevi, being a worker, being divorced, or being an atheist are brought together, they are treated as a ‘crime.’




We want to continue being women who speak of peace in a culture of violence that fiercely defends the right to be provoked by those who are different. That is why we must reshape the language of politics through women’s voices and rebuild its culture around the language of peace.”




The conference’s first session continued with contributions from participants, followed by a question-and-answer session.

title: Süper Lig 10'uncu hafta maçı: Erzurumspor FK kendi evinde Çorumspor'a farklı yenildi
content:
Süper Lig'in 10’uncu hafta maçında Erzurumspor FK. Kendi evinde Çorumspor’a 3-1 yenildi

20. dakikada konuk ekip öne geçti. Paslaşarak kullanılan duran topun devamında ceza sahasına doğru yapılan ortayı savunma karşıladı. Orta yuvarlağın önüne doğru açılan topu Cengiz Ünder kale alanı sol çaprazına doğru tekrar ortaladı. O bölgede kendini boşa çıkaran Çağlar Söyüncü, sağ ayağının içiyle yaptığı vuruşta meşin yuvarlak uzak direğin dibinden ağlara gitti: 0-1.

32. dakikada kendi yarı alanından paslaşarak çıkan konuk ekipte Cengiz Ünder, sağ kanattan içeri katederek topu ters kanattaki Kyziridis'e aktardı. Bu futbolcunun uzak köşeye gönderdiği şutta meşin yuvarlak yandan auta çıktı.

42. dakikada ev sahibi ekipte Orhan Ovacıklı'nın sağ kanattan ceza sahasına gönderdiği ortada topla buluşan Giorbelidze, ceza sahası ön çizgisinden yakın köşeye sert vurdu. Kaleci Felipe, gole izin vermeyerek son anda uzandığı topu kornere çeldi.

Karşılaşmanın ilk yarısı Çorum FK'nin 1-0 üstünlüğüyle sona erdi.

55. dakikada ev sahibi ekipte Orhan Ovacıklı'nın sağ kanattan ceza sahasına gönderdiği ortada Giorbelidze, kale alanında kafa vuruşunu yaptı. Kaleci Felipe, yakın mesafeden üzerine gelen topu kontrol ederek gole izin vermedi.

71. dakikada sol kanada gönderilen pasta araya giren Gerxhaliu, meşin yuvarlağı kalecisi Ertuğrul Taşkıran'a aktardı. Ertuğrul'un bekletmeden uzaklaştırmak istediği top kısa düştü. Ceza sahası önünde meşin yuvarlağı önünde bulan Ramirez, kaleciyle karşı karşıya kaldığı pozisyonda yaptığı vuruşla topu ağlara gönderdi: 0-2.

74. dakikada ev sahibi ekip farkı bire indirdi. Rakip kalede baskısını artıran ev sahibi takımda Kerk'in savunma arkasına gönderdiği pasla topla buluşan Diabate, ceza sahasının çaprazından yaptığı sert vuruşla meşin yuvarlağı ağlarla buluşturdu: 1-2.

79. dakikada konuk ekip farkı tekrar ikiye çıkardı. Ramadani'nin sağ kanattan ceza sahasına gönderdiği ortada Orhan Ovacıklı'nın müdahalesinde topun eline çarptığı gerekçesiyle konuk ekip penaltı bekledi. VAR incelemesinin ardından hakem Kadir Sağlam, penaltı noktasını gösterdi. Atışı kullanan Ramirez, meşin yuvarlağı kaleci Ertuğrul Taşkıran'ın sağından ağlara gönderdi: 1-3.

Karşılaşma, Arca Çorum FK'nin 3-1 üstünlüğüyle sona erdi.

title: Özgür Çelik'ten Bakırköy operasyonuna tepki
content:
İktidarın muhalefet belediyelerine yönelik operasyonları kapsamında Bakırköy Belediyesi soruşturmasında 20'si belediye görevlisi 39 kişinin tutuklanmasının ardından Yeni Parti İstanbul İl Başkanı Özgür Çelik bir açıklama yaptı. Operasyonları siyasi olarak niteleyen Çelik, "Yandaşlara, vurgunlarla zenginleşenlere dokunmayanlar, söz konusu muhalifler olunca peşinen cezaevine gönderiyor" dedi.

Özgür Çelik sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada şu ifadelere yer verdi:

"Bakırköy Belediyemize gerçekleştirilen siyasi operasyonlar ile yeri yurdu belli olan, yıllarca devlete ve halka hizmet etmiş belediye çalışanları ve bürokratlar tutuklandı.

Yandaşlara, vurgunlarla zenginleşenlere dokunmayanlar, söz konusu muhalifler olunca peşinen cezaevine gönderiyor. Tükenmiş iktidarın kurduğu ikili hukuk düzeninde, yargıyı elinde oyuncağa çevirenlerin yürüttüğü süreçlerden adalet de hukuk da çıkmadığını milletimiz görüyor. Elbet, bu zorbalık dönemi son bulacak.

Ayşegül Başkanımızın, meclis üyelerimizin, bürokratlarımızın ve tüm yol arkadaşlarımızın yanındayız. Cennet ülkemizde cehennemi yaşatmaya, milyonların nefesini kesmeye çalışanlara izin vermeyeceğiz. Halkın yanında olanlar kazanacak, güzel Türkiye’miz yeniden nefes alacak."

title: Polonya'da hükümetin yargı adımlarına karşı protesto
content:
Polonya’nın başkenti Varşova’da göstericiler, hükümetin yargı kurumlarına yönelik müdahalelerine tepki göstermek için sokağa çıktı. Szucha Caddesi boyunca toplanan kalabalık, Cumhurbaşkanı Karol Nawrocki’ye destek sloganları attı.

Yüksek Mahkeme başkanının, hükümet yanlısı yargıçlar tarafından idari kararla görevden uzaklaştırılması protestoların gerekçesi oldu. Göstericiler, Anayasa Mahkemesi binası çevresinde toplanarak hükümetin yargı alanındaki adımlarına karşı çıktı.

Polis ekipleri, gösterinin düzenlendiği bölgede güvenlik önlemleri aldı.

Polonya'da hükümet ile cumhurbaşkanlığı arasındaki gerilim, Anayasa Mahkemesi'nin yönetimi üzerinden açık bir siyasi çatışmaya dönüştü. 30 Ekim Cuma günü mahkemenin en kıdemli yargıcı Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, Mahkeme Başkanı Bogdan Swieczkowski ile Başkan Yardımcısı Bartlomiej Sochanski'nin görevlerini askıya aldığını ve mahkemenin yönetimini üstlendiğini duyurdu. Kararın ardından mahkeme binası çevresinde polis önlemleri artırılırken, muhalefet partisi Hukuk ve Adalet (PiS) öncülüğünde protestolar düzenlendi.

31 Ekim Cumartesi günü de devam eden krizde Cumhurbaşkanı Karol Nawrocki, yaşananları anayasal düzene müdahale olarak nitelendirerek parlamentodaki siyasi parti temsilcileriyle acil görüşme çağrısı yaptı.

Cumhurbaşkanı Nawrocki, mahkemedeki gelişmeler üzerine Senegal'e gerçekleştirdiği resmi ziyareti yarıda keserek Polonya'ya döndü. Gece saatlerinde Anayasa Mahkemesi'ne giden Nawrocki'nin binaya girişi sırasında yargıçlarla tartışma ve arbede yaşandı. Görüntülere yansıyan olayda Nawrocki'nin yargıçların arasından geçerek ilerlediği görüldü.

Cumartesi sabahı açıklama yapan Cumhurbaşkanlığı, mahkemedeki gelişmeleri "anayasal düzenin ihlali ve devletin anayasal bir organının zorla ele geçirilmesi" olarak nitelendirdi. Nawrocki, parlamentodaki siyasi parti gruplarının temsilcileriyle acil görüşmeler gerçekleştireceğini duyurdu.

Başbakan Donald Tusk ise hükümetin adımlarını savunarak, önceki PiS iktidarı döneminde zedelendiğini ileri sürdüğü hukuk devletini yeniden tesis etmenin zorunlu olduğunu söyledi.

Mahkeme Başkanı Swieczkowski'nin görevden uzaklaştırılmasına tepki gösteren yüzlerce kişi, 30 Ekim gecesi mahkeme binası önünde toplandı. Gösterilere PiS lideri Jarosław Kaczynski, eski Başbakan Mateusz Morawiecki ve aşırı sağcı siyasetçiler de katıldı.

Polis, bazı göstericilerin güvenlik çitlerini aşmaya çalıştığını ve güvenlik güçlerine cisimler attığını açıkladı. Olaylar sırasında üç kişi gözaltına alındı. Polis, müdahalenin mahkemenin iç işleyişine değil, bina çevresindeki kamu düzeninin sağlanmasına yönelik olduğunu bildirdi.

PiS lideri Kaczynski, hükümetin adımlarını Anayasa Mahkemesi'ne saldırı olarak nitelendirerek protestoların sürdürülmesi çağrısında bulundu.

Krizin hukuki boyutunda da yeni gelişmeler yaşandı. Adalet Bakanı ve Başsavcı Waldemar Zurek, Swieczkowski ve Sochanski hakkında dokunulmazlıklarının kaldırılması için Anayasa Mahkemesi'ne beş başvuru iletti. Başvuruların dördü Swieczkowski, biri Sochanski hakkında.

Zurek'in açıklamasına göre başvurularla birlikte iddialara ilişkin 50 ciltlik dosya da mahkemeye gönderildi.

Yargıç Korwin-Piotrowska ise 3 Kasım'da Anayasa Mahkemesi yargıçlarının genel kurulunu toplantıya çağırdı. Toplantıda mahkemenin 2027 yılı bütçesinin ele alınması da bekleniyor. Korwin-Piotrowska, bazı yargıçların görevlerini yerine getirmesinin engellendiğini ve bunun mahkemenin çalışmalarını aksattığını savunuyor.

Polonya'daki mevcut çatışmanın temeli, 2015-2023 yılları arasında iktidarda bulunan PiS döneminde yapılan yargı düzenlemelerine dayanıyor. PiS hükümetinin Anayasa Mahkemesi ve diğer yargı kurumlarında gerçekleştirdiği atamalar, ülkede yargı bağımsızlığı tartışmalarına yol açmış, Avrupa Birliği de bu düzenlemeler nedeniyle Polonya'ya yönelik yaptırımlar uygulamıştı.

2023'te iktidara gelen Donald Tusk liderliğindeki koalisyon, yargı bağımsızlığını yeniden tesis etme ve önceki dönemin düzenlemelerini değiştirme sözü verdi. Ancak bu süreçte cumhurbaşkanlığı makamı ile hükümet arasında yetki çatışması yaşandı.

Cumhurbaşkanı Nawrocki, parlamentonun seçtiği bazı yargıçların yemin törenlerini gerçekleştirmeyi reddederken, PiS döneminde göreve gelen Mahkeme Başkanı Swieczkowski de yeni parlamento çoğunluğunun seçtiği yargıçların görevlerine başlamasına izin vermedi.

title: Ankara'da kızını ve birlikte yaşadığı kişiyi öldüren zanlı yakalandı
content:
Ankara – Mamak ilçesinde kızı Elif Kesen (19) ve birlikte yaşadığı Ercan Oruç’u (53) öldüren Bülent Kesen (55) yakalandı.

Mamak ilçesinde dün akşam saatlerinde Bülent Kesen, kızının birlikte yaşadığı Ercan Oruç'un evine gitti. Evin önünde Kesen, üzerindeki tabancayı çıkarıp Ercan Oruç ve kızı Elif Kesen'e ateş ederek kaçtı. İhbar üzerine polis ve sağlık ekipleri bölgeye sevk edildi. Sağlık ekibinin yaptığı kontrolde Ercan Oruç ve Elif Kesen'in hayatını kaybettiği belirlendi.

Oruç'un cenazesi, Adli Tıp Kurumu'nda yapılan otopsinin ardından toprağa verilmek üzere Kırıkkale'ye gönderildi. Kesen'in otopsi işlemleri ise sürüyor.

Öte yandan olayın ardından kaçan Bülent Kesen, polisin çalışması sonucu yakalanarak gözaltına alındı. Emniyette sorgusu süren Bülent Kesen'in, kadın kuaförü olan Ercan Oruç ve yanında çalışan kızı Elif Kesen'in ilişkilerini onaylamadığını, bu nedenle öldürdüğü belirtildi.
